24_karat.name: 24 Karat
24_karat.description: The 24 Karat is a golden enemy that appeared in Golden mode, which is exclusive to Sandbox mode.

notice.text: 24 Karat was previously removed on the 29th of October 2020, though it has been made available through the Sandbox mode later.

stats.Spawned By:
- Mystery Boss (Golden, wave 38 onwards)
- Gold Titan

Description: The **24 Karat** is a golden enemy that appeared in Golden mode, which is exclusive to Sandbox mode. It has slightly fast speed while having health comparable to that of the Slow Boss. Its main trait was the fact that it is immune to splash damage due to it being a golden enemy. This means that most splash damage that comes from a tower, such as the Rocketeer, is useless against this.
The **24 Karat** can be spawned by the Gold Titan, and by the Mystery Boss upon its death in Golden mode, from wave 38 onwards.
Appearance: **Variant 1**

The current version of the **24 Karat** has no face and is colored gold from head to legs. It is slightly larger than the Golden. The **24 Karat** wears a short-sleeved shirt and a gold necktie. The shirt and legs are a different shade of gold compared to its arms. It also wears a golden fedora.
**Variant 2**

The first version of the **24 Karat** was nearly the same as the Golden, except that it wore a golden fedora. Additionally, the **24 Karat** used the glass material. Its head and fedora were bright golden, while its torso and legs were a slightly darker of gold.
Strategy: - Due to their high health and above average speed, high DPS towers such as the Pursuit, Ranger and Turret are recommended against this.
- The **24 Karat** is immune to splash damage. Towers that deal splash damage, like the Rocketeer, Mortar and Demoman, are useless against this enemy as they deal no damage.
- It is not, however, immune to all forms of splash damage. The Paintballer, Hallow Punk, Grenade, AirStrike and Nuke can still damage it.
- You can slow down the **24 Karat** by using the Freezer, DJ Booth and Electroshocker.
- As it has the Stun Immunity, it cannot be knocked back or stunned, only slowed down.
Trivia: - **24 Karat** is a reference to 24 karat (or 24 carat) gold, which is 99.99% pure gold.
- This makes the metal very soft, meaning that it is not stronger than lower karats of gold.
- Because of the Mystery Boss, the **24 Karat** can appear before its first wave appearance in Golden mode.
Update History: - First wave appearance changed from wave 59 to wave 39 on Hard mode (later Golden Mode).
- **NOTE**: While the **24 Karat** was removed in the Overhaul Update, one change was made to it, though it could never be seen in-game due to its removal. That change is:
- Partial Electric Immunity replaced with Energy Immunity.
- **24 Karat** can now be summoned in Sandbox mode and appears in the Sandbox exclusive Golden mode.
- Now has the Stun Immunity instead of the Energy Immunity.
- **24 Karat** can no longer be summoned in Sandbox mode.
- **24 Karat** can now be summoned in Sandbox mode and appears in the Sandbox exclusive Golden mode.

Description: **A** was an enemy which only appeared in the Hidden Wave and therefore only appeared in Fallen mode. As with the other lettered enemies that were in the game (B and C), it appeared after the Creator spawned.
**A** had a high amount of health and fast speed.
Appearance: **A** had black reflective skin, a white lab coat, and green granite torso and legs. It was similar in appearance to B and C. It was about the same size as the Abnormal.
Strategy: - Because of its high health, high DPS towers like the Turret, Minigunner, Ranger and Accelerator, are highly recommended.
- Additionally, Commander and DJ Booth should be used to boost said towers.
- Due to **A's** fast speed, you should use towers that slow enemies down, like the Electroshocker, Sledger, Freezer, Frost Blaster or Toxic Gunner.
Trivia: - This enemy was similar to B and C in terms of naming and appearance.
- This enemy was similar to M and J, from *Tower Battles*.
Update History: - **A** now appears in the legacy Hidden Wave, which is exclusive to Sandbox mode.
- **A** no longer appears in the legacy Hidden Wave, as it has been removed.

Description: The **Abnormal** is the first enemy that appears in Molten, Fallen, Challenge Trials and Fallen Arena PVP modes. It also appears in Badlands II and Pizza Party maps, and in The Takeover Event. Compared to the Normal, the **Abnormal** is faster and has more health. It also appears in the Sandbox exclusive Legacy Fallen and Golden modes.
The **Abnormal** can be spawned by the Dark Necromancer and from the Mystery upon its death in Legacy Fallen, Hardcore and Golden modes.
Logbook Description: "*The Abnormal zombie is a mutation from your basic zombie. It is faster and has more health than its predecessor, and can usually be found in your typical horde.*"
Appearance: **Variant 1**
The current version of the **Abnormal** has a desaturated green skin color and a dirty dark brown torso and legs. It has dark green veins on its arms and head.
It has two randomly chosen animations, one of which has it confidently walking upright, while the other is remarkably similar with the key difference being that it is leaning forward.
**Variant 2**
**Variant 1**

The current version of the legacy **Abnormal** in Hardcore mode has a reflective desaturated light green skin color and black diamond-plated torso and legs. Its face has two scars, which forms an "X" on its face.
**Variant 2**

The current Enemies Beta version of the legacy **Abnormal** has a desaturated dark green skin color with lighter green veins running along its head and arms. It has a dark greyish-blue torso and legs.
**Variant 3**
The second version of the **Abnormal** had a reflective light green skin color, a purple granite torso and legs, and a sad face.
**Variant 4**
The first version of the **Abnormal** had a salmon skin color, a brown pebble torso, darker brown pebble legs and a drooling zombie face.
**Variant 3**

The current version of the legacy **Abnormal** in Hardcore mode has a reflective desaturated light green skin color and black diamond-plated torso and legs. Its face has two scars, which forms an "X" on its face.
**Variant 4**

The current Enemies Beta version of the legacy **Abnormal** has a desaturated dark green skin color with lighter green veins running along its head and arms. It has a dark greyish-blue torso and legs.
**Variant 5**
The second version of the **Abnormal** had a reflective light green skin color, a purple granite torso and legs, and a sad face.
**Variant 6**
The first version of the **Abnormal** had a salmon skin color, a brown pebble torso, darker brown pebble legs and a drooling zombie face.
Strategy: - Most towers can deal with the **Abnormal** effectively.
- Any tower catered towards early-game, like the Cowboy, Golden Soldier, Brawler, Militant or Golden Cowboy is recommended.
- It is unnecessary to try to get stronger, more expensive towers like the Minigunner solely to deal with **Abnormals**, as cheaper options fare well against them already.
- Towers that can deal damage to multiple enemies are especially effective against **Abnormals** as they spawn in hordes. Such towers include the Electroshocker, Assassin, Pyromancer and Shotgunner.

- While slightly risky, it is sometimes ideal to avoid defending against the first few waves of **Abnormals** and simply let them reach the exit, as their low health makes it unlikely to make you lose, especially with high base health.
- You can use the Medic to heal the base health back, but it is not necessary.
- As you are not spending money on defenses, you can use the Farm more effectively for the first few waves to get better towers when stronger enemies appear.
Trivia: - While the Legacy version of the **Abnormal** can drop a Logbook, getting it will only give the player the modern **Abnormal** in the Index.

Description: The **Abnormal Boss** is a large enemy that is the first (non-major) boss to appear in Legacy Fallen mode and Golden mode, alongside a few challenges. The **Abnormal Boss** is slightly faster than the Heavy.
Outside of Sandbox mode, the **Abnormal Boss** has been completely replaced by the Elite Abnormal.
Appearance: **Variant 1**

The current version of the **Abnormal Boss** has a reflective light green skin color and a black diamond-plated torso and legs. It has one pair of grey chains wrapped around its left arm, three pairs around its right arm and a pair wrapped around its torso. The **Abnormal Boss's** face has two scars, which forms an "X" on its face.
**Variant 2**

The Enemies Beta version of the **Abnormal Boss** is a humanoid with a waist in its rig. It has a dark green skin color and a dark greyish-blue torso and legs. Veins can be seen on its arms and head and it has no face. It also wears black armbands with grey spikes on them.
**Variant 3**

The second version of the **Abnormal Boss** had a reflective light green skin color and a magenta granite torso and legs. It had one pair of grey chains wrapped around its left arm, three pairs around its right arm and a pair wrapped around its torso. It also had a drooling zombie face with glowing magenta eyes.
**Variant 4**
The first version of **Abnormal Boss** had a salmon skin color, a brown pebble torso with tumors and darker brown pebble legs. It also had a drooling zombie face with glowing red eyes.
Strategy: - The **Abnormal Boss** has much higher health than the enemies that make their debut before it, along with defense. Thus, it is recommended to invest in additional defense before its debut.
- Most towers that have a sizeable DPS can deal with the **Abnormal Boss** quite effectively.
- Almost any tower catered towards early game, like the Ace Pilot, Gladiator, Golden Scout, Militant or Golden Crook Boss is recommended.
- Stronger towers like the Brawler, Minigunner or Golden Minigunner can fare pretty well if you are able to afford them.

- Later on, towers that can deal damage to multiple enemies can also be effective against **Abnormal Bosses** as they will spawn more frequently. Such towers include the Demoman, Executioner, Mortar and Shotgunner.
- Splash damage also ignores defense, making splash damage towers even more effective.
- The Military Base's units deal full collision damage to enemies with defense, making multiple Level 2 Military Bases very effective against this enemy.
- Early game towers with defense dropping, like the Cryomancer, Frost Blaster or Pyromancer can be useful at both killing the **Abnormal Boss** and decreasing its defense.
- Decreasing its defense is not required however, as the **Abnormal Boss** has a negligible amount of defense.
- Multiple such towers, like the Toxic Gunner, Freezer or Frost Blaster can also be used to slow it down.
Trivia: - The current appearance of the **Abnormal Boss** looks similar to the current appearance of Boss1 from *Tower Battles*.
Update History: - No longer appears in Golden mode as it has been removed.
- Speed increased from Slightly Slow to Below Average.
- Now has a new appearance with the Enemies Beta modifier active.
- No longer appears naturally in Fallen mode, as it has been replaced by the Fallen Squire.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Two Hearts & Two Brains** - On death, the **Abomination** will reanimate itself, regaining half of its health, including the health gained from the Mutation modifier. It will also have its name changed from **Abomination** to **Reanimated**, lose one of its heads, gains a red outline and red glowing veins on its arms.

Description: The **Abomination** is a fast and tanky enemy that appears in Polluted Wasteland II. It has a very high amount of health, fast speed and low defense. It also has Stun Immunity, making it harder to slow down. Upon death, the **Abomination** will turn into the **Reanimated**. This gives it half of its health back, including the Shield Health gained from the Mutation modifier and a slight appearance change.
The **Abomination** replaces the Tank in Oops! All slimes! Challenge Map. The **Abomination** used to be spawned by the Nuclear Monster, if it was not close enough to the exit.
Appearance: The **Abomination** is a large humanoid with a waist and lower arms in its rig. It has a dark blue skin color and the ends of its limbs are coated in a green fluid. It has black armbands with grey spikes and abs with tumors and wounds on its chest. It has grey shoulder-pads which have cuts and blood on them. It also has two faceless heads, one being larger than the other. When it becomes the **Reanimated**, its larger head will explode, with blood particles and a red spot being where the head once was, and it will also gain glowing red veins on its upper arms and a red outline.
Strategy: - Use high DPS towers such as the Accelerator, Ranger, Pursuit and Engineer to defeat this enemy.

- Do note that when the **Abomination** transforms into the **Reanimated**, the Accelerator will lock onto a different enemy. This may end up letting the **Reanimated** get past it, if you do not have any other high DPS towers.

- Note that, outside of its debut wave (where it has the Boss attribute), the Hacker can convert the **Abomination**, completely cancelling its **Two Hearts & Two Brains** ability and making it far less threatening.
- The Hacker can also slow down the **Abomination** in the process, rendering it almost entirely irrelevant if you have enough damage to deal with it in the first place.
- The Commander and DJ Booth can be very useful at decreasing the firerate of towers and increasing their range.

- The Electroshocker and Warden will not stun it but only slow it down because of its Stun Immunity. Additionally, the Warden will slow it down for a shorter amount of time due to the **Abomination's** size.
- Knockback towers like the Brawler cannot knock it back as it has the Stun Immunity.
- Due to this, it's generally best to use freezing towers such as the Freezer or Frost Blaster to stall it.
Trivia: - The **Abomination** is the first enemy to revive itself from death.
- The Commander used to improperly call this enemy a Tank. This was due to the Polluted Wasteland II dialogue being borrowed from the Fallen mode dialogue before the Halloween 2022 Update.
- The Commander also mentioned it being able to throw boulders, something that neither the Tank nor **Abomination** can do.
- The Tank used to be able to throw boulders before the Overhaul Update. The Commander dialogue for the Tank was not updated when the Tank lost its ability.
- The **Abomination** was based on a fan idea from the Tower Defense Simulator Discord server.
Update History: - Energy Immunity replaced with Stun Immunity.
- Health decreased from 20,000 to 6,000 in Oops! All slimes!.
- None of the changes are applied to the legacy version.
- Speed increased from Fast (6) to Very Fast (8.5).
- **Bug**: Appears twice in the Index, one of them not loading in any model for the preview.
- **Bugfix**: No longer appears twice in the Index.
Notes: - ↑ Only the first **Abomination** is a Boss enemy.

Description: The **Agent Ducky** was an enemy that appeared in Bathroom Approach as part of the Ducky Revenge Event and its rerun in the Spring Frenzy Battle Pass. It has high health and average speed. It has one ability where the **Agent Ducky** pulls out a silenced pistol and shoots a tower in its range of 20 with it, stunning it for 5 seconds or dealing 400 damage if it targeted a unit.
The **Agent Ducky** can also be spawned by the Operator Ducky.
Logbook Description: "*Agent 42. Their stealth missions are legendary in the duck intelligence community, and their gadget collection would make even Spy Ducky jealous. Their most notable weapon is a heat-seeking briefcase that tracks its target. Agent 42’s secret code name is "Quackles", though they prefer to keep that classified.*"
Appearance: The **Agent Ducky** is a regular yellow duck with an orange beak and flippers, which wears an agent suit. The suit is black with a white shirt and a red tie. On the back of its head, it has a black barcode. It carries a silenced pistol, which it uses to stun towers with.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Bathroom Approach is listed instead.
- As the **Agent Ducky** has quite high health, high DPS towers like the Pursuit, Crook Boss, Ranger or Minigunner are recommended here.
- Some stronger early-game towers like the Mortar can also still be helpful at handling these enemies.
- The Pursuit and Mortar are especially useful here, as they will not get stunned by the **Agent Ducky**.
- You can place down multiple cheap towers to bait the **Agent Ducky's** attack, though this is not necessary.
Trivia: - The sound after a shot is fired is similar to that of the James Bond chord.
- The **Agent Ducky** is a reference to Agent 47 from the *Hitman* game series.
- Its agent name, *Agent 42*, is a reference to Agent 47's name.
- The barcode seen on the back of the **Agent Ducky's** head is a reference to the Agent 47's barcode, also placed on the back of his head.
- The heat-seeking briefcase mentioned in the Logbook description is the ICA Executive Briefcase.
- In the Easy difficulty of Bathroom Approach, the dialogue for the **Agent Ducky** is shown on Wave 9, even though it first appears on Wave 8.
- The **Agent Ducky** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Flesh Shilling** - Spawns Fleshlings every 0.25 seconds when damaged. When up to six Fleshlings are spawned in a short period of time, there is a few seconds of cooldown before it can spawn anything again.

Description: The **Amalgamation** is an enemy that exclusively appears in Polluted Wasteland II. It has a high amount of health and an average speed. It has one ability, when it takes damage, it will spawn up to six Fleshlings. It will also emit blood particles when it spawns a Fleshling. The **Amalgamation** replaces the Giant Boss in Polluted Wasteland II. The **Amalgamation** also has the Stun Immunity and Freeze Immunity, which makes stuns only slow it down instead of fully stopping it, prevents it from being knocked back and makes it immune to being frozen or chilled. Its legacy version available in Sandbox only does not have Freeze Immunity.

The **Amalgamation** used to be spawned by the Nuclear Monster when it used its *Nuclear Summon* ability. This means it could also appear in Oops! All slimes!, if spawned by the Nuclear Monster. It also could have been spawned by the Mystery Boss before the Halloween 2022 Update.
Appearance: The **Amalgamation** is a mutated, hulking and faceless humanoid with a waist and lower arms in its rig. It has a light red skin color and black pants. It has a bear trap shackled around its right leg and a larger bear trap fitted around its neck. It has multiple clumps of flesh and smaller humanoids on its torso and arms.
Strategy: - High DPS towers, such as the Ranger, Turret, Golden Minigunner, Accelerator or Engineer are recommended to take down the **Amalgamation**.

- Be aware that if the Accelerators locks on to the **Amalgamation**, the Fleshlings that it spawns will get past the Accelerator. Due to this, placing other towers like the Engineer to kill them is highly recommended while the Accelerators focus on killing the **Amalgamation**.
- The Commander can be very useful at boosting the firerate of towers, making them deal more damage against the **Amalgamation** and its Fleshlings.
- Slowdown towers can be useful against this, though it has multiple immunities making it harder to slow down.
- Freeze and chillness is completely ineffective against it, as it has the Freeze Immunity.
- Due to its Stun Immunity, it cannot be knocked back and stuns only slow it down instead of stunning it.
- It also spawns as a Boss enemy when it first spawns, making it immune to even more stalls, such as the DJ Booth, Toxic Gunner, Jester confusion and a stronger immunity to stun slowdown.
Trivia: - The **Amalgamation**, despite never being intended to appear in a server with more than four players, has MEGA Servers health scaling. It increases its health by 150 for every player after 4 players.
- This is most likely carried over from the original Amalgamation, which also increased its health by 150.

- Interestingly, the **Amalgamation's** Fleshlings, despite being an enemy unique to Polluted Wasteland II have the same health scaling as the **Amalgamation**. This was also most likely carried over from the original Amalgamation.
- The Commander used to improperly call this enemy a Giant Boss.
- This is because the Commander's dialogue for Fallen mode was not changed in Polluted Wasteland II before the Halloween 2022 Update.
Update History: - **Bugfix**: Can now can be attacked by towers.
- **Bug**: Spawned Fleshlings in Sandbox mode are invisible without the Legacy modifier.
- None of the changes are applied to the legacy version.
- **Bug**: Appears twice in the Index, one of them not loading in any model for the preview.
- **Bugfix**: No longer appears twice in the Index.
Notes: - ↑ Only the first **Amalgamation** is a Boss enemy.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Regeneration** - Heals 3% of its maximum health every second.

Description: The **Amalgamation** was an enemy that only appeared in Polluted Wasteland, replacing the Giant Boss. While replacing the Giant Boss whenever it was meant to spawn in Fallen mode in Polluted Wasteland, the **Amalgamation** was much faster than the Giant Boss while also having 3,000 more health. In addition, the **Amalgamation** had a constant health regeneration ability, which made it hard to kill without teamwork.
The **Amalgamation** used to spawn from the Mystery Boss upon its death in Polluted Wasteland Fallen mode only.
Appearance: The **Amalgamation's** appearance was similar to the second version of the Tank (with even more likeness to the removed Tank 2). It had regular arms and red skin. Its torso was slightly bloated and tumors could be seen on its left arm and back. The **Amalgamation** had black pants with bones sticking out of its arms. It also had a happy drooling face with red glowing eyes. It had the same walking animation as the Wasted Boss. The **Amalgamation** emitted healing particles every time it healed.
Strategy: - The **Amalgamation** is extremely dangerous when it first debuts. Major preparations must be made multiple waves before it spawns.
- High DPS towers are required to take the **Amalgamation** down. The DJ Booth and Commander help massively.
- Placement is key; if given any breathing room, the **Amalgamation** will heal up all the damage it has taken. Ensure your towers cover as much path as possible.
- The Ranger with its long range can be good for this. The DJ Booth also boosts range.
- The Swarmer's *Beehive Grenade*, when stacked, can take the **Amalgamation** out.
- The Farm should be used to get these towers.

- The Military Base can be surprisingly good at dealing with the **Amalgamation**. The Tank and Railgun Tank do massive collision damage, and with enough of them the **Amalgamation** can be defeated with relative ease.
- This requires multiple players to commit to using the Military Base.
- Slowing towers can be beneficial considering the **Amalgamation's** fast speed.
- Later on in the game, **Amalgamations** may still pose a threat, especially when spawned in excess from Mystery Bosses and boosted by Circuits.

- By this point, many high DPS towers, inclusive of Accelerators and Rangers, should have been placed down. There should also be chaining of the Commander's *Call to Arms* ability, and the DJ Booth boosting every single tower.
Trivia: - The Commander improperly calls this enemy a Giant Boss.
- This is because the Commander's dialogue for Fallen mode was not changed in Polluted Wasteland.
Update History: - *Regeneration* ability changed from regenerating 10% of its current health every second to 5% of its current health every second.
- *Regeneration* ability changed, from regenerating 5% of its current health every second to 3% of its max health every second.

abilities.label: Ability 1
abilities.text: **Dramatic Entrance** - When spawning, the **Awakened Fallen King** appears slightly in front of the entrance, glitching all the players' screens and smashing the ground, followed by a loud screech and a massive shockwave with purple lightning that stuns towers for 5 seconds and deals 200 damage to units.

abilities.label: Ability 2 Cooldown: 45
abilities.text: **Fallen Comet** - The **Awakened Fallen King** slams its sword into the ground, lifts its right arm up then moves it back down slowly and then pulls out the sword, making a large number of purple spikes fall down from the sky, stunning towers for 5 seconds and dealing 50 damage to units with no range limit for the ability.

abilities.label: Ability 3 Cooldown: 25
abilities.text: **Sword Swing** - The **Awakened Fallen King** slashes its sword three times, with the arc increasing until a full circle area on the last slash. Each slash will stun towers for 6 seconds and damages units in its area by 100.

abilities.label: Ability 4 Cooldown: 15
abilities.text: **Summon** - The **Awakened Fallen King** will raise its sword in the air, summoning forty Fallen Giants (40% chance), Fallen Shields (20% chance) and Fallen Heroes (40% chance). As this can only be used once and the Fallen King using the ability counts as an **Awakened Fallen King** usage, this ability ends up unused in most normal matches.

abilities.label: Ability 5 Cooldown: 50
abilities.text: **Undead Charge** - The **Awakened Fallen King** will raise its sword forward, summoning five Necrotic Skeletons with a 0.25 delay between each spawn.

abilities.label: Ability 6
abilities.text: **Complete Awakening** - After reaching 500,000 health, the **Awakened Fallen King** throws away its shield and then does a large stomp, stunning towers for 4 seconds. Speed is increased after this ability.

Description: The **Awakened Fallen King** is a boss that appears in the Hidden Wave. It is the second and later third phase of the Fallen King, it boasts significantly higher health than its first form and possesses more abilities.
The **Awakened Fallen King** has six abilities:

- Its first ability, *Dramatic Entrance*, only happens when the **Awakened Fallen King** first spawns. It will appear slightly in front of the entrance, dropping from the sky. This creates a shockwave upon landing, stunning any tower hit for 5 seconds and deals 200 damage to units.
- The second, *Fallen Comet*, makes it slam its sword into the ground, which creates multiple purple spikes that fall down from the sky, stunning towers for 5 seconds and dealing 50 damage to units.

- The third is *Sword Swing*, which makes it slash its sword three times, with the arc increasing until a full circle area on the last slash. Each slash will stun towers in its area for 6 seconds and deals 100 damage to units.

- The fourth and fifth abilities, *Summon* and *Undead Charge* are both abilities that summon enemies, with the difference being the enemies it summons. *Summon* summons forty enemies, which are the Fallen Giants with a 40% chance, Fallen Shields with a 20% chance and Fallen Heroes with a 40% chance, while *Undead Army* only summons five Necrotic Skeletons with a 0.25 second delay between each one. As the *Summon* ability can only be used once and the Fallen King using the ability counts as an **Awakened Fallen King** usage, this ability ends up unused in most normal matches.

- Its sixth ability is *Complete Awakening*, which happens when the **Awakened Fallen King** has lost 500,000 of its health. It makes it throw away its shield and then do a stomp, stunning all towers hit for 4 seconds. After this ability, the **Awakened Fallen King** becomes faster, almost doubling its speed.
Appearance: The **Awakened Fallen King** wears metal armor, with a glowing purple shard-shaped core in the middle and a purple diamond in its waist. He also wears purple boots with small purple shards in the middle of each. Its neon purple right arm only has a shoulder pad, with the armor's "stripes" on the arm being neon pink. The left arm has a shoulder pad and large purple crystals. It wears a metal helmet on its head, which is broken on the left side of its face and reveals a crack in its left eye, both eyes also glowing purple. It wears a crown over the helmet, with the middle of the crown having a purple crystal, the sides having a few purple spikes and the top of the crown having large purple crystals. Compared to its original form, the crystals in the helmet and shoulders are taller and spikier in the awakened form.

It wields a large, glowing purple sword with a black handle in its right arm, with the tip of the sword being white and there being two spiky crystals on the sides near the handle. It also wields in its left hand a large metal shield with a glowing purple shard in the middle of it and three purple spikes on the sides.

The **Awakened Fallen King** has a spawn animation, glitching all the players' screens and smashing the ground, followed by a loud screech and a massive shockwave with purple lightning that stuns towers.
When defeated, the **Awakened Fallen King** will disintegrate in a purple beam of light and screech loudly.
Strategy: - Right when the Fallen King dies, you can use the DJ Booth's *Drop The Beat* ability on Red track to melt its defense due to it losing the Boss attribute, which will consequently reduce the defense of the **Awakened Fallen King**.

- Due to a bug, towers like the Pyromancer, Cryomancer, Electroshocker and Freezer can also drop the Fallen King's defense, so if you use them in combination, you can effectively remove the defense of the **Awakened Fallen King**, making it significantly easier to deal with.
- Towers that deal high DPS, such as the Engineer, Turret, Ranger, Pursuit, Gatling Gun are highly recommended.
- You should try to upgrade all placed towers to max level. The $50,000 that Hidden Wave gives should help with this.
- Due to Aggro enemies directing damage away from the **Awakened Fallen King** such as the Fallen Shield, moving towers may be required.

- The **Awakened Fallen King** alongside the multiple other enemies that can stun like Fallen Honor Guard will be constantly using their abilities, which results in a large amount of towers being stunned for long periods of time.
- The Medic is therefore recommended.
- It is still recommended to bring stun immune DPS towers, such as the Ranger and Pursuit.

- The Engineer will perform extremely well against the **Awakened Fallen King** due to the stunning abilities not having an effect on the War Machine Sentry when its bubble shield is activated. However, if the Engineer is not unstunned before another ability which can damage units is performed by the **Awakened Fallen King**, or another enemy like the Fallen Guardian, then the Engineer's effectiveness is dramatically reduced.
- The Golden Minigunner will be heavily affected by the amount of stuns performed due to it having to rev-up after being stunned.
Trivia: - The **Awakened Fallen King** is technically not a separate enemy, but instead, the second and later third phase for the Fallen King, as they are the same enemy internally.
- Uniquely, unlike other such enemies like the Abomination, it does not change phases shortly after being defeated. It actually takes it multiple waves to appear.
- Additionally, multiple parts of the Hidden Wave, such as its wave structure, are also tied to the Fallen King enemy.
- Because of this, the enemies summoned by the **Awakened Fallen King** are called "*Fallen King's _____*" instead of "*Awakened Fallen King's _____*".
- This is also the reason why the **Awakened Fallen King** cannot drop a Logbook for the **Awakened Fallen King**.
- An unused version of the **Awakened Fallen King** was depicted in the *Error Buster* badge, which was later used for the Fallen mode badge after the 2nd of August 2024.
- It was depicted with a similar appearance to the version of the legacy Fallen King, with purple accents and slightly altered features.
- As the **Awakened Fallen King** was not widely publicized, it was speculated that the **Awakened Fallen King** was cancelled.
- The **Awakened Fallen King** depicted on the game icon and renders has a large grin similar to Patient Zero, however the **Awakened Fallen King** lacks one in-game.

- The **Awakened Fallen King's** theme has past motifs from Phoqus' previous works. Distinct motifs include the intro of the legacy Hidden Wave, the second track used in the Hardcore Lobby, The Great Finale ambience, the original lose theme, the Void Reaver's current theme and the **Plushie** DJ Booth's theme.
- The **Awakened Fallen King** is the first naturally spawning enemy not to spawn at the start of the path.
- The **Awakened Fallen King** spawns slightly in front of the entrance.
Update History: - **Bug**: If a player rejoins, the **Awakened Fallen King** disappears and sometimes later re-appears using the Fallen King model.
- **Bug**: Defense cannot be dropped by poison and electric defense dropping towers.
- **Bug**: *Fallen Comet* ability can cause frame drops.
- *Summon* ability now can summon Fallen Shields with a 20% chance.
- *Summon* ability now summons Fallen Giants and Fallen Heroes with a 40% chance instead of 15%.
- *Summon* can no longer summon Corrupted Fallens and Possessed Armors.

- **Bugfix**: No longer can be slowed down by the DJ Booth.

- **Bugfix**: **Awakened Fallen King's** defense can now be dropped by poison and electric defense dropping towers, if it has no Boss attribute, though the Jester still cannot drop it.
- **Bug**: Boss health bar now sometimes displays its name as just "Fallen King", instead of "Awakened Fallen King".

Description: The **Balloon** is an enemy which only appears in Hardcore and Voidcore modes. It has a balloon tied to its back which makes it fly, making it immune to collision damage, as well as making it undetectable by some towers and units. The balloon on its back pops when the **Balloon** loses all of its Shield Health, making the enemy vulnerable to collisions and ground towers. Its speed is also reduced by diving its speed by 1.5.
The **Balloon** can be spawned by the Grave Digger in Hardcore mode. The **Balloon** can also be spawned from the Mystery upon its death in Hardcore mode.
Logbook Description: "*It’s not entirely clear why they are tied to the balloon. Perhaps it was a cruel joke by the Mandrakes, but the Balloon is left stranded regardless. The Void army is organized for what its needs are and, as it turns out, the Balloons are incredibly useful in battle. At first the Void Caster simply stared at the hundreds bumping against one another in the Vault, but then praised the little bush Mandrakes for their ingenuity.*"
Appearance: **Variant 1**

The **Balloon** has grey with a purple torso and legs. On its arms and head, it has purple veins. It flies in the air thanks to a balloon that is strapped to its back with rope. Once it loses all of its Shield Health, the balloon pops and it will drop down to the ground.
**Variant 2**

The legacy **Balloon** has light red skin, a brown torso and legs, and is faceless. It has one red balloon tied to its back. When it loses its shield health, the balloon pops and the **Balloon** walks along the path like any other regular enemy.
Strategy: - Cheap towers with flying detection like the Engineer, Crook Boss, Operator, Golden Soldier or Ace Pilot can be used to take the **Balloon** down with relative ease. However, it is still recommended to continue investing in flying detection due to the denser quantities of **Balloons** that spawn later on.
- Once it loses its Shield Health, the **Balloon** can be dealt with extremely easily, as it no longer has the Flying attribute.
Trivia: - The **Balloon** could be based on the Balloon Zombie from *Plants vs. Zombies*.
- The **Balloon** could also be based on the Bloons from the *Bloons Tower Defense* series.

balloon_kid.description: The Balloon Kid is an enemy only found in Pizza Party. It has a mediocre amount of health and an above average speed.

Description: The **Balloon Kid** is an enemy only found in Pizza Party. It has a mediocre amount of health and an above average speed. However, it holds a balloon which it uses to float in the air, making it a Flying enemy. This also means that it cannot collide with units, as well as being undetectable by the majority of towers and units.
Appearance: The **Balloon Kid** is a robot that resembles a child. It has tan skin, grey pants, black shoes, a striped red and blue torso, sleeves, propeller hat and a balloon that it holds, which it uses to float in the air. It has a red nose and the left side of its face is torn open. It also has two red buttons on its torso. Its propeller hat's propeller spins as the **Balloon Kid** flies.
It makes a popping sound on death.
Strategy: - Towers with flying detection are the best way to deal with the **Balloon Kid**.
- The Ranger and Golden Soldier are very strong options.
- The Militant is another option, but may be unreliable due to its lower DPS.
- As these spawn in hordes, the Executioner and Mortar can be quite effective at clearing them out.
- The Ace Pilot and Pursuit can deal with **Balloon Kids** fairly effectively, but be mindful of their circling and targeting mechanics, which could let some **Balloon Kids** past.
- Alternatively, if you do not have any towers with flying detection, you can use a UAV to make other towers target **Balloon Kids**.
- Do note that the UAV only lasts 30 seconds and can only be used four times, so you cannot completely rely on it for flying detection, though it can allow you to survive a few waves without it.
- You can also use the Commander's *Support Caravan* ability to spawn in Gunner APCs and Missile APCs if your main DPS does not have flying detection.

- There are many towers that do not have flying detection but can damage **Balloon Kids** in other ways. Most of these methods are not viable ways to deal with the **Balloon Kids**. Another detectable enemy must be nearby for these to happen.
- Explosions from towers can damage the **Balloon Kid** indirectly.
- Only the Mortar, Ace Pilot and Pursuit can directly target **Balloon Kids** with splash damage. Others require a nearby detectable enemy.
- Some ground towers, like the Gladiator, can hit the **Balloon Kid** while it is in the air, if they are on a high platform or leverage, though this is extremely unlikely to occur.
- The Brawler tower is able to hit the **Balloon Kid** using its *Reposition* ability.
Trivia: - The **Balloon Kid** is based on Balloon Boy from the *Five Nights at Freddy's* series.
Update History: - **Bug**: **Balloon Kid** does not have a hover Hitbox, preventing its health bar from being seen.
- **Bug**: Propeller hat is not affected by Time Scale.
- **Bug**: Appears twice in the Index, one of them not loading in any model for the preview.

- **Bugfix**: Now has a hover hitbox, though it is quite small, only covering a portion of its torso.
- **Bugfix**: No longer appears twice in the Index.
- **Bug**: **Balloon Kid's** model does not appear in the Index.

Strategy: - Early game towers like the Golden Scout, Cowboy, Golden Cowboy or Crook Boss can do quite well against these.
- As these enemies spawn in large numbers, towers that can damage multiple enemies at once, such as the Executioner, can be useful against this.
Trivia: - The Elf unit from the Elf Camp is based on this enemy.

bat_solar_eclipse.name: Bat
bat_solar_eclipse.description: The Bat was an enemy that appeared in the third and fourth night of the Solar Eclipse Event.

notice.text: Bat (Solar Eclipse) has been removed from the game as of the 26th of January 2022 as it was part of the Solar Eclipse Event.

bat_solar_eclipse.mode_appearance:
- Solar Eclipse Night III
- Solar Eclipse Night IV

Description: The **Bat** was an enemy that appeared in the third and fourth night of the Solar Eclipse Event. It did not spawn naturally and was instead spawned by the Vampire on death. While it had lower health than the Vampire, it had faster speed. Additionally, it was a Flying enemy, so most towers could not attack it.
Appearance: The **Bat** was a humanoid bat. It had dark purple skin with fur around its neck and black bat wings. It also had purple hair and red glowing eyes.
Strategy: - Towers such as the Ace Pilot and Pursuit are recommended against this enemy.
- These towers can also deal splash damage, allowing them to clear out hordes of **Bats** faster.
- The Ranger and Hunter, paired with the Commander's *Call to Arms* ability, can perform well against these enemies.
- The Mortar may not be a very good choice because of its slow firerate and lack of damage.
- Additionally, Mortar's projectile explodes on the ground. At low levels, the Mortar may only deal small amounts of damage to the **Bat**.
- The **Bat** can get hit by a Level 4+ Electroshocker in its chain reaction.
- The Pyromancer can set this on fire if there is another detectable enemy near it.
- However, it can only set the **Bat** on fire at Level 5, as the flames are too small to hit the **Bat** at any level below Level 5.
- Despite being a flying enemy, units from the **Classic** Military Base and from the regular Crook Boss can still collide with it, though they cannot detect it.
Update History: - Now appears in the Totality Tower.

bat_trick_or_threat_town.name: Bat
bat_trick_or_threat_town.description: The Bat was an enemy that appeared exclusively in Trick or Threat Town as part of the Halloween 2020 Event. They were spawned after a Vampire was killed.

notice.text: Bat (Trick or Threat Town) has been removed from the game as of the 8th of May 2021 as it was part of the Halloween 2020 Event.

Description: The **Bat** was an enemy that appeared exclusively in Trick or Threat Town as part of the Halloween 2020 Event. They were spawned after a Vampire was killed. They had low health but were quite fast (faster than the Vampire). They could not be detected by ground towers or be hit by units. They were also hidden, meaning that the scope of towers that could hit the **Bat** was severely limited.
Appearance: The **Bat** took the appearance of a regular cave-dwelling bat. It was completely black and relatively small compared to the Vampire, while also flying above the ground.
Strategy: - The only towers that can detect the **Bat** are Level 4+ Ace Pilots, Level 5 Pursuits and Level 2+ Snipers.
- Rangers are useless against **Bats** since they do not have hidden detection.
- Mortars cannot detect **Bats**, but it can hit them indirectly with its explosion.
- Most splash damage towers can hit the **Bat**, even if the tower cannot detect it, as long as the enemy gets caught in the explosion.
- As these appear late in the game, you can save for an expensive hidden detection upgrade for an effective cliff or air-based tower.
- For example, the Level 5 Ace Pilot is a great counter to this enemy.
- When the **Bat** initially spawns from the Vampire, it flies low enough for it to be hit by the Pyromancer, Gladiator and Shotgunner.
- However, this is extremely unlikely to occur as there needs to be another enemy that can be detected by these towers in the vicinity of the **Bat**.
- On very rare occasions, the Electroshocker can hit the **Bat** via a chain reaction.
- As the **Bat** is very small, this heavily slows it down.
Trivia: - This was very similar to the Bat that appeared in Nightmare Carnival, except that this version could not be detected by ground towers, while the Nightmare Carnival version can.
- Appearance-wise, the two enemies looked identical.
- Similar to the Balloon, some ground towers like the Electroshocker, Pyromancer, Gladiator and Shotgunner could hit the **Bat** while it was in the air, if it spawned low enough.

bat_nightmare_carnival.name: Bat
bat_nightmare_carnival.description: The Bat was an enemy that appeared exclusively in Nightmare Carnival as part of the Halloween 2019 Event. It was spawned after a Vampire was killed.

notice.text: Bat (Nightmare Carnival) has been removed from the game as of the 9th of November 2019 as it was part of the Halloween 2019 Event.

Description: The **Bat** was an enemy that appeared exclusively in Nightmare Carnival as part of the Halloween 2019 Event. It was spawned after a Vampire was killed. It was also spawned by Jack O' Bot. It was quite fast (faster than the Vampire and Ghost) while also having a considerable amount of health.
As the **Bat** was flying, it could not be hit by collisions from units, like Tanks from the Military Base. It was also hidden, so it could not be targeted by towers without hidden detection.
Appearance: The **Bat** took the appearance of a regular cave-dwelling bat. It was completely black and relatively small compared to the Vampire, while also flying above the ground.
Strategy: - The Military Base's units (like the Humvee 3) and SWAT Van (from the Enforcer) are useless against **Bats** as they cannot target or collide with the **Bat**.
- The Crook Boss's units are also useless against **Bats**, as they cannot detect them.
- Despite being a flying enemy, the **Bat** could be detected by ground towers.
- This makes the Minigunner and Turret very useful against it.
- Due to the **Bat's** high speed, a Level 3+ Pyromancer is recommended to slow them down.
- A Level 0-2 Pyromancer cannot detect the **Bat**, as the Pyromancer only receives hidden detection on Level 3.
- If a Vampire with low health is reaching the end of the map, try not to kill it as it will turn into a **Bat**, doing considerably more damage to the base.
- The Freezer's *Ice Age* ability can freeze **Bats**, even though the ability appears on the ground.
Trivia: - This was the first enemy to be immune to collisions, tied with the Witch, though the **Bat** was immune from collision from all units, while the Witch was only immune from collision by the Tank and Railgun Tank.
- This was the second enemy to fly, after the UFO and tied with the Witch.
- The **Bat** was based on R2D's Cavebat.
- The **Bat** appeared on the Hunter's original **Halloween** skin.

beehive.name: Beehive
beehive.description: The Beehive was an enemy that only appeared in Eggy Island hard mode as part of the Spring 2020 Event. This did not appear in easy mode.

notice.text: Beehive has been removed from the game as of the 26th of May 2020 as it was part of the Spring 2020 Event.

Description: The **Beehive** was an enemy that only appeared in Eggy Island hard mode as part of the Spring 2020 Event. This did not appear in easy mode. This enemy moved incredibly quickly with bees.
At half health (175), the **Beehive** would lose its bees and its speed would be reduced.
Appearance: The **Beehive** had a yellow torso and legs, and cyan blue skin. It also had a sad face. It wore a yellow neckguard. When the **Beehive** was covered in bees, it had a beehive on its head. When it was not covered with bees it had a basic smile and the beehive was removed.
Strategy: - Try to immediately remove the bees from the **Beehive**.
- As the **Beehive** appear in large numbers, it is recommended to use the Mortar or Rocketeer to defeat these.
- If these are not at hand, the Minigunner can be sufficient.
- You can use the Pyromancer, Freezer, Frost Blaster and Electroshocker to slow the **Beehive** down so that it is easier to attack.
Trivia: - This was the first enemy to have a negative downgrade when it lost health.
- The **Beehive** looked similar to the Sugrawr without the bees.

Description: The **Blight Walker** was an enemy that appeared on The Nightmare Realm and Containment in the Hexscape Event. It had a high amount of health and quite fast speed. It also had the Freeze Immunity and Stun Immunity, making it harder to slow down. On some waves, it also could spawn with the Bloated and Nimble attributes.

It had two abilities. The first ability was *Spit Burst*, which made it fire out three purple spit balls at towers. These created an explosion which applied a 20% Fatigue Debuff to towers, including non-humanoid towers, in a radius of 4. This debuff lasted 5 seconds. The second ability was *Heal Trail*, which left a trail that applied a regeneration buff to an enemy. This regeneration lasted 0.1 seconds and only healed 15 health of an enemy.
Appearance: The **Blight Walker** had maroon skin, with its appearance resembling that of an animal. It had four legs, large mouth and a tail. It wore a large skull with horns on its head, which had its jaw on its torso. It also had a few bones attached to its legs. It wore brown bandages around its legs. It wore grey shoulder-pads with spikes and a grey chestplate. It left a trail of purple goo as it walked.
Strategy: - The **Blight Walker** is a fast enemy with high health, high range or fast firing towers like the Ranger, Gatling Gun and Mortar are best to kill it.
- Multiple early-game towers like the Golden Crook Boss, Cowboy or Golden Soldier can also be used.
- The **Blight Walker** leaves a healing trail as it walks, which heals enemies.
- You can try to kill it quickly so that it can heal as little enemies as possible, however, its healing is not that significant

- Placing cheap towers as bait can be useful to make the **Blight Walker** not target your better towers. Do note, however, that its ability creates an explosion. If other towers are near the distraction tower, they will still be affected.
- The Commander can be used to partially mitigate its debuffs.

Description: The **Blighted** is a tanky enemy that appears in Hardcore and Voidcore modes. Its first debut spawned at Wave 19 in Hardcore mode and Wave 18 in Voidcore mode, which combined with its high health and average speed makes it a decent threat.
Appearance: The **Blighted** has grey skin. Its body is torn apart on its head and arms, exposing its glowing pink insides. It only wears purple pants and a belt. On its body, it has grey veins and multiple pink flowers.
Strategy: - Towers that deal high DPS, such as the Saboteur, Crook Boss, Engineer or Golden Minigunner are recommended against the **Blighted**.
- The first **Blighted** that spawns is a Boss enemy, making it harder to stall. Therefore, stalling towers such as the Freezer and Electroshocker are not recommended against it for its debut.
- Afterwards, it will always have the Stun Immunity, making stunning towers only slow it down.
- On certain waves it will also spawn in with the Freeze Immunity, making freezing towers do nothing to it.
Trivia: - The **Blighted** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Blighted** now appears in Nil Zone II as part of the Halloween 2026 Live Events.
- **Blighted** no longer spawns in Nil Zone II, as the Halloween 2026 Live Event has ended.
Notes: - ↑ Only the first **Blighted** that spawns is a Boss enemy.

Description: The **Blighted** was an enemy that used to have high health and average speed. It had more health and was slightly faster than the Slow Boss, making the **Blighted** a very dangerous enemy if not prepared for. When added, the **Blighted** used to be spawned by the Necromancer 2, though this was removed shortly after its addition.
The **Blighted** no longer appears in the game. It has since been replaced (appearance-wise) with the Heavy.
Appearance: The **Blighted** was a normal-sized enemy with grey skin, a light green granite torso and dark green granite legs. It had a drooling zombie face. The **Blighted** also emitted green and dark green particles from its torso.
Strategy: - The Outlaw, Minigunner and Turret are able to deal with the **Blighted** very well due to their high DPS.
- Additionally, you should use the Commander to boost these towers' firerate.
- As **Blighteds** typically spawn in hordes, a few Rocketers should fare well against them.
Trivia: - When they were initially added, **Blighteds** and Necromancer 2s were considered to be the most dangerous enemies in the game due to the sheer amount of health they had.
- They were later nerfed as they were deemed too difficult to defeat.
- **Blighteds** could have gotten stuck on corners and would not move forward if the Necromancer 2 that spawned them died.

blizzard_wizard.name: Blizzard Wizard
blizzard_wizard.description: The Blizzard Wizard, internally referred to as Frost Acolyte, is a summoner enemy that appears in the Frost mode. It has a high amount of health and a average speed.

abilities.label: Ability Cooldown: 15
abilities.text: **Summon** - Summons in two Snow Minions and a 1 delay between each spawn.

Description: The **Blizzard Wizard**, internally referred to as **Frost Acolyte**, is a summoner enemy that appears in the Frost mode. It has a high amount of health and a average speed. It has the Stun Immunity and Freeze Immunity, making it immune to being fully stopped by stuns, fully immune to knockback and fully immune to freeze.
It has one ability, where it summons in two Snow Minions.
Appearance: The **Blizzard Wizard** is a creature with blue skin. It has no legs and instead floats above the ground. It wears a grey robe with blue accents and a hood. On its arms, it wears grey bands with blue crystals on them. It also has a black belt. It carries a blue staff with its right arm, which it uses to summon in Snow Minions.
Strategy: - DPS towers like the Accelerator, Turret, Ranger or Pursuit can be useful against it due to its high health, though early-game towers like the Golden Scout can still be effective against it.
- Switching your towers' targeting to *Last Enemy* is recommended because of its ability, which can summon in hordes of Snow Minions if not killed quickly.
- Usually due to their health, having one or two towers set to that is enough.
- As the **Blizzard Wizard** has the Stun Immunity and Freeze Immunity, it cannot be stunned, knocked back or frozen.
- Any stuns will only slow it down.
Trivia: - The **Blizzard Wizard** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Bug**: **Frost Acolyte's** model does not load in the Index.
- **Bug**: Throwing a Flash Bang at a **Frost Acolyte** while it is summoning enemies breaks the enemy, making it stop moving.
- **Bugfix**: **Frost Acolyte's** model now loads in the Index.
- Cash given increased from $4,750 to $5,000 on death.
- Now summons two Snow Minions with Health Regen with a 0.75 delay between each spawn.
- No longer summons a Bloated Permafrost.
- First wave appearance chamged from 19 to 23.
- Name changed from *Frost Acolyte* to *Blizzard Wizard*.
- Cash given decreased from $5,000 to $2,250 on death.
- Speed increased from Below Average (2.8) to Average (3.3).
- The Snow Minions spawned no longer gain Health Regen.

bomber_elf_krampus_frosthold.name: Bomber Elf
bomber_elf_krampus_frosthold.description: The Bomber Elf was the fourth enemy to appear in Krampus Frosthold as part of the Krampus' Revenge Event.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Explosive Delivery** - Upon its death, the **Bomber Elf** explodes, stunning nearby towers caught in the blast.

Description: The **Bomber Elf** was the fourth enemy to appear in Krampus Frosthold as part of the Krampus' Revenge Event. Unlike previous enemies that appeared in the first stage, it did not appear in large hordes. However, it had faster speed and higher health than all enemies that appeared before it. Additionally, its ability, *Explosive Delivery*, made it dangerous against unprepared defenses.
Appearance: The **Bomber Elf** was a pale-skinned humanoid. It had full orange garb with white fur, with a hazard sign on its Christmas hat. It had a black belt and shoes.
It carried a giant present wrapped with black shaded diamond pattern wrapping paper and an orange ribbon holding it together. A lit fuse protruded from the top of the present.
Strategy: - It is recommended to place towers apart in order to avoid them all getting stunned by the **Bomber Elf's** ability.
- Towers that cannot get stunned, like the Ace Pilot or the Pursuit, can be very useful at clearing out enemies when other towers are stunned.
Trivia: - Weirdly, Santa's dialogue for the **Bomber Elf** appears on Wave 5, which is two waves earlier than the **Bomber Elf's** actual debut.

bomber_elf_cold_ambush.name: Bomber Elf
bomber_elf_cold_ambush.description: The Bomber Elf was a fast enemy that appeared in Cold Ambush as part of the Violent Night Event. It had a fast speed but a low amount of health.

notice.text: Bomber Elf (Cold Ambush) has been removed from the game as of the 4th of February 2023 as it was part of the Violent Night Event.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Explosive Delivery** - Upon its death, the **Bomber Elf** explodes and stuns nearby towers caught in the blast.

Description: The **Bomber Elf** was a fast enemy that appeared in Cold Ambush as part of the Violent Night Event. It had a fast speed but a low amount of health. However, upon death, it would explode, stunning any tower caught in the explosion.
Appearance: The **Bomber Elf** had pale skin. It had an orange shirt with white fur along the sleeves, as well as stitch lines on the sides of the arms. It had a black belt, darker orange pants and black shoes. It also wore an orange Christmas hat with a yellow and black hazard emblem on it.
In its hands was a giant present wrapped with black shaded diamond pattern wrapping paper and an orange ribbon holding it together. A lit fuse protruded from the top of the present.
Strategy: - High DPS towers like the Minigunner, Ranger, Accelerator or Engineer are recommended against this.
- The Ranger can be especially useful, as its high range allows it to kill the **Bomber Elf** from a distance. Additionally, it cannot be stunned by the **Bomber Elf**.
- These towers should have their firerate and range boosted by the Commander and DJ Booth respectively.
- DJ Booth's Range Buff also allows your towers to deal with the **Bomber Elf** from a further distance, making it less likely for them to get stunned.
- The Medic can be quite helpful as you can use its ability to cleanse towers of the **Bomber Elf's** stun.
Trivia: - The Bomber Elf unit from the Elf Camp is based on this enemy.

bones_solar_eclipse.name: Bones
bones_solar_eclipse.description: The Bones was an enemy that first appeared on Wave 5 of the Rotfield map. It had higher health than the Undead and Mummy, but walked slightly slower than the Mummy.

notice.text: Bones (Solar Eclipse) has been removed from the game as of the 26th of January 2022 as it was part of the Solar Eclipse Event.

Description: The **Bones** was an enemy that first appeared on Wave 5 of the Rotfield map. It had higher health than the Undead and Mummy, but walked slightly slower than the Mummy.
Appearance: The **Bones** was entirely made out of marble white parts that resembled a skeleton. It did not have a full torso, but instead had the bone cage for it. Its head was slightly smaller than usual and had two large black eyes.
Strategy: - The **Bones** are quite easy to defeat, as they have a fairly low health and speed.
- Starter towers like the Scout or Soldier should be sufficient to defeat them.
- Cheap towers with high DPS such as the Crook Boss, Minigunner, and Gladiator are very useful against this.
- Additionally, you can use Commander and DJ Booth to boost these towers' firerate and range, respectively.
- Do note that the low cash supply in Rotfield may limit the potential of these towers.
- The Toxic Gunner and Freezer, among other slowing towers, are useful for slowing this down, giving your towers more time to defeat it.
- The Ace Pilot's bombs and bullets do a good job at eliminating this enemy, as they spawn in hordes.
Trivia: - The **Bones** had a death animation where it would fall into a pile of bones and its head would roll a short distance.

bones_trick_or_threat_town.name: Bones
bones_trick_or_threat_town.description: Bones was an enemy that appeared exclusively in Trick or Threat Town as part of the Halloween 2020 Event.

notice.text: Bones (Trick or Threat Town) has been removed from the game as of the 8th of May 2021 as it was part of the Halloween 2020 Event.

Description: **Bones** was an enemy that appeared exclusively in Trick or Threat Town as part of the Halloween 2020 Event. They were slightly slower than the Mummy and slightly faster than the Undead. **Bones** also had more health than these two enemies.
**Bones** could be spawned by the Reaper.
Appearance: The **Bones** was entirely made out of marble white parts that resembled a skeleton. It did not have a full torso, but instead had the bone cage for it. Its head was slightly smaller than usual and had two large black eyes. It had a slightly different walking animation to the Undead and Mummy.
Strategy: - These are relatively easy to defeat, so long you have the capabilities of defeating the Mummy and Undead that appears before this.
- As they can spawn in hordes, splash-damage towers, like the Rocketeer, can help in defeating these enemies.
Trivia: - The **Bones** had a death animation where it would fall into a pile of bones and its head would roll a short distance.
- The **Bones** would have cracks on its body the more it got damaged. It also became slightly darker in color.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Weakening Bile** - Upon its death, the **Boomer** explodes into a bile bubble that applies a 50% Fatigue Debuff and 15% Range Debuff for 10 seconds and deals 400 damage to units in a radius of 9.

Description: The **Boomer** is an enemy that explodes upon its death, which debuffs towers caught in the bile bubble. It has average health but slightly fast speed. The **Boomer** appears in Intermediate mode.
When the original Polluted Wasteland was in the game, the **Boomer** did not spawn in Golden and Fallen modes and was instead replaced by the Splitter.
Appearance: The **Boomer** is a large humanoid with a waist in its rig. It has a green skin color and a crimson-brown torso, waist and legs. It has a bloated chest and stomach with tumors, which has a dark green explosive device strapped on it. The explosive has an orange caution symbol, red and blue wires and an antenna with a flashing red light on it.
Strategy: - The **Boomer** is quite fast, allowing it to quickly get to your towers and debuff them.
- Additionally, it often times spawns alongside other, at times faster or aggro enemies, which distract the towers from the **Boomer** and allowing it to get closer to your towers.
- Killing the **Boomer** before it gets within range of your towers is the most ideal way to deal with **Boomers**. Keep in mind that it has quite a long debuff time.
- Placing your towers away from the path is a good way to avoid the **Boomer's** debuff.
- Long-range towers, such as the Hunter are the best at keeping a distance away from the **Boomer**.
- The Engineer's sentries can also be useful, as the sentries cannot be debuffed.

- The DJ Booth allows towers to shoot the **Boomer** from further away, potentially defeating it before it blows up near your towers. It can also increase the damage of towers, allowing them to defeat it more quickly.
- It and the Commander can also partially negate the **Boomer's** debuffs.
- The Mercenary Base can also further contribute to the speedrun demise of the **Boomer** with its damage buff.

- While the Medic is not able to shield towers from the Fatigue Debuff or Range Debuff, the shield on towers is not broken by them, meaning its Firerate Buff can be used to partially mitigate the **Boomer's** debuffs.
- Towers which are normally immune to stuns by default are not immune to the debuffs either.
Trivia: - The **Boomer** is based on the *Left 4 Dead* zombie, the Boomer.
Update History: - No longer appears in Fallen mode, as it has been replaced by the Elite Boomer there.
- Gives $2,500 on death in Molten mode.
- Updated firerate type debuff applied to be the Fatigue Debuff instead of the Firerate Debuff. Because of this, effectiveness of the debuff has been reduced.
- **Bug**: Closing Index entry causes death SFX to play.
- No longer appears in Badlands II.
- **Bug**: No longer creates an explosion VFX upon death, unless triggered while it has Corpse or when its converted by the Hacker.
- No longer appears in Molten mode.
- **Bug**: Index icon does not load, as it has been moderated and removed by Roblox.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Explode** - Upon its death, the **Boomer** explodes into a bile bubble that applies stuns towers.

Description: The **Boomer** is a legacy enemy that appears in Legacy Fallen mode and Golden mode, both of which are only available through Sandbox mode. It has decently high health and walks at a rather slow speed. Upon death, it will explode into a bile bubble that stuns towers.
Appearance: **Variant 1**

The current version of the **Boomer** is a bloated enemy with a light green skin color and a green torso and darker green legs. It has a bloating stomach and its torso occasionally emits green particles. It is faceless and trudged when it walks.
**Variant 2**

The Enemies Beta version of the **Boomer** is a large humanoid with a waist in its rig. It has a green skin color and a crimson-brown torso, waist and legs. It has a bloated chest and stomach with tumors, which has a dark green explosive device strapped on it. The explosive has an orange caution symbol, red and blue wires and an antenna with a flashing red light on it.
**Variant 3**

The first version of the **Boomer** was a bloated enemy with a light green skin color and a green torso and darker green legs. It had a bloating stomach and its torso occasionally emitted green particles. It had a drooling zombie face and trudged when it walked. When it was first added, its walking animation had it flailing its arms around.
Strategy: - When first encountering it, the **Boomer** does not pose as a serious threat as there are few enemies to take advantage of the **Boomer's** stun.
- However, at later waves, the **Boomer** will be accompanied by many strong enemies that spawn behind it, like the Giant Boss and Summoner Boss.
- The **Boomer** can also potentially spawn in hordes from Mystery Bosses, which may lead to many more towers getting stunned.
- Killing the **Boomer** before it gets within range of your towers is the most ideal way to deal with **Boomers**. Keep in mind that it has quite a long stun time.
- Placing your towers away from the path is a good way to avoid the **Boomer's** stun.
- Long-range towers, such as the Turret are the best at keeping a distance away from the **Boomer**.
- The Ranger and Pursuit can be very effective against the **Boomer** as they cannot be stunned.
- The Engineer's sentries can also be useful, as the sentries cannot be stunned and the **Boomer** does not deal damage to units.
- The DJ Booth allows towers to shoot the **Boomer** from further away, potentially defeating it before it blows up near your towers.
- You can use the Medic's ability to cleanse towers of the **Boomer's** stun.
- The Gladiator and Level 4 Warden can block the **Boomer's** stun.
- This is ineffective if there are multiple **Boomers**, as there is a cooldown after blocking a stun where the Gladiator is unable to block stuns.
Trivia: - The **Boomer** is based on the *Left 4 Dead* zombie, the Boomer.
- This enemy replaced the Boomer 1, Boomer 2 and Carrier after the MEGA Update.
- Prior to the Frost Invasion Event, the **Boomer** used an edited version of the Sad Zombie face from the Roblox catalog.
Update History: - Can no longer be spawned by the Summoner Boss.
- No longer appears in Golden mode as it has been removed.
- Now has a new appearance with the Enemies Beta modifier active.
- **Boomer** removed from Fallen mode and Badlands II as it as been replaced by its modern variant.
- **Boomer** re-added, now can be spawned in Sandbox mode.
- **Boomer** now appears in Golden mode and Legacy Fallen mode, if activated through Sandbox mode.
- **Boomer** no longer appears in Golden mode and Legacy Fallen mode, as they have been removed.
- **Boomer** now appears in Golden mode and Legacy Fallen mode, if activated through Sandbox mode.
- **Bug**: No longer creates an explosion upon death.

boomer_1.name: Boomer 1
boomer_1.description: The Boomer 1 was an enemy that exploded upon its death, stunning nearby towers in its radius. It was a fairly strong enemy with an average speed.

notice.text: Boomer 1 has been removed from the game as of the 13th of October 2019.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Explode** - Upon its death, the **Boomer 1** explodes into a bile bubble that stuns all towers caught in the bubble

Description: The **Boomer 1** was an enemy that exploded upon its death, stunning nearby towers in its radius. It was a fairly strong enemy with an average speed.
The **Boomer 1** appeared in The Heights during the SFOTH Event.
The **Boomer 1** no longer spawns and has since been replaced by the Boomer.
Appearance: The **Boomer 1** was a bloated enemy, but similar in size to the Normal. The head and arms were light aqua green, while its torso and legs were slightly dark aqua green. It had a sad zombie drooling face.
Strategy: - Rapid-firing towers, such as the Minigunner or Sentry, can kill the **Boomer 1** before it reaches your towers.
- The Commander can also assist in killing this enemy quicker by boosting the firerate of your towers.
- The Demoman and Rocketer can kill hordes of these through splash damage, preventing them from getting anywhere near your towers.
- Additionally, the Outlaw can also be used to kill the **Boomer 1s** from afar without the risk of being stunned.
Trivia: - The **Boomer 1** was based on the *Left 4 Dead* zombie, the Boomer.

- The "*Do you get the pun?*" and "*Hahaha...*" narration that appeared for this enemy were the only narrations to be played a significant amount of time after the enemies had come out before the MEGA Update.
- The narration played when the game assumed the **Boomer 1** had exploded, though it could be played before or after the **Boomer 1** had exploded.

boomer_2.name: Boomer 2
boomer_2.description: The Boomer 2 was mostly regarded as a heated version of the Boomer 1. However...

notice.text: Boomer 2 has been removed from the game as of the 13th of October 2019.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Explode** - Upon its death, the **Boomer 2** explodes into a large bile bubble that stuns all towers caught in the bubble.

Description: The **Boomer 2** was mostly regarded as a heated version of the Boomer 1. However, it was still affected by the flames of the Pyromancer and was just a stronger version of the Boomer 1. The **Boomer 2** was a much bigger threat compared to the Boomer 1 due to its higher health and larger explosion size.
Appearance: The **Boomer 2** had a bloated appearance, similar to the Boomer 1. The only difference to the Boomer 1 was the **Boomer 2's** red skin tone, pinkish torso and dark red legs.
Strategy: - Rapid-firing towers, such as the Minigunner or Sentry, can kill the **Boomer 2** before it reaches your towers.
- The Commander can also assist in killing this enemy quicker by boosting the firerate of your towers.
- The Demoman and Rocketer can kill hordes of these through splash damage, preventing them from getting anywhere near your towers.
- Additionally, the Outlaw can also be used to kill the **Boomer 2s** from afar without the risk of being stunned.
- The Pyromancer and Freezer can be used to slow the **Boomer 2** down.
Trivia: - Even though the **Boomer 2's** appearance and narration prior to its debut suggested that they were immune to the Pyromancer, it was not.
- The **Boomer 2** had no direct replacement in the MEGA Update, though it could be argued that the Boomer was the replacement for both the Boomer 1 and **Boomer 2**.

Description: The **Brain Bound** was an enemy that appeared in Failed Gateway as part of the Hexscape Event. It also appeared in Containment, but only when spawned by Corrupted Titus. It had a decently high amount of health, some defense and it was quite fast, being faster than the Pawn. It also occasionally spawned with the Bloated, Aggro and Tank attributes.
Appearance: The **Brain Bound** was a wooden construct with a brown body. It had a dark brown shirt and short parts that were also torn. It had multiple metal plates on its hands and knee-pads, all with various colors and grey spikes. It also had a metal head piece with wires and a lens on its head.
Strategy: - **Brain Bounds** can be dealt with by strong, cost-effective early game towers, such as the Crook Boss and Golden Soldier.
- Some **Brain Bounds** will have the Aggro attribute, potentially letting other enemies leak past.
- Towers that can hit multiple enemies at once are recommended to prevent this.
- Units from towers like the Crook Boss or Mercenary Base are also useful for dealing with leaks.
- In Hard mode, some **Brain Bounds** will spawn with the Tank attribute.
- Towers with a fast firerate like the Minigunner can be used to deal with this.
- Units' collision damage is a great way to deal with Tank **Brain Bounds**. Similarly, the Trapper's traps will deal heavy damage to them.
Update History: - **Bug**: Poison and electric defense dropping does not decrease **Brain Bound's** defense.
- **Bugfix**: Poison and electric defense dropping now drops **Brain Bound's** defense, though the Jester still cannot drop it.

Description: The **Breaker** is an enemy that appears in the Easy, Casual, Intermediate, Molten, Fallen, Challenge Trials, Pizza Party, Badlands II and PVP modes. It does not appear naturally in most cases, and is instead spawned by the Breaker2. The only exception to this is Badlands II, where it does spawn naturally on one wave. It has the lowest amount of health out of all the Breaker enemies, usually having half the amount of the Breaker2, but is also the fastest of them all. Unlike its parent enemies, it does not spawn anything upon death. When first spawned by the Breaker2 it is temporarily invincible to all forms of damage.
The **Breaker** also appeared as part of the The Classic Event, Tower Defense Simulator x PLS DONATE Event and The Takeover Event.
The **Breaker** was replaced by the Png Bot in Headache Headquarters.
Appearance: **Variant 1**

The **Breaker** is a humanoid with a cyan torso and legs that have a triangle pattern design of varying sizes with the colors being light blue and dark blue, depending on which side the triangle is on. Its arms and head are made out of blue construction paper, with the front and back faces of each part being separate halves held together by small strips of tape.
If spawned from the Breaker2, the **Breaker** jumps up with its left arm pointed upwards before falling to the ground. It plays a squeaking sound and emits blue confetti particles on death.
**Variant 2**
The **Breaker** has a baby blue skin color. It has a cyan torso and legs with a plaid stitch mark pattern on them.
Strategy: - The **Breaker** can prove to quite dangerous due to its slightly high health and speed, as well as it being spawned by the Breaker2.
- Fairly cheap high DPS towers like the Minigunner and Golden Crook Boss are very useful.
- Strong early game towers like the Golden Scout, Ace Pilot, Assassin or Militant are effective, though weaker ones like the Scout or Soldier may falter.
- As these spawn in hordes, area of effect towers like the Demoman, Rocketeer, Pyromancer or the Shotgunner can be quite useful against them.
- Later on, high DPS towers like the Accelerator, Minigunner or Engineer can effectively kill these.
- Be aware that you do not earn any cash from damaging the **Breaker** in any mode, as it does not appear naturally.
- The Toxic Gunner, Frost Blaster and Electroshocker can be used to slow down the **Breaker** while also dealing decent damage to it.
Trivia: - The **Breaker's** animation when spawning from a Breaker2 is a reference to Mario from the *Super Mario Bros* franchise.
- The **Breaker** has the most gamemode appearances, appearing in twelve gamemodes total, alongside the Breaker2, Breaker3, Breaker4 and Necromancer.
- The functionality of this enemy is very similar to the Solar Shard, Lunar Shard and Dust from the Solar Eclipse Event.
- The appearance of this enemy is similar to the Super Mystery.
- Unlike the other Breaker enemies, this enemy has a sprinting animation as opposed to a standard walking one.
- There was a bug where units would instantly be destroyed upon collision with a freshly spawned **Breaker**, regardless of the unit's or the enemy's health.

- This was due to an oversight where the **Breaker**, when spawned from the Breaker2, gained a fraction of a second of invulnerability upon being spawned, instantly killing the unit without taking any damage itself.
- Since v1.17.0, units no longer take damage from invulnerable enemies.
- The legacy **Breaker**, along the Breaker2, Breaker3 and Breaker4, will turn into a opaque recolored version of itself when turned into a unit by the Hacker.
