Description: The **Breaker2** is an enemy that appears in Easy, Casual, Intermediate, Molten, Fallen, Challenge Trials, Pizza Party, Badlands II and PVP modes. While it appears in all PVP ranks, it can only be sent by a player in Basic Arena PVP. It has a decent amount of health and a slightly fast speed, being slightly faster than the Hidden. Upon death, it will spawn one Breaker, which has less health but is faster. The Breaker, when spawned, is temporarily invulnerable to all forms of damage. Because of this, the **Breaker2** can easily overwhelm unprepared players.

The **Breaker2** is spawned by the Breaker3 upon its death, and is temporarily invulnerable to all forms of damage. The Grave Digger (both the regular and legacy version) also has a chance to spawn the **Breaker2** with its *Triumphing Sheol* ability on Easy mode, as well as on Hardcore mode if the Enemies Beta modifier is active. It can/could also be spawned by the Mystery Summoner, Summoner Boss, Hardcore mode's Necromancer Boss and Void Reaver if the Enemies Beta modifier is active.
The **Breaker2** also appeared as part of the The Classic Event, Tower Defense Simulator x PLS DONATE Event and The Takeover Event.
The **Breaker2** was replaced by the Png Bot2 in Headache Headquarters. The **Breaker2** replaces the Mystery in any map with the Enemies Beta modifier active.
Appearance: **Variant 1**

The **Breaker2** is a humanoid with a dark green torso and legs that have a square pattern design of varying sizes and shades of green. Its arms and head are made out of light green construction paper, with the front and back faces of each part being separate halves held together by small strips of tape. It has a small blue humanoid on its chest that represents the Breaker.

If spawned from the Breaker3, the **Breaker2** jumps up with its left arm pointed upwards before falling to the ground. It plays a squeaking sound and emits small waves and green confetti particles on death.
**Variant 2**

The legacy **Breaker2** has a pastel light green skin color. It has a pale green torso and legs with a plaid stitch mark pattern on them. It has a dark cyan humanoid on its chest, representing the Breaker.
It plays a crumbling sound on death.
Strategy: - The **Breaker2** can prove to be quite dangerous due to its high health, speed and its ability to spawn a Breaker.
- Fairly cheap high DPS towers like the Minigunner or Golden Crook Boss are very useful.
- Strong early game towers like the Golden Scout, Ace Pilot, Assassin or Militant are effective, though weaker ones like the Scout or Soldier may falter.
- Setting your towers to *Strongest* targeting can help against **Breaker2s** as it avoids the Breaker's invincibility frames.
- As these spawn in hordes, area of effect towers like the Demoman, Assassin, Pyromancer or the Shotgunner can be quite useful against them.
- Later on in the game, natural **Breaker2** spawns are not as threatening, though it can be dangerous because of the Breaker4.
- Stronger area of effect towers, like the Electroshocker, Golden Pyromancer, Rocketeer or Mortar are effective against all forms of breakers.
- Be aware that you do not earn any cash from damaging the Breaker that the **Breaker2** spawns in every mode.
- The Breaker that spawns from the **Breaker2** does not need to be killed for wave progression to occur.
- The Frost Blaster, Freezer and Electroshocker can be quite efficient at slowing these down while also dealing decent damage to them.
Trivia: - The **Breaker2's** animation when spawning from a Breaker3 is a reference to Mario from the *Super Mario Bros* franchise.
- The **Breaker2** has the most gamemode appearances, appearing in twelve gamemodes total, alongside the Breaker, Breaker3, and Necromancer.
- Breaker4 formerly appeared in Easy mode, but was removed in v1.85.0.
- The functionality of this enemy is very similar to the Solar Shard, Lunar Shard and Dust from the Solar Eclipse Event.
- The appearance of this enemy parallels the Mystery, and its first appearance greatly resembles the Enemies Beta appearance of it.
- The Commander improperly called this enemy a Mystery in legacy Hardcore mode. This was due to the regular mode dialogue being unchanged to account for the Enemies Beta modifier.
- This mistake does not apply to Easy mode, since as of v1.33.0, the Commander now properly mentions the **Breaker2** in that mode.
- There was a bug where units would instantly be destroyed upon collision with a **Breaker2**, regardless of the unit's or the enemy's health.

- This was due to an oversight where the Breaker spawning from this enemy gained a fraction of a second of invulnerability upon being spawned, instantly killing the unit without taking any damage itself.
- Since v1.17.0, units no longer take damage from invulnerable enemies.
- The legacy **Breaker2**, along the Breaker, Breaker3 and Breaker4, will turn into a opaque recolored version of itself when turned into a unit by the Hacker.

The Breaker2 has less health and no defense, but is faster and can spawn one Breaker upon death. Because three of them spawn from the Breaker4 upon death, they will create huge hordes of enemies, which can easily overwhelm unprepared players.

- Area of effect towers like the Rocketeer, Mortar, Pyromancer or Electroshocker are a good option against the **Brick Man**, as multiple are spawned by the Necromancer.

Strategy: - Use high DPS towers, such as the Accelerator, Ranger and Turret to kill the **Bruh**.

Trivia: - The **Bruh**, as the name suggests, played a very specific Bruh sound effect when killed.

abilities.text: **Throw** - The **Brute** throws a rock, which splits into four smaller rocks, at a random tower or unit. Stuns towers for 5 seconds and deals 500 damage to units per rock. Has a minimal attack range of 10 and maximum attack range of 25. Unusable in PVP.

Description: The **Brute** is the final boss of Easy mode and one of the Challenge Trials mini-bosses. It also appeared in The Takeover Event. For most of its appearances it is a Boss enemy, making it have various resistances and immunities, which includes being resistant to stuns from stunning towers, immune to being frozen by freezing towers, slowed down by the Toxic Gunner, Electroshocker confused by the Jester, damaged from the Nuke's fallout and slowed down by the DJ Booth. Unlike most other final bosses however, it is not considered one by default, meaning there are some circumstances where it lacks these immunities.

The **Brute** has very high health compared to anything that spawns before, but to compensate, it walks very slowly. It has two abilities. Its first, *Smash*, in which it slams its fists onto a tower or unit, stunning it and other nearby towers for 3 seconds and doing 1,000 damage to units. Its second, *Throw*, has it throw a rock at a nearby tower or unit, which then splits into four smaller rocks. Each rock stuns towers for 5 seconds and does 500 damage to units per rock. It is completely unable to use any of these abilities in PVP.
Appearance: The **Brute** is a large hulking humanoid with a waist and lower arms in its rig. It has a pale green skin color, an orange torso, waist and legs, with the former having white stripes. It wears black shoes and has a black harness with white buckles. It also has black braces with white spikes and chains attached, along with indented lower arms. It also has two heads, with the left one being larger.
Whenever one of its fists hits the ground, the screen shakes and makes a stomp sound. On death, the **Brute** will repeatedly bang its lower arms on its chest before falling forward onto the ground.
Strategy: - As the **Brute** has the lowest health out of all main final bosses, starter towers like the Sniper, Soldier or Shotgunner are capable of defeating it.
- The Sniper can especially be a decent option due to its Stun Immunity gained from being a cliff tower.
- Since this is the cliff Stun Immunity, it also means that the Sniper can be used as a distraction due to it still being targetable by enemy abilities.
- Strong DPS towers like the Minigunner or Ranger can also be used against it, though they are not necessary outside of Challenge Trials.
- As the **Brute** only has stunning attacks, splash damage towers like the Demoman are not particularly useful against the **Brute**.

- You can place down towers like the Scout or use a unit spawner like the Crook Boss to create distractions which the **Brute** will target instead of your DPS towers, though this is not necessary due to its rather low health.
Trivia: - The **Brute** shared its design with the Dummy Boss from the Tutorial before the v1.74.0 update.
- Despite sharing the same design and icon, they were two separate enemies and therefore give two separate Logbooks.
- The Logbook it drops will not unlock its legacy version in Sandbox mode, as it has been completely removed from the game.
Update History: - **Bug**: **Brute** is affected by the All Paths modifier.
- **Bug**: **Brute** goes into its default pose for a short time after finishing its *Smash* ability.
- **Bug**: **Brute** now appears in Headache Headquarters as part of April Fools 2025 Event.

brute_the_heights.name: Brute
brute_the_heights.description: The Brute was an enemy that appeared in The Heights as part of the SFOTH Event. It had the same walkspeed as the Stone Viking...

notice.text: Brute (The Heights) has been removed from the game as of the 13th of October 2019 as it was part of the SFOTH Event.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Rock Throw** - The **Brute** briefly stops, picks up a rock and flings it at towers, stunning them for a period of time.

Description: The **Brute** was an enemy that appeared in The Heights as part of the SFOTH Event. It had the same walkspeed as the Stone Viking, but had less health than the Crystalite. It was able to stun towers through its *Rock Throw* ability.
The **Brute** could also be spawned by the Swordmaster.
Appearance: The **Brute** was slightly more broad than the Slow, while being smaller than the Slow Boss. It had muscular arms, grey skin, walked with a hunchback and had its head slightly tilted. It also had blue glowing eyes. It wore grey shorts, had straps around its body and wore a gladiator helmet.
Strategy: - The **Brute** is weaker than the Crystalite, meaning that, in terms of health, the **Brute** is generally easier to kill.
- However, the **Brute** is capable of stunning towers with its *Rock Throw* ability, making them pose a huge threat if underestimated.
- If you have any cheap towers, such as the Scout, they can be used to distract the **Brute**, while long-range towers, such as the Outlaw, can be used to kill the **Brute** from a distance away.
- Alternatively, you can place your towers away from the path so that the rocks thrown by the **Brute** are less likely to hit them, as the **Brute's** *Rock Throw* ability has limited range.
Trivia: - The design of the **Brute** was very similar to R2D's Tank which in turn was inspired by the Tank in *Left 4 Dead*.
- The name **Brute** was likely based on R2DA's Brute.
- The **Brute** was also similar in design to the Tank 1 and Tank 2.
- The arms of the **Brute** were taken from the Superhero bundle from the Roblox catalog.
- The **Brute's** helmet is a re-textured version of the Spiked Helm of Shining Righteous Truth accessory from the Roblox catalog.

bug.name: Bug
bug.description: The Bug was an enemy that could only be found in the legacy Hidden Wave, which meant it could only be found in Fallen mode.

notice.text: Bug has been removed from the game as of the 4th of December 2021.

Description: The **Bug** was an enemy that could only be found in the legacy Hidden Wave, which meant it could only be found in Fallen mode.

The **Bug** was extremely fast and had a very high amount of health. This enemy was extremely difficult to defeat without correct precautions and it could have easily made you lose the Hidden Wave without the right towers.
Appearance: The **Bug** had a very similar appearance to the Error and Glitch, though more glitch particles were emitted from the **Bug** and it had an emblem of a bug on the front torso. While it was alive, the color of the **Bug** changed every second. It was also faceless. When it ran, a colorful glitch trail was left behind.
Strategy: - Do not underestimate the **Bug** as if it was a Glitch or an Error due to its high amount of health.
- Every tower must be maxed out and prepared for enemies like this in the Hidden Wave, so it is recommended to bring certain towers in order to beat the wave.
- DJ Booths and Commanders are needed for range and Firerate Buffs respectively.
- Level 5 Rangers are also highly recommended to defeat this, though their firerates must be boosted due to the incredibly high speeds attained by the **Bug**.
- The Electroshocker is quite useful against the **Bug** as it can slow hordes of them down for a long period of time.
- The Frost Blaster and Freezer can also be used, though they can only freeze **Bugs** one at a time.
- The Sledger can be used to freeze hordes of **Bugs** due to its piercing, though due to its slow swingrate, some **Bugs** may not be frozen at all.
- The Toxic Gunner can also be helpful, as it slows the **Bug** by up to 50%, though it may take a while to slow down a horde of **Bugs**.
- If you are using the Accelerator, use the Freezer or Electroshocker to give time for the Accelerator to charge up.
Trivia: - The **Bug's** health is a reference to the IT'S OVER 9000 meme.
Update History: - Now leaves a glitch trail as it runs.
- **Bug** now appears in the legacy Hidden Wave, which is exclusive to Sandbox mode.
- **Bug** no longer appears in the legacy Hidden Wave, as it has been removed.

Description: The **Builder** was an enemy that appeared in Narratorium as a part of The Final Act Event. It had the highest health out of all enemies that appeared so far, but it was only as fast as the Attendee. It has one ability where it throws a brick at a tower or unit, which upon impact splits into three additional bricks. Any tower hit by them was stunned for 2 seconds while units received 150 damage.
Logbook Description: "*The Builder is a creature created specifically to help the Narrator construct his grand visions. It handles all construction work, from laying foundations to adding decoration. The builder is only animated by a soul which Righty and Lefty can steal from a living being.*"
Appearance: The **Builder** is a plushie with a yellow head, black legs and arms, and an orange torso. On its torso, it has a zipper while on its head it wears a yellow and blue hard hat. It has two black button eyes and a giant open mouth with a visible tongue.
Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in The Narratorium is listed instead.
- Early-game towers like the Crook Boss, Golden Soldier or Golden Crook Boss are pretty useful here.
- The Toxic Gunner and Electroshocker can be used to kill multiple at once.
- Later on, the **Builder** becomes rather weak, meaning most towers should be capable of defeating them, including late-game towers like the Accelerator, Turret, Ranger or Pursuit.
Trivia: - The **Builder** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Builder** removed from the main game, now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.

Description: The **Builder Elf** was an enemy that first appeared on Wave 18 in Krampus Frosthold as part of the Krampus' Revenge Event. It had a somewhat high health and a slightly slow speed. It most often spawned behind groups of Papa Breads, which acted as shields for it. It had one ability, *Build-A-Soldier*, which made it stop moving and started to make four to six Toy Soldiers.
Appearance: The **Builder Elf** was a large pale-skinned humanoid. It wore a green shirt with white fur along the sleeves, as well as stitch lines on the sides of the arms. It had a black and yellow belt, dark green pants, and black shoes. It wore a green Christmas hat, as well as yellow goggles with blue lenses and an apron with black and yellow straps. It wielded a green wooden hammer in its right hand.
Strategy: - High-damaging towers, like the Accelerator and Minigunner, can reliably deal with the **Builder Elf**.
- Splash damage towers like the Mortar can deal with this enemy's spawns.
- In certain cases, the Pyromancer can be a viable option against the Toy Soldiers that spawn.

Description: The **Bulwark** is a high health enemy that appears in Molten mode. It has a high amount of health and slightly slow speed, making it quite tough to take down. It also has Stun Immunity, meaning that it cannot be knocked back or stunned, only being slowed down by stuns.
Appearance: The **Bulwark** is a large entity with dark crimson skin. It has a giant mutated right arm with chains wrapped around it and a thin left arm with an arm-band, that has a chain attached to it. It has multiple giant scars on its skin. On its head, it has a single yellow neon eye. Multiple molten rocks stick out of its body. It wears a tattered piece of leather which covers its lower parts. It also has a grey neck guard.
It has a death animation, where it falls forward, with its mutated arm completely detaching in the process.
Strategy: - High DPS towers, such as the Crook Boss, Hunter, Ranger and Turret are recommended to take this enemy down.
- The DJ Booth and Commander can be used to boost these towers.
- Due to its Stun Immunity, it will not be stopped by stuns and will instead only be slowed down, making towers like the Tesla far less effective.
- It will also be unable to be knocked back by towers like the Brawler.
Trivia: - The **Bulwark** looks like a combination of the Living Experiment and Tank 2.

bunny.name: Bunny
bunny.description: The Bunny was an enemy that only appeared in Eggy Island as part of the Spring 2020 Event.

notice.text: Bunny has been removed from the game as of the 26th of May 2020 as it was part of the Spring 2020 Event.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Carrot Throw** - The **Bunny** throws a carrot which stuns a specific tower and all towers in the immediate impact area.

Description: The **Bunny** was an enemy that only appeared in Eggy Island as part of the Spring 2020 Event. It appeared in easy mode (with 750 health) and in hard mode (with 2,000 health). The **Bunny** moved quite slowly in easy and about average in hard mode.
The **Bunny** had the ability to throw carrots, which stunned a specific tower and any other towers in the immediate impact area.
Appearance: The **Bunny** had a cat face with bunny ears. It had white skin with a grey egg imprinted on its torso, and a white beard. The **Bunny** carried a carrot to throw at towers. When the **Bunny** died, a death animation played.
Strategy: - The **Bunny** is probably the first major threat in Eggy Island. Make sure you have enough Minigunners to deal with it, ideally with a Commander boosting them.
- In hard mode, you can also use the Outlaw to deal with the **Bunny**.
- You can use cheap towers such as the Soldier and Scout to distract the **Bunny** away from your main towers.
- In addition, this will slow the **Bunny** down as it needs to stop to attack towers.
- The Pyromancer is recommended to slow the **Bunny** down.
- In hard mode, you can alternatively use the Freezer, Electroshocker and Frost Blaster to slow this enemy down.
- Try not to cluster towers close together as the **Bunny's** *Carrot Throw* can stun all towers close to its intended target.
Trivia: - The **Bunny** was likely based on *R2DA's* Easter Brute in terms of attack and appearance.

buried.name: Buried
buried.description: The Buried was an enemy that appeared exclusively in Trick or Threat Town as part of the Halloween 2020 Event.

notice.text: Buried has been removed from the game as of the 8th of May 2021 as it was part of the Halloween 2020 Event.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Burrow** - When it reaches half of its health or lower, it will sink into the ground. It cannot be damaged in most circumstances. Further along the path it will re-emerge.

Description: The **Buried** was an enemy that appeared exclusively in Trick or Threat Town as part of the Halloween 2020 Event.
The **Buried** had average speed and about average health for the time it appeared. However, the main threat was its ability to bury underground.

Once it lost at least half of its health (at 62 health or lower), it would bury itself into the ground and moved along the path underground. It would then pop out later on down the path, passing many of your towers.
Appearance: The **Buried** had teal green skin, with its torso and legs colored brown. Its rib and right leg were cut open and exposed. Bone could be seen in these cuts. It also had a shocked face. Its head was slightly tilted downwards.
Strategy: - When **Buried** reaches half of its health or lower, it buries itself underground, making itself untargetable by most towers.
- They can still be damaged by an explosion, though another targetable enemy must be present on the surface.
- It can be targeted by Accelerator while it is underground (or in the process of sinking underground), so long the Accelerator was locked onto it as it began to sink underground.
- While it is underground, the Accelerator cannot detect it.
- The Electroshocker can still hit the **Buried** while it is underground via a chain reaction.

- Fire damage from the Pyromancer and bee damage from the Swarmer can inflict damage on the **Buried** while it is underground, so long the effects were applied before the **Buried** went underground.
- When it emerges, the **Buried** will be immobilized for half second and can be attacked.
- Military Bases will pass over this enemy when it is buried, but units can still collide with the **Buried** a second before it emerges or buries.
- This tower is recommended against the **Buried** as they will emerge later on down the path.
- You can spread your defenses around the map to ensure no **Buried** reaches the end of the map.
- Making **Burieds** go underground sooner is effective as they will arise from underground sooner. This allows your towers to have a higher chance of killing them before they reach the end.
- If a **Buried** is instantly killed (or damage dealt exceeds the remaining health left, and the **Buried** is still overground), the **Buried** does not sink underground.
- Therefore, for this reason, Level 3+ Rangers are very effective against **Burieds**.
Trivia: - When **Buried** buried itself, it would walk very slowly under the path.
- It was possible to see the **Buried's** health (and where it was) if you put your cursor on the path to where it was.

- You were able to see **Buried** when it was buried, when it crossed under the bridge in Trick or Threat Town. The animation of the **Buried** underground was the same walk animation it used above the ground.
- The shocked face on the **Buried** is based on the ﾟдﾟ emoticon, popularized from 2channel.

burnt_gingerbread.name: Burnt Gingerbread
burnt_gingerbread.description: The Burnt Gingerbread was an enemy that appeared in Village of Despair as part of the Christmas 2019 Event.

notice.text: Burnt Gingerbread has been removed from the game as of the 26th of January 2020 as it was part of the Christmas 2019 Event.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Fireball** - The **Burnt Gingerbread** throws a fireball at a tower, setting it alight, stunning the tower for about 10 seconds.

Description: The **Burnt Gingerbread** was an enemy that appeared in Village of Despair as part of the Christmas 2019 Event. It had the same speed as the Gingerbread, though it had less health. However, the main threat of the **Burnt Gingerbread** was that it was able to throw fireballs at towers. This stunned the tower for a lengthy period of time when hit, allowing other enemies to get past. It was also a hidden enemy.
The **Burnt Gingerbread** could have been spawned by Krampus.
Appearance: The **Burnt Gingerbread** took a similar appearance to the Gingerbread, though the **Burnt Gingerbread** was more burnt (or darker). It had glowing red eyes, frosting buttons and a frosting smile. The **Burnt Gingerbread** was set alight with a yellow flame.
Strategy: - Because the **Burnt Gingerbread** targets a random tower in its range, it may be wise to deploy a cheap tower, like the Scout, to distract the **Gingerbread** away from your main towers.
- The Pyromancer cannot slow the **Burnt Gingerbread** down (or target it) as it is immune to burn.
- If you want to slow the **Burnt Gingerbread**, then you can use the Freezer or Frost Blaster.
- Multiple **Burnt Gingerbreads** tend to throw their fireballs at one tower. This stuns the affected tower for a very long time as the stuns stack up.
- If the tower is important to your survival, it may be best to just sell it and replace it, saving a lot of time.
- As **Burnt Gingerbreads** are hidden enemies, you will need Outlaws or a couple of Level 2 Minigunners to deal with them.
- For cheap hidden detection, a Level 2 Soldier provides decent defense.
Trivia: - The **Burnt Gingerbread** may be based on the Christmas 2018 Elemental from *R2DA*.
- Additionally, when the **Burnt Gingerbread** used its *Fireball* ability, it made the same noise (albeit lower pitched) as the Gingerbread Minion's pain sound.
- The head used for the **Burnt Gingerbread** was a re-textured version of the Gingerbread Man Head accessory from the Roblox catalog.

c.name: C
c.description: C was an enemy which only appeared in the Hidden Wave and therefore only appeared in Fallen mode.

notice.text: C has been removed from the game as of the 4th of December 2021.

Description: **C** was an enemy which only appeared in the Hidden Wave and therefore only appeared in Fallen mode. As with the other lettered enemies in the game (A and B), it appeared after the Creator spawned.
**C** had a high amount of health and was very fast, faster than A and B.
Appearance: **C** had black reflective skin, a white lab coat, and red granite torso and legs. This was similar in appearance to A and B. It was about the same size as the Abnormal.
Strategy: - Because of its high health, high DPS towers like the Turret, Minigunner, Ranger and Accelerator, are highly recommended.
- Additionally, Commander and DJ Booth should be used to boost said towers.
- Due to **C's** fast speed, you should use towers that slow enemies down, like the Electroshocker, Sledger, Freezer, Frost Blaster or Toxic Gunner.
Trivia: - This enemy was similar to A and B in terms of naming and appearance.
- Out of all lettered enemies, **C** had the highest amount of health and fastest speed.
- This enemy was similar to M and J, from *Tower Battles*.
Update History: - **C** now appears in the legacy Hidden Wave, which is exclusive to Sandbox mode.
- **C** no longer appears in the legacy Hidden Wave, as it has been removed.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Explode** - The **Carrier** will, upon its death, create a huge bile bubble which stuns all towers caught in the radius. The **Carrier** will also split into four Swarms upon its death.

Description: The **Carrier**, in-game referred to as **Carrier 1** despite there only being one Carrier enemy, was a large, four-legged enemy, whom upon its death, exploded into 4 Swarms, and created a large green bile bubble that stunned towers that were caught within it.
Appearance: The **Carrier** had four dark green legs with claws. It was taller and wider than the average enemy. It had a long, light green, bent neck as well as a green head with glowing red eyes and a smile face, and it did not possess arms.
Strategy: - The **Carrier** will not destroy or stun any Military Base units or Crooks from the Crook Boss if any of them are caught in the explosion upon the **Carrier's** death.
- This makes units very useful in defeating the Swarms that spawn, if your towers are stunned.
- Long-range towers, such as the Outlaw and Sniper, are effective against the **Carrier** as they can shoot it from a long distance away and not be caught in the explosion.
- The explosion radius is nearly unavoidable by ground towers.
- If required, you can use the Freezer's *Ice Drop* ability to stop the **Carriers** or the Swarms in their track, before they get to close to your towers.
Trivia: - In the game, this was called the *Carrier 1*, even though there was never a *Carrier 2*.
- The **Carrier's** design was inspired by the Mutant Creeper, a modded mob in *Minecraft*.
- Before the first wave in which the **Carrier** appeared, the text "*Awwww man....*" was a reference to the song Revenge by CaptainSparklez's when he says, "*Creeper? Awww man.*"

cart.description: The Cart was an enemy that appeared exclusively in D00M's Revenge as part of the Duck Hunt Event.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Spillage** - Upon its destruction, the **Cart** spawns three Eggrolls.

Description: The **Cart** was an enemy that appeared exclusively in D00M's Revenge as part of the Duck Hunt Event. Currently, it can be spawned again in Sandbox mode, though not through Logbooks as **Cart** does not appear in Ducky Revenge Event. Instead, Mother Ducky has to be summoned to spawn it into the match. It had high health but slightly slow speed. Upon death, it would spawn three Eggrolls.
The **Cart** can be spawned by the Mother Ducky.
Appearance: The **Cart** is a light brown wooden cart filled with seven Eggrolls.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in D00M's Revenge is listed instead.
- Cheap towers like the Soldier and Golden Scout fare well against the **Cart**.

- Multiple Snipers are recommended for their long range, letting them defeat the **Cart** from further away, making it easier to deal with the Eggrolls spawned. In addition, the Sniper can also counter the Flying Ducky that debuts later on in the game.
- As the **Cart** is able to spawn multiple Eggrolls, towers that can damage multiple enemies at once, like the Executioner, are recommended.
Trivia: - Unlike other spawns, the **Cart** appeared on the enemy that it spawned from before it dies. This meant that you could damage both the Mother Ducky and **Cart** at the same time, if you had a tower that hits multiple enemies.
- Weirdly, the **Cart** contained seven eggs, but when killed it only spawned three Eggrolls.
Update History: - **Cart** can now be appear in Sandbox mode, only when the player summons the legacy Mother Ducky.
- **Bug**: No longer properly positioned behind the Mother Ducky.
- **Bug**: Sometimes has issues summoning in Eggrolls.

Description: The **Cat** was an enemy that appeared in Pls Donate as part of the Tower Defense Simulator x PLS DONATE Event. It had a high amount of health while also being quite fast, with only the Guest being faster. It also had 25% defense, Stun Immunity and Freeze Immunity. On some waves, it could spawn as a Hidden or Bloated enemy. Additionally, the Corrupted Haz3mn could summon them as Bloated.
Appearance: The **Cat** was a black cat with purple eyes and a purple tail.
Strategy: - Early game towers like the Crook Boss, Militant or Military Base can be useful against it, though towers with high DPS like the Minigunner, Mercenary Base or Engineer can also be useful.

- The Military Base and Mercenary Base can be especially useful, as its collision damage bypasses defense. The Crook Boss also can do that with its goons, though their main source of damage is their guns.
- As this enemy spawns in hordes, AOE towers like the Pyromancer, Mortar or Electroshocker can be useful against them.
- The Pyromancer and Electroshocker can also be useful at reducing its defense, though as it is quite low this is not necessary.
- Freeze defense dropping towers cannot be used, as it has the Freeze Immunity.
Trivia: - This enemy's appearance is based on the cat seen on Hazem's Roblox avatar.
- Because of this, it could also be seen on the Corrupted Haz3mn.
- The **Cat'**s voice is from Enthrallist's cat but pitched up.
Update History: - **Bug**: Jester's defense dropping does not reduce **Cat's** defense.

cavalry.name: Cavalry
cavalry.description: The Cavalry is a large enemy that appears in Badlands II, later being the guardian enemy for the Gunslinger.

stats.Attributes:
- Stun Immune
- Freeze Immune
- Bloated (Wave 25 only)

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Gunfight** - The **Cavalry** shoots a tower, stunning for a few seconds.

Description: The **Cavalry** is a large enemy that appears in Badlands II, later being the guardian enemy for the Gunslinger. The **Cavalry** spawns before the Gunslinger, on the left and right paths of the Badlands II map. It has very high health, low amount of defense and a slightly slow speed. It has one ability, where it shoots a tower, stunning it for a few seconds.

The **Cavalry** is, uniquely, completely unaffected by the All Paths modifier, a trait that in Badlands II it only shares with the Gunslinger. It will instead alternate between paths, similarly to how enemies spawn in multi-pathed maps without All Paths.
Appearance: The **Cavalry** is a giant humanoid with a waist and lower arms in its rig. It has a very desaturated green skin color. Its head is missing a patch of skin, revealing its skull. It wears a dark grey button up shirt with five yellow buttons, navy blue pants and very dark brown boots. It has a yellow and black belt with a gold buckle and a holster on its waist and a bandolier on its torso. It also has gold chevrons on its elbows and wears black gloves. It wears a beige cowboy hat and has a crimson shawl.

The **Cavalry** wields an 1860 Spencer lever action rifle to shoot towers and has a cartoonish walk as it holds it, having the rifle lean against its shoulder. It has a death animation, where it fall backwards, dropping its rifle in the process.
Strategy: - Multiple high DPS towers, such as the Accelerator, Engineer, Golden Minigunner or Turret are recommended.
- The Commander can be useful at boosting the firerate of these towers.
- You can use the Nuke consumable to instantly kill six **Cavalries**.
- Due to its immunities, stalling towers are far less effective against it.

- It cannot be frozen or chilled, as it has the Freeze Immunity. This also indirectly prevents it from having its defense dropped from freezing and prevents the Sledger from dealing double damage to it.
- As it has the Stun Immunity, it cannot be knocked back. Stuns will also only slow it down instead of stunning it.
- The Medic can be helpful at shielding towers from the **Cavalry's** stuns.
Trivia: - The **Cavalry** appears to be based on US cavalrymen in the American Old West and 19th century.
- This enemy resembles more of a foot soldier rather than an actual cavalry unit due to the fact that they have no horses to mount on.
- Uniquely, they also seem to march in sync with each other.
- The weapon of the **Cavalry**, as mentioned before, is the 1860 Spencer Lever Action Rifle, which was heavily adopted by the US Cavalry in the 19th century.
Version History: - **Bug**: **Cavalry's** death animation sometimes breaks, causing it to stand up instead of laying down.
- None of the changes were applied to its legacy version.
- **Bug**: Appears twice in the Index, one of them not loading in any model for the preview.
- **Bugfix**: No longer appears twice in the Index.

- Strong early-game towers like the Militant, Golden Scout or Golden Cowboy are very effective here.
- Towers with area of effect capabilities, like the Electroshocker or Mortar, can also be useful here.

- Towers that decrease defense, like the Pyromancer, Electroshocker or Cryomancer can be used to allow your towers to deal more damage to them, as well as making them slower when affected by certain defense dropping towers.
- High DPS towers, such as the Minigunner can be quite effective against this enemy, although they might cost a bit too much to be utilized when it first spawns.

Description: The **Chained Boss** is a slow and tanky boss, similar to the Slow Boss. It has far more health than many enemies that come before it, but is also slow, making it a shield for enemies behind it.
The **Chained Boss** only appears in Golden mode, which is locked behind Sandbox mode. The **Chained Boss** used to be spawned from the Mystery Boss upon its death in Golden mode.
Appearance: **Variant 1**

The current version of the **Chained Boss** has a reflective dark green skin, and a rusted torso and legs. Chains are wrapped around both of its arms, torso and right leg. Rusted parts can be seen coming out from its back. It has a slash on its face.
**Variant 2**

The unused version of the **Chained Boss** had a reflective dark green skin, and a rusted torso and legs. Chains were wrapped around both of its arms, torso and right leg. Rusted parts could be seen coming out from its back. It had glowing yellow eyes and a drooling zombie face. It walked slightly hunchbacked and had a twisted left leg.
**Variant 3**

The **Chained Boss** was slightly taller than the Slow Boss, and walked with its head slightly tilted forwards. It had light green skin, a green pebble torso and grey pebble legs. Its eyes were also glowing yellow and it had a drooling zombie face. A chain was wrapped around its torso. It also had rusty parts coming out of where its heart would be, front and back. Its head also appeared to have a tumor on the right side.
Strategy: - High DPS towers such as the Minigunner or Turret can easily defeat the **Chained Boss**.
- The Ranger also works well against this enemy.
- If needed, the Commander can decrease the firerate of these towers.
- Later on during the game, **Chained Bosses** spawn in hordes quite close to each other.
- For this reason, splash damage towers such as the Rocketeer and Mortar are quite effective against it.
Trivia: - The **Chained Boss** was not considered a boss before being renamed in the MEGA Update as it was simply called the *Chained*.
- For a brief period of time, the **Chained Boss** actually appeared naturally in Fallen mode on a single wave. However, this was later changed to Giant Bosses.
- The Uber Mystery also had a chance to summon in the **Chained Boss** in Fallen mode.
Update History: - Basic Freeze Immunity replaced with Freeze Immunity.
- First wave appearance changed from wave 52 to wave 22 on Hard mode (later Golden mode) and wave 28 on Insane mode (later Fallen mode).
- **Chained Boss** no longer naturally appears in Insane mode.
- **NOTE**: While the **Chained Boss** was removed in the Overhaul Update, multiple changes were made to it, though they could never be seen in-game due to its removal. These are:
- Freeze Immunity and Partial Electric Immunity removed.
- **Bug**: Rust parts at the front of its torso fall into the void.
- **Chained Boss** now appears in Golden mode, if activated through Sandbox mode.
- Because of changes made with updates, its appearance has been updated.
- **Chained Boss** no longer appears in Golden mode, as it has been removed.
- **Chained Boss** now appears in Golden mode, if activated through Sandbox mode.
Notes: - ↑ Only the first **Chained Boss** is a Boss enemy in Golden mode.

champion_templar.description: The Champion Templar is the final boss of Challenge Trials and all three PVP arenas.

- Challenge Trials
- Basic Arena
- Molten Arena
- Fallen Arena

stats.Base Health:
- 30,000 (Basic Arena PVP)
- 50,000 (Molten Arena PVP)
- 75,000 (Fallen Arena PVP)
- 400,000 (Challenge Trials)
- 10,000 (Sandbox)
stats.Attributes:
- Stun Immune
- Blessed (Fiery Boon)
- Boss Immunities:

  - Nuke Fallout Damage
  - DJ Booth Slowdown

abilities.label: Ability 1 Cooldown: 40 Attack CD: 5
abilities.text:
**Weaponry Switch** - The **Champion Templar** takes 2.5 seconds to alternate between its two weapons: the minigun and the hammer.
While using its minigun, *The Hammer Throw* and *Fiery Boon* abilities are deactivated. Whereas when using its hammer, the *Focused Fire* ability is deactivated.

abilities.label: Ability 2 Cooldown: 6 Attack CD: 6
abilities.text: **Focused Fire** - The **Champion Templar** locks onto a target and charges up a powerful shot from its minigun. After a short delay, it unleashes a continuous bullet barrage for 4 seconds, dealing 600 damage to units in a wide, growing beam and stunning towers caught in the path for 4 seconds. Has a firerate of 0.05 and a range of 20.

abilities.label: Ability 3 Cooldown: 10 Attack CD: 6
abilities.text: **Hammer Throw** - The **Champion Templar** hurls a massive hammer with great force, creating a shockwave upon impact. The explosion deals 600 damage to all units in a large radius, stuns towers for 4 seconds, and applies a 25% Range Debuff for the same duration as the stun. Has an explosion radius of 10 while the attack itself has a range of 25.

abilities.label: Ability 4 Cooldown: 20 Attack CD: 6
abilities.text: **Fiery Boon** - The **Champion Templar** slams the ground, creating a defensive aura that boosts nearby enemies' defense by 100% for 30 seconds through the Blessed attribute. The impact also deals 600 damage to nearby units and stuns towers for 4 seconds. Has a range of 15.

Description: The **Champion Templar** is the final boss of Challenge Trials and all three PVP arenas. It has higher health than all enemies that appear before it and has multiple abilities capable of stunning towers, damaging units and supporting enemies.

It has four abilities, with one of them being *Weaponry Switch*. This makes it swap between its hammer and minigun for 2.5 seconds. Depending on which mode is currently active, it can use different abilities.

When wielding its minigun, it can only use its *Focused Fire* ability. This makes it lock onto a target within its range of 20 units, then charge up a powerful shot. After a short delay will cause it to fire with a firerate of 0.05, dealing 600 damage to units and stunning towers for 4 seconds. It will keep firing for 4 seconds.
When wielding its hammer, it has two abilities, *Hammer Throw* and *Fiery Boon*.

- *Hammer Throw* makes the *Champion Templar* throw its hammer at a target within its range of 25 units, creating an explosion with a radius of 10 on impact. This explosion applies a 4 second stun and 4 second 25% Range Debuff to towers, while also dealing 600 damage to units.

- *Fiery Boon* makes the **Champion Templar** slam the ground with its hammer, creating a defense aura that makes enemies, including itself, Blessed. The impact from the aura will also damage all units by 600 and stun towers for 4 seconds within its range of 15.
Logbook Description: **Variant 1**

"*Champion Templars were the Fallen King's most legendary warriors. Only a handful of these fighters existed, and they were equipped with the most prestigious weaponry the kingdom could offer. When the Queen's curse swept through the kingdom, the sacred grounds protected the Templars from corruption. When the curse tainted their people into seeking out endless war, the Templars had to make a choice. They left their kingdom to join Two X, even if it meant fighting against the people they once swore to protect. In the Old World, they stood with Two X against Lord Exo's forces and were thought to be slain in the war. Although, one Templar had survived. The Fallen attempted to resurrect the others, hoping to restore the glory they once represented, but failed. The lone survivor searches to avenge what their kingdom once was, and slay their fallen King.*"
**Variant 2**

"*Dating back to ancient Robloxian times, the Templar were considered some of the strongest warriors, composed of the fiercest victors from Exo's gladiatorial battles. They fought side by side in Exo's army of the Fallen, equipped with the most prestigious and advanced weaponry. After Exo vanished, the Templar went extinct. Many attempts have been made to resurrect them for the Fallen’s modern army using the corpses of their ancestors, but none have lived up to their former legacy.*
*Now, in the wake of renewed competitive spirit, one Templar awakens—resuming his original duty as the final Champion.*"
Appearance: **Variant 1**

The **Champion Templar** wears gold and white armor with red accents, two bulky shoulder pads each with a spike on top, a knight-like helmet with two eye sockets and silver horns. Various parts of its armor contain gold crosses. It wields a hammer-minigun fusion weapon which can switch between a minigun and hammer mode.
**Variant 2**

The **Champion Templar** wears white and black armor with silver accents, two bulky shoulder pads each with a spike on top, a knight-like helmet with two eye sockets and silver horns. Various parts of its armor contain black crosses. It wields a hammer-minigun fusion weapon which can switch between a minigun and hammer mode.
Strategy: - The **Champion Templar** is backed by plenty of Brutes, Molten Titans and Fallen Guardians. It is advised to bring high-end towers like the Accelerator, Necromancer, Mercenary Base and Minigunner to defeat it.
- Unstunnable towers like Pursuit and Ranger can be useful against the **Champion Templar** as they can consistently deal full damage without being stunned.
- The **Champion Templar** boasts extremely short cooldowns with heavy stuns, so towers like the Medic can be helpful to counteract *Focused Fire* and *Hammer Throw*.
- High-end DPS towers are suggested to take down Blessed enemies, and defense melting towers like the Pyromancer are invaluable to have, due to the incredibly high defense values.

- Although it may seem like due to Blessed, defense melting towers would be far more effective, this is not actually the case, as the value melted does not change. For instance, with 100% Defense, the Pyromancer will reduce it to 50%. If that same enemy has Blessed, the Pyromancer will not reduce it to 100% but instead will still reduce it down by 50% to 150%.
- Mortar and Rocketeer can be great picks as well, since they completely negate defense, and can chew down the horde to reduce *Fiery Boon* effectiveness.
- Baiting out the **Champion Templar's** attacks can be incredibly useful, as its attacks ravage your defending capabilities otherwise.
Trivia: - The **Champion Templar** Logbook can only be obtained through Challenge Trials.
- The **Champion Templar** is the first and currently the only PVP enemy to have different appearances based on the team it spawned in.
- If spawned outside of PVP mode (most notably in Challenge Trials), it would take the appearance of the Red Team spawn.
- The **Champion Templar** is a reimagining of the legacy Templar enemy.
- Because of this, it is likely named after the Knights Templar, a Catholic medieval chivalric order, most infamously known for the Crusades.
- The **Champion Templar** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
- Interestingly, inside the **Champion Templar**’s torso lies a mini **Champion Templar** with no animations.
Update History: - **Bug**: **Champion Templar** clips into the ground when made larger or smaller.
- **Bug**: **Champion Templar** has collidable parts while using some of its abilities.
- **Bug**: **Champion Templar** has no animations in its Index entry.
- **Bug**: Logbook description incorrectly uses "Templar were" instead of the correct "Templars were".
- **Bug**: All sounds except hammer slam no longer play.
- **Bug**: Boss attribute health bar no longer appear.
- **Bugfix**: No longer clips into the ground when made larger or smaller.
- **Bugfix**: Boss attribute health bar now properly appear.

charge.name: Charge
charge.description: The Charge is a very fast enemy that appeared in Golden mode, which is only accessible through Sandbox mode. It is noticeably faster than most enemies in the game.

notice.text: Charge was previously removed on the 29th of October 2020, though it has been made available through the Sandbox mode later.

Description: The **Charge** is a very fast enemy that appeared in Golden mode, which is only accessible through Sandbox mode. It is noticeably faster than most enemies in the game. However, it has low health compared to other enemies that spawn around the same time in Golden mode. It has the Stun Immunity, meaning it only gets slowed down by stuns instead of being stunned and it cannot be knocked back.
The **Charge** could be spawned from the Mystery upon its death in Golden mode, from wave 27 onwards.
Appearance: **Variant 1**

The **Charge** has a red granite torso and legs, with 67% of its head and left arm being neon blue. It is slightly smaller than an average enemy. The rest of its head and right arm is neon red. On its torso was a neon light blue lightning bolt. It wears white snow goggles as well as two metal armbands around its arms, one higher on the blue arm and the other lower on the red arm. Blue sparks are emitted from its torso. It is faceless.
**Variant 2**

The **Charge** had a red granite torso and legs, with 67% of its head and left arm being neon blue. It was slightly smaller than an average enemy. The rest of its head and right arm was neon red. On its torso was a neon light blue lightning bolt. It wore white snow goggles as well as two metal armbands around its arms, one higher on the blue arm and the other lower on the red arm. Blue sparks were emitted from its torso.
Strategy: - Using towers that can slow down the **Charge**, such as the Electroshocker, Frost Blaster, Pyromancer and Freezer, are highly recommended.
- Be aware that stunning towers like the Electroshocker will only slow the **Charge** down instead of stunning it.

- **Charges** mostly spawn in groups, so splash damage towers such as the Rocketeer and Mortar are recommended. You may also want other towers with high range, such as the Turret or Ranger, to assist with any **Charges** that survive.
- Placement is crucial. Even with a tower's high range, the **Charge** can still pass through if the tower does not have enough map coverage.
- Using the Commander to boost firerate will help.
- The Military Base's Tanks and Railgun Tanks can absorb damage from damaged **Charges** quite easily while also being able to damage them.
Trivia: - It was hinted that the **Charge** may be a fusion between the Bolt and Glitch, judging by its asymmetrical looks.
- The **Charge** originally had a more stable running animation compared to the Bolt.
- When the Uber Mystery was in the game, it had a chance to spawn the **Charge** on Fallen mode when it died, despite the **Charge** only naturally spawning on Golden mode.
- The **Charge's** goggles are a re-textured version of the Laser Spec Special Forces Goggles accessory from the Roblox catalog.
Update History: - **NOTE**: While the **Charge** was removed in the Overhaul Update, multiple changes were made to it, though they could never be seen in-game due to its removal. These are:
- Partial Electric Immunity replaced with Energy Immunity.
- **Charge** now appears in Golden mode, if activated through Sandbox mode.
- Because of changes made with updates, its appearance has been updated and its Partial Electric Immunity has been replaced with the Stun Immunity.
- **Charge** no longer appears in Golden mode, as it has been removed.
- **Charge** now appears in Golden mode, if activated through Sandbox mode.

chunky_ducky.description: The Chunky Ducky was a tanky enemy that appeared in Bathroom Approach as part of the Ducky Revenge Event.

Description: The **Chunky Ducky** was a tanky enemy that appeared in Bathroom Approach as part of the Ducky Revenge Event. As a large enemy, it has high health and below average speed. It also has 50% defense, reducing most forms of damage by 33%.
Logbook Description: "*Chunky Ducky aspires to be as wide and double-thick as Fat Ducky. However, the Evil Duckies would often be found knocking Chunky Ducky over and rolling him across the room. When Chunky Ducky lies down, it's not uncommon for a duckling or two to go missing beneath him. He means well, but is simply misunderstood.*"
Appearance: The **Chunky Ducky** is a massively wide yellow duck with black eyes, an orange beak and flippers. It is significantly larger than most other duckies and it has an extremely wide body. It has three animations that it can randomly have, where all three also have differently shaped eyes. The first animation has it have a happy expression, the second has it have a serious expression while the third one has its eyes partially closed, likely because it is scared.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Bathroom Approach is listed instead.
- The Minigunner, Ranger and Pursuit can easily deal with the **Chunky Ducky**.
- As this enemy has high health with defense, you could use slowing towers such as the Tesla or Electroshocker to slow them down and decrease their defense.
- Do note that the **Chunky Ducky** has Freeze Immunity, so towers like the Freezer are unable to affect it.
- AOE towers like the Mortar, Rocketeer or bottom path Pursuit can be used to deal damage to the **Chunky Ducky** and the hordes of enemies it generally spawns with.
Trivia: - The **Chunky Ducky** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Short-Circuit** - Upon its death, the **Circuit** will speed up nearby enemies by 25%. This can stack.

Description: The **Circuit**, internally referred to as **Circuit2**, is an enemy that appears in Polluted Wasteland II and Challenge Trials. It has a somewhat high amount of health and a slightly fast speed. The **Circuit** has one ability, where on death, it speeds up nearby enemies by 25% with no limit, similar to the Speedy King.

The **Circuit** could be spawned by the Nuclear Monster. This means it could also appear in Oops! All slimes!, if spawned by the Nuclear Monster. It also could be spawned by the Mystery, Wave 27 onwards.
Appearance: The **Circuit** has glowing bright blue skin and a dark blue torso and legs. It has an energy pack on its back with an antenna that emits yellow sparks and six large batteries connected to it. It has a glowing desaturated yellow lightning bolt on its chest and desaturated yellow veins can be seen on its body. It also emits blue pulses and yellow particles from its torso and its head twitches whenever it runs.
It plays a thunder strike sound and visual on death.
Strategy: - High DPS towers, such as the Ranger, Golden Minigunner, Accelerator or Engineer are recommended to take down the **Circuit**.
- The Commander and DJ Booth should be used to boost the firerate and range of these towers.
- Slowing towers, such as the Electroshocker, DJ Booth and Warden, may be useful against the **Circuit** and enemies that were sped up by it.
- As the **Circuit** has the Stun Immunity, the Electroshocker and Warden will only slow it down instead of stopping it completely while knockback towers like the Brawler will not knock it back.
- As it has Freeze Immunity, freezing towers cannot be used on it, though they can still be used on enemies boosted by it, as long as they are not Freeze Immune themselves.
- Be aware that if an enemy gets boosted by other **Circuits**, the freeze will be negated. This also applies to other enemies being boosted by the **Circuit**.
Trivia: - The **Circuit** is currently the only Polluted Wasteland II enemy to replace two enemies.
Update History: - **Bug**: Its ability can cause frozen enemies to start moving temporarily.
- Energy Immunity replaced with Stun Immunity.
- None of the changes are applied to the legacy version.
- **Bug**: **Circuit** no longer uses the death sound effect.
- Cash given is now mode dependent.
- Gives $875 every 25% health lost in Polluted Wasteland II.
- Gives $250 every 25% health lost in Challenge Trials.
- Default value is $1 every 25% health lost.
- Health increased from 1,500 to 2,500 in Polluted Wasteland II and Sandbox mode.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Super Charge** - The **Circuit** shocks nearby enemies with lightning, increasing movement speed by 25-50% at random intervals. The ability can stack multiple times.

Description: The **Circuit** was a very fast enemy that appeared in Hardcore mode (it used to appear in Polluted Wasteland in Fallen mode, replacing the Error). Currently, it can only be spawned in Sandbox mode if the player has the Sandbox Plus+ gamepass. The **Circuit** has quite high speed and somewhat high health. However, the **Circuit** has the *Super Charge* ability, letting it make itself and surrounding enemies faster, including major bosses (like the Fallen King). If you are really unlucky, multiple *Super Charges* can stack, making strong enemies extremely fast, even faster than the Error and Glitch, making it a very dangerous enemy. The **Circuit** also has Stun Immunity, which makes the Warden and Electroshocker only slow it down and making knockback towers not knock it back.
The **Circuit** can be spawned from the Mystery upon its death in Hardcore mode, from wave 44 onwards.
Appearance: **Variant 1**
The current version of the **Circuit** is identical to its original version, except it has no mouth.
**Variant 2**

The original version of the **Circuit** had a near complete blue appearance. It was slightly smaller than the average enemy. It had lightning particles in both hands and also had a blue threatening face, with blue glowing eyes. Some blue glitch particles could be briefly seen emitting from its torso. When a *Super Charge* occurred, electricity bolts can be seen above its head and a mouth beside its face.
Strategy: This strategy refers to the state of the game while the **Invisible** still appeared in the Hardcore mode.
- This enemy must be defeated quickly. If not, it can speed enemies up to speeds greater than the Glitch and Fallen Rusher.

- This can speed up large enemies, such as the Slow King and Vindicator, and even major bosses like the Fallen King. Taking into account the ability to stack, this has the potential to be the most dangerous enemy in the game.
- Fast-firing towers, such as the Minigunner, paired with the Commander, are recommended to defeat the **Circuit** quickly.
- Long range towers, like the Ranger, are also recommended.
- The Accelerator is not recommended against the **Circuit** as it will likely get out of its range before the Accelerator can charge up.
- Not to mention when the Accelerator targets an enemy it will not change targets before the enemy is killed, which may cause the **Circuit** to slip by.
- You can counter this by slowing down the **Circuit** with the Frost Blaster, Toxic Gunner, Sledger, Harvester or Freezer to allow your Accelerators to charge up and attack it.
- The Rocketeer and Mortar can damage hordes of **Circuits**. However, be aware that the **Circuit** may outrun the projectiles from these towers.
- The Electroshocker, Toxic Gunner, Sledger, Harvester and Warden can be used to slow down the **Circuit**.

- Do note that the Stun Immunity that the **Circuit** has prevents stunning towers like the Electroshocker from stunning it, with it only being slowed down instead and it cannot be knocked back because of it.
- The Military Base's Tank and Railgun Tank are the best in halting the advance of the **Circuit** as it can easily sprint past all of your defenses.
Trivia: - The **Circuit**, alongside the Speedy King, the Circuit from Polluted Wasteland II and the Commander enemy are the only enemies to make other enemies faster.
- The **Circuit** is the second (and currently only) Polluted Wasteland exclusive enemy to appear outside Polluted Wasteland.
- The Rusher was the first enemy to appear outside it; it had a chance to be spawned from a Mystery when it died after wave 28 in Fallen mode. However, this no longer occurs.
- Due to Polluted Wasteland being removed, the **Circuit** is the only Polluted Wasteland enemy to appear in the game.
Update History: - **Bug**: Its ability can cause frozen enemies to start moving temporarily.
- **Bugfix**: *Super Charge* indicator no longer disappears after 5 seconds.
- Partial Electric Immunity replaced with Energy Immunity.
- No longer appears in Polluted Wasteland as it has been removed.
- Energy Immunity replaced with Stun Immunity.
- **Circuit** removed from the main game, as it has been directly replaced by Speedy King. Now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.
- No longer appears in the Index.

Trivia: - Its appearance is based on the Citizen 1 and Citizen 2 units that appeared in the Halloween 2020 Event.

Description: The **Cobalt Guard**, internally referred to as **Guard Plush**, is a tanky enemy that appears in Pizza Party. It has a high amount of health and an average speed, though unlike the Shotgunner that appears before it, it has no defense. It is also a Lead enemy, meaning only towers with lead detection can damage it. It is also Stun Immune, making it only get slowed down by stuns and immune to knockback.
Appearance: The **Cobalt Guard** is a large humanoid with a waist and lower arms in its rig. It is entirely made of plush fabric shown by the stitches that can be seen throughout its body. It wears a dark purple crusader helmet, chestplate with white horns, leggings, belt, boots knee-pads and shoulder-pads as well as black braces with dark purple spikes. A pair of small white eyes in an angry expression can be seen in the eyeholes of the helmet.
The **Cobalt Guard** has a death animation where it will fall to its knees before falling forward.
Strategy: - High DPS towers with lead detection, like the Accelerator, Engineer, Ranger or Pursuit are quite effective against this.
- The Firework Technician can be used to give all your towers lead detection for a brief period of time.
- The Commander and DJ Booth can be also used to boost the DPS of your towers.
- The **Cobalt Guard** is quite fast, though due to its immunities it is harder to stall.
- Its Stun Immunity prevents it from being knocked back and makes stuns only slow it down.
- Other forms of stalling, such as the DJ Booth's slowdown, are unaffected.
- The Frost Blaster can freeze and deal good damage to them.
Trivia: - Unlocking the **Cobalt Guard's** logbook will not grant you the ability to summon the Cobalt Guard from the Solar Eclipse Event.
- This is due to the **Cobalt Guard's** internal name being *Guard Plush*.
Update History: - **Bug**: **Cobalt Guard** slightly floats above the ground when made larger or smaller.
- Cash given increased from $1,000 to $1,500 every 25% health lost.
- **Bugfix**: No longer floats above the ground when made larger or smaller.

cold_mist_krampus_frosthold.name: Cold Mist
cold_mist_krampus_frosthold.description: The Cold Mist was a hidden and ghost enemy that first appeared in the second phase of Krampus Frosthold as part of the Krampus' Revenge Event.

notice.text: Cold Mist (Krampus Frosthold) has been removed from the game as of the 31st of January 2024 as it was part of the Krampus' Revenge Event.

Description: The **Cold Mist** was a hidden and ghost enemy that first appeared in the second phase of Krampus Frosthold as part of the Krampus' Revenge Event. It had a medium amount of health for its debut and an above average speed. However, as the **Cold Mist** was a Hidden and Ghost enemy, only a limited amount of towers can target it and units cannot collide with it. This allowed it to easily overwhelm unprepared defenses.
Appearance: The **Cold Mist** was a translucent humanoid figure that glowed blue. It floated above the ground, having a wispy tail instead of legs, with its head pointing down toward the ground. It wore a translucent dark blue chain with a lock.
Strategy: - The **Cold Mist** can be dangerous because it is a hidden enemy with high health.
- Towers with high damage and hidden detection capabilities, like the Minigunner or Accelerator can be useful against this enemy.
- Area of effect towers with hidden detection, like the Golden Pyromancer, Pyromancer or Executioner can be useful at clearing out hordes of **Cold Mists**.
- Similar towers without hidden detection, like the Pursuit or Mortar, despite being unable to target the **Cold Mist**, can still deal damage to it if they are indirectly caught in its explosion.
- Towers placed at the back might have an easier time dealing with the **Cold Mist**, as it will be separated away from other high health enemies.
- As this enemy is a ghost enemy, units cannot collide with.
- They can, however, still damage it if the unit has hidden detection or if their attacks can indirectly hit.
Trivia: - The **Cold Mist** borrows the model of the Ghost, an enemy from the Lunar Overture Event.
- The lock and chain the **Cold Mist** wears is also reminiscent of the Wraith from the Solar Eclipse Event.
- On the 24th of December 2023, it was stated officially that the **Cold Mist's** health was lowered, despite no actual change occurring.

Description: The **Cold Mist** was an enemy that appeared exclusively in Outpost 32 as part of the Frost Invasion Event. Currently, it can be spawned in Sandbox mode. Compared to the Snowy, the **Cold Mist** had slightly higher health with slower speed. However, the **Cold Mist's** was a hidden and ghost enemy, meaning that only certain towers could target and damage it, making it a potential danger early on.
Upon its death, the Frost Mystery had a chance to spawn the **Cold Mist**.
Appearance: The **Cold Mist's** entire body is black and translucent. It is faceless and blue smoke particles were emitted from its torso. The **Cold Mist** floats a small distance above the path. Its head is slightly tilted downwards.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Outpost 32 is listed instead.
- The Military Base is useless against the **Cold Mist**, as its units will go right through them, as the **Cold Mist** is a ghost enemy.
- For the same reason, the Crook Boss' units cannot collide with nor detect the **Cold Mist**, also making them useless.
- Level 2 Minigunners are your best bet against the **Cold Mist**, as they perform very well against it.
- You can also use the Accelerator since it has hidden detection from Level 0.
- The Crook Boss also fares decently well against the **Cold Mist**, though its range is not optimal.
- It is generally advised that multiple players save for the Minigunner starting from the beginning of the game, to ensure sufficient DPS against the **Cold Mist** once it debuts.
- The Pyromancer is close to useless against the **Cold Mist**, as it cannot target them.
- However, its flames can still damage the **Cold Mist**, so long there is another detectable enemy in range.
- Later on during the match, you can use a Level 4 Ace Pilot to grant hidden detection to other towers that cannot detect **Cold Mists**, like the Ranger.
- However, the Ace Pilot will only grant hidden detection for 15 seconds at the start of the match, making this fairly unreliable.

- While most splash damage towers do not have hidden detection, such as the Rocketeer and Mortar, if another detectable enemy is nearby, the **Cold Mist** may be indirectly damaged if caught in the explosion.
Trivia: - The **Cold Mist** was very similar to the Ghost in the Halloween 2020 Event in terms of functionality and animation.
Update History: - **Cold Mist** can now be summoned in Sandbox mode, only when the player has the Cold Mist's Logbook from the Operation I.C.E Event.
- No longer copies the statistics of the modern version in Sandbox mode.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Call to Arms** - The **Commander** will stop moving and start shaking for a brief period of time before emitting radio waves from its head, speeding up itself and nearby enemies.

Description: The **Commander** is an enemy that appears in Pizza Party. It has a high amount of health and an above average speed. It is also immune to being frozen by freezing towers and has the Stun Immunity, which makes it only be slowed down instead of stunned by the Warden and Electroshocker and makes it immune to knockback. It has one ability where it will stop moving and start shaking for a brief period of time before emitting radio waves from its head, which speeds up the **Commander** and nearby enemies.
The **Commander** replaces the Tank in Pizza Party.
Appearance: The **Commander** is a robot that resembles the Level 0 Default Commander. It has white skin, blue uniform with yellow markings, an upturned collar and a yellow lapel, blue tilted cap, black torso and shoes and dark blue pants. It has black button eyes and black sewed mouth. On the lower part of its torso, there is a large mouth with white teeth and a red bloody tongue that goes through a part of its upper torso, and coming up out of the back, holding a stool in place. Part of its head and left arm are also torn off, revealing its endoskeleton and wires. It also has an oversized radio in place of a hand which it uses to speed up other enemies.
On death, it will shake and flail its arms around, emit yellow sparks and then power down and fall forward. It also plays a powering down sound when it dies.
Strategy: - When the **Commander** first appears on Wave 25, it is not much of a threat as only a few enemies spawn after it for it to speed up.
- However, subsequent waves have the **Commander** spawn alongside more strong enemies like hordes of Shotgunners and Cobalt Guards, making it a significant threat.
- High DPS towers like the Golden Minigunner, Accelerator or Engineer are recommended against it.
- The Commander tower can also be quite useful at decreasing these tower's firerate, boosting their DPS.
- You can try to kill the **Commander** before it can speed any enemies up, though this is not necessary.
- As the **Commander** has Freeze Immunity, the Freezer, Frost Blaster and Sledger cannot freeze this enemy.
- The Electroshocker and Warden can only slow it down instead of stopping it completely while knockback towers like the Brawler cannot knock it back, because of its Stun Immunity.
- Additionally, because of the **Commander's** size, the Warden will only slow it down for a shorter amount of time.
Trivia: - The **Commander**, alongside the Shivergeist, the Circuit and the Speedy King are the only modern enemies to boost the speed of nearby enemies.
- The **Commander** might be based on Nightmare Fredbear from the *Five Night's at Freddy's* series.
Update History: - Energy Immunity replaced with Stun Immunity.
- **Bug**: Appears twice in the Index, one of them not loading in any model for the preview.
- Cash given increased from $2,000 to $3,000 every 25% health lost.
- **Bugfix**: No longer appears twice in the Index.
Notes: - ↑ Only the first **Commander** is a Boss enemy.

abilities.label: Ability 1 Cooldown: 35
abilities.text: **Summon** - Slams its staff, summoning six random enemies with a 0.5 second delay between each spawn. These enemies can be the Giant Skeleton (60% chance) and the Necromancer (40% chance).

abilities.label: Ability 2
abilities.text: **Cloak** - Becomes a Hidden enemy at half health.

Description: The **Conjurer** is an enemy that appears in Badlands II. It has high health and walks at a slow speed.

The **Conjurer** has two abilities. The first ability is *Summon*, which causes it to slam its staff, summoning six random enemies with a 0.5 delay between each spawn. These enemies can be the Giant Skeleton (60% chance) and the Necromancer (40% chance). Its second ability, *Cloak*, only happens when it loses half of its health. This turns it into a Hidden enemy, making it untargetable by towers without hidden detection.
Appearance: The **Conjurer** has light maroon skin. It wears a brown shirt and pants, as well as a light brown scarf, bandages and dark brown gloves. On its head, it wears a grey and light red metal helmet with horns, which resembled a skull. It wears grey and red shoes and padding around its waist. It walks with a staff.
Strategy: - High DPS towers, like the the Turret, Pursuit, Minigunner or Accelerator can be useful here.
- High DPS towers with splash damage capabilities can be especially useful, as they can hit both the **Conjurer** and the enemies it summons. Such towers include the Ranger, Pursuit and Engineer.
- At half health, the **Conjurer** will become Hidden, so make sure you have sufficient hidden detection source.
- The Ace Pilot and Firework Technician can be used to give towers that do not have hidden detection, such as the Ranger hidden detection, allowing them to kill it.
- Area of effect towers like the Mortar, Rocketeer or Electroshocker can be useful at dealing with enemies spawned by the **Conjurer**.
- No cash can be generated from summoned enemies. This includes the Cowboy's cash generation.
- However, this also means that the Cowboy will deal more DPS to the summons, as attacking summoned enemies does not make it spin its guns, making it attack for longer.
- The **Conjurer** has multiple immunities, meaning it is far harder to slow down.
- As it has the Freeze Immunity, it cannot be frozen or chilled by freezing towers. This also means it cannot have its defense dropped through freeze.
- Its Stun Immunity prevents it from being knocked back by towers. It also makes it only get slowed down by stuns instead of fully stunned.

Description: The **Conjurer** was the second boss to appear in The Nightmare Realm and Containment as part of the Hexscape Event. It had a high health and walked at a below average speed. It has Freeze Immunity and Stun Immunity, while also being a Boss enemy when it first spawned in The Nightmare Realm, granting it additional immunities for its first appearance. On some waves, it also appeared with Bloated and Nimble attributes.

The **Conjurer** had two abilities. The first ability was *Summon*, which caused it to slam its staff, summoning five Forsaken Skulls. Its second ability, *Cloak*, only happened when it lost half of its health. This turned it into a Hidden enemy, making it untargetable by towers without hidden detection.
Appearance: The **Conjurer** had light maroon skin. It wore a brown shirt and pants, as well as a light brown scarf, bandages and dark brown gloves. On its head, it wore a grey and light red metal helmet with horns, which resembled a skull. It wore grey and red shoes and padding around its waist. It walked with a staff.
Strategy: - High DPS towers with hidden detection like the Ace Pilot, Gatling Gun, Engineer and Minigunner are strongly recommended to kill the **Conjurer**
- Towers without hidden detection, like the Ranger, cannot attack it after it loses half of its health, as it becomes a Hidden enemy.
- The Ace Pilot can be used to give such towers hidden detections.
- The **Conjurer** has quite high defense. Because of this, defense dropping towers like the Pyromancer or DJ Booth can be useful against it.
- As it has the Freeze Immunity, freeze defense dropping towers cannot drop its defense.
- Because of its immunities, it cannot be knocked back, frozen or chilled, and it is only slowed down instead of being stunned by stunning towers.

- Additionally, when it first spawns it is a Boss enemy, making it immune to even more forms of stalling. The only towers capable of slowing it down as a Boss are stunning towers like the Electroshocker or Trapper.
Trivia: - The **Conjurer** used the same animations as the Fallen Summoner, and shared the basis of its ability functionality with it.

Description: The **Conserver** was the final boss of The Nightmare Realm, second night of the Hexscape Event. It had a high amount of health but walked much slower than every enemy that appeared before it. It was also a Boss enemy, granting it multiple immunities.
The **Conserver** had four abilities:

- The first was *Endbringer*, which was only activated if all the Super Computer parts were not fixed before the **Conserver** spawned. This made the **Conserver** have its health multiplied by 7.5, with the base health going from 80,000 to 600,000 in the Easy difficulty and from 400,000 to 3,000,000 in the Hard difficulty.

- Its second ability was *Spirit Release*, which made it fire out multiple skulls from its body. These stunned towers for 3 seconds while also applying a 40% Scared Debuff for 10 seconds, including non-humanoid towers. Towers would also have ghosts appear out of them.
- The third ability was *Summon*, which summoned ten Forsaken Skull with a 0.3 delay between each and seven Bloated Hex Revenants with a 0.8 delay, while also healing itself by 1,000.
- Its last ability, *Void Smash* made it slam its club on the ground, creating multiple thorns that stunned any tower hit for 4 seconds.
Appearance: The **Conserver's** body was made entirely out of what appears to be molten slag or lava. It wore black armor, which covered most of its body. Its helmet had multiple horns. Additionally, it had spikes seen around its head that resembled teeth. On its back, it had the Artificial God Cube. It wielded a black club with neon red insides, which had three eyes on it.
Strategy: - Super Computer should be fixed by purchasing every single Super Computer Parts before the **Conserver** spawns. Otherwise, its health will be multiplied by 7.5, making it extremely hard to beat if playing on the Easy difficulty, but outright impossible to kill in the Hard difficulty.

- High DPS towers, like the Engineer, Accelerator, Ranger or Minigunner, are great choices against the **Conserver**. While expensive, they can be upgraded quite easily as the **Conserver** gives $40,000 every 5% health lost.
- Because of this, more expensive towers like the Turret or Gatling Gun can also be afforded, despite their high costs.
- The DJ Booth can be useful at reducing their upgrade costs, making it easier to afford them, while also boosting their damage and range.
- The Commander can also be used to boost the DPS of your towers.
- The **Conserver** can reduce tower range by 40% for multiple seconds with its *Spirit Release* ability.
- This can be partially mitigated using the DJ Booth's Range Buffs, with its purple track providing the biggest buff.
- The Medic can be useful at cleansing stuns from towers with its ability, though it cannot be used to remove debuffs applied by the **Conserver**.
- The Golden Cowboy and Cowboy can be great methods of affording expensive towers with high DPS.
Trivia: - Under specific conditions, the **Conserver** had the highest health in the game. If in a hard difficulty trio, with a broken Super Computer, and Bloated, the **Conserver** could have 6,375,100 health.
Update History: - Cash given changed from $40,000 to $7,500 every 5% health lost.
- Health increased from 400,000 to 425,000 in Hard difficulty.
- Cash given increased from $7,500 to $40,000 every 5% health lost.
- Health decreased from 425,000 to 400,000 in Hard difficulty.
- **Conserver** can no longer have its defense decreased.
