abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Shrike Death** - Upon its death, the **Controlled** spawns a Shrike Crystal.

Description: The **Controlled** appeared to be a normal enemy with average speed and low health for its debut. However, it could turn very deadly as it was able to spawn a Shrike Crystal upon its death, which stunned towers near it. This allowed other enemies to pass through without being attacked by towers, creating a very dangerous situation.
Appearance: The **Controlled** was faceless, aside from a drooling zombie mouth. It had a headcrab on its head and a grey bandanna. The **Controlled** had grey diamond-plated wristbands and leg-bands. Its skin was grey, and it had a black pebble torso and legs.
Strategy: - You should not underestimate the **Controlled**, as it can easily overwhelm your towers due to its ability to spawn Shrike Crystals.
- The **Controlled** spawn in hordes, but while it appears that towers that deal splash damage may be useful, they can lead to your downfall.
- This is because the **Controlleds** can spawn multiple Shrike Crystals, which are immune to splash damage, meaning your towers may get stunned for a while, if you rely on such towers.
- Additionally, short range towers like the Gladiator may not be able to reach the Shrike Crystals.
- Against the **Controlled**, high DPS towers, such as the Minigunner, are very effective.
- Additionally, the Crooks from the Crook Boss are also useful, but you should not rely on them.
Trivia: - The **Controlled** seemed to be a reference to the Shrike from the *Marvel Cinematic Universe*.
- The **Controlled's** design was most likely inspired from the Headcrab Zombie from the *Half-Life* series.

- High DPS towers like the Accelerator, Pursuit or Golden Minigunner can quickly deal with the **Cookie Guard**.

Description: The **Corpse** is an enemy that only appears when spawned through the Corpse attribute. Uniquely, its statistics are actually heavily based on the enemy that summoned it, instead of having its own statistics, though it does have some statistics that do not change. This is because the **Corpse** is not its own enemy, it is actually the enemy it spawned from with a changed display name and altered statistics.

Most notably, it has 100% defense, and it has the Corpse, Stun Immunity and Burn Immunity attributes. Its health is 75% of the enemy that it spawned from. Additionally, some of the attributes the enemy it spawned from are also inherited. The only exception to this is Hidden, which is removed upon the enemy's death.
Appearance: The **Corpse** does not have a consistent appearance, as the model it uses is based on the enemy it spawned from, though it does have certain characteristics which are consistent between them all. The **Corpse** is the body of the enemy it spawned from made entirely out of black molten rocks. Any images present on the enemy, such as faces, will remain on them even as a **Corpse**.
Strategy: - The **Corpse** is not a threatening enemy, as it cannot move to the entrance, meaning losing to it is impossible. Its main purpose is to act as a shield for enemies behind it.
- However, it can be relatively annoying with its 100% defense and tendency to distract towers from attacking actual enemies.
- Towers like the Electroshocker or Toxic Gunner can be used to drop its defense, as it is very high. The Pyromancer cannot be used since it has Burn Immunity.
- Towers like the Ranger or Mortar can be used to take care of any corpses that are too far away from your main defenses with their high range.
- The **Corpse** is required to be killed before a match can end.
- Waves can be skipped while only **Corpses** are on the path, as that still grants the wave clear bonus. Additionally, infinite waves cannot be skipped at all.
- If you have the DJ Booth, you can exploit this by repeatedly using its *Drop The Beat* ability on Green track to make as much cash as you want.
- As the **Corpse** is technically not a unique, summoned enemy, but instead the slightly altered version of the enemy it spawned from, the Cowboy is able to generate cash from it.
Trivia: - The **Corpse** is not actually its own enemy; it is just the enemy it spawned from which has been revived and had its statistics and appearance altered.
- A **Corpse** of an enemy still keeps the ability of said enemy.
- This can lead to weird things happening, for example, a **Corpse** of a Warden will be able to move after using its *Heartfelt Laser* ability.
- This makes the **Corpse** technically have the most amount of abilities in game.
- The **Corpse** is quite similar and likely inspired from the Petrified, a *Tower Battles* enemy.
Update History: - **Bug**: Jester's defense dropping does not reduce **Molten Corpse's** defense.
- **Bug**: **Molten Corpse** is sometimes impossible to kill, softlocking the game.

- **Bug**: **Molten Corpse** will start for some enemies start moving if their non-**Molten Corpse** forms was killed during an ability. Once that ability ends as a **Molten Corpse**, it will begin walking.
- **Bugfix**: **Molten Corpse** no longer has a chance to be impossible to kill.

Description: The **Corrupted Conserver** was the final boss of Nil Zone as part of the first Halloween 2025 Live Event. It can currently only be accessed through Sandbox mode if the player has its Logbook. It had a high amount of health though it walked quite slowly. It was also a Boss enemy, granting it multiple immunities, making it significantly harder to slow down.

The **Conserver** has three abilities. Its first ability is *Spirit Release*, which makes it fire out multiple skulls from its body. These stun towers for 3 seconds while also applying a 40% Scared Debuff for 10 seconds. Towers will also have ghosts appear out of them. The second ability is *Summon*, which summons five Enigmas with a 0.3 delay between each, ten Actor2s with a 0.8 delay and five Unknown Bosses with a 0.8 delay, while also healing itself by 1,000. Its last ability, *Void Smash* makes it slam its club on the ground, creating multiple thorns that stun any tower hit for 4 seconds.
Appearance: The **Corrupted Conserver's** body is made entirely out of what appears to be purple molten slag or lava. It wears black armor, which covers most of its body. Its helmet has multiple horns. Additionally, it has spikes seen around its head that resemble teeth. It wields a black club with neon purple insides, which has three eyes on it.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Nil Zone is listed instead.
- High DPS towers like the Golden Minigunner, Accelerator, Turret or Engineer are recommended against this.

- High range towers that cannot be stunned like the Ranger and Pursuit are also useful, as they can attack the **Corrupted Conserver** at all times while also being mostly unaffected by its Scared Debuff.
- The Commander and DJ Booth can be useful at providing boosts to your towers.
- The Medic can be used to shield your towers from stuns, but it cannot be used to shield them from the Scared Debuff. It can also provide boosts to towers it shields.

- The **Corrupted Conserver's** *Summon* ability will summon in high numbers of enemies, which due to them at best being 25% of the **Corrupted Conserver's** health can easily overwhelm your defenses.
- AOE towers like the Mortar or Rocketeer can be helpful, though do note that the ability contains Actor2s which are immune to Splash Damage.
- Stalling towers can be helpful as the enemies summoned on top of being quite strong are way faster than the **Corrupted Conserver**. Such towers include the Electroshocker and Toxic Gunner.
Trivia: - The **Corrupted Conserver** has one of the strongest summons in the entire game, as they have a total health of 273,500 with Defense and the healing of the ability accounted for, but not Enigma's summons.

- If Enigma summons are accounted for, the lowest possible value is five Actor1s without Bloated or Health Regen, which increases it to 288,500, while the highest is five Actor3s with Bloated, which increases it to 473,500.
Update History: - **Corrupted Conserver** removed from the main game, now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.
Notes: - ↑ Base health is 462,500; on Wave 15 always spawns with Bloated which doubles it.

Description: The **Corrupted Conserver** was the second boss that appeared in Containment as part of the Hexscape Event. It was a corrupted version of the Conserver, making it stronger in most cases. It had a high amount of health though it walked quite slowly. It was also a Boss enemy, granting it multiple immunities, making it significantly harder to slow down.
The **Corrupted Conserver** had three abilities:

- Its first ability was *Spirit Release*, which made it fire out multiple skulls from its body. These stunned towers for 3 seconds while also applying a 40% Scared Debuff for 10 seconds, including non-humanoid towers. Towers would also have ghosts appear out of them.
- The second ability was *Summon*, which summoned ten Forsaken Skull with a 0.3 delay between each and seven Bloated Hex Revenants with a 0.8 delay, while also healing itself by 1,000.
- Its last ability, *Void Smash* made it slam its club on the ground, creating multiple thorns that stunned any tower hit for 4 seconds.
Appearance: The **Corrupted Conserver's** body was made entirely out of what appears to be purple molten slag or lava. It wore black armor, which covered most of its body. Its helmet had multiple horns. Additionally, it had spikes seen around its head that resemble teeth. It wielded a black club with neon purple insides, which had three eyes on it.
Strategy: - High DPS Towers, such as the Accelerator, Engineer, Ranger and Golden Minigunner, are great choices when it comes to taking down the **Corrupted Conserver**. You should already have some of these towers placed down by the time the **Corrupted Conserver** arrives, which makes it less of a threat.

- However, towers that are expensive to upgrade, such as the Turret, are not optimal against the **Corrupted Conserver**, due to it only giving $7,500 per 5% of its health lost. It is also not viable due to the limited space for towers to be placed.
- The Gatling Gun is also not viable, due to it being disabled in this event by the Gatling Gun Banned modifier that is applied on the Containment map.
- The DJ Booth is especially useful against the **Corrupted Conserver** due to its discount track, while also buffing nearby towers damage and range.
- The Commander also can be used to give a DPS boost.
- The **Corrupted Conserver** can reduce tower range by 40% for multiple seconds with its *Spirit Release* ability.
- This can be partially mitigated using the DJ Booth's Range Buffs, with its purple track providing the biggest buff.
- However, If DJ Booth’s purple track (25% Range Buff), with Ranger’s Range Buff (15%), this debuff will be removed entirely, but however, towers will not gain any benefit from this.
- The Medic can be useful at cleansing stuns from towers with its ability, though it cannot be used to remove debuffs applied by the **Corrupted Conserver**.
Update History: - **Corrupted Conserver** can no longer have its defense decreased.

Description: The **Corrupted Fallen** is a quick enemy that appears in Fallen mode. It also appears in The Takeover Event. It is a stronger version of the Fallen. It has a decent amount of health and a rather fast speed. The **Corrupted Fallen** also has the Health Regen attribute, meaning it regenerates 2% of its max health every two seconds.
The **Corrupted Fallen** can be spawned by the Fallen King with its *Summon* ability. The Awakened Fallen King was previously able to summon it using its *Army of Chaos* ability.
Logbook Description: "*Corrupted Fallen were both the King's and Queen's personal servants. They stood up closest to her during the sacrifice and witnessed her final moments. The corruption crawls across their bodies, slowly consuming them as time moves on. It doesn't seem that they are bothered by this, but regular Fallen tend to stay away from them.*"
Appearance: The **Corrupted Fallen** is a corrupted version of the Fallen. It has black skin. It wears a white blindfold and appears to be crying behind it. It has multiple blue spikes on its on its body. It has two arm-bands with chains attached to it.
Strategy: - The **Corrupted Fallen** is quite a step-up compared to its non-corrupted counterpart, the Fallen. While not having much of a step-up in HP, it spawns with the Health Regen attribute. This means that it should not be left on low health. Instead, it should be dealt with as soon as possible.
- Applying high DPS towers, like the Minigunner, Engineer, Accelerator and Turret can take it out with ease, as well as clearing out hordes of **Corrupted Fallens**.
- The Commander, DJ Booth and Mercenary Base can also be useful at boosting your towers.
- Area of effect towers, like the Mortar, Electroshocker or Rocketeer can be useful at clearing out the hordes of **Corrupted Fallens** that appear later on.

- Because of its high speed, slowing towers such as the Cryomancer, Tesla and Freezer can be used to negate their speed. Though since the **Corrupted Fallen** does not have any immunities, any tower can be used to slow it down.
- If any **Corrupted Fallens** leak, the Military Base can be used to catch any off-guard. Though long-ranged towers such as the Ranger can also be utilized.

**Corrupted Haz3mn** had three abilities that could be used at any time:

Description: **Corrupted Titus** is the final boss of Nil Zone II in Halloween 2026 Live Events, and previously appeared as a major boss in Containment as part of the Hexscape Event. It is the corrupted version of Titus; thus, its abilities are stronger. It has high health and a slightly slow speed. It renames itself to **Big Titus** via glitch effects on its boss HP bar.

It has two abilities. The first is *Void Stream*, targeting towers in proximity, diminishing them with a 60% Firerate Debuff (150% increase) and regenerating 10 health per tower inflicted. Its second ability was *Dark Decoy*, whichs summon five Neuro Runners and five Bloated Brain Bounds, all with a 0.2-second delay between each spawn; in addition, it also temporarily gains Aggro and Tank attribute, and a permanent 5% defense increase.
Appearance: **Corrupted Titus** has grey skin, with part of its face being purple with neon purple veins. Its right arm was replaced with a mechanical arm, and has three claws and a laser blaster around the gauntlet. It has grey hair. It wears a grey shirt and blue pants, and dark brown shoes. On its left arm, it has a metal shoulder-pad, multiple brown bandages and a brown glove with black brass knuckles with spikes. It also wore a grey bandana. On its torso, it has a large brown belt attached to a brown armor piece that protects its mechanical arm and to the torso. It has a brown belt with pouches and a grey plate with "*CRR6PT*" engraved on it. It also had grey knee-pads.
Strategy: - High DPS towers like the Ranger, Engineer or Accelerator are recommended against this. The Juggernaut and Kingpin given as part of the preset loadouts during the 2026 Nil Zone event are also highly effective.
- Support towers like the Commander or DJ Booth can be used to boost their statistics. The Commander can also be used to partially mitigate its Firerate Debuff.
- While defense dropping towers, like the Pyromancer or DJ Booth, can be used to drop its defense, this is not necessary as it is not that high, resulting in a minimal DPS increase.
- As it is a Boss enemy, it is significantly harder to slow down since multiple of its immunities either reduce the effectiveness of the slowdown or prevent it entirely.
Trivia: - The belt of **Corrupted Titus** wore had the nameplate "*CRR6PT*", which is a wordplay on the word "*corrupt*".
- **Corrupted Titus** was added to pay homage to the unused Corrupted Penumbras enemy that was intended for The Great Finale.
Update History: - **Bug**: Poison and electric defense dropping towers now can drop its defense.
- **Bug**: **Corrupted Titus** receives damage at rapid speed from unit collision, if the damage dealt is to its healed health.
- **Corrupted Titus** can no longer have its defense decreased.
- **Bugfix**: Poison and electric defense dropping towers now can drop its defense if it is not a Boss enemy, though the Jester still cannot drop it.
Notes: - ↑ Base health is 500,000; by default, it spawns with Bloated, which doubles its base health.

Description: The **Creator** was a major boss that appeared in the Legacy Hidden Wave. Because of that, this boss could only be fought in Fallen mode. For a major boss, the **Creator** moved quite quickly and had an insane amount of health that will test even the most experienced of players. The **Creator** could spawn enemies that could easily overwhelm you if you were not careful. It was also immune to being burnt by the Pyromancer, being stunned by the Electroshocker, being frozen by the Freezer, Frost Blaster or Level 3+ Sledger, and being slowed down by the Toxic Gunner.
Appearance: The **Creator** looked like one of BelowNatural's past avatars, the creator of the game, hence the name. It wore a dark purple Viking helmet, a black reflective bow-tie and has glowing purple eyes. It had reflective black skin and appeared to be faceless, aside from the glowing eyes. It wore a granite waistcoat that was dark blue, grey and purple. Its torso was granite purple while its legs were black granite. It had dark purple elbow-pads and two different gloves; one glove was the standard fingerless glove that most towers and enemies use and was also dark purple, while the other glove was longer and appeared to have fingers and was also black. It had dark grey knee-pads and black boots. It had twisted metal protruding from its lower torso and right leg.
Strategy: - Use what you would to defeat a very strong boss. This includes **Golden** Minigunners, Rangers, Turrets and Accelerators.

- The Commander and DJ Booth are a must for this boss, as they all support towers in defeating the **Creator**. If possible, try to constantly have the Commander's *Call to Arms* ability always active.

- The **Creator** is immune to being frozen by the Freezer, Sledger and Frost Blaster, and being stunned by the Electroshocker. It is also immune to being slowed down by the Toxic Gunner. None of these towers except the Electroshocker can slow down the **Creator**. They can however, be useful at slowing down the enemies summoned by the **Creator**.

- The **Creator** is also immune to burn damage from the Pyromancer, though normal (non-burn) damage can still harm it. However, as the Pyromancer deals very little non-burn damage, it is recommended to sell it once the **Creator** appears.
- The **Creator** can spawn enemies with incredibly high amounts of health, such as the Glitched Giant. Make sure you deal with them alongside the **Creator**.
- The **Creator** can stun towers with its *Stomp* and *Lightning* move. If you have a tower slot for it, consider using the Medic's ability.
- Cliff towers, like the Ranger, can be stunned by the *Stomp* ability despite them being immune to most other stomps.
- Units are not harmed by the **Creator's** *Stomp*.
Trivia: - The **Creator** is a reference to BelowNatural's "official" outfit.
- When the **Creator** spawned, it waved its arms in the air and screams.
- This was somewhat similar to the Void from *Tower Battles*.
Update History: - Speed increased from Extremely Slow to Slow.
- Speed decreased from Slow to Very Slow (1.25).
- Burn Immunity and Freeze Immunity added.
- Summoned enemies no longer give money when damaged.
- **Bug**: **Stomp** ability's animation did not play; shockwave created was not visible.
- **Creator** can no longer be slowed down by the Toxic Gunner.
- **Creator** now appears in the legacy Hidden Wave, which is exclusive to Sandbox mode.
- *Summon* can no longer summon Developer 1, Developer 2 and Developer 3.
- Due to changes made with updates, Energy Immunity has been replaced with Stun Immunity.
- **Bugfix**: **Stomp** ability animation works again; shockwave is also now visible again.
- **Creator** no longer appears in the legacy Hidden Wave, as it has been removed.

crying_angel_krampus_frosthold.name: Crying Angel

notice.text: Crying Angel (Krampus Frosthold) has been removed from the game as of the 31st of January 2024 as it was part of the Krampus' Revenge Event.

Description: The **Crying Angel** was an enemy that first appeared in the second phase of Krampus Frosthold as part of the Krampus' Revenge Event. For its debut, it had a medium amount of health and a below average speed. It was also a Flying enemy, meaning that you needed to use towers with flying detection to kill it. It was immune to being frozen and slowed down by freezing towers.
It could be spawned by the Krampus from its *Secret Santa* ability.
Appearance: The **Crying Angel** was entirely made out of translucent blue ice. Its torso and legs were darker than its head and arms. It had two light blue wings connected to its torso with blue chains, which were wrapped around its torso. It also had a light blue spiked halo floating above its head.
Strategy: - The Ace Pilot and Pursuit can deal great amounts of damage to this enemy.
- Keep in mind that due to the speed of **Crying Angels**, they can escape the range of these two towers.
- The Mortar can clear out hordes of **Crying Angels** quickly, while also dealing a lot of damage to other enemies that appear.
- Multiple Golden Soldiers can be very effective against this.
- A couple Level 0 Rangers can kill the **Crying Angel** pretty easily, due to their high range and damage.
- A couple of Electroshockers can clear out hordes of **Crying Angels** due to their chaining, although keep in mind their low firerate, low range and the speed of the **Crying Angels**.
- While towers with flying detection are the only consistent way to kill **Crying Angels**, other towers can damage them indirectly.

- With the exception of the Mortar, Ace Pilot and Pursuit, explosive towers cannot detect the **Crying Angel**. If another enemy that can be detected by such a tower is present, then the **Crying Angel** can be damaged, so long it is within the explosion radius.
- The **Crying Angel** can get hit if it is in chain reaction with the Electroshocker even before it is at Level 2.
- The Sledger and Gladiator will be able to hit the **Crying Angel** if another detectable enemy is nearby as their hitboxes can hit the **Crying Angel**.
Trivia: - The **Crying Angel's** name may be based on the Weeping Angel from *Doctor Who*.
- On the 24th of December 2023, it was stated officially that the **Crying Angel's** health was lowered, despite no actual change occurring.
- The **Crying Angel's** wings were uploaded to the Roblox catalog as the Crying Angel Wings UGC accessory.

Description: The **Crying Angel** was an enemy that appeared exclusively in Outpost 32 as part of the Frost Invasion Event. Currently, it can only appear in Sandbox mode. For its debut, it had a low amount of health, but it had a somewhat fast speed. The **Crying Angel** was also a Flying enemy, meaning that ground towers and units could not detect it, though some units could collide with it.
Upon its death, the Frost Mystery had a chance to spawn the **Crying Angel**, from wave 19 onwards.
Appearance: The **Crying Angel** is entirely made out of dark grey granite, from head to legs. It has two dull blue wings with chains across its wings. The **Crying Angel** also has a neon blue outline around its body, plus it has a neon blue halo above its head. As a Flying enemy, it hovered a distance above the ground. Its head was slightly tilted downwards.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Outpost 32 is listed instead.
- Only cliff and air-based towers can target the **Crying Angel**.
- However, explosions can indirectly hit the **Crying Angel**.

- With the exception of the Mortar, Ace Pilot and Pursuit, explosive towers cannot detect the **Crying Angel**. If another enemy that can be detected by such a tower is present, then the **Crying Angel** can be damaged, so long it is within the explosion radius.
- Be aware that the projectile explodes on the ground. At low levels, the Mortar may only deal small amounts of damage to the **Crying Angel**.
- A Level 5 Pyromancer can set the **Crying Angel** on fire, so long another detectable enemy is nearby.
- Any Pyromancer at a lower level will not be able to set the **Crying Angel** on fire as its flames will be too small to hit them.
- As with all enemies in the Frost Invasion Event, the Pyromancer deals double fire damage to the **Crying Angel** (though normal damage is not doubled).
- Ace Pilots and Pursuits deal great amounts of damage to this enemy.
- A couple of Ace Pilots fare well against the **Crying Angel**.
- Snipers and Rangers can be an option against the **Crying Angel**, though do be aware of limited cliff space near the start of the map.
- Some ground towers like the Electroshocker and Gladiator can hit the **Crying Angel**.
- The **Crying Angel** can get hit if it is in chain reaction with the Electroshocker.
- The Sledger and Gladiator will be able to hit the **Crying Angel** is another detectable enemy is nearby as their hitboxes can hit the **Crying Angel**.

- The Archer and Slasher (through its passive *Knife Throw* ability) can hit the **Crying Angel**, so long the Frost Spirit is nearby, since these towers will aim upwards, which can hit the **Crying Angel**
- Units (from the Crook Boss and Military Base) cannot detect the **Crying Angel** as it is a flying enemy.
- However, units from the Crook Boss can collide and deal damage to the **Crying Angel** through its collision.
- The Military Base's units cannot collide with the **Crying Angel** at all.
Trivia: - The **Crying Angel's** name may be based on the Weeping Angel from *Doctor Who*.
- The **Crying Angel's** wings are the Chained Angel Wings accessory from the Roblox catalog.
- The **Crying Angel** looks somewhat similar to the Frost Spirit without its robe.

Eventually, crystals will sprout from their bodies and solidify into a large solid mass while keeping their soul core intact. They are almost entirely immune to damage except in specific circumstances, and are widely feared among the army. Even so, they keep a careful watch over the wandering Souls, and will actively check to make sure none stray a bit too far.*"
Appearance: The **Crystalian** is an entity made out of black stone and purple crystals. It has multiple spikes protruding from its body and white eyes on its head. It has a hole in its torso, exposing its gem. This gem is the main source of its power, which it uses to fire beams at towers.
Strategy: - Various abilities like *Call to Arms* or *Ubercharge* are best used while it is using *Heartfelt Ray*, as it does not have Tank during it.

- Towers that have a high firerate, like the Juggernaut, Golden Minigunner and Turret are recommended against the **Crystalian**, due to them being able to attack it more frequently when it still has the Tank attribute.
- Towers that can summon Units, such as the Crook Boss, Kingpin and Mercenary Base can deal normal collision damage to the **Crystalian**, as collision damage bypasses Tank.
- The Units can deal more damage with their ranged attacks as well.
Trivia: - The **Crystalian** was originally called the *Crystalline*.
- The **Crystalian** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - Cash given on death decreased from $30,000 to $20,000.
Notes: - ↑ https://x.com/squeeezewhiz/status/2063833534717190324

crystalite.name: Crystalite
crystalite.description: The Crystalite was an enemy that appeared exclusively in The Heights as part of the SFOTH Event. It had the same speed as the Normal Boss and Necromancer.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Explode** - The **Crystalite** will, upon its death, create a bile bubble which stuns nearby towers upon its death.

Description: The **Crystalite** was an enemy that appeared exclusively in The Heights as part of the SFOTH Event. It had the same speed as the Normal Boss and Necromancer. It also had more health than the Necromancer and Normal Boss (and far more than the Stone Viking). Upon its death, the **Crystalite** would create a small bile bubble, which would stun nearby towers.
Appearance: Compared to the average enemy, the **Crystalite** had quite an unusual design as it had four light grey legs, with three black claws on each. It had a grey neck and a light grey head with white glowing eyes. It had a smile face, but did not have any arms. There were also white glowing horns on the **Crystalite**. The **Crystalite** had two colored neon crystals on its neck, one being yellow and the other being blue, and a pink crystal chunk on its front left leg.
Strategy: - If you can, try to kill the **Crystalite** away from towers, so when the **Crystalite** is killed, fewer towers will be stunned.
- Long-range towers, such as the Outlaw and John, can be used as they can be placed away from the path, not getting affected by the **Crystalite's** stun.
- The **Crystalite's** higher health means that high DPS towers, such as the Outlaw and Minigunner, are recommended.
- The Freezer and Pyromancer are useful in slowing down the **Crystalite**.
- The Freezer's *Freeze Drop* ability can be used to slow down hordes of **Crystalites**, giving more time for your towers to attack it.
Trivia: - The **Crystalite** was a re-skin of the Carrier and it performed a similar ability to the Carrier, except that the **Crystalite** did not spawn other enemies.
- Both were added at the same time.
- **Crystalite** was a portmanteau of the words "crystal" and "stalactite".

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Spooking Flash** - Upon death, the **Cursed Horror** explodes, creating a shockwave underneath that stuns towers for 2 seconds and deals 100 damage to units.

Description: The **Cursed Horror** was a large, Flying enemy that appeared in Containment as part of the Hexscape Event. It had a decent amount of health and a quite fast speed. Upon death, it would explode as an electric orb, creating a shockwave, stunning any tower for two seconds and damaging any unit caught from it by 100. It also had the Stun Immunity, Freeze Immunity and Burn Immunity.
Appearance: The **Cursed Horror** was a giant, flying beast with an exposed skull. It had a tail and what appeared to be hair. Its skull was grey and has yellow lights in its eyeholes.
Strategy: - Due to its high health and fast speed, towers with flying detection and high DPS are recommended.

- The Ranger is likely the best option, as it is immune to its stuns and has quite large range, allowing it to cover the entire map. Other towers like the Engineer or Golden Crook Boss can also be effective.

- While it cannot collide with units due to it being a Flying enemy, it can still wreak havoc with its *Spooking Flash*, allowing it to deal damage to units on death, killing weaker units or weakening them.

- This is especially bad for units which stay on the path, leading to them stacking up, like units from the Crook Boss or some from the Mercenary Base, as a **Cursed Horror** that flies above such groups of units can easily damage or even kill them all.
- Because of its immunities, it cannot be frozen, knocked back, burned or chilled, while also only being slowed down by stuns.

- As it is a Flying enemy, there are not many towers that can detect it, meaning a lot of them with some exceptions, like the Hallow Punk or Electroshocker, would not be able to target it even if it was not immune.
Update History: - **Bug**: Poison and electric defense dropping do not decrease **Cursed Horror's** defense.
- **Bug**: **Cursed Horror** floats higher when its size gets changed.
- **Bugfix**: Poison and electric defense dropping now drops **Cursed Horror's** defense, though the Jester still cannot drop it.

- You should use slowing towers, like the Toxic Gunner, Sledger or Electroshocker to slow this enemy down due to its fast speed.
- Due to its short range, the Sledger may be less effective at slowing down this enemy compared to the other towers.

Description: The **Cursed Skeleton** is a health regenerating enemy that appears early on in Voidcore mode and far later in the waves in Hardcore mode. It has higher health and speed than the Hefty, though instead of Defense, it has Health Regen.
Logbook Description: "*Even in death one shall serve the Void. Corpses of those whose realms were devoured decompose in the peaceful quiet and are scavenged by Odds or Swifts. They are then brought back to the Void Caster as an offering, as she then attaches a Phantom or an Odd’s soul directly into it. Many of the Swifts, Heftys and Odds don’t like interacting with the Cursed Skeleton, as they fear what it would be like not having flesh.*"
Appearance: **Variant 1**
The **Cursed Skeleton** is a grey and purple skeleton which has vines, flowers and various other plants covering or growing inside of it. It has glowing purple eyes.
**Variant 2**

The legacy **Cursed Skeleton** is made entirely of blackish-purple parts that resemble a skeletal humanoid. It does not have a full torso, but instead has the bone cage for it. Its head is slightly smaller than most other enemies, and has two large glowing purple eyeholes. It also emits purple particles and the ends of its limbs are covered in a purple fluid.
It plays a bone shaking sound on death.
Strategy: - **Cursed Skeletons** can be easily dealt with by towers that deal a lot of damage, such as the Saboteur, Engineer, Crook Boss, Golden Crook Boss or Operator.
- As the **Cursed Skeleton** spawns in groups, splash damage towers such as the Mortar, Rocketeer and Golden Demoman can also be useful against it.

- The Bloated **Cursed Skeletons** on Wave 9 and 12 of Voidcore can be very challenging to deal with if DPS is lacking. It is recommended to use cost-efficient DPS towers to deal with them effectively.
Trivia: - The modern **Cursed Skeleton** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
- The legacy **Cursed Skeleton** is very similar to the Hallow Bones that appeared in the Halloween 2020 Event.
- It is also quite similar to the cursed enemies that appeared in the Solar Eclipse Event.
- The legacy **Cursed Skeleton's** death sound is similar to the Skeleton's hurt sound from *Minecraft*.

Description: The **Dancer** was an enemy that appeared in The Narratorium as a part of The Final Act Event. It had high health and average speed. It had both the Stun Immunity and Freeze Immunity, which made it harder to slow down.
Logbook Description: "*When Dancers take the stage, their fractured masks conceal the agonized expressions of those trapped behind them. Known for their flexibility, they practice endlessly until dance becomes the only movement their bodies can remember*."
Appearance: The **Dancer** is a dark creature which wears a red coat, tophat and shoes, all three with golden accents. On its tophat, it has a golden gear. It wears a white mask with red lipstick and cheeks. It carries a black and golden cane with its right hand.
Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in The Narratorium is listed instead.
- High DPS towers like the Accelerator, Mercenary Base, Golden Minigunner, Warlock or Ranger are recommended against this.
- Towers like the DJ Booth or Commander can be used to boost their statistics.
- As the **Dancer** has both the Stun Immunity and Freeze Immunity, knockback towers like the Brawler and freezing towers like the Freezer cannot be used on it.
- While stunning towers like the Electroshocker can still be used, they will only slow it down instead of fully stopping it.
- While the DJ Booth cannot knock it back, its slowdown is not affected by its immunities.

Description: The **Dark Necromancer** is a summoner enemy that only appears in the Legion and Juggernaut challenges, if the map chosen does not have the Enemies Beta modifier. It also appears in the Sandbox mode exclusive Legacy Fallen and Golden modes. It used to appear in Fallen mode, though it has been replaced by the Fallen Necromancer after its rework in August of 2024.

While the **Dark Necromancer** is slower than the Heavy, it has somewhat high health, more than the Abnormal Boss. Additionally, it can summon multiple enemies every few seconds, in groups of four. These enemies are the Abnormal, Quick, Heavy and Shadow. When Polluted Wasteland was in the game, the **Dark Necromancer** did not spawn the Heavy, and instead spawned the Radioactive.
The **Dark Necromancer** can be spawned from the Mystery Boss upon its death in Legacy Fallen mode and Golden mode.
The **Dark Necromancer** is replaced by the (Enemies Beta) Necromancer in any map with the Enemies Beta modifier active.
Appearance: **Variant 1**

The current version of the **Dark Necromancer** wears a black dominus. It has a light grey reflective skin color and is faceless. It has a black marble torso and legs, and wears a dark grey cloak with a cape and sleeves that have dark magenta rims. Its arms have navy pebble bandages. It wears grey diamond-plated shoes and has light grey chains wrapped around its torso and arms. It wields a grey summoning staff with a magenta orb on top. It walks hunchbacked and has a twisted left leg.
**Variant 2**

The first version of the **Dark Necromancer** had a light grey skin color and a light grey torso with darker grey legs. It had a dark navy dominus with a ripped cloak that was connected to its legs, and its head was concealed by darkness. It had grey skull shoulder-pads with glowing light red eyes. It wielded a slightly retextured version of the Zombie Staff gear.
Strategy: - The **Dark Necromancer** can be a slight threat when it first appears. Towers like the Minigunner, Ace Pilot, Shotgunner and Cowboy can easily wipe out the **Dark Necromancer** and its summoned enemies.
- High DPS towers like the Accelerator or Turret can also be used, though they are quite expensive to upgrade.

- You can set these towers to target *Strongest* so that they will target the **Dark Necromancer** first, before moving onto its summoned enemies, although this is not required due to the lack of health its summons may have.
- Area of effect towers, like the Mortar, Rocketeer, Gladiator or Electroshocker can be quite useful as they can both damage the **Dark Necromancer** and the enemies it summons.
- Do note that you do not earn any money from the summoned enemies.
Trivia: - The staff wielded by the original **Dark Necromancer** was a re-textured version of the Zombie Staff gear from the Roblox catalog.
- The cape used by the current **Dark Necromancer** is a re-textured version of the Guardian of the Night Cape accessory from the Roblox catalog.
- A statue of the **Dark Necromancer** could be seen on one of the cliffs in Trick or Threat Town.
Update History: - Speed increased from Slow to Above Average.

Description: The **Deep Freeze** is a Lead enemy that appears in the Frost mode. Like most of that mode's enemies, it first appeared in the Operation I.C.E Event. It has a decent amount of health and average speed. As it is a Lead enemy, only towers with lead detection can damage it. Additionally, it also has the Stun Immunity, making it harder to stall.
Logbook Description: "*The Deep Freeze is a formidable addition to the Frost Army. These slow but sturdy creatures clear paths for smaller units. Protected by reinforced armor as they travel the battlefield, Deep Freezes are natural frontline leaders in combat.*"

This armor is grey and dark grey with a few blue spikes coming out of it on its shoulders and the helmet. It also has visible fingers on its armor. Upon its death, it will fall to the ground and its helmet will fall of, revealing its black head and blue horns.

Description: The **Deep Freeze** was an enemy that appeared exclusively in Outpost 32 as part of the Frost Invasion Event. It can now only appear in Sandbox mode. It had a high amount of health, but walked slowly. It also had 50% defense which reduced most forms of damage. The **Deep Freeze** could not be frozen as it had Freeze Immunity.
Appearance: The **Deep Freeze** has baby blue skin, and white snow textured torso and legs. A tumor can be seen on its head. White spikes can be seen coming out of its shoulders. White ice chunks can be seen sticking out of its arms and legs. Its head is slightly tilted downwards and had a twisted left leg.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Outpost 32 is listed instead.
- You should use high DPS towers, like the Accelerator, Ranger, Minigunner or Turret, to defeat the **Deep Freeze**.
- However, be aware that due to the 50% defense, it will take longer than normal to defeat the **Deep Freeze**.
- You may want to use the Commander's *Call to Arms* ability to boost the firerate of these towers.
- Defense is ignored by splash damage, meaning that towers and units that deal splash damage will do 100% damage if the **Deep Freeze** is caught in the epicenter.
- This makes towers like the Rocketeer and Mortar very useful against the **Deep Freeze**.
- Upon collision, units, like the Railgun Tank, will ignore defense and deal full collision damage towards the **Deep Freeze**.
- As the **Deep Freeze** has quite high defense, you can use a Level 2 Pyromancer to lower its defense, allowing your towers to deal more damage to it.
- Additionally, as with all enemies in the Frost Invasion Event, the Pyromancer deals double fire damage to the **Deep Freeze** (though normal damage is not doubled).
- You can also use other defense dropping towers, like the Electroshocker or Freezer. However, these are more expensive and less effective as they only drop 20% defense.
- The **Deep Freeze** cannot be frozen by the Freezer, Frost Blaster or Sledger.
- If you want to slow the **Deep Freeze** down, then you must use the Electroshocker or Toxic Gunner.
Trivia: - This version of the **Deep Freeze** was quite similar to the Deep Freeze from Village of Despair in appearance.
- Another version of the Deep Freeze existed prior to the MEGA Update that has since been removed, though that version looked very different to this version of the **Deep Freeze**.
Update History: - **Deep Freeze** can now be summoned in Sandbox mode, only when the player has the Deep Freeze's Logbook from the Operation I.C.E Event.
- **Bug**: **Deep Freeze** has no health in Sandbox, causing it to break.
- No longer copies the statistics of the modern version in Sandbox mode.
- **Bugfix**: **Deep Freeze** no longer breaks, as it now has health in Sandbox mode.

deep_freeze_village_of_despair.name: Deep Freeze
deep_freeze_village_of_despair.description: The Deep Freeze was an ice elemental enemy. It appeared in Village of Despair as part of the Christmas 2019 Event.

notice.text: Deep Freeze (Village of Despair) has been removed from the game as of the 26th of January 2020 as it was part of the Christmas 2019 Event.

Description: The **Deep Freeze** was an ice elemental enemy. It appeared in Village of Despair as part of the Christmas 2019 Event.

For its debut, the **Deep Freeze** had a high amount of health, higher than the Frozen. However, it walked quite slowly. The **Deep Freeze** could not be frozen by the Freezer and Frost Blaster as it had Freeze Immunity.
The **Deep Freeze** could also have been spawned by Krampus.
Appearance: The **Deep Freeze** was larger than the Frozen. It had blue skin, and its torso and legs were white marble. The **Deep Freeze** also had a spiky neckguard, while its back was also spiky. White ice chunks could be seen sticking out of the **Deep Freeze's** arms and legs. On the side of its head, a tumor could be seen.
Strategy: - The **Deep Freeze** is the first high health enemy you encounter in Village of Despair. Make sure you have enough Minigunners and Outlaws to deal with this.
- A Commander may also be required when you first encounter this.
- The **Deep Freeze** is slower than the Snowman and Burnt Gingerbread, meaning that those enemies can pass the **Deep Freeze** and act as a shield.
- In this case, it is best to have a Rocketeer on hand to defeat the weaker enemies.
- The **Deep Freeze** is completely immune to the Freezer and Frost Blaster, including the Freezer's *Ice Age*.
- If you want to slow it down, then you can use the Pyromancer.
Trivia: - While an enemy existed before the MEGA Update that was also called Deep Freeze, it had very little in common with this variant of the **Deep Freeze**.
- The Deep Freeze that appeared in Outpost 32 had a very similar appearance to this version of the **Deep Freeze**.

deep_freeze_premega.name: Deep Freeze
deep_freeze_premega.description: The Deep Freeze was an ice elemental enemy. Compared to the Frozen, the Deep Freeze was slightly slower, but it had more health.

notice.text: Deep Freeze (Pre-MEGA) has been removed from the game as of the 13th of October 2019.

Description: The **Deep Freeze** was an ice elemental enemy. Compared to the Frozen, the **Deep Freeze** was slightly slower, but it had more health. The **Deep Freeze** was immune to the Freezer's basic freeze, but not its *Ice Drop*.
Appearance: **Variant 1**

The second version of the **Deep Freeze** had sky blue skin and was faceless. Its torso and legs were marble blue. It also had rusty blue armbands. A tumor could be seen on the **Deep Freeze's** head.
**Variant 2**
This version of the **Deep Freeze** had blue skin and was faceless. Its torso and legs were black ice. It also had rusty blue armbands. A tumor could be seen on the **Deep Freeze's** head.
Strategy: - Rocketers and Demomen can easily wipe out hordes of **Deep Freezes**.
- The Outlaw, with the Commander's Firerate Buff, can also be helpful in defeating this.
- The Pyromancer can be used to slow the **Deep Freeze** down to allow your towers more time to kill it.
- Despite being an ice elemental enemy, this can be frozen by the Freezer's *Ice Drop* ability.
- However, the Freezer cannot freeze the **Deep Freeze** with its normal attack.
Trivia: - While enemies that used the same name as the **Deep Freeze** appeared in Village of Despair and Outpost 32, they had very little in common with this variant of the **Deep Freeze**.
- The **Deep Freeze** had the quickest appearance change in the entire game, with its appearance being changed later the same day it was added.
Update History: - **Bug**: **Deep Freeze** does not have Basic Freeze Immunity.
- **Bugfix**: Now has the Basic Freeze Immunity.

demon.name: Demon
demon.description: The Demon is an enemy that appears in Pizza Party, though only when summoned by the Reaper. It has a high amount of health, but it walks at an below average pace.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Unholy Martyrdom** - Spawns seven Sins upon death.

Description: The **Demon** is an enemy that appears in Pizza Party, though only when summoned by the Reaper. It has a high amount of health, but it walks at an below average pace. It has the Burn Immunity and Stun Immunity, making it immune to being set on fire, immune to being stunned, only slowed down and immune to knockback. Upon death, it summons seven Sins.
Apperance: The **Demon** is a large humanoid with a waist in its rig. It has a red skin tone and a dark red torso, waist, legs and a pair of wings made of magma. It has muscular arms and reddish-black horns with red stripes on its head.
The **Demon** has a death animation where it will kneel and reach for the sky before flashing red and turning into ash, with its body then disassembling and fading away.
Strategy: - High DPS towers, like the Pursuit, Engineer, Accelerator, Ranger or Turret are recommended against this.
- As it always spawns in groups and summons groups of enemies on death, high DPS towers with splash damage capabilities, like the Ranger, Pursuit or Engineer can be especially useful here.
- The Commander and DJ Booth can be used to boost the statistics of these towers.
- Area of effect towers, like the Mortar or Electroshocker can be helpful at clearing out the **Demons** and their Sins.
Trivia: - The amount of Sins spawned by the **Demon** upon death is a reference to the seven deadly sins.
- The **Demon** was originally going to have 6,666 health, referencing the number 666, which is famously known as the "*Number of the beast*".

demon_lunar_overture.name: Demon
demon_lunar_overture.description: The Demon was the second boss that appeared in the second act of the Lunar Overture Event, though only the first Demon that spawned considered as a Boss.

notice.text: Demon (Lunar Overture) has been removed from the game as of the 21st of December 2023 as it was part of the Lunar Overture Event.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Unholy Martyrdom** - Spawns seven Sins upon death.

Description: The **Demon** was the second boss that appeared in the second act of the Lunar Overture Event, though only the first **Demon** that spawned considered as a Boss. It was a high-health enemy with decent speed and multiple immunities, such as Burn and Stun immunities. While it was a boss enemy, it was also immune to being frozen by freezing towers and being slowed down by the Toxic Gunner, as well as 35% defense.

The **Demon** had one ability, where upon death it would kneel down and disintegrate, spawning seven Sins. The **Demon** could also be spawned by the Reaper, however, the **Demon** spawned had reduced health and a faster speed.
Apperance: The **Demon** was a large humanoid with a waist in its rig. It had a red skin tone and a dark red torso, waist, legs and a pair of wings made of magma. It had muscular arms and reddish-black horns with red stripes on its head.
The **Demon** had a death animation where it would kneel and reach for the sky before flashing red and turning into ash, with its body then disassembling and fading away.
Strategy: - High DPS towers, like the Accelerator, Minigunner or Pursuit are very useful against this.
- High DPS towers with the ability to hit multiple enemies at once, like the Pursuit or Ranger can hit multiple Sins that the **Demon** spawns on death at once, making it more effective against it.
- The Commander and DJ Booth can be useful at boosting their firerate and range respectively.
- Area of effect towers, like the Mortar or Executioner can be useful at clearing out the Sins spawned by the **Demon** upon its death.
- Defense dropping towers, like the Electroshocker or Freezer can be useful at decreasing the **Demon's** defense, though it is not necessary as they decrease its defense by a minimal amount.
- The Pyromancer and Golden Pyromancer should not be used as the **Demon** has Burn Immunity, meaning that it cannot be set on fire nor have its Defense reduced.
- When it first spawns on Wave 14, it is a boss enemy, therefore it cannot be frozen by freezing towers, slowed down by the Toxic Gunner or completely stopped by the Warden and Electroshocker.
- This also means that it is unaffected by the Witch's ability.
- After Wave 14, the **Demon** is no longer a boss, reducing its immunities to only being immune to the Warden's and Electroshocker's stun, only being slowed down by them.
Trivia: - The amount of Sins spawned by the **Demon** upon death is a reference to the seven deadly sins.
- When the **Demon** was spawned by the Reaper, the Sins that it spawned did not have their health decreased, making them have more health in total than the **Demon**.
Notes: - ↑ Only first **Demon** spawned as a boss.

demon_nightmare_carnival.name: Demon
demon_nightmare_carnival.description: The Demon was an enemy that appeared exclusively in Nightmare Carnival as part of the Halloween 2019 Event. Currently, it can only appear in Sandbox mode.

notice.text: Demon (Nightmare Carnival) was previously removed from the game on the 9th of November 2019 as it was part of the Halloween 2019 Event, though it has been made available through the Sandbox mode.

Description: The **Demon** was an enemy that appeared exclusively in Nightmare Carnival as part of the Halloween 2019 Event. Currently, it can only appear in Sandbox mode. It can be considered the first non-major "boss" that appeared on the map due to its high health. It had more health than the Scarecrow, but was also slightly slower than it. The **Demon** was immune to the Pyromancer's burn (and therefore slowdown).
The **Demon** could have also been spawned by Jack O' Bot.
Appearance: **Variant 1**

The Demon has a red, hell-like appearance. It has a dark red granite torso and even darker granite red legs. Its head and arms are light red. It has dark red granite wings on its back and grey horns with red details on top of its head.
**Variant 2**
The first version of the **Demon** is similar to the second version, except it had a snarling demon face with red eyes.
Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Nightmare Carnival is listed instead.
- You should get as many Minigunners as soon as possible to deal with the **Demon** due to its health and high speed.
- You can use the Freezer to slow down the **Demon**.
- The Pyromancer cannot be used to slow this down. It can still attack the **Demon**, but it will only deal non-burn damage.
- The Military Base can help weaken the **Demon**, but it is not reliable enough as its units have a slow spawnrate.
Trivia: - The face used by the **Demon** was the Beast Mode face from the Roblox catalog.
- The **Demon** may loosely be based on *Tower Battles's* Demon.
Update History: - **Demon** can now be summoned in Sandbox mode, only when the player has the Demon's Logbook from Pizza Party.
- Due to changes made with updates, its face has been removed.
- No longer copies the statistics of the modern version in Sandbox mode.

dev.name: Dev
dev.description: The Dev was an enemy that appeared in Pls Donate as part of the Tower Defense Simulator x PLS DONATE Event.

notice.text: Dev has been removed from the game as of the 4th of December 2024 as it was part of the Tower Defense Simulator x PLS DONATE Event.

Description: The **Dev** was an enemy that appeared in Pls Donate as part of the Tower Defense Simulator x PLS DONATE Event. It had a high amount of health, quite high defense and also an average speed. It was Freeze Immune and Stun Immune.
Appearance: The **Dev** had pale skin. It wore a black shirt with a white Roblox logo, black pants and shoes. It had a yellow and blue construction helmet and it had a hammer in its right hand.
Strategy: - High DPS towers like the Minigunner, Engineer or Mercenary Base are quite useful against this.
- As it has quite high defense, defense dropping towers like the Pyromancer or Electroshocker can be effective against this.
- As it has Freeze Immunity, freeze defense dropping towers cannot be used.
Trivia: - This enemy's name is a shortening of the word developer, as this enemy is based on Roblox developers.
- It wore the Builders Club Hard Hat on its head.
- The **Dev** originally had a slightly different appearance. It was significantly larger, bigger than the Breaker4, it had a different shirt and walked differently.
Update History: - **Bug**: Jester's defense dropping does not reduce **Dev's** defense.

Description: The **Ducky** was the first enemy appeareds in Bathroom Approach as part of the Ducky Revenge Event and its rerun in the Spring Frenzy Battle Pass. It has medium health and average speed.
The **Ducky** can be spawned by Eggroll 1, Eggroll 2 and Eggroll 3.
Logbook Description: "*A new duckling filled with gentle quacks and boundless possibilities. Could they become an Agent? A Pilot? A Spy? The road ahead is bright with few obstacles in their path. With determination in their heart and curiosity in their eyes, they waddle forward into countless adventures. The future holds endless potential!*"
Appearance: The **Ducky** is a normal, yellow duck with an orange beak and orange flippers. It has three animations that it can randomly have, where all three also have differently shaped eyes. The first animation has it have a happy expression, the second has it have a serious expression while the third one has its eyes partially closed, likely because it is scared.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Bathroom Approach is listed instead.
- The **Ducky** itself is quite weak, though it generally spawns in high numbers.
- Area of effect towers like the Pyromancer or Mortar are effective at clearing them out.
- Single target DPS towers can also be useful here, such towers include the Cowboy, Engineer or Ace Pilot.
- Later on, high DPS towers like the Pursuit, Ranger or Minigunner can deal with it quite easily.
Trivia: - The **Ducky** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Bug**: **Ducky** clips into the ground when made larger or smaller.
- **Ducky** removed from the main game, now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.
- **Ducky** re-added to the main game, now appears in Bathroom Approach.
- Health decreased from 6 to 4 in Easy difficulty.
- Speed increased from Average (3) to Above Average (3.5).
- Cash given increased from $8 to $16 on death in Easy difficulty.
- Cash given increased from $10 to $16 on death in Hard difficulty.
- **Bugfix**: No longer clips into the ground when made larger or smaller.
- **Ducky** removed from the main game, now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.

Description: The **Ducky** was an enemy that appeared exclusively in D00M's Revenge as part of the Duck Hunt Event. Currently, it can be spawned again in Sandbox mode. It had low health and an above average speed, but to compensate, it spawned in high numbers. Beyond wave 10, its health would increase over time.
The **Ducky** could be spawned by the Eggroll.
Appearance: The **Ducky** is a normal yellow duck with black eyes and an orange beak and feet.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in D00M's Revenge is listed instead.
- Cheap towers like the Soldier and Golden Scout fare well against the **Ducky**.
- Multiple Snipers are recommended for their long range. In addition, the Sniper can also counter the Flying Ducky that debuts later on in the game.
- As many of these spawn, towers that can damage multiple enemies at once, like the Executioner, can clear out hordes of this enemy.
- Like the Sniper, the Executioner can counter the Flying Ducky. Do be aware that its hidden detection is too expensive to deal with Spy Duckies, a hidden enemy that debuts later on in the game.
Trivia: - After the Duck Hunt Event ended, the **Ducky** could be seen in the lobby, floating on the small stream that surrounded the wooden Minigunner statue in some iterations of the lobby.
- This enemy can be seen in some of the **Ducky** skins, like the Farm, Accelerator and Mortar.

ducky_d00m_d00ms_revenge.name: Ducky D00M
ducky_d00m_d00ms_revenge.description: Ducky D00M was the final boss for D00M's Revenge as part of the Duck Hunt Event. It held a very high amount of health with an above average speed.

notice.text: Ducky D00M (D00M's Revenge) has been removed from the game as of the 28th of May 2022 as it was part of the Duck Hunt Event.

stats.Attributes:
- Energy Immune
- Boss Immunities:
  - Freeze Immunity
  - Energy Immunity
  - Poison Slowdown

abilities.label: Ability 1
abilities.text: **Rocket Barrage** - **Ducky D00M** fires a barrage of rockets into the air which crash into the ground, stunning towers within the rockets' explosions. Can only be used after *Rage Mode* is activated.

abilities.label: Ability 2
abilities.text: **Chainsaw Dash** - **Ducky D00M** pulls out a chainsaw and dashes towards the base dealing 100 damage and stunning towers that get hit. If **Ducky D00M** is close to the center of the map, it may maneuver to hit more towers.

abilities.label: Ability 3
abilities.text: **Trundle** - A passive ability that causes towers to be stunned if **Ducky D00M** ran over them.

abilities.label: Ability 4
abilities.text: **Minigun Spray** - **Ducky D00M** fires its miniguns underneath its wings, which stuns any towers hit. Can only be used after *Rage Mode* is activated.

abilities.label: Ability 5
abilities.text: **Nerd n' Shotgun** - **Ducky D00M** fires its side guns, which produces a shotgun-like spray of bullets, stunning towers hit and dealing at least 50 damage to units.

abilities.label: Ability 6
abilities.text: **Nerd Laughter** - **Ducky D00M** squeals loudly, shaking the camera.

abilities.label: Ability 7
abilities.text: **Rage Mode** - At half health, it squeals for a medium duration, its body extends further from the tread-tracks and it gains the ability to use *Rocket Barrage* and *Minigun Spray*. Three P3NGUs spawn in.

Description: **Ducky D00M** was the final boss for D00M's Revenge as part of the Duck Hunt Event. It held a very high amount of health with an above average speed. Uniquely, it could not spawn until the last plot of land was cleared, which prevented it from spawning in perpetuity.

**Ducky D00M** is unique in that, like P3NGU, it did not directly try to reach the base. Instead, it would circle around the map, firing off its abilities, only directly attacking the base with its *Chainsaw Dash* ability.

- **Ducky D00M** had seven abilities. Its first ability, the *Rocket Barrage* ability, caused **Ducky D00M** to fire off a barrage of rockets in certain directions. Towers caught in the rockets' explosions were stunned. This could only happen during its *Rage Mode* ability.
- Its second ability, the *Chainsaw Dash* ability, made it retract out two chainsaws as it charged towards the base, dealing 100 damage, and stunned any towers that it ran over during this ability.
- Its third ability, the *Trundle* ability, was a passive ability that simply caused towers to be stunned if run over by **Ducky D00M**.
- Its fourth ability, the *Minigun Spray* attack, made **Ducky D00M** spray its miniguns at towers, which stunned them. This could only happen during its *Rage Mode* ability.

- Its fifth ability, the *Nerd n' Shotgun* ability, caused **Ducky D00M** to fire its side guns, which shot out bullets in a shotgun-like fashion, which stunned towers and dealt at least 50 damage to units.
- Its sixth ability, the *Nerd Laughter* ability, caused **Ducky D00M** (or the "nerd") to squeal loudly, which simply shook the camera, disorienting players.

- Its seventh and final ability is its *Rage Mode* ability. At half health, it gained its ability to use the *Rocket Barrage* and *Minigun Spray* attacks mentioned before. Three P3NGUs were also spawned in when *Rage Mode* was activated.
Appearance: **Ducky D00M** was a giant robot duck armored with steel plates. On its head there were two big red horns and two smaller ones behind it. It had glowing red eyes and an orange beak. On its stomach was a hatch, which when opened showed a yellow duck with black eyes, orange beak and black glasses that controlled **Ducky D00M** using numerous levers inside of the torso. The duck that controlled **Ducky D00M** was described as a "nerd". It walked with treaded feet, with legs that could extract. On its wings, there were two blasters that were used to attack towers. There were also two miniguns and two quad missile launchers under its wings. Upon activating *Rage Mode*, **Ducky D00M's** body extended itself further from the tread-tracks.
Strategy: - It is recommended to stall **Ducky D00M** from spawning to give yourself more time to place and upgrade towers.
- You can stall **Ducky D00M's** spawn by leaving one plot of land not purchased. You can purchase it later when you are ready.
- This is generally not necessary, as you will get a lot of cash from **Ducky D00M** itself along with passive income.

- Do note that, if you decide to stall the game for about half an hour, the game will begin spawning only P3NGUs, which combined with their absurdly high health will render the game practically impossible.
- Due to its *Chainsaw Dash* ability, it is recommended to keep as much health as possible. It is not recommended to let some enemies leak early on due to this ability.
- Placing Medics earlier on to heal any lost health ensures that enough health may be kept for the *Chainsaw Dash*.
- However, do note that after **Ducky D00M** spawns, no more health can be healed back.
- Towers with high DPS, like the Minigunner, Pursuit, Ranger, and Accelerator are highly recommended for defeating **Ducky D00M**.
- The Commander can be used to decrease the firerate of these towers. Its *Call to Arms* ability should be used when **Ducky D00M** is in range of your towers.
- Additionally, the DJ Booth can be very useful in increasing these towers' range so that **Ducky D00M** stays in the range of your towers for longer.
- The Ranger is highly recommended as **Ducky D00M** often walks out of range of most ground towers. The Ranger has a high enough range to cover the whole map and constantly attack **Ducky D00M**.
- The Pursuit can also be useful as its large circling range allows it to reach **Ducky D00M** while it is in the outskirts of the map.
- They are recommended to be set to *Strongest* to help kill **Ducky D00M** faster instead of wasting shots on weaker enemies.
- The Medic can be very useful at cleansing stuns caused by **Ducky D00M** and other enemies, such as from P3NGU or the Long Ducky.
Trivia: - **Ducky D00M** is a new version of Ducky D00M that appeared in Eggy Island during Spring 2020 Event, which is controlled by Ducky D00M's son (the "nerd") that has come for revenge.
- **Ducky D00M** has the fastest speed for a major boss in the game, beating even the Void Reaver during its *Void's Deathwish* ability.

- **Ducky D00M** could destroy objects on the D00M's Revenge map by running into them. These included the trees and the table with a sign listing prices for food. This was purely visual and did not affect gameplay.

Description: **Ducky D00M** (or **Ducky Doom**) was a major boss and the final enemy to appear in Eggy Island as part of the Spring 2020 Event. It appeared on wave 10 in easy mode and wave 15 in hard mode. **Ducky D00M** had 10,000 health in easy mode and 100,000 health in hard mode. It walked at an extremely slow speed, akin to the Raider Boss.

Even though **Ducky D00M** walked at a slow speed, it had two very powerful moves that could leave your towers immobilized. The *Ground Pound* ability involved **Ducky D00M** jumping up, doing a backflip and creating a large shockwave, stunning towers nearby. The *Dual Miniguns* ability involved **Ducky D00M** pulling out two miniguns from under its wings and shooting at towers in one direction. Any towers hit by the lasers from the miniguns would be stunned. Both of these moves disabled towers for about 20 seconds.
Appearance: **Ducky D00M** was a large black duck with mechanical legs. It was larger than the average enemy. Underneath both of its wings, it had orange four barreled miniguns. **Ducky D00M** had an orange beak with two teeth sticking out. It had red menacing eyes and red devil horns.
Strategy: **Easy Mode**
- The Minigunner is the only effective option against **Ducky D00M**.
- The Commander will greatly help with defeating **Ducky D00M**.
- The Pyromancer cannot slow down **Ducky D00M**. Sell it when only **Ducky D00M** is left.
**Hard Mode**
- Minigunners, Turrets and Outlaws are all effective against **Ducky D00M**.
- Having large amounts of Minigunners is a viable option as **Ducky D00M** stuns lots of towers at once.
- If there is a large amount of Minigunners, it is likely that many will not be stunned after **Ducky D00M** uses its abilities.
- The Commander, DJ Booth and John are good support towers to bring against this boss to boost your towers.
- You can use the Medic's ability to cleanse all towers when stunned as the Medic is immune to all of **Ducky D00M's** attacks.
- The Pyromancer, Frost Blaster and Freezer (including the Freezer's *Ice Age* ability) are unable to slow down **Ducky D00M**.
- However, you can use the Electroshocker to slow down **Ducky D00M**.
- Interestingly, **Ducky D00M** is slowed down by 30%, not 15% experienced by other major bosses, like the Fallen King. This makes the Electroshocker quite an effective tower against this boss.
Trivia: - **Ducky D00M** was the first event boss with different health based on difficulty.
- Other event bosses had variable health, like the Swordmaster and Raider Boss, based on the number of players in the game.
- **Ducky D00M's** *Dual Miniguns* attack was similar to the Templar's attack, except **Ducky D00M** used two miniguns instead of just one.
- This boss could be considered a merge between *R2DA's* Pumpkinator and Ducky bosses.
- Most of **Ducky D00M's** design was modelled from the Evil Duck, which in turn was based on the Rubber Duckie, both being Roblox accessories.
- A new version of Ducky D00M appears in D00M's Revenge, though it is controlled by the son of the **Ducky D00M** which came for revenge.
Update History: - Can no longer stun the Medic.

Description: **Ducky D00M III**, internally referred to as **Ducky D00M 3**, was a Boss enemy that appeared in Bathroom Approach as part of the Ducky Revenge Event. It is the final boss of the Easy difficulty for the event, and the third Boss the player encounters in the Hard difficulty. It has a high amount of health, decent amount of Defense and a very slow speed.
**Ducky D00M III** has three abilities:

- The first one, *Rocket Barrage*, has it fire out 10 rockets from its rocket launchers at towers and units in its range of 30 and minimal range of 15. These rockets stun towers for 5 seconds, apply a 30% Fatigue Debuff to towers for 10 seconds and deal 500 damage per missile to units.

- The second ability is *Chainsaw Slash*, where it pulls out two chainsaws and starts breathing out fire at towers and units in its range of 10. This stuns towers for 6 seconds and deals 5,000 damage to units with each tick.

- The third and last ability is *Minigun Spray*, which makes it pull out two miniguns from under its wings and then begins firing at towers and units in its range of 20. This stuns towers for 8 seconds and deals 50 damage to units every 0.05 seconds.
Logbook Description: "*Ducky D00M is the creation of Nerd Duck that is geared towards getting revenge on the TDS team for deactivating their portal and causing their realm to suffer. With the help of the other ducklings and rough schematics, he managed to put together a weapon worthy of destroying his enemies.*"
Appearance: **Ducky D00M III** is a giant duck mech which in the Easy difficulty is powered by a God Cube fragment. It has a mostly black body with red legs and small grey metal reinforcements. On its torso, it has a small hatch, with the inside containing an operating room for the mech. On the sides of the torso, it has two wings, which contain hidden chainsaws, miniguns and rocket launchers, all used to attack towers and units. On its head, it wears a spiked helmet and a grey exhaust pipe. It has neon red eyes and an orange beak, out of which it can breathe out fire. It has grey treadmill feet which it uses to move on the path. These treadmills have spikes on them.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Bathroom Approach is listed instead.
- **Ducky D00M III** spawns on the orange path in the Hard difficulty and on the yellow path in the Easy difficulty.

- This means that in the Easy difficulty, you do not need to focus your DPS on the right side as much, though in the Hard difficulty you will need some defenses on the other side, as waves continue past Wave 20 and the Nerd Ducky can jump between sides.
- High DPS towers like the Ranger, Pursuit, Golden Minigunner, Turret or Accelerator are recommended against this.
- As the Ranger and Pursuit are stun immune, they are immune to most of its attacks except *Rocket Barrage*, as while stun immune, they are not fully debuff immune.
- The Commander and DJ Booth can be used to boost the DPS of these towers.
- Due to a bug, burn and freeze defense dropping towers, like the Pyromancer, Freezer or Cryomancer, can be used to drop its defense, allowing your towers to deal more damage to it.
- Other sources of defense dropping, these being the Electroshocker, Toxic Gunner and DJ Booth cannot be used, as they work as intended and do not decrease Boss enemy defense.
- The Medic can be used to shield towers from stuns, but it cannot be used to help with the Fatigue Debuff applied by **Ducky D00M III's** *Rocket Barrage* ability.
Trivia: - **Ducky D00M III** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Bug**: **Ducky D00M III** slightly floats above the ground when made larger or smaller.
- **Bug**: **Ducky D00M III** cannot have its defense dropped by the Jester.

- **Bug**: **Ducky D00M III** blocks tower placement around itself, even though it does not even physically cover up these parts of the map.

- Cash given changed from $1,750 every 1% health to $150,000 on death in Hard difficulty.

Description: The **Dummy Boss**, internally referred to as **TutorialBoss**, was the final boss for the Tutorial. Currently, it can only be spawned in Sandbox mode if the player has its Logbook. It had a high amount health and a quite slow speed. Additionally, as it was a Boss enemy, it had various immunities. This includes things like that it could not be frozen, only slowed down by stunning towers like the Electroshocker and Trapper, could not be slowed down by the Toxic Gunner, could not be confused by the Jester, it could not be knocked back, it could not be slowed down by the DJ Booth and it could not be damaged by the Nuke's fallout damage. However, since none of these effects could be used in the Tutorial, these immunities were not important.
Appearance: The **Dummy Boss** is a large hulking humanoid with a waist and lower arms in its rig. It has a pale green skin color, an orange torso, waist and legs, with the former having white stripes. It wears black shoes and has a black harness with white buckles. It also has black braces with white spikes and chains attached, along with indented lower arms. It also has two heads, with the left one being larger.
Whenever one of its fists hits the ground, the screen shakes. On death, the **Dummy Boss** will repeatedly bang its lower arms on its chest before falling forward onto the ground.
Strategy: This strategy refers to the state of the game while the **Dummy Boss** still appeared in the Tutorial.
- As this enemy only appears in the Tutorial, the only options are placing down multiple Snipers, Scouts, Demomans and Minigunners.
- The Minigunner happens to be the fastest way to beat it.
- If the player intentionally tries to lose, the match will not end in a loss. Instead, the player will triumph. This means it is impossible to lose against it through normal means.
- If you are trying to get its Logbook, the Scholar Skill cannot be used to boost the odds of getting it, as Skills are disabled in the Tutorial.
Trivia: - The **Dummy Boss** has the lowest health for a major boss in the entire game.
- The **Dummy Boss** is the first enemy to make the screen shake without an ability.
- The second enemy would be Patient Zero who shakes the screen whenever it takes a step after its *Index Case* ability is activated.
- The **Dummy Boss** has Stun Immunity. However, this immunity is useless as not a single tower available in the Tutorial can stun enemies, though it has use in Sandbox mode.
- The **Dummy Boss's** appearance is based on the Abomination from Polluted Wasteland II.
- The **Dummy Boss** is the first and currently only, major boss to have no abilities.
- The **Dummy Boss** shares its design with the Brute from Easy mode.
- Despite sharing the same design and icon, they are two seperate enemies and therefore give two separate Logbooks. This also means it is no longer possible to get it.
- The **Dummy Boss** drops the lowest cash upon death, being only $1 upon death.
Update History: - **Dummy Boss** can no longer be confused by the Jester.
- **Dummy Boss** is now immune to the fallout damage from the Nuke.
- **Dummy Boss** is now immune to knockback.

- **Bugfix**: No longer can be slowed down by the DJ Booth.

Description: The **Elite Abnormal** is an enemy that appears on Wave 9 of Intermediate mode, Wave 8 of Molten mode, Challenge Trials, Badlands II and Molten Arena PVP mode. It also appears in The Takeover Event. It serves as the first major threat to the mode, appearing as a bulky enemy with a decent defense. It debuts in this wave as a boss in Molten mode. It is a significantly stronger version of the Abnormal, having its health increased massively while walking at the same speed.
Appearance: The **Elite Abnormal**, akin to the Abnormal, has a desaturated green skin color with darker green veins running through. It has a muscular body. It wears torn dark shirt with two front pockets and pants. The sleeves and pant legs of these clothes are ripped in half. It also wears greay, spiked braces with chains connected to its sides.
Strategy: - While the **Elite Abnormal** has decent health while also being faster than other enemies with similar purpose, like the Normal Boss or Fallen Squire.
- Early-game towers with decent DPS, such as the Electroshocker, Militant, Golden Cowboy or Ace Pilot can be quite effective against this.
- Later on, high DPS towers like the Minigunner, Crook Boss or Hunter can kill this with ease.
- As it is quite fast, decent early-game towers with stalling capabilities like the Freezer or Electroshocker can be quite useful.
- Do note that it is significantly harder to slow down on Wave 8, as it is a Boss enemy on that wave.
- While defense dropping towers can be used to drop its defense, as it is quite low this is not necessary.
- If used, do note that as it spawns as a Boss enemy on Wave 8 in Molten mode, it can only have its defense dropped through burn or chillness.
Trivia: - While the dialogue on Wave 8 properly calls it the **Elite Abnormal**, the voiceline for that dialogue actually calls it the *Abnormal Boss*.
- Considering how similar the **Elite Abnormal** is to the Abnormal Boss, it is likely these actually shared their names at one point.
