elite_boomer.name: Elite Boomer
elite_boomer.description: The Elite Boomer is an enemy from Molten mode that explodes upon its death, which debuffs towers caught in the bile bubble.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Weakening Bile** - Upon its death, the **Elite Boomer** explodes into a bile bubble that applies a 50% Fatigue Debuff and 17.5% Range Debuff for 10 seconds and deals 600 damage to units in a radius of 10.

Description: The **Elite Boomer** is an enemy from Molten mode that explodes upon its death, which debuffs towers caught in the bile bubble. It has average health but slightly fast speed.
When killed, it creates a large explosion with a radius of 10. This applies a 50% Fatigue Debuff and 17.5% Range Debuff for 10 seconds. It also deals 600 damage to units.
Appearance: The **Elite Boomer** has green skin. It has a bloated chest and stomach, with multiple tumors also being visible across its body. It wears multiple pieces of armor, including light yellow shoulder-pads, chestplate and helmet, with a few tubes on its arms. On its chest, it has multiple light yellow explosives attached to it with red neon lights, strapped to it with grey bandages. On its arms, it also has grey bandages.
Strategy: - The **Elite Boomer** is quite fast, allowing it to quickly get to your towers and debuff them.
- Additionally, it often times spawns alongside other, at times faste, which distract the towers from the **Elite Boomer** and allowing it to get closer to your towers.
- Killing the **Elite Boomer** before it gets within range of your towers is the most ideal way to deal with **Elite Boomers**. Keep in mind that it has quite a long debuff time.
- Placing your towers away from the path is a good way to avoid the **Elite Boomer's** debuff.
- Long-range towers, such as the Turret are the best at keeping a distance away from the **Elite Boomer**.
- The Engineer's sentries can also be useful, as the sentries cannot be debuffed.
- The DJ Booth allows towers to shoot the **Elite Boomer** from further away, potentially defeating it before it blows up near your towers.
- It and the Commander can also partially negate the **Elite Boomer's** debuffs.
- You cannot use the Medic's ability to protect towers of the **Elite Boomer's** debuff.
- Additionally, it is not possible to use any stun immune towers to stop the **Elite Boomer** from debuffing.
Trivia: - The **Elite Boomer** was originally added in Fallen mode then ended up getting removed from it, leading to it being unused.
- This would later be changed in v1.84.0, where it would be brought back into the main modes through Molten mode.
Update History: - **Elite Boomer** added, replacing Boomer in Fallen Mode.
- **Bug**: No longer creates an explosion VFX upon death, unless triggered while it has Corpse.
- **Elite Boomer** removed from the main game, now only exists in Sandbox mode if the player has its Logbook.
- **Elite Boomer** re-added to the main game, now appears in Molten mode.
- Speed increased from Slightly Fast (4.5) to Fast (6),

Description: The **Elite Lead** is a tanky Lead enemy that appears in Hardcore and Voidcore modes. It has high health and average speed. It initially spawns with Lead, meaning only towers with lead detection can damage it, and with the Stun Immunity, meaning stuns are less effective on it while knockback does not affect it. However, once it loses all of its Shield Health, it will lose its covering and also the Lead and Stun Immunity attributes it has by default. To compensate however, it will increase its speed to 5 once all of its coverings are lost.
Logbook Description: "*Taking the same concept as the Lead, the Elite Lead are Swifts who have fallen victim to the same process as the Odds. Though, more careful consideration was taken for their armor due to mobility reasons.*"
Appearance: The **Elite Lead** is a humanoid entirely covered with grey metal armor. Upon losing all of its Shield Health, it will usually lose most of its metal coverings, revealing that it is an entity with grey skin, purple substance on its hands and purple veins. In its torso, it has a giant hole with a purple crystal.

The **Elite Lead** will lose one piece of its armor covering (head, torso, left leg, right leg, left arm, right leg) at random every time it loses one sixth of its Shield Health, or a covering loss every 25 health lost. In cases of it receiving more than 25 damage, like 50 damage at once, it will lose multiple pieces at once, which in the previously listed 50 damage's case that being two pieces of armor. The only exception to this is it losing all of its Shield Health, as this happening does not actually remove any armor. This means there will always be at least one piece of armor left on the **Elite Lead**, with it even being possible to have it keep all of its armor if the Shield Health received 150 damage at once.
Strategy: - The **Elite Lead** has the Lead attribute until its shield health is depleted.
- Towers with lead detection like the Engineer, Golden Scout and Saboteur are required for dealing with the **Elite Lead**.
- Once its coverings is removed, other towers like the Crook Boss or Minigunner can also be used even if they do not have lead detection.
- The **Elite Lead** also has the Stun Immunity, making stuns only slow it down.
- Once it loses its Shield Health, it will lose this immunity, making stuns far more effective.
Trivia: - The **Elite Lead** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Elite Lead** added, replacing the Lead Boss.

Description: The **Elite Mystery** is a summoner enemy that appears in both Hardcore and Voidcore modes. It has decent health and slightly fast speed. As it is an upgraded version of the Mystery, it will spawn a random enemy on death. This has a 31.58% chance to be the Voidling, 21.05% chance to be the Void Floater, 31.58% chance to be the Void Reaper and 15.79% chance to be the Elite Phantom.

Strategy: - The **Elite Mystery** is one of the most dangerous enemies in the gamemodes it appears in. Bringing dedicated counters against it is recommended.
- AOE towers like the Rocketeer, Mortar and Tesla are extremely useful against the **Elite Mystery**, as it often appears in groups. However, they may not fare as well against the enemies it spawns.
- As two of the enemies summoned in by the **Elite Mystery** have either Hidden or Flying, towers with hidden and flying detection are required.

- As with many other Hardcore mode enemies, the **Elite Mystery** has Stun Immunity, meaning towers that stun, such as the Electroshocker and Warden will be significantly less effective at dealing with it.
Trivia: - The **Elite Mystery** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.

Description: The **Elite Phantom** is a Hidden enemy that appears in Hardcore and Voidcore modes. It is a stronger version of the Phantom, having higher health and faster speed than it. As it is a Hidden enemy, towers need hidden detection to target it.
Logbook Description: "*The Elite Phantom has existed long enough to draw in and crush countless others within its core that it has enhanced its natural abilities. The pull around them is stronger, to the point that standing next to one is a sure-fire way to be dragged into an unfortunate end. The sound around them also seems to distort, but it is still not known why.*"
Appearance: The **Elite Phantom** is a translucent ghost with a purple body. In place of its legs, it has a tail, allowing it to float above the path. It wears a purple shirt with a hood, which has three purple crystals on top.
Strategy: - Due to the **Elite Phantom's** fast speed, it is not recommended to use towers with low range against it.
- Freezing towers, such as the Freezer, Frost Blaster and Cryomancer can be useful at stalling the **Elite Phantom**.
- Do note that **Elite Phantoms** gain Freeze Immunity on Wave 35 of Voidcore mode.
- A Level 4+ Ace Pilot can be used to give towers without hidden detection, like the Kingpin hidden detection, allowing them to take this enemy down.
- The DJ Booth and Commander can be used to help kill **Elite Phantoms** quicker.
Trivia: - The **Elite Phantom** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Elite Phantom** added, replacing the Shadow Boss.
- **Elite Phantom** now appears in Nil Zone II as part of the Halloween 2026 Live Events.
- **Elite Phantom** no longer spawns in Nil Zone II, as the Halloween 2026 Live Event has ended.

elite_soul.name: Elite Soul
elite_soul.description: The Elite Soul is a Hidden enemy that appears in both Hardcore and Voidcore modes.

Description: The **Elite Soul** is a Hidden enemy that appears in both Hardcore and Voidcore modes. It is a stronger version of the Soul, having higher health than it but slower speed. It being a Hidden and Ghost enemy means towers need hidden detection to target it and units cannot collide with it. It also has the Stun Immunity, making it harder to stall.
Logbook Description: "*Elite Souls are regular Souls of those who died from either having their realm destroyed by the Void or by succumbing to the eternal nothing. Elite Souls are created from the regular souls having found enlightenment. Basically, a higher purpose for their recreation as a servant to the Void Caster. For their loyalty, she will grant them the unique gift of wings. Sometimes, the Elite Souls will flutter their wings as a sign of joy. If there is a group of them, they then just sound like a group of angry pigeons.*"
Appearance: The **Elite Soul** has a translucent white body with no legs and pink wings on its back it uses to float above the path. Above its head it has a giant floating purple halo. It wears a white, purple and black robe that covers most of its body.
Strategy: - Towers with high DPS and hidden detection, such as the Accelerator, Engineer and Turret are recommended against the **Elite Soul**.
- Towers without it can also be used but only if given hidden detection through for example the Ace Pilot or Firework Technician.
- Due to it being a Ghost enemy, units cannot collide with it, reducing the effectiveness of certain units like the Riot Guard or making them entirely useless against it like the Hallow Guard.

- This however does not mean units are completely useless against it, as they can still target it with their ranged attacks, making units like the Rifleman or Tommy Goon 2 better than it as they cannot die to the **Elite Soul** colliding with them.
Trivia: - The **Elite Soul** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Elite Soul** added, replacing the Soul Boss.
- Health increased from 22,222 to 25,000 in Voidcore mode.

Description: The **Elite Void Rusher** is a fast enemy that appear in both Hardcore and Voidcore modes. It is a stronger version of the Void Rusher, having same speed and Defense but way higher health and Shield Health. Once its Shield Health is depleted, its shield will break causing it to become slower and losing all of its Defense.
Logbook Description: "*The Elite Void Rusher’s shield is made out of a special material forged in the Void. It’s faster, heavier, and more armored than the Void Rusher. It will continue to charge forward regardless of its own safety to cut an opening for the army to seep into. They are fundamentally the most important fighters on the battlefield, and it’s best not to take them lightly. They are what punches the hold[sic] for the Void to flow through.*"
Appearance: The **Elite Void Rusher** has a black body with purple lines going across it. It wears purple boots, chestplate, shoulder-pads and helmet, all with gold accents. It carries a purple and gold shield which is broken once all of its Shield Health is depleted.
Strategy: - The **Elite Void Rusher** is essentially a much stronger version of the Void Rusher, having much higher health and Shield Health while also maintaining the same speeds. This makes it more threatening than the Void Rusher, as its high Shield Health can be much more difficult to deplete, allowing it to maintain its extremely swift speed.
- DPS towers with higher upgrades such the Accelerator, Juggernaut, Kingpin, Ranger and Golden Minigunner are beneficial to melting down its high Shield Health in order to slow it down.
- Support towers like the Commander, DJ Booth or Medic can also aid in increasing the DPS of your towers.
- Just like the Void Rusher, towers like the Electroshocker, Frost Blaster, Sledger or Freezer can counter the **Elite Void Rusher's** extremely fast speed.
- The Golden Pyromancer, Pyromancer or Freezer can also decrease the high Defense of the **Elite Void Rusher**, making it easier to kill it.
Trivia: - The **Elite Void Rusher** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.

Description: The **Enraged** is an enemy that appears in Easy, Casual, Basic Arena PVP and Molten Arena PVP modes. It also appears in The Takeover Event. It has a low amount of health but a quite fast speed. At later waves, it can gain various attributes that make it harder to deal with, including Bloated, which doubles its health, and Nimble, which doubles its speed.
Appearance: **Variant 1**
The **Enraged** is a humanoid with a grey skin color and dark brown torso and legs. It has a glowing red outline on its body as well as glowing light red veins on its arms and head.
**Variant 2**
The legacy **Enraged** has dark red skin, black torso and legs. It has a neon red outline around its body.
Strategy: - Towers with decent DPS, like the Cowboy, Militant, Minigunner and Ace Pilot can be quite effective against this.
- Additionally, these towers have hidden detection for when the **Enraged** becomes Hidden on some waves, such as on Wave 14 of Casual and Intermediate modes.
- Area of effect towers like the Mortar, Pyromancer, Golden Pyromancer, or Rocketeer can be quite useful as the **Enraged** spawns in hordes.
- Due to their fast speed, especially with the nimble attribute, slowing towers like the Freezer, Electroshocker, Frost Blaster or Cryomancer can be quite useful.
- Some of these towers could also be useful at killing the **Enraged**, due to their high damage.
Trivia: - The **Enraged** existed in the game's code a few years before it was properly added, although it looked different from its current appearance.
- This appearance would later be added to Sandbox mode as a legacy enemy.

- The legacy **Enraged** also had more variants, these being the *Enraged Boss* and the *Enraged Giant*, though they were never added as they were intended for the 2021 PVP mode which was never released.

Description: The **Error** was a very fast enemy that appeared in Hardcore mode and the Sandbox exclusive Legacy Fallen mode. While it has somewhat low health compared to other enemies that spawn during its debut (like the Tank or Slow King), its speed is high enough to overcome weaker defenses. The **Error** also has Stun Immunity, which makes it immune to the Warden and Electroshocker's stun, being only slowed down and makes it immune to knockback.
The **Error** can be spawned from the Mystery upon its death in Hardcore mode, Wave 43 onwards and in Legacy Fallen mode, Wave 37 onwards.
Appearance: The **Error** is a chaotic multi-colored enemy with no face. It has a red head, left arm and right leg. It also has a salmon colored torso and left leg. It has a yellow right arm, which holds a very reflective navy DVD disk. On its torso is an emblem of a navy DVD. It emits large glitch particles of various colors from its torso. It also plays a brief error sound upon death. It runs with both of its arms pointing upwards, flailing.
Strategy: - The strategy against the **Error** is mostly the same as the strategies to be used against the Glitch, but keep in mind that the **Error** has much higher health compared to the Glitch, and also appears in conjunction with tougher enemies, like the Tank, Boomer, Summoner Boss.
- Using towers that deal high DPS, such as the Golden Minigunner, Engineer, Accelerator and Ranger, are highly recommended against the **Error**.
- While the Accelerator can be used against **Errors**, be aware of its charge-up time. The delay may allow some **Errors** to get past.
- The Commander is almost essential against the **Error** as the firerate boost it provides can allow towers to attack the **Error** more often before it moves out of range.
- The DJ Booth can also be very helpful, as the range boost will keep **Errors** in the range of towers for longer.
- The Electroshocker, Sledger and Warden can be used to slow this down.
- Do note that the Stun Immunity that the **Error** has causes stunning towers like the Electroshocker to only slow it down instead of stunning it while knockback towers will not knock it back.
- The Sledger may not be able to attack all the **Errors** that enter its range as its range is short. However, if timed correctly, it can freeze multiple **Errors** at once.
Trivia: - The **Error** may be a reference to DVD Man (originating from one of M.U.G.E.N.s' games).
- The **Error** may be inspired by *Tower Battles's* Error from Wave 0000000.
- The **Error's** disc may look different on different angles depending on the map.
- This is due to it being very reflective.
- As its name suggests, the **Error** makes an error sound when it dies.
- The **Error** is a variant of the Glitch, which also appears in Legacy Fallen mode.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Festive Swipe** - The **Evil Elf** stops in its place and slashes its scythe at a tower, stunning it.

Description: The **Evil Elf** was an enemy that first appeared on Wave 20 in Krampus Frosthold as part of the Krampus' Revenge Event. It had a high amount of health, it moved somewhat quickly and had a high amount of defense. It had one ability, *Festive Swipe*, where it stopped moving and slashed its scythe at a tower, stunning it. It was also immune to being frozen, slowed down and having its defense dropped by freezing towers, while also only being slowed down by the Electroshocker and Warden, making it a very threatening enemy.
It could be spawned by the Krampus from its *Secret Santa* ability.
Appearance: The **Evil Elf** was a hulking elf with pale-green skin. Its rig had lower arms and a waist. It had a dark blue shirt with white fur along the sleeves, as well as stitch lines on the sides of the arms. It had a black line going down the middle of its torso and waist, as well as down the sides of its sleeves. It also had black stains on its torso and upper arms. It had dark navy pants and black shoes. It also wore a dark blue Christmas hat.

It wielded a red and white striped candy cane themed scythe. On the end opposite of the blade are six holly leaves. The blade itself is a yellow and red striped piece of metal wedged into the bottom of the candy cane.
Strategy: - High DPS towers like the Accelerator, Ranger and Engineer are recommended against this enemy.
- These towers should have their firerate and range boosted by the Commander and DJ Booth respectively.
- The Ranger cannot be stunned by the **Evil Elf**, nor can the Engineer's sentries be destroyed by it, making them both very effective.
- The Medic can be used to cleanse the stuns from towers stunned by the **Evil Elf's** *Festive Swipe* ability.
- Slowing towers can be useful in delaying the **Evil Elf's** advance.
- Freezing towers cannot freeze or slow the **Evil Elf** down due to its Freeze Immunity.
- The Electroshocker and Warden are less effective against the **Evil Elf** due to its Stun Immunity, only being able to slow it down as opposed to stunning it.
- The Toxic Gunner and Jester are the only options that are unaffected by the **Evil Elf's** immunities.
- Defense dropping towers like the Pyromancer can be used to reduce the **Evil Elf's** defense.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Festive Swipe** - The **Evil Elf** stops in its place and slashes its scythe at a tower, setting towers caught in its scythe on fire for a period of time.

Description: The **Evil Elf** was an enemy that first appeared on Wave 18 in Cold Ambush as part of the Violent Night Event. It had a very high amount of health, a high amount of defense and walked quite fast for its health. It had one ability, *Festive Swipe*, where it would stop moving and slash its scythe at a tower, setting it on fire. Additionally, it was immune to being frozen and immune to being stunned by the Warden and Electroshocker. All of this made it a very threatening enemy.
Appearance: The **Evil Elf** was a hulking elf with pale-green skin. Its rig had lower arms and a waist. It had a dark blue shirt with white fur along the sleeves, as well as stitch lines on the sides of the arms. It had a black line going down the middle of its torso and waist, as well as down the sides of its sleeves. It also had black stains on its torso and upper arms. It had dark navy pants and black shoes. It also wore a dark blue Christmas hat.

It wielded a red and white striped candy cane themed scythe. On the end opposite of the blade are six holly leaves. The blade itself is a yellow and red striped piece of metal wedged into the bottom of the candy cane.
Strategy: - High DPS towers like the Accelerator, Ranger and Engineer are recommended against this enemy.
- These towers should have their firerate and range boosted by the Commander and DJ Booth respectively.
- The Ranger cannot be stunned by the **Evil Elf**, nor can the Engineer's sentries be destroyed by it, making them both very effective.
- The Medic can be used to cleanse the stuns from towers stunned by the **Evil Elf's** *Festive Swipe* ability.
- Slowing towers can be useful in delaying the **Evil Elf's** advance.
- The Freezer, Frost Blaster and Sledger cannot slow the **Evil Elf** down due to its Freeze Immunity.
- The Electroshocker and Warden are less effective against the **Evil Elf** due to its Energy Immunity, only being able to slow it down as opposed to stunning it.
- The Toxic Gunner can be used at its maximum potential, slowing the **Evil Elf** down by 25%.
- Defense dropping towers like the Pyromancer can be used to reduce the **Evil Elf's** defense.

- As the **Evil Elf** stops moving to use its ability, you could use cheap towers like the Scout to distract the **Evil Elf**, causing it to use its ability on the tower, stopping it from moving and buying more time to defeat it.

Description: The **Executioner**, internally referred to as **Executioner Plush**, is a boss in Pizza Party, debuting on Wave 35. It has an extremely high amount of health and walks at a slow speed. The **Executioner** has one ability where it throws its axe at a random tower, stunning any tower hit by it.
Appearance: The **Executioner** is a plushie version of the Level 5 **Eclipse** Executioner. It has a dark purple helmet with horns with blue glow inside of it, dark purple shoulder-pads, chestplate and leg padding. It has yellow button kneepads, a purple belt and a giant yellow button on its torso. It also wears purple gloves and shoes.
The **Executioner** wields a large grey and red axe which it uses to attack towers.
Strategy: - High DPS towers, such as the Pursuit, Ranger, Engineer and Turret are recommended to take this enemy down.
- The DJ Booth and Commander can be used to boost these towers.
- The Medic can be used to shield towers, preventing them from being stunned by the **Executioner's** *Head Chopping* ability.

- You can also use towers that are immune to stuns, such as the Ranger and Pursuit.
- When it first spawns, it is a boss enemy, limiting the amount of towers that can slow it down.
- Confusion, Slowness, and poison effects cannot slow it down at all, so using towers with these effects to stall it is not advised on its debut wave.
- Freezing towers cannot freeze it, but can still slow it down through chill.
- Cheap towers can be placed on the side of the map to bait the **Executioner**, making it target insignificant towers instead of your main DPS towers.

- It can also be used to stall the **Executioner**. While performing its ability, it will stop moving, giving you more time to kill it. This, however, requires towers to be in range, which makes it pretty useful to have a cheap distraction tower near it at all times. Regardless, this is not mandatory.

While created to perform a role, when it's not acting it will happily follow around anyone it finds interesting. Sometimes the Exo Follower will antagonize Narrator, but it only reminds him of the Old World days.*"

- As the **Exo Follower** is quite fast, stalling towers like the Freezer, Electroshocker, Frost Blaster or Toxic Gunner can be used to slow it down.

Description: The **Fallen** is a fast enemy that appears in Fallen, Fallen Arena PVP and Legacy Fallen modes. It also appears in The Takeover Event. This enemy has a decent amount of health and is noticeably much faster than most enemies that have spawned before it, including the Quick, Breaker2 and Invisible.

The **Fallen** can be spawned by the Fallen King, Fallen Reaper and Void Reaver. The Fallen Reaper can spawn the **Fallen** from wave 26 onwards. It could also be spawned by the former Nuclear Fallen King. The **Fallen** could have been spawned from the Mystery upon its death in Fallen mode, from wave 21 onwards.
Logbook Description: "*The Fallen were once ordinary citizens who lived within Paradise's borders. As magic began to fade, they swore an oath to defend their kingdom. They supplied the army with weapons, food, and clothing, keeping soldiers equipped and fed. Their society was built on strength and trust, and though they received basic training, they never expected to see combat. When the Queen's curse swept through their kingdom, it transformed these supporters into mindless soldiers.*"
Appearance: **Variant 1**
The **Fallen** wears a turquoise T-shirt and grayish-white skin and has a slightly darker colored head and legs. It wears a white bandana around its head. It also has a sprinting animation.
**Variant 2**
The **Fallen** wears a dark blue T-shirt and torsos that have patches of lighter color and black skin. It also has a sprinting animation.
Strategy: - These enemies are strong and fast, and are quite a step up from the Fallen Squire. Cheap towers with high DPS are the best way to fend these enemies off, boosted by the DJ Booth and/or Commander.
- Such towers include the Golden Cowboy, Militant, Engineer and Minigunner.
- Higher level Military Bases can be quite strong against **Fallens** due to the Tank and Railgun Tank's high health.
- Slowing towers can be useful due to **Fallen's** speed. The Frost Blaster, Cryomancer and Electroshocker are by far the most useful ones.
- Some slowing towers like the Sledger, Tesla or Frost Blaster can also be used to kill groups of **Fallens**, due to their high damage and ability to hit multiple enemies.
Trivia: - The **Fallen** can be spawned by the Fallen Reaper beginning from Wave 25 before its first wave appearance in Hardcore mode.
- The Fallen mode appearance of the **Fallen** oddly looks like the Hidden Zoomer, having similar walking animations and designs.
- Multiple **Fallens** are seen locked behind a cage or jail cell in the Fallen Mode trailer, suggesting they are prisoners.

Description: The **Fallen Angel** is a Flying enemy that appears in Fallen mode. It is the second Flying enemy that appears in that mode, having higher health than the Fallen Seraph with the same speed. Additionally, it has Health Regen, which causes it to regenerate 2% of its health every 2 seconds.
Logbook Description: "*Fallen Angels were the kingdom's most devoted followers, blessed by Two X himself for their unwavering faith. They served as spiritual guardians, their presence bringing comfort to all who saw them. However, the Queen's sacrifice corrupted their blessings and tarnished their purity. As the curse consumed them, it became a symbol that their kingdom truly died.*"
Appearance: The **Fallen Angel** is an angel, hovering above the ground using its black wings. It wears blue armor which consists of a helmet, shoulder-pads, chestplate, leggings, shoes and gloves. It has a few crystals on its helmet. Above its head, it has a black halo. It has a hole in the middle of its torso.
Strategy: - As the **Fallen Angel** is a Flying enemy, the number of towers that can target it is limited.
- DPS towers that have flying detection, such as the Engineer, Ranger or Pursuit are the best options against it.
- The UAV can be used to give your towers flying detection, making the **Fallen Angels** quite easy to deal with.

- Area of effect towers with flying detection, like the Mortar, Tesla or Spotlight Tech, can be useful at dealing with these, though due to this enemy's high health such towers may not be capable of killing this enemy on their own.
- The Tesla can also be useful at slowing them down, giving your towers more time to kill them.
- While the **Fallen Angel** does not have any immunities, it gains an immunity to being knocked back which is given by default to any Flying enemy.
- This means that towers like the DJ Booth, Brawler or Warlock are fully or partially unable to stall it.

Description: The **Fallen Dreg** is an enemy that appears in Fallen mode. It also appears in The Takeover Event. It has quite high amount of health for its debut, and a relatively quicker speed than the Abnormal. It has Corpse by default, making it spawn a Corpse on death.
Logbook Description: "*Fallen Dregs were laborers who once lived in Paradise. When the Queen's curse took hold, their bodies were engulfed with flames that burn eternally. They wear the traditional armor of their society, which once featured a bright white gem at its center. Even in death, their corpses continue to burn as a reminder of the Queen's sacrifice.*"
Appearance: The **Fallen Dreg** has blue skin. It does not have a head or a torso, exposing its blue skeleton. It also has a skull, It wears a grey and blue chestplate, shoulder-pads, arm-pads, knee-pads, shoes and pants, and it has a grey cape with a gem upfront. It also has blue fire coming out of the top of its skull.
Strategy: - The **Fallen Dreg** has a higher health than both the Abnormal and Quick, as well as the Fallen Skeleton itself. It is also faster than the Abnormal, making it a rather dangerous enemy.
- Cheap early-game towers with decent DPS, like the Cowboy, Brawler, Golden Scout or Trapper can be used.
- As they spawn in hordes, splash damage towers like the Mortar or Rocketeer can clear them out quite well.
- The **Fallen Dreg** spawns with the Corpse attribute by default, which allows it to spawn a corpse of itself upon its death. Because of this, it will act as a shield for enemies behind it.

- In the earlier waves upon and after its debut, it is best to set some of your towers to *First*, *Random*, or *Strongest* depending on the wave, that deal less damage such as the Scout to deal with the **Fallen Dreg's** corpse, as a low damage output won't be affected much by the corpses 100% defense. The rest of your towers should focus on defeating the other enemies that spawn alongside.
- You can use early defense dropping towers like the Electroshocker to drop the **Fallen Dreg's** defense, though, this is usually not recommended.
Trivia: - The **Fallen Dreg** existed in the game prior to its proper addition, though it went unused as it was scrapped before the release of the v1.27.0 Fallen mode rework.
- It was later properly introduced in v1.67.0 as a replacement for the Heavy.
- However, the Commander still mentioned the Heavy until v1.68.0.
- The current appearance is a recolored version of the Korblox Undead.

Description: The **Fallen Giant** is a tanky enemy that appears in Fallen and Fallen Arena PVP modes. It also appeared in The Takeover Event. It has a high amount of health and decently fast for the amount of health it has. It is a Boss enemy when it first spawns in Fallen mode.
Logbook Description: "*Fallen Giants were the kingdom's most honored guardians. They stood watch over the throne room, where they witnessed the Queen's sacrifice. They are vessels of magic lacking free will, and the curse only magnified their power. Massive in size, they make for great defenders and one could tell a Giant was coming by the shaking of the ground upon each step.*"
Appearance: The **Fallen Giant** is a large, hulking entity with black skin. It has multiple blue cracks in its body. It wears a torn, off-white coat, cyan-grey gloves and has strange tubing and devices on its head. Its skull is partially exposed and it has a knife on its back.
Strategy: - The **Fallen Giant** is quite a step-up in difficulty compared to other enemies that debut before it. Despite not having defense by default at all, its high health and relatively early arrival make up for this.
- Using high, relatively affordable DPS towers, such as the Engineer, Hunter, Ranger and Golden Minigunner can be sufficient to take this enemy down.
- The DJ Booth, Commander and Mercenary Base can be used to boost these towers.

- On Wave 25, three **Fallen Giant's** appear along with the debut of the Fallen Jester. This combo is extremely deadly due to the Fallen Jester's *Devious Tricks* ability that can give the **Fallen Giants** Bloated and Blessed, greatly buffing them. In total, all three of them with Bloated have a combined health of 24,000, as well as 100% defense from the Blessed attribute.

- You should use high DPS towers such as the Turret, Ranger and Accelerator to focus on the **Fallen Giants** and a few focused on the Fallen Jester. Because the Fallen Jester is faster, it is best to set some towers to *First* and the rest to *Strongest* or *Last* to maximize the damage potential.
- The Saboteur can be used to force your towers to target the Fallen Jesters.
- The **Fallen Giant** has the Stun Immunity, making it only get slowed down by stuns and making it fully immune to knockback.
- Do note however that certain forms of stalling, like freeze or some specific cases like the Confusion Ducky, the duration of the stall will be shorter due to its larger size.
Trivia: - The model used by the **Fallen Giant** was originally made for the Giant Boss, though it was later re-textured and used for the **Fallen Giant**.
- The Giant Boss model would not be added until the 18th of September 2025.
- The knife that is on the **Fallen Giant** is the Bombo's Survival Knife from the Roblox Catalog.

Description: The **Fallen Guardian** is a large guardian enemy that appears in the Sandbox exclusive Legacy Fallen mode. Although it could not spawn naturally in The Classic Event, the Fallen King could summon the **Fallen Guardian** during *Rage Mode*. The **Fallen Guardian** always spawns just before the Fallen King and Void Reaver (it also used to appear before the Nuclear Fallen King spawns). It also appears when the Fallen King (and formerly the Nuclear Fallen King) summons them during *Rage Mode*. It also appeared in the legacy Hidden Wave and The Classic Event before its removal.

The **Fallen Guardian** is an extremely difficult enemy to defeat due to its high health (far higher than the Summoner Boss and Slow King) and below average walkspeed. Additionally, it has a defense of 80%, meaning that the damage capabilities of most towers are reduced drastically. On top of that, the **Fallen Guardian** has the ability to thrust its spear at towers, stunning them for a period of time.
The **Fallen Guardian** is replaced by the Nuclear Guardian in Polluted Wasteland II, the Cavalry in Badlands II and the Minigunner in Pizza Party.
Appearance: **Variant 1**

The current **Fallen Guardian** is similar to its original version, except it dominus is now dark turquoise. It is now also right-handed and has a twisted left leg. Its neon parts are now light purple.
**Variant 2**

The original **Fallen Guardian** had black reflective skin. It wore dark turquoise granite armor, which comprised of armbands, knee-pads, sleeves and chestplate. It had black granite gloves, its torso was dark turquoise granite, and it wielded a spear with purple halos near the head. It also wore a black marble dominus. On its dominus, there were parts which were neon purple. Purple smoke was emitted from their torso.
Strategy: - Deal with the **Fallen Guardian** before moving on to the major boss that it spawns in front of. With high health, faster speed, the ability to stun towers and extremely high defense, the **Fallen Guardian** protects the major boss and can overwhelm poorly prepared defenses.

- As the **Fallen Guardian** has quite high defense, defense dropping towers like the Freezer, Pyromancer or Jester can be quite useful at dropping it. Some towers, like the Freezer, Frost Blaster or Toxic Gunner can also be useful at slowing it down.
- However, freezing towers and Warden can only freeze or stun the **Fallen Guardian** for a shorter period of time due to its size.
- Because of its Stun Immunity, stunning towers like the Electroshocker can only slow it down instead of stopping it completely while knockback towers cannot knock it back.
- Having a concentrated group of Sledgers may be able to impede **Fallen Guardians**.
- The Accelerator, Ranger, Engineer, Golden Minigunner and Pursuit are excellent towers against the **Fallen Guardian** due to their high DPS.
- The Commander can decrease the firerate of these towers, especially with its *Call to Arms* ability.
- The Ranger and Pursuit can be very useful, as they cannot be stunned.
- Be aware that if the Accelerator is stunned by the **Fallen Guardian**, it will have to charge up again.

- It is best to place towers a distance away from the path so that they cannot get stunned.

- Splash damage towers, like the Mortar and Rocketeer, can be useful against the **Fallen Guardian**, as they spawn in groups and splash damage ignores defense, dealing full damage to the **Fallen Guardian**.

Description: The **Fallen Hazmat** is an enemy that appears in Fallen and Fallen Arena PVP modes. It also appears in The Takeover Event. It has a decent amount of health, and it has above average speed, 60% defense and multiple immunities. These immunities prevent it from being set on fire, prevent it from being stunned, only being slowed down by stuns, prevent it from being knocked back and prevent it from being frozen or chilled by freezing towers.
Logbook Description: "*Fallen Hazmats were created after the curse had taken hold over the kingdom. Unlike the other Fallen, the Hazmats are manifestations of the curse itself. They are more violent and unpredictable than other Fallen, driven by a hunger to prove their worth. Despite their chaotic nature, they remain loyal to the Fallen King and constantly search for powerful enemies to fight and cursed artifacts to bring to their master.*"
Appearance: The **Fallen Hazmat** has black skin. It wears bluish-grey armor with a lock on its chest, covering up most of its body. Its helmet has two horns sticking out of its sides.
Strategy: - Towers with decent DPS, such as the Militant, Golden Soldier, Ace Pilot or Brawler can be quite effective against this.
- High DPS towers, like the Turret, Minigunner, Crook Boss or Accelerator can also fare well against this.
- As this generally spawns in hordes, area of effect towers like the Tesla, Mortar or Rocketeer can be useful against this.
- Because of its immunities, knockback and freeze cannot be used to slow it down.
- Stuns can still be used, but because of its Stun Immunity it will only be slowed down instead of fully stunned.
- Various less commons stalls, like the confusion and poison slowdown from towers like the Saboteur are not affected by any of their immunities.
- Because of its immunities, freeze and burn defense dropping towers cannot drop its defense.
- This should not be a huge problem due to its low health.
Trivia: - A **Fallen Hazmat** is seen delivering a God Cube fragment to the Fallen King in the Fallen Mode rework trailer.
- This behavior is directly referenced at the end of the **Fallen Hazmat's** Logbook description.
- It is voiced by Enthrallist.

Description: The **Fallen Hero** is a variant of the Fallen enemy that appears in the Sandbox exclusive Legacy Fallen mode. It can be a threat to your defenses due to its high health and high defense of 50%, which decreases the damage dealt by most towers by about 33%, though due to damage dealt rounding up this is not always the case. It moves at an above average speed.

It can be spawned by the Fallen King and Void Reaver. It can be spawned by the Mystery Boss upon its death on Wave 38 onwards in Fallen mode and in Hardcore mode, wave 46 onwards. The Nuclear Fallen King also could spawn the **Fallen Hero**.
Appearance: The **Fallen Hero** has reflective black skin, dark blue granite armor and pants, and there are glowing purple parts on its shoulder-pads resembling skulls. It also wears a completely black reflective dominus.
Strategy: - High DPS towers, such as the Ranger, Minigunner, Accelerator and Engineer are very useful against this.

Puddles from multiple **Fallen Honor Guards** can stack and be applied multiple times.

Description: The **Fallen Honor Guard** is a mini boss that appears only in Fallen mode. It also appeared in The Takeover Event. It has a high amount of health, the highest for a non-boss enemy in the entire mode, only being beaten by the Fallen King and its Hidden Wave version, Awakened Fallen King. While it does have a high amount of health, it is slow. It has two abilities, first being *For Honor*, where it smashes its flails to the ground, creating a shockwave that stuns any tower and damages any unit caught in it. The second ability is *Guard's Grace,* which makes it leave a puddle of goo every 0.5 seconds which lasts for 6 minutes. This trail of goo applies a 10% speed buff to any enemy that walks over it for 1 second. Puddles from multiple **Fallen Honor Guards** can stack their effects.
Logbook Description: "*Fallen Honor Guards were the elite of the elite, chosen personally by the King to protect the kingdom's most sacred sites. They were there when the King failed to find new magic, and they stood guard as the Queen met her end. They are the Fallen King's most prized guards who had fallen, just as he did.*"
Appearance: The **Fallen Honor Guard** is a hulking humanoid. It has black skin with multiple blue veins. It also has a few bandages around its arms. It has very dark teal and silver armor with cyan gems plating its whole body and a frog-mouth helm with cyan gems covering its whole head, and two large, spiked flails connected to its arms, which it smashes into the ground when using its *For Honor* ability. The gem on its chest plate emits blue light. All of its armor is covered in small amounts of dirt. When it walks, it leaves behind a purple trail, makes loud footsteps and shakes the screen.
Strategy: - Deal with this enemy as soon as possible. Leaving it alive for too long will allow its *Guard's Grace* ability to leave a vast amount of goo, with a whopping 6 minute lifespan, on the path behind itself. This can give enemies that spawn behind it a huge advantage, allowing them to progress further.
- In addition, the goo will most likely last towards the final wave, allowing the Fallen King to take advantage of the 10% speed buff.
- High DPS towers, such as the Accelerator, Engineer and Turret should be used to defeat it quickly.
- The DJ Booth, Commander and Mercenary Base can be used to boost these towers.
- Furthermore, one should expect to fight the next wave with the **Fallen Honor Guard** still alive, as its debut wave lasts an extremely short amount of time.

- To deal with the waves that arrive alongside it, splash damage or multi-target towers are highly recommended. The Tesla, Rocketeer and Mortar are all excellent options, though it may be best to put Rocketeer/Mortar on *Strongest* or *Random* targeting to allow them to utilize their explosion radius more consistently.
- The Medic can be used to shield towers, preventing them from being stunned by the **Fallen Honor Guard's** *For Honor* ability.
- Alternatively, you can place cheap towers along the path to divert the ability away from your main damage towers.
- You can also use towers that are immune to stuns, such as the Ranger and Pursuit.
- When it first spawns, it is a Boss enemy, limiting the amount of towers that can slow it down.
- As it has Stun Immunity by default, stunning towers cannot stun it regardless of if it is a boss or not, only slowing it down and it cannot be knocked back by towers with knockback.
- One of the **Fallen Honor Guard** in Hidden Wave can regenerate its health, and spawn in hordes.
- Towers that can stall hordes of enemies such as Cryomancer and Jester are required so that your towers can attack them for longer.
- Due to bugs, freezing towers can complete stop the **Fallen Honor Guard** from moving if it is frozen while performing its *For Honor* ability.
- As it has Stun Immunity, the Tesla is a much less effective option, however it can still be brought to deal with other enemies.
- Due to multiple of them spawning, high DPS towers with Stun Immunity such as Ranger and Pursuit are heavily advised.
Update History: - **Bug**: **Fallen Honor Guard** slightly floats above the ground when made larger or smaller.

Description: The **Fallen Jester** is a support enemy that appears in Fallen mode and also appears in The Takeover Event. It has the same speed as the Fallen Squire but it has much higher health than it. It has one ability, *Devious Tricks*, which makes it throw a gift on the path which buffs enemies. This creates an explosion with an explosion radius of 5. This can apply either the Bloated or Blessed attributes. The **Fallen Jester** cannot buff itself, other **Fallen Jesters** or Boss enemies.

The **Fallen Jester** will not target other **Fallen Jesters**, itself, the Fallen Angel, Fallen Seraph, Warden and the Fallen King, its Awakened Fallen King form included. This, however, does not mean they cannot receive attributes from it. As long as they are not a **Fallen Jester** or a Boss, they can still receive them, just indirectly.
Logbook Description: "*Fallen Jesters entertained the royal court, their performances bringing joy even as hope vanished along with the magic. They put on spectacular shows and gave gifts unlike anything anyone had seen, yet they could never change the despair seen in the faces of their audience. The day the Queen died, as did their laughter. The curse turned their gifts into tainted presents that strengthen their army. Their performances continue, but no one is there to watch.*"
Appearance: The **Fallen Jester** wears a black and blue jester outfit and shoes, a brown belt and black and grey comedy mask. It has black gloves with grey spiked arm-bands. It has black horns on its shoulders. It holds a black and blue present which it uses to buff enemies with.
It has a death animation where it falls over on its back, its present falling on its face in the process.
Strategy: - The **Fallen Jester** should be killed as soon as possible. While it is not dangerous on its own, its ability to buff other enemies can make it very dangerous.
- DPS towers like the Engineer, Turret, Ranger or Minigunner can be used to kill it.
- Stalling towers like the Tesla or Freezer can be used to slow down the **Fallen Jester**.

- The Gatling Gun is extremely useful against this enemy, as you can manually shoot at it first as well as enemies nearby when using *FPS* mode to kill it before it uses its *Devious Tricks* ability. However, if it is low level, it might not be able to kill the **Fallen Jester** fast enough.

- On its debut wave, three Fallen Giants appear alongside it. This combination is highly dangerous because the **Fallen Jester** can apply Bloated and Blessed to them, giving them a total of 8,000 health with 100% defense each and a combined total of 24,000 health.

- It is reccommended to first set some of your towers to *Last* so they can directly target the **Fallen Jester**, as it spawns behind the Fallen Giants. If it uses its *Devious Tricks* ability on them, set your *Last* targeting towers to *Weakest* and keep the rest of your towers attacking the buffed Fallen Giants.
- The Saboteur can also be used to force your towers to target it.

- Defense melting towers such as the Pyromancer and Toxic Gunner are extremely beneficial in lowering the high 100% defense applied by the **Fallen Jester** to enemies from the Blessed status effect, in addition to enemies that already have defense applied to them by default, added with the 100% defense mechanism.
- Additionally, splash damage towers like the Mortar and Rocketeer are effective as they fully ignore defense.

abilities.text: **Bone Armor** - Gains 15% defense as its health is reduced until it reaches at least 60% defense. This roughly happens when it loses 20% of its health it had when spawned or when it loses 20% of its health it had after last gaining defense.

abilities.label: Ability 5 Cooldown: 45
abilities.text: **Fallen Comet** - The **Fallen King** slams its sword into the ground, lifts its right arm up then moves it back down slowly and then pulls out the sword, making a large number of purple spikes fall down from the sky, stunning towers for 5 seconds and dealing 50 damage to units with no range limit for the ability.

Description: The **Fallen King** is the final boss of Fallen mode and The Takeover Event.

While it walks quite slowly, it has a high amount of health and multiple abilities, that allow it to summon enemies, stun towers or to make itself stronger. It is also immune to being stunned by towers like the Electroshocker and only slowed down, frozen by freezing towers like the Freezer, slowed down by the Toxic Gunner, knocked back by towers like the Brawler, confused by the Jester, damaged by the Nuke's fallout damage, slowed down by the DJ Booth or have its defense reduced.
It has five abilities:
- First is *Undead Charge*, which makes it raise its sword forward, summoning five Necrotic Skeletons with a 0.25 second delay between each one.

- The second ability, *Summon*, is another summoning ability, though this one makes the **Fallen King** raise its sword in the air, which summons forty enemies, which can be the Fallen Hero, Fallen Giant, Corrupted Fallen, Possessed Armor and Fallen Necromancer. Only can happen once.
- The third ability, *Sword Swing*, makes it slash its sword multiple times, stunning towers for 6 seconds and damaging units by 100 each swing.

- The fourth ability is *Fallen Comet*, where it impales its sword into the ground, causing multiple shards to fall down from the sky, stunning towers for 5 seconds and dealing 50 damage to any unit hit.

It also has a fifth ability, *Bone Armor*, which is a passive ability that happens when the **Fallen King** loses health, making it gain Defense until it reaches a Defense of 60% or higher. It uses the following equation to decide if it should increase its Defense:
Default Health−Current HealthDefault Health×100

Default health initially is the starting health value of the **Fallen King**, which for example in solo matches is 250,000 while current health is just how much health it currently has. Once the result of the equation is equal or higher to 20, and as long as its current Defense is not the same or higher as its max Defense, its Defense will increase by 15% and the default health value will change into whatever its health was at the moment of the Defense getting increased. For example, if it increases its Defense while its current health is 160,000, default health will change to that number, and then its Defense will be increased by 15%. Due to this, the required damage for it to increase starts out at 20% of its max health and gets lower with each requirement. Therefore, it will increase its Defense after losing at least 20% of its health, then 36%, 51.2% and 59.4%, varied based on the health the **Fallen King** had during each increase.

Because of how its *Bone Armor* mechanic works, in Challenge Maps where the **Fallen King** has lower health, it will instantly gain Defense due to its default health being 250,000 and its current health being for example 75,000. This would make a number larger than 20 in the equation, making it have Defense instantly. In the case of it having its health increased, this is entirely dependent on the source. For example, the Bloated attribute will boost its default health value, meaning it will gain 15% more Defense at 400,000 health, but the Double Health modifier will not boost it, meaning it will gain a Defense boost at the same health as without it, that being 200,000 health.
Logbook Description: "*The Fallen King once ruled his kingdom with wisdom and compassion. When magic began to fade, he searched everywhere for salvation, but failed. When he returned, it was too late. As a last resort, the Queen used her life to cast an ancient spell, believing it would bring magic back to their kingdom. Instead, it released a curse that consumed everything. Now, he rules an empty kingdom with an insatiable army that only hungers for battle. They raid endlessly, fighting because war is the only outlet they have left. Deep within, despite him not recognizing it, the King searches for someone strong enough to end his torment and finally grant him the peace he failed to give his people.*"
Appearance: The **Fallen King** wears a silver and dark grey armor, with cyan spikes on its shoulders as well as cyan details on its arms, torso and legs. A cyan diamond can be found in its lower torso, and it wears silver boots with small diamonds in their front. The **Fallen King** also wears a helmet that shows its cyan glowing eyes and a cyan crown with crystals in it. Lastly, it carries a sharp cyan sword as well as a shield, with a diamond in the middle and cyan spikes on the sides.

When defeated, the **Fallen King** will throw its sword on the ground and disappear in a beam of light. That animation is different upon triggering the Hidden Wave, where it will later come back with some differences as the Awakened Fallen King.
Strategy: - As with most major bosses, high DPS towers such as the Minigunner, Pursuit, Ranger, Turret and Accelerator are recommended to deal with the **Fallen King**.
- The Commander, Mercenary Base and DJ Booth can also be used to boost these towers.
- They should also be able to take care of the **Fallen King's** summons pretty easily.
- The Ranger and Pursuit are immune to stuns from the **Fallen King's** abilities, making them very useful against it.
- As the **Fallen King** has the Boss and Stun Immunity attribute, it cannot be shocked, stunned or frozen by most towers.
- The Freezer, Frost Blaster and Sledger can only chill the **Fallen King** instead of freezing it.
- The Electroshocker, Tesla and Warden also cannot stun it, and have a weaker slowing effect on it.
- However, these towers can be useful against the enemies that appear before the **Fallen King**.
- The Toxic Gunner cannot slow this enemy down as it is immune to its slowing effect. It can, however, be useful against the enemies that appear before it.
- The Jester cannot confuse the **Fallen King**, but it can slow it down with its ice bombs.

- Make sure to sell any Farms to maximize the number of towers attacking the **Fallen King**. They do not produce any income anymore, still count towards your tower limit, and can be replaced by a more useful tower.

- The Cowboy and Golden Cowboy can still produce income, so you can keep them if you need more cash for your towers. However, this is generally not necessary, as you will get a lot of cash from damaging enemies and the **Fallen King** itself.

- If you want to activate the Hidden Wave, it will be helpful to bring the Gatling Gun, as you can manually aim at the **Fallen King** to quickly kill it instead of having to set your towers to *Strongest* targeting.
Trivia: - The **Fallen King** carries both its sword and shield like the Fallen King before the Overhaul Update, compared to the Fallen King iteration from 2020-2024 which had its shield on the left arm and only revealed its sword in abilities.
Update History: - **Bug**: Poison and electric defense dropping does not decrease **Fallen King's** defense.

Description: The **Fallen King** is the final boss in the Sandbox exclusive Legacy Fallen mode. It was also formerly the final boss in the The Classic Event.

Although it moves somewhat slowly (during its *Rage Mode*, it moves much faster), it has an extreme amount of health and many abilities that can stun several towers and destroy units, making it one of the most difficult challenges in the game. Additionally, the **Fallen King** is a Boss enemy, making it immune to most forms of stalling and the Nuke's fallout damage. It stops moving when performing its *Stomp*, *Rage Mode*, *Block* and *Summon* abilities.
Appearance: **Variant 1**

The **Fallen King** appears to be a being of living stone as the boss appears to be entirely made of granite stone. It is much larger than most enemies that spawn before it, even larger than a normal-sized player. It wears a crown and cape akin to a king's attire, a sword in its scabbard and has a shield on its left hand, all made of stone as well. It has reflective black skin and radiates purple energy.

It is wearing full body armor, including purple boots, and appears to be faceless. However, it gains light blue eyes, a purple-red aura and emits red light upon *Rage Mode*. The armor has multiple light blue glowing parts, on its torso, armbands and kneepads.
**Variant 2**
This version of the **Fallen King** was nearly the same as the original version, except the sword it carried was a glowing purple sword with a purple crystal in the middle of it.
**Variant 3**

The original **Fallen King** appeared to be a being of living stone as the boss appears to be entirely made of granite stone. It wore a crown and cape akin to a king's attire, a sword on its right hand and a shield on its left hand, all made of stone as well.

It was wearing full body armor, including black boots, and appeared to be faceless. However, it gained purple eyes, a purple-red aura and emitted red light upon *Rage Mode*. It radiated purple energy. It was much larger than every enemy that spawned before it.
Strategy: - High DPS towers like the Accelerator, Turret, Engineer and Ranger are recommended against the **Fallen King**.
- The Ranger and Pursuit are immune to all stuns from the **Fallen King's** abilities, making them very useful against the **Fallen King**.
- The **Fallen King** cannot be slowed down by the Toxic Gunner or confused by the Jester.
- As it is a boss enemy, it cannot be frozen though it can still be slowed down through chillness by freezing towers, though it will be less effective.
- Stunning towers like the Electroshocker can only slow it down instead of stunning it.

- While the **Fallen King** performs its *Block* ability, it becomes immune to all sources of damage. It is immobile while the ability is active, as this is mainly to waste time or waste ability duration.
- This can be used as a breathing point to manage your troops, but do not use abilities such as the Commander's *Call to Arms* while this ability is still active.
- Units will pass through the **Fallen King** as it performs its *Block* ability.
- The **Fallen King** will also briefly become immune to all attacks when *Rage Mode* is activated.
- Sometimes, the **Fallen King** may use this ability early when most of the enemies are still alive, which gives your towers more time to attack the enemies that are in front of the **Fallen King**.
- The **Fallen King** is accompanied by four Fallen Guardians. They are always in front of the **Fallen King**. They should be fought first since they are faster than the **Fallen King**.
- Beware of the **Fallen King's** *Stomp* attack. This covers an enormous radius around the boss, stunning any ground troops caught in the radius.
- Cliff towers and air-based towers, such as the Ranger and Pursuit are not affected by this attack.
- You can use the Medic's ability to shield towers from stuns. The Medic itself is immune to all of the **Fallen King's** attacks.
- The *Stomp* attack will instantly destroy most units caught in the shockwave, as it deals 500 damage to all units.
Trivia: - The first version **Fallen King's** sword and shield are very similar to the Epic Golden Sword and Shield, and its crown is identical to the Korblox Ice Crown, both items from the Roblox catalog.
- During Hardcore Testing BETA, the **Fallen King** had a different type of sword. It was a re-textured version of the Cythrex' Sword accessory from the Roblox catalog.
- The **Fallen King** could be based on a phenomenon of a king losing his kingdom.
- Fallen Kingdom by CaptainSparklez is a viral example of this.
- It could also represent a sort of fallen or lost kingdom, given some of the enemy names that appeared earlier.
- The **Fallen King** was the only major boss of the three main gamemodes (Easy, Molten, Fallen) that was not in the game before the MEGA Update.
- The **Fallen King** used to appear alongside the Molten Boss on the second version of the "You Lost" screen.
- The cape used by the original **Fallen King** was a re-textured version of the Black Iron Cape accessory from the Roblox catalog.
- A crewmate version of the original **Fallen King** can be seen on the *Suspicious...* badge and the April Fools 2021 thumbnail.
- The **Fallen King** can be seen as a chess piece in the Chess Board map, representing the King chess piece.
- The **Fallen King** is the first major boss to have a variation of itself, being the Nuclear Fallen King.
- The **Fallen King** was originally leaked alongside the Frozen, Deep Freeze and Frost Hero. However, it was not released until the MEGA Update.
- The **Fallen King's** stomp radius is actually larger than the Void Reaver's stomp radius despite being weaker.
- Prior to the Overhaul Update, the **Fallen King** was one of the few enemies and the only boss to gain a shield. This shield reduced the damage dealt by most towers to 3.
- The Logbook it drops only unlocks the entry for the modern version but not the legacy **Fallen King**.

Description: The **Fallen Necromancer** is a summoner enemy that appears in Fallen, Fallen Arena PVP modes and The Takeover Event. It has high health but has a speed slightly slower than the Fallen Squire. It has an ability where it slams its staff, summoning eight Fallen Skeletons.
Logbook Description: "*Fallen Necromancers were priests who used to tend to the dead, ensuring peaceful passage to the afterlife. When the Queen's sacrifice destroyed the boundary between life and death, they gained the power to raise the fallen. The curse allowed them to cast dark rituals that bind souls to corpses. Now, they are protected by the very dead they once laid to rest.*"
Appearance: The **Fallen Necromancer** has no legs and greyish skin. It has a silver crown that has a blue shard in the middle and silver horns. It has a tiger skull with horns on each shoulder, possibly serving as shoulder pads. It wears a grey scarf and a necklace with possibly shark teeth on it, and a blue crystal. Its arms have bluish-grey arm plates, bandages and metal. It has a grey chest-plate. It also wears a belt.
It wields a grey staff with a skull at the top, and holds it over its shoulder while walking. It slams the staff to the ground and conjures purple smoke when using its *Summon* ability.
It has a death animation where it spins while falling to the ground, dropping its staff.
Strategy: - The **Fallen Necromancer** can be a threat when it first appears, as it can summon many Fallen Skeletons if not killed quickly, creating hordes, especially in groups.
- Early game towers like the Militant, Golden Cowboy, Ace Pilot, Brawler or Golden Scout can take care of the **Fallen Necromancer** quite quickly.
- High DPS towers like the Turret, Minigunner, Hunter and Accelerator can also be quite useful.

- Do note that the Accelerator, if locked onto the **Fallen Necromancer** or other strong enemies, will ignore the Fallen Skeletons the **Fallen Necromancer** summons until the targeted enemy is defeated or leaves its range.

- The Ranger may struggle against the hordes of Fallen Skeletons the **Fallen Necromancer** summons due to its slow firerate. It can be set to *Strongest* to target and kill the **Fallen Necromancer** while other towers take care of the Fallen Skeletons.
- Area of effect towers, like the Mortar, Rocketeer and Tesla can be quite useful as they can damage both the **Fallen Necromancer** and the Fallen Skeletons it summons.
- Do note that you do not earn any money from the summoned enemies.
- The **Fallen Necromancer** and its Fallen Skeletons move at a somewhat fast pace. You may want to use slowing towers like the Freezer, Warden or Tesla, though this is not necessary.

- Do note that because of its Stun Immunity, it is only slowed down by stuns and cannot be knocked back. Additionally, when it first spawns, it is a boss enemy, making chillness and stun slowdown the only forms of stalling that can slow it down.

- Stalling towers with the ability to hit multiple enemies, such as the Tesla, Freezer or Frost Blaster, are particularly effective against the **Fallen Necromancer** as they can also stall the summoned Fallen Skeletons without taking their attention away from the **Fallen Necromancer**.

Description: The **Fallen Reaper** was a summoner enemy which only appeared in Hardcore mode. Currently, it can only be spawned in Sandbox mode if the player has the Sandbox Plus+ gamepass. It has one ability; it periodically swings it scythe forwards into the ground to summon random enemies. At its debut, it can spawn the Invisible or Hefty, though it can begin to spawn the Fallen Soul or Fallen starting from wave 25 or the Lava starting from wave 38.

The **Fallen Reaper** has an average amount of health for its debut and moves at an average speed. It also has Stun Immunity, which prevents the Warden and Electroshocker from completely stopping it, instead slowing it down and prevents it from being knocked back.
Appearance: The **Fallen Reaper** is similar to the Dark Necromancer, but it does not have legs. Instead, it floats slightly above the path. It has reflective black skin, a dark black marble jacket with grey skull shoulder pads with neon purple eyes and a dark grey dominus. A dark purple chain is wrapped around its torso. It wields a neon purple scythe that can summon enemies.
Strategy: This strategy refers to the state of the game while the **Invisible** still appeared in the Hardcore mode.
- Deal with this enemy as soon as possible before its summons threaten your defenses.
- From wave 25, if the **Fallen Reaper** is left unattended, it will start to spawn Fallen Souls which can increase the firerate of your towers, making them shoot slower.
- They can also spawn Fallens which are very quick and may outrun your towers.
- High DPS towers, like the Minigunner, Accelerator and Ranger, can deal with the **Fallen Reaper**.
- You may want to set their targeting to *Strongest* to ignore the summoned enemies, though this may be risky.
- The Electroshocker and Sledger can be quite useful at slowing this down. They can also deal a decent amount of damage to both the **Fallen Reaper** and the enemies it spawns.
- Do note that stunning towers like the Warden cannot stop it completely due to its Stun Immunity, slowing it down instead. Additionally, this immunity also makes it immune to knockback.
- The Military Base's Tank can be effective against the **Fallen Reaper** and the enemies it summons.
Trivia: - The **Fallen Reaper's** scythe is very similar to the Molten Boss's scythe, except that it is colored purple.
- The **Fallen Reaper** could be considered the Fallen version of the Reaper.
- The **Fallen Reaper** is the only way for the Fallen Soul to appear in Hardcore mode.
- The **Fallen Reaper** can also spawn Fallens way before its debut wave (46) in Hardcore mode.
Update History: - Energy Immunity replaced with Stun Immunity.
- **Bug**: **Fallen Reaper** no longer uses the death sound effect.
- **Fallen Reaper** removed from the main game, as it has been replaced by Void Reaper. Now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.

Logbook Description: *"Fallen Rushers were the kingdom's frontline shield, trained to charge head-first into battle. Their role was to push through the enemy defenses. They wore light armor for speed and most knew they would not survive, but they did it willingly to protect those who followed after them. Their shield can be destroyed, leaving them defenseless."*

Description: The **Fallen Rusher** was an extremely fast enemy that only appeared in Hardcore mode. Currently, it can only be spawned in Sandbox mode if the player has the Sandbox Plus+ gamepass. Although it has low health, it holds a shield and moves extremely fast, being faster than every enemy currently in the game. This makes it a very dangerous threat if you do not have the right towers. It will lose its shield when all of its shield health has depleted, making it run at a fast pace.
Appearance: The **Fallen Rusher's** appearance is similar to the Rusher enemy from Polluted Wasteland and Legacy Fallen. It has black reflective skin and granite, dark turquoise torso and legs. It wears a mask with purple neon parts, a chestplate with purple parts, and black and neon purple armbands. It also has black boots, gloves and knee-pads. While running, it holds up a shield in front of it with its left arm.
Strategy: This strategy refers to the state of the game while the **Invisible** still appeared in the Hardcore mode.
- Destroy the **Fallen Rusher's** shield to slow it down as soon as possible.
- High DPS towers, such as the Minigunner, Turret and Engineer, can deal with these enemies quickly.
- The Commander can boost the firerate of towers, making it easier to deal with **Fallen Rushers**.
- The Accelerator is also recommended, however be aware that the **Fallen Rusher** may outrun its charge-up time if placed in a bad spot.
- Military Base vehicles, Elf Camp's units and Crook Boss minions can be useful against the **Fallen Rusher** if it gets past your towers.
- The Toxic Gunner can be useful to slow down these enemies to a slower and more manageable speed for a few seconds.
- As they have average size, the Electroshocker, Frost Blaster and Freezer can stop the **Fallen Rusher**.
- The Sledger is generally not recommended against this, as the **Fallen Rusher** can easily avoid being hit by it due to its slow firerate and low range.
- A Level 5 Golden Pyromancer can easily break the shields of a horde of **Fallen Rushers**.
Trivia: - The **Fallen Rusher** is the fallen version of the Rusher, but significantly weaker.
- A new version of the **Fallen Rusher** was added to Fallen Mode.
- This is the second fastest enemy in the game when it has its shield, with the Imposter being faster.
- The speed of the **Fallen Rusher** is nearly the same as the player walk speed, having a speed of 15 while the player has a speed of 16.
- The **Fallen Rusher** uses a similar shield to the legacy Fallen King.
- The **Fallen Rusher** used a regular walking animation when it did not have its shield during Hardcore Testing BETA.
- It now uses a similar animation to the Fallen when it loses its shield.
- The sound effect that plays when the **Fallen Rusher** loses its shield is a lower pitched version of the sound effect of the Lead Boss losing its covering.
Update History: - **Bug**: Has a broken animation in Sandbox mode.
- **Bug**: Uses its no shield walking animation while still having its shield in the Index.
- No longer copies the statistics of the modern version in Sandbox mode.
- **Bugfix**: Animation now works in Sandbox mode.
- **Fallen Rusher** removed from the main game, as it has been replaced by Void Rusher. Now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.
- No longer appears in the Index.

Description: The **Fallen Seraph** is a Flying enemy that appears in Fallen mode. It is the first flying enemy the player encounters in the mode. As it is a flying enemy, only towers with flying detection can target it. It has a decent amount of health and decent speed.
Logbook Description: "*Fallen Seraphs were the kingdom's messengers, blessed with wings to carry word from Two X's throne. They flew above the realm, often heard singing tales of the kingdom's history. When the Queen's curse spread, their songs grew quiet, and their wings changed from a vibrant glistening scarlet to coal black.*"
Appearance: The **Fallen Seraph** has blue skin. Its torso and legs are dark blue. It has dark blue wings on its back. It also has a dark blue halo above its head with dark blue chains on its torso.
Strategy: - Towers with flying detection, such as the Ranger, Militant, Golden Soldier or Ace Pilot are recommended against this.
- As they spawn in hordes, the Tesla, Mortar and Hallow Punk can be useful against them.
- The Commander's *Support Caravan* ability can be useful against these enemies, as the Gunner APC and Missile APC have flying detection.
- While the **Fallen Seraph** does not have any immunities, it gains an immunity to being knocked back which is given by default to any Flying enemy.
- This means that towers like the DJ Booth, Brawler or Warlock are fully or partially unable to stall it.
- The UAV can be useful by providing flying detection to your towers.
- The Gift Bomber cannot collide with the **Fallen Seraph**.
Trivia: - In Christianity, a seraph is a class of angel with six wings.
- Oddly, the Fallen Angel bears more similarity to a seraph, leading to the possibility that the names of these two enemies were switched.
- The **Fallen Seraph** looks very similar to the Crying Angel from Krampus Frosthold and the Crying Angel from Outpost 32.
Update History: - Speed decreased from Fast (6) to Above Average (4).
- Cash given increased from $500 to $1,000 on death.
- First wave appearance changed from Wave 29 to Wave 22.
- Speed increased from Above Average (4) to Slightly Fast (4.5).

Description: The **Fallen Shield** is a very large enemy that appears in Fallen, Fallen Arena PVP modes and also The Takeover Event. It has high health, Shield Health, a decent speed and 50% defense, which reduces most forms of damage by 33%. It has Stun Immunity, making stunning towers only slow it down and preventing knockback towers from knocking it back. It is a Boss enemy when it first spawns.
When it loses all of its Shield Health, the **Fallen Shield** will begin charging, increasing its speed temporarily, slowing down back to its regular speed after a few seconds.
The **Fallen Shield** can be spawned by the Awakened Fallen King with its *Army of Chaos* ability.
Logbook Description: "*Fallen Shields were trained to absorb incoming attacks while protecting their allies. They stood before the throne as the final defense to invaders. The curse tarnished them as all fell under control of the Fallen King. They protect nothing now but the one who once had everything.*"
Appearance: The **Fallen Shield** wears dark teal and silver armor. This armor covers most of its body, with the exception of its left arm. This arm has blue skin with multiple bandages wrapped around it. It wields a massive shield in front of it and a mace to its side. When its ability activates, it changes stance and charges forward with particles trailing behind it. When it is defeated, it has a death animation where it tosses its shield, then falls over.
Strategy: - The **Fallen Shield** mainly appears right before other high-health enemies that spawn, such as the Fallen Summoner, serving to protect and tank incoming damage to allow these enemies to progress further. In some of the later waves, it will be the first to appear and further lead enemies along the path that are behind it.
- This is also problematic when it spawns with status effects like Bloated and Nimble, further protecting and leading the horde.
- You should utilize high DPS towers, such as the Accelerator, Engineer and Turret to defeat the **Fallen Shield** as quickily as possible.
- The DJ Booth, Commander and Mercenary Base can be used to boost these towers.

- In addition, it may be best to drain all of the **Fallen Shield's** Shield Health first, as its *Charge of the Light Brigade* ability automatically triggers after it loses all of its shield health. You can set some towers to *Strongest* to target it directly.
- As the **Fallen Shield** is quite fast for its health, towers that slow down enemies, such as the Trapper, Tesla or Warden can be pretty useful here.
- When it first spawns, the only way to slow it down is by stunning it, as its immunities prevent all other forms of stalling from affecting it.
- It cannot be frozen or chilled by freezing towers, making them useless against it.
- You can use defense dropping towers, such as the Pyromancer to decrease this enemy's defense.
Update History: - **Bug**: Poison and electric defense dropping does not decrease **Fallen Shield's** defense.

- **Bug**: It is possible to stunlock the **Fallen Shield** by constantly stunning it during its animation before it gains the speed boost. Has to be stuns specifically, like the Flash Bang or Trapper's bear trap, not shock like from the Electroshocker.
