Description: The **Fallen Skeleton**, which uses a display name of *Skeleton* in-game, is an enemy that appears in Fallen mode, Fallen Arena PVP mode, Badlands II and The Takeover Event. The **Fallen Skeleton** can be spawned by the Fallen Necromancer. In Badlands II, it is turned into a Hidden enemy for all of its natural spawns.
Logbook Description: "*Fallen Skeletons are the remains of those who died as the magic began to fade. The Fallen Necromancers discovered they could bind these bones with cursed energy, giving them life once more. Now, they rise from the ground to serve as shields for their summoners as some wander aimlessly within the army. In death, they finally have purpose, though it is not the kind they had hoped for.*"
Appearance: The **Fallen Skeleton** is made entirely of desaturated sand colored parts that resemble a skeletal humanoid. It does not have a full torso, but instead has the bone cage for it. Its head is much smaller and is shaped like a skull, with a part of the spine column attached to it. It emits light blue flames from its eye sockets.
On death, the **Fallen Skeleton** falls into a pile of bones while playing a bone shaking sound.
Strategy: - The **Fallen Skeleton** has much more health than both the Abnormal and Quick, making it quite dangerous against weak defenses. It is therefore best to invest in additional defense before and after it appears.
- Great early game DPS towers like the Brawler, Militant, Shotgunner and Ace Pilot can deal with the **Fallen Skeleton**.

- Stronger towers such as the Minigunner and Hunter can fare against it more effectively if you can afford them. Utilizing the Farm and Cowboy are reccommended to boost your income in case you plan to do so.

- Later on in the game, after the Fallen Necromancer makes its debut, the **Fallen Skeleton** can be a threat as many can be summoned by the Fallen Necromancer if it is not killed quickly, leading to other problems.
- Killing the Fallen Necromancer before it can summon any **Fallen Skeletons** is recommended.
- Towers like the Soldier, Golden Scout, Militant or Ace Pilot can be quite effective against this.
- High DPS towers like the Minigunner and Accelerator can be prepared specifically for this enemy if early game towers are not enough, using the Farm to get them as they may be quite expensive.
- Do note that the Accelerator, if locked onto the Fallen Necromancer or other strong enemies, will ignore the **Fallen Skeletons** until the targeted enemy is defeated or leaves its range.

- The Ranger struggles against hordes of **Fallen Skeletons** due to its slow firerate. It can instead be set to *Strongest* to target and kill the Fallen Necromancer while other towers take care of the **Fallen Skeletons**.

- Area of effect towers, like the Mortar, Rocketeer or Gladiator can be quite useful as they can damage all the **Fallen Skeletons** when they are in a group, as well as the Fallen Necromancer at once.

- While you cannot earn any money from the **Fallen Skeleton** outside of Badlands II as it appears as a summoned enemy later on, you can still gain money from the **Fallen Skeleton** when it appears in the early game, as it spawns by itself, making it not a summoned enemy.
- The **Fallen Skeleton** moves at a somewhat fast pace. You may want to use support towers to slow them down, though this is not usually necessary.
- In the early game, cheap stunning towers like the Electroshocker can be utilized.

- Later on, the Sledger, Frost Blaster and a higher level Electroshocker are particularly effective as they can slow multiple **Fallen Skeletons** down at once. Additionally, their high damage makes them also useful at killing **Fallen Skeletons**.

Description: The **Fallen Soul** is an enemy that appears in Fallen and Fallen Arena PVP modes. It has a decent amount of health with above average speed. As it is a Hidden enemy, only towers with hidden detection can target it.
Logbook Description: "*Fallen Souls were the spirits of those who died before the curse took hold. The Queen's sacrifice broke down the wall between life and death, pulling these souls back into the now-corrupted realm. They drift through battlefields, unable to rest or return to the kingdom they once knew. They are nearly invisible — most people only feel a cold breeze as they pass by.*"
Appearance: The **Fallen Soul** has dark blue skin. It does not have a head, torso or legs, though it does have a brown skull and rib cage. It wears a grey helmet with blue spikes, grey cloth around its waist and has chains wrapped around its arms. It also had multiple blue spikes on its shoulders and grey gloves.
Strategy: - Most early game towers gain hidden detection. Such towers are recommended to deal with early **Fallen Souls**.
- Single target towers, like the Militant, Golden Soldier, Ace Pilot or Assassin, can also clear out groups of **Fallen Souls**, although they will require more cash to successfully eliminate them.
- As **Fallen Souls** spawn in hordes, the Golden Pyromancer is particularly useful, being able to damage multiple enemies at once and having hidden detection by default.
- The Pyromancer can also be useful against **Fallen Souls**, although it costs more and does not have hidden detection at base level.

- Though the Trapper cannot detect hidden enemies, its traps will still work against them. In particular, its landmines can be used to eliminate groups of **Fallen Souls** due to its high splash damage.
- For splash damage towers that cannot target **Fallen Souls**, such as the Mortar, if a **Fallen Soul** is caught up in an explosion, they will take damage from the explosion range.
- This means that another detectable enemy must be near the **Fallen Soul** for a splash damage tower to hit the **Fallen Soul**.
- Similarly, the Tesla cannot target the **Fallen Soul**, however, it can hit it if there are other detectable enemies nearby.
Trivia: - The model used by the **Fallen Soul** is a slightly modified model of the Korblox Soul.

Description: The **Fallen Soul** was an enemy that only appeared in Hardcore mode. Currently, it can only be spawned in Sandbox mode if the player has the Sandbox Plus+ gamepass. It can only be summoned by the Fallen Reaper when it uses its ability from wave 25 onwards. It does not appear naturally.

While it has low health and above average speed, its main ability is to slash at towers with its axe. This will apply a 75% Fatigue Debuff to towers, increasing their firerate and decreasing their DPS, not inclusive of the Firerate Bug. It also has Stun Immunity, which makes the Warden and Electroshocker only slow it down instead of completely stopping it and prevents it from being knocked back.
Appearance: The **Fallen Soul** appears to be a knight about the same size as the Abnormal. Its entire body has a dark, reflective complexion. It has black armor that has a purple gem at the front and skull shoulder-pads that have purple eyes, similar to the Fallen Hero. Its helmet has black horns. It wields an axe on its right arm. This axe is held upside down, similar to the Fallen Swordmaster.
Strategy: This strategy refers to the state of the game while the **Invisible** still appeared in the Hardcore mode.
- As this enemy is decently fast but weak, Level 3 Military Bases can deal with these quickly.
- The Humvee 2 and Humvee 3 can instantly kill the **Fallen Soul** by colliding with it.
- However, they might come in swarms from the Fallen Reaper, so prepare any high DPS towers such as the Minigunner.
- It is recommended to place your towers away from the path to prevent the **Fallen Soul** from attacking and debuffing them.

- Because this spawns along with the minions of the Fallen Reaper, it will be paired up with Invisibles, Hefties and Fallens. Make sure your towers have hidden detection to deal with the Invisibles, and that your DPS is high enough to deal with the Hefties and Fallens.
- A Commander should be placed to boost the firerate of nearby towers, both passively and with its *Call to Arms*.
- If any towers are hit by the **Fallen Soul**, the Commander can mitigate some of the effects.
Trivia: - Unlike the Soul and Soul Boss, this is not a hidden or ghost enemy.

Logbook Description: "*Fallen Squires served as attendants to the kingdom's Champions. They trained restlessly and were known for their loyalty and dedication. When the curse was released, their Champions fell and it drove them to search endlessly for the Templars. On the battlefield, the Fallen Squires are unmatched in combat. Description: The **Fallen Summoner** is a summoner enemy that appears in Fallen mode. It also appears in The Takeover Event. It is a stronger version of the Fallen Necromancer. It moves slower but has way more health and stronger abilities. It has two abilities, the first is *Summon*, where it summons three Necrotic Skeletons. Its second ability, *Ghost State*, only happens when it loses half of its health. It will become a Hidden enemy, which also makes it slightly translucent.
Logbook Description: "*Fallen Summoners were high priests who once called upon Two X's power to protect their people, but no one answered. Those who once commenced sacred rituals and called upon lost magic now raise armies of Necrotic Skeletons to fight in the Fallen King's apocalypse.*"
Appearance: The **Fallen Summoner** has black skin. It has neon blue eyes and a white mouth. It wears a black and blue robe with a hood. This robe has a few blue gems on it. The robe's hood has horns on it. It wears skull shoulder-pads with neon blue eyes and black horns. It walks with a staff which, when used, creates purple smoke.
Upon death, it falls to its knees and drops its staff, dropping to the ground shortly after.
Strategy: - The **Fallen Summoner** mainly spawns at the very back of Wave 30 and other later waves that it appears on. In most cases, it spawns behind higher health enemies like the Fallen Tank and the Fallen Shield that tank the majority of damage, allowing the **Fallen Summoner** to continuously summon Necrotic Skeletons.

- Dealing with this enemy as soon as possible is crucial, as leaving it alive for too long can allow it to summon a vast number of Necrotic Skeletons, in addition to the number of enemies ahead of it that can otherwise be overwhelming to your defense.

- To target it, you can set some high DPS towers like the Turret, Minigunner or Crook Boss to *Last* to directly target the **Fallen Summoner**, as it will most likely appear in the very back of the horde.
- However, you should still keep the majority of your defense set to *First* to deal with tankier and faster enemies in front of it to maintain the defense output.
- The Saboteur can also be used to force towers to target it while also increasing how much damage it receives.

- High DPS towers with splash damage capabilities can be very beneficial, as they can hit both the **Fallen Summoner** and the enemies it summons. Such towers include the Ranger, Pursuit, Minigunner and Engineer.
- In addition, area of effect towers like the Mortar or Tesla can be useful at dealing with the enemies spawned by the **Fallen Summoner**.
- At half health, the **Fallen Summoner** will become Hidden, so make sure you have sufficient hidden detection source.
- The Ace Pilot and UAV can be used to give towers that do not have hidden detection, such as the Ranger hidden detection, allowing them to kill it.
- The Tesla can be very useful at slowing it down, however do note that it does not have hidden detection.
- No cash can be generated from summoned enemies. This includes the Cowboy's cash generation.
- However, this also means that the Cowboy will deal more DPS to the summons, as attacking summoned enemies does not make it spin its guns, making it attack for longer.

Description: The **Fallen Swordmaster** was a major boss that only appeared as the third boss in Hardcore mode. Currently, it can only be spawned in Sandbox mode if the player has the Sandbox Plus+ gamepass. It was based on the Swordmaster from the SFOTH Event. This version, however, has over three times the base health of the Swordmaster.

As with most major bosses, the **Fallen Swordmaster** has an extremely high amount of health. While the **Fallen Swordmaster** walks quite slowly, after it uses its *Refusing Will* move (a variant of Rage Mode that activates at half health), it will speed up in movement, making it very dangerous. While it cannot spawn any enemies of its own, its abilities can stun lots of towers in a short period of time.
Appearance: The **Fallen Swordmaster** has reflective black skin and glowing purple eyes. It has a dark red crown that is slightly tilted, a purple undershirt, and dark purple tattered pants and jacket. It wields two Darkheart swords that are held upside down. Being a major boss, it is significantly larger than the average enemy.
Strategy: - Towers that deal high DPS, like the Golden Minigunner, Pursuit, Turret, Engineer and Accelerator can be useful to take down the **Fallen Swordmaster** quickly.
- The Ranger can also be used, due to its high DPS and Stun Immunity.
- Cheap towers can provide a distraction for the **Fallen Swordmaster's** *Dagger Throw*.
- This can be particularly useful as the **Fallen Swordmaster** stops moving to throw its swords.
- However, do beware that the attack stuns towers around the target, meaning that poor placement can stun lots of towers at once.
- If possible, try to spread out your towers.
- In addition, after the **Fallen Swordmaster's** *Refusing Will* ability is activated, the **Fallen Swordmaster** can throw 4-5 swords at towers, instead of 3.
- However, this wastes a tower slot in the late game which can be used to deal more damage.
- Units can be quite useful against the **Fallen Swordmaster**, as it has no attack that destroys units before they collide.
- This makes the Engineer's sentries very useful against the **Fallen Swordmaster**.
- However, once the **Fallen Swordmaster** activates its *Refusing Will* ability, all units will phase through it, given that it temporarily gains Full Immunity.
- The Commander's *Call to Arms* ability is recommended against the **Fallen Swordmaster**.

- You can time the ability to avoid the **Fallen Swordmaster** from performing its *Refusing Will* move. If it has recently performed an ability, and you can kill the **Fallen Swordmaster** quickly from when it reaches 75,000 health, this move will not be performed.
- The DJ Booth can also be used so that towers that are out of range of the **Fallen Swordmaster** can attack while being out of the range of some of the **Fallen Swordmaster's** attacks.
- You can use the Medic's ability to shield towers from stuns performed by the **Fallen Swordmaster**.
Trivia: - The **Fallen Swordmaster** is the resurrected version of the original Swordmaster, as stated by a tweet.
- It also suggests that other Pre-MEGA enemies were meant to be brought back, however only the **Fallen Swordmaster** and Lava were brought back into the game.
- The **Fallen Swordmaster** could be spawned before the Overhaul Update through commands.
- Weirdly, the health of the **Fallen Swordmaster** was increased in MEGA Servers, despite it not being able to spawn in a MEGA Server without admin commands.
- The **Fallen Swordmaster** can be seen as a chess piece in the Chess Board map, representing the Queen chess piece.
- The Void Swordmaster is the successor to the Fallen Swordmaster.

Description: The **Fallen Tank** is an enemy that appears in Fallen, Challenge Trials and Fallen Arena PVP modes. It also appears in The Takeover Event. It has a high amount of health and a fast speed, as fast as the Corrupted Fallen.
Logbook Description: "*Fallen Tanks were siege specialists who broke through enemy lines during the kingdom's golden age. They wore the heaviest armor and were the quickest in their class. When cursed, their bodies fused with their equipment, making them significantly more resilient.*"
Appearance: The **Fallen Tank** is a knight completely covered in grey and blue armor. On its knee-pads, shoulder-pads and belt, it has multiple blue gems. It has chains on its arms. It constantly stumbles on the path as it walks.
When killed, the **Fallen Tank** will trip and fall on to the ground.
Strategy: - High DPS towers, such as the Accelerator, Engineer and Turret are recommended to take this enemy down.
- The DJ Booth, Commander and Mercenary Base can be used to boost these towers.
- The Necromancer's units can also be used to quickly deal with it, though note that this may not be the most consistent counter.

- Because of the **Fallen Tank's** fast speed, long-ranged towers such as the Ranger can be a great counter, as it has one of the largest ranges in the game, being able to cover most of the maps. This means that the **Fallen Tank** will take more time to get out of its range.

- Do be aware that certain maps with a shorter path length, like Dead Ahead are not suited for long-ranged towers due to the extremely short amount of time that it takes for enemies to reach the base. Because of this flaw paired with the **Fallen Tank's** fast speed, you are better off using towers with instant high DPS capabilities. Longer maps such as Four Seasons adapt better to long-range towers.
- Stalling towers, such as the Warden, Tesla, Freezer or Archer, can be used to slow the **Fallen Tank** down, as it is quite fast.
- Due to its large size, certain forms of stalling like freeze or knockback will slow it down for a shorter amount of time.

- Note that, in the Hidden Wave, this is practically mandatory in order to handle the Nimble and Bloated Fallen Tanks that spawn there. For your own sake, bring some form of stalling if you dare to attempt Hidden Wave.

abilities.label: Ability 2
abilities.text: **Smash** - Smashes its hammer into the ground which causes a straight purple shockwave, stunning towers and dealing 60 damage to units. Can be only used while its hammer has been taken out.

Description: The **Fallen Titan** was an enemy that only appeared in Hardcore mode. Currently, it can only be spawned in Sandbox mode if the player has the Sandbox Plus+ gamepass. For its debut, it had a high amount of health, presenting a major challenge. It also had Shield Health, meaning that you did not earn any money from the initial 1,000 health. Initially, it spawns with its hammer on its back. However, at some point, it will stop to wield its hammer. While this reduces its speed, it can now use its hammer to stun towers and damage units. A shield also appears when it takes out its hammer, however it is only visual. Additionally, it has Stun Immunity, meaning that it cannot be completely stopped by the Warden and Electroshocker and it cannot be knocked back.
Appearance: The **Fallen Titan** has reflective black skin and a neon purple faceless face. It wears a dark purple granite galea helmet, with horns sticking out the side of it. It also wears a dark purple chestplate, knee-pads and shoulder-pads, which are spiky. Its torso and legs are dark purple too. It wears black boots and gloves. Its head is slightly tilted sideways. On its back is a deep granite sharp hammer with spikes on it. This can be held by the **Fallen Titan** after its *Hammer* ability. Purple particles are emitted from its boots, torso and hammer.
Strategy: This strategy refers to the state of the game while the **Fallen Titan** still appeared in the Hardcore mode.
- Due to its high health, high DPS towers are recommended against this, such as the Accelerator, Minigunner, Turret and Ranger.
- While it may seem like the damage is capped at 40 due to its shield, this shield is only visual. For example, a tower like the Ranger can deal full damage to it, even if the damage is over 40.
- The Engineer can be very useful against this enemy, as the Engineer's sentries can continue attacking the **Fallen Titan** even when the Engineer is stunned.
- While the **Fallen Titan** can damage its units, the damage dealt is low and can only destroy Sentry and Rifle Sentry (without shield) in one hit, while others will survive.
- You can also use the Medic to make the Engineer itself immune to stuns, making the sentries practically invulnerable to the stuns.
- Make sure to defeat the **Fallen Titan** as fast as possible. If you can, try to kill it before it can equip its hammer.
- You may want to set your towers' targeting to *Strongest* to ensure this.
- It is not possible to use the Medic to prevent its stuns, as when hit by the shockwave, the shield will disappear and the tower will end up getting stunned.
- Towers like Freezer, Sledger, Warden and Frost Blaster will only slow down the **Fallen Titan** for a short amount of time due to its large size.
- The Electroshocker and Toxic Gunner are unaffected by its size.
- It also has Stun Immunity, which prevents stunning towers like the Warden from stunning it, slowing it down instead and makes knockback towers like the Brawler not knock it back.
- As the **Fallen Titan** takes out its hammer when there are towers nearby, reducing its speed, it may be beneficial to place down few cheap towers next to the path to slow it down.
- As it can stun towers with its hammer, it is recommended to put such towers very close to the path away from where most towers are placed to prevent the **Fallen Titan** from stunning them.
Trivia: - The **Fallen Titan** is quite similar to the original Frost Hero in terms of abilities.
- In terms of appearance, it is similar to the legacy Molten Titan and the legacy Fallen Soul.
- The **Fallen Titan** is the first enemy to have two death animations.
- The first only occurs when its *Hammer* ability has not been used. It will fall with the hammer on its back.
- The second only occurs when its *Hammer* ability has been used. It will fall with the hammer on the side.
- The horns on the **Fallen Titan** are a re-textured version of the Fiery Horns Of The Netherworld accessory from the Roblox catalog.
- The helmet worn by the **Fallen Titan** is a re-textured version of the Winged Helm of the Redcliff Elite accessory from the Roblox catalog.
- The shoulder guards worn by the **Fallen Titan** are a re-textured version of the Crushing Crystals Pauldrons accessory from the Roblox catalog.
- The hammer used by the **Fallen Titan** is an altered version of the Ice Sledge from *Reason 2 Die: Awakening.*
- The **Fallen Titan** will always use its *Hammer* ability a few seconds after spawning. If there are no towers nearby, it will put the hammer back on its back.
- The Shield that the **Fallen Titan** has is purely visual. The damage dealt to it can be higher than 40 even when the Shield is active.
- This results in the **Fallen Titan** being the only enemy currently with Shield, albeit the latter not functioning as intended.
Update History: - **Bug**: **Fallen Titan** freezes towers instead of stunning them.
- **Bug**: *Smash* ability hitbox size is significantly larger than it should be.

Description: **Felipe**, internally referred to as the **Trophy**, was the final boss of the Backyard Legends Event. It had high health but very slow speed.

It had two abilities. Its first, *Smash*, in which it slams its fists onto a tower or unit, stunning it and other nearby towers for 3 seconds and doing 1,000 damage to units. Its second, *Throw*, had it throw a rock at a nearby tower or unit, which then splits into four smaller rocks. Each rock stuns towers for 5 seconds and does 500 damage to units per rock.
Appearance: **Felipe** has green skin, a bulky body and large lower arms. It wears a white Adidas T-shirt with the sleeves being black, black shorts, nylon webbing containing a packet of sports bottle, backwards sports cap, white socks and stylized Adidas shoes. Both sleeves have a white Adidas symbol on the sides while having three horizontal stripes on the top of each sleeve; at the bottom, it contains one white line. On the right of **Felipe's** shirt, there is a black Adidas symbol patch. The T-shirt has a black collar and a stylized fade black honeycomb pattern starting from half of the torso down until the waist.

Description: **Fey Yoshida** was the final enemy in the Metaverse Champions Event. However, **Fey Yoshida** was not a major boss. Compared to other enemies that spawned in the Metaverse Champions Event, **Fey Yoshida** had high health, but had the same speed as the Normal Boss.

Defeating **Fey Yoshida** rewarded players with AJ's Crate Drop #4, if they had not earned the crate from any other Week 4 AJ Striker game in the Roblox Metaverse Champions Event. This crate would open to reward AJ's Drone Swarm.
Appearance: **Fey Yoshida** was one of the champions of the Roblox Metaverse Champions Event. Unlike most other enemies in the game, **Fey Yoshida** used an Rthro package. It had grey skin, pink hair, purple cap and white headphones. It wore a green to blue fade jacket, and had a purple shirt and pants. It also wore black shoes. **Fey Yoshida** was seen doing the Praisin emote while moving.
Strategy: - The Minigunner can easily defeat **Fey Yoshida**.
- Placing many Scouts and Snipers can also be effective.
- The Rocketeer may be useful in clearing other enemies that spawn alongside **Fey Yoshida**, though its poor single target damage makes it ineffective against **Fey Yoshida** itself.
- You can allow **Fey Yoshida** to get to the end, provided you have enough health remaining when the wave ends.
- Do note that you can use the **Golden** skins of the provided towers to aid you.
Trivia: - **Fey Yoshida** is one of the opposing teams to AJ in the Metaverse Champions Event, hence why it is referred to as AJ's "*arch nemesis*".
- **Fey Yoshida** is the first enemy to use an entirely Roblox made package, the second being the Korblox Deathwalker.

Description: The **Fleshling** is an enemy that appears in Polluted Wasteland II. It is an enemy that is introduced naturally on Wave 15, preceding the appearance of the Amalgamation within the same wave. After Wave 15, it only spawns when the Amalgamation takes damage. It has low health, but is slightly fast and always spawns in groups.
Appearance: The **Fleshling** is a humanoid with a light red skin color. It has a bear trap fitted around its head and it has multiple clumps of flesh and smaller humanoids sticking out of its body.
Strategy: - High DPS towers, such as the Ranger, Pursuit or Engineer are recommended to take down this enemy.
- All the listed towers also receive splash damage capabilities at certain Levels, making them able to damage multiple **Fleshlings** at once.
- The Accelerator can also be quite powerful against **Fleshlings** , though do note that it might lock on the Amalgamation causing the **Fleshlings** to slip by.
- Since multiple of them spawn at once, towers that can damage multiple enemies like the Golden Pyromancer, Mortar or Electroshocker can be good at dealing with groups of **Fleshlings**.
Trivia: - The **Fleshling**, despite never being intended to appear in a server with more than four players, has MEGA Servers health scaling. It increases its health by 150 for every player after 4 players.
- Due to 150 being close to as much as its regular health, its health is basically doubled in five player servers and tripled in six player servers.
- This is most likely carried over from the original Amalgamation, which also increased its health by 150.
Update History: - None of the changes are applied to the legacy version.

That desire for speed and weaponry in his veins set his sights on the next best thing — engineered flight. When he was young, he would gaze upon the stars at night, wishing he could eat the glistening lights above.*"
Appearance: The **Flying Ducky** is a duck with an orange beak and orange flippers, as well as having yellow body. It wears a blue pilot suit with a white shirt and black tie and a helmet. It also has wings which it spreads out, then constantly flaps them, which allows it to fly.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Bathroom Approach is listed instead.

- As the **Flying Ducky** spawns in hordes, the Mortar and Electroshocker can be especially useful, due to them being able to damage multiple at once.

It had a decently fast speed, slower than the Hex Minion, but it had significantly more health than it. It also had Freeze Immunity and Stun Immunity by default, while also occasionally appearing with the Bloated and Nimble modifiers applied.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Reanimation** - Upon death, the **Frankenstein** would fall onto the ground. Shortly after, lightning would strike it, reviving it with 2,100 health and changing its name to *Revived Frank*.

Description: **Frankenstein** was the first boss that appeared in the second act of the Lunar Overture Event, though only the first **Frankenstein** that spawns was considered a boss. It was a high-health, slow enemy that was immune to being completely stopped by the Warden and Electroshocker, being only slowed down instead. Because it was a boss enemy, it was also immune to being frozen by freezing towers and being slowed down by the Toxic Gunner, with an additional 35% defense. Additionally, on some waves, **Frankenstein** spawned as a hidden enemy.

**Frankenstein** had one ability, where upon death it would come back to life by being struck by a lightning bolt. After it was reanimated, its health changed to 2,100, its name changed from *Frankenstein* to *Revived Frank* and it had blue and yellow electricity appear on it.
Appearance: The **Frankenstein** was a large humanoid with a waist, lower arms and lower legs in its rig. It had a lime green skin tone with dirt all over it, had a dark green torso, waist and pants. It wore a greenish-black coat with long sleeves and three grey buttons. It had one bolt on each shoulder, a thin metal beam going down each arm, two bolts sticking out of the sides of its head, short dark green hair and stitches with a red line under its hairline.

On its first and second deaths, it would fall onto its back. After its first death, for its *Reanimation* ability, it would be struck by yellow lightning, causing it to rise back up and gain blue and yellow electricity particles across its body.
Strategy: - High DPS towers like the Accelerator, Minigunner, Ranger or Pursuit are recommended against the **Frankenstein**.
- Do note that, on later waves, some **Frankensteins** spawn as Hidden enemies, so you will be required to bring a decent DPS tower to deal with them.
- The Commander and DJ Booth can be useful at boosting their firerate and range respectively.
- Defense dropping towers like the Pyromancer can be quite useful at decreasing its defense, allowing your towers to deal more damage to it.
- When it first spawns on Wave 11, it is a boss enemy, therefore it cannot be frozen by freezing towers, slowed down by the Toxic Gunner or completely stopped by the Warden and Electroshocker.
- This also means that it is unaffected by the Witch's ability.
- After wave 11, **Frankenstein** is no longer a boss, reducing its immunities to only being immune to the Warden's and Electroshocker's stun, only being slowed down by them.
- As such, towers like the Sledger are strong options for dealing with **Frankenstein** past wave 11.

- Be careful if **Frankenstein** gets very close to the end of the path, as you may not have enough time or damage to kill the **Revived Frank**. Thus, it is highly important to kill them as soon as possible. This enemy requires a total of 4,900 damage to successfully be defeated.
Trivia: - Contrary to common belief, **Frankenstein** is the erroneous term to call the monster. As stated in the original 1818 novel *Frankenstein*, the monster is actually called Frankenstein's Monster or the Creature, while Dr. Frankenstein is the creator of the monster.
- This enemy may be purposely called **Frankenstein** as a reference to the common misconception.
- In the original novel, the monster is revived using electricity. The lightning bolt that turned the **Frankenstein** into the **Revived Frank** may be a reference to this.
- As the **Frankenstein** died twice, when it received a pumpkin hat on its head, it would drop **Pumpkins** two times instead of the usual one.
- The **Frankenstein** and Abomination are the only enemies that can revive themselves after being killed, though the Abomination is the only one that is still in the game.
Notes: - ↑ Only first **Frankenstein** spawned as a boss.

abilities.text: **Frozen Banner** - Grabs a heavy grey banner before throwing it at a tower or unit in its range of 30. This creates a 15 debuff range around the banner which applies a 10% Firerate Debuff to towers. This banner lasts 30 seconds on the map.

Description: The **Frost Champion** is a major mini boss that appears in Frost Mode on Wave 33. It has a high amount of health and slightly slow speed.

The **Frost Champion** has three ability, though it cannot use one until 10 seconds have passed since spawning. There is also an attack cooldown of 5 set for all of its abilities. These abilities are:
- *Summon*, which makes the **Frost Champion** summon five enemies with a 0.75 delay between each. There is a 60% chance for it to be a Frost Invader and a 40% chance for it to be the Unstable Ice.

- *Spear Thrust*, where it winds up its spear and thrusts it at a tower or unit in its range of 25. This will stun towers hit in its hitbox that has a length of 20 for 4 seconds and damage units by 1,000 damage. Due to the spear actually not reaching to the end of its ability range, in rare circumstances the **Frost Champion** will target towers that it cannot reach with its spear, making it do absolutely nothing.

- *Frozen Banner*, which has the **Frost Champion** grab a heavy grey banner from its back and throw it at a tower or, despite it doing nothing to them, unit in its range of 30. This creates a debuff range of 15 around the banner which for 30 seconds will apply a 10% Firerate Debuff to towers.
Appearance: The **Frost Champion** has blue skin and a green head. It wears light blue and grey pants, chestplate, shoulder-pads, wrist-pads, knee-pads, shoes and helmet. On its helmet, it has two blue horns, with the left one being longer. Around its neck it has blue fur. It also wears a grey belt with a blue crystal. It wields a long grey and blue spear.
Strategy: - High DPS towers such as Accelerator, Juggernaut, Turret, Ranger and Gatling Gun are recommended due to its high health.
- Towers capable of buffing firerate or damage such as Commander, DJ Booth and Medic are useful in maximizing DPS when the **Frost Champion** reduces it with its *Frozen Banner* ability.
- Do note however that the Medic cannot protect towers from the *Frozen Banner* ability, as its shield does not prevent debuffs.
- Its *Summon* ability summons in the Frost Invader, which is a Lead enemy and the Unstable Ice, which is a Hidden enemy, meaning appropriate lead detection and hidden detection towers are needed.
- However, by this stage of the game, these should not be particularly difficult to deal with.
Update History: - **Bug**: Uses a placeholder icon instead of the intended one.
Notes: - ↑ Applies only to the **Frost Champion** on Wave 33 in Frost mode.

Description: The **Frost Hero** is a strong enemy that appears in the Frost mode. Like most of that mode's enemies, it first appeared in the Operation I.C.E Event. It has a high amount of health, however, it is one of the slowest enemies in the mode to compensate for that. When initially spawning in, it is a Flying enemy. It has one ability, where it targets up to three towers. With each hit, it freezes the targeted tower for 5 seconds, similarly stunning any other tower hit and also dealing 250 damage to units. All hits boost its Defense by 10% with no limit while on its third hit, it will float up into the air, making it a Flying enemy briefly.
Logbook Description: "*Frost Heroes are the champions of their craft, the most fearless fighters in the Frost Spirit's army. Adorned with the finest crystallized armor and woven Crystalline Frost Spinner silk, their decorated appearance matches their weapon—forged by The Maker himself. As the most devoted members of the Frost Army, Frost Heroes are capable enough to strike and stun towers.*"
Appearance: The **Frost Hero** has its entire body covered in blue, crystalized armor, which consists of a helmet, chestplate, spiked shoulder-pads, gloves, leg padding and shoes. It also wears a dark blue shirt and pants made out of Crystalline Frost Spinner Silk. On its torso, it also has a brown belt. On its back, it has a set of blue angelic wings, which it can use to fly in the air. In its right hand it wields a grey sword with blue crystals on the edges, which it uses to attack towers with.
Strategy: - High DPS towers like the Pursuit, Ranger, Accelerator or Engineer are great against the **Frost Hero** due to its high health.
- The Ranger and Pursuit are especially useful, due to their high range and stun immunity.
- The Medic can be used to shield towers from its attack, though do note that it attacking towers three times may lead to a tower getting hit more than once.
- Towers with flying detection can be useful as they will not stop for brief periods of time from it becoming a Flying enemy, though this is not a requirement for a tower to easily take it down.
- The **Frost Hero** initially has no Defense, though it will gain 10% Defense with each swing, making it receive less damage from towers the longer it is on the path.
- Towers like the Pyromancer, Freezer, Electroshocker or Toxic Gunner can be used to reduce its Defense.
Trivia: - Previously, every new iteration of the **Frost Hero** would coincidentally have its health doubled, starting from Pre-MEGA. However, this version has since broken that streak.
- This **Frost Hero** in the Easy difficulty is also the weakest iteration of the **Frost Hero**.
- If the tradition continued, **Frost Hero** would currently have 160,000 health.
- The tip on the right side of its sword has a missing texture. This can also be seen on its Index icon.
- The **Frost Hero** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
- The **Frost Hero** was planned to be given an ability where it would spawn mid-way into the map instead of at the entrance in v2.8.0 though this was cut.

Description: The **Frost Hero** was an enemy that appeared in Outpost 32 as part of the Frost Invasion Event. Currently, it can only appear in Sandbox mode. The **Frost Hero** also appeared in the legacy Hidden Wave, and therefore Fallen mode. It had a high amount of health but walked quite slowly. It has two main attacks which are used to stun or freeze towers, meaning that they can not attack for a period of time.
Appearance: The **Frost Hero** has black reflective skin and blue neon eyes. It wears a dark blue galea helmet, black gloves, black metal-plated wristbands with a neon blue crystal embedded in it and is covered with full body armor. This armor has a neon blue crystal on its chestplate and neon blue spikes sticking out of the shoulder-pads. Included in this armor are black metal-plated leggings, and dark blue knee-pads and boots. The **Frost Hero** also has dark blue wings. It wields an ice sword in its right hand which it carries above its shoulder.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Outpost 32 and Hidden Wave is listed instead.
- High DPS towers, such as the Minigunner, Ranger, Accelerator or Turret, are recommended against the **Frost Hero** due to its high health.
- Due to its attack relying on towers being close to the path, the Ranger and Turret, combined with the DJ Booth are especially recommended for their long range.
- You should use the Commander's *Call to Arms* ability to boost the firerate of these towers.
- As this enemy has quite a lot of health, you may want to use the Toxic Gunner to slow this down, allowing your towers more time to deal more damage to it.
- Doing so is essential in the Hidden Wave.
- The Electroshocker cannot slow this down for an extensive period of time, due to its large size, while freezing towers cannot freeze it due to its Freeze Immunity.
- Cheap towers, such as the Scout, can easily distract this enemy, keeping your main towers attacking.
- This is not recommended in the Hidden Wave, as all tower slots should be used for high DPS or support towers.
- In Outpost 32, as with all enemies in the Frost Invasion Event, the Pyromancer deals double fire damage to the **Frost Hero** (though normal damage is not doubled).
- This does not occur in the Hidden Wave.
- Do keep in mind that the Pyromancer will speed up this enemy by 15%.
Trivia: - The **Frost Hero** looks similar to the Titan from *Tower Battles*.

- The **Frost Hero** was tied with the Nuclear Guardian for having the second highest health in the game for an enemy that is not a major boss, even having higher health than some removed major bosses, like the Mechanical Rot or Molten Boss.
- The **Frost Hero's** helmet is the Ice-Nine Drone Helm accessory from the Roblox catalog.
- The **Frost Hero's** sword is the Frostburn Sword accessory from the Roblox catalog.
- The **Frost Hero's** wings are the Dark Shoulder Wing Set accessory from the Roblox catalog.
- The **Frost Hero** only appeared twice in Outpost 32, once in wave 19, and again in wave 20.
- The **Frost Hero** unintentionally replaced the Village of Despair Frost Hero in Hidden Wave.
Update History: - Replaced the Frost Hero (Village of Despair) in the Hidden Wave.
- **Frost Hero** can now be summoned in Sandbox mode, only when the player has the Frost Hero's Logbook from the Operation I.C.E Event.
- **Bug**: None of its abilities work anymore.
- **Frost Hero** now appears in the legacy Hidden Wave, which is exclusive to Sandbox mode.
- **Frost Hero** no longer copies the statistics of its modern version.
- **Frost Hero** no longer appears in the legacy Hidden Wave, as it has been removed.

Description: The **Frost Hero** was an ice elemental enemy that appeared in Village of Despair as part of the Christmas 2019 Event. It also used to spawn in the Legacy Hidden Wave which meant it could spawn on Fallen mode.

Due to its high health, it posed a significant threat despite its slow speed. The **Frost Hero** also possessed two abilities capable of stunning towers: the *Rock Throw* ability which inflicted a prolonged stun on a single tower, and the *Sword Swing* ability which could stun a group of towers.
Appearance: The **Frost Hero** was quite a large enemy, about the same size as the Fallen Guardian. It had a blue frost mask and helmet, dark blue granite wings, full blue armor (including chestplate, shoulder-pads and leggings). It also wielded a sword. It had a drooling zombie face and blue skin. Its torso and legs were black.
Strategy: - The Electroshocker can be used to slow the **Frost Hero** down to allow your towers more time to kill it.
- The Freezer and Frost Blaster can actually be quite useful against this enemy as it is not immune to their freeze.
- However, due to the **Frost Hero's** size, these towers can only slow it down for a short period of time compared to an average-sized enemy.
- Cheap towers, such as the Scout, can be used to distract this enemy, keeping your main towers attacking it.
- However, this wastes a tower slot in the late game which can be used for towers that deal more damage.
- You can use the Medic's ability to cleanse towers, if they were stunned by the **Frost Hero**, so long the Medic isn't stunned itself.
- As usual, high DPS towers, such as the Minigunner, Ranger, Accelerator and Turret, are recommended against this enemy.
Trivia: - The **Frost Hero** was loosely based on the Titan from *Tower Battles* in terms of abilities.
- A version of the Frost Hero existed before the MEGA Update, though it was completely different to this variant of the **Frost Hero**.
Update History: - **Frost Hero** removed from Village of Despair.
- **Bug**: *Rock Throw* cannot be seen, but can still stun towers.
- **Frost Hero** removed and replaced by Frost Hero (Frost Invasion) in Hidden Wave.

Description: The **Frost Hero** was the final enemy to appear on Insane mode.

It had more health than the Gravekeeper. It could therefore be considered a major boss due to this, and the fact that it was immune to the Freezer's *Ice Drop* ability, which only major bosses were immune. However, the **Frost Hero** was duplicated on two-pathed maps, such as Badlands, unlike other major bosses.
The **Frost Hero** could smash its hammer into the ground near towers, stunning them for a period of time.
Appearance: The **Frost Hero** wore a sky blue dominus, with sky blue skull shoulder-pads. It had a similar appearance in appearance to the Fallen Hero. Instead of having a face, its head was illuminated blue. Its skin was baby blue, and its torso and legs were sky blue. Its skin, torso and legs were in the ice texture. It wielded an ice hammer to attack towers.
Strategy: - The Pyromancer can be used to slow the **Frost Hero** to allow your towers more time to kill it.
- Cheap towers, such as the Scout, can easily distract this enemy, keeping your main towers attacking.
- If you can, try to place your towers away from the path, as the **Frost Hero's** *Ice Hammer* range is quite short.
- If you cannot do so, try to place your towers separated from each other. If they are grouped together, they are all at risk of being stunned by one attack.
- As usual, high DPS towers, such as the Minigunner, Commando and Turret, are recommended.
- Outlaws and Rocketers are recommended against this enemy as they appear two and three times during wave 67 and wave 68.
- You can use the Commander's *Call to Arms* ability to decrease the firerate of these towers.
- You can also use the John's *Gorilla Noises* ability to increase the damage of these towers.
Trivia: - Due to a bug, the **Frost Hero** was initially not immune to the Freezer's *Freeze Drop* ability.
- The **Frost Hero's** hammer was the Harbinger of Fimbulwinter gear from the Roblox catalog.
- The skull shoulder pads used by the **Frost Hero** are the The Ice Skull of Nevermoor accessory from the Roblox catalog.
Update History: - **Bug**: **Frost Hero** does not have Freeze Immunity.
- **Bugfix**: **Frost Hero** now has the Freeze Immunity.

Description: The **Frost Hunter** is a strong enemy that appears in the Frost mode. Like most of that mode's enemies, it first appeared in the Operation I.C.E Event. It is effectively a stronger version of the Snow Minion, as it has higher health, Defense and faster speed. Its ability is similarly also made stronger, as it deals more damage and freezes towers instead of debuffing them, allowing it to affect more towers.
Logbook Description: "*Frost Hunters are some of the most ferocious units in the Frost Spirit’s army. Talented spear throwers, they ruthlessly hunt down their targets, strategizing in groups to corner them before making their move. The sharp spikes on their shoulder pad are used to charge their enemies in battle. They throw javelins at towers and units.*"
Appearance: The **Frost Hunter** is an entity with blue skin. It is a warrior which wears a grey and blue helmet, chestplate, shoes and leg padding. It also wears a brown glove on its left arm, a blue ice shoulder-pad on its left arm and a blue cape with ice on the edges. It wields a blue javelin made entirely out of ice, which it throws at towers to stun them and at units to damage them.

- Because of this, towers like the Pursuit and Brawler are still technically immune to its attack as they will not be targeted, but other forms of stun immunity like the Medic's shield will not protect towers from the freeze.

Description: The **Frost Necromancer** is a summoner enemy that appears in the Frost mode. Like most of that mode's enemies, it first appeared in the Operation I.C.E Event. It has a high amount of health and average speed. Upon using its *Forbidden Arts* ability, it will summon in nine Frost Undead with a 0.15 delay between each one. After using it, it will also set its Shield Health to 3,500, granting it Health Regen until all of its Shield Health is depleted. This makes its summons act as a distraction that lets it regenerate its health.
Logbook Description: "*Frost Necromancers are artists, rejuvenating life into the corpses of the fallen and employing them to do their bidding. With staffs filled with energized ice, they willfully control their minions and grant them unique modifiers. Though shunned by the Frost Realm as tainted beings, Frost Necromancers remain beloved by the Frost Spirit to raise the dead.*"
Appearance: The **Frost Necromancer** is a floating, grey skeleton which wears purple robes. Its torso is black. On its back, it carry multiple skeletal parts, which are attached to it through chains wrapped around its torso. It wields a grey staff which has a lantern attached to it. This lantern contains energized ice, which allow them to summon and control the Frost Undead.
Strategy: - High DPS towers like the Pursuit, Ranger, Gatling Gun or Accelerator are great against the **Frost Necromancer** due to its high health.
- High DPS towers with area of effect capabilities, like the Gatling Gun or Pursuit are especially useful, as they can deal with both the **Frost Necromancer** and the enemies it summons.

- The **Frost Necromancer** will generally spawn in at the end of groups of enemies stronger enemies, like the Frost Hero and Frost Spirit. This shields it from most damage, allowing it to summon in as many enemies as possible and give it more time to regenerate its health..
- You can set towers to "*Last Enemy"*, which will generally make them target the **Frost Necromancer** and kill it far faster, making the waves it spawns on easier.
Trivia: - The **Frost Necromancer** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.

Description: The **Frost Necromancer** was a high-health summoner enemy that appeared exclusively in Outpost 32 as part of the Frost Invasion Event. Currently, it can only appear in Sandbox mode, though it copies the Operation I.C.E Event Frost Necromancer statistics, while also having its ability not work. Compared to the Frost Hero, which debuted on the same wave in Outpost 32, it had lower health and the same speed. However, the **Frost Necromancer** could have posed a threat due to its significantly higher health than most enemies that came before it, along with its ability to summon four Snow Minions.
Appearance: The **Frost Necromancer** has black reflective skin, and black granite legs and torso. It wears a black granite textured cloak, complete with a hood and cape. On its shoulders are skull pauldrons. Black chains run along its torso, arms and shoulders. Its torso and leg are cut open and exposed, and its left leg is slightly carved in around its knees. Its arms are also slightly carved in around the elbows. The **Frost Necromancer** wears blue metal-plated wristbands. On its torso is a neon blue crystal. It is faceless and also wears a blue face covering, which covers the bottom half of its face. The **Frost Necromancer** wields a blue crystal staff to summon Snow Minions. This staff emits white particles while its torso emitted light blue smoke. Its head is tilted slightly downwards.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Outpost 32 is listed instead.
- High DPS towers, such as the Ranger, Minigunner and Accelerator, are recommended to take down the **Frost Necromancer** due to its high health.
- You should use the Commander's *Call to Arms* ability to boost the firerate of these towers.
- You can use the DJ Booth to increase the range of your towers to prevent this enemy from going out of range of your defenses.
- This also aides in ensuring that any Snow Minions that spawn cannot get out of range of your towers.
- As with all enemies in the Frost Invasion Event, the Pyromancer deals double fire damage to the **Frost Necromancer** (though normal damage is not doubled).
- While the Snow Minions that spawn should not be a huge issue at this stage of the game, you can use towers that hit multiple enemies such as the Mortar or Pursuit to easily defeat these.
Update History: - **Frost Necromancer** can now be summoned in Sandbox mode, only when the player has the Frost Necromancer's Logbook from the Operation I.C.E Event.

Description: The **Frost Ravager** is a strong and fast enemy that appears in the Frost mode. Like most of that mode's enemies, it first appeared in the Operation I.C.E Event. It has a high amount of health and initially an average speed. However, three seconds after spawning in, it will speed up, close to doubling its speed and it will keep that speed until it runs out of its Shield Health. As it has multiple immunities, it will be harder to slow down while running through the map.
Logbook Description: "*Guardians of the Frost Realm and Frost Spirit, Frost Ravagers are deadly foes transformed into the most fearsome defensive entities. Carrying the light of the Frost Spirit, they wield thick, heavy shields made of Umbrite. As their shields are depleted, Frost Ravagers speed up toward their targets.*"
Appearance: The **Frost Ravager** is an entity with a white body. Its arms are covered with ice armor, which also has spikes on it. On its torso, it has three neon blue crystals and it wears a belt with blue padding. On its head, it has a small blue mask with two eye holes, revealing its two, neon blue eyes. It wields a grey heavy shield made out of Umbrite which has chains wrapped around it.
Strategy: - The **Frost Ravager** is quite dangerous due to its high health, especially when using *Leading Dash*, which can make it move at a much faster speed.
- High range and DPS towers like the Pursuit, Ranger, Accelerator or Engineer are great against the **Frost Ravager.**
- The Ranger and Pursuit are especially useful, as their high range allows them to keep it in range for longer.
- As it has quite high defense, defense dropping towers like the Pyromancer or Electroshocker can be useful against it.
- As it has the Freeze Immunity, freeze cannot be used to drop its defense until it has lost its Shield Health.
- You cannot use knockback towers like the Brawler, because of its Stun Immunity.
- Stunning towers like the Electroshocker can still be used, though they will only slow it down instead of stunning it.
Trivia: - Upon first spawning, it will use its no shield animation though with its shield on the side. If the Shield Health is depleted before it gets to start dashing, this animation will become permanent.
- As a result of this, its death animation will now have it fall over with its shield to the side, something normally not possible to see.
- The Umbrite material mentioned in the **Frost Ravager's** logbook description may have been named after The Umbra.
- The **Frost Ravager** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.

- In the Operation I.C.E Event, the **Frost Ravanger's** abilities and behavior would be almost identical to that of the Fallen Shield, except that the speed increase and duration were the only difference then.

Description: The **Frost Ravager** was an enemy that appeared exclusively in Outpost 32 as part of the Frost Invasion Event. Currently, it can only appear in Sandbox mode, though in there it is quite broken as most of its functionality is gone. It had an extremely high amount of health, but luckily it had quite slow speed. The **Frost Ravager** also had freeze immunity.

Initially, the **Frost Ravager** spawned with a shield, which granted it Shield Health, in which you cannot earn any money from the **Frost Ravager**. It also had 50% defense when it had its shield, reducing most forms of damage. When it lost its shield, it no longer had defense, but it would have increased speed.
Appearance: The **Frost Ravager** had arctic blue skin. Its arms were slightly crystallized. The **Frost Ravager** had dark blue granite legs and torso. Three neon white crystals could be seen on the **Frost Ravager's** torso. It also had blue spikes sticking out of its shoulders and arms. It had white glowing menacing eyes. When it spawned, the **Frost Ravager** carried a large white ice shield across its front.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Outpost 32 is listed instead.
- High DPS towers, such as the Ranger or Accelerator, are recommended to take down the **Frost Ravager**.
- You should use the Commander's *Call to Arms* ability to boost the firerate of these towers.
- You can use the DJ Booth to increase the range of your towers to prevent this enemy from going out of range of your defenses.
- Defense is ignored by splash damage, meaning that towers and units that deal splash damage will deal 100% damage if the **Frost Ravager** is caught in the center of the explosion.
- This makes the Mortar somewhat useful against the **Frost Ravager** but be wary, since the Mortar has low DPS for its cost.
- Upon collision, units, like the Railgun Tank, will ignore defense and deal full collision damage to the **Frost Ravager**.
- You can use towers like the Pyromancer or Electroshocker to reduce the defense of the **Frost Ravager**, allowing your towers to kill it faster.
- Note that the **Frost Ravager** will lose its defense once it loses its Shield Health.
- Additionally, as with all enemies in the Frost Invasion Event, the Pyromancer deals double fire damage to the **Frost Ravager** (though normal damage is not doubled).
Trivia: - In terms of appearance, the **Frost Ravager** was similar to the Frost Invader.
- The **Frost Ravager's** shield was similar to the Vindicator's in terms of functionality.
- Unlike the Vindicator, the **Frost Ravager** will speed up when it loses its Shield.
- On the Frost Invasion Event thumbnail, the **Frost Ravager** has dark blue skin instead of blue skin, and a dark blue shield instead of a grey one. This appearance was never seen in-game.

Description: The **Frost Spirit** is the final boss of Frost Mode. It was also the final boss in Easy and Hard difficulty in the Operation I.C.E Event, where it appeared Wave 25 at Easy difficulty and Wave 40 at Hard difficulty in Outpost 32. It moves at a very slow speed, however it possesses an high amount of health, and in Operation I.C.E Event, an even higher health count than most other event bosses. Its health was boosted by 50% in *True Form* - a version which was activated in both Easy and Hard difficulty in Operation I.C.E Event through the Elite Token activation for the Roblox Winter Spotlight Event.
The **Frost Spirit** has seven abilities, three of them can be used at any point, three of them are only used by it after entering its second phase and one which is its second phase activation:

- The first ability is *Frost Spikes*, where the **Frost Spirit** swings its scythe into the ground, creating a forward column of ice that freezes towers and units caught in it for 4 seconds, also dealing 1,600 damage to units.

- Its second and last ability usable at any point is *Summon*, where it slams its scythe down and raises its hand upwards, summoning nine enemies. These can be the Yeti (50% chance, 1.5 delay), Frostbane (35% chance, 0.75 delay) and Blizzard Wizard (15% chance, 1.5 delay). Each enemy has a 20% chance to be Bloated.

- Its third ability is *Antarctic Armageddon*, which happens at 80% health. This makes it fly up into the air, temporarily becoming Flying and losing Lead permanently, gaining a new appearance and then landing, creating a visual shockwave that does not stun towers or damage units. After this, it can use four more abilities.

- The first of these abilities is *Ice Storm*, which makes it summon 120 icicles from the sky, which fall down and can stun towers and units, freezing them for 7.5 seconds and dealing 3,200 damage to units.

- The next ability is *Ice Beacon*, which makes it summon three Ice Beacons. These would heal the **Frost Spirit** by 4,500 every second while they were still on the path. They will be instantly killed when the **Frost Spirit** is at max health. During this ability, the **Frost Spirit** will become immobile and gain the No Target attribute. All damage dealt to it at that time will be redirected to the Ice Beacons it has summoned, regardless if the tower actually hit them or not.
- The next ability is *Switch Path*, where the **Frost Spirit** will jump to another path. This only works on maps with more than one path.

- The last ability is *Laser Sweep*, which makes the **Frost Spirit** fire a laser beam from its face, sweeping it in a 360 degree arc, freezing every tower and unit caught in it for 6 seconds and dealing 1,000 damage to units.
- The last ability is its third phase, *True Spirit*, which is triggered at 32% of its health. This will give it Hidden permanently.
Logbook Description: "*The Frost Spirit is one of the most powerful entities in the Frost Realm. Leading his own army, he commands all creatures under his domain. His followers fight unwaveringly for his cause as he demands absolute order and sacrifice to fulfill his desires. Once enraged, his arrack[sic] patterns change.*"
Appearance: The **Frost Spirit** is an entity with purple skin with multiple dark purple veins on its body. On its right hand, it has blue fingers which it uses to hold its staff with. It wears a white robe, which has a fur outline around it and a hood, which covers most of its head other than its neon blue face. On its shoulders, multiple blue and purple thorns stick out, which are going through its robe. On its back, it has two purple and blue ice wings, which it uses to fly above the path during some of its abilities. Multiple chains are wrapped around its body and wings, with some being attached to the bands on its arms and torso. It also wears dark grey pants and grey shoes. It holds a giant scythe which it uses to perform some of its abilities. On top of its head, it has a blue halo.

During *Antarctic Armageddon*, its appearance will change. Most notably, its halo will turn purple and the crystals that form it will become uneven and bent. On its wings, the chains that surrounded it will be removed. Similarly, the collar it wears around its neck will disappear, though the chains connected to it will still remain there. Its walking animation will also change, with the easiest to spot change being its chains on its arms now swinging more as it moves.
Strategy: - The **Frost Spirit** to a degree incorporates every detection into itself, meaning a variety of DPS towers is needed to kill it.
- It at first spawns with Lead, meaning lead detection towers like the Accelerator, Turret, Ranger or bottom path Juggernaut are required.

- Once it has reached 80% of its health, it will gain *Switch Path* and *Ice Beacon* abilities, the former making it a Flying enemy temporarily while the latter makes it summon three Flying enemies, meaning flying detection towers like Ranger, Pursuit, top path Juggernaut or Kingpin can be used against these.
- Once it has reached 32% of its health, it will become a Hidden enemy, meaning hidden detection towers like the Accelerator, Turret, Engineer or Juggernaut can be used.
- Support towers like the Commander, Medic and DJ Booth are extremely beneficial in buffing your towers.
- Do note that the Medic's shield cannot protect your towers from freezes, though its *Ubercharge* can give them Freeze Immunity temporarily.
- As all of its abilities freeze, Stun Immunity has little use against it, though the Gatling Gun can still fire when frozen.
- The Mercenary Base's Field Medic can be used to protect units from being frozen or damaged, though do note there is a cooldown before it can be applied after it has been broken.
- As the **Frost Spirit** has the Boss and Freeze Immunity attributes, it is heavily resistant or fully immune to most forms of stalling.
Trivia: - The **Frost Spirit** is a returning boss from the Frost Invasion Event; awakened by Master Kronus and the Children of Exo during the Operation I.C.E Event to attack *T.D.S*, the fictional organization that the player is fighting for.

extra.Ability 1: Frostbite Slam - The Frost Spirit swings its scythe into the ground, creating a forward column of ice that freezes towers caught in the column.
extra.Ability 2: Nausea Stomp - The Frost Spirit quickly jumps and stomps, creating a blast which applies an 150% Fatigue Debuff to towers.
extra.Ability 3: Antarctic Mist - The Frost Spirit breathes a cold mist, freezing all the towers caught in it. This also deals 450 damage per tick to units.
extra.Ability 4: Flying Frost - When the Frost Spirit reaches half its health, it will use its wings to hover a short distance above the ground to increase its speed.

Description: The **Frost Spirit** was a major boss that appeared exclusively in Outpost 32 as the final boss of the Frost Invasion Event. Currently, it can only appear in Sandbox mode, though it copies the Operation I.C.E Event Frost Spirit statistics there. It moved at an extremely slow pace, but had one million health, surpassing every enemy's health in the game at the time.
The **Frost Spirit** had four abilities.
- Its first ability was its *Frostbite Slam* attack, which froze towers hit, meaning that they could not attack.
- Its second ability, its *Nausea Stomp* attack, caused towers' firerate to be increased by an 150% Fatigue Debuff, thereby making them shoot slower.

- Its third ability was its *Antarctic Mist* attack. This attack caused the **Frost Spirit** to breathe cold mist, freezing any towers caught in the breath. This attack also dealt damage to units, 450 damage per tick.

- Its fourth and final ability was *Flying Frost*, a variant of a Rage Mode. During this state, its wings caused it to be lifted a short distance off the ground, increasing its speed. None of these abilities work in Sandbox mode.
Appearance: The **Frost Spirit** has black reflective skin, while its torso and legs are dark blue marble. It wears a blue-grey robe, hood, complete a furry collar, and boots. It has light blue wings which it can use to fly a short distance above the ground during its ability. Neon blue spikes can be seen on its shoulders and above its head was a neon blue halo. Black chains are wrapped around its legs, arms and wings. Around its neck, it wears a chain with a grey lock on it. It also has menacing neon blue eyes. The **Frost Spirit** wields a scythe to attack towers. Chains run along the top of the scythe and the blade was neon blue.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Outpost 32 is listed instead.
- You can use Turrets, Accelerators, Pursuits and Rangers to take down the **Frost Spirit** and other enemies that spawn before it. This is recommended due to the **Frost Spirit's** high health.
- The Commander's **Call to Arms** ability can be useful in boosting these towers' firerate, allowing more damage to be done over time.
- The Commander also allows you to mitigate the effects of the *Nausea Stomp*, as it cancels out the increase in firerate.
- As the **Frost Spirit** is likely going to get out of your towers' range, especially if they are placed near the start of the map, you should use the DJ Booth to boost the range of these towers.
- The **Frost Spirit** will always use the middle left path, relative to the direction that enemies move towards.
- You should sell towers on the right paths that do not reach the middle left path. You should also sell towers that the **Frost Spirit** has moved out of range of.

- You should also sell towers that deal damage to multiple enemies, like the Rocketeer, if you have towers that deal more DPS to a singular enemy, like the Minigunner, as the **Frost Spirit** does not spawn any enemies.

- The Military Base is not recommended against the **Frost Spirit**, as it is unlikely that its units will collide with the **Frost Spirit**, or even be in range of the **Frost Spirit** as its units can spawn on different paths, which may not be on the same path as the **Frost Spirit**.
- As with all enemies in the Frost Invasion Event, the Pyromancer deals double fire damage to the **Frost Spirit** (though normal damage is not doubled).
- However, as the Pyromancer speeds up enemies when they are on fire, you should sell any Pyromancers remaining when it is just the **Frost Spirit** alive.
- The Medic cannot cleanse towers if they are frozen, nor is it immune to being frozen by the **Frost Spirit**.
- The Gladiator cannot block any of the **Frost Spirit's** attacks, even though the blocking animation plays.
- After the **Frost Spirit** activates its *Flying Frost* ability, it will hover in the air a short distance above the path.
- However, units will still be able to collide with it as it is not technically a Flying enemy.
Trivia: - The **Frost Spirit's** wings are the Chained Angel Wings accessory from the Roblox catalog.
- The **Frost Spirit** is the first boss in the game to reach 1,000,000 base health, followed by The Umbra.
- Although the Void Reaver is older and reaches up to 1,200,000 base health, that enemy did not have that much health until V1.2.1 which was released well after the Frost Invasion Event.
- The **Frost Spirit's** *Antarctic Mist* ability is similar to Lord Sinister's *Infernal Storm* ability.
- If you look closely at the animation, you can see him take the pose of Lord Sinister, which means the animation was directly re-used.
- When the **Frost Spirit** activates its *Flying Frost* ability, the animation may stutter.
- The **Frost Spirit** depicted on the Frost Invasion 2021 Badge has a golden halo, whilst the one in-game had a neon blue one.
- The **Frost Spirit's** cape is the Frost Lord Cape accessory from the Roblox catalog.
- The **Frost Spirit** returned in the Operation I.C.E event, which is a retelling of the Frost Invasion Event.
- The **Frost Spirit** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Frost Spirit** can no longer be slowed down by the Toxic Gunner.
- **Frost Spirit** can now be summoned in Sandbox mode, only when the player has the Frost Spirit's Logbook from the Operation I.C.E Event.
- **Bug**: No longer uses any of its abilities.

Description: The **Frost Tank** was an ice version of the original version of the Tank. It only appeared in Village of Despair as part of the Christmas 2019 Event.
It had the same speed as the Tank, but had lower health. Like the Tank, it could throw boulders at towers with the *Rock Throw* ability to stun them.
Appearance: The **Frost Tank** had a similar appearance to the original version of the Tank, being mostly a recolor of the tank that looked more frosty and icy. It was a buffed up enemy with light blue glowing eyes and a drooling zombie face. It had muscular arms and light blue skin. It wore blue granite shorts, walked with a hunchback and had its head slightly tilted. It had blue horns sticking out of the sides of its head. There were also ice crystals on its back and on its shoulders.
Strategy: - High DPS towers, such as the Holiday Archer, Minigunner and Outlaw are effective choices to defeat this enemy, though it may take a while due to the **Frost Tank's** high health.
- Using the Commander can help significantly, especially with its *Call of Arms* ability.
- The Pyromancer and Freezer can slow the **Frost Tank** down, making them great support choices against it.
- You can place other towers away from the main group of towers to distract the **Frost Tank**.
- You can also spread out your towers to mitigate the effects of its *Rock Throw* ability.
- Alternatively, you can use the Medic's ability to cleanse the stun, as long the Medic is not already stunned from the attack.

Description: The **Frozen** was an enemy that appeared exclusively in Outpost 32 as part of the Frost Invasion Event. It can now be spawned in Sandbox mode. Compared to the Snowy, the **Frozen** had slightly higher health and slightly faster speed.
Upon its death, the Frost Mystery had a chance to spawn the **Frozen**.
Appearance: The **Frozen** has light blue skin. Its torso and legs are baby blue. The **Frozen** has no facial features.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Outpost 32 is listed instead.
- Placing down two Pyromancers on both sides of the path near the portal is recommended, as these can severely weaken hordes of **Frozens**, along with any Snowies that spawn.
- As the Pyromancer deals double fire damage (normal damage is kept the same), it can be very effective against **Frozens** at later upgrades.

- Be aware that early on, two Pyromancers is not sufficient to kill all the **Frozens** that spawn. You can eventually upgrade the Pyromancers to Level 3 in order to clean up all the **Frozens** that appear.
- Towers like Minigunner and Crook Boss can clear up any remaining **Frozens** that spawn.
- Because the **Frozen** spawns in hordes, towers that deal damage to multiple enemies can be extremely useful in dealing with the **Frozen**.
- Splash damage towers, like the Rocketeer and Mortar, can also be used.
- The Electroshocker and Toxic Gunner can be very useful in stalling these enemies.
- As the **Frozen** spawns in hordes, the Electroshocker can be useful in stalling many **Frozens**.
- The Freezer, Frost Blaster and Level 3 Sledger can freeze the **Frozen**, giving towers more time to attack it.
- As the base health on Outpost 32 is 200, and the **Frozen** has 25 health, it is fine to let some through.
Trivia: - This enemy was very similar to the Frozen from the Christmas 2019 Event, except that its head shape is slightly different.

Description: The **Gatekeeper** was the second major boss that appeared in Krampus Frosthold as part of the Krampus' Revenge Event. It had a very high amount of health but it walked quite slowly. The **Gatekeeper** could not be frozen or or have the chillness effect applied to it by freezing towers, slowed down by the Toxic Gunner and it could only be slowed down by the Electroshocker and Warden instead of being stunned.

It had one ability, *Key Toss*. This ability made the **Gatekeeper** throw its large key at the towers. The key would travel in a circular direction, which stunned towers hit by it before it returned back to the **Gatekeeper**.
Appearance: The **Gatekeeper** had pale skin and large pointy ears. It wore a jester's uniform, with alternative red and green colors on its clothing, red pants and gloves, and a brown belt. It had a red and green four-way pointed hat on its head that drooped downward, with the bottom part of it being entirely made out of gold, which also had multiple red and green jewels attached to it. It wore a golden breastplate, pauldrons and shoes, as well as golden lining on its clothes and face. It wielded a very large gold key that it used to attack towers with.
Strategy: - Towers with high DPS towers, like the Accelerator, Minigunner or Engineer are recommended against the **Gatekeeper**.
- Stun immune towers, such as Ranger and Pursuit can be especially effective.
- The Commander and DJ Booth can be also useful at boosting the firerate and range of the towers respectively.
- As multiple weaker enemies accompany the **Gatekeeper** when it spawns, towers like the Pyromancer or Mortar can be useful at clearing them out.
- Placing down cheap towers as a distraction, like the Pyromancer or Commander, can be pretty useful at making the **Gatekeeper** not target your main offensive towers.
- The **Gatekeeper** can target cliff towers like Sniper and Ranger, but cannot stun them. These towers can also be used to prevent the **Gatekeeper** from attacking other important towers.
- The **Gatekeeper** cannot be frozen or slowed down by freezing towers or slowed down by the Toxic Gunner.
- The Jester's confusion bomb can be quite useful at slowing down the **Gatekeeper**.
- The Warden and Electroshocker can also be used, though they will only slow it down instead of stunning it.
