abilities.label: Ability 1
abilities.text: **Key Toss** - The **Gatekeeper** throws the large key in its hand at towers. The key travels in a circular direction, stunning towers hit by it before returning back to the **Gatekeeper**.

abilities.label: Ability 2
abilities.text: **Key Hurl** - The **Gatekeeper** throws the large key in its hand at the Christmas tree. The key travels in a circular direction, hitting the tree and dealing 140 damage to the base. It also stuns towers hit by it before returning back to the **Gatekeeper**.

Description: The **Gatekeeper** was a major boss that exclusively appeared in Cold Ambush as part of the Violent Night Event. It had a high amount of health and a slightly slow speed. Unlike most other enemies in Cold Ambush, it did not head to the exit, but instead walked around on the plots, similar to the Ripped Elf.

It had two abilities, the first one being *Key Toss*. This ability made the **Gatekeeper** throw its large key at the towers. The key would travel in a circular direction, stunning towers hit by it before returning back to the **Gatekeeper**. The second ability, *Key Hurl*, was similar to *Key Toss*. However, instead of directly attacking towers with the key, the **Gatekeeper** would attack the Christmas tree with it, dealing 140 damage to the base as well as stunning any tower hit by the key.
Appearance: The **Gatekeeper** had pale skin and large pointy ears. It wore a jester's uniform, with alternative red and green colors on its clothing, red pants and gloves, and a brown belt. It had a red and green four-way pointed hat on its head that drooped downward, with the bottom part of it being entirely made out of gold, which also had multiple red and green jewels attached to it. It wore a golden breastplate, pauldrons and shoes, as well as golden lining on its clothes and face. It wielded a very large gold key that it used to attack towers and the Christmas tree with.
Strategy: - High DPS towers like the Accelerator, Ranger and Engineer are recommended against this enemy.
- These towers should have their firerate and range boosted by the Commander and DJ Booth respectively.
- The Ranger cannot be stunned by the **Gatekeeper**, nor can the Engineer's sentries be destroyed by it, making them both very effective.
- The Medic can be used to cleanse the stuns from towers stunned by the **Gatekeeper's** abilities.
- Try to have as much base health as possible so that you have a higher chance of surviving the **Gatekeeper's** *Key Hurl*.
- Buying more plots increases your maximum base health and passive base health regeneration.
- If you avoid skipping waves, they will pass more slowly, giving you more time to passively regenerate base health this way.
- The Medic can be used to heal back additional base health if the passive regeneration is not enough.
- As the **Gatekeeper** does not try to reach the base, and its abilities are not affected by stunning towers, trying to slow it down is nearly useless.
- The Freezer, Frost Blaster and Sledger cannot slow the **Gatekeeper** down due to its Freeze Immunity.
- The Toxic Gunner cannot slow the **Gatekeeper** down due to its poison immunity.
- The Electroshocker and Warden are able to slow it down, but for a significantly lesser time due to the **Gatekeeper's** large size and the fact it is considered a major boss.
- Defense dropping towers like the Pyromancer can be used to reduce the **Gatekeeper's** defense.
Trivia: - This is the first major boss to ever have defense.

- While Wox the Fox does have defense with the Lost Souls modifier, this is due to it increasing the defense of all enemies by 20%; it does not have defense naturally and it is not a change made specifically to it.

ghost.name: Ghost
ghost.description: The Ghost is an enemy that appears in Pizza Party. It is a Hidden enemy, meaning it requires hidden detection for it to be targeted.

Description: The **Ghost** is an enemy that appears in Pizza Party. It is a Hidden enemy, meaning it requires hidden detection for it to be targeted. Additionally, it has the same amount of health as the Heavy and is significantly faster than it, though it lacks its defense.
Appearance: The **Ghost** is a translucent green-white humanoid that floats slightly above the ground. It wears a tattered long-sleeve shirt that is the same color as its body. It also has a tail instead of legs, which moves as it floated on the path.
Strategy: - Most early game towers gain hidden detection. Such towers are recommended to deal with early **Ghosts**.
- As **Ghosts** spawn in hordes, the Golden Pyromancer is particularly useful, being able to damage multiple enemies at once and having hidden detection by default.
- The Pyromancer can also be useful against **Ghosts**, although it costs more and does not have hidden detection at base level.
- Single target towers, like the Golden Crook Boss or Shotgunner can also clear out groups of **Ghosts**, although they will require more cash to successfully eliminate them.
- Though the Trapper cannot detect Hidden enemies, its traps will still work against them. In particular, its landmines can be used to eliminate groups of **Ghosts** due to its high splash damage.
- For splash damage towers that cannot target **Ghosts**, such as the Mortar, if a **Ghosts** is caught up in an explosion, they will be dealt splash damage.
- This means that another detectable enemy must be near the **Ghost** for a splash damage tower to hit the **Ghost**.
- Similarly, the Electroshocker cannot target the **Ghost**, however, it can hit it if there are other detectable enemies nearby.
Trivia: - Interestingly, despite being called a **Ghost**, it is not a Ghost type enemy.
Update History: - **Bug**: **Ghost** is difficult to select when trying to do so on its arms.
- **Bug**: **Ghost** cannot be hit with Gatling Gun's *FPS* ability when targeting certain parts of its arm.

Description: The **Ghost** was the third enemy that appeared in the second and third night of the Solar Eclipse Event. Currently, it can be spawned in Sandbox mode. It had higher health and faster speed than all the enemies before it. It was also a Hidden and Ghost enemy, so only a few towers could have dealt with them effectively early in the game. It was also immune to Splash Damage and Pyromancer's burn damage. This enemy could have been very threatening to those unprepared.
Appearance: The **Ghost** is a faceless, white, translucent enemy, which floats slightly above the ground.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in the Solar Eclipse Event is listed instead.
- Cheap towers with high DPS and hidden detection, such as the Scout, Crook Boss and Soldier are recommended against this.
- For the Scout, Crook Boss and Soldier, you can use their **Golden** skins for better performance.
- As these spawn in hordes, you can place down a few Level 2 Gladiators to quickly kill them.
- The **Ghosts** are immune to Splash Damage, so towers like the Mortar and Rocketeer are useless against this.
- The Swarmer's *Beehive Grenade* ability will also not apply the stinging effect on them.
- The Military Base is useless against this, as it cannot collide with the **Ghost** or detect it.
- At Level 4+, the Ace Pilot is able to give towers in its range temporary hidden detection for 15 seconds, allowing towers without hidden detection to be able to attack the **Ghost**.
- However, be aware that it is quite expensive to afford early on, when the **Ghost** first appears.
Trivia: - In terms of appearance and immunities, the 2020 and the 2021 version of the **Ghost** are very similar.
Update History: - **Ghost** can now be summoned in Sandbox mode, only when the player has the Ghost's from Pizza Party Logbook.
- No longer copies the statistics of the modern version in Sandbox mode.

Description: The **Ghost** was an enemy that appeared exclusively in Trick or Threat Town as part of the Halloween 2020 Event. While the **Ghost** had half the health of the Bones and an average speed, the **Ghost** was a far more dangerous threat because it was a hidden enemy. It also could not be burnt or hit by splash damage. As it was a ghost enemy, it could not collide with units. All these factors made the **Ghost** a challenge to kill without the right towers.
The **Ghost** could also be spawned by Lord Sinister.
Appearance: The **Ghost's** body was glowing white and was translucent. It had the Ghostface as its face. It floated a small distance above the path and emitted light.
Strategy: - Military Base units are ineffective against the **Ghost**, as they pass through the units.
- Make sure to have hidden detection by wave 6, as four **Ghosts** will spawn.
- The most effective towers for this are Militants, Shotgunners or Minigunners.
- Several Level 3+ Minigunners are probably your best bet against this enemy.
- Accelerators can also be used to kill **Ghosts**.
- The Commander's *Call to Arms* ability is effective if towers have hidden detection, but the Commander itself will not attack the **Ghost**.
- Even if the **Ghost** is caught in an explosion, it will not be dealt any damage due to its Splash Damage Immunity.
- The Pyromancer cannot burn the **Ghost**, even if a detectable enemy is beside the **Ghost**. However, the **Ghost** can still be dealt non-burn damage by the Pyromancer.
- The Electroshocker and Frost Blaster can slow down the **Ghost**, so long they have hidden detection.
Trivia: - In terms of appearance and immunities, the 2019 and 2020 **Ghost** were very similar.

Description: The **Ghost** was an enemy that appeared exclusively in Nightmare Carnival as part of the Halloween 2019 Event. The **Ghost** could be a very annoying enemy as it was as fast as the Scarecrow, had more health than it, and was Hidden.
The **Ghost** could be spawned by the Reaper and Jack O' Bot. It was also immune to the Pyromancer and splash towers, even if those towers had hidden detection.
Appearance: The **Ghost's** body was glowing white and was translucent. The head was the only part of the **Ghost** that was not translucent as it had the Ghostface as its face. The **Ghost** emitted light from its body.
Strategy: - It is recommended that at least two players place towers with hidden Detection before Wave 9 so you are able to kill a decent amount of **Ghosts**.
- Be aware that more **Ghosts** spawn in greater numbers after this wave. You will need to have adequate defenses.
- Multiple Level 2+ Minigunners and Level 2+ Outlaws are the standard methods to defeat the **Ghosts**.
- The Military Base may also be useful if the **Ghosts** evades all your towers as its units can collide with the **Ghosts**.
- The **Ghost** has explosive immunity, so even if it is caught in the explosion radius of a tower like the Rocketeer, it will be dealt zero damage.
- **Ghosts** are immune to fire, so Level 3+ Pyromancers are not recommended to deal with this enemy.
- **Ghosts** are also immune to the Freezer's basic freeze, as an extension of their explosive immunity, if they are caught in the projectile explosion.
- They are not immune to Freezer's *Ice Age* ability.
Trivia: - The **Ghost** was the first event enemy to be hidden, along with the Bat.
- The Hidden Zoomer does not count as it could be targeted by towers that did not have hidden detection.
- The **Ghost** was the first event enemy to have Splash Damage Immunity.

Description: The **Ghoul** is an enemy that appears only in Intermediate mode. It also appeared in The Takeover Event. It has a decently high health and a slightly slow speed. On all waves, it appears as a Hidden enemy, which means towers must have hidden detection to be able to target it. The only time it spawns without it is if the Patient Zero summons it. On certain waves, it can also have other attributes, like Bloated and Slime, making it quite dangerous.
Due to a bug, **Ghouls** with the Slime attribute do not spawn the Slime upon death.
Appearance: The **Ghoul** is a tall humanoid with a waist, lower arms and lower legs in its rig. It has a light green skin color, torn dark grey shorts, a belt and a ragged white lab coat. It has exposed green veins, multiple tumors on its body and a malnourished chest. It has green glowing eyes and black patches of hair on its head, with a few strands on the sides.
Strategy: - Towers with hidden detection and a good amount of DPS like the Assassin, Cowboy, Militant, Crook Boss or Golden Crook Boss can be effective against it.
- Later on, high DPS towers like the Minigunner, Crook Boss or Hunter can kill these with ease.
- Towers with high damage can be quite useful against it, such towers include the Military Base and Trapper.
- Splash damage towers like the Rocketeer can prove effective in clearing out **Ghouls** in later waves due to its hidden detection and high splash DPS, considering they appear in large groups.
- While other splash damage towers such as the Mortar and Demoman cannot target **Ghouls** directly, they can still be hit by their splash radius if another detectable non-hidden enemy is nearby.
- Stalling towers like the Freezer and the Warden can be utilized to slow the **Ghoul** down.
- Other stallers such as the Sledger and the Tesla, despite not being able to detect the **Ghoul**, can still indirectly hit the **Ghoul** if a enemy nearby is detectable.
Update History: - **Bug**: **Ghouls** with the Slime attribute do not spawn the Slime upon death.
- **Ghoul** is now immune to the fallout damage from the Nuke while it is a boss enemy.
- **Ghoul** is now immune to knockback while it is a boss enemy.
- **Bug**: Can be slowed down by the DJ Booth while a boss.
- **Bugfix**: No longer can be slowed down by the DJ Booth while a boss.
- **Ghoul** can no longer have its defense dropped while a Boss enemy.
- Now appears in Mid Rank PVP Test.
- No longer appears in the PVP Test as it has been removed.
- Now appears in Sk8 P4rk Noob and Pro difficulties as part of The Takeover Event.
- Has 250 health in the Pro difficulty.
- Gives $88 every 50% health lost in the Pro difficulty.
- No longer appears in Sk8 P4rk, as it has been removed.
- First wave appearance changed from 7 to 16 in Intermediate mode.
- Cash given increased from $100 every 50% health lost to $650 on death.
Notes: - ↑ Only the first **Ghoul** that spawns in Intermediate mode is a Boss enemy.

Description: The **Giant Boss** is a slow and large enemy with a large health and defense pool that appears in Intermediate mode, Challenge Trials and the Sandbox exclusive Legacy Fallen mode. It could also appear in The Takeover Event if summoned by Patient Zero. It moves at a slower speed compared to the Necromancer, but can easily pass through weak defenses due to its high health. It has Stun Immunity and Freeze Immunity making it harder to stall.
It can be spawned from the Mystery Boss upon its death in the Hardcore mode, Legacy Fallen mode and Golden mode.
Appearance: **Variant 1**

The **Giant Boss** is a large, hulking entity with green and grey skin. It has multiple green cracks in its body. It wears a torn, off-brown coat, brown gloves and has strange tubing and devices on its head. Its skull is partially exposed and it has a knife on its back.
**Variant 2**
**Variant 1**

The current version of the **Giant Boss** has a bronze skin color with a diagonal scar on its face. It has a brown granite torso, sleeves and legs, along with a brownish-black slate glove on its left arm, with a brown granite cuff on it. Additionally, it has dark grey chains wrapped around both of its arms. A knife is embedded into its back, with multiple spikes emerging from the location, as well as more emerging from the front of the torso. It emits an occasional bronze particle as well. Its head is slightly tilted downwards and has a twisted left leg.
**Variant 2**

The Enemies Beta version of the **Giant Boss** is a large humanoid with a waist, lower arms and lower legs in its rig. It has a yellowish-green skin color, and a dark brown torso, waist and legs, all coated in dirt. It has a knife impaled on its back, with red blood particles being emitted from the location. It also has veins on its head and arms and wears black armbands with white spikes on them.
**Variant 3**

The first version of the **Giant Boss** is quite similar to the current version. Unlike the current version, its torso, sleeves and legs were a slightly lighter shade of bronze. It also had no gloves nor chains on it. It was faceless and also had rectangular rebar emerging from its back. A knife also appeared to be stabbed into the back of the **Giant Boss**. Its head was slightly tilted downwards and it had a twisted left leg for its second animation.
**Variant 3**

The current version of the **Giant Boss** has a bronze skin color with a diagonal scar on its face. It has a brown granite torso, sleeves and legs, along with a brownish-black slate glove on its left arm, with a brown granite cuff on it. Additionally, it has dark grey chains wrapped around both of its arms. A knife is embedded into its back, with multiple spikes emerging from the location, as well as more emerging from the front of the torso. It emits an occasional bronze particle as well. Its head is slightly tilted downwards and has a twisted left leg.
**Variant 4**

The Enemies Beta version of the **Giant Boss** is a large humanoid with a waist, lower arms and lower legs in its rig. It has a yellowish-green skin color, and a dark brown torso, waist and legs, all coated in dirt. It has a knife impaled on its back, with red blood particles being emitted from the location. It also has veins on its head and arms and wears black armbands with white spikes on them.
**Variant 5**

The first version of the **Giant Boss** is quite similar to the current version. Unlike the current version, its torso, sleeves and legs were a slightly lighter shade of bronze. It also had no gloves nor chains on it. It was faceless and also had rectangular rebar emerging from its back. A knife also appeared to be stabbed into the back of the **Giant Boss**. Its head was slightly tilted downwards and it had a twisted left leg for its second animation.
Strategy: - When dealing with the **Giant Boss** when it debuts, high DPS towers are best fit. Such towers include the Pursuit, Accelerator, Minigunner, Crook Boss and Ranger.
- The Commander should be used to further boost the firerate of these towers.

- Do note that the Accelerator will remain locked onto the **Giant Boss** until it is defeated or leaves its range, letting other enemies get past. Other towers should be placed to deal with these enemies when using the Accelerator.
- The Military Base's Tank and Railgun Tank are quite strong against the **Giant Boss**, as their collision and splash damage ignore the **Giant Boss's** defense.
- Do note that their ranged gun damage is still affected by defense.

- It is not generally recommended to skip Wave 28 on Intermediate mode until the **Giant Boss** is defeated. Otherwise, the enemies from the following wave may overcome your towers while they are still trying to deal with the **Giant Boss**, with the **Giant Boss** acting as a meat shield.

- Compared to its arrival in Hardcore mode, it has significantly less health, but appears more oftenly. Because of this, not only are high DPS towers a good option, but AOE towers like the Mortar and Rocketeer can deal with hordes of **Giant Bosses** that appear later on.
- Multiple towers can take advantage of the **Giant Boss** slow speed.
- Short-ranged towers like the Gladiator are able to get many more hits in, making them more effective.
- The Military Base and Crook Boss' units will have more time to shoot at the **Giant Boss** before colliding into it.

- Most slowing towers are on the table when it comes to slowing the **Giant Boss** down. The Cryomancer, Frost Blaster and Electroshocker are most effective against the **Giant Boss's** tendency to spawn in hordes and against singular **Giant Bosses** in Hardcore mode. The same goes for Intermediate mode, though only its singular appearance rather than its horde tendency.
- Do note that the **Giant Boss** debuts as a boss on Wave 28 in Intermediate mode, making it immune to all forms of stuns.
- As the **Giant Boss** has the Stun Immunity, shock or stun based stalling towers like the the Warden, Tesla or Electroshocker will only slow it down.
- Furthermore, towers that can knockback enemies, such as the Brawler, cannot knock it back.
- Do note that the **Giant Boss'** large size will reduce the slowing capabilities of freezing towers and the Warden.

Description: The **Giant Skeleton** is an enemy that appears in Badlands II, Polluted Wasteland II, Challenge Trials and Story Mode. It has a high amount of health and a below average speed. It is also immune to being stunned, only being slowed down, and immune to knockback from towers.
The **Giant Skeleton** can be spawned by the Conjurer with its *Summon* ability, the Necromancer King with its *Cursed Summon* and the *Nuclear Summon* from the Nuclear Monster.
Appearance: The **Giant Skeleton** is a larger version of the Skeleton with a waist, lower arms and lower legs in its rig. It is made entirely of white parts that resemble a skeletal humanoid. It does not have a full torso, but instead has the bone cage for it. Its head is slightly smaller than most other enemies and it has two large black eyeholes.
On death, the **Giant Skeleton** falls into a pile of bones while playing a bone shaking sound.
Strategy: - When dealing with the **Giant Skeleton** when it first debuts, high DPS towers are best fit. Such towers include the Pursuit, Engineer, Golden Minigunner, Accelerator and Ranger.
- Towers with large range, such as the Ranger or Pursuit can be very useful here, as they can reach all three of the paths the **Giant Skeleton** will spawn in.
- The Commander should be used to further boost the firerate of these towers.
- Later on, **Giant Skeletons** will spawn in hordes. Splash damage towers, like the Rocketeer or Mortar can deal lots of damage to these hordes.

- Most slowing towers are on the table when it comes to slowing the **Giant Skeleton** down. The Cryomancer, Electroshocker, Warden and Freezer are most effective due to the **Giant Skeleton's** tendency to spawn in hordes, while still being very effective against singular **Giant Skeletons**.
- As the **Giant Skeleton** has Stun Immunity, stunning towers like the Warden and Electroshocker will only slow it down.
- As it has Stun Immunity, it cannot be knocked back.
Update History: - **Giant Skeleton** now appears in Blind Faith as part of the Null & Void Event.
- Health increased from 1,800 to 5,000 in Sandbox mode.
- **Bug**: Health change is also applied in Badlands II.
- Cash given now depends on the mode.
- Gives $2,000 every 50% health lost in Blind Faith's Easy and Hard difficulties.
- Gives $3 every 50% health lost by default.
- **Giant Skeleton** no longer appears in Blind Faith as the Null & Void Event ended.
- **Bugfix**: No longer has 5,000 health in Badlands II.
- **Bugfix**: Now gives $2,000 every 50% health lost instead of $3 every 50% health lost in Badlands II.
- Now appears in Polluted Wasteland II.
- Now appears in Rock Bottom and Surface Tension.
- Gives $3,000 every 50% health lost in Rock Bottom.
- Gives $300 every 50% health lost in Surface Tension.
Notes: - ↑ Only the first **Giant Skeleton** in Badlands II is a Boss enemy.

Description: The **Giant Skeleton** was an enemy that appeared in the second act of the Lunar Overture Event. It had a high amount of health but a slightly slow speed. It did not have a full torso, but instead had the bone cage for it. Its head was slightly smaller than most other enemies and had two large black eyeholes.

Description: The **Gingerbread** exclusively appeared in Village of Despair as part of the Christmas 2019 Event. It had slightly more health than the Snowman and moved faster than it. Upon the **Gingerbread's** death, the dynamite on its back exploded, stunning nearby towers.
The **Gingerbread** could be spawned by Krampus.
Appearance: The **Gingerbread** was completely toasted brown, to resemble a gingerbread man. It had a circular head with red glowing eyes and three red dynamite sticks attached to its back. It had three white icing buttons lined vertically on the middle of its torso, as well as an iced smile.
Strategy: - The Pyromancer can burn the **Gingerbread**, which slows it down.
- This can also be slowed down by the Freezer and Frost Blaster.
- Try to kill this enemy away from towers to avoid them being stunned.
- Long-ranged towers like the Outlaw are very effective at this, as their long range allows them to kill the **Gingerbread** from afar.
- Additionally, try to space out your towers so that not all of them are stunned once the **Gingerbread** is defeated.
- Later on during the game, the Medic's ability can be used to cleanse towers that are stunned.
Trivia: - This enemy may be based on the Gingerbread Minion from R2DA.
- This was the first enemy that appeared in Village of Despair that could be affected by the Freezer and Frost Blaster as the Frozen and Snowman could not be frozen.
- The head that the **Gingerbread** used is the Gingerbread Man Head accessory from the Roblox catalog, except the eyes are retextured to be glowing red.

Description: The **Glitch** is an enemy that only appears in the Sandbox exclusive Legacy Fallen mode. it also has extremely high speed, being the fastest enemy in Challenges. While it has relatively low health for its debut, its high speed makes it a very dangerous threat. It also has Stun Immunity, which prevents it from being completely stopped by the Warden and Electroshocker, only being slowed down instead and makes it immune to knockback.
The **Glitch** can be spawned by the Mystery upon its death in Legacy Fallen mode from Wave 27 onwards only.
Appearance: The **Glitch** is a volatile multi-colored enemy with no face. It has a white head, neon orange torso, blue right arm, magenta left arm, salmon right leg, and cyan left leg, all of which are either translucent or glowing. Glitched particles of various colors are emitted whenever the **Glitch** runs. It also makes a brief beeping sound upon death.
Strategy: - High DPS towers like the Minigunner, Golden Soldier, Turret or Golden Minigunner can be quite effective against the **Glitch**.
- Using the Commander to boost their firerate can be very helpful against this enemy.
- Using the DJ Booth to boost the range of your towers can also be very helpful, as the **Glitch** can easily run past towers like the Accelerator or Minigunner due to their charge up time and range.
- Using towers that can slow down the **Glitch** is highly recommended.

- Do note that the **Glitch** has Stun Immunity, which makes stunning towers like the Electroshocker only slow down the **Glitch** instead of completely stopping it and prevents it from being knocked back.

- The Sledger is not recommended against this enemy, as the **Glitch** can easily avoid being hit by the Sledger because of its slow firerate and low range. However, multiple Sledgers can still be effective against this.
- Because of the **Glitch's** high speed, towers with slow firerate and short range, such as the Shotgunner, Demoman and Gladiator, will perform poorly against these enemies.
- A group of Level 5 Gladiators can perform well against the **Glitch**.
- Projectile based towers, like the Mortar or Demoman, can also miss the **Glitch** due to its speed.
- Area of effect towers, such as the Executioner, Rocketeer or Mortar can be used against **Glitches**, as they mostly spawn in groups.
- The Military Base's Tank and Railgun Tank, as well as the Mercenary Base's Riot Guard can absorb damage from damaged **Glitches** somewhat well.
- However, do not rely solely on this as a horde of **Glitches** can wipe through all of your units.
Trivia: - This was at one point the fastest enemy in the game, tied with the Bug.
- This record was beaten by the Fallen Rusher while it has its shield.
- The Error is a variant of the **Glitch** that also appears in Legacy Fallen mode.
- Prior to the 26th of May 2020, the Error was faster than the **Glitch**.
- Unlike the **Glitch**, the Error has shield health.
- The **Glitch** makes a beep sound when it dies, specifically this sound.
Update History: - No longer appears in Hidden Wave.
- Speed increased from Swift to Extremely Swift (12).
- Energy Immunity replaced with Stun Immunity.
- No longer appears in Fallen mode, as it has been replaced by the Fallen Rusher.
- **Glitch** now appears in Legacy Fallen mode, if activated through Sandbox mode.
- **Glitch** no longer appears in Legacy Fallen mode, as it has been removed.
- No longer appears in Pizza Party.
- No longer appears in Badlands II.
- **Glitch** now appears in Legacy Fallen mode, if activated through Sandbox mode.
- **Bug**: No longer appears in the Index.
- **Bug**: **Glitch** no longer uses the death sound effect.
- No longer appears in public rotation of Challenge Maps, as they exclusively appear within Sandbox mode.

glitched_giant.name: Glitched Giant
glitched_giant.description: The Glitched Giant was a special enemy that only appeared in the legacy Hidden Wave, and thus only appeared in Fallen mode.

notice.text: Glitched Giant has been removed from the game as of the 4th of December 2021.

Description: The **Glitched Giant** was a special enemy that only appeared in the legacy Hidden Wave, and thus only appeared in Fallen mode.

The **Glitched Giant** walked at a slightly fast speed and had an insane amount of health. This enemy was incredibly dangerous for this reason. The **Glitched Giant** could also be spawned by the Creator.
Appearance: The **Glitched Giant** had a similar to style the first version of the Giant Boss, with the same spikes attached to the enemy. However, a sword was stabbed into the back instead of a knife. It was also faceless. It had a granite shirt and pants. Its arms, spikes, shirt, pants and head were sometimes glowing neon and can be a different range of colors. The colors change every second. Glitchy particles could be seen emitting from its torso, similar to the Glitch. It had a twisted left leg.
Strategy: - As with other Legacy Hidden Wave enemies, high DPS towers, such as the **Golden** Minigunner, Accelerator, Turret and Ranger, are recommended.
- The Commander is highly recommended to boost the firerate of these towers.

- The Freezer, the Frost Blaster and the Sledger can slow down this enemy, allowing you towers more time to attack the **Glitched Giant**. This is recommended as they have an outrageous amount of health.
- Be aware that, due to the **Glitched Giant's** large size, it can only be slowed down for a shorter period of time compared to an average-sized enemy.
- The Electroshocker can only slow the **Glitched Giant** for a shorter period of time instead of fully stopping it due to its large size and Stun Immunity.
- The Sledger is recommended to freeze this enemy because it performs one of the highest DPS as a support tower.
- The Toxic Gunner can permanently slow down the **Glitched Giant** by 50%, making it recommended to use.
Trivia: - The **Glitched Giant** is a fusion between the Glitch, Giant Boss and Bug, inheriting traits from all three enemies.
Update History: - Speed increased from Below Average to Slightly Fast (5).
- Partial Electric Immunity replaced with Energy Immunity.
- **Glitched Giant** now appears in the legacy Hidden Wave, which is exclusive to Sandbox mode.
- Because of changes made with updates, its Energy Immunity has been replaced with the Stun Immunity.
- **Glitched Giant** no longer appears in the legacy Hidden Wave, as it has been removed.

gold_guard.name: Gold Guard
gold_guard.description: The Gold Guard is a large guardian enemy exclusive to Golden mode, which is exclusive to Sandbox mode. The Gold Guard always spawns before the Gold Titan.

notice.text: Gold Guard was previously removed on the 29th of October 2020, though it has been made available through the Sandbox mode later.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Trident Impale** - Impales a tower, solidifying and stunning them for a brief period of time.

Description: The **Gold Guard** is a large guardian enemy exclusive to Golden mode, which is exclusive to Sandbox mode. The **Gold Guard** always spawns before the Gold Titan. Its main purpose is to protect the Gold Titan.

It can impale towers with its trident, stunning them for a brief period of time. It has Freeze Immunity, making it impossible to freeze and chill, and the Stun Immunity, making it impossible to knock back and making it only get slowed down by stuns.
Appearance: The **Gold Guard** is made entirely of gold, with a light yellow dominus, pauldrons and a trident. The pauldrons are skull-shaped and had glowing neon eyes. It also wears a light-yellow robe and has light yellow wings. The **Gold Guard** is faceless, and its head is glowing neon.
Strategy: - Despite the common sense of taking the **Gold Guards** down first, they are not too much of a threat given their inferior attacks when compared to the Gold Titan. However, they will reach the exit first, so keep that in mind.
- In any case, it is a good idea to take these down before all attacking towers switch to the Gold Titan.
- Due to their high DPS, Pursuits, Rangers and Turrets are excellent options against these enemies.
- Additionally, the Commander and DJ Booth can be used to boost the DPS of your towers.
- The Medic's ability can cleanse towers stunned by **Gold Guard**.
- Due to its immunities, it cannot be frozen, chilled or knocked back by towers, reducing the number of towers that can stall it.
- Stunning towers will also only slow it down instead of stunning it.
Trivia: - The **Gold Guard** is the only golden enemy that does not have the Splash Damage Immunity.
Update History: - **NOTE**: While the **Gold Guard** was removed in the Overhaul Update, multiple changes were made to it, though they could never be seen in-game due to its removal. These are:
- No longer has Splash Damage Immunity.
- Partial Electric Immunity replaced with Energy Immunity.
- **Gold Guard** can now be summoned in Sandbox mode and appears in the Sandbox exclusive Golden mode.
- Now has the Stun Immunity instead of Energy Immunity.
- Now solidifies towers when stunning them.
- **Gold Guard** no longer appears in Sandbox mode.
- **Gold Guard** can now be summoned in Sandbox mode and appears in the Sandbox exclusive Golden mode.

abilities.label: Ability 2

abilities.label: Ability 3
abilities.text: **Gilded Rain** - Rains down golden fists marked with a red dot from the sky, solidifying any tower hit with golden crystals.

Description: The **Gold Titan** was the third major boss to be added into the game and is the final boss in Golden mode, which is exclusive to Sandbox mode.

The **Gold Titan** walks quite slowly, slower than the Chained Boss, but it has a high amount of health. It is immune to most splash damage and is a Boss enemy, granting it multiple full or partial stalling immunities and some damage immunities.

Its sword is used to stun towers. With this sword it can stab the ground which would stun all towers in the nearby vicinity. It can spawn 3-5 24 Karats at the start of the map, meaning that you need towers to tackle these enemies. The enemy can rain golden fists from the sky as well, making an explosion upon landing, solidifying towers. It could also smash the ground in one direction, solidifying all towers in that direction, though this no longer happens in Sandbox mode.
Appearance: The **Gold Titan** is made of golden blocks to create a robot-type enemy. In its right hand, it wields a golden sword. It has a single rectangular eye in the middle of its head. It is much taller than most enemies. A golden aura pulsates out of its head.
Strategy: - When using any of its attacks, the **Gold Titan** will become immobile. You should use that to your advantage.
- If your towers are crystallized, you can sell them and replace them, if you want to.
- Most splash damage towers, like the Rocketeer, Mortar and Demoman, are useless against the **Gold Titan** as they will deal no damage towards the **Gold Titan** and its summons.
- There are still some sources of splash damage that can damage them. These include the Paintballer, Hallow Punk, Grenade, AirStrike and Nuke.
- Sell them and replace them with high DPS towers such as the Pursuit, Turret or Accelerator.
- Some towers, like the Ranger and Pursuit, despite dealing splash damage, are useful against the **Gold Titan** as they can deal non-splash damage.
- The Commander and DJ Booth can help massively as they can boost the DPS of your towers.
- Due to it being a Boss enemy, many forms of stalling are ineffective against it.
- It cannot be frozen, but it can still be chilled by freezing towers.
- It is only slowed down by stuns instead of being stunned.
- Knockback, DJ Booth slowdown, Harvester slowdown and Toxic Gunner slowdown are completely unable to slow it down.
- It also cannot be damaged by the Nuke's fallout damage.
Trivia: - This was the third major boss to be added to the game, though if you count the Swordmaster as a major boss, this was the fourth to be added.
- *Gilded Rain* appears to rain down golden fists with a diamond shaped eye on them. This is weird considering that the **Gold Titan** appears to have no visible fingers.
- The **Gold Titan** is a based on the Aurelionite from *Risk of Rain 2*.
- A dead **Gold Titan** can be seen lying on the ground in Gilded Path, with its sword next to it, likely representing the removal of Golden mode.
Update History: - **Bugfix**: **Gold Titan** is no longer prone to errors.
- **Gold Titan** now appears at wave 60 instead of wave 56.
- First wave appearance changed from wave 60 to wave 40 in Hard mode (now Golden mode).
- New final wave music, Fallen Boss.
- **NOTE**: While the **Gold Titan** was removed in the Overhaul Update, multiple changes were made to it, though they could never be seen in-game due to its removal. These are:
- Summoned enemies no longer give money when damaged.
- **Gold Titan** can now be summoned in Sandbox mode and appears in the Sandbox exclusive Golden mode.
- Due to changes made with updates, its Energy Immunity has been replaced with the Stun Immunity.
- **Bug**: **Gold Titan** does not use any of its abilities.
- **Gold Titan** can no longer be summoned in Sandbox mode.
- **Gold Titan** can now be summoned in Sandbox mode and appears in the Sandbox exclusive Golden mode.
- *Golden Summoning* summon count decreased from 5-8 to 3-5.
- **Bugfix**: **Gold Titan** now uses its abilities, except *Midas' Slash*.
- **Bug**: **Gold Titan** will sometimes freeze in place if it uses *Shining Sword Stab*.
Notes: https://discord.com/channels/587355301083349002/587355301674614854/607379123907592234 (Tower Defense Simulator Server)

golden.name: Golden
golden.description: The Golden is a golden enemy, as the name suggests. It has an above average speed while having slightly more health than the Abnormal Boss.

notice.text: Golden was previously removed on the 29th of October 2020, though it has been made available through the Sandbox mode later.

Description: The **Golden** is a golden enemy, as the name suggests. It has an above average speed while having slightly more health than the Abnormal Boss. Uniquely, it is immune to splash damage. This meant that the Rocketeer, Mortar and Demoman were useless against this.
The Mystery has a chance to spawn the **Golden** upon its death in Golden mode, wave 21 onwards. It was also spawned by the Gold Titan, though this no longer happens in Sandbox mode.
Appearance: The **Golden** has no face and the enemy was colored gold from the head to the legs. Its torso and legs are a darker shade of gold compared to its arms and head.
Strategy: - Splash damage towers are practically useless against this, 24 Karats, Gold Guards and the Gold Titan as they all have immunity to splash damage.
- It is best to limit the amount of Rocketeers or Demomen you place down. This does not necessarily mean that they are overall useless since they are very effective against the Summoner Boss.
- Despite the fact that the Commando, Pursuit and Military Base deal splash damage, they are still quite effective against the **Golden** due to the fact that they deal non-splash damage.
- Due to the fact that **Goldens** have Splash Damage Immunity, you must take them down one by one with high DPS towers such as the Turret, Minigunner or Outlaw.
- The Electroshocker and Pyromancer can be used to slow groups of these down.
- The Freezer's basic freeze cannot freeze **Goldens**, but the Frost Blaster and Freezer's *Ice Age* ability can freeze it.
Trivia: - When the Uber Mystery was in the game, it had a chance of spawning the **Golden** upon its death in Fallen mode.
- Multiple dead **Goldens** can be seen laying on the ground in Gilded Path.
Update History: - First wave appearance changed from wave 56 to wave 58.
- **Golden** moved from wave 56 to wave 20 of Hard mode (now Golden Mode).
- Speed increased from Slow to Above Average (4).
- **Golden** now appears in Golden mode, if activated through Sandbox mode.
- **Golden** no longer appears in Golden mode, as it has been removed.
- **Golden** now appears in Golden mode, if activated through Sandbox mode.

Description: The **Goo** is an enemy that appears in Polluted Wasteland II. It does not appear naturally and is instead spawned by the Super Slime upon its death. It has a high amount of health and a very fast speed. Upon death, the **Goo** will explode into a slime bubble that stuns all towers caught in it.
Appearance: The **Goo** is a faceless humanoid with a green skin color and a brown torso and legs. All of its body parts are encased in translucent green slime, which constantly emits green particles.
Strategy: - Use high DPS towers such as the Accelerator, Ranger, Pursuit and Engineer to defeat this enemy.
- The Commander and DJ Booth can be very useful at boosting the firerate and range of these towers.
- Towers that can damage multiple enemies, such as the Rocketeer, Mortar and Electroshocker can be useful as multiple **Goos** spawn when the Super Slime is killed.
Trivia: - This enemy is very similar to the Goo that appeared in Trick or Threat Town.
Update History: - Now has 800 health in Pizza Party.
- **Bug**: **Goo** no longer appears, as the Radioactive Slime no longer summons it.
- No longer appears in Pizza Party.

goo_trick_or_threat_town.name: Goo
goo_trick_or_threat_town.description: The Goo was a completely lime green enemy. It was faceless. All of its body parts were encased in a slime capsule which was slightly translucent.

notice.text: Goo (Trick or Threat Town) has been removed from the game as of the 8th of May 2021 as it was part of the Halloween 2020 Event.

Description: The **Goo** was an enemy that appeared exclusively in Trick or Threat Town as part of the Halloween 2020 Event. It did not appear naturally; instead, two **Goos** spawned when a Slime died. It was the fastest enemy in the event, being a bit faster than the Witch. It also had fairly high health, 200 more than the Hallow Bones.
Appearance: The **Goo** was a completely lime green enemy. It was faceless. All of its body parts were encased in a slime capsule which was slightly translucent. It emitted goo particles from its body. It had an awkward running animation.
Strategy: - Since the **Goo** is quite fast, you may want to use the Electroshocker, Freezer or Frost Blaster to slow it down.
- Because of the **Goo's** high speed, the Ranger paired with the DJ Booth can be quite useful against it, as the Ranger has a very long range.
- The Commander's *Call to Arms* ability can also help against the **Goo**, as the ability boosts the Ranger's slow firerate.
- Setting your Rangers to *First* is recommended for this, as they will target stronger enemies otherwise, leaving your base vulnerable.
- The Military Base's Tanks and Railgun Tanks are useful if the **Goo** outruns your towers.
- Do note that it can be expensive to upgrade the Military Base in Trick or Threat Town.
Trivia: - The **Goo** is inspired by the Goo from *Tower Battles*.

Description: The **Grandmother Ducky** was an enemy which appeared in Bathroom Approach as part of the Ducky Revenge Event and its rerun in the Spring Frenzy Battle Pass. It has a decent amount of health and slightly fast speed.
Upon death, it will spawn three aged eggrolls, which can be the Aged Eggroll 1, Aged Eggroll 2 and Aged Eggroll 3. These enemies will then summon a Fat Ducky upon death.
Logbook Description: "*Grandma Ducky is the sweetest, most endearing duck around. Full of love and compassion for all of the ducklings, she’ll spend countless hours telling them stories and baking them homemade buckwheat cookies. One by one she’ll sit each duckling on her lap and preen their little heads before sending them off to explore the world.*"
Appearance: The **Grandmother Ducky** is a regular, yellow duck with an orange beak, orange flippers and grey hair, which represents its age. It wears light yellow and pink knitted clothes, and grey glasses. It uses a stroller to help it walk. It holds two wooden knitting needles and a green yarn.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Bathroom Approach is listed instead.
- As the **Grandmother Ducky** summons three eggrolls upon death, it is quite a dangerous enemy.

- Single target towers like the Pursuit, Golden Crook Boss, Turret or Golden Minigunner can also be helpful.

abilities.label: Ability 1 Cooldown: 35
abilities.text: **Summon** - The **Grave Digger** raises its shovel and smites itself with lightning, being electrocuted within the process. Spawns multiple random enemies from the ground for 8 seconds, all with different chances of spawning and delays between next spawn.

abilities.label: Ability 2 Cooldown: 60

abilities.label: Ability 3 Cooldown: 45
abilities.text: **Shovel** - The **Grave Digger** digs out pieces of dirt from the ground, which it flings into the air. These stun towers for 3 seconds and deal 700 damage to units upon landing.

Description: The **Grave Digger** is the final boss for Casual mode and one of the Challenge Trials mini-bosses. It also appeared in The Classic Event. The **Grave Digger** has Stun Immunity, reducing the effectiveness of the stun from stunning towers like the Electroshocker and Warden, while also preventing it from being knocked back. As it is a Boss enemy, it is also immune to being frozen by freezing towers, slowed down by the Toxic Gunner, confused by the Jester, damaged from the Nuke's fallout and slowed down by the DJ Booth.

It has very high health compared to anything that spawns before, but to compensate, it moves very slowly. In addition, it can stun towers and damage units by performing its *Stomp* or *Shovel* abilities, both having different stun duration and damage values. It can also perform its *Summon* ability which spawns multiple enemies. These enemies all have different odds of spawning and start a delay before another enemy be spawned.
The **Grave Digger** was replaced by the Toilet Boss in Headache Headquarters.
Appearance: **Variant 1**

The **Grave Digger** is a hulking humanoid with a waist, lower arms and lower legs in its rig. It has a desaturated light green skin color and has grey legs. It wears a ragged grey cloak with a hood, sleeves and coattails, which has white accents and patches of cloth sewn on. It has tan bandages wrapped on its legs and lower arms, which have green fluid stains on them. It wears black boots with brown laces, white pauldrons with grey edges, and two brown belts with white buckles, with one on the torso and one on the waist. It has a light grey tombstone with a crown shape at the top chained to its back. It has an angry face with glowing red eyes, sharp teeth and stitches at the sides of its mouth. It wields a shovel with a dark brown wooden handle and a light grey metal spade and end.

For its *Summon* ability, it will point its shovel skyward, where lightning will then continuously strike on it until the ability ends. For its *Stomp* ability, it stomps its right foot, creating a white shockwave and a small crater in the ground. For its *Shovel* ability, it digs its shovel into the ground, and brings it back up, which flings cubes of brown dirt at towers.

It has a death animation where it will place its shovel on the ground to act like a cane, before trembling, dropping the shovel and falling to its knees and hands. It then outstretches its right hand before falling face first onto the ground. Due to a bug, the **Grave Digger's** corpse despawns before the death animation finishes, and can only fully be viewed with Time Scale set to a higher setting.
**Variant 2**

The first version of the **Grave Digger** was a very large humanoid with a desaturated green skin color. It wore a ragged black cloak with a cape, hood and sleeves and had granite dark green legs. It had a glowing red eyes, had white bandages wrapped around its arms and legs and wore grey diamond plate boots. It had a light grey tombstone chained to its back and had brown belts with grey buckles on its torso. It wielded a large shovel with a brown wooden handle and a grey metal spade and cap.

For its *Summon* ability, it will dig its shovel into the ground repeatedly. For its *Stomp* ability, it would stomp its right foot into the ground, creating a white shockwave. On death, it slowly fell on its back whilst dropping its shovel and emitting a low groaning sound.
Enemies Spawned: - 0.05 second delay before another enemy can be spawned.
- 0.05 second delay before another enemy can be spawned.
- 0.1 second delay before another enemy can be spawned.
- 0.1 second delay before another enemy can be spawned.
- 0.2 second delay before another enemy can be spawned.
- 0.2 second delay before another enemy can be spawned.
- 0.3 second delay before another enemy can be spawned.
Strategy: - Multiple early-game towers like the Militant, Hunter, Crook Boss and Cowboy should be enough to defeat the **Grave Digger**.
- High DPS towers, like the Minigunner, Ranger or Accelerator can also be used, though they can be quite expensive for Casual mode.
- The Commander, Medic and DJ Booth should be used to support these towers.

- Be aware that the **Grave Digger** can spawn multiple enemies at once. This means that if the Accelerator locks onto the **Grave Digger**, you may need to place other towers like the Minigunner or Turret to deal with the summoned enemies.
- Rocketeers, Demomen and Mortars can be helpful against this boss as they are able to kill the enemies summoned from the *Summon* ability fairly well.
- Towers near the path are vulnerable to the *Stomp* and *Shovel* abilities. Placing towers away from the path can help avoid some of them getting stunned.
- Towers with Stun Immunity, like the Ranger, Brawler or Gatling Gun can be used as they cannot be stunned.
- The Medic can also be used to make towers which are not normally immune to stuns immune to them.
- If you want to kill the **Grave Digger** quickly, instant damage methods such as airdropping Riot Guards or multiple Bear Traps from Trapper can be effective.

- Using the Nuke consumable can greatly wound the **Grave Digger** by reducing it to 10,000 health, though this is not recommended as the **Grave Digger** is fairly weak and the consumable could be used for bigger threats.
Trivia: - There is a Roblox bundle based on the **Grave Digger**, namely the Grave Digger bundle.
- Weirdly, the bundle used to call the **Grave Digger** a goblin in its name, despite it not being a goblin in-game.
- The individual items of the bundle, such as the Grave Digger Goblin - Torso, still call it a goblin.
- The **Grave Digger's** final wave music is a remixed version of Cursed Abbey.
- Coincidentally, the Raider Boss also used the same song, just not remixed.
- According to 1x1x1x1 in Classic Forest Camp, the **Grave Digger** is its camping buddy.
- The animation played when summoning is a reference to the Eureka Effect's teleport ability from Team Fortress 2.
- The **Grave Digger** loves tacos, as revealed through the Halloween 2025 Live Events.
Update History: - *Stomp* stun time decreased significantly in Easy mode.
- **Grave Digger** can no longer be confused by the Jester.
- **Grave Digger** is now immune to the fallout damage from the Nuke.

gravekeeper.name: Gravekeeper
gravekeeper.description: The Gravekeeper was considered to be the first major boss of the game to appear. It was the final enemy that appeared in Easy mode.

notice.text: Gravekeeper has been removed from the game as of the 13th of October 2019.

abilities.label: Ability 1
abilities.text: **Tombstone** - The **Gravekeeper** will raise its hammer in the air, creating four (rarely eight) Tombstones next to it.

abilities.label: Ability 2
abilities.text: **Smash** - The Gravekeeper will raise its hammer and smash it onto the ground, creating a 20 stud shockwave radius, stunning nearby towers.

Description: The **Gravekeeper** was considered to be the first major boss of the game to appear. It was the final enemy that appeared in Easy mode. The **Gravekeeper** would later be removed, and, replaced with the Grave Digger in Release v1.0.

The **Gravekeeper** walked slower than the Slow Boss but had far higher health compared to the Slow Boss. It could spawn 4-8 Tombstones which needed to be destroyed. These Tombstones could have spawned Normals, Slows, Hiddens and Normal Bosses. It also had the ability to smash its hammer into the ground, creating a shockwave which stunned nearby towers.
Appearance: The **Gravekeeper** had green skin, a grey torso, wore a grey cloak with sleeves and had dark green legs. The **Gravekeeper** also had a chain wrapped around its torso, a black hood, and one red eye (the other was covered by an eye patch). The **Gravekeeper** also wielded a giant rusty hammer and had a Tombstone on its back.
Strategy: - The Freezer's *Ice Drop* ability can handle the two **Gravekeepers** that spawn on wave 55.
- Commanders can be used to boost high DPS towers such as the Minigunner and Turret.
- Towers near the path are vulnerable to the *Hammer Smash*. Try to locate towers away from the path, if possible.
- The Tombstones the **Gravekeeper** spawns may cause a problem if no towers can reach them. Locate a tower near them, or rely on Military Base units or crooks from the Crook Boss to clear them up.
- Multiple Outlaws can be used against this as it has long range and high damage.
Trivia: - There was a glitch where you could place a tower on the body of the **Gravekeeper** when it was killed, allowing for more towers to be placed on maps like Doomspire where placement space was limited.
- As with the other major bosses at the time, towers will fire on the **Gravekeeper** for a few seconds after its death.
- The eyepatch used by the **Gravekeeper** is the Eyepatch accessory from the Roblox catalog.

gravestone.name: Gravestone
gravestone.description: The Gravestone was an enemy that appeared in Blind Faith as part of the Null & Void Event.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Undead Surprise** - Upon destructions, spawns a random skeleton. Which skeleton is made depends on how the **Gravestone** was made.

Description: The **Gravestone** was an enemy that appeared in Blind Faith as part of the Null & Void Event. It is an immobile Aggro enemy, meaning that it cannot kill the player directly though it can distract towers from targeting it.

When destroyed, it will create a skeleton, with the skeleton created depending on how the **Gravestone** was made. If summoned by the Null Necromancer, it can spawn the Giant Skeleton, Hallow Guard and Executioner Skeleton. If summoned by the player in Sandbox mode, it will always spawn a Hallow Guard.
Logbook Description: "*The Gravestone was carefully created by Grave Digger. After his mutation, he spent days carving thousands of these stone heads. The Necromancers discovered how to enchant them, binding their magic to each stone so that the dead would rise wherever one is placed.*"
Mutation: Assumes that Mutation is activated and a **Gravestone** is created on the earliest wave possible of the Hard difficulty.
Appearance: The **Gravestone** is a dark grey gravestone with a crack in it and a black skull on top.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Blind Faith is listed instead.
- The **Gravestone** itself is not a threat as it cannot kill the player directly, though it can lead to other enemies getting past your towers.
- Defense dropping towers can be used to reduce its high defense of 130%.
- As it has the Freeze Immunity, freezing towers cannot be used for this.
Trivia: - Prior to the v2.3.0, the **Gravestone** had the highest Defense of all enemies in the game, at 130%. This would end up being overtaken by the Vindicator, with a ludicrous 150% base Defense.
- The **Gravestone** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Gravestone** removed from the main game, now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.
- **Bug**: Cannot be spawned in Sandbox mode.
- **Bugfix**: Can now be spawned in Sandbox mode.

grizzly.name: Grizzly
grizzly.description: The Grizzly was a bear that only appeared in Eggy Island hard mode as part of the Spring 2020 Event. It did not appear in easy mode.

notice.text: Grizzly has been removed from the game as of the 26th of May 2020 as it was part of the Spring 2020 Event.

abilities.label: Ability 1
abilities.text: **Heal** - Heals about 50 health. Red crosses can be seen when the **Grizzly** is healing.

abilities.label: Ability 2
abilities.text: **Claw** - Attacks a nearby tower. Any tower caught in the range of the claw attack is stunned for a while.

abilities.label: Ability 3
abilities.text: **Beehive** - Chews on a beehive which makes it immune to most forms of damage.

Description: The **Grizzly** was a bear that only appeared in Eggy Island hard mode as part of the Spring 2020 Event. It did not appear in easy mode.

The **Grizzly** had a high amount of health (though it had 250 less health than Sir Hopsalot in hard mode). It walked slightly faster than Sir Hopsalot. It had three abilities. *Heal* healed **Grizzly** by about 50 health. The *Claw* attack stunned nearby towers within its range. The *Beehive* ability made it immune to most forms of damage.
Appearance: The **Grizzly** had the appearance of a brown bear. On its torso, it had partial white fur. It had three sharpened claws on each hand and appeared to be wearing a partial black mask.
Strategy: - Try not to leave the **Grizzly** unaccompanied for too long.

- If it crosses to the other island and you have no towers there, the **Grizzly** will be able to use its *Heal* ability which will most certainly end the game, even if the **Grizzly** is at low health.
- The Enforcer's SWAT Van or the Military Base units can collide with the **Grizzly**, even when it uses its *Beehive* ability, dealing full collision damage.
- Try to place towers away from the path so that they are not targeted by the **Grizzly**.
- The Outlaw is the ideal tower to use for the **Grizzly** as they are normally out of range for this attack.
- When the **Grizzly** is performing its *Beehive* ability, do not activate any new abilities (such as the Commander's *Call of Arms*) as they will have no effect on the **Grizzly**.
Trivia: - The sound **Grizzly** made when eating the beehive was the same sound the Heavy, from *Team Fortress 2*, makes when eating his Sandvich.
- The head of the **Grizzly** was a re-textured version of the Undead Teddy accessory from the ROBLOX catalog.

guest.description: The Guest was an enemy that appeared in Pls Donate as part of the Tower Defense Simulator x PLS DONATE Event.

Description: The **Guest** was an enemy that appeared in Pls Donate as part of the Tower Defense Simulator x PLS DONATE Event. It was faster and has higher health than the Noob that appeared before it. On some waves, it was a Hidden enemy. Additionally, on some waves, it spawned with the Bloated, Nimble and Slime attributes.
Appearance: The **Guest** had white skin. It wore a black shirt and pants that covered up most of its body, alongside a black and red cap. It had a large Roblox logo on its shirt, specifically the one used between the 26th of September 2009 up until the 11th of August 2010. On its sleeves, "*GUEST*" could be seen written in red.
Strategy: - Early game towers like the Crook Boss, Militant or Military Base can be useful against it.
- As this enemy spawns in hordes, AOE towers like the Pyromancer, Mortar or Electroshocker can be useful against them.
Trivia: - The **Guest** is based on Guests, more specifically the male guest avatar used between the 5th of April 2011 up until 12th of July 2016. which is also known as BillyBloxxer.
- The cap worn by the **Guest** is the Red Roblox Cap from the Roblox catalog.

abilities.label: Ability 1
abilities.text: **Skull Shot** - The **Gunslinger** takes out its revolver and shoots multiple towers, creating a shockwave on impact which stuns towers that are caught in it and damages units by 500.

abilities.label: Ability 2
abilities.text: **Shell Rain** - The **Gunslinger** takes out its double-barreled shotgun and fires it into the air, making shells rain down onto the map, which upon landing create a shockwave that stuns any tower caught in it and deals 500 damage to units.

abilities.label: Ability 3
abilities.text: **Crossbones Crossfire** - The **Gunslinger** takes out its Gatling gun from its coffin, after which it rotates its Gatling gun while constantly firing haphazardly, stunning towers briefly and damaging units by 20 damage per bullet.

abilities.label: Ability 4
abilities.text: **Time's Up** - Upon the **Gunslinger** reaching 50% health, it will take out both of its weapons and scream, temporarily decreasing all nearby tower's range by 50% with the Scared Debuff. Also creates a brief sandstorm on the map, though this is not guaranteed to happen.

Description: The **Gunslinger** is the final boss of Badlands II.

Although it moves slowly, it has a large amount of health and many abilities that can stun lots of towers and destroy units, making it one of the most difficult bosses to defeat in the game. Additionally, the **Gunslinger** is immune to being stunned by the Electroshocker and Warden and it is instead slowed down, frozen by freezing towers like the Freezer, Frost Blaster and Sledger, slowed down by the Toxic Gunner, confused by the Jester, knocked back, damaged by the Nuke's fallout damage and slowed down by the DJ Booth.
The **Gunslinger** has four abilities:
- Its first, *Skull Shot*, makes it fire its revolver at multiple towers, creating a shockwave on impact that stuns towers and deals 500 damage to units.

- Its second ability, *Shell Rain*, makes it fire its double-barreled shotgun into the air, making multiple shells fall from the sky, which upon hitting the ground create a shockwave that stuns towers and deals 500 damage to units.
- Its third, *Crossbones Crossfire*, has its Gatling gun fire haphazardly, stunning many towers and damaging multiple units in the process by 20 damage per bullet.

- Its fourth, *Time's Up*, is a rage mode ability where the **Gunslinger** takes out both of its weapons and screams, decreasing the range of nearby towers by 50% with the Scared Debuff. It also creates a brief sandstorm on the map, though this is not guaranteed to happen.
The **Gunslinger** only spawns on the middle path on Wave 30, ignoring the All Paths modifier.
Appearance: The **Gunslinger** is a large skeletal humanoid with a waist and lower arms in its rig. It wears brown pants that cover its waist and legs as well as a black shirt that covers its torso and arms. It has a skull for a head, with an angry expression, as well as a dark brown cowboy hat. It has black shoulder-pads, grey and black arm-pads and brown gloves on each arm.

It has a dark grey scarf, a black chestplate and two brown bandoliers filled with yellow bullets on its torso. It has a brown wooden coffin on its back, which conceals a mounted black and golden Gatling gun. It also has a steampunk themed black and gold blunderbuss and double barrel shotgun hanging off of the coffin. It has black and grey knee-pads and brown shoes on its legs, as well as a belt on its waist, with yellow bullets stored on it.
The **Gunslinger** has a death animation, where it be lit entirely on fire and fall forward. After the fire disappears, it will appear completely black.
Strategy: - High DPS towers, such as the Accelerator, Turret, Engineer, Golden Minigunner and Ranger are recommended to defeat the **Gunslinger**.
- The Pursuit can also be useful here, as it is immune to stuns and debuffs, making it unaffected by all of the **Gunslinger's** abilities.
- The Ranger is immune to stuns from the **Gunslinger's** abilities, making it very useful against the **Gunslinger**.
- The Turret can be a bit useful here, as it is immune to the Scared Debuff applied by the **Gunslinger**.

- Make sure to sell any Farms to maximize the number of towers attacking the **Gunslinger**. They do not produce any income anymore, count towards your tower limit and can be replaced by a more useful tower.
- In Badlands II, due to the high number of enemies that spawn, you will have more than enough money by the time the **Gunslinger** spawns, meaning that you can sell your Farms earlier.

- The Cowboy and Golden Cowboy can still produce income, so you can keep them if you need more cash for your towers. However, this is generally not necessary, as you will get a lot of cash from damaging enemies and the **Gunslinger** itself.
- Because of this, you can also sell your Cowboys or Golden Cowboys at later waves, if you can place down any other high DPS towers.
- The DJ Booth can be used to partially mitigate the effects of the **Gunslinger's** Scared Debuff.
- It can also be useful at increasing your tower's range and decreasing its upgrade costs.
- You can also try to replace your towers after the *Time's Up* ability, though this is not necessary.
- The Medic can be quite useful for shielding your towers from stuns.
- Do note that the Medic's shield cannot be used to protect towers from the Scared Debuff.
- The **Gunslinger** cannot be slowed down by most towers.
- Due to how short the map is, the Jester can be useful to stall the boss.
- The Warden and Electroshocker can slow down the **Gunslinger** instead of stunning it, though because of its large size, the Warden can only slow it down for a shorter amount of time.
- It is also immune to being frozen by the Freezer, Frost Blaster and Sledger, due to its freeze immunity.
- The Frost Blaster and Sledger can, however, be useful against the enemies that appear before the **Gunslinger**.
- The Toxic Gunner cannot slow this down as the **Gunslinger** is immune to its slowdown. It can, however, be useful against the enemies that appear before it.
- The Jester cannot confuse it, though it can still slow it down with its ice bombs.
Trivia: - The **Gunslinger's** name is the word for men in the American Old West who had gained a reputation for being dangerous with a gun.

- Upon death, the **Gunslinger** will burst into flames and collapse. This is likely a reference to how people or animals perish in the desert due to the scorching heat, leading to dehydration and death. Due to the environment, their bones never fully decompose.
- The Level 5 **Badlands** skin for the Cowboy and Golden Cowboy is heavily based on this enemy.
- The scream that can be heard when the **Gunslinger** performs its *Time's Up* ability is the same one that can be heard while fighting the Nuclear Monster.
- Due to a bug, Badlands II matches may sometimes have more than four players, making it a MEGA Server. This will cause the **Gunslinger's** health to increase by 15,000 for each player.
Update History: - **Bug**: **Gunslinger** does not use any of its abilities except *Time's Up*.
- **Gunslinger** can no longer be confused by the Jester.
- **Gunslinger** is now immune to the fallout damage from the Nuke.
- **Bug**: *Crossbones Crossfire* ability bullet trails no longer appear.
- **Bug**: Can be slowed down by the DJ Booth.
- **Bugfix**: No longer can be slowed down by the DJ Booth.
- **Gunslinger** can no longer have its defense dropped.
- **Bug**: Appears twice in the Index, one of them not loading in any model for the preview.
- **Bug**: **Gunslinger** occasionally stops moving after using some of its abilities.
- **Bugfix**: **Gunslinger** no longer stops moving after using some of its abilities.
- **Bugfix**: No longer appears twice in the Index.

hallow_bones.name: Hallow Bones
hallow_bones.description: The Hallow Bones was an enemy that appeared exclusively in Trick or Threat Town as part of the Halloween 2020 Event.

notice.text: Hallow Bones has been removed from the game as of the 8th of May 2021 as it was part of the Halloween 2020 Event.

Description: The **Hallow Bones** was an enemy that appeared exclusively in Trick or Threat Town as part of the Halloween 2020 Event. It moved faster than the Bones and slower than the Witch. It had an average amount of health, for its debut.
The **Hallow Bones** could be spawned by the Reaper and Lord Sinister.
Appearance: The **Hallow Bones** was structured similar to the Bones. It was entirely made out of marble dark grey parts to represent a skeleton. It did not have a full torso, but instead had the bone cage for it. Its head was slightly smaller than usual and had two large yellow eyes. It had a slightly different walking animation.
Strategy: - Use Rangers to quickly kill the **Hallow Bones** and do damage to the Reaper or Lord Sinister that can spawn the **Hallow Bones**.
- Since **Hallow Bones** usually spawn in hordes, explosive towers, such as the Rocketeer and Mortar, are useful when attempting to defeat this.
- However, note that the movement speed of the **Hallow Bones** might outrun the projectiles.
- Fast-firing towers, such as the Minigunner and the Turret, are able to deal significant amounts of damage to the **Hallow Bones**.
Trivia: - The **Hallow Bones** had a death animation where it would fall into a pile of bones and its head would roll a short distance.
- This was also the same animation used for the Bones.

Appearance: The **Hallow Guard** is made entirely of white parts that resemble a skeletal humanoid. It does not have a full torso, but instead has the bone cage for it. Its head is slightly smaller than most other enemies and has two large flaming blue eyeholes. It wears a brown belt, grey shoulder-pads, crown and a chestplate, which as a black skull with neon blue eyes on it.

hallow_guard_lunar_overture.name: Hallow Guard
hallow_guard_lunar_overture.description: The Hallow Guard was an enemy that appeared in the second act of the Lunar Overture Event.

notice.text: Hallow Guard (Lunar Overture) has been removed from the game as of the 21st of December 2023 as it was part of the Lunar Overture Event.

Description: The **Hallow Guard** was an enemy that appeared in the second act of the Lunar Overture Event. It was a tanky enemy with high health, high defense and an average speed, which spawned in hordes. It had Stun Immunity, which made the Electroshocker and Warden only slow it down instead of fully stopping it. Additionally, it was immune to splash damage.

The **Hallow Guard** could be spawned by the Reaper, however, the **Hallow Guard** spawned had random health. The health was higher than 2,500, but lower than 3,000. It was also slightly smaller and faster.
Appearance: The **Hallow Guard** was a large skeletal humanoid with a waist, lower arms and lower legs in its rig. It had a ribcage instead of a torso and wore a grey chestplate with a dark grey skull that had glowing blue parts. It also wore grey shoulder-pads with spikes as well as a brown belt with a grey buckle. It had a pair of black eyeholes in its head with blue flames being emitted from them.
On death, the **Hallow Guard** would fall into a pile of bones while playing a bone shaking sound.
Strategy: - High DPS towers like the Accelerator, Minigunner or Pursuit are quite effective against this.
- The Commander and DJ Booth can be useful at boosting their firerate and range respectively.
- As the **Hallow Guard** is immune to splash damage, splash damage towers are useless against the **Hallow Guard**.
- Towers that deal both regular and splash damage are also less effective against it.
- Defense dropping towers like the Pyromancer or Electroshocker can be useful against this, as it has a pretty high defense.
Trivia: - Although the **Hallow Guard** did not have the ghost immunity, units could not collide with it.
- Although this enemy shares the name with the Hallow Guard from Trick or Threat Town, the only similarity is that they are both skeletons.

debuts.title: The Haunted Past (Lunar Overture Event, Act II)

hallow_guard_trick_or_threat_town.name: Hallow Guard

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Slash** - Attacks towers with its sword, stunning them for a while.

Description: The **Hallow Guard** was an enemy that appeared exclusively in Trick or Threat Town, and was the first enemy to spawn, as part of the Halloween 2020 Event. Currently, it can be spawned again in Sandbox mode, It also has 35% defense which means that the **Hallow Guard** may take a while to defeat. Additionally, it can stun towers with its *Slash* ability.
Appearance: The **Hallow Guard** is very similar to the Hallow Bones, except that it is much taller than it. It is entirely made out of marble dark grey parts to represent a skeleton. It does not have a full torso, but instead has the bone cage for it. Its head is slightly smaller than usual and has two large yellow eyes. Fire is emitted from its eyes. It has dark marble armor and helmet. It holds a sword which is used to slash at towers.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Trick or Threat Town during its event is listed instead.
- Due to their high health and defense, the Ranger is the best tower against the **Hallow Guard**.
- Placing down multiple Level 3+ Rangers is recommended to take down this enemy.
- The Accelerator and Turret can also be used.
- Be aware that if the Accelerator is stunned, it will have to go through its lengthy charge-up again.
- The Minigunner can also be used, but due to the **Hallow Guard's** defense, it will only deal half damage towards it.
- You can lower the **Hallow Guard's** defense by using the Pyromancer, Freezer or Electroshocker.
- If you can, try to place towers away from the path so that they cannot be targeted by the **Hallow Guard**.
- Cliff and air-based towers cannot be targeted, making them ideal against the **Hallow Guard**.
- Using the Commander's *Call to Arms* ability to boost the firerate of towers attacking this enemy is a good idea.
Trivia: - The **Hallow Guard** had a death animation where it would fall into a pile of bones and its head would roll a short distance.
- When the **Hallow Guard** was first added, its death animation did not play correctly.
- Instead it just stood still. This prevented units from getting past it.
- The **Hallow Guard** may be a reference to the Wither Skeleton from *Minecraft*.
Update History: - **Bug**: Death animation does not play; instead it stands still.
- **Hallow Guard** can now be summoned in Sandbox mode, only when the player has the Hallow Guard's Logbook from the Null & Void Event.

Description: The **Hazard** is a quick enemy that only appears in some challenges and the Sandbox exclusive Legacy Fallen mode. While the **Hazard** gives off the impression that its immune to certain effects; it is not immune to anything, though it has a defense of 15%. It has 50 health in total and also has 50 shield health. It is slightly faster than the Fallen.
The **Hazard** can be spawned by the Mystery upon its death in Legacy Fallen mode, wave 29 onwards.
Appearance: **Variant 1**

The **Hazard** is an enemy with a desaturated light green skin color. It has a yellow diamond-plated torso and legs, with black and yellow tanks and a breathing apparatus strapped onto its torso. It also has a mask with a black glass visor strapped onto its head. It also has black and yellow armbands on its arms, with the black parts being made of diamond-plating.
**Variant 2**

The Enemies Beta version of the **Hazard** has a light green skin color, as well as a black torso, arms and legs. It wears a yellow and black hazmat suit, which consists of shoulder-pads, a vest, gas tanks, shoes and a helmet with a grey screen.
Strategy: - Splash damage towers, like the Demoman, Mortar and Rocketeer, are recommended against the **Hazard** since they mostly spawn in groups, Additionally, splash damage ignores its defense, dealing full damage.
- Other towers that can hit multiple enemies, like the Electroshocker or Executioner can also be used.
- Towers with decent DPS, such as the Minigunner, Turret and Accelerator, will certainly help against **Hazards**.
- Slowing towers like the Electroshocker, Warden or Sledger can be quite useful against this.
- Due to its average size and lack of immunities, these towers can easily stop a horde of **Hazards** in its track.
- Towers that drop defense, such as the Pyromancer, Electroshocker or Freezer, can be effective against the **Hazard**, allowing your towers to deal more damage to it.
- This is not required however, as the **Hazard** has negligible defense and low health.
Trivia: - The **Hazard** was likely inspired by the Ticker from *R2DA*.
- Despite hazmat suits being known to be flame-retardant, the **Hazard** is not immune to poison or fire.
- There is a skin series that has a similar appearance to the current appearance of the **Hazard**, namely the **Hazmat** from the Premium Crate.
- The mask that the **Hazard** wears is the Fire Fighter Hazard Mask accessory from the Roblox catalog.
- The mask that the Enemies Beta **Hazard** wears is a re-textured version of the Hazmat Isolation Helmet accessory from the Roblox catalog.
- The Enemies Beta **Hazard** uses a slightly altered version of the Hazardous's model.
Update History: - Speed increased from Fast to Very Fast (8).
- Now has a new appearance with the Enemies Beta modifier active.
- No longer naturally appears in Fallen mode, as it has been replaced by the Fallen Hazmat.
- **Hazard** now appears in Legacy Fallen mode, if activated through Sandbox mode.
- **Hazard** no longer appears in Legacy Fallen mode, as it has been removed.
- No longer appears in Badlands II.
- **Hazard** now appears in Legacy Fallen mode, if activated through Sandbox mode.
- **Bug**: No longer appears in the Index.
- No longer appears in public rotation of Challenge Maps, as they exclusively appear within Sandbox mode.

The **Hazardous** could be spawned by the Mystery upon its death in Polluted Wasteland II.
