It walks with its head slightly tilted downwards and its arms pointing forward. It also emits light green particles.
Strategy: - Strong early-game towers like the Golden Crook Boss, Golden Cowboy or Engineer can clear this out quite easily.
- Because this enemy spawns in large hordes, the Electroshocker and the Mortar can be really helpful against it.
- The Electroshocker can also slow it down, which gives your towers more time to kill it.
Trivia: - This enemy's appearance appears to be based on the Ticker from *R2DA*.

Description: The **Hazmat** is an enemy that appears in Casual, Intermediate, Challenge Trials, Basic Arena PVP and Molten Arena PVP modes. It also appeared in The Takeover Event. It can also be sent by a player in Basic Arena PVP, which is the only way for it to appear there. It has a decent amount of health, a slightly fast speed and 60% defense. Additionally, it always spawns with the Stun and Freeze Immunity, making it harder to slow down. On multiple waves, it also appears with the Health Regen and Slime attributes.
It can be spawned by the Grave Digger with its *Triumphing Sheol* ability. Patient Zero also used to be able to summon it. Due to a bug, it used to replace the Hazardous in Polluted Wasteland II.
Appearance: **Variant 1**

The **Hazmat** has a dark green skin color. It wears a yellow and black hazmat suit, which consists of single glove, a vest, gas tank, shoes and a helmet with a broken screen. It has three different walking animations that are randomly chosen when it spawns.
**Variant 2**

The **Hazmat** had a light green skin color, as well as a black torso, arms and legs. It worea yellow and black hazmat suit, which consists of shoulder-pads, a vest, gas tanks, shoes and a helmet with a translucent grey screen. It had three different walking animations that were randomly chosen when it spawns.
Strategy: - High DPS towers like the Accelerator, Minigunner or Engineer can be quite useful against this.
- Area of effect towers, like the Rocketeer, Mortar or Pyromancer can be quite useful against this, as it spawns in groups.
- Additionally, splash damage towers bypass its Defense, allowing them to deal full damage to it and making them especially useful against the **Hazmat**.
- Defense dropping towers like the Pyromancer, Electroshocker or DJ Booth can be useful against this, as it has quite high defense.
- Additionally, the Pyromancer or Jester can be quite efficient at killing **Hazmats**.
- As it has Freeze Immunity, freezing towers cannot be used to drop its defense.
- It cannot be knocked back as it has the Stun Immunity.
Trivia: - Between the 23rd and 31st of May 2024, the **Hazmat** accidentally replaced the Polluted Hazmat in Polluted Wasteland II. This made Wave 7 and the following waves significantly harder due to the steep health increase.
- Before the issue was fixed altogether, the **Hazmat's** health was reduced to 60 in Polluted Wasteland II to balance the mode out.
- The randomized animations are inspired by the Ticker from *Reason 2 Die: Awakening*.
- The icon for the Hazmat uses its first appearance instead of its current appearance.
- This is due to the icon used being actually taken and uploaded a day before v1.45.0 released, where at the time it used that appearance. The icon was never updated for its new appearance.

- **Bug**: Now replaces the Hazmat in Polluted Wasteland II.
- Health decreased from 150 to 60 in Polluted Wasteland II.
- **Bugfix**: No longer replaces the Polluted Hazmat.
- **Bugfix**: Poison and electric defense dropping now drops **Hazmat's** defense, though the Jester still cannot drop it.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Axe Throw** - The **Headless Jaxe** throws its axe at a random tower or unit, stunning any tower hit by it. This attack deals at least 60 damage to units hit by it.

Description: The **Headless Jaxe** was an enemy that appeared in the fourth night of the Solar Eclipse Event. It was the first boss that spawned on the fourth night. It had a high amount of health but it walked slowly. It had one ability where it threw its axe at a tower, stunning any tower hit by it.
Appearance: The **Headless Jaxe** is a headless version of the Jaxe, which had an overall slightly darker body. It had green skin. It wore a black cape, grey chestplate with a green shard, shoulder pads and knee pads. It also had black wristbands and orange armbands on both of its arms. It wielded a large axe to attack towers. It emitted green fire above its torso.
Strategy: - Towers with high DPS, such as the Ranger, Accelerator or Minigunner are recommended.
- You can use the Commander and DJ Booth boost the firerate and range of these towers respectively.
- The Ranger, Ace Pilot and Pursuit cannot be stunned by the **Headless Jaxe's** *Axe Throw* ability, making them strong options.
- Concentrated groups of ground towers should be avoided, as the **Headless Jaxe** can stun multiple towers at once with its ability.
- You can use cheap towers like the Scout to distract the **Headless Jaxe's** *Axe Throw* ability away from your main attacking towers.
- The *Axe Throw* ability will destroy most units if they are hit by it, with the exception of the Tank and Railgun Tank.
Trivia: - The **Headless Jaxe's** head is missing as upon the defeat of the Jaxe in Rotfield, its head fell off.
- This head was later turned into a candy bucket for the Candy Throw emote, as suggested by the emote's description.
- The **Headless Jaxe** might be a reference to the Headless Horseman.

healing_beacon.description: The Healing Beacon, internally referred to as just Beacon, is a support enemy that appears in Hardcore and Voidcore modes.

Description: The **Healing Beacon**, internally referred to as just **Beacon**, is a support enemy that appears in Hardcore and Voidcore modes. It is not a regular as on top of only appearing when summoned, it is completely invulnerable to damage, has only 1 health and when entering the exit deals no damage and instead just disappears. It instead has a lifetime of 6, which means once 6 seconds pass, it will disappear from the path.
When on the path, it will heal any enemy on the circle, which has a radius of 8, by 1,100 every 0.1 seconds.
Appearance: The **Healing Beacon** is a purple incantation circle. It has multiple purple plus signs and waves coming out of it.
Strategy: - It is impossible to stop or kill the **Healing Beacons**.
- Kill the Void Cultist as quickly as possible to limit the amount of **Healing Beacons** spawned.
Trivia: - The **Healing Beacon** is the second fastest enemy in the game.
- With only 1 health, it also has the lowest health of any enemy in the game.
- Despite appearing as a spawnable enemy in Sandbox mode, you cannot collect this logbook.
- Therefore, the only way to spawn this enemy in is to have the Sandbox Plus+ gamepass.
- The **Healing Beacon** is the second evergreen enemy to have its Logbook unobtainable, the first being the Molten Hazmat.
- The **Healing Beacon** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Bug**: Lifetime is not affected by Time Scale.
- **Bug**: **Healing Beacon** has a broken icon in Sandbox mode.

health_cultist.name: Health Cultist
health_cultist.description: The Health Cultist is a support-type enemy that appears in Sandbox and only appeared in Hardcore mode. The Health Cultist heals enemies within its range.

notice.text: Health Cultist was previously removed on the 5th June 2026, though it has been made available through the Sandbox mode later.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Heal** - Raises its arms, creating an incantation circle which restores the health of enemies in its radius and itself by 2.5% of their maximum health every 0.2 seconds, and walks at a slower speed.

Description: The **Health Cultist** is a support-type enemy that appears in Sandbox and only appeared in Hardcore mode.

The **Health Cultist** heals enemies within its range. Healed enemies are visually indicated by a glowing green incantation circle underneath them and floating green crystals around them. This will heal enemies by 2.5% of the maximum health every 0.2 seconds. As it heals other enemies, it will cause problems if not dealt with quickly.
When it is not healing, the **Health Cultist** walks quite quickly, but its legs do not move. When it is healing enemies, it walks quite slowly. It also has quite high health.
Appearance: The **Health Cultist** appears to be a normal-sized enemy with a dark black granite robe. Some parts of the robe are light green. Green spikes stick out from its neck. It also wears a black granite hood over its faceless head. Its skin is black, reflective and metallic.
Strategy: This strategy refers to the state of the game while the **Health Cultist** still appeared in the Hardcore mode.
- Due to the fact that the **Health Cultist** can heal itself and other enemies, it must be dealt with as soon as possible.
- This effectively makes enemies with high health unkillable for the duration of its ability.
- High DPS towers like the Accelerator or Engineer are recommended, as their DPS may outpace **Health Cultist's** healing ability.
- The Ranger can also be quite useful against the **Health Cultist**, as its high damage allows it to take out enemies quickly, leaving the **Health Cultist** with no time to heal them.
- Be aware that if you are using small groups of Rangers, its slow firerate means that in between shots, the **Health Cultist** can heal any health lost.
- The Commander can partially circumvent this by decreasing their firerate.
- Fast firing towers, such as the Minigunner or Turret, are highly recommended to take out the Mega Slows and the Slow Kings that are protecting the **Health Cultist**.
- There are periods of time where the **Health Cultist** does not heal any enemies.
- During this window of opportunity, you can activate the Commander's *Call to Arms* ability which can help in defeating the **Health Cultist** and other enemies.
- The **Health Cultist** cannot heal back any shield health lost.
- Make sure all your towers are set to either *First* or *Strongest* when the **Health Cultist** appears.
- Having a mix of targeting settings means that the **Health Cultist** will be able to heal more enemies as damage is more spread out.

- The Military Base's Tank and Railgun Tank can be quite useful against the **Health Cultist** as it can deal an instant burst of damage upon collision, killing enemies before they can be healed by the **Health Cultist**.
- Support towers, such as the Frost Blaster and Electroshocker can help to slow down the **Health Cultist**, and keep it away from healing a horde.

- It is possible to permanently stall the **Health Cultist**, preferably with a level 5 Brawler, if you leaked it. It will keep healing, and one level 5 Brawler will not do enough DPS to take it down. And due to how Hardcore mode's economy system works, you can do this to make a lot of cash.
Trivia: - After being defeated, the **Health Cultist** used to float in the air and explode. Green lightning would strike its body, though this would not grant enemies any additional buff.
- Unusually, the **Health Cultist** only appears once in Hardcore mode, despite not being a major boss.
- The healing ability is similar to the removed enemies, the Witch Doctor, as it heals nearby zombies within its range.

- However, the Witch Doctor can heal 20% of an enemy's current health at random times. They also cannot heal themselves. The **Health Cultist** heals enemies much more quickly, can heal itself and heals 2.5% of an enemy's maximum health.
- The **Health Cultist** had several variants before it was added to the game.
- One variant an orange color scheme while the other had a purple color scheme.
- The incantation circle the **Health Cultist** creates is a reference to *Doctor Strange*, a superhero from the *Marvel* comics.
- The **Health Cultist's** hood is a re-textured version of the Hood of the International Order of Buildmasters accessory from the Roblox catalog.
Update History: - **Health Cultist** removed from the main game, as it has been replaced by Void Cultist. Now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.
- No longer appears in the Index.

Description: The **Heavy Voidling**, internally referred to as **Elite Voidling**, is a high health enemy that appears in Hardcore and Voidcore modes. It has high health and fast speed.
It has two abilities:

- The first and only ability seen in regular gameplay is *Stamp of Execution*, where the **Heavy Voidling** stomps at a tower in its range of 10, creating a shockwave with a radius of 10 that stuns towers for 2.5 seconds and deals 150 damage to units.

- The second ability is *Lane Switch*, which makes the **Heavy Voidling** jump from one path to another, temporarily becoming a Flying enemy. As there are no maps with more than one path in either mode it appears in, this ability goes entirely unused.
Logbook Description: "*Heavy Voidlings were created by Void Cultists as a means of remedying their pacifism. In their mind, stealing an unsuspecting Swift and cramming them into a suit of armor may have been questionable at best, but it was for protecting those who embraced the Void. The Cultists felt this was entirely reasonable, however the Swift inside the suit felt differently. The Cultists have noted the Swift’s complaints and will take them into careful consideration at the next ceremony. They have not yet held the next ceremony.*"
Appearance: The **Voidling** has purple skin and neon pink eyes. Both of its arms are cut off. It wears grey armor on its feet, shoulders neck and waist, strapped to it with brown clothing. On its back it has a small black cape. It also has multiple neon pink crystals growing on its body.
Strategy: - High DPS towers like the Juggernaut, Accelerator, Turret, Engineer or Ranger can be used to take it down.
- Such towers with Stun Immunity can be especially useful, as this means they cannot be stunned by the **Heavy Voidling**.
- Support towers like the DJ Booth, Commander and Medic can be used to boost their DPS.
- The **Heavy Voidling** moves at a fast pace and can be dangerous if not targeted.
- Using towers that can stall enemies like the Electroshocker, Freezer, DJ Booth or Hacker is recommended to slow it down.
Trivia: - The **Heavy Voidling's** ability to jump between paths goes unused in both Hardcore and Voidcore modes as neither mode actually contains maps with more than one path.
- This means it can only actually be seen in Sandbox mode.

- Originally, the **Heavy Voidling** did not have this ability while the Voidling did. Because of this, the enemy got renamed from *Elite Voidling* to *Heavy Voidling* as Elite is typically used for stronger versions of enemies with base mechanics inherited.
- The **Heavy Voidling** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - Cash given on death decreased from $20,000 to $16,000 in Voidcore mode.
Notes: https://x.com/NimTheOne/status/2068735888285106554

Description: The **Hex Corpse** was an enemy that appeared in The Nightmare Realm and Containment in the Hexscape Event. It had moderately high health, defense and speed. Upon death it split into an Upper Body and a **Lower Body**. When transformed into **Lower Body**, it healed back to full health, though all of its statistics remained unchanged. On some waves, it could spawn with Bloated.
Appearance: The **Hex Corpse** had black skin and giant teeth covering face. It wore torn brown clothes. Its torso was cut in half. Upon turning into the **Lower Body**, its upper torso, head and arms disappeared, leaving only its lower torso and legs.
Strategy: - Early-game towers, like the Golden Crook Boss, Cowboy, Militant and Golden Soldier can be quite effective against this.
- The **Hex Corpse** turns spawn the Upper Body when killed, effectively doubling its health when it turns into the **Lower Body**.
- Towers that can damage multiple enemies at once, such as the Pyromancer, Electroshocker or Mortar can be useful here.
- As the Upper Body is significantly slower than the **Lower Body**, it is not as big of a threat as **Lower Body**.
- Defense dropping towers can be used to drop its defense. Such towers include the Pyromancer and Freezer.
- Do note that the dropped defense will not be transferred over to the Upper Body, as that is a different enemy.
Trivia: - **Hex Corpse** and **Lower Body** looked like they were separate enemies, with **Lower Body** even having *Hex Corpse's* next to its name. However, this was not actually the case, as they were the same enemy, which could be seen in multiple ways.
- Their statistics were identical, with the only differences being visual.

- The **Hex Corpse** did not generate cash on death, implying it did not die. However, **Lower Body** did generate cash on death, despite being a summoned enemy which should make it impossible for it do so.

- The Cowboy could generate cash from the **Lower Body**, despite the name suggesting it was a summoned enemy, which should be impossible. However, for the Upper Body, it could not generate cash from it.
Update History: - **Bug**: Poison and electric defense dropping does not decrease **Hex Corpse's** defense.
- **Bug**: Using the Gatling Gun's *FPS* ability does not deal damage to **Lower Body**.
- **Bug**: Damage dealt to the **Hex Corpse's** regenerated health does not increase various damage based meters, like the Accelerator's overcharge or Engineer's scrap meter.
- **Bug**: Units instantly kill the **Hex Corpse** upon collision after it has turned into the **Lower Body**.
- **Bugfix**: Using the Gatling Gun's *FPS* ability now deals damage to **Lower Body**.
- **Bugfix**: Poison and electric defense dropping now drops **Hex Corpse's** defense, though the Jester still cannot drop it.

Description: The **Hex Mimic** was a summoner enemy that appeared in The Nightmare Realm as part of the Hexscape Event. It had a decent amount of health, same as the Forsaken Skull with Shield Health included, but was slower than it with its base speed.

It had two abilities, both only activated after losing a certain amount of health. The first ability, *Forbidden Treasure*, was activated upon losing all of its Shield Health. It would start to spit out Hex Wraiths and Hex Minions from itself with random attributes. Enemies and attributes had specific chances to be chosen. Its second ability was activated when it reached 30% of its health, with that being *Panic Mode*. This would give the **Hex Mimic** the Nimble attribute and make it summon enemies faster.
Appearance: The **Hex Mimic** was a large brown and grey chest with a light maroon torso, legs and arms. It had large, grey teeth and a red tongue inside of the chest. On top of its chest, it also had multiple grey spikes. It wore brown pants.
Enemies Summoned: The **Hex Mimic** could summon two enemies, that being the Hex Wraith with a 33.3% chance and the Hex Minion with a 66.7% chance. These both have a 2 second delay between each spawn. However, each one could spawn with a random attribute, with these being:

Once in its *Panic Mode*. Its summons would change. Its minimal delay would be halved and it will gain a second Aggro modifier in its pool, which has a base weight of 50. This causes the modifier chances to shift:
Strategy: - Early-game towers, like the Golden Crook Boss, Cowboy, Militant and Golden Soldier can be quite effective against this.
- The **Hex Mimic** is a summoner enemy, which can summon enemies with various attributes.
- It can summon Hidden enemies, meaning that hidden detection or towers that can damage them indirectly are needed to deal with this.
- It can summon Aggro enemies, making all your towers target them instead of the enemy they were targeting before.
- Towers that can damage multiple enemies at once, such as the Pyromancer or Electroshocker can be useful in such cases.
- The Trapper will target these enemies, however, its traps that were placed on the path will still be able to damage other enemies and not the Aggro enemies.
- Units will target the Aggro enemy if they have a ranged attack, however, they can still be used to collide with enemies that are in front of it.
- Area of effect towers like the Pyromancer, Mortar or Electroshocker can be used to deal damage to both the **Hex Mimic** and the enemies it summons.
Trivia: - The **Hex Mimic** is likely based on Mimics, a fictional monster appearing in various media that takes the form of a large chest, which when opened generally reveals that it is a living creature with a set of teeth and a tongue.

Description: The **Hex Spawn** was the first enemy to appear in The Nightmare Realm and Containment as part of the Hexscape Event alongside the Hex Minion. It had a decent amount of health and an above average speed. On some waves, it could spawn with Bloated or Aggro.
Appearance: The **Hex Spawn** had a light maroon skin with multiple red veins. It also wore grey pieces of armor, consisting of shoulder-pads, chestplate and short, alongside brown knee-pads and a belt. Multiple red crystals could be seen on its armor.
Strategy: - Strong early-game towers like the Golden Crook Boss, Militant, Cowboy and Golden Soldier can be used to kill this quickly.
- The Pyromancer and Golden Pyromancer can be useful here, as it can kill multiple of them with its flames.
- On some waves, the **Hex Spawn** will spawn with Aggro, making it force towers to target it.
- Towers that can damage multiple enemies at once, such as the Pyromancer or Electroshocker can be useful here.

- The Trapper can be useful in such situations, as while it will still target it, its traps will damage any enemies that get past the Aggro **Hex Spawns**. Similarly, unit collisions can also be effective.

abilities.text: **Spooky Tricks** – **Hex Weaver** throws a turquoise orb on the path, which applies either Bloated or Nimble to enemies. Cannot apply attributes to other **Hex Weavers** or Bosses.

Description: The **Hex Weaver** was a support enemy that appeared in Containment as part of the Hexscape Event. It had decent health, average speed and 50% defense. It also had Stun Immunity.

The **Hex Weaver** had one ability, *Spooky Tricks*, where it threw a green orb on the path that applied attributes to other enemies. The explosion applied Bloated or Nimble attributes to enemies. It could not apply attributes to **Hex Weavers** or Bosses.
Appearance: The **Hex Weaver** had black skin. It wore a grey shirt and shoes, blue pants, dark grey armbands with bloody spikes and dark grey shoulder-pads. It also worr a dark grey skull with multiple horns on its head. It held a turquoise orb in its hands, which it used to apply attributes to enemies.
Strategy: - While not a threat on its own, especially considering how multiple enemies at this stage of the mode are significantly stronger than it, its ability to apply makes it very dangerous.
- DPS towers like the Engineer, Ranger or Accelerator can be used to kill it.
- Stalling towers can be used to slow down enemies that are given the Nimble attribute.
- Defense dropping towers, like the Golden Pyromancer or DJ Booth can be used to drop its defense.
Trivia: - The **Hex Weaver's** animations and ability were identical to the Fallen Jester.
Update History: - **Bug**: Poison and electric defense dropping do not decrease **Hex Weaver's** defense.

- **Bug**: **Hex Weaver** can completely negate the stalling effects from towers, such as freeze or DJ Booth slowdown, if during the debuff it applies Nimble to the enemy. This will make it walk at its regular Nimble speed while the debuff effects are still on it.
- **Bugfix**: Poison and electric defense dropping now drops **Hex Weaver's** defense, though the Jester still cannot drop it.

abilities.text: **Devious Slash** – **Hex's Maw** swings two times with its sword in an obtuse arc, stunning towers for 3.5 seconds and dealing 150 damage to units.

Description: The **Hex's Maw** was the third boss that appeared in The Nightmare Realm and Containment as part of the Hexscape Event. It had the Stun Immunity, making it immune to knockback and stuns, being only slowed down by stuns. When it first appeared, it was a Boss enemy, granting multiple immunities. It also occasionally spawned as a Bloated, Nimble or Freeze Immune enemy.
It had an ability, *Devious Slash,* where it swung in a wide arc with its sword, stunning towers for 3.5 seconds and dealing 150 damage to units.
Appearance: The **Hex's Maw** had light maroon skin. It wore a brown shirt, pants and cape. It also wore red shoes, grey spiked shoulder-pads, chestplate, padding around its waist and elbow-pads. On its head, it had a grey metal mask with long horns, which resembled a skull. It held a large grey sword with its blade split in half, only slightly connected in certain spots.
Strategy: - As the **Hex's Maw** appears on Wave 16, high DPS towers like the Accelerator, Gatling Gun, Engineer and Minigunner are recommended.
- Support towers such as the Commander and DJ Booth can be useful at providing boosts to your towers.
- The Ace Pilot can be used to give such towers hidden detections.
- The **Hex's Maw** has quite high defense. Because of this, defense dropping towers like the Pyromancer, Freezer or DJ Booth can be useful against it.
- Because of its immunities, it cannot be knocked back, frozen or chilled, and it is only slowed down instead of being stunned by stunning towers.

- Additionally, when it first spawns it is a Boss enemy, making it immune to even more forms of stalling. The only towers capable of slowing it down as a Boss are stunning towers like the Electroshocker or Trapper.
Trivia: - The **Hex's Maw** used the same animations as the Fallen Guardian, and shared the basic functionality of its ability with it.
Update History: - **Bug**: Poison and electric defense dropping does not decrease **Hex's Maw's** defense.
- **Hex's Maw** can no longer have its defense dropped while a Boss enemy.
- **Bugfix**: Poison and electric defense dropping towers now can drop its defense, though the Jester still cannot drop it.
Notes: - ↑ Only first **Hex's Maw** spawned in The Nightmare Realm is a boss.

Description: The **Hidden** is an enemy that cannot be attacked by towers without hidden detection that appears in Easy, Casual, Legacy Molten, Intermediate, Molten, Basic Arena PVP and Molten Arena PVP modes, and the Tutorial. It serves to introduce the need for hidden detection, and can be a nuisance without it. It is slightly faster than the Normal and Abnormal.

The Grave Digger had a chance to spawn the **Hidden** with its *Triumphing Sheol* ability in Easy mode. The **Hidden** was also formerly spawned by the Necromancer before its replacement. The Tombstone could also spawn the **Hidden** before its removal. The Mystery can summon the **Hidden** upon death.
It also appeared as parts of the SFOTH Event, Metaverse Champions Event and The Classic Event.

Strategy: - Most early game towers tend to gain hidden detection on one of its upgrades; these towers are sufficient to deal with early **Hiddens**. Such towers include the Soldier, Sniper, Shotgunner, Militant, Assassin, and Golden Scout.

- As **Hiddens** spawn in hordes, the Golden Pyromancer is particularly useful, being able to damage multiple enemies at once and having hidden detection by default. The regular Pyromancer also gains hidden detection at Level 2 and is a less effective, but still strong tower against **Hiddens**.
- If you can use the Farm well, the Minigunner and Accelerator are feasible choices, though they are not necessary and are fairly expensive, especially in Easy mode.
- For splash damage towers that cannot target **Hiddens**, such as the Mortar and Demoman, if a **Hidden** is caught up in an explosion, they will be dealt splash damage.
- This means that another detectable enemy must be near the **Hidden** for a splash damage tower to hit it.
- While the Rocketeer has hidden detection, it should not be used early on due to its high upgrade and placement costs.
Trivia: - On some devices, older versions of the **Hidden** may have translucent white skin instead of black skin, with certain graphics settings.
- The headband used by the second, third and current versions of the **Hidden** is the Shadowy Pirate accessory from the Roblox catalog.

- The cape used by the legacy **Hidden Boss** is a re-textured version of the Guardian of the Night Cape accessory from the Roblox catalog.

hidden_zoomer.name: Hidden Zoomer
hidden_zoomer.description: The Hidden Zoomer was an enemy that only appeared during the Area 51 Event. It was slightly faster than the Zoomer and had more health than it.

notice.text: Hidden Zoomer has been removed from the game as of the 13th of October 2019 as it was part of the Area 51 Event.

Description: The **Hidden Zoomer** was an enemy that only appeared during the Area 51 Event. It was slightly faster than the Zoomer and had more health than it.
Despite its name suggested that it was hidden, towers without hidden detection could still target the **Hidden Zoomer**.
Appearance: The **Hidden Zoomer** had grey skin, a grey fabric torso, black fabric legs and black wristbands. It had no eyes and wore a black headband. Its running animation was similar to the Naruto run. The **Hidden Zoomer** was very similar to the Zoomer in many regards.
Strategy: - Despite the fact that it is called the **Hidden Zoomer**, it is not actually hidden.
- The Freezer and Pyromancer can be used to slow the **Hidden Zoomer** down.
- Fast firing towers, such as the Minigunner, are very effective against **Hidden Zoomers**, while slow firing towers, such as the Sniper, struggle against it.
- You can also use the Demoman and Rocketer to damage groups of **Hidden Zoomers**, though you may need a Commander to boost their firerate.
Trivia: - The **Hidden Zoomer** was not actually hidden and could be attacked by any tower.
- Therefore, the first hidden event enemy was the Ghost.
- The **Hidden Zoomer** was based on the character of Naruto.
- This itself is based on the *Storm Area 51, They Can't Stop All of Us* Facebook event which said: "*If we naruto run[sic], we can move faster than their bullets.*"
- The running animation is the Naruto run, another reference of Naruto.
- The **Hidden Zoomer** uses the Black Ninja Headband of the Silent Sun accessory from the Roblox catalog.
- The **Hidden Zoomer** is a reference to a nickname for Generation Z.
- The **Hidden Zoomer** being based off *Naruto* is a stereotype that younger people are fonder of anime.

hunter_eggy_island.name: Hunter
hunter_eggy_island.description: The Hunter was an enemy that only appeared in Eggy Island as part of the Spring 2020 Event. It appeared in easy mode and hard mode with the same amount of health.

notice.text: Hunter (Eggy Island) has been removed from the game as of the 26th of May 2020 as it was part of the Spring 2020 Event.

stats.Speed:
- Average (Easy Mode)
- Above Average (4, Hard Mode)

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Bow** - Shoots an arrow at a tower, stunning it for a few seconds.

Description: The **Hunter** was an enemy that only appeared in Eggy Island as part of the Spring 2020 Event. It appeared in easy mode and hard mode with the same amount of health. It had average speed in easy mode and above average speed in hard mode. The **Hunter** could shoot arrows at towers, stunning them for a while.
Appearance: The **Hunter** had a smile face. It had sky blue skin and its torso and legs were green. It had a quiver strapped on its back with arrows stashed in it. It also wielded a longbow to shoot arrows at towers.
Strategy: - Due to its low health, Snipers and Pyromancers can be used to defeat this with ease.
- In hard mode, it is also recommmended to use the Pyromancer to slow down the **Hunter** due to its higher speed.
- In hard mode, the Rocketeer may be useful as the **Hunter** normally spawns behind a horde of Zombeggs and Sugrawrs.
- You can use cheap towers, such as the Scout, to distract the **Hunter** away from your main attacking towers.
- When the **Hunter** shoots its arrow, it also stops moving, giving you more time to attack it with other towers.
Trivia: - This was the only enemy that appeared in both easy and hard mode, in Eggy Island, that had the same amount of health in both modes.
- This enemy resembled the Holiday Archer quite greatly. They both had similar animations and sounds.

husk.name: Husk
husk.description: The Husk is a fast enemy that appears in Badlands II. It has a decent amount of health and a fast speed, making it a relatively strong enemy.

Description: The **Husk** is a fast enemy that appears in Badlands II. It has a decent amount of health and a fast speed, making it a relatively strong enemy. Its modern version always spawns with Corpse, meaning it turns into a Corpse upon death.
The **Husk** replaces the Fallen in Badlands II.
Appearance: The **Husk** has a very desaturated green skin color and a dark khaki torso and legs. It has a patch of missing skin on its head, exposing its skull. It also has a hole in its torso, exposing a chest cavity, as well as its ribs. It has dark green veins on its arms and it emits tan particles from its torso.
Strategy: - These enemies are strong and fast, and are quite a step up from the Necromancer. Cheap towers with high DPS are the best way to fend these enemies off.
- Such towers include Level 3 Minigunners, Level 2 Rangers and Level 3 Golden Crook Bosses.
- It is recommended to use both Commander and DJ Booth for their respective boosts.
- The Accelerator can also be used, but is inconsistent due to its long charge-up and cooldown times. Only the Level 5 Accelerator can hold off **Husks** without additional support.
- Level 0-4 Accelerators can still be very strong with support from slowing towers.
- The Military Base can be quite strong against **Husks** due to the Tank and Railgun Tank's high health.
- Be aware that only one unit spawns per Military Base on Badlands II, which will go down a random path. The units may not go on the path where you need them.
- Multiple Level 4 Gladiators or Level 5 Ace Pilots can also effectively deal with the **Husk**, although they may need supports depending on how many are on the map.
- Towers that can damage multiple enemies at a time are very effective here, as the **Husk** spawns in large hordes. Such towers include the Executioner, Rocketeer and Mortar.
- Slowing towers are recommended due to the **Husk's** high speed. The Frost Blaster and Freezer are by far the most useful against this.
Trivia: - The Level 0-4 **Badlands** skin for the Cowboy and Golden Cowboy is based on this enemy.
Update History: - None of the changes are applied to the legacy version.
- **Bug**: Appears twice in the Index, one of them not loading in any model for the preview.
- **Bugfix**: No longer appears twice in the Index.

ice_beacon.name: Ice Beacon
ice_beacon.description: The Ice Beacon is a Flying enemy that appears in the Frost mode. Like most of that mode's enemies, it first appeared in the Operation I.C.E Event.

Description: The **Ice Beacon** is a Flying enemy that appears in the Frost mode. Like most of that mode's enemies, it first appeared in the Operation I.C.E Event. It has a high amount of health, but it moves at a ridiculously slow speed, so slow it is basically immobile. This enemy's only purpose is being used by the Frost Spirit during its *Ice Beacon* ability.
Appearance: The **Ice Beacon** is a floating crystal made out of ice.
Strategy: - The only way for this enemy to kill you is if you purposefully try to die, or if it spawned at the exit, which is very unlikely to happen. Therefore, just having a lot of flying detection DPS is enough to destroy this.
- Towers with splash damage capabilities can help with this, as they can hit multiple of them at once.
Trivia: - The **Ice Beacon** is the only enemy from the Operation I.C.E Event to not have a description in the Index.
- The **Ice Beacon** is the second slowest enemy in the game, only behind the Void Eye.
- The **Ice Beacon's** model comes from the **Fallen** Accelerator's crystal.
Update History: - **Bug**: **Ice Beacon** floats above the ground when made larger or smaller.
- **Ice Beacon** removed from the main game, now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.
- **Ice Beacon** re-added to the main game, now appears in Frost mode.

imposter.name: Imposter
imposter.description: The Imposter is a joke enemy that can only be spawned through its Logbook, which can only be obtained if spawned by a developer while they are admin abusing.

notice.text: Imposter is content only available through the Sandbox mode.

imposter.mode_appearance:
- Sandbox via Logbooks
- Originally:
- April Fools 2021

Description: The **Imposter** is a joke enemy that can only be spawned through its Logbook, which can only be obtained if spawned by a developer while they are admin abusing. It was originally added as part of April Fools' Day 2021 and was exclusive to Fallen mode. Only one **Imposter** spawned per entrance on Fallen mode, which is at the start of wave 1. It was later re-added on 6th of March 2024 as a commands only enemy, and would remain that way until 2025 where due to Logbooks, it would be possible to obtain it for Sandbox mode.
The **Imposter** has extremely high health and speed for its debut during April Fools' Day 2021, being much faster than the Fallen Rusher.
Appearance: The **Imposter** has red skin with a black outline (to mimic a cartoon style), and a blue visor. It has a fast wobbling animation as it ran.
April Fools Strategy: As this enemy only appears in Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the April Fools 2021 update is listed.
- Towers that rely on units, such as the Military Base are ineffective, as the **Imposter** will pass through the units.
- High DPS towers for early game are necessary to kill the **Imposter**.
- Towers such as the **Golden** Scout and **Golden** Soldier are highly recommended.
- You can also use towers like the Electroshocker, Frost Blaster or Freezer to give your towers more time to attack it.
- The **Imposter** is not hidden (despite being a Ghost enemy), so hidden detection is not required.
- The best map to defeat the **Imposter** in is Polluted Wasteland as it crosses the middle multiple times.
- Outside of Polluted Wasteland, it is unlikely that you will be able to kill the **Imposter**. Therefore, you can use the Medic to heal back your base health.
- This makes using Farms less viable as you have less base health to sacrifice.

- Unless you have over 198 base health or deal enough damage to the **Imposters** where you do not lose all your base health, dual lane maps, such as Winter Stronghold, are impossible to beat on Fallen mode, as two **Imposters** would spawn at the beginning of Wave 1.
Badge: When the imposter is SUS! You have 1 minute...
Trivia: - Despite originally being a ghost enemy, towers without hidden detection could still target and attack the **Imposter** as it is not a hidden enemy.
- This made **Imposter** the first ghost enemy to not also be a hidden enemy.
- The **Imposter** is the fastest enemy in the game.
- The **Imposter** is a reference to the game *Among Us*.
- When the **Imposter** spawns and dies, it plays a unique sound effect.
- The former sound is taken from *Among Us* itself, being the death sound to indicate that you have been murdered.
- The latter sound is an audio clip from Yelling "among us" sound effect.
- The Commander dialogue is a reference to the Hello is this the Imposter from Among Us? YouTube meme.
- The misspelt *Among Us* as *Amogus* is a reference to the Amogus meme.
- Killing the **Imposter** awarded the *Suspicious...* badge.
- Originally, it had a requirement of one minute, which was the time until the first wave ends.
- The *When the imposter is SUS!* in the badge description is a reference to the When the imposter is sus! meme.
- The **Imposter** may have been based on the Golden Zombie from *Tower Battles*.
- Initially, the **Imposter** would get stuck running on the first bridge of Autumn Falling due to a glitch, making it easy to kill.
- This was patched soon after the **Imposter** was added, rendering the strategy useless.
- The word *Imposter* is more commonly known (and spelt) as *Impostor*.
- However, both variants of the word are correct and the game referred to this enemy as the **Imposter**.

- Despite no longer naturally appearing in the game, the **Imposter** could appear as an enemy for the Kill *ENEMY*! quest between the 6th of March 2024 and 8th of March 2024. As it has 99 health, the number of kills required is 101.

- Additionally, it was not the only enemy that did not currently appear in the game to appear in this quest during that period. There was also an enemy called the Arrow, with a requirement of one kill. However, this enemy had never actually appeared anywhere in the game at the time, unlike the **Imposter**.
- The Arrow would later appear in Headache Headquarters, however, its health would be heavily reduced, as it previously had nine billion health. The Imposter would not make an appearance.
Update History: - No longer is a ghost enemy.
- No longer gives a badge upon death.
- Now gives a badge upon death.
- **Imposter** can now be summoned in Sandbox mode, only if the player obtained its Logbook whenever developers spawned it in.

invisible.name: Invisible
invisible.description: The Invisible was a Hidden enemy that only appeared in Hardcore mode. Currently, it can only be spawned in Sandbox mode if the player has the Sandbox Plus+ gamepass.

notice.text: Invisible was previously removed on the 5th of June 2026, though it has been made available through the Sandbox mode later.

stats.Spawned By:

- Mystery (Hardcore only)
- Fallen Reaper

Description: The **Invisible** was a Hidden enemy that only appeared in Hardcore mode. Currently, it can only be spawned in Sandbox mode if the player has the Sandbox Plus+ gamepass. The **Invisible** cannot be attacked by towers without hidden detection. Compared to the Abnormal, it is slightly faster than it. It also has more health than the Hefty.
The **Invisible** could be spawned by the Grave Digger on Hardcore mode. The Mystery could also spawn the **Invisible** upon its death in Hardcore mode.
Appearance: The **Invisible** is a completely transparent enemy with a slightly noticeable light blue outline. It is faceless.
It will fade completely, then fade back into view at regular intervals.
Strategy: This strategy refers to the state of the game while the **Invisible** still appeared in the Hardcore mode.
- Towers with hidden detection are the best way to attack the **Invisible**.
- Most early game towers gain hidden detection. Such towers are recommended to deal with early **Invisibles**.
- Towers such as the Militant or the Golden Soldier are good example.
- As the **Invisible** spawns in hordes, the Golden Pyromancer is particularly useful.
- The Warden is also a great option, although it is slightly costly to get.
- Towers like Minigunner and Accelerator are likely too expensive for when **Invisibles** debut. However, they are great at dealing with **Invisibles** later on in the game.
- For splash damage towers that cannot target **Invisibles**, such as the Mortar, if an **Invisible** is caught up in an explosion, they will be dealt splash damage.
- This means that another detectable enemy must be near the **Invisible** for a splash damage tower to hit the **Invisible**.
- Units (like Military Base vehicles) cannot target the **Invisibles** but can damage **Invisibles** through collision.
- The Level 2 Military Base is viable against **Invisibles**.
- The Pistol Goon and Tommy Goon 1 do have hidden detection though, so they can be useful against the **Invisible**.
- However, do not rely on the Pistol Goons, as they do not have enough DPS to suffice.
- The Frost Blaster can be quite useful against the **Invisible** because of its freeze and piercing projectile.
- Multiple Level 0 or 1 Trappers can also be a good counter against **Invisibles**.
Trivia: - The **Invisible**, true to its name, is barely noticeable.
- The **Invisible** can be even harder to notice in maps with bright colors.
- During private Hardcore testing, the **Invisible** had 35 health.
- When killed, the **Invisible** leaves behind the same particles the Mystery does.
Update History: - **Bug**: Now emits the Mystery's death particles on death.
- **Invisible** removed from the main game, as it has been replaced by Phantom. Now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.
- No longer appears in the Index.

abilities.text: **Subzero Tricks** - Throws a block of ice on the path, which gives enemies the Aggro attribute. Has an explosion radius of 5. Cannot buff other **Jack Frosts**, itself or boss enemies. While using this ability, it will lose Hidden.

Description: **Jack Frost**, internally referred to as the **Trickster Elf**, is a support enemy that appears in the Frost mode. It has average speed and high health. It has one ability where it will throw its block of ice at an enemy. This will apply Aggro to any enemy hit in its explosion radius of 5. This will not affect any **Jack Frosts** or Boss enemies. The **Jack Frost** will also not target Frost Ravagers, Frost Hunters or Mega Frost Mysteries, though they can still get it if hit indirectly.
The **Jack Frost** is a Hidden enemy for majority of the time, though while it is using its ability, it will lose that attribute allowing other towers to attack it.
Appearance: **Jack Frost** has cyan blue skin and holds a transparent and cloudy ice block. It wears a grey and white mask over its eyes. On its head, it has white hair and cyan pointy ears. The cuffs of its coat are baby blue, and its wrists are covered by leathery brown guards. Its coat is primarily purple. On its shoulders, it wears protective guards as well. It wears a belt around its waist, with a crescent moon shaped buckle. Its leggings match the color of its coat. It has tall brown boots with metallic grey knee-pads.
Strategy: - While **Jack Frost** itself is quite weak, its main threat comes from its ability.
- It can apply Aggro to enemies, which will make towers target an enemy with it instead of the enemy they should with their targeting.
- High DPS towers like the Accelerator, Turret, Ranger or Pursuit can be effective against it.
- You can also use the Saboteur's *Aggressive Toxins* ability to make all towers target them, quickly killing them before they buff any enemy.

- Although some of these towers do not have hidden detection, they can still be used as while using its ability it will not be a Hidden enemy. They will however still be less effective compared to towers with hidden detection.
Trivia: - **Jack Frost** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
- **Jack Frost's** name is a reference to Jack Frost, a snow elf originating from England.
Update History: - **Bug**: **Trickster Elf's** model does not load in the Index.

- Speed increased from Slow (1.7) to Average (3.25).

jack_o_bot.name: Jack O' Bot
jack_o_bot.description: Jack O' Bot appeared exclusively in Nightmare Carnival as the final boss of the Halloween 2019 Event. It had a high amount of health and three abilities.

notice.text: Jack O' Bot has been removed from the game as of the 9th of November 2019 as it was part of the Halloween 2019 Event.

stats.Attributes:
- Boss Immunities:
  - Freeze Immunity
  - Burn Immunity

abilities.label: Ability 1
abilities.text: **Jack O' Minigun** - **Jack O' Bot** fires lasers from its right arm machine gun in a sweeping fashion. This will stun any towers hit.

abilities.label: Ability 2
abilities.text: **Jack O' Bombs** - **Jack O' Bot** fires three explosive pumpkins at three different towers. These pumpkins explode upon impact, stunning all towers within the explosion radius.

abilities.label: Ability 3
abilities.text: **Hallowed Laugh** - **Jack O' Bot** stands still while laughing and spawning various enemies.

Description: **Jack O' Bot** appeared exclusively in Nightmare Carnival as the final boss of the Halloween 2019 Event. It had a high amount of health and three abilities. Despite its very slow speed and the huge length of the map, it was very difficult to defeat due to a combination of its abilities and the enemies it spawned.
It had three abilities:

- The first ability it could perform was its *Jack O' Bombs* attack. With this attack, **Jack O' Bot** shot three explosive pumpkins at three random towers. On impact, the pumpkins would explode, and all towers within the explosion radius would be set on fire (stunning them). This disabled them from attacking for a long period of time.
- Its second ability was the *Jack O' Minigun*. With this attack, **Jack O' Bot** shot lasers at nearby towers, doing so in a sweeping fashion, stunning all towers hit for a period of time.

- Its third, and final, ability was *Hallowed Laugh*. This ability could spawn Jaxes, Mummies, Frankensteins, Ghosts, Witches, Bats, Swamp Things, Demons, Scarecrows, Strong Mummies and Clowns in front of the **Jack O' Bot**.
Appearance: **Jack O' Bot** was a giant pumpkin robot armed with a laser machine gun and an arm cannon. It had a pumpkin head (similar to Sinister P), pumpkins on its shoulders and a fleshed-out torso, but everything else appeared to be mechanical. It had a skull below its torso, and a metal pad on its chest. It was extremely tall due to its mechanical legs.
Strategy: - Use towers with high DPS and decent range against this boss. Towers such as the Minigunner and Turret are strongly recommended against this boss.
- Once **Jack O' Bot** goes out of range of these towers, relocate them to further weaken the boss.
- Outlaws and even Sentries, when set to *Strongest*, can be very effective at dealing damage to **Jack O' Bot**.
- Rocketeers are very useful at dealing with the enemies **Jack O' Bot** spawns because these enemies normally spawn in hordes.
- The Military Base can also deal lots of damage to **Jack O' Bot** (and the enemies it spawns) when upgraded to Level 5.
- Commanders are highly recommended since they can boost the firerate of towers.

- Because **Jack O' Bot** stuns towers with its *Jack O' Minigun* and *Jack O' Bombs* abilities, the Medic's ability can be very useful in cleansing your towers from **Jack O' Bot's** stun, provided it is not stunned itself.
- The Pyromancer and Freezer (including the *Ice Age* ability) cannot slow down **Jack O' Bot**, but they can still be useful in slowing down the enemies that **Jack O' Bot** spawns.
- Do not underestimate the enemies **Jack O' Bot** spawns, especially the Swamp Thing and Jaxe, as their high health can be extremely detrimental.
- Place towers near the end of the map to prevent these enemies reaching the end. Freezers are recommended to delay the Jaxe.
- If you can, try not to cluster towers close together as they will all get stunned when attacked with **Jack O' Bot'**s *Jack O' Bombs* and *Jack O' Minigun* abilities.
Trivia: - **Jack O' Bot's** name is a combination of the words "jack o' lantern" and "robot".
- **Jack O' Bot** was likely based on the Pumpkinator boss from *R2DA* which, in turn, was based on the Pumpkinator from *Fairly Odd Parents*.
- However, its name was based on the Jack-O-Bots from *Fairly Odd Parents*.
- A similar enemy to **Jack O' Bot** can be seen in the legacy Hidden Wave, the Mechanical Rot.
- The Mechanical Rot may be a reincarnation or rebuilt version of **Jack O' Bot**, hence its name.
- **Jack O' Bot** was the second enemy to use R15 animations, after the Gold Titan.
- In Act II of the Lunar Overture Event, **Jack O' Bot** is the final boss, its name changed to Jack-o-Bot.
- It is confirmed in this event that **Jack O' Bot** was actually sent by The Umbra to fight the players.
Update History: - Final wave music changed from Lunar Abyss to Jack O Bot.

jackobot.description: Jack-o-Bot, internally referred to as Jackobot, was the fourth and final boss of the second act in the Lunar Overture Event.

abilities.label: Ability 1

abilities.label: Ability 2
abilities.text: **Jack-o-Bombs** - **Jack-o-Bot** fires three to six explosive pumpkins at different towers. These pumpkins explode upon impact, stunning all towers within the explosion radius, including cliff towers.

Description: **Jack-o-Bot**, internally referred to as **Jackobot**, was the fourth and final boss of the second act in the Lunar Overture Event. Being the final boss, it had a very high amount of health, much higher than all other bosses before it, though it walked at an extremely slow pace. As it was a boss enemy, it was immune to being slowed down by the Toxic Gunner, could not be frozen by freezing towers and could only be slowed down by the Warden and Electroshocker. It was also unable to be affected by the Witch's ability.

**Jack-o-Bot** had two abilities. Its first one was *Hallow Hellraiser*, where **Jack-o-Bot** would start firing its right arm machine gun in a sweeping fashion, stunning towers. The second ability was *Jack-o-Bombs*, in which **Jack-o-Bot** would fire between three to six explosive pumpkins at different towers. These pumpkins would explode upon impact, creating green smoke and stunning all towers hit by the explosion.
Appearance: **Jack-o-Bot** was a giant mechanical pumpkin robot with a pumpkin head (similar to Sinister P) and pumpkin shoulders, controlled by an unknown humanoid. On its hands it was armed with a minigun on the right and an explosive pumpkin launcher on the left. In its chest, there was a small cockpit which houses the humanoid controlling **Jack-o-Bot**, along with two control sticks. It had mechanical legs and treaded feet. The humanoid controlling **Jack-o-Bot** had yellow skin, a red torso and blue pants.
Strategy: - High DPS towers like the Accelerator, Engineer and Golden Minigunner are very effective against **Jack-o-Bot**.
- Towers that are immune to stuns, like the Pursuit, are also strong options.
- Cliff towers like the Ranger are actually able to be stunned by **Jack-o-Bot**.
- The DJ Booth and Commander can be also helpful at boosting your towers' range and firerate respectively.
- Alongside **Jack-o-Bot**, hordes of various enemies also spawn, even after it has spawned. Because of this, splash damage towers like the Mortar or Rocketeer can be useful at clearing them out.
- After other enemies are cleared out, though, splash damage towers become less effective, as **Jack-o-Bot** lacks a summoning ability.
- Placing the Accelerator further back ensures it does not lock onto **Jack-o-Bot** too early and let the other enemies pass.
- The Medic is quite useful, as it can cleanse your towers from **Jack-o-Bot's** stun.
- Because of its immunities, it cannot be frozen by freezing towers or slowed down by the Toxic Gunner.
- The Warden and Electroshocker can only slow it down instead of stunning it.
- It is not necessary to attempt to slow **Jack-o-Bot** as it is already an extremely slow enemy.

- Placing expendable towers can be fairly useful to distract **Jack-o-Bot** into using its abilities on them instead of your main DPS towers. These towers can be the cheap towers you used for the early game or support towers with unlimited placement limit, like the Golden Soldier or Commander.
Trivia: - The **Jack-o-Bot** is a returning boss from the Halloween 2019 Event, despite having a small name difference.
- The **Jack-o-Bot** has multiple UGC accessories made based on it, some of which were obtainable by triumphing The Haunted Past.
- There are two accessories that could have been obtained, these being Jack O' Bot Head and Jack O' Bot Chestplate.
- There are also two accessories that were never obtainable, these being Jack O' Bot Shoulder Cannon and Jack O' Bot Shoulder Minigun.
- While **Jack-o-Bot** is named and referred to as *Jack-o-Bot* in The Haunted Past, its UGC accessories call it *Jack O' Bot*.
- The humanoid seen controlling **Jack-o-Bot** could be a reference to the Baller from *Roblox Boss Fighting Stages*.
- This was the slowest enemy in the game at the time of the Lunar Overture Event.
- **Jack-o-Bot** was the only boss that could stun cliff towers after they gained a full Stun Immunity.
- Some other bosses were once able to stun cliff towers, such as the legacy Grave Digger, but those were unintentional bugs.
Update History: - **Bug**: **Jack-o-Bot** sometimes gets stuck and stops moving.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Axe Throw** - The **Jaxe** throws its axe at a random tower, stunning any tower hit by it. This attack deals atleast 60 damage to units hit by it.

Description: The **Jaxe** was the boss of the first night in the Solar Eclipse Event. It had significantly higher health than the enemies that appeared before, however it was also much slower. The **Jaxe** had one ability, where it would throw its axe at a tower, stunning any tower hit. It would also deal at least 60 damage to units.
Appearance: The **Jaxe** had green skin and an orange pumpkin head with a scar on its left eye. It wore a black cape, grey chestplate, shoulder-pads and knee-pads. It also had black wrist-bands and orange arm-bands on both of its arms. It wielded a large axe to attack towers.
Strategy: - Use high DPS towers with cheap costs, such as the Swarmer, Pursuit and the Minigunner to defeat the **Jaxe**.
- Because of its early wave debut, and the low amount of health that other enemies have, towers like the Ranger and Accelerator may not be feasible in this night.
- Multiple level 3 Scouts can also fend off well against the **Jaxe**.
- Multiple level 3 Crook Bosses can also defeat the **Jaxe** due to their high DPS and cheap price.
- You can use the Commander and DJ Booth to boost the firerate and range of towers respectively.
- Because of its size and immunities, towers that slow down enemies are very ineffective against the **Jaxe**.
- The Electroshocker can only slow down the **Jaxe** instead of stunning it because of its Energy Immunity. It can also only slow it down for a shorter amount of time because of its size.
- Spacing out your towers can minimize the amount of towers stunned by the *Axe Throw*.
- While the *Axe Throw* ability cannot directly target units, it can still damage them.
Trivia: - The **Jaxe** had the third lowest health for a major boss in the entire game, only beaten by the Ripped Elf and the Dummy Boss.
- The **Jaxe** is the first narrator that is also an enemy.
- The **Jaxe's** legs used the R6 rig, while the rest of its body used an R15 rig.
- The **Jaxe** is based on the original Jaxe from Halloween 2019's Nightmare Carnival.
- The **Jaxe** had the shortest name of any major boss, at a mere 4 characters.
- Upon defeat, the **Jaxe's** head would fall and roll for a short distance.
- This head is later turned into a candy bucket that is used in the Candy Throw emote, as suggested by the emote's description.
- The **Jaxe's** *Axe Throw* ability uses the same laugh as the Lord Sinister's *Sinister Taunt*.
- A similar enemy to the **Jaxe,** the Headless Jaxe, could have been seen in Totality Tower.
- The cape used by the **Jaxe** was the Guardian of the Night Cape accessory from the Roblox catalog.
- The **Jaxe** was unintentionally added to the legacy Hidden Wave when it was added to Sandbox Mode.
- This is because the **Jaxe** replaced the Nightmare Carnival Jaxe as both of them shared the same name.
- A similar case happened with the Village of Despair Frost Hero, which was unintentionally replaced by the Frost Invasion Frost Hero in the Frost Invasion update.
Update History: - **Jaxe** now appears in the legacy Hidden Wave, which is exclusive to Sandbox mode.
- **Jaxe** no longer appears in the legacy Hidden Wave, as it has been removed.

Description: The **Jaxe** was an enemy that first appeared in Nightmare Carnival as part of the Halloween 2019 Event. It was very dangerous then due to its high health and average walk speed. It could also be spawned by Jack O' Bot.
The **Jaxe** also appeared in the legacy Hidden Wave, and therefore Fallen mode. Again, it had very high health, moved at an average speed and could stun towers by swinging its axe.
Appearance: The **Jaxe** had a pumpkin head and green skin. Its torso was black and its legs were cobblestone black. It wore a black cape and a metal wristband on its left arm. It had cobblestone and metal-plated armor, complete with an orange gem in the middle of its chestplate. It wielded a grey skull axe to attack the towers.
Strategy: - High DPS towers, such as the Minigunner, Accelerator, Turret and Ranger are recommended against the **Jaxe**.
- The Commander is highly recommended in order to boost the firerate of towers.
- The Freezer, Sledger, Frost Blaster and Electroshocker can also be very useful in slowing the **Jaxe** down.
- Be aware that, due to the **Jaxe's** large size, they can only be slowed down for a shorter period of time compared to an average-sized enemy.
- You can also use Toxic Gunner to slow down this enemy by 50%.
Trivia: - The **Jaxe** is loosely based on Jack from *Tower Battles*.
- The head of the **Jaxe** is the Sinister P. accessory from the Roblox catalog.
- The axe of the **Jaxe** is the Fiery Dragon Axe - a Target exclusive item! accessory from the Roblox catalog.
- The **Jaxe's** name is a portmanteau of the words "Jack" in "Jack-o" and "axe"

Description: The **Knight** was an enemy that appeared in the first and third act of the Lunar Overture Event. It had a decent amount of health, with defense and either above average or below average speed depending the mode. Additionally, it had an ability where it will attack a tower in its range, stunning it for a few seconds.
Appearance: The **Knight** wore white and grey fully body armor, with a purple cape. It wielded a wooden sword and held a wooden shield with poorly plastered orange and purple panels. While running, it held up its shield in front of it with its left arm. It has grey eyes.
Strategy: - Multiple cheaper towers, like the Golden Scout, Golden Soldier, Militant or Crook Boss can kill this quite easily.
- Towers with the capability to damage chains of enemies at once, like the Executioner or the Pyromancer, are extremely useful against this enemy.

Trivia: - The **Knight** shares similarities with the Knight from Solar Eclipse Event.
- The internal name of the **Knight** is *Knight Plush*.
- The **Knight** had a rather slow attack animation, which often caused it to die while in the process of stunning a tower.

Description: The **Korblox Deathwalker** was the final boss of the second and third mission of The Classic Event, and the first boss of the fifth mission in the same event. It had a high amount of health though it walked quite slowly. Additionally, as it was a Boss enemy, it had multiple immunities to prevent it from being stunned, frozen, confused, knocked back by any tower or slowed down by the DJ Booth. It was also immune to the slowdown from the Toxic Gunner and the fallout damage from the Nuke. However, no towers except the Freezer with its freeze applied such effects in The Classic Event.

The **Korblox Deathwalker** could not be spawned in Sandbox Mode through normal means. Instead, you had to go to either Classic Winter, Classic Island Chaos or Classic Castle through their Challenge Maps in the challenge tab, then spawn the modern Grave Digger, and the **Korblox Deathwalker** will appear instead. It could not be affected by the Double Health and Boss modifiers, like all Korblox enemies.
Appearance: The **Korblox Deathwalker** was a large ghostly figure which only has skeleton arms and parts of legs. Its torso was replaced by a giant flame and it had no head, only blue flaming eyes. It wore a brown hood with a cape that has four black wings attached to it. On its arms it had blue shoulder-pads and armbands with grey accents. It also had a brown belt with blue crystals and a brown cloth attached to the back of it. It wielded a large brown and grey scythe.
Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Classic Castle is listed instead.
- High DPS towers like the Minigunner or Accelerator are very effective against this.
- Towers that fully or partially are immune to stuns, like the Pursuit, Ranger or Engineer can be very useful as they cannot get stunned.
- In Classic Winter, the Militant and Military Base perform quite well against it.
- The Commander can be quite useful at boosting the firerate of your towers, if it is available.
- While the Freezer could be used to slow down the **Korblox Deathwalker** in Classic Winter, this is not necessary.
Trivia: - The **Korblox Deathwalker** model is taken from a bundle of the same name.
- On the boss health bar icon, the **Korblox Deathwalker's** eyes did not appear.
Update History: - **Bug**: **Korblox Deathwalker** is unaffected by the Double Health and Boss modifiers.

It has a high amount of health but is rather slow. It has one ability, *Forbidden Arts*, where it summons four random enemies. These can be the Korblox Undead with a 75% chance and Korblox Warrior with a 25% chance. Each spawn has a 0.4 second delay between each other and each spawn spawns with a random attribute. This can be Nimble with 35% chance and Bloated with a 65% chance.
Logbook Description: "*Frost Necromancers are artists, rejuvenating life into the corpses of the fallen and employing them to do their bidding. With staffs filled with energized ice, they willfully control their minions and grant them unique modifiers. Though shunned by the Frost Realm as tainted beings, Frost Necromancers remain beloved by the Frost Spirit to raise the dead.*"
Appearance: The **Korblox Necromancer** is a floating, grey skeleton which wears purple robes. Its torso is black. On its back, it carries multiple skeletal parts, which are attached to it through chains wrapped around its torso. It wields a grey staff which has a lantern attached to it. This lantern contains energized ice, which allows them to summon and control its summoned enemies.
Event Strategy: - High DPS towers, like the Ranger, Minigunner, Pursuit or Golden Minigunner can be useful against this.
- The Commander and DJ Booth can also be useful at boosting the statistics of these towers.
- Splash damage towers like the Mortar, Rocketeer or Trapper can be used to deal with the **Korblox Necromancer** itself and the hordes of enemies it summons.
Trivia: - The **Korblox Necromancer** reuses the same model and animations as the Frost Necromancer in the Operation I.C.E Event.
- This is pointed out by the Commander in-game, mentioning how it has seen that enemy somewhere before.

- Additionally, the **Korblox Necromancer** still uses **Frost Necromancer** as its internal name. This means that for example, when its Logbook is picked up, it will refer to it as the *Frost Necromancer*, not *Korblox Necromancer*.
Update History: - **Korblox Necromancer** added as an enemy to the Sandbox mode replacing the Frost Necromancer.
- **Korblox Necromancer** added to Korblox Temple Impossible difficulty.
- Now appears in Korblox Temple Mega difficulty.
- No longer appears in Korblox Temple Mega difficulty.
- **Korblox Necromancer** removed from the main game, now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.
- **Korblox Necromancer** removed and replaced by the Frost Necromancer.
Notes: - ↑ Only the first **Korblox Necromancer** is a Boss.

abilities.label: Ability 1
abilities.text: **Ryanair Flight** - Jumps between the two middle paths by casting a spell onto where it is about to land. Upon landing, icicles from the ground and a shockwave are formed, freezing towers, damaging units and after few seconds applying a 75% Fatigue Debuff to all towers near the landing site.

abilities.label: Ability 2
abilities.text: **Secret Santa** - **Krampus** throws 4–8 gifts onto random paths around the map where **Krampus** would be if it was on those paths, spawning Papa Breads, Evil Elves, Packed Ices, Crying Angels, Frozens, Cookie Guards, Snow Golems and Tough Cookies.

abilities.label: Ability 3
abilities.text: **Freezing Spell** - Creates a forward shockwave of ice which freezes towers, damages units and after few seconds applying a 75% Fatigue Debuff to all towers caught in the line.

abilities.label: Ability 4
abilities.text: **Raining Spikes** - Creates 25 to 30 icicles in the sky which begin falling down onto the ground that upon landing freeze towers for 5-7 seconds, dealing 100 damage to units and after few seconds applying a 75% Fatigue Debuff to all towers hit.

abilities.label: Ability 5
abilities.text: **Germanic Stomp** - Stomps on the ground causing a shockwave that stuns towers for 6-10 seconds, damages units by 500 and after few seconds applies a 75% Fatigue Debuff to all towers hit.

abilities.label: Ability 6
abilities.text: **Body Slam** - **Krampus** jumps into the air and begins falling, making ice spikes rise from the ground upon landing that freeze towers, damage units and after few seconds apply a 75% Fatigue Debuff to all towers hit.

abilities.label: Ability 7
abilities.text: **Lapland Turned Red** - At half health **Krampus** takes off its mask and screams, gaining 50,000 shield health, becoming Hidden for a few seconds and increasing the frequency of its abilities. **Krampus** is invulnerable while using this ability.

Description: **Krampus** was the third and final boss that appeared in Krampus Frosthold as part of the Krampus' Revenge Event. As with most major bosses, it had an extremely high amount of health, but walked quite slowly. It was immune to being frozen and having the chillness effect applied to it from freezing towers, it could not be slowed down by the Toxic Gunner, and the Electroshocker and Warden could only slow it down instead of stunning it.
**Krampus** had seven abilities:
- Its *Ryanair Flight* ability caused **Krampus** to hop between the two middle paths of the map. When **Krampus** landed, it created a large shockwave, stunning towers around it.

- Its *Secret Santa* ability summoned a large number of enemies by **Krampus**, from 4-8 gifts which were thrown onto any of the four paths. These enemies could be the Papa Bread, Evil Elf, Packed Ice, Crying Angel, Frozen, Cookie Guard, Snow Golem and Tough Cookie.
- Its *Freezing Spell* attack created a shockwave of ice that stunned towers.
- Its *Raining Spikes* ability summoned 25-30 large icicles that rained down on the map and stunned towers hit for 5-7 seconds and dealt 100 damage to units.
- Its *Germanic Stomp* ability makes it stomp on the ground, creating a shockwave that stuns towers for 6-10 seconds and deals 500 damage to units.
- Its *Body Slam* ability made it jump into the air and start falling, which created ice spikes upon landing that stunned towers.

- When **Krampus** reached half health, it activated its *Lapland Turned Red* rage mode ability. It would take off its mask and scream, gained 50,000 shield health, sped up, became Hidden for a few seconds and started to use its abilities more frequently. It was invulnerable while it was screaming.

All abilities that stunned towers also applied a 75% Fatigue Debuff to affected towers a few seconds after, including towers that could not get stunned like the Ranger and non-humanoid towers that normally could not have debuffs applied to them like the Pursuit.
Appearance: **Krampus** was a giant, anthropomorphic half-goat and half-demon. It had black skin, red horns and light blue glowing eyes. It wore red and black shoulder-pads with blue spikes, black and red shirt with a hood, red elbow-pads, black pants, and red and grey knee-pads. Multiple parts of it clothing also had light grey fur on its edges. It also wore a large black helmet. On its back it had a staff powered by a God Cube shard, which it used to attack towers.
Upon entering *Lapland Turned Red*, it would take off its helmet and expose its face, and also gained blue neon lines on its skin.
Strategy: - High DPS towers, like the Accelerator, Ranger and Pursuit should be used against **Krampus**.
- The Ranger, Pursuit and Ace Pilot can be especially useful as they are immune to stuns, though they are still affected by the Fatigue Debuff.

- As **Krampus** becomes hidden for a few seconds after **Lapland Turned Red**, DPS towers with hidden detection like the Accelerator and Golden Minigunner are useful against this, as they can keep attacking **Krampus** even while it is hidden.
- The DJ Booth and Commander are useful for boosting the towers' range and firerate respectively.
- The Commander can also be useful at mitigating the effects of the Fatigue Debuff it applies to all towers shortly after they get hit by its abilities.
- The Medic's *Cleansing* ability is extremely useful for cleansing stuns from **Krampus'** abilities, though it cannot cleanse the Fatigue Debuff.
- All abilities that stun also damage units, making spawner towers like the Military Base and Necromancer worse against this.
- The Engineer can still be useful as its sentries have a shield, which prevents them from being damaged as long as the Engineer is not stunned itself.

- Area of effect towers, like the Mortar and Golden Pyromancer are highly recommended to deal with the hordes of enemies that spawn before and after **Krampus**, as well as enemies spawned by **Krampus'** *Secret Santa* ability.
- **Krampus** has the ability to jump between paths. Because of this, towers should be placed so that they can cover both paths of the map.
- Do note that this ability can also stun your towers.
- The DJ Booth can be especially helpful at increasing the range of your towers.
- The Ranger is mostly unaffected by this, due to its high-range allowing it to cover most if not all of Krampus Frosthold in certain spots.
- Because of its immunities, freezing towers and Toxic Gunner cannot stall **Krampus**.
- The Electroshocker and Warden can only slow down **Krampus** instead of stunning it.
- The Jester's confusion bombs can be very effective at stalling **Krampus**.
Trivia: - **Krampus** was a returning boss from the Christmas 2019 Event, with the Krampus' Revenge Event's name stating that it had come back for revenge. It received a visual overhaul, and while its abilities got many visual changes, they roughly retained the same mechanics.
- Unlike its previous version, **Krampus'** abilities were powered by the God Cube, with a fragment of it being included in **Krampus'** staff.
- **Krampus** was the only boss enemy that could become Hidden, as it briefly became Hidden after using its *Lapland Turned Red* ability.
- Unlike all other Hidden enemies, it did not change its transparency over time during that ability, most likely due to it being a temporary attribute.
- **Krampus** was the first enemy that can change which path it was on with its *Ryanair Flight* ability.

- **Krampus**, alongside Ducky D00M from D00M's Revenge, Primordial Drakobloxxer and Frost Spirit from the Operation I.C.E Event had the second highest number of abilities in the game, only behind the Rift Walker.
- In folklore, the Krampus is a half-goat, half-demon monster in some legends. During the Christmas season, his role is to punish children who have misbehaved.
- He originated from Germany.
- **Krampus'** boss theme was a remix of the original Krampus boss theme.
- Interestingly, the theme played in the last stage of Krampus Frosthold instead of the final wave where **Krampus** appeared in.
- A re-textured version of the helmet worn by **Krampus** was uploaded as an UGC, it is called Krampus' Helmet.
