abilities.label: Ability 1
abilities.text: **Stomp** - **Krampus** roars and slams its staff into the ground. This creates a shockwave, stunning all towers hit by it.

abilities.label: Ability 2
abilities.text: **Summon** - **Krampus** summons Frozen, Gingerbreads, Burnt Gingerbreads, Snowmans, Deep Freezes and Yetis.

abilities.label: Ability 3
abilities.text: **Crystallize** - **Krampus** creates a line of ice with its staff, freezing all towers in the line.

abilities.label: Ability 4
abilities.text: **Icicle Storm** - **Krampus** summons a snowstorm, causing fog to descend. It rains icicles which can hit towers, stunning them for a long period of time. It can only occur after *Rage Mode*.

abilities.label: Ability 5
abilities.text: **Rage Mode** - **Krampus** takes off its helmet, stands still, and heals 100,000 as part of its *Rage Mode*. Becomes immune to most forms of damage while doing this (except unit collision damage). It can only occur once.

Description: **Krampus** appeared exclusively in Village of Despair as the final boss of the Christmas 2019 Event. As with most major bosses, it had an extremely high amount of health, but walked very slowly.

**Krampus** had five abilities. Its *Stomp* attack created a large shockwave, stunning towers around it. Its *Summon* ability summoned a large number of enemies. These enemies could have been the Frozen, Gingerbread, Burnt Gingerbread, Snowman, Deep Freeze and Yeti. Its *Crystallize* attack created a line of ice that froze towers for a long time so that they could not attack. When **Krampus** reached half health, it would activate its *Rage Mode*, healing itself. During this attack, it was immune to most attacks for about 15 seconds, excluding unit collision damage. It then gained the *Icicle Storm* attack, which caused icicles to fall around the map, freezing most, if not all, towers.
Appearance: **Krampus'** appearance resembled an ice warrior as it wore dark blue granite robes to symbolize the cold. It had blue skin, had two large pauldrons and wore a large ice helmet, complete with horns. It also wore black granite shoes. It had light blue glowing eyes. It initially spawned with an ice staff on its back, but few seconds after spawning it would take out its ice staff, which would be used to perform many of its abilities. The staff emitted white light when wielded, however, it would not emit light if it was on **Krampus'** back.

During *Rage Mode*, **Krampus** would briefly emit blue sparks. It would take off its helmet, revealing its head. Its eyes changed from light blue to blue. The skin turned from dark blue to black with blue parts. **Krampus** also emitted blue light, instead of white light that was emitted from its ice staff.
Strategy: - The Medic's ability is very useful against this boss due to the fact that most of its attacks stun towers for a long while. The ability can cleanse towers of their stun.
- This is best taken advantage of by having a spare tower slot for the Medic, ready to place down whenever towers are stunned.
- As always, Outlaws, Minigunners and Turrets are the best towers against this boss due to their high DPS.
- The DJ Booth can be used to boost the range of these towers. This is recommended due to the map layout and the fact that most of **Krampus'** attacks stun towers near its vicinity.
- The Commander can be used to boost the firerate of these towers. This is recommanded heavily with Outlaws due to their mostly high firerate.
- If **Krampus** passes the bridge, sell towers on the first island and place them near the end.
- A few Rocketeers may be useful in killing the enemies that **Krampus** spawns.
- You cannot slow this boss down by any means, such as the Freezer or Pyromancer.
- The Pyromancer will deal non-burn damage to it, but it cannot burn it.
- Likewise, the Freezer can deal damage to it, but it cannot freeze it.
- In both cases, it is best to just sell these towers and place down another tower that has high DPS.
- **Krampus** debuts with four Frost Heroes spawning in front of it, which can easily stun the majority of your towers.
Trivia: - In folklore, Krampus is half-goat, half-demon. During the Christmas season, he punishes children who have misbehaved.
- Krampus originated from Germany.
- Krampus may be loosely based on Frosty, in terms of design, from *Tower Battles*.
- The shoulder pauldrons on *Krampus'* were a re-textured version of the Left Pauldron of the Void and the Right Pauldron of the Void accessories from the Roblox catalog.
- The horns worn by Krampus are a re-textured and resized version of the Ram Horns accessory from the Roblox catalog.
- This was the first boss to have a *Rage Mode* ability (the Fallen King's *Rage Mode* was added after **Krampus**).
- This is, so far, the only enemy with a unique *Rage Mode* theme.

- When **Krampus** activated its *Rage Mode*, **Krampus** puts its ice staff behind its back, then an ice blue aura and snowflake particles can be seen around its torso. **Krampus** took off its mask, revealing its face.
- When the Christmas 2019 Event ended, **Krampus'** helmet could be found in the lobby on the beach.
- **Krampus'** head was the The Scorched accessory from the Roblox catalog.
- **Krampus** would always use its *Stomp* ability and then a second random ability few seconds after spawning.
- Additionally, it would always use its *Icicle Storm* ability after its *Rage Mode*.
- **Krampus** came back in the Krampus' Revenge Event to take revenge, receiving visual improvements and similar abilities.

abilities.text: **Time Scale** - The hourglass on **Kronus'** back will glow green, as the player's screen glitches to grey. In this state, the game's Time Scale is set to 0.2x, with **Kronus** ignoring the Time Scale and walking at normal speed. Lasts 10 seconds.

abilities.label: Ability 2 Cooldown: 15 Attack CD: 5

abilities.label: Ability 4 Cooldown: 20 Attack CD: 5
abilities.text: **Summon** - **Kronus** points its staff, summoning in various enemies for 2 seconds. These can be the the Null Crook Boss (80% chance, 0.45 second delay), Null Warden (5% chance, 0.6 second delay) and Null Electroshocker (15% chance, 0.5 second delay).

Description: **Kronus** was the first major boss that appeared in Blind Faith as part of the Null & Void Event. It had higher health than majority of the enemies in the event, though it was also one of the slowest.
**Kronus** has four abilities:

- *Time Scale*, which makes it change the Time Scale of the match to 0.2x, though **Kronus** will continue to walk at normal speed. During this period, the entire map will turn grey and Time Scale will no longer be possible to change by the player.
- *Sweeping Ice* makes **Kronus** spin its staff in the direction of a tower, summoning in an aftershock of ice that freezes towers for 5 seconds and deals 2,000 damage to units.
- *Ice Storm*, where **Kronus** points its staff in the air, summoning 25 icicles from the sky that freeze towers for 5 seconds and deal 1,000 damage to units.

- *Summon* has **Kronus** point its staff, which summons in random enemies for 2 seconds. These can be the the Null Crook Boss (80% chance, 0.45 second delay), Null Warden (5% chance, 0.6 second delay) and Null Electroshocker (15% chance, 0.5 second delay).
Logbook Description: "*When Trick or Threat Town was attacked, three brothers were saved by TDS from Lord Sinister. But the Town’s reputation was destroyed- some said it was too dangerous to visit. As the brothers left, Kronus found a God Shard that was left behind, along with Narrator. That’s when Narrator promised that Lord Exo would rebuild the town, and the brothers could live together once more.*"
Appearance: **Kronus** is one of the Children of Exo. It is a figure shrouded in a red cloak, with cybernetic elements across its body, such as its mechanical left arm. **Kronus** also wears a grey mask, concealing its face, with what appears to be bullets crossed along its body. **Kronus** has a neon-green hourglass on its back, as well as wielding a staff with a shard of the God Cube.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Blind Faith is listed instead.
- High DPS towers like the Accelerator, Turret, Ranger or Pursuit are recommended here.

- As **Kronus** uses freezing attacks, stun immune towers do not have a large advantage here since it does not make them immune to freeze, though they can still be useful due to **Kronus** summoning in Null Electroshockers.
- The Commander and DJ Booth can be used to boost the statistics of your towers.
- The Medic cannot be used here, as it cannot shield towers from freeze.
Trivia: - The Boss health bar for **Kronus** displays that it enters rage mode after reaching 75% of its health, however, when that happens, there are no actual changes on the enemy.

- This is to be due to a leftover statistic which is a phase 2 threshold set to 75% of its health that appears to have been taken from the Frost Spirit due to them using the same threshold at the time, them sharing freeze based abilities that function similarly and **Kronus** having another unused statistic, this time a health multiplier for *Roblox Winter Spotlight*.
- **Kronus** first appeared in the Hexscape Event, where it would be just known as "*???*". It would not be until the Null & Void Event that it would become an enemy.
- The staff wielded by **Kronus** uses the same model as Krampus' staff from Krampus' Revenge Event.
- **Kronus** is named after Kronos, the King of the Titans and god of time in Greek mythology. Hence having an ability, **Time Scale**, that can manipulate time.
- **Kronus** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Kronus** removed from the main game, now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.
- **Bug**: Cannot be spawned in Sandbox mode.
- **Bugfix**: Can now be spawned in Sandbox mode.

notice.text: Lava was previously removed on the 5th of June 2026, though it has been made available through the Sandbox mode later.

- Fallen Reaper (Wave 38 onwards)

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Regeneration** - Regenerates 15% of its health every second.

Description: The **Lava** was an enemy which only appeared on Hardcore mode. Currently, it can only be spawned in Sandbox mode if the player has the Sandbox Plus+ gamepass. It has mediocre health for its debut and has average speed. However, its main ability is to heal 15% of its health back every second. If left undamaged, the **Lava** can easily become an issue.

The **Lava** can be spawned by the Void Reaver, Fallen Reaper (wave 38 onwards) and Molten Boss (on Hardcore mode only). The Mystery can also spawn the **Lava** upon its death in Hardcore mode, wave 38 onwards.
Appearance: **Variant 1**

The **Lava** has red glowing skin, black rusted torso and legs, and metal-plated armbands. While walking, its head tilts slightly forward and it sticks out its arms. Smoke is emitted from its torso. It is about the same size as the Abnormal.
**Variant 2**
The **Lava** had light red glowing skin, black cobblestone torso and legs, and a metal-plated wristband on its right arm. Smoke was emitted from its torso.
Strategy: This strategy refers to the state of the game while the **Invisible** still appeared in the Hardcore mode.
- Do not give time for the **Lava** to heal its health back.
- Make sure that you concentrate all damage to them at once. If you spread out damage across the map, the **Lava** will have more time to heal its health back.
- The Railgun Tank can collide with the **Lava**, instantly killing it or leaving it severely weakened. This reduces the efficiency of the **Lava** healing back its lost health.
- Splash damage towers such as the Mortar can be quite effective against this, as they can hit multiple **Lavas** at once.
- Fast firing towers, like the Minigunner, Accelerator and Turret, can be used to constantly attack the **Lava**, preventing it healing back any health.
- The Ranger can also be used. However, do be aware that the **Lava** can heal back its health between shots due to its slow firerate.
- The Commander's *Call to Arms* ability is highly recommended as it allows them to quickly deal damage towards the **Lava**.
- Despite being a fire enemy, it is not immune to the Pyromancer which can mitigate the regeneration effect the **Lava** has.
Trivia: - There was an unused variant **Lava** that was added on the 15th of August 2019 and removed in the MEGA Update, but did not appear naturally.
- It was meant to be added to the game proper, alongside the Frozen and Deep Freeze, but this was cancelled.
- Therefore, the **Lava** could only be spawned by commands.
- This version of the **Lava** could also regenerate health, similar to the current version.
- It also had similar statistics, but it had 1,000 health instead of 700 and had Burn Immunity.
- This was similar to the Molten's ability at the time, which could also regenerate health.
- Although both enemies bear no resemblance to each other, the **Lava's** regeneration ability is similar to that of the Amalgamation.
- Despite being a fire elemental enemy, the **Lava** does not have Burn Immunity.
- The **Lava** looks similar to the old Lava from *Tower Battles*.
Update History: - **Lava** removed from the main game, now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.
- No longer appears in the Index.

lawnmower.name: Lawnmower
lawnmower.description: The Lawnmower was an Area 51 enemy that only appeared during the Area 51 Event. Though it was slower than the Alien...

notice.text: Lawnmower has been removed from the game as of the 13th of October 2019 as it was part of the Area 51 Event.

Description: The **Lawnmower** was an Area 51 enemy that only appeared during the Area 51 Event. Though it was slower than the Alien, it had much more health than anything that appeared before it, making it dangerous to the unprepared.
Appearance: The **Lawnmower** was a bloated humanoid driving a green lawnmower. The humanoid itself had light green skin, a white bloated torso and khaki legs. It wore shades and had a sad drooling face. It was holding a Bloxy Cola while sitting awkwardly on the lawnmower.
Strategy: - Due to this enemy being relatively strong for its debut, you may need to buy more towers or upgrade your current ones to kill it.
- High DPS towers, such as the Minigunner or Crook Boss, are very useful for this.
- Additionally, due to its slow speed, the Outlaw can also be effective when dealing with this enemy.
- The Freezer and Pyromancer can be used to slow this enemy down.
Trivia: - This enemy was initially called *Boomer* even though it did not explode when it was killed.
- It was named as such because the humanoid on the **Lawnmower** uses the same model as the Boomer 1 and Boomer 2, possibly as an oversight.
- Unlike the other Area 51 enemies, the **Lawnmower** appeared to bear no reference to Area 51 itself.

lead.name: Lead
lead.description: The Lead is a Lead enemy that appears in Hardcore and Voidcore modes. It has decent health and speed.

Description: The **Lead** is a Lead enemy that appears in Hardcore and Voidcore modes. It has decent health and speed. It initially spawns with Lead, meaning only towers with lead detection can damage it, and with the Stun Immunity, meaning stuns are less effective on it while knockback does not affect it. However, once it loses all of its Shield Health, it will lose its covering and also the Lead and Stun Immunity attributes it has by default.
Logbook Description: "*Molten material was poured on the bodies of Odds and molded by the blacksmiths. If they were lucky enough to survive, it would be nearly impossible for the Leads to take damage. In fact, this worked so well that Odds were beginning to run from the selection process, with many dragged back. If the Odds still had their individuality, it was most apparent during this part.*"
Appearance: The **Lead** is a humanoid entirely covered in grey metal. Upon losing all of its Shield Health, it will usually lose most of its metal coverings, revealing that it is an entity with grey skin and purple veins. In its torso, it has a giant hole. It has two walking animations it can choose from.

The **Lead** will lose one piece of its armor covering (head, torso, left leg, right leg, left arm, right leg) at random every time it loses one sixth of its Shield Health, or a covering loss every 6-7 health lost. In cases of it receiving more than 7 damage, like 14 damage at once, it will lose multiple pieces at once, which in the previously listed 14 damage's case that being two pieces of armor. The only exception to this is it losing all of its Shield Health, as this happening does not actually remove any armor. This means there will always be at least one piece of armor left on the **Lead**, with it even being possible to have it keep all of its armor if the Shield Health received 40 damage at once.
Strategy: - Cheap towers that have lead detection like the Engineer, Mortar, Golden Pyromancer or Saboteur are recommended against the **Lead** due to its lead coverings, though as it loses its Lead after its Shield Health is depleted, other towers can also help in taking it out.
- The Cowboy and Golden Cowboy do not have lead detection, but their shots at the **Lead** still count towards their income generation, allowing them to earn extra cash.
Trivia: - The **Lead** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Bug**: Crystal in its body is made out of grey plastic.

Description: The **Lead** was an enemy which only appeared on Hardcore mode. Currently, it can only be spawned in Sandbox mode if the player has the Sandbox Plus+ gamepass. It has somewhat high health for its debut, but luckily it is quite slow. As it is a Lead enemy, it cannot be damaged by towers without lead detection.
The **Lead** could be spawned by the Grave Digger in Hardcore mode. The Mystery could also spawn the **Lead** upon its death in Hardcore mode.
Appearance: The **Lead** is completely metal-plated from its head to its legs. It is faceless. It is about the same size as the Abnormal. Its head is slightly tilted downwards.
Strategy: This strategy refers to the state of the game while the **Invisible** still appeared in the Hardcore mode.
- Any tower with splash, fire, electric, poison and collision damage will damage the **Lead**.
- The Golden Pyromancer and Electroshocker are perhaps the most effective towers against the **Lead** due to their DPS and ability to damage multiple **Leads**.
- The Freezer can slow down the **Lead**, but is unable to damage it.
- The Cryomancer and Frost Blaster can both damage the **Lead** as well as slow it down, making it a great option against it.
- Units can also deal with the **Lead** well, as most of them have a pretty decent amount of health.
- Similarly, the Trapper's spikes are also very effective against **Leads**
- Bombs from the Ace Pilot can damage the **Lead**, but its bullets cannot.
- The Swarmer cannot damage the **Lead** without its ability.
- A Level 3+ Sniper, Warden or Ranger can damage the **Lead** directly, but these are relatively expensive options.
- Likewise, the Accelerator and Level 1+ Pursuit can easily defeat the **Lead**.
- A Level 3 Golden Scout is a relatively cheap option to deal with multiple Leads.
- Multiple Level 0 Brawlers or a Level 2 Brawler can also work pretty well.
- Low level Engineers might struggle with multiple **Leads** due to it having to take time to build sentries, which cannot damage them.
Trivia: - This enemy was based on the Lead Bloon from the *Bloons Tower Defense* series.
- **Lead**, alongside the Lead Boss and Lead Balloon have unique spark particles when they are hit by an attack that cannot detect lead enemies.
Update History: - **Lead** removed from the main game, now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.
- No longer appears in the Index.

lead_balloon.name: Lead Balloon
lead_balloon.description: The Lead Balloon was an enemy which only appeared on Hardcore mode. Currently, it can only be spawned in Sandbox mode if the player has the Sandbox Plus+ gamepass.

notice.text: Lead Balloon was previously removed on the 5th of June 2026, though it has been made available through the Sandbox mode later.

stats.Speed:
- Above Average (4.25, With Balloons)
- Fast (Estimated 6.25, Without Balloons)

Description: The **Lead Balloon** was an enemy which only appeared on Hardcore mode. Currently, it can only be spawned in Sandbox mode if the player has the Sandbox Plus+ gamepass. While it has low health for its debut, it is quite fast. While the **Lead Balloon** is in the air, it cannot collide with units, or be detected by most ground towers and units.

It is also a Lead enemy, meaning it cannot be damaged by towers without lead detection. This severely reduces the amount of towers that can harm the **Lead Balloon**. With its balloons popped, it is no longer a Flying enemy. However, despite having no visible metal coverings, it is still a Lead enemy.
The **Lead Balloon** can be spawned from the Mystery upon its death in Hardcore mode, wave 40 onwards.
Appearance: The **Lead Balloon** is a faceless humanoid with reflective dark green skin, and a reflective dark grey torso and legs. It has three lead balloons tied to its back, which, after taking enough damage, pop into yellow particles and drops it lower to the ground. When it loses all shield health, all the balloons would have popped and the **Lead Balloon** would become grounded, removing its flying attribute and making it walk along the path.
Strategy: This strategy refers to the state of the game while the **Lead Balloon** still appeared in the Hardcore mode.
- While the **Lead Balloon** is floating, the **Lead Balloon** is a lead and flying enemy. This limits the towers that can both detect and damage the **Lead Balloon**.
- Multiple Level 3+ Rangers are the best option to deal with the **Lead Balloon**, with or without its balloons.
- A Level 2+ Tesla is equally good for this, especially because of its area damage, allowing it to take down multiple **Lead Balloon**s at once, while also stunning them.
- Level 4 Snipers can also be used to kill the **Lead Balloon** despite their mediocre DPS, but you need a large amount of them.

- A few level 3+ Toxic Gunners are also a great option to eliminate the **Lead Balloon**, with and without its balloons. However, Toxic Gunner is an event tower that is currently unobtainable outside of special offers.
- The Ace Pilot, Mortar and Pursuit can detect and damage the **Lead Balloon** with its splash damage.

- However, the Ace Pilot's projectiles explode on the ground, limiting the damage dealt to the **Lead Balloon**. It will also have a hard time hitting **Lead Balloons** when they are grounded due to the enemy's fast speed.

- The Engineer can be used to deal with this, but do note that only the tower itself can detect and damage them. None of the Engineer's sentries can detect it, with only War Machine Sentry being able to damage it.
- The Firework Technician can be used to give your towers both Lead and Flying detections, along with granting them extra firepower with fireworks.
- Weirdly, the Elf Camp's units can handle this enemy quite well, despite being unable to collide with it.
- The Hunter and Executioner are able to detect the **Lead Balloon**, but are unable to damage it.
- The Commando's missiles are in fact fully capable of damaging **Lead Balloons** and could be a potentially effective way of bursting them down due to the constant splash damage.
- Units cannot directly damage the **Lead Balloon** while it is floating, though explosions from some of the units may indirectly hit it.
- The Shotgunner, Electroshocker, Saboteur and Swarmer are unable to detect the **Lead Balloon** while it is floating, but are able to damage it.
- This will only occur if there are other enemies near the **Lead Balloon**.
- Once the **Lead Balloon's** shield health has been depleted, all of its balloons would have popped.
- Once this happens, any tower can detect the **Lead Balloon**, but cannot damage it if they do not have lead detection.
- Be aware that its speed increases significantly while on the ground
Trivia: - The **Lead Balloon** may be a reference to the Lead Bloon in the *Bloons Tower Defense* series.
- During Hardcore Testing BETA, the **Lead Balloon's** balloons did not pop as it had no shield health.
- Oddly, when the **Lead Balloon's** balloons pop, it is no longer a flying enemy, yet is still considered a lead enemy, despite not having any metal coverings.
- The **Lead Balloon**, alongside the Lead and Lead Boss have unique spark particles when they are hit by an attack that cannot detect lead enemies.
- In logbooks, the Lead Balloon is called “SUPER MEGA LEAD BALLOON” and has 99,999,999,999 health.
Update History: - **Bug**: Uses the animation without balloons in the Index while also still wearing its balloons.
- **Lead Balloon** removed from the main game, now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.

lead_boss.name: Lead Boss
lead_boss.description: The Lead Boss was a large enemy which appeared only on Hardcore mode. Currently, it can only be spawned in Sandbox mode if the player has the Sandbox Plus+ gamepass.

notice.text: Lead Boss was previously removed on the 5th of June 2026, though it has been made available through the Sandbox mode later.

stats.Speed:

- Slightly Fast (Estimated 4.6, Without Covering)
stats.Spawned By:
- Grave Digger (Hardcore only)
- Mystery (Hardcore)
- Mystery Boss (Hardcore)

Description: The **Lead Boss** was a large enemy which appeared only on Hardcore mode. Currently, it can only be spawned in Sandbox mode if the player has the Sandbox Plus+ gamepass. It had high health for its debut, but was quite slow while it has full metal coverings. As it is a Lead enemy, it cannot be damaged by towers without lead detection.

The **Lead Boss** loses its metal coverings based on how much damage it received, and how many times it was damaged. Because of this, the **Lead Boss** can lose its metal coverings at different times depending on what towers are damaging it. After its health drops below 80-151 health (depending on how the metal coverings are destroyed), enough of its coverings would have been destroyed so that the **Lead Boss** loses its Lead properties and thus can be attacked by all towers and units. As more and more metal coverings are destroyed, the **Lead Boss** speeds up. After its health drops below 30-121 health, all of its metal coverings would have been removed and it would have become significantly faster than before.
The **Lead Boss** could be spawned by the Grave Digger in Hardcore mode. The Mystery and Mystery Boss could also spawn the **Lead Boss** upon their deaths in Hardcore mode.
Appearance: **Variant 1**
The current **Lead Boss** is similar to the first version, however when it is exposed, it is faceless instead.
**Variant 2**

The original **Lead Boss** was completely metal-plated from its head to its legs. After more damage was dealt to the **Lead Boss**, some of the metal covering was destroyed. After enough damage has been done, the **Lead Boss** was exposed. It had blue skin, and its torso and legs were brown. It had a drooling zombie face and is larger than the Abnormal.
Strategy: This strategy refers to the state of the game while the **Invisible** still appeared in the Hardcore mode.
- Like the Abnormal Boss, the **Lead Boss** is a major spike in health compared to previous enemies, and additional defense is necessary.
- Lead detection is required to take this boss down. The Golden Pyromancer is a good option, and multiple Level 1 Trappers can also be effective, as well as a Level 3 Golden Scout.
- These are also the most effective options to deal with **Lead Bosses** that spawn from Mysteries early on.
- A Level 2 Brawler can be effective at taking down the **Lead Boss**, but if you have additional defenses without lead detection, then one or two Level 0 should be able to take down its lead armor.
- The Elf Camp's units deal low collision damage, but in the mid game Gift Bombers and Ripped Elves are effective to damage the **Lead Boss**.
- The Level 1+ Pursuit is a cost effective option that can also detect flying enemies, though it might be too expensive early on in the game.
- After the metal coverings have been removed, all towers can damage the **Lead Boss**. Towers like the Golden Scout or Ace Pilot are now more useful.
- Be aware that the **Lead Boss** may get out of range of these towers before its metal coverings get removed.

- Slowing towers like the Sledger, Frost Blaster or Electroshocker can be used, though the Freezer is unable to damage the **Lead Boss**. The Electroshocker, Warden, Frost Blaster, Cryomancer, Sledger and Toxic Gunner can damage the **Lead Boss**.
- In particular, Level 3+ Wardens are very good against **Lead Bosses** as Wardens deal lots of damage and have lead detection, meaning they can kill **Lead Bosses** very quickly.
- Mysteries are able to spawn the **Lead Boss** in huge numbers. Additional defense is even more important here, especially if the **Lead Bosses** from previous waves had proven troublesome.
- Earlier hordes of Mystery spawned **Lead Bosses** should be dealt with using the same tactics above.
- When in the mid game, towers like the Accelerator and Ranger become options and are fairly good at dealing with such hordes. The Commander and DJ Booth are also helpful.
- Once the metal coverings are removed, all high DPS towers can be used.
Trivia: - The **Lead Boss** may be a reference to the Lead Bloon in the *Bloons Tower Defense* series.
- Without the metal covering its body, this enemy looks similar to the Zombegg and the Eggsplosive.
- It also looks similar to the Speedy from *Tower Battles*.
- The **Lead Boss**, alongside the Lead and Lead Balloon have unique spark particles when they are hit by an attack that cannot detect lead enemies.
Update History: - **Bug**: **Lead Boss** does not speed up after losing its covering.
- **Bugfix**: **Lead Boss** now speeds up after losing its covering.
- **Bug**: **Lead Boss** no longer uses the death sound effect.
- **Lead Boss** removed from the main game, as it has been replaced by Elite Lead. Now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.
- No longer appears in the Index.

left_hand.name: Left Hand
left_hand.description: The Left Hand, internally referred to as Hand Boss, alongside the Right Hand, was the final boss of the third act in the Lunar Overture Event.

notice.text: Left Hand has been removed from the game as of the 21st of December 2023 as it was part of the Lunar Overture Event.

stats.Attributes:
- Stun Immune
- Boss Immunities:
  - Freeze Immunity
  - Stun Immunity
  - Poison Slowdown

abilities.label: Ability 1
abilities.text: **Temper Fist** - Balls up into a fist and smashes down on a tower, creating a shockwave that stuns towers hit by it.

abilities.label: Ability 2
abilities.text: **Finger Gun** - Shoots multiple missiles from its index finger at random towers, stunning any tower caught in its explosion.

abilities.label: Ability 3
abilities.text: **Vanquish** - Grabs a tower and crushes it, killing it and giving the player that placed it down some cash. Can happen multiple times in a row.

abilities.label: Ability 4
abilities.text: **Summoning Trickery** - Dangles its fingers over a path and summons five enemies.

Description: The **Left Hand**, internally referred to as **Hand Boss**, alongside the Right Hand, was the final boss of the third act in the Lunar Overture Event. It had a high amount of health, much higher than any other enemy before it, but it could not enter the base like other enemies and did not take damage the same way as other enemies. As it is a boss enemy, it was immune to being slowed down by the Toxic Gunner, could not be frozen by freezing towers and could only be slowed down by the Warden and Electroshocker.
The **Left Hand** had four abilities:
- The first ability, *Temper Fist*, made it move towards a tower, ball up to a fist and smash it, creating a shockwave that stunned any tower.
- Its second ability, *Finger Gun*, made it fire multiple missiles from its index finger at random towers, stunning any tower caught in the explosion.
- Its third ability, *Vanquish*, made it move towards a tower, grab it, squash it and then return to its original position, which killed the tower. It can do this multiple times in a row.
- Its last ability, *Summoning Trickery*, made it dangle its fingers over a path, summoning five enemies, which could be any enemy that appeared before it.
Appearance: The **Left Hand** was a disembodied human hand wearing a white glove.
The **Left Hand** had a death animation where it would make various hand signals before shrinking into nothing and emitting confetti after it disappeared.
Strategy: - Spotlights are the only reliable way to attack the **Left Hand** and Right Hand.
- Both the **Left Hand** and Right Hand cannot be targeted by towers directly, but can still be damaged indirectly from explosions or stray projectiles.
- Enemies that spawn around the map have a chance of dropping a single Battery when killed. These should be collected before Wave 14, as each Spotlight requires 10 Batteries to be used.
- In cases of emergency, it can also be used to confuse enemies coming towards the exit, so that you do not lose due to them.

- It is recommended to stay next to the Spotlight which will have its duration end soon, so that it can be quickly activated again. After this, move to the next Spotlight which has the lowest amount of time before it deactivates.
- The **Left Hand** has several abilities where it will quickly move around the map. Players using Spotlight should retarget them as fast as possible.

- The **Left Hand** cannot make the player lose by itself. However, enemies that spawn alongside it will if you do not have enough DPS, especially when combined with the **Left Hand** and Right Hand's abilities.
- Multiple high DPS towers, like the Minigunner, Accelerator or Ranger are recommended to deal with them.
- Towers like the Golden Soldier can be quite effective against them when there are multiple of them placed down.
- The Medic is a reliable tower to cleanse stuns.
- Do note that the **Left Hand** can kill your towers.
- It is advised to have bait towers, however it is not a requirement since the only way to kill the **Left Hand** is by using the Spotlight.
Trivia: - The **Left Hand** was given to the Narrator as a gift from Lord Exo. Its name is *Lefty*.
- The **Left Hand** was most likely inspired by the Crazy Hand from *Super Smash Bros*.
- The fact that the **Left Hand** has 300,000 health could also be a reference to the Crazy Hand having 300 health in *Super Smash Bros*.
- After losing to the **Left Hand** and Right Hand, a laugh could be heard.
- This along with the Right Hand are the second bosses to have the ability to kill towers, with the first being the Raider Boss.
- The **Left Hand** spawned slightly before the Right Hand.

Description: The **Living Experiment** is an enemy that appears in Intermediate, Challenge Trials and Molten Arena PVP modes. It also appears in The Takeover Event. It has a high amount of health, a below average speed and a decent amount of defense. Additionally, when it first spawns, it is a boss enemy, making it fully or partially immune to multiple forms of stalling. On some waves, it also spawns with various immunities, making it harder to kill.
Due to a bug, **Living Experiments** with the Slime attribute do not spawn the Slime upon death.
Appearance: The **Living Experiment** is a large humanoid with a waist, lower arms and lower legs in its rig. It has a light green skin color, and wears a tattered light blue hospital gown with a stitched seam going down the back, white bandages wrapped across its torso and metal plating with a glowing green piston on its back.

It has a thin right arm with an armband with chains on it, as well as a large bionic arm with multiple glowing green pistons and a green glass container. It also has a large metal neck-guard with glowing green parts, as well as glowing green eyes, patches of black hair and a metal device with green lights and light brown stitch lines surrounding it on its head.

It has a death animation, where it falls forward, with its bionic arm completely detaching in the process. The death animation is also accompanied by a sound, consisting of it grunting and metal thumping noises.
Strategy: - Towers with decent DPS, like the Minigunner, Militant or Cowboy are recommended against this.
- On its debut wave, the **Living Experiment** is surrounded by a hordes of Armored and Slows, which can be incredibly problematic.
- Area of effect towers like the Pyromancer, Rocketeer, or Mortar can excel at clearing out the hordes, allowing DPS towers to focus on the **Living Experiment** itself.
- Some of them like the Rocketeer and Mortar also have sufficient DPS to deal with the **Living Experiment** itself on their own.
- As the **Living Experiment** has Defense, you can use Defense bypassing towers like the Trapper or Military Base to deal with this.
- As these towers also have AOE attacks, they can be also used to deal with the hordes of enemies it usually spawns with.
- Defense dropping towers, like the Pyromancer or Freezer can be used to reduce its defense, allowing your towers to deal more damage to it.
- While the **Living Experiment** does not have any immunities to crowd control by default, it is a large enemy, making certain forms of stalling like freeze or knockback less effective on it.
Trivia: - Despite the Commander stating that the **Living Experiment** can heal enemies around it, it has no such ability.
Update History: - **Bug**: Poison and electric defense dropping does not reduce **Living Experiment's** defense.
- **Bug**: **Living Experiments** with the Slime attribute do not spawn the Slime upon death.
- **Living Experiment** is now immune to the fallout damage from the Nuke while it is a boss enemy.
- **Living Experiment** is now immune to knockback while it is a boss enemy.
- **Bug**: Can be slowed down by the DJ Booth while a boss.
- **Bugfix**: No longer can be slowed down by the DJ Booth while a boss.
- **Living Experiment** can no longer have its defense dropped while a Boss enemy.
- **Bugfix**: Poison and electric defense dropping towers now can drop its defense, though the Jester still cannot drop it.
- **Bug**: **Living Experiment's** has no animations in its Index entry.
- Now appears in Mid Rank PVP Test, where it has 3,000 health.
- No longer appears in the PVP Test as it has been removed.
- Now appears in Molten Arena PVP, carrying over all of its PVP Test statistics.
- Now appears in Sk8 P4rk Pro difficulty as part of The Takeover Event.
- Cash given is now mode dependent.
- Majority of modes now give $625 every 25% health lost.
- The Takeover Event Pro difficulty gives $750 every 25% health lost.
- Default value is $1 every 25% health lost.
- No longer appears in Sk8 P4rk, as it has been removed.
- First wave appearance changed from 16 to 18 in Intermediate mode.
- Cash given increased from $625 to $850 every 25% health lost.

Description: **Lord Sinister** was a major boss that appeared exclusively in Trick or Threat Town as the final boss of the Halloween 2020 Event. As with most major bosses, **Lord Sinister** had an extremely high amount of health, but walked very slowly.
**Lord Sinister** had three abilities:
- Its *Sinister Taunt* ability spawned a random number of enemies from the ground. These could have been the Reanimated, Slime, Hallow Bones and Ghost.
- Its *Hallowed Slam* ability involved **Lord Sinister** slamming its axe into the ground, creating a forward shockwave that stunned towers.
- Finally, its *Infernal Storm* ability involved **Lord Sinister** breathing fire at towers, setting them alight, stunning them. This attack also dealt damage to units, 150 damage per tick.
Appearance: **Lord Sinister** was a large demonic-like boss. It had a black pumpkin head, with glowing yellow eyes and mouth, and wore a black rusted crown. It wore bronze armor, which included a large chestplate, pauldrons and leggings. On its torso was an engraving of a spooky pumpkin face. **Lord Sinister's** arms were neon yellow and it wore grey gloves with white knuckles. **Lord Sinister's** legs were marbled crimson. Around its left leg was a neon yellow chain. **Lord Sinister** wielded a large axe with its right hand. The axe's design appeared to have a face.
Strategy: - Towers that have a high DPS output are recommended, such as the Ranger, Minigunner and Turret.
- Because Trick or Threat Town has lots of suitable cliff space, the Ranger is ideal.
- The Commander's *Call to Arms* ability can be used to boost the firerate of towers. If you have multiple Commanders, you can chain their abilities to ensure firerate is always at its lowest.
- Due to **Lord Sinister's** Freeze Immunity, the Frost Blaster and Freezer cannot slow down **Lord Sinister**.
- The Electroshocker can only slow down **Lord Sinister** instead of stunning it. Additionally, it can only slow it down for a very short period of time due to its large size.
- Make sure that you have sufficient towers after the path crosses the bridge, otherwise enemies that **Lord Sinister** spawns may get out of range.
- The Ghost can especially cause havoc as it has hidden and ghost immunity, meaning it cannot collide with units.
- **Lord Sinister's** stuns can stun towers for a long period of time. You can use the Medic's ability to cleanse your towers of **Lord Sinister's** stun.
- While units, like the Railgun Tank and Citizen 1, can be effective against **Lord Sinister's** summoned enemies, **Lord Sinister's** *Infernal Storm* can pretty much destroy most units.
Trivia: - **Lord Sinister** is based on *Lord Sinister* from a boss fight game made by BelowNatural, which is no longer playable. Footage of it can be found here.
- **Lord Sinister** that appears in Tower Defense Simulator can be considered a remake of that *Lord Sinister*.
- **Lord Sinister** is the first enemy to have voice acting.
- **Lord Sinister's** voice actor is Razuatix, a retired Tower Defense Simulator developer.
- **Lord Sinister** has an unused voiceline that could be heard during the April Fools 2022, if it was picked as the random sound. The voiceline was: *"It's harvesting season!"*
- This voiceline was likely meant to be one of the playable sounds for *Hallowed Slam*.
- The Gladiator's **Pumpkin** skin is heavily based on **Lord Sinister**.
- When **Lord Sinister** died, its head fell off and rolled a short distance. **Lord Sinister** also screamed "*Nooo!*".
- The Level 5 **Graveyard** Farm has a statue of **Lord Sinister**, possibly being its grave.
- **Lord Sinister's** theme (*Harvesting Season Theme*) was a remix of Mega Man Star Force 2 OST - T27: Wave Battle (Boss Theme).
- Interestingly, the original track was used by Lord Pumpkin Jr., an event boss in *R2DA* which BelowNatural worked on.
- **Lord Sinister's** axe design was based on the Horseless Headless Horsemann's Headtaker from *Team Fortress 2*.
- **Lord Sinister's** crown was the Black Iron Crown of Pwnage accessory from the Roblox catalog.
- Weirdly, the health of the **Lord Sinister** was increased in MEGA Servers by 15,000 per player, despite it not being able to spawn in a MEGA Server without admin commands.

- High damage towers such as the Accelerator, Minigunner, Ranger and Turret should be used to take care of this enemy.

abilities.label: Ability 1

abilities.text: **Well Fed** - At half health, **Mecha-claus** takes out a cookie and eats it, gaining around 20,000 health.

Description: **Mecha-claus**, internally referred to as **Santabot**, was the final boss for Cold Ambush as part of the Violent Night Event. It had a very high amount of health and an average speed. Uniquely, it could not spawn until the last plot of land is cleared, which prevented it from spawning in perpetuity.

**Mecha-claus** was unique in that, like the Ripped Elf and Gatekeeper, it did not directly try to reach the base. Instead, it would circle around the map, firing off its abilities, only directly attacking the base with its *War on Christmas* ability.
**Mecha-claus** had four abilities:

- Its first ability, *Snowball Bombardment*, made **Mecha-claus** take out its snowball minigun and fire it at towers, making them rain down onto the map and stunned any tower hit and dealing damage to units.

- Its second ability, *War on Christmas*, had **Mecha-claus** take out its present missile launcher and fire it, making a present missile land on the Christmas tree, dealing 250 damage to your base health.

- Its third ability, *Explosive Surprise* made **Mecha-claus** take out a present bomb from its sack. It would then throw this present bomb into the air, which later lands on its head. This present bomb then turned into multiple other present bombs that fell down onto the map, stunning any tower hit.
- Its fourth and last ability, *Well Fed*, was a rage mode ability. It is activated at half health and made **Mecha-claus** eat a cookie, which caused it to regenerate around 20,000 health.
Appearance: **Mecha-claus** was a giant Christmas-themed robot built by the elves to beat the players, which resembled Santa Claus. It was mainly made out of grey metal, with its legs and hands being painted red. Its thighs and chest have embroidered golden markings on them. Its head was made of grey metal, and had a dark red visor in place of the face. On its head was a light grey metal beard with a green and red part at the bottom, as well as dark dray eyebrows. **Mecha-claus** also wore a red Santa hat with embroidered gold markings and a green button.

**Mecha-claus** also wore a bandolier, with a golden bauble, a red embroidered bauble, and a blank green bauble, each with a fuse coming out of the cap. Its shoes were reddish-brown boots with two buckles around them. It had a red sack strapped to its back, filled with presents. It had abs and a brown belt on its lower torso.

**Mecha-claus** wielded two weapons, one of which was a snowball minigun which it used to stun towers, and the other was a present missile launcher, which it used to deal damage to the base. It also had present bombs which it used to stun towers.
Strategy: - High DPS towers like the Accelerator, Ranger and Engineer are recommended against this.
- These towers should have their firerate and range boosted by the Commander and DJ Booth respectively.
- The Ranger cannot be stunned by **Mecha-claus**, nor can the Engineer's sentries be destroyed by it, making them both very effective.
- The Ranger is even more effective as it has a high enough range to constantly damage the **Mecha-claus** as it is able to walk out of range for most ground towers.
- The Medic can be used to cleanse the stuns from towers stunned by **Mecha-claus'** abilities.
- You are able to stall **Mecha-claus** from spawning by not purchasing a single plot. This has several applications.
- You will have more time to place and upgrade your towers to prepare for **Mecha-claus**.
- This is generally not needed, as you will have no shortage of cash during the fight itself.
- You will have more time to let the passive base health regeneration fully regenerate your base health.
- This is useful to give yourself the highest chance of surviving **Mecha-claus'** *War on Christmas* ability.
- Do note that this means you will have less passive income and passive base health regeneration for the rest of the game.
- Try to have as much base health as possible so that you have a higher chance of surviving **Mecha-claus'** *War on Christmas*.
- It may be helpful to leave one plot not purchased, letting the passive base health regeneration heal the base health back during Wave ???.

- Do note that even with full base health, there is still a fair chance *War on Christmas* will end up overwhelming you, as it has little to no cooldown and can be performed multiple times in quick succession, rapidly draining your base health.
- As this is all down to chance, there is no true way to prevent this from occurring. The best you can do is try to defeat **Mecha-claus** as soon as possible.
Trivia: - **Mecha-claus** was built by the elves from the Violent Night Event after they have been turned against Santa by an unknown source. It would later be used against the players.
- Due to a bug, Cold Ambush matches sometimes had more than four players, making it a MEGA Server. This would cause **Mecha-claus's** health to increase by 15,000 for each player.
- Interestingly enough, if you zoom inside **Mecha-Claus's** head, you will able to see a green figure with an elf hat controlling it from inside.
- In the Violent Night Event trailer, elves can be seen building **Mecha-Claus**, likely intended to be controlled manually by an elf.
Notes: - ↑ **Mecha-claus** did not spawn until the last plot is bought. Otherwise, the game continued in perpetuity, with the wave reading ???. When **Mecha-claus** spawned, the wave changed to ❄️ (Snowflake emoji).

Description: **Mechanical Rot** is the final boss of the second Halloween 2025 Live Event in Nil Zone.
**Mechanical Rot** has three abilities:
- Its first ability is *Minigun*, where **Mechanical Rot** will start firing its right arm machine gun in a sweeping fashion, stunning towers for 6 seconds and dealing 50 damage to units per tick.

- The second ability is *Cannon*, in which **Mechanical Rot** will fire six explosive pumpkins at different towers. These pumpkins would explode upon impact, creating green smoke with a radius of 6 that stuns all towers hit by the explosion for 6 seconds while also dealing 50 damage to units.

- The last ability is *Summon*, where the **Mechanical Rot** starts laughing anywhere between 6 and 16 seconds. During this, it will summon enemies, each with their own chance to be summoned and delay before the **Mechanical Rot** can summon another enemy.
Logbook Description: "*When the world went blank, the mechanical rot was cast into the Nil Zone. Memory stripped and soul hollowed, the actor rebuilt himself and his machine anew — not from purpose, but from the echo of what purpose once was.*"
Appearance: **Mechanical Rot** is a giant mechanical pumpkin robot with a pumpkin head (similar to Sinister P) and pumpkin shoulders, controlled by a a corrupted actor. On its hands it is armed with a minigun on the right and an explosive pumpkin launcher on the left. In its chest, there is a small cockpit which houses the actor controlling **Mechanical Rot**, along with two control sticks. It has mechanical legs and treaded feet. The actor controlling **Mechanical Rot** is a dark entity covered in purple binary.
Enemies Summoned: While using its *Summon* ability, it will being laughing for between 6 and 16 seconds. During this period, it can spawn any of the following enemies with the following chances and delays before next enemy spawns:
- 1 second delay before another enemy can be spawned.
- 2 second delay before another enemy can be spawned.
- 1.5 second delay before another enemy can be spawned.
- 1.5 second delay before another enemy can be spawned.
- 2 second delay before another enemy can be spawned.

- 0.25 second delay before another enemy can be spawned.
- 0.5 second delay before another enemy can be spawned.
- 0.25 second delay before another enemy can be spawned.
- 0.25 second delay before another enemy can be spawned.
Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Nil Zone is listed instead.
- High DPS towers like the Accelerator, Turret, Engineer and Golden Minigunner are very effective against the **Mechanical Rot**.
- Stun immune towers like the Pursuit or Ranger can also be useful as they cannot be stunned by it.
- The DJ Booth and Commander can be also helpful at boosting your towers' range and firerate respectively.
- The Medic is quite useful, as it can protect your towers from **Mechanical Rot's** stun while also providing protected towers with buffs.
- As the **Mechanical Rot** initially spawns with Boss in the Nil Zone, it cannot be stalled through most methods.
- Stun towers like the Warden, Electroshocker or Archer cannot stun it but only slow it down.
- Freezing towers like the Freezer, Cryomancer or Elementalist similarly are unable to freeze it, but can still apply chill to it.
Trivia: - Originally, BelowNatural wanted to name this enemy something along the lines of **Corrupted Jack O' Bot**. It ended up being given the name **Mechanical Rot** after a suggestion from Nim.
- The **Mechanical Rot** is a reimagined version of the Mechanical Rot from the legacy Hidden Wave.
- Based on its Logbook and its appearance, this version appears to be the Jack-o-Bot actor who was warped into the Nil Zone sometime after the The Haunted Past.
- Through logbooks of the other actor enemies, it can be inferred that this most likely happened at the same time as the "*Glitch*" which prevented The Great Finale from happening properly.
- The laugh that plays when it uses its *Summon* ability is the same laugh as the Lord Sinister laugh.

Description: The **Mechanical Rot** was an enemy that only appeared during the Legacy Hidden Wave, and therefore Fallen mode. Currently, it can only appear in Sandbox mode. The **Mechanical Rot** was considered a major boss. This enemy had the third highest health out of all the enemies in the Hidden Wave, with the Frost Hero being the second with 80,000 health and the Creator being the first with 600,000 health. It can attack towers with its *Rotting Minigun*, stunning towers that it hits for a long period of time. The only redeeming thing about the **Mechanical Rot** is that it walked very slowly, even slower than the Creator.
Appearance: The **Mechanical Rot** boasts the same texture and design scheme as Jack O' Bot, but some of the colors are a bit darker, including the pumpkin head.

The **Mechanical Rot** is armed with a laser machine gun and an arm cannon. It has a black pumpkin head, pumpkins on its shoulders and a fleshed-out torso, but everything else appears to be mechanical. It has a skull below its torso, and a metal pad on its chest. It is extremely tall due to its mechanical legs. It appears to be a rotting version of Jack O' Bot, which tied into the **Mechanical Rot** name.
Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in the Hidden Wave is listed instead.
- As with most Hidden Wave enemies, high DPS towers, such as the Accelerator, Ranger and Turret, are recommended.
- The Commander is essential to boost the firerate of towers.
- Try to kill the **Mechanical Rot** as quickly as possible, as it can stun large swathes of towers, allowing fast enemies, like the Bug, or the Creator to walk past.
- Its very slow speed allows it to be overtaken by most enemies, meaning that when the Creator comes out, the **Mechanical Rot** becomes incredibly hard to kill.
- The Freezer, Sledger and Frost Blaster cannot freeze the **Mechanical Rot** due to its large size and Freeze Immunity.
- The Toxic Gunner cannot slow this down because of its poison immunity.
- The Electroshocker can only slow down the **Mechanical Rot** instead of stunning it. Additionally, it can only slow it down for a very short period of time due to its large size.
- If you have a Medic that is not stunned, its ability can be used to cleanse your towers if they are stunned from the *Rotting Minigun*.
- As with most other enemies in the Hidden Wave, the Commander's *Call to Arms* ability is essential in defeating this enemy.
- While the Pyromancer cannot burn the **Mechanical Rot**, it can still deal non-burn damage to it.
Trivia: - The head of the **Mechanical Rot** is a re-textured version of the Sinister-P Sinister P. accessory from the Roblox catalog.
- The pumpkin shoulders of the **Mechanical Rot** are re-textured versions of the Happy Jack-o'-Lantern accessory from the Roblox catalog.
- The **Mechanical Rot** may be a reincarnation or rebuilt version of Jack O' Bot, hence its name.
- The **Mechanical Rot** may be a reference to the Expired Jack from Wave 0000000 in *Tower Battles*.
Update History: - **Mechanical Rot** can no longer be slowed down by the Toxic Gunner.
- **Mechanical Rot** now appears in the legacy Hidden Wave, which is exclusive to Sandbox mode.
- **Mechanical Rot** no longer appears in the legacy Hidden Wave, as it has been removed.
- **Mechanical Rot** can now be summoned in Sandbox mode, only when the player has the Mechanical Rot's from Nil Zone Logbook.
- **Bug**: **Mechanical Rot** breaks when targeting towers, causing it to get stuck.

Description: The **Mega Slow** was a large and tough enemy which only appeared on Hardcore mode. Currently, it can only be spawned in Sandbox mode if the player has the Sandbox Plus+ gamepass. While it had slightly slow speed, it had very high health for its debut. This makes it a very dangerous threat. Additionally, it has 15% defense, reducing the effectiveness of some towers. It also has Stun Immunity, which makes the Electroshocker and Warden only slow it down and makes it immune to knockback.
The **Mega Slow** can be spawned by the Void Reaver and Grave Digger, in Hardcore mode only. The Mystery Boss can also spawn the **Mega Slow** upon its death in Hardcore mode.
Appearance: **Variant 1**

The first and current **Mega Slow** is a large enemy. It is slightly smaller than the Giant Boss. It has a reflective green skin color and is faceless. It has tumors on its left arm and head. Its torso, sleeves and legs are granite black. It also has a metal armband on its right arm and has hooks growing on both of its shoulders. It also has a small black axe stabbed into its back. It walks slightly hunchbacked and has a twisted left leg.
**Variant 2**
The second **Mega Slow** was similar to its current version except it had only one hook on its shoulder.
Strategy: - Because of the **Mega Slow's** early appearance and the increased prices of towers and upgrades in Hardcore mode, it may be the downfall of most players if they are unprepared for it.
- For this reason, Farms are heavily recommended so that you will be able to afford more expensive upgrades sooner.
- Depending on the length of the map, most players can continue farming until the **Mega Slow** reaches the main defense, assuming it is set up in the back.
- Additionally, if multiple Lead Bosses were spawned from Mysteries on previous waves, the **Mega Slow's** debut can easily lead to a defeat on a shorter map.
- If you are playing on a map with the Enemies Beta modifier, Lead Bosses will be less of a problem on their own, as Mysteries are replaced by Breaker2s.
- High DPS towers, such as a couple Level 2 Golden Minigunners, Accelerators or Turrets, are highly recommended against the **Mega Slow**.
- If you are using Turret to take down the **Mega Slow**, extra towers may be required depending on the map as it has less DPS than Accelerator.
- The Engineer is not recommended because it has slow DPS at low levels.

- Level 3 Golden Scout and Level 2 Golden Soldier spam are effective against the **Mega Slow** if there are enough of them, although towers with lead detection, such as the Golden Pyromancer or Mortar, will also be needed to deal with the Lead Bosses that spawn before the **Mega Slow**.

- The Military Base's Tanks and Humvee 3s can be effective against this enemy, as they deal full collision damage to defense enemies. Once the **Mega Slow** begins to spawn in hordes, however, their effectiveness is reduced.
- A Level 4 Golden Scout can easily take down the **Mega Slow** for a relatively cheap price.
- You can use slowing towers, such as the Toxic Gunner, Electroshocker, Warden or Sledger to slow this enemy down.
- As the **Mega Slow** has the Stun Immunity, stunning towers like the Electroshocker will only slow it down instead of completely stopping it. Additionally, it prevents it from being knocked back.
- Freezing towers and the Warden can only slow it down for a shorter period of time compared to an average-sized enemy, due to its large size.
- The Electroshocker, Freezer, Cryomancer and Frost Blaster can also remove the **Mega Slow's** defense, allowing your towers to deal more damage.
- This can stack, so the Freezer/Frost Blaster/Cryomancer and Electroshocker can together remove up to 53% of its defense.
- The Pyromancer can also remove 50% of **Mega Slow's** defense, allowing your towers to deal even more damage.
- Poison defense dropping towers like the Toxic Gunner can also drop 50% of its defense.
Trivia: - The appearance of the **Mega Slow** is similar to the old design of the Boss4 from *Tower Battles*.
- Weirdly, the health of the **Mega Slow** was increased in MEGA Servers, despite it not being able to spawn in a MEGA Server without admin commands.
- When the **Mega Slow** was frozen by the Sledger prior to the 23rd of March 2022, it had a chance to create a huge wall of ice.
- This was due to one of its hooks being able to fall off of itself and fall far below the map, and the ice would attempt to encompass the hook.
Update History: - **Bug**: The hook on the left shoulder of the **Mega Slow** falls off.
- **Bugfix**: The hook on the left shoulder of the **Mega Slow** no longer falls off.
- Energy Immunity replaced with Stun Immunity.
- **Bug**: **Mega Slow** no longer uses the death sound effect.
- **Mega Slow** removed from the main game, as it has been replaced by Blighted. Now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.
- No longer appears in the Index.

Description: The **Mimic Umbra** is a large enemy that appears in Pizza Party. It has a high amount of health, somewhat high defense and an above average speed. It has two immunities, the Burn Immunity, which makes it immune to being set on fire, and the Stun Immunity, which prevents it from getting stunned, being only slowed down instead and prevents it from being knocked back. It also has Corpse, making it turn into a Corpse on death.
Appearance: The **Mimic Umbra** is a plushie that resembles The Umbra. The **Mimic Umbra** has black skin and hair with buns. It wears a magenta chestplate and leggings, with yellow patterns on them, black shoes and clothing. It also wears a purple crown with yellow headpieces. It has yellow buttons for eyes.
Strategy: - High DPS towers, such as the Golden Minigunner, Accelerator, Ranger and Engineer are very useful against this.
- Additionally, you can use Commander and DJ Booth to boost these towers' firerate and range, respectively.
- Freezing towers can be quite effective against the **Mimic Umbra**, as it is not immune to freeze.

- Because of its Stun Immunity, the Warden and Electroshocker can only slow it down instead of stunning it. Additionally, the Warden will only slow it down for a shorter amount of time because of its size.
- It cannot be knocked back by knockback towers like the Brawler as it has the Stun Immunity.
- Defense dropping towers, such as the Freezer, Cryomancer or Electroshocker, can be useful against the **Mimic Umbra** due to its somewhat high defense.
- Towers that reduce defense through burn, such as the Pyromancer or Molten Monster, cannot be used to drop its defense due to the **Mimic Umbra** having the Burn Immunity.
Trivia: - The **Mimic Umbra** is a call-back to the Solar Eclipse Event's The Umbra.
- The **Mimic Umbra** having 16,000 health is a reference to The Umbra's debut in Totality Tower being Wave 16.
Update History: - Energy Immunity replaced with Stun Immunity.
- **Bug**: Appears twice in the Index, one of them not loading in any model for the preview.
- Cash given increased from $4,000 to $6,250 every 25% health lost.
- **Bugfix**: No longer appears twice in the Index.

Description: The **Minigunner** is a mini-boss enemy that appears in Pizza Party, later being the guardian enemy for Wox the Fox. It has a high amount of health, below avearge speed and a low amount of defense. It has one ability, where it fires its minigun at nearby towers, stunning all towers hit for a few seconds and dealing 20 damage per bullet to units. The **Minigunner** also has Stun Immunity, which makes it immune to being stunned, being only slowed down instead and it cannot be knocked back.
The **Minigunner** replaces the Fallen Guardian in Pizza Party.
Appearance: The **Minigunner** is a robot that resembles the sixth version of the Level 0 Default Minigunner. It has a red torso, pants, sleeves and button knee-pad, black vest, backpack and shoes, and bandolier. The left side of its face, upper part of its left arm and part of its left leg are torn open, revealing wires and its endoskeleton. Its left sleeve is also torn. It has red buttons for eyes and a black smile. It wields a Vulcan M61 which it uses to stun towers.
On death, it will shake, emit yellow sparks and then power down. It also plays a powering down sound when it dies.
Strategy: - High DPS towers, such as the Accelerator, Engineer, Golden Minigunner or Turret are recommended due to its high health. The Commander can be useful at boosting the firerate of these towers.
- Placing another tower near the **Minigunner** can potentially bait it and prevent it from stunning other towers or damaging units, though this is not necessary.
- Defense dropping like the Pyromancer or Golden Pyromancer can be useful at decreasing the **Minigunner's** defense.
- This is not required however, as the **Minigunner** has negligible defense.
- Do note that when it first spawns, it is a Boss enemy, making it immune to defense reductions.
- Because of its ability to stun towers, the Medic can be helpful at shielding towers, protecting them from the **Minigunner**.
Trivia: - Many elements of the **Minigunner's** appearance draw from the **Plushie** Minigunner, like the knee-pad being a button and the minigun being taken directly from the skin.

Description: The **Molten Boss** appears as the final boss in the Sandbox exclusive Legacy Molten mode.

Like most other major bosses, the **Molten Boss** moves very slowly, but it has an extremely high amount of health. It also has Burn Immunity, making it immune to burn damage. Additionally, as it is a boss enemy, it is immune to being frozen, slowed down by the Toxic Gunner, confused by the Jester, damaged by the Nuke's fallout, knocked back, slowed down by the DJ Booth and it is only slowed down by the Electroshocker and Warden instead of being stunned.
It has three abilities:
- Its first ability is *Magma Stomp* which will create a shockwave and stun towers that are hit.

- Its second ability is *Scythe Slam* which will summon six random enemies. In Hardcore, it summoned in Molten Titan and Lava, in Molten it summoned Molten Titan and Molten, while in Sandbox mode is only summons in Normals.
- Its third attack is *Fireball*. The **Molten Boss** throws an explosive fireball at a tower. This sets the targeted tower and all surrounding towers on fire, stunning them for a period of time.
Appearance: **Variant 1**
The current version of the **Molten Boss** is similar to the third version, except it has a slash across its forehead, with drooping lines leaking from it.
**Variant 2**

The third version of the **Molten Boss** had glowing orange-red skin. It had magma horns on its head as well as magma arms. It had menacing orange eyes and walked slightly hunchback. It had black cobblestone armor, completed with pauldrons, gloves and boots, with a sun insignia imprinted on its torso. It also had metal armbands. Flaming spikes could also seen on its back torso and legs. As it walked, it left behind a lava trail. On its back was an orange-red scythe.
**Variant 3**

The second version **Molten Boss** had glowing orange-red skin. It had magma horns on its head as well as magma arms. It had red eyes. It had black cobblestone armor, complete with pauldrons, armbands, gloves and boots, with a sun insignia imprinted on its torso. Flaming spikes could also seen on its back torso and legs. As it walked, it left behind a lava trail. On its back was an orange-red scythe.
**Variant 4**

The first version **Molten Boss** had glowing orange-red skin. It had magma horns on its head as well as magma arms. It had red eyes and walked slightly hunchback. It had a black cobblestone shirt, with a sun insignia imprinted on its torso. Its legs were also black cobblestone. As it walked, it left behind a lava trail. Smoke was emitted from its torso. It wielded an orange-red scythe.
Strategy: - As with most major bosses, the Minigunner, Pursuit, Ranger, Turret and Accelerator are recommended for their high DPS.
- The Commander can also be used to boost the firerate of these towers with its ability.
- The DJ Booth can also help increase the range of these towers, decrease their high prices, or increase their damage output, or all three at Level 5.
- You can set a DJ Booth to its Red track to maximize damage output while also increasing range and decreasing upgrade costs of towers in its range.
- You cannot defend your towers against the *Fireball* attack if your towers do not have immunity to stun. Additionally, the attack has quite a long range.
- You can mitigate its effects by not grouping towers together.

- Air-based towers, cliff towers and the Medic are immune to this attack. Additionally, the Gladiator and Warden can block this stun, so long as they do have not blocked another attack within the last few seconds.
- A few bait towers can be used to distract the **Molten Boss**, making it less likely to throw the fireball at other towers.
- You can use the Medic to shield towers from the **Molten Boss's** *Fireball* and *Stomp* stun.
- The Toxic Gunner cannot be used to slow this down.
- Stunning towers like the Electroshocker can only slow it down instead of stunning it. Similarly, freezing towers can also only slow it down instead of stunning it.
- The Jester's confusion cannot confuse it, but its ice bombs can still slow it down.
- It cannot be slowed down by the DJ Booth.
Trivia: - Until the Gravekeeper was added, this was the only regular major boss in the game.
- However, the Swordmaster predates the **Molten Boss** by six days.
- The **Molten Boss** used to spawn Moltens instead of Lavas in Molten mode.
- There was once a glitch where you could place a tower on the body of the **Molten Boss** when it was killed.
- The **Molten Boss** was originally the logo of Paradoxum Games, the group that owns Tower Defense Simulator.

- Before the MEGA Update, the phrase "*Everything changed... When the Fire Nation attacked.*", which was played before the **Molten Boss** appeared, was a reference to the opening of the show *Avatar: The Last Airbender*.
- The magma horns on the **Molten Boss** are a retextured version of the Fiery Horns Of The Netherworld accessory from the Roblox catalog.
- The pauldrons worn by the **Molten Boss** are a retextured version of the Crushing Crystals Pauldrons accessory from the Roblox catalog.
- The Commander's dialogue before the **Molten Boss** appeared called the **Molten Boss** the Molten Titan, likely due to a developer oversight.

- Given the fact that the "Boss" suffix tends to be used more often for enemies who are stronger versions of weaker enemies (For instance, Speedy Boss being the name of stronger versions of the weaker Speedy enemy), the name "Molten Titan" seems to be more fitting for the **Molten Boss** and vice versa. It's entirely possible that the two respective enemies' names were swapped in development, whether it be on purpose or accidental.
- Prior to the MEGA Update, the **Molten Boss** had two additional abilities.
- The first was *Scythe Raise* which healed between 350 and 735 health over a period of 3.5 seconds.
- The second was *Scythe Swing*. The **Molten Boss** would swing its scythe, stunning all towers in a 15-stud radius.
- The **Molten Boss** appeared alongside the legacy Fallen King on the old "You Lost" screen.
- The **Molten Boss'** third final wave music is the same song as Battle Royale by Alec Koff.
- The current theme is a remix of the same song.

Description: The **Molten Demon** is an enemy that appears in Molten and Molten Arena PVP modes, and in The Takeover Event. It spawns in groups starting on Wave 11 of Molten as Hidden enemies, but it can also be summoned by the Molten Necromancer.
Appereance: The **Molten Demon** has a light red skin, with a few light brown flesh appearing on its body, some of it stitched up. It has two horns coming out of its head.
Strategy: - The **Molten Demon** can be a threat when it first appears, as it is quite speedy and comes early, becoming a run-killer to loadouts without early hidden detection. Many can stack with the ones summoned by the Molten Necromancer in later waves if it is not killed quickly.
- They can be killed fairly quickly, so one or two hidden detection towers can take them out.
- Towers like the Cowboy, Militant, Military Base or Electroshocker can be effective against this.
- High DPS towers like the Minigunner and Crook Boss can be prepared specifically for this enemy if early game towers are not enough, using the Farm to get them as they may be quite expensive.
- Area of effect towers, like the Trapper, Rocketeer or Electroshocker can be quite useful as they can damage all the **Molten Demons** as well as the Molten Necromancer at once, if spawned from it.
- The **Molten Demons** summoned by the Molten Necromancer can sometimes spawn with the Nimble attribute. As such, some towers with high, sustained damage are needed, combined with hidden detection.
- If you do not have much hidden detection, you can use the UAV or a Level 4+ Ace Pilot to give hidden detection.
- Do note that you do not earn any money from the **Molten Demons** summoned by Molten Necromancer, but you gain money for killing naturally spawned **Molten Demons**.
Update History: - Now appears in Mid Rank PVP Test.
- No longer appears in the PVP Test as it has been removed.
- Now appears in Molten Arena PVP, carrying over all of its PVP Test statistics.
- Now appears in Sk8 P4rk Master difficulty as part of The Takeover Event.

Description: The **Molten Golem** is an enemy that appears on wave 16 of Molten and Molten Arena PVP modes. It can also appear in The Takeover Event. It has high health and decent defense, though is walks slower than all enemies that appeared before it. It also has the Stun Immunity, making it harder to slow down. When it first spawns, it is a Boss enemy, granting it multiple immunities.
Appereance: The **Molten Golem** is a tall entity which has had most of its body replaced with mechanical parts. It only has its torso and right arm as the only non-mechanical parts, though they still contain some metal parts. It has red skin. It has mechanical grey arms, head with yellow eyes and teeth, multiple pieces of scrap covering its head and a grey metal arm with an orange neon part at the end. - Any form of Defense dropping can be used to drop its defense, as long as it is not a Boss enemy.
- Unlike some other molten enemies, it does not have the Burn Immunity, meaning burn defense dropping can be used here.

Description: The **Molten Hazmat** is an enemy that never appears naturally and is also never summoned by other enemies. The only way for it to appear is for another player to send it in PVP, specifically the Molten Arena.

It is nearly identical to the Elite Hazmat, as they share most of their statistics except health. The **Molten Hazmat** has 100 more health than the Elite Hazmat, however, because sending it changes its health to 300, they are effectively identical gameplay wise.
Appearance: The **Molten Hazmat** has a dark green skin color. It wears a white and black hazmat suit, which consists of single glove, a vest, gas tank, shoes and a gas mask. It has three different walking animations that are randomly chosen when it spawns.
Strategy: - Towers with high DPS, like the Minigunner, Ranger, Accelerator and Engineer can defeat this quite easily.
- As this generally spawns in hordes, area of effect towers like the Electroshocker, Mortar or Rocketeer can be useful against this.
- Because of its immunities, knockback and freeze cannot be used to slow it down.
- Stuns can still be used, but because of its Stun Immunity it will only be slowed down instead of fully stunned.
- Because of its immunities, freeze and burn defense dropping towers cannot drop its defense.
Trivia: - The **Molten Hazmat** is the first ever PVP exclusive enemy to get actually added to the game.
- There were other enemies planned in the past, such as the Enraged, Enraged Boss and Enraged Giant for the 2021 PVP, but they were never added alongside that version of the mode.
- The **Molten Hazmat** has an Index entry but its Logbook is unobtainable.
- This is the first evergreen enemy to have its Logbook unobtainable.
Update History: - Health now changes to 300 when sent.
Notes: - ↑ It is only available through sending from Wave 15 in Molten Arena PVP.
- ↑ It is only available through sending from Wave 15 in Mid Rank PVP Test.
