Description: The **Molten Warlord** is a major boss that appears on Wave 35 of Molten mode as the final boss. It also appears in The Takeover Event.

Like most other major bosses, the **Molten Warlord** moves very slowly, but it possesses a deceptively low amount of health compared to Frost Spirit or Fallen King. However, due to it having an ability that heals it by up to 1 million health but never exceeding its maximum health, its health becomes comparable to the Fallen King without its Defense.
The **Molten Warlord** has six abilities:

- Its first ability is *Eruption Slam*, where the **Molten Warlord** slams its weapon into the ground, creating three shockwaves in a straight line that stun every tower hit for 5.5 seconds and deal 225 damage to any unit caught in them.
- Its second ability, *Hammer Slam*, makes it slam its weapon three times, creating three shockwaves around it that stun towers for 4.5 seconds and deal 1,000 damage to units.

- Its third ability, *War Cry*, has the **Molten Warlord** breathe out fire, temporarily gaining Aggro, healing itself by a varying amount above 2,000,000. The health regenerated cannot be higher than its maximum health, meaning it heals the **Molten Warlord** back to full health. Additionally, the regenerated health is not consistent, as while it should not be lower than 2,000,000, it will often be a different higher value like 2,133,158.

Afterwards, it will summon eight enemies, which can be the Molten Mech (15% chance), Molten Golem (35% chance), Elite Boomer (20% chance) and Molten Necromancer (30% chance). While this ability can technically be used on its own, this will not happen under normal circumstances, meaning in majority of matches it will only be used as part of *Unchained Pandemonium*.

- Its fourth ability is *Fireball*, where the **Molten Warlord** fires out a flaming orb at towers, which applies a 60% Fatigue Debuff to them for 10 seconds an deal 225 damage to any unit caught in it.

- Its fifth ability is *Unchained Pandemonium*, which happens when it reaches 35% of its health. The **Molten Warlord** will remove its mask, which makes it temporarily become completely invulnerable. Then it will immediately perform the *War Cry* and *Molten Rain* abilities. This will also unlock *Molten Rain*.

- After entering rage mode, it can now use its sixth ability, *Molten Rain*. This ability makes it summon 25 meteors that fall down from the sky, stunning towers for 5 seconds and dealing 225 damage to units.
Appearance: The **Molten Warlord** appears as a glowing orange lava shaped into that of a humanoid figure. Its armor is made out of metal and molten rock, though the molten rocks mainly appear as random rocks scattered around its body, rather than as an actual piece of armor. Its metal armor consists of leggings, which have lava dripping from the footwear, grey gloves, small pieces of metal attached to its arms and a chestplate with a sun-like symbol engraved into it. On its head, it wears a grey skull mask and a small head piece. It has two horns on its head which are impaled with nails. It wields two weapons in its arms, a large grey hammer in its left hand and a large brown pickaxe in its right hand.
Upon using the *Unchained Pandemonium* ability, the **Molten Warlord** removes its mask, revealing its menacing orange eyes.
The **Molten Warlord** has a death animation where it drops both of its weapons and looks at both of its hands, shaking before exploding.
Strategy: - Towers such as the Hunter, Ranger, Turret, Crook Boss, Minigunner and Engineer, are recommended against the **Molten Warlord** for their high damage output.
- As these are all highly expensive towers, it is recommended to have a DJ Booth set to the Green track.
- The DJ Booth can give a reduced discount on the Red and Purple tracks at Level 5, which boost Damage and Range respectively.
- It is effective to chain the Commander's *Call to Arms* ability to maximize damage output.
- As the **Molten Warlord** has lower health than most other bosses, multiple Brawlers and Wardens can kill it fairly quickly.
- You can use the Medic to shield towers, preventing them from being stunned. This, however, does not make them immune to the **Molten Warlord's** Fatigue Debuff.
- Because of its **Unchained Pandemonium** ability, it becomes a substantially harder enemy to defeat after it uses this ability.

- This makes using *Call to Arms* or other tower-buffing items like consumables likely a waste, as they do not impact or remove the Tank or Aggro attributes. However, these are both temporary and so should not make a huge impact.
- You can have a single cheap tower away from the main defense to bait the **Molten Warlord** into stunning it instead of the important towers.
- The Nuke is very useful against it, as if dropped when it is at below 75,000 health, it can instantly get it to 0 health, preventing it from healing back lost health at 35% health.
- Do note that the **Molten Warlord** is immune to the Nuke's fallout damage, which somewhat reduces its effectiveness.
Update History: - **Molten Warlord** added, replacing the Molten Boss in Molten mode.
- **Bug**: **Molten Warlord** is affected by the All Paths modifier.

- **Bugfix**: **Molten Warlord** is no longer affected by the All Paths modifier.

Description: The **Mutagenic Blight**, internally referred to as **Hex Weaver**, is a support enemy that appears in Polluted Wasteland II. It has high health, slightly slow speed and 50% defense, reducing most forms of damage by 33%. It is also introduced in its wave as a Boss, giving it the immunities that the modifier includes. The **Mutagenic Blight** has one ability, *Uncontrollable Mutation*, where it throws a green orb on the path that applies attributes to other enemies in an explosion range of 5. The explosion applies Bloated or Nimble attributes to enemies. It can not apply attributes to Bosses or other **Mutagenic Blights**.
The **Mutagenic Blight** can be spawned by the Nuclear Monster.
Appearance: The **Mutagenic Blight** has black skin. It wears a grey shirt and shoes, blue pants, dark grey armbands with bloody spikes and dark grey shoulder-pads. It also wears a dark grey animal skull with multiple horns on its head. It holds a turquoise orb in its hands, which it uses to apply attributes to enemies.
It has a death animation where it falls over on its back, its orb falling on its face in the process.
Strategy: - While not a threat on its own, especially considering how multiple enemies at this stage of the mode are significantly stronger than it, its ability to apply buffs to other strong enemies makes it very dangerous.
- As with most other high-health enemies, DPS towers like the Engineer, Ranger or Accelerator are recommended.
- Stalling towers can be used to slow down enemies that are given the Nimble attribute.
Trivia: - The **Mutagenic Blight** is a renamed version of the Hex Weaver.
- The **Mutagenic Blight** animations and ability are identical to the Hex Weaver and the Fallen Jester.

- Similarly to the Fallen Jester, the **Mutagenic Blight** has an ignore list of enemies it will not throw its orbs at. However, that list is actually reused from the Hex Weaver, meaning none of the enemies in it can actually be seen.
- Enemies which can be seen being ignored by the **Mutagenic Blight** in Sandbox include the **Mutagenic Blight** itself, Reaver, Reaper and Conjurer.
- The Reaver did not appear in the Hexscape Event, meaning it is likely just a typo of Reaper.
- Enemies which no longer appear in any capacity but are still ignored include the Titus, Conserver and Hex's Maw.
Update History: - **Bug**: **Mutagenic Blight** can completely negate the stalling effects from towers, such as freeze or DJ Booth slowdown, if during the debuff it applies Nimble to the enemy. This will make it walk at its regular Nimble speed while the debuff effects are still on it.
- Speed decreased from Average (3) to Slightly Slow (2).
Notes: - ↑ Only the first **Mutagenic Blight** is a Boss enemy.

Description: The **Mystery Boss** is an enemy that will spawn a random enemy upon its death. The enemy spawned depends on the mode and wave. As the name implies, the **Mystery Boss** mostly spawns bosses that have high health or enemies that are quick, meaning that it is a very dangerous enemy. Its health depends on the mode you are playing on.
The **Mystery Boss** appears in the Sandbox exclusive Legacy Molten, Legacy Fallen and Golden modes.

The **Mystery Boss** is spawned by the Mystery Summoner, Summoner Boss, Necromancer Boss and Void Reaver. The Grave Digger used to be able to summon it in the Easy mode. If a map has the Enemies Beta modifier active, it is not spawned by these enemies as they spawn the Breaker4 instead.
The **Mystery Boss** is replaced by the Breaker4 in any map with the Enemies Beta modifier active.
Appearance: The **Mystery Boss** is a large translucent humanoid with a glowing orange question mark on its torso. All of its body parts are colored indigo and are made of a glass material. Its left leg is twisted and its head is pointing slightly downwards as it walks. It is also faceless.
Enemies Spawned: The **Mystery Boss** is able to spawn more enemies after its debut. *Italic* names can be spawned from the **Mystery Boss's** debut.
Strategy: - High DPS towers are recommended, supported by the DJ Booth and Commander.
- The **Mystery Boss'** random nature is not as impactful as the Mystery's. However, some enemies still pose a significant threat without the right towers.
- An overflow of Fallen Heroes, 24 Karats or Molten Titans may be overwhelming with their massive combined health.
- In general, high DPS towers accompanied by support towers is the best answer against all high health enemies.
- Shadow Bosses may be dangerous without adequate hidden defense.
- Hidden defense should be strong. Most high DPS towers have hidden detection, so Shadow Bosses should not be a major issue with them.
- As **Mystery Bosses** and their spawns come in hordes, towers that can deal damage to multiple enemies like the Mortar, Rocketeer, Gladiator and Executioner are effective.
- However, some of these towers may not fare so well against high health enemies. High DPS towers should be used to counter those.
- Be aware that you do not earn any cash from damaging enemies that the **Mystery Boss** spawns in every mode.
- The enemies that spawn from the **Mystery Boss** do not need to be killed for wave progression to occur.
- If you are speedrunning a map, you should focus on killing the **Mystery Bosses** first by setting your towers' targeting to *Weakest* before moving onto the enemies that spawn.
- Be aware that the spawned enemies may outrun your towers if you switch target settings.
- Using towers that can damage multiple enemies can remedy this.

- The Sledger, Frost Blaster and Electroshocker are probably the best slowing towers against **Mystery Bosses** as they can hit multiple enemies at once, though others like the Toxic Gunner are still viable.
- Be aware of the enemies' size and immunities, which may cause some of these towers to be less effective.
- Some enemies from the **Mystery Boss** like the Giant Boss have defense, so defense dropping towers can be useful.
Trivia: - There was a glitch whereby the **Mystery Boss**, after its death, could go to the next turn and stop there with its walking animation still playing. This was just a visual bug and did not affect gameplay in any way.
- For some reason, the **Mystery Boss** debuts on wave 29 for Golden mode.
- However, the text associated with the **Mystery Boss** appeared on wave 32, like Molten and Fallen modes.

- The same thing occurs with the Fallen Hero, Molten Titan, 24 Karat and Super Toxic which all can be spawned on wave 38 from the **Mystery Boss**, which is before their debut on wave 39 on Fallen, Molten, Golden modes and, formerly, Polluted Wasteland II, respectively. However, this is intentional.
- Prior to the Entity System Update, summoned enemies from the **Mystery Boss** used to say "*Mystery's* ______" instead of "*Mystery Boss's* ______".
- The question mark on the **Mystery Boss** is a re-textured version of the Question Mark accessory from the Roblox catalog.
- Prior to the Entity System Update, **Mystery Bosses** summoned by the Summoner Boss could be stuck in the air.

The **Mystery Summoner**, while having more health than the Speedy Boss, is slower than it. However, its main threat is the Mysteries and Mystery Bosses, or the Breaker2s and Breaker4s that it spawns. It also previously had Freeze Immunity.
Appearance: **Variant 1**
The current version of the **Mystery Summoner** was identical to its previous version, except it lacks a mouth.
**Variant 2**

The second version of the **Mystery Summoner** had lime green skin and walked hunchbacked. Its torso and legs were marble green and it wore marble dark green shoes. On its torso was a glowing green question mark. It also wore a light green cape. It had grey diamond-plated armbands and dark green wrappings around its left arm. It had menacing glowing green eyes, a drooling zombie face and it wore a green bowler hat. It held a mystery staff to summon enemies. It had a twisted left leg.
**Variant 3**

The original version of the **Mystery Summoner** had light green skin, its torso was marble green and its legs were dark marble green. On its torso was a glowing green question mark. It had green glowing eyes, had a drooling zombie face, had green diamond-plated armbands, and wore a green bowler hat. It also carried a mystery staff to summon enemies.
Strategy: - A couple of high DPS towers such as Minigunners, Turrets, Accelerators or Rangers can kill this easily.
- Additionally, you should use the Commander and DJ Booth to boost these towers.

- Try to kill the **Mystery Summoner** before it spawns a horde of Mysteries and Mystery Bosses, which may cause serious problems as they can spawn enemies with high health, such as the Slow Boss and the Speedy Boss.
- For maps that have a distance between the entrance and where the main towers are, this enemy may pose a threat.
- Treat the **Mystery Summoner** like the Necromancer. Subdue the enemies it spawns, then focus on the boss.
- For this reason, the Rocketeer, Mortar and Demoman can be quite useful against the **Mystery Summoner** as they can harm the enemies it spawns in large numbers.
- Piercing towers like Archer or Shotgunner can also damage most or all of the enemies spawned if positioned correctly.
Trivia: - The appearance of the **Mystery Summoner** is a reference to the Batman villain, The Riddler.
- The appearance is also quite similar to the Seventh Doctor from *Doctor Who* who carries an umbrella with a question mark-shaped handle.
- There was a short period of time when the **Mystery Summoner** was added (then called the **Mystery Boss**) where it was called the Speedy Boss due to a bug.

Description: The **Narrator** was the final boss The Final Act Event. It had far higher health than the Producer but walks slightly slower than it. As it was a Boss enemy in the event, most stalls were either weaker or did not work on it at all.
The **Narrator** has five abilities:
- *Hand Laser*, which fires ten thin laser beams from the fingertips of both hands. These apply a 25% Fatigue Debuff and Scared Debuff which last 22.5 seconds.
- *Hand Slam*, where both hands raise up and curl into fists, then slam the ground stunning towers for 6 seconds and dealing 75,000 damage to units in 12.5 radius.
- *Hand Summon*, which the **Narrator** spawns three MiniHands with a 1.5 second delay between each one.

- *Boss Base Attack*, the **Narrator** becomes immune to all damage and twirls its wand, summoning an orange fireball that spins around the **Narrator** for a few seconds. When the fireball reaches the tip of his wand, it uses it to strike the base and dealing damage equal to 40% of the max base health, accounting for the max possible Medic overheal but not the Skills overheal. This can be stopped with the four Spotlights aimed at **Narrator**, which if done right should make the **Narrator** get highlighted.

- *Dichromatic Crossfire*, a rage mode ability that happens at half health. In it, both hands' index and middle fingers fire a purple and an orange infernal beam separately, which rotate in random directions for 3 seconds. The **Narrator** also temporarily gains the Tank attribute.
Logbook Description: "*The Narrator is a performer from the Old World who used to be the right-hand man of Lord Exo. After being used for his revival, he achieved his theatrical moment on stage, striking a deal with Commander. He relies on his hands Righty and Lefty who were empowered by Lord Exo, making them some of the most powerful entities in existence.*"
Appearance: The **Narrator** has a dark grey body with stubby-legs from the belowknee down, and a white half-mask face, having a golden-like cut on the cheek of said mask, and having a crescent moonlike shape that curves upwards that is a reddish pink. And to add to its legs, it has two edges at its ankles that look like undefined small wings. Has no mouth on the other side of its halfmasked face, but it has a sharp white mouth a fourpointed star acting as its eye there too. The **Narrator** also wears a dark velvet suit with gold accents, with gold buttons and a dark red jabot with a golden star, having a dark velvet top hat with red feathers and two golden lines, one on the brim of its hat, and another one on the top. It has golden shoulder-pad epaulettes, having a jacket with flared out collars, the edge of said collars having gold too, with a gold line on each wristband of the jacket, also having ruffled ends at the very end of each wrist. It has a tail coat connected to his jacket, which has golden edges. It also has white gloves. It carries a magician stick with its right hand.
Behind it, it has two giant floating hands named Lefty and Righty. These are giant disembodied human hands wearing a white glove.
Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in The Narratorium is listed instead.
- High DPS towers, like the Ranger, Turret, Accelerator, Warlock or Golden Minigunner.
- The Ranger is especially useful, as they have map-wide range and immunity to the stuns from the **Narrator's** attacks.
- The Medic can also be used to shield normally not stun immune towers from these attacks.
- The Commander, DJ Booth and Mercenary Base can be used to boost the statistics of these towers.
- The **Narrator** can damage the base health with its *Boss Base Attack* ability, dealing 40% of the max base health as damage.
- To stop this, players need to redirect all the Spotlights so that they point at the **Narrator**.
- You can target multiple Spotlights at once; doing so is easier than targeting one Spotlight at a time.
- The **Narrator** will gain a yellow outline if all of the Spotlights are successfully redirected to him, allowing player to know they succeeded stopped him from using this ability.
- Due to the base damage being 40%, this means you can under most circumstances miss stopping the ability twice.
- It is not possible to survive for longer with the help of the Medic, as the ability accounts for its overheal.
- The ability does not increase how much damage it deals when the players has overheal from Skills, meaning that in Easy mode, it is possible to increase how many hits you can take before dying.
- The **Narrator** can summon in multiple MiniHands on the path, however, these are not meant to kill the player under most circumstances.
- They can only kill if spawned directly at the exit.
Trivia: - The **Narrator's** boss theme, In Bright Lights, samples lyrics from *The Mind Electric*, a song by *Tally Hall* / *Miracle Musical*.
- The **Narrator** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
- The **Narrator** appears in the asymmetrical horror game *FORSAKEN* as a skin for the killer Noli in which it can be obtained by beating Hardcore mode.
Update History: - **Bug**: **Narrator's** model does not turn into a hologram properly when converted by Hacker.
- **Bug**: **Narrator** still uses its abilities whenever converted by Hacker.
- **Bug**: *Boss Base Attack* will automatically stun the **Narrator** on any map that does not have the Spotlight.
- **Bug**: **Narrator's** hands do not have any animations in the Index.

abilities.text: **Summon** - Slams its staff into the ground, creating purple smoke and summoning five Skeletons (Brick Men in Headache Headquarters). Some summons can be Hidden, though the Summoner version does not do that.

Description: The **Necromancer** is a summoner enemy that appears in Easy, Basic Arena PVP, Intermediate, Molten Arena PVP, Casual mode, Challenge Trials, Badlands II and Polluted Wasteland II. It also appears in the tutorial and first chapters of Story mode. It has high health and decent speed. It has one ability where it uses its staff to summon five Skeletons, which may be Hidden. Skeletons were replaced by Brick Men in Headache Headquarters by the Brain Rot modifier.

The **Necromancer** originally was added as an enemy internally called *Summoner* with the display name of *Necromancer*, though on the 24th of February 2024, a new modern version of the legacy Necromancer would be added, which would be identical to the *Summoner* in terms of design, while also being quite similar in its statistics and ability. The *Summoner* variant is now rarely used, as it has been slowly replaced by the *Necromancer* variant in all new modes. Only sometimes Challenge Maps have it still appear. Both of these enemies, despite technically being different enemies, will be listed as one enemy due them being quite similar and serving the same purpose.

In any Challenge Map mode that has the Dark Necromancer and the Enemies Beta modifier active, the **Necromancer** replaces the Dark Necromancer. The **Necromancer** can be spawned by the Nuclear Monster with its *Nuclear Summon* ability and can be spawned by the Conjurer with its *Summon* ability. The Grave Digger used to spawn it with its *Triumphing Sheol* ability. It used to also be spawned by the Mystery Boss on the Molten mode before the 11th of December 2024, as well as in Polluted Wasteland II before the Halloween 2022 Update and in Easy mode before the 19th of July 2024.
The **Necromancer** also appeared in The Classic Event, Tower Defense Simulator x PLS DONATE Event and The Takeover Event.
Appearance: The **Necromancer** is a humanoid with a waist in its rig. It has a very desaturated light green skin color, and some of the skin on its head is missing, exposing a light grey skull. It has a black torso, sleeves, legs and cape. It has a light grey chain wrapped around its torso. It wields a dark brown wooden staff that has a small skull with light red streaks as well as grey horns on top of it, which it uses to summon Skeletons.
Strategy: - The **Necromancer** can be a threat when it first appears, as it can summon many Skeletons if not killed quickly, creating hordes, especially in groups.
- Killing the **Necromancer** before it can summon any Skeletons is recommended.
- Early game towers like the Soldier, Ace Pilot, Militant, Brawler or Golden Scout can take care of the **Necromancer** quite quickly.

- High DPS towers like the Minigunner, Crook Boss and Accelerator can be prepared specifically for this enemy if early game towers are not enough, with use of the Farm to get them as they may be quite expensive.

- Do note that the Accelerator, if locked onto the **Necromancer** or other strong enemies, will ignore the Skeletons the **Necromancer** summons until the targeted enemy is defeated or leaves its range.

- The Ranger and Sniper struggle against the hordes of Skeletons the **Necromancer** summons due to their slow firerate. They can be set to *Strongest* to target and kill the **Necromancer** while other towers take care of the Skeletons.
- Area of effect towers, like the Mortar, Rocketeer, Shotgunner or Mercenary Base's Grenadiers can be quite useful as they can damage both the **Necromancer** and the Skeletons it summons.
- The Hacker can be decent here, as it damage the **Necromancer** by converting the summoned Skeletons into hologram clones.
- The Skeletons the **Necromancer** summons have a chance to be Hidden, so ensure your towers are upgraded to have hidden detection.
- In Intermediate mode, the Slime enemy has the potential to turn into the **Necromancer**. As Slimes often come in large groups, it is easy to get overwhelmed.
- Do note that you do not earn any money from the summoned enemies.
- The **Necromancer** and its Skeletons move at a somewhat fast pace. You may want to use crowd control towers like the Freezer, Warden or Electroshocker, though this is not necessary.

- Stalling towers with the ability to hit multiple enemies, such as the Electroshocker, Freezer or Frost Blaster are particularly effective against the **Necromancer** as they can also stall the summoned Skeletons without taking their attention away from the **Necromancer**.
Trivia: - The **Necromancer** has the second most gamemode appearances, appearing in seven gamemodes total, behind the Breaker, Breaker2, Breaker3 and Breaker4.
- The Commander improperly mentioned this enemy as a Dark Necromancer.
- This is because the Commander's dialogue for Fallen mode is not changed when the Enemies Beta modifier is applied.
- Skeletons summoned by the **Necromancer** are called "*Summoner's Skeleton*" instead of "*Necromancer's Skeleton*".
- However, this is not the case in Easy mode. In that mode, the Skeletons are properly called "*Necromancer's Skeleton*".
- The **Necromancer** is also instead referred to as a "*Summoner*" when it is mentioned in the Halloween 2022 Update's update log.

- The **Necromancer** was the only enemy in Headache Headquarters that was not replaced by the Brain Rot modifier in 2024, though in 2025 two more enemies would not be replaced, these being the Speedy Boss and Brute.
- However, the Skeletons it would usually summon were replaced by Brick Men, and its health was increased to 1,200.

Description: The **Necromancer** was a summoner enemy that had the ability to spawn enemies every five seconds, which only appears in Legacy Molten mode. The enemies it can spawn are the Hidden, Slow, Speedy and Normal, which are mainly used to focus towers away from the **Necromancer**. These summoned enemies do not give money when damaged.

The **Necromancer** is slightly slower than the Slow and has the same speed as the Slow Boss. The **Necromancer** can be spawned by the Mystery Boss upon its death in Legacy Molten mode. The **Necromancer** also appeared in The Heights as part of the SFOTH Event. It could have been spawned by the Swordmaster.
Appearance: **Variant 1**

The current version of the **Necromancer** has grey skin, a twisted left leg and walks hunchbacked. It is faceless with pink glowing eyes. It wears a black cloak and its torso and legs are wool black. It has grey diamond-plated shoes and chains are wrapped around its arms. It has two large black shoulder-pads and a black hood. It holds a summoning staff with a purple orb on top.
**Variant 2**
The third version of the **Necromancer** is similar to the fourth version, except it had a drooling zombie face with pink glowing eyes.
**Variant 3**

The second version of the **Necromancer** had a ripped black cloak. It has grey skin, glowing blue eyes and a drooling zombie face. It was slightly taller than the Normal Boss. Its torso was grey, had black legs, black sleeves, grey skull shoulder-pads with black eyes and a brown hood. It wielded a staff that summoned enemies.
**Variant 4**

The first version of the **Necromancer** had grey skin, glowing blue eyes and a drooling zombie face. Its torso and legs were black, had black sleeves, grey skull shoulder-pads and a brown hood. It wielded a green skull staff that summoned enemies.
Strategy: As this enemy no longer appears naturally, strategy for its most recent intentional appearance will be listed instead.
- The **Necromancer** spawns many enemies, making splash damage towers, such as the Demoman, Mortar and Rocketeer, pretty effective against the **Necromancer** and the enemies that are summoned.
- If the **Necromancer** can get past your main towers, and there are no defenses near the end of the path, these enemies can reduce your base health significantly.
- Multiple early-game towers that deal high DPS, like the Militant, Crook Boss or Cowboy, can easily kill the **Necromancer**.
- You can also save up money for a mid-game tower, like the Ranger and Minigunner.
- These towers can be set to *Strongest* to attack the **Necromancer** first, but this may risk summoned enemies getting past your defenses.
- The Gladiator can be quite useful against the **Necromancer** as it can kill the enemies that spawn, as well as damaging the **Necromancer** at the same time.
- The Pyromancer and Shotgunner are more advanced examples of this.
- The summoned enemies do not give money when damaged.
- However, the Cowboy and Golden Cowboy can still generate money from them.
Trivia: - The staff held by second version of the **Necromancer** is a Roblox item, the Zombie Staff.
- This staff was first used by the removed Necromancer 2.
- The staff held by first version of the **Necromancer** is the Cliche Staff of Zombie Infection gear from the Roblox catalog.

- The hood used by the first and second versions of the **Necromancer** is the Viridian Hood accessory from the Roblox catalog.
- The hood used by the third and fourth versions is a re-textured version of it.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Summon** - Spawns three Strongs.

Description: The **Necromancer 2** was a summoner enemy that summoned three Strongs. It was a stronger version of the Necromancer, as it had higher health and summoned stronger enemies. It was slower than most enemies that debuted alongside it, such as the Slow Boss, meaning that these enemies could easily overtake the **Necromancer 2** as it was slower.
The **Necromancer 2** was replaced by the Summoner Boss after the MEGA Update.
Appearance: The **Necromancer 2** had green skin, a crown, black skull shoulder-pads, diamond-plated armbands, black legs and wore a black robe across its torso. The **Necromancer 2** carried a staff which was used to spawn Strongs.
Strategy: - If not prepared, this is quite a big threat.
- If the **Necromancer 2** is allowed to spawn hordes of Strongs, you can be easily overwhelmed with the volume of enemies.
- Try to have most of your towers at the start to prevent the **Necromancer 2** summoning lots of these enemies.
- The Rocketer is recommended to kill the hordes of **Necromancer 2s**, as well as wiping out the hordes of Strongs.
- Most towers struggle to kill the **Necromancer 2**.
- High damage towers, such as the Outlaw, should be set to *Strongest* to kill the **Necromancer 2** instead of the Strongs that spawn.
Trivia: - This enemy was replaced by the Summoner Boss.
- However, it may also be considered the previous incarnation of the Dark Necromancer, as that can be considered the "second Necromancer".
- The **Necromancer 2** used to spawn Blighteds instead of Strongs. This was changed as this made the game considerably harder.
- In a leak it was shown that the **Necromancer 2** was originally meant to spawn Boomer 1s, this however never happened in the game.
- At some corners, some of the Blighteds would suddenly stop moving if the **Necromancer 2** was killed.
- The skull shoulder pads used by the **Necromancer 2** are the The Riddling Skull accessory from the Roblox catalog.
- The staff held by the **Necromancer 2** is the Zombie Staff gear from the Roblox catalog.
Update History: - Now summons the Strong instead of the Blighted.
- **Necromancer 2** removed and replaced with Summoner Boss.

Description: The **Necromancer Boss** was a high health summoner enemy which only appeared in Hardcore mode. Currently, it can only be spawned in Sandbox mode if the player has the Sandbox Plus+ gamepass. It behaves similar to the Mystery Summoner and Summoner Boss, as it spawns Mysteries and Mystery Bosses with its staff. With the Enemies Beta modifier active, it spawns Breaker2s and Breaker4s. However, this enemy spawns between 8-10 Mysteries/Breaker2s and Mystery Bosses/Breaker4s, causing huge problems if left alone for too long.
Appearance: The **Necromancer Boss** has reflective black skin. It wears a unique reflective purple fade cloak. Its torso and pants are also reflective purple fade. The **Necromancer Boss** wears a reflective white skull mask, and it has pink glowing eyes. It wears a reflective purple fade top hat with two small white horns on on the front. It also wields a spiked stone staff that emits purple flame at the end. When summoning enemies, the flame emits purple particles.
Strategy: This strategy refers to the state of the game while the **Invisible** still appeared in the Hardcore mode.
- Due to its high health and enemies it spawns, the **Necromancer Boss** must be dealt with as soon as possible.

- If the **Necromancer Boss** is left alive for too long, it can create a huge army of Mysteries and Mystery Bosses, or a huge army of Breaker2s and Breaker4s, so it is recommended to deal with the **Necromancer Boss** quickly.
- This is especially noticeable on long maps such as Marshlands and Four Seasons.
- High DPS towers, such as the Ranger and Turret are recommended against the **Necromancer Boss**.
- Rangers having their targeting set to *Strongest* can deal massive damage to the **Necromancer Boss**, combined with the Commander's *Call to Arms* ability.
- Do be aware of enemies like the Fallen Swordmaster distracting Rangers if they are set to *Strongest*.
- Turrets can deal with the enemies spawned from the boss, as its damage and firerate can defeat all of the enemies spawned.
- Minigunners can also quickly deal with the summoned enemies.
- The Accelerator can lock onto the **Necromancer Boss**, though summoned enemies from the **Necromancer Boss** can get past multiple Accelerators.

- The enemies spawned by the **Necromancer Boss'** minions may prove troublesome, such as the Circuit and the Speedy King, which can speed up nearby enemies, leading to multiple fast enemies leaking through.
- You can play on a map with the Enemies Beta modifier to ensure this does not happen, as Mysteries and Mystery Bosses are replaced by Breaker2s and Breaker4s in those maps.
- Towers that can deal damage to multiple enemies, such as the Engineer, Executioner or Golden Pyromancer, can be great at dealing with enemies summoned by the **Necromancer Boss**.
- Units from the Military Base can deal with the **Necromancer Boss**, through their collision.
- Freezing towers and the Warden can be used to slow this down, however because of its large size they only freeze or stun it for a shorter amount of time compared to an average-sized enemy.
Trivia: - The appearance and name of the **Necromancer Boss** is similar to one of the variants of the Necromancer Boss from *Tower Battles*.
- The **Necromancer Boss** has a death animation where it holds its hand to its heart, trembles violently, and falls to the ground.
- Prior to the Entity System Update, enemies summoned by the **Necromancer Boss** were uniquely temporarily immune to damage.

abilities.text: **Cursed Summon** - The **Necromancer King** spins its staff, creating a purple smoke and summoning five Giant Skeletons. Legacy version summons Cursed Skeletons instead.

Description: The **Necromancer King**, internally referred to as the **Summoner2** and formerly known as **Necromancer Boss**, which is also the name for its legacy version, is a summoner enemy that appears in Polluted Wasteland II and Challenge Trials. It has a very high amount of health, higher than all enemies that appeared before it, and an above average speed, faster than the Warden. It also has one ability, where it will spin its staff, summoning five Giant Skeletons. Unlike the Necromancer, its underling counterpart, it does not pause to summon enemies, making it more threatening. It also has Freeze Immunity, making it immune to being chilled or frozen, and it has Stun Immunity, which makes it only slow down by 40% instead of stunned by stunning towers like the Warden and Electroshocker and immune to knockback.
Appearance: The **Necromancer King** has a desaturated dark green skin color and a black torso, legs, sleeves and cape. Some of its head is missing skin, revealing its skull. It has grey metal shoulder-pads that resemble skulls with a purple interior and a grey metal neck-guard, with purple gems decorating it. It also wears a crimson leather belt with a purple crystal and a metal crown with multiple diamond shaped crystals on them. It wields a brown wooden staff with a metal base, which has a gem, and a skull on top, which has light red streaks on it. It uses this staff to summon Giant Skeletons. It also emits purple particles.
Strategy: - Deal with this enemy as soon as possible. Leaving the **Necromancer King** alive for too long will allow it to summon a vast amount of Giant Skeletons.
- The Ranger, Accelerator, Minigunner and Turret are great at dealing with the **Necromancer King** and the Giant Skeletons it summons.
- You may want to set these towers to *Strongest* to ignore the enemies that the **Necromancer King** spawns. The Saboteur can also be used for this purpose.
- You can boost the firerate of these towers with the Commander's *Call to Arms* ability whenever the **Necromancer King** spawns.
- Splash damage towers, such as the Rocketeer or Mortar, can be great at dealing with the Giant Skeletons the **Necromancer King** summons.
- They can also be useful at dealing damage to the **Necromancer King**. Do note, however, that these towers do not have enough DPS to deal with the **Necromancer King** on their own.
- Do note that you do not earn any money from the summoned enemies.
- Because of the **Necromancer King's** immunities, freezing towers like the Freezer, Frost Blaster and Sledger cannot freeze or slow it down.

- Stunning towers such as the Electroshocker can only slow it down, while knockback towers such as the Brawler cannot knock it back. Additionally, the Warden will slow it down for a shorter amount of time because of its size.
Trivia: - Despite now being called the **Necromancer King**, Commander still refers to it as the "*Necromancer Boss*" in Challenge Trials.
Update History: - Health is now based on gamemode.
- Now has 60,000 health in Polluted Wasteland II.
- Now has 14,000 health in Badlands II.
- Now has 14,000 health in Enemies Beta Fallen mode and Pizza Party.
- **Bug**: **Necromancer Boss** has 14,000 health in Polluted Wasteland II instead of 60,000.
- **Bugfix**: **Necromancer Boss** now has the correct amount of health in Polluted Wasteland II.
- **Bug**: **Necromancer Boss** has 14,000 health in Polluted Wasteland II instead of 60,000.
- No longer appears in Enemies Beta Fallen, as it has been replaced by the Fallen Summoner.
- **Bugfix**: Now has 60,000 health in Polluted Wasteland II due to Enemies Beta getting removed.
- No longer appears in Pizza Party.
- No longer appears in Badlands II.
- None of the changes are applied to the legacy version.
- Name changed from *Necromancer Boss* to *Necromancer King*.
- Speed increased from Average (3.25) to Above Average (4).
- Cash given is now mode dependent.
- Gives $5,000 every 20% health lost in Challenge Trials.
- Gives $40,000 every 20% health lost in Polluted Wasteland II.
- Default value is $1 every 20% health lost.
- Health increased from 75,000 to 125,000 in Polluted Wasteland II.
- No longer summons five Cursed Skeletons.
Notes: - ↑ Only the first **Necromancer King** in Polluted Wasteland II and Challenge Trials is a Boss enemy.

abilities.label: Ability 1
abilities.text: **Gooey Demise** - Upon death, applies an 35% Firerate Debuff (~53.85% increase) to towers for 3 seconds and deals 40 damage to units in an explosion radius of 15.

abilities.label: Ability 2
abilities.text: **Essence of Life** - Upon death, leaves four purple goo puddles on the path that last 15 seconds. These heal any enemy that walks over them by 60 every 0.5 seconds.

Description: The **Necrotic Skeleton** is an enemy that appears in Fallen mode, Challenge Trials and Badlands II. In Challenge Maps and The Takeover Event, it does not appear naturally, and is instead summoned by the Fallen King and Fallen Summoner. In all other modes, it does appear naturally, though in Badlands II, it is always a Hidden enemy. It has a decent amount of health and walks quite fast. The **Necrotic Skeleton** is also a support enemy, as it has two abilities which debuff towers and buff enemies, both upon death.

Its first ability is **Gooey Demise**, which causes it to apply a 35% Firerate Debuff (53.85% increase) to every tower in its 15 radius for 3 seconds. Its second ability is *Essence of Life*, which makes it leave four puddles of purple goo on the path. These puddles heal any enemy that walks over them by 60 every 0.5 seconds. They last 15 seconds.
Logbook Description: "*Necrotic Skeletons were once Fallen Necromancers who pushed their dark arts too far. The curse consumed them entirely, leaving only bones saturated with volatile necromantic energy. When destroyed, they unleash the corruption stored within, spreading the curse to everything nearby. They are warnings of what happens when one embraces the darkness completely.*"
Appearance: The **Necrotic Skeleton** is made entirely of sand colored parts that resemble a skeletal humanoid. It does not have a full torso, but instead has the bone cage for it. Its head is a skull with large neon blue eyes and horns. It wears a grey chestplate and shoulder-pads.
Upon death, the **Necrotic Skeleton** will fall over and create a trail of purple goo in front of it.
Strategy: - The **Necrotic Skeleton** is a support enemy. Upon death, it will both debuff towers and buff enemies.
- It will debuff towers by applying an 35% Firerate Debuff to them, though it is quite short.
- The Commander and Medic can be used to partially mitigate its Firerate Debuff.
- Its puddles will heal any enemy that walks over it by 60 health every 0.5 seconds, regenerating their health.

- As it is rather fast, it will get to the front of enemies quite quickly, allowing it to regenerate their health. Additionally, it will be swiftly killed by towers as its health is much lower than most enemies that appear around the same time as it.
- High DPS towers, like the Minigunner, Turret and Accelerator can be quite effective against this, as it has quite low health.
- High DPS towers with splash damage capabilities, such as the Ranger and Pursuit can be quite useful, as they can damage both the **Necrotic Skeletons** and the enemies that summoned them.
- In Badlands II, it is recommended that these towers have hidden detection, due to the **Necrotic Skeleton** being a Hidden enemy there.
- The Firework Technician or Ace Pilot can be used to give hidden detection to your towers, if you lack it, while the Spotlight Tech can be used to expose the **Necrotic Skeletons**.
- Area of effect towers, like the Mortar, Rocketeer and Tesla can be quite useful at killing the **Necrotic Skeletons**, as they spawn in hordes.
Update History: - **Bug**: Poison and electric defense dropping towers do not drop its defense.
- **Bugfix**: Poison and electric defense dropping now drops **Necrotic Skeleton's** defense, though the Jester still cannot drop it.
- Now appears in High Rank PVP Test.
- Now appears naturally in Fallen Mode on Wave 26.
- Speed increased from Slightly Fast (5) to Fast (7).
- Now gives $2,000 on death in Fallen.
- Now appears in Sk8 P4rk Extreme difficulty as part of The Takeover Event.
- No longer appears in Sk8 P4rk, as it has been removed.
- Health increased from 1,000 to 1,400 in Fallen mode.
- Cash given decreased from $2,000 to $1,400 on death in Fallen mode.

Description: The **Nerd Ducky**, internally referred to as the **Nerd Duck**, was the final boss of the Ducky Revenge Event and its rerun in the Spring Frenzy Battle Pass on the Hard difficulty, where it appeared on Wave 25. As a major boss, it has very high health and has boss immunities such as being immune to the Nuke fallout damage, the Jester and Biologist's confusion effects, the DJ Booth's slowdown from *Drop the Beat* and the Toxic Gunner's slowdown. To compensate, it walks quite slowly.
It has six abilities:

- The first, *Ducky Decoy* has it jump to another path while also temporarily becoming a Flying enemy, leaving a Mega Ducky without boosted defense behind but with health reduced to 10,000. It always moves paths in a cycle: Starts on yellow, then jumps to orange, then green, then blue and then goes back to yellow.
- The second, *Ducky Stampede* has it spawn ten Elite Duckies and one Mega Ducky with 100% Defense.
- The third, *Ducky Reposition*, has it target a tower with a beam and swap its location with another tower.

- The fourth, *Ducky Discharge* has it supercharge itself, damaging the base by 30 health, stunning all towers for 8 seconds and dealing over 100,000 damage to units. Can reduce the base's health to below zero. If a Bunny Sentry is on the map, it will launch itself at the **Nerd Duck**, stopping the ability.

- The fifth, *Ducky Blast*, has it fire out multiple missiles at a minimum of five targets, applying a 30% Fatigue Debuff (~23.07% firerate increase) to towers for 8 seconds. As for units, it deals no damage and does not affect them in any way.
- The sixth, *Nerd Rage*, has it power up its left arm and slam the ground, stunning towers for 6 seconds and dealing 1,500 damage to units.

When the **Nerd Ducky** is defeated, it begins to fall apart, first its right arm, then its left arm, then the bunny ears which are launched into the sky, and then it falls over on its back, tossing the duck inside out in the process. The bunny ears then fall back down to the ground.
Logbook Description: "*The latest invention by Nerd Duck: a state-of-the-art machine wing-crafted by the mechanist nerd who equipped it with the latest engineering of duck weaponry. With the discovery of the God Shard, its energy output allowed Nerd Duck to harness its power and advance currently known duck technology. This masterpiece stands as Nerd Duck’s prized creation.*"
Appearance: The **Nerd Ducky** is a huge mech based on a rabbit, powered by a God Cube fragment. The mech itself is adorned with white plating. In its chest, there is a cockpit where the **Nerd Ducky** pilots the mech and located on its back is a red core. The arms are more square near the shoulder while the forearms are more circular. Located in both arms are compartments that contain missile launchers, and both arms have four grey fingers. The legs are grey except for the thighs which are white, and the feet resemble that of a rabbit. Finally, the head is flat and heavily resembles that of a rabbit, with red eyes, a small grey nose and two large ears.
The **Nerd Ducky** controlling the giant mech is a small yellow duck with an orange beak, two white teeth and orange flippers. It wears a white shirt, blue swear, a black bowtie and grey glasses.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Bathroom Approach is listed instead.
- **Nerd Ducky** will initially spawn on the left side, however, it will keep hopping between paths afterwards.
- This makes high range towers, like the Ranger or Pursuit very useful here.
- The DJ Booth can be used to boost the range of your towers, allowing them to cover more of the track, though this will mostly help out the already high range towers.
- High DPS towers like the Ranger, Pursuit, Golden Minigunner, Turret or Accelerator are recommended against this.
- As the Ranger and Pursuit are stun immune, they are immune to most of its attacks except *Ducky Blast* ability, as they are not fully debuff immune.
- The Commander and DJ Booth can be used to boost the DPS of these towers.
- It is recommended to buy Bunny Sentries before Wave 25, as they can stop the *Ducky Discharge* ability.
- The Medic can be used to cleanse towers from stuns, but it cannot be used to help with the Fatigue Debuff applied by **Nerd Duck's** *Ducky Blast* ability.
Trivia: - The **Nerd Ducky** is the second enemy to specifically target map elements, the first being The Umbra.
- The **Nerd Ducky**, however, is the first enemy to be able to destroy map elements, rendering them unusable.
- When you spawn the **Nerd Ducky** in a different map, the first ability, *Ducky Decoy*, has it jump to the exit.
- The **Nerd Ducky** quacks were created by Enthrallist using duck calls.
- The **Nerd Ducky** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Bug**: **Nerd Duck** clips into the ground when made larger or smaller.
- **Bug**: *Ducky Decoy* does not set Mega Duck's health to 10,000 properly.
- **Bug**: **Nerd Duck** is ridiculously far away in its Index.
- **Bug**: **Nerd Duck** blocks tower placement near it, blocked area has Damage Indicators appear in it.
- **Nerd Duck** removed from the main game, now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.
- **Nerd Ducky** re-added to the main game, now appears in Bathroom Approach.
- Name changed from *Nerd Duck* to *Nerd Ducky*.
- Health increased from 800,000 to 1,000,000 in Hard difficulty.
- Speed decreased from Slow (1.525) to Extremely Slow (0.75).
- Cash given changed from $12,500 every 1% health lost to $156,250 every 12.5% health lost.
- Base health damage increased from 25 to 30.
- **Bugfix**: *Ducky Decoy* now properly sets Mega Ducky's health to 10,000, though it is only noticeable in Sandbox mode.
- **Bug**: When **Nerd Ducky** uses its *Ducky Decoy* ability, the animation for said ability will play continuously until it activates another ability or if it dies.

- **Nerd Ducky** removed from the main game, now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.

Description: The **Neuro Runner** was a fast enemy that appeared relatively early on in Failed Gateway as part of the Hexscape Event. It also appeared in Containment, though only when summoned by Corrupted Titus. It had a fair amount of health for its debut, high defense and a fast speed, making it a dangerous enemy to unprepared defenses. Additionally, it had Freeze Immunity, making it immune to being chilled or frozen, and Stun Immunity, making it immune to being stunned, and instead being slowed down.
Appearance: The **Neuro Runner** was a wooden construct with a brown body, though the ends of its legs were made out of metal scraps. It had dark brown shirt and pants, alongside even darker gloves. It also had multiple dark brown bandages around its gloves. It wore multiple pieces of grey metal armor, knee-pads, armbands, chestplate and armor around the gloves, with some of them having spikes. On its back, it had an energy pack which lead to an energy core located on its chestplate, which gave it its speed. It also had a metal head piece with wires and a lens on its head and a grey metal face mask.
Strategy: - The **Neuro Runner** can be defeated using stronger towers like the Golden Soldier, Soldier, Crook Boss or Brawler.

- These also often spawn in groups, accompanied by multiple Aggro enemies. Having some towers in the back may be needed in cases where Aggro enemies make **Neuro Runners** run out of your tower's ranges.
- The **Neuro Runner** is immune to being slowed down by freezing towers or frozen by them and can only be slowed down by the stunning towers like the Electroshocker, making it harder to slow down.

- The Toxic Gunner is not affected by any of its immunities and has a pretty long poison time and quite cheap to afford, making it a decent option, especially when set to *Random* to slow down as many as possible.
- It can also be pretty effective at dealing damage.
- As Stun Immunity also prevents enemies from being knocked back, towers like the Brawler cannot be used to slow it down.
- Its defense can be reduced by towers like the Pyromancer or Trapper, however, it cannot be reduced by the freezing towers due to its Freeze Immunity.
Update History: - **Bug**: Poison and electric defense dropping does not decrease **Neuro Runner's** defense.
- **Bugfix**: Poison and electric defense dropping now drops **Neuro Runner's** defense, though the Jester still cannot drop it.

Description: The **Nightshade** is a summoner enemy that appears in both Hardcore. Voidcore and the Halloween 2026 Live Event. It is a stronger version of the Mandrake, boasting higher health, walking faster and summoning in stronger enemies. Upon death, it spawns in two Elite Mysteries, one Blighted and three Bloated and Nimble Mandrakes.
Logbook Description: "*The Nightshade are creatures that were once Odds, but the Odd had died in some way. If the corpse was lucky enough to have fallen onto the flora of the Void, they were then consumed by the overgrowth and turned into a Nightshade. It’s up for debate whether you could call them living, as the flowers have completely set root throughout their entire bodies, but it wouldn’t be far-fetched to say they are being controlled by it. The flowers throughout the Void sometimes have sentience, as flora finds nutrients through corpses as they decompose. Sometimes, a Nightshade will wander. Not to anything specific. It just drifts to wherever the flowers feel like going that day.*"
Appearance: The **Nightshade** is a bush primarily containing flowers. On top of the bush, there are multiple purple crystals. Under the bush, two legs can be seen.
Strategy: - High DPS towers like the Juggernaut, Accelerator, Turret, Engineer or Ranger can be used to take this down.
- As it summons in multiple enemies on death, a lot of which also have some sort of summoning ability, towers with some AOE capabilities like the Ranger, Pursuit or Engineer can be especially useful.
- Support towers like the Commander, DJ Booth and Medic can be used to boost the DPS of your towers.
Trivia: - The **Nightshade** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - Elite Mystery spawns decreased from 3 to 2.
- Now summons one Blighted on death.
- **Nightshade** now appears in Nil Zone II as part of the Halloween 2026 Live Events.
- **Nightshade** no longer spawns in Nil Zone II, as the Halloween 2026 Live Event has ended.

Description: The **Ninja** was an enemy that could not be attacked by towers without hidden detection. Without hidden detection, the **Ninja** was a nuisance. Compared to the Hidden, the **Ninja** was slightly faster and also had more health.
The **Ninja** appeared in Golden and Fallen modes. It was replaced by its counterpart, the Hidden, in Beginners and Molten modes.
Upon its death, the Mystery could have spawned the **Ninja** in Golden and Fallen modes. The Dark Necromancer could have also spawned the **Ninja**.
Upon Golden mode's reappearance through Sandbox mode, it has been fully replaced by the Shadow.
Appearance: The **Ninja** had black fabric legs, headband and torso. It had black skin and a drooling zombie face. It also had a swordpack on its back.
Strategy: - Towers with hidden detection are the best way to attack **Ninjas**.
- Most early game towers gain hidden detection. Such towers are recommended to deal with early-game **Ninjas**.
- The Level 2 Minigunner is a strong option as the **Ninja** is quite strong and early game towers may not output enough damage to defeat it.
- Use of the Farm to get the Minigunner early is recommended.
- For splash damage towers that cannot target the **Ninja**, such as the Rocketeer, if a **Ninja** is caught up in an explosion, they will be dealt splash damage.
- This means that another detectable enemy must be near the **Ninja** for a splash damage tower to hit the **Ninja**.
- Units (like Military Base vehicles and Crook Boss Crooks and Mafias) cannot target the **Ninja** but can damage the **Ninja** through collision.
- The Level 2 Military Base is fairly viable against the **Ninja**.
- However, do not rely on Crooks or Mafias as they have very low health.
- You can use the Frost Blaster to slow this down, though it is not necessary.
- The Electroshocker, while not having hidden detection, can hit the **Ninja** with a chain reaction if another detectable enemy is near it.
- Although the Pyromancer does not have hidden detection, its flames can pierce through enemies, so the **Ninja** can be hit if there is another detectable enemy near it.
- The Freezer's *Ice Age* ability can slow the **Ninja** down. In addition, if a **Ninja** is caught in a Freezer's splash radius, it will be frozen.
Trivia: - The **Ninja** used the Swordpack accessory from the Roblox catalog.
- The headband used by the **Ninja** is the Black Ninja Headband of the Silent Sun accessory from the Roblox catalog.
- This enemy was replaced by the Shadow in the Overhaul Update.

Description: The **Normal** is the first enemy in the Easy, Casual, Intermediate, Basic Arena PVP, Molten Arena PVP and Legacy Molten modes. It also appears in the tutorial and first chapters of Story mode. As the first enemy that spawns, it has fairly mediocre speed and low health.

Description: The **Nuclear Fallen King** was the final boss of Polluted Wasteland Fallen mode. It replaced the Fallen King in Polluted Wasteland.

It moved somewhat slowly (during *Rage Mode*, it moved quite fast for a major boss), but had an outstanding amount of health, had lots of abilities that could stun lots of towers and could destroy units, proving to be one of the hardest challenges of the game. However, it only spawned in Polluted Wasteland, which was a long map with multiple loops, making the enemy far more balanced. It stopped moving when performing its *Stomp* and *Block* move. It had many immunities, namely burn, freeze, energy and Splash Damage.
Appearance: The **Nuclear Fallen King** was a radiant green version of the Fallen King. It carried a jade sword and shield. The **Nuclear Fallen King** had a granite dark green dominus with glowing green horns. Its armor was granite dark green and appears to be glowing neon green on some parts. It had a dark green belt, gloves and boots. It also had a granite dark green cape. Green smoke and green particles were emitted from its torso. It was normally faceless but upon *Rage Mode* being activated, it would gain green glowing eyes.
Strategy: - Be aware of the Circuits that the **Nuclear Fallen King** may spawn as it can speed it up massively.
- They must be killed quickly otherwise the **Nuclear Fallen King** will easily walk past all of your defenses.
- The **Nuclear Fallen King** has lots of immunities that limits the amount of towers that can be effective against it.
- It has Freeze Immunity, so it cannot be frozen by the Freezer or Frost Blaster.
- However, these towers can be useful against the enemies it spawns, especially the Circuit and Rusher.
- Due to its large size and Energy Immunity, the Electroshocker can slow the **Nuclear Fallen King** down for a very short period of time instead of stunning it.
- It has Burn Immunity, so the Pyromancer cannot burn the **Nuclear Fallen King**. However, it can still deal non-burn damage to it.
- The **Nuclear Fallen King** also has Splash Damage immunity.
- While this makes the Mortar and Rocketeer useless against the **Nuclear Fallen King** itself, they may be useful in clearing out the enemies that the **Nuclear Fallen King** can spawn.
- Military Base units can still damage the **Nuclear Fallen King** with collision and gun damage, but not cannon damage.
- When the **Nuclear Fallen King** performs its *Block* ability, it cannot be damaged from any source. It is immobile while this move is performed, as this is mainly to waste time/ability duration.
- This can be used as breathing room to manage your towers, but do not use abilities, such as the Commander's *Call to Arms*, during this move.
- The **Nuclear Fallen King's** *Block* prevents all forms of damage. Units, like the Military Base Tank, will pass through the **Nuclear Fallen King** without dealing collision damage.

- The **Nuclear Fallen King** is accompanied by four Fallen Guardians. They are always in front of the **Nuclear Fallen King**. They should be fought first since they are faster than the **Nuclear Fallen King**.
- You do not need to kill the Fallen Guardians spawned by the **Nuclear Fallen King** when it performs its *Rage Mode* ability as they will not give money when damaged.
- You can still earn money from damaging them with the Cowboy and **Golden** Cowboy.
- However, if they get past by the **Nuclear Fallen King**, they should be dealt immediately as they can easily walk past your defense due to their high health and defense.
- Beware of the **Nuclear Fallen King's** *Stomp* attack. Its shockwave covers an enormous radius around the boss, stunning any ground troops caught in the radius.
- The Medic's ability can cleanse towers, as long as the Medic itself is not stunned.
- This ability also deals 750 damage to all units. This destroys all units instantly, except for the Railgun Tank.
- Cliff towers, such as the Ranger, are not immune to any attack as the *Acid Rain* attack occurs for every ability used.
- However, the Pursuit and Ace Pilot are immune to all attacks as they are air-based towers.
- While the **Gladiator** can block one stun every 5-10 seconds, due to the *Acid Rain* attack, it will likely always be stunned after an attack.
- Try to place towers away from the path as the **Nuclear Fallen King** will perform its *Acid Rain* attack for every ability it uses.
- Multiple high DPS towers, such as Minigunners, **Golden** Minigunners, Turrets, Rangers and Accelerators are recommended against the **Nuclear Fallen King**.

- Make sure to sell any Farms to maximize the amount of towers attacking the **Nuclear Fallen King**. They do not produce any income anymore, count towards your tower limit, and can be replaced by more useful towers.
Trivia: - The **Nuclear Fallen King's** theme is a remix of the old You Lost! theme.
- After the Overhaul Update, when the **Nuclear Fallen King** died, its death animation did not play.
- Additionally, after *Rage Mode* was activated, its sword had purple sparks, which is only meant to occur for the Fallen King.
- The animation for the *Stomp* attack also did not play.
- Unlike the Fallen King, the **Nuclear Fallen King** did not gain shield health when *Rage Mode* is activated.
- Prior to the Overhaul Update, the **Nuclear Fallen King** was one of the few enemies to gain a shield. This shield reduced the damage dealt by most towers to 3.
- The sword wielded by the **Nuclear Fallen King** is a modified version of the Immortal Sword: Venom's Bite.
Update History: - Summoned enemies no longer give money when damaged.
- *Rage Mode* can now spawn between 2-4 Fallen Guardians instead of 2-3.
- Partial Electric Immunity replaced with Energy Immunity.
- Units no longer deal damage to **Nuclear Fallen King** during *Rage Mode* and *Block* ability, but instead pass through it.
- **Bug**: Death animation does not play; instead the **Nuclear Fallen King** continues walking until it gets to a corner. There it will remain to the end of the match.

Description: The **Nuclear Guardian** is a large guardian enemy that appears in Polluted Wasteland II. It has a very high amount of health but a slightly slow speed. It has one ability, where it slashes a nearby tower with its scythe, stunning them. The **Nuclear Guardian** replaces the Fallen Guardian in Oops! All slimes! Challenge Map.
Appearance: The **Nuclear Guardian** is a very large humanoid with a waist and lower arms in its rig. It has a desaturated dark green skin color and a black torso, waist and legs. It wears a black hood with grey feathers beside it, and has a grey metal bird beak along with two glowing green eyes. It wears grey shoulder-pads with glowing green insides, armbands with glowing green diamonds on the center of all of its sides and a chestplate with a green glowing diamond in the middle, with wiring connecting it to two cross shaped buttons. It wields a grey scythe that glows green which it uses to attack towers.

The **Nuclear Guardian** has a death animation, where it will convulse while emitting sparks and small explosions, before all of its green lights turn dark grey with it subsequently falling backwards. It also plays a bird cawing sound on death.
Strategy: - High DPS towers, such as the Engineer, Ranger, Pursuit and Accelerator are needed to use against this, due to its high health.
- You should also use the Commander to boost these towers' firerate, making them deal more damage to it.
- The Medic is highly recommended so that you can protect towers from stuns caused by the **Nuclear Guardian** from your towers, as it stuns quite frequently.

- You can use defense dropping towers, such as the Golden Pyromancer, Pyromancer, Electroshocker or Toxic Gunner to decrease the **Nuclear Guardian's** defense, allowing your towers to deal more damage to it.
- As freezing towers drop defense when an enemy is frozen or slowed down, they cannot be used as the **Nuclear Guardian** has the Freeze Immunity.
- Freezing towers cannot freeze or slow down the **Nuclear Guardian** due to its Freeze Immunity.
- The Warden and Electroshocker can also only slow it down instead of stunning it while knockback towers like the Brawler cannot knock it back, as it has the Stun Immunity.
- Because of its size, the Warden will only slow it down for a shorter amount of time.
Trivia: - The scythe wielded by the **Nuclear Guardian** is a re-textured version of the Molten Boss' scythe.
- The **Nuclear Guardian's** design is based on the Nuclear Fallen King's design.
- The mask worn by the **Nuclear Guardian** may be a reference to a plague doctor.
- However, unlike a plague doctor, the beak on the mask worn by the **Nuclear Guardian** can open and close.
Update History: - Energy Immunity replaced with Stun Immunity.
- Health decreased from 80,000 to 14,000 in Oops! All slimes!.
- None of the changes are applied to the legacy version.
- **Bug**: Appears twice in the Index, one of them not loading in any model for the preview.
- **Bugfix**: No longer appears twice in the Index.

Description: The **Nuclear Monster** is the final boss of Polluted Wasteland II. It has an extremely high amount of health—exceeding the health of every non-event enemy in-game—but has a very slow speed. It is also immune to being frozen by freezing towers, slowed down by the Toxic Gunner, knocked back, damaged through the Nuke fallout, confused and slowed down by the DJ Booth. Additionally, it can only be slowed down by the Electroshocker and Warden instead of stunned. The **Nuclear Monster** replaces the Fallen King in the Oops! All slimes! challenge.
The **Nuclear Monster** has six abilities:

- The first ability, *Nuclear Summon*, summons multiple random enemies. The modern version is not guaranteed to summon anything, while legacy always summons something. This ability for the modern version summons Splitters, Necromancers, Giant Skeletons, Mutagenic Blights and Rushers. legacy version can spawn the Toxic, Super Toxic, Slime, Circuit, Abomination, Amalgamation, Rusher, Cursed Skeleton, Shadow Boss, Necromancer and Super Mutant. It can only spawn one Abomination, and up to three Amalgamations and Rushers when using the ability, though it cannot summon an Abomination when near the exit.

- The second ability is *Boxing Knockout*, where the **Nuclear Monster** will charge up its right hand and then punch the ground with it, creating a large shockwave that stuns any tower hit by it and deals 500 damage to units.

- The third ability is *Acid Eruption*, where the **Nuclear Monster** will hold its chest and start shaking uncontrollably, shooting out multiple acidic balls onto the map, stunning any tower caught in their radius and dealing 120 damage to units.
- The fourth ability is *Nuclear Beam*, in which **Nuclear Monster** will fire a green energy beam from its chest that stuns any tower caught in it.

- The fifth ability is *Blindly Shooting*, where the **Nuclear Monster** will howl into the air, which decreases the range of all towers by 15% with the Scared Debuff and damages units by 400. This ability is most often performed alongside the *Nuclear Summon* ability.

- The last ability is *Nuclear Meltdown*, a rage mode ability, where the **Nuclear Monster** will stomp three times, use the *Blindly Shooting* ability and then use a random ability. It will then become faster and gain a green outline. Legacy's *Nuclear Summon* ability will also lose the ability to summon Amalgamations, Abominations and Super Toxics.
Appearance: The **Nuclear Monster** is a robotic monster with a bull-shaped mask, green devil horns, green skin and a red head. It has mechanical hands as well as a mechanical bull mask with glowing green horns and eyes. Its torso is cut open, there being a grey robotic heart with a green glowing core, which can be used to fire green beams. It also has grey shoulder-pads, an energy pack on its back and numerous green humanoids sticking out of its body.
The **Nuclear Monster** has a death animation, where it will convulse and emit sparks, before all of its green lights turn a dark grey as it falls to its knees and then forward.
Strategy: - Multiple high DPS towers, such as the Engineer, Accelerator, Pursuit, Golden Minigunner and Turret are needed to eliminate the **Nuclear Monster**.
- The Pursuit is immune to both stuns and debuffs, making it unaffected by all of the **Nuclear Monster's** abilities.
- The Ranger is immune to stuns, making it very useful against the **Nuclear Monster**.
- As the **Nuclear Monster** will apply the Scared Debuff quite often, the Turret can be effective here because of its debuff immunity, though it is not stun immune.
- The Commander and Mercenary Base are highly recommended to boost the firerate and damage of your towers.

- The DJ Booth is extremely useful at increasing your tower's range due to how big the map is, keeping the **Nuclear Monster** in range for longer and partially mitigating the *Blindly Shooting* ability.
- It cannot slow down the **Nuclear Monster** as it is a boss enemy.
- The Medic is extremely useful at shield towers from the stuns caused by the **Nuclear Monster**.
- Do note that the Medic cannot shield towers from the Scared Debuff applied by it.
- Freezing towers like Freezer, Frost Blaster and Sledger can only slow down the **Nuclear Monster** as it is immune to freeze.
- The Toxic Gunner cannot slow down the **Nuclear Monster** as it is immune to its slowing effect.
- The Electroshocker and Warden can slow down the **Nuclear Monster** instead of completely stopping it, though the Warden can only slow it down for a shorter amount of time due to its large size.
- Multiple Electroshockers boosted by the Commander can be somewhat effective at slowing down the **Nuclear Monster** and the enemies it summons.
- The Jester's confusion bombs cannot confuse the **Nuclear Monster**, but it can still slow it down with its ice bombs.
Trivia: - The **Nuclear Monster** has the second most base health out of any other enemy in the entire game, following the Rift Walker.
- However, the **Nuclear Monster** does have the most base health in the game if excluding event enemies.
- The **Nuclear Monster's** theme is a remix of the Nuclear Fallen King's theme.
- The design of the **Nuclear Monster** likely takes inspiration from the Icon Of Sin from *Doom*.
Update History: - **Nuclear Monster** can now only spawn one Abomination, three Amalgamations and Rushers maximum per ability.
- Can no longer summon the Abomination if near the exit.
- **Nuclear Monster** can no longer summon Amalgamations, Abominations and Super Toxics after activating *Nuclear Meltdown*.
- **Bug**: Final wave music does not play.
- **Nuclear Monster** can no longer be confused by the Jester.
- **Nuclear Monster** is now immune to the fallout damage from the Nuke.
- **Nuclear Monster** is now immune to knockback.
- **Bug**: Now spawns the modern Slime instead of the Radioactive Slime.
- Health decreased from 1,500,000 to 750,000 in Oops! All slimes!.
- **Bug**: Can be slowed down by the DJ Booth.
- **Bugfix**: No longer can be slowed down by the DJ Booth.
- **Nuclear Monster** can no longer have its defense dropped.
- None of the changes are applied to the legacy version.
- As it has Bloated, its health is effectively unchanged, as the attribute doubles its health to 1,500,000.
- *Blindly Shooting* Scared Debuff decreased from 50% to 15%.
- Summons are now no longer guaranteed to happen. The amount summoned is also far lower.

Description: The **Null Accelerator**, internally referred to as the **Corrupted Accelerator**, was one of the Boss enemies that appears in Blind Faith as part of the Null & Void Event. It had a high amount of health and an average speed.

The **Null Accelerator** has one ability where it targets two towers, stunning them for 6 seconds. After this stun ends, these two towers have their positions swapped. This attack bypasses all forms of protecting towers from stuns, including the tower being a cliff tower, the tower having Stun Immunity and the tower being shielded by the Medic.
Logbook Description: "*Accelerator watched the creature raise a version of his own particle accelerator, the device hummed loudly. In a flash of purple light, it fired — and suddenly Accelerator found himself standing where Engineer had been. Accelerator's mind couldn't understand. How did the Nil Zone copy something this complex, then change it?*"
Appearance: The **Null Accelerator** is a corrupted recreation of the Level 5 Accelerator. It wears grey body armor which covers most of its body. On its head, it wears a grey and purple hood and a white mask, which has a hole on it. On its back, it has two grey and purple energy canisters. It has purple goo all around its body and a few spikes coming out of its skin. It fires plasma beams using its corrupted right arm.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Blind Faith is listed instead.
- High DPS towers like the Accelerator, Ranger or Pursuit are decent options against the **Null Accelerator**.
- Towers with high range or with range that allows them to be effective when placed anywhere are best options against the **Null Accelerator**. Such towers include the Ranger or Pursuit.

- It is possible to sell and replace all swapped towers so that they are back in their original positions, though due to the **Null Accelerator** appearing multiple times, this is not particularly worthwhile, with the exception of towers reliant on being in a good spot like support towers.

- It is impossible to protect towers from the **Null Accelerator's** stun, as it bypasses all forms of protecting it from them. This includes cliff towers, Stun Immunity towers, Temperance curse and towers shielded by the Medic.
Update History: - **Bug**: Killing the **Null Accelerator** while it is using its ability on two towers will cause the targeted towers to remain stunned until another **Null Accelerator** successfully swaps their places. As them being targeted again is not guaranteed, they may remain permanently stunned.

Description: The **Null Brawler**, internally referred to as the **Corrupted Brawler**, was an enemy that appeared in Blind Faith as part of the Null & Void Event. It had a decent amount of health and an above average speed.

It has one ability, *Distorted Reposition*, where it jumps from one path to another. If there is only one path, it will just slightly behind or in front of itself, landing on the same path. While jumping, it becomes a Flying enemy. Upon landing, it creates a shockwave with a radius of 15, which stuns towers hit by it for 3 seconds and deals 1,500 damage to units. This ability has a range of 30, meaning it will not be performed if the **Null Brawler** has no towers near it.
Logbook Description: "*Brawler ducked under a right hook, slipped left, and drove an uppercut into its stomach. As the creature doubled over, landed a clean shot to its face. Brawler bounced on his toes, rolling his shoulders, and spat to the side. "Felt good, didn't it?" As the creature stood, Brawler could swear the thing was grinding back at him.*"
Appearance: The **Null Brawler** is a corrupted recreation of the Level 5 Brawler. It has purple skin and hair, with parts of its body being covered in purple goo. It wears a red vest, blue overalls and black shoes. On its left arm, it has grey and orange mechanical fists, while on its right, it has purple fingers.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Blind Faith is listed instead.
- High DPS towers like the Accelerator, Turret, Ranger or Engineer can be used to deal with the **Null Brawler**.
- Towers with flying detection can be useful, as they can attack it at all times, though this is not that important as it is only a Flying enemy for a short amount of time.
