Description: The **Null Commander**, internally referred to as the **Corrupted Commander**, was a major boss that appeared in Outpost 16. Serving as its final boss for the first night of the Null & Void Event.
It had three abilities:
- The first ability is *Open Fire*, in which, upon activation, it started shooting towers or units in its range of 30, stunning them for 6 seconds or dealing 200 damage to Units respectively.

- Its second ability, *Call To War*, spawned six Bloated Null Scouts, four Bloated Null Crook Bosses and one Null Pyromancer. All of the summoned enemies will also have their Defense set to 50%, overriding whatever value they were normally set to.
- Its third and final ability is *Summon APCs*, which spawned three Null Missile APCs at one of the entrances.
Logbook Description: "*When the Null Commander emerged from the tear, Commander froze, his weapon lowering at the sight before him. Dispatcher's voice cut through the shock, snapping him back to reality. Commander raised his gun and fired, but the bullets ricocheted off its armor. But when the Null Commander chuckled and raised its radio, Commander's blood ran cold.*"
Appearance: The **Null Commander** is a corrupted recreation of the Commander. It has purple skin and parts of its body appear to have been replaced by mechanical parts. It has one metal eye with a green lens. It wears a black cap with the Paradoxum Games logo on it and also wears a blue jacket. On its right shoulder, it has a grey spiked shoulder-pad. Various purple spikes appear on its body.
The **Null Commander** holds a Desert Eagle in its right hand and a radio in its left hand, both of which are used to perform its abilities.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Outpost 16 is listed instead.
- The **Null Commander** can be taken down quite easily by towers like the Golden Minigunner, Accelerator, Ranger or Pursuit.
- Large numbers of weaker towers, like the Golden Scout, can also defeat it.
- Support towers like the Commander and DJ Booth can be helpful at boosting the statistics of your towers.
- The **Null Commander** is one of the faster boss enemies in the game, making stalling towers useful against it, though as it is a Boss most forms of stalling will not work on it.
- Freezing towers can be useful here as while Boss enemies are immune to the freeze, they only gain a partial immunity to its chillness.
- Similarly, stunning towers like the Electroshocker are useful, as they still get slowed down.
- There are a few curses which can be taken to help take down the **Null Commander**.
- While Temperance does apply Mutation, this will have no effect on the **Null Commander** as it only spawns once. This means the Stun Immunity given to towers can be very helpful here.
- If taken on Wave 20, the Mutation modifier will do nothing as there is no wave past Wave 20, making it only boost rewards by 20%.
- The Chariot can be useful as it boosts the damage and firerate of towers at the final wave.
Trivia: - The **Null Commander's** sound distortion filter was also used for The Maw's chase theme.
- Oddly, on the **Null Commander's** badge and matchmaking renders, it is seen with a green glowing eye, however this never appears in game.
- The **Null Commander** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Bugfix**: **Null Commander** now uses its correct icon.
- **Null Commander** removed from the main game, now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.
- **Bug**: Cannot be spawned in Sandbox mode.
- **Bugfix**: Can now be spawned in Sandbox mode.
Notes: - ↑ Only a Boss in Outpost 16.

When killed, it will press a button that will fire lightning at towers, causing it to hit up to 5 towers and units in its explosion range of 15. This will stun towers for 5 seconds and deal 1,000 damage to units.
Logbook Description: "*The Null Electroshocker emerged crackling with purple energy, voltage surging through his body. He trembled with power, storing massive quantities of it within his body as he prepared to release a destructive burst. Electroshocker's eyes narrowed. Disgusting.*"
Appearance: The **Null Electroshocker** is a corrupted recreation of the Electroshocker. It wears black full body armor with a helmet that has a blue visor, and grey knee-pads. Large parts of its body are covered in purple goo that has blue veins going over it.
On its back, it has a giant tesla coil which it uses to unleash lightning at towers and units.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Banlands and Blind Faith is listed instead.
- High DPS towers like the Accelerator, Engineer and Turret can reliably take multiple of them down due to their mediocre health for where they spawn.
- As they spawn in groups, AOE towers like the Rocketeer and Mortar are extremely effective.
- Its recommended to not put towers near the path to lessen the chance of your towers getting stunned by the **Null Electroshocker** death ability.
- Similarly, high range towers are also helpful as the ability can only stun towers in a specific range, which is easier to not be in if the tower has high range.
- Unstunnable towers like the Ranger and Pursuit can be used to take them out safely and at a long range before they can reach your ground units.
- It is possible to prevent towers from getting stunned in various ways.

- The most reliable method would be choosing the Temperance curse, as it gives every tower stun immunity. Do note however that it comes with Mutation, which severity entirely depends on the wave it was activated on.

- The Medic can be used to shield towers, preventing them from being stunned while it is active. However, do note that **Null Electroshockers** spawn in hordes, meaning it is likely for them to hit one tower more than once.
Trivia: - While its appearance mostly resembles the Level 5 default skin for the Electroshocker, the tesla coil on its back is very similar to the tesla coil used by the **Classic** Electroshocker skin.

It had a high amount of health and a decent amount of Defense, though it walks rather slowly. It has two abilities, both of which used to weaken towers and units.

The first ability is *Attack*, where the **Null Engineer** targets either a tower, which results in it getting stunned for 1 seconds, or a random unit, which leads to it receiving 3,000 damage. The other ability is **Spawn Turret**, where it creates a Null Sentry on the path. This Null Sentry will debuff a random. Both abilities have a range of 20, meaning they will not be used if there is no tower in range.
Logbook Description: "*When the Null Engineer emerged from the tear it caught Engineer's attention. She watched as the creature placed down a turret identical to her own. Engineer's jaw tightened as she pulled down her goggles. "Cheap knockoff," she muttered, goggles guiding her own turret as it whirred to life.*"
Appearance: The **Null Engineer** is a corrupted recreation of the Engineer. It has red skin and grey hair. Its left arm has been replaced with a prosthetic arm. It wears a black shirt, maroon overalls with yellow buttons, grey bandages, black shoes and a black glove. On its head, it wears a red hard hat with goggles on top. On its back, it has a small radio.
With its right arm, it wields a Attack which it uses to stun towers and damage units, while in its left, it holds a wrench used to make Null Sentries.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Blind Faith is listed instead.
- High DPS towers like the Ranger, Pursuit, Turret or Accelerator are recommended to take this down.
- While the **Null Engineer** does stun, this is not a large issue as the stun time is quite low, allowing towers which are not stun immune to still perform decently.

- As the **Null Engineer** initially spawns as a Boss, most forms of stalling are ineffective against it and it cannot have its Defense reduced.
- For all of its future appearances, it only has the Stun Immunity, meaning it cannot be knocked back and stuns will only slow it down.

Logbook Description: "*The Nil Zone's creatures defy all logic. When the God Shard experiment failed, the fabric that separated the Nil Zone tore, allowing it to replicate the Overworld. - Towers with decent DPS like the Golden Scout, Rocketeer, Minigunner and Accelerator are quite decent against the **Null Freezer**.

- Towers which are placed multiple times are especially useful here, as the explosion is quite small. This means only one tower or unit will be hit on average, which hurts low placement towers like Turret or Gatling Gun far more.
- As the **Null Freezer** freezes towers, towers immune to stuns are not immune to its freeze.
- While the Pursuit does have the Freeze Immunity, it does not work and it still gets frozen regardless.

- Units that do not stop moving are quite effective against the **Null Freezer** due to its horrible aim. As it will aim at where it stood originally, it will miss any moving unit, making them basically immune to its attack.
- This makes towers like the Mercenary Base, Military Base and Necromancer useful against it.

- Units that stop to move or are stationary however, are pretty ineffective as they will always be hit by it. Such units include the Rifleman, Biologist plants and Crook Boss goons, though as a lot of them will be spread out rather than stacked in one place, only one will be hit generally.
- Interestingly, It will also target units still in their death animation as long as the actual model has not disappeared yet.
Trivia: - While the **Null Freezer** can actually hit multiple towers or enemies at once, this is extremely unlikely to happen as its size means the units or towers basically have to be standing in one spot.
- The **Null Freezer** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.

abilities.label: Ability 5
abilities.text: **Null Aura** - Upon reaching half of its health, uses a random ability, changes animations and creates an aura with a radius of 12 around itself which gives any tower in it a 15% Firerate Buff. Lasts for as long as the tower is in its range.

Description: The **Null Guardian** was a major boss that appeared in Banlands. Served as its final boss for the second night of the Null & Void Event. It had far higher health than the Null Commander and only walked slightly slower than it. It also had the Stun Immunity.
The **Null Guardian** had four abilities.
- The first ability, *Cosmic Spear*, made it rain down comets on towers and units. This targeted up to 10 towers and units, stunning any hit for 2 second or dealing 1,500 damage to it.
- The second ability, *Null Bubble*, had it form a bubble of void around a tower. This applied a 25% Range Debuff to any tower inside of it.
- The third ability, *Summon Clones*, had it summoned three Null Guardian Clones.
- The fourth ability, *Lane Switch*, had it teleport to the adjacent path.

- The last ability, *Null Aura*, which happened when it reaches half of its health. This made it slam the ground, changing its animations and creating an aura with a radius of 12. This aura will apply a 15% Firerate Buff to any tower with it, as long as the tower is in the visible circle. This can stack with other Firerate Buffs.
Logbook Description: "*The Null Guardian has existed within the Nil Zone since before the Old World, appointed to this role by the Rift Walker himself. He patrols endlessly, destroying any who enter the "Place Between Realms". The Guardian is connected to the chaotic energy of the Nil Zone, allowing him to perceive and experience the realm's history within it.*"
Appearance: The **Null Guardian** is a heavily armored entity with black skin and purple eyes. Its armor consists of a chestplate, helmet, shoulder-pads leggings and arm armor, with only certain parts of its body like its face being exposed. On its hands, it has a few fingers with electricity coming out of them. In the middle of its torso, it has a ball of dark energy that has purple lightning around it.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Banlands is listed instead.
- The **Null Guardian** can be taken down quite effectively by towers like the Golden Minigunner, Accelerator, Ranger or Pursuit.
- Support towers like the Commander and DJ Booth can be helpful at boosting the statistics of your towers.
- The **Null Guardian** summons in three Null Guardian Clones which have a high amount of health.

- While they are clones, they do not keep the **Null Guardian's** Boss attribute. This means they are more prone to various effects in the game. This makes the Hacker useful here, as it can convert these clones into friendly clones.
- The **Null Guardian** is one of the faster boss enemies in the game, making stalling towers useful against it, though as it is a Boss most forms of stalling will not work on it.
- Freezing towers can be useful here as while Boss enemies are immune to the freeze, they only gain a partial immunity to its chillness.
- Similarly, stunning towers like the Electroshocker are useful, as they still get slowed down.
- There are a few curses which can be taken to help take down the **Null Guardian**.
- While Temperance does apply Mutation, this will have no effect on the **Null Guardian** as it only spawns once. This means the Stun Immunity given to towers can be very helpful here.
- If taken on Wave 25, the Mutation modifier will do nothing as there is no wave past Wave 25, making it only boost rewards by 20%.
- The Chariot can be useful as it boosts the damage and firerate of towers at the final wave.
Update History: - **Bug**: **Null Guardian's** model does not load in the Index.
- **Bug**: **Null Guardian's** Logbook description is completely empty.
- **Bug**: **Null Guardian** gives towers a Firerate Buff when using the Null Aura ability.
- Speed decreased from Slightly Slow (2) to Slow (1.8).
- Null Guardian Clones no longer receive Aggro from the **Null Guardian** when summoned.
- **Bugfix**: **Null Guardian** now uses its correct icon.
- **Bugfix**: **Null Guardian** now has a Logbook description.

- **Bugfix**: Can now be spawned in Sandbox mode.

abilities.text: **Corrupted Heal** – Stops moving, giving it a Defense of 100% and proceeds to start healing every enemy in its range of 30 for 6 seconds. This will increase health of each affected enemy by 150 every 0.2 seconds.

Description: The **Null Medic**, internally referred to as **Corrupted Medic**, was a support enemy that appeared in Banlands and Blind Faith as part of the Null & Void Event. It had a decent amount of health and an above average speed. While it was using its ability, it also gained 100% Defense, effectively doubling its health against most damage sources.

It had one ability, *Corrupted Heal*, where it stopped moving which gave it a Defense of 100%. While standing still, it will begin to heal enemies, including itself, by 150 health every 0.2 seconds for 6 seconds.
Logbook Description: **Variant 1**

"*As enemies flooded through the tear, Null Medic followed. Her healing beam flickered with the unstable energy of the Nil Zone. The original Medic couldn't help but smile creepily, the thought of dissecting it crossing her mind. Medic couldn't help but notice every detail down to the scars that mirrored her own.*"
**Variant 2**

"*As enemies flooded through the tear, Null Medic followed. Her healing beam flickered with the unstable energy of the Nil Zone. The original Medic stood terrified, watching her reflection stumble forward healing the creatures before it. Medic couldn't help but notice every detail down to the scars that mirrored her own.*"
Appearance: The **Null Medic** is a corrupted recreation of the Medic. It has dark purple skin and white hair. It wears a purple coat, grey shoes, purple gloves and torn purple pants. It has purple goo covering its right arm, which on some spots has neon pink balls and blue spikes. It holds a medi gun, which it uses to heal itself and other enemies.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Banlands and Blind Faith is listed instead.
- Having rather high health, ability to heal itself and a Defense of 100% when healing enemies, towers like the Accelerator, Engineer or Turret are recommended against this.

- Due to its slow speed and it stopping to heal enemies, it will often end up at the end of hordes. Therefore, it is possible to set towers to target the last enemy, making it far more likely for them to target it.

- As the **Null Medic** always spawns alongside other enemies, it is possible to use AOE towers like the Rocketeer or Mortar to take down both the **Null Medic** and the enemies it is healing at once.

- As the **Null Medic** is immune to freeze and stun, it is far harder to slow down, though as the **Null Medic** itself is not a threat but instead its healing, stalling it would have very little effect.
Trivia: - When converted by the Hacker, the **Null Medic** will continue using its ability every few seconds. However, rather than targeting enemies, it will begin targeting units instead.
- This does not appear to actually boost the health of targeted units.
- Unlike the Field Medic, it can target non humanoid units like the Railgun Tank.
- The **Null Medic** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Bug**: **Null Medic** has a broken idle animation.
- **Bug**: Ability healing tick is not affected by Time Scale.
- Health decreased from 3,500 to 1,750 in Easy difficulty.
- **Bugfix**: **Null Medic** now uses its correct icon.

Description: The **Null Runner** was the first enemy that appeared in Outpost 16, Banlands and Blind Faith as part of the Null & Void Event. It had lower health than the Nulling but it was far faster than it.
Logbook Description: "*Null Runners are quick enemies that can scale most surfaces with their strong grip and claws. They hunt methodically, stalking their prey and wearing them down to exhaustion. These creatures often tease the weaker Nullings, at least until a Null Dredge shows up.*"
Appearance: The **Null Runner** is a thin, purple enemy. Tendrils sprout from its body, with a slightly more saturated color. It has an exposed set of teeth, which are slightly yellowed. Its joints are slightly more saturated - with them being its elbows, knees and midsection. It has a dome-like head, with no eyes and small horns.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Outpost 16, Banlands and Blind Faith is listed instead.
- The **Null Runner** is quite weak, meaning most early-game towers can handle it.
- Single target towers like the Golden Scout, Militant or Cowboy can be used.
- AOE towers like the Toxic Gunner, Rocketeer, Military Base or Mortar can clear these out quite well, as it generally spawns in hordes.
- Later on, the **Null Runner** becomes rather weak, meaning most towers should be capable of defeating them, including late-game towers like the Accelerator, Pursuit or Golden Minigunner.
Trivia: - The **Null Runner** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Bug**: **Null Runner** is positioned sideways in the Index.
- **Bugfix**: **Null Runner** is now properly positioned in the Index.
- **Bugfix**: **Null Runner** now uses its correct icon.
- **Null Runner** removed from the main game, now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.
- **Bug**: Cannot be spawned in Sandbox mode.
- **Bugfix**: Can now be spawned in Sandbox mode.

Description: The **Null Scout**, internally referred to as **Corrupted Scout**, was an enemy that appeared in Outpost 16, Banlands and Blind Faith as part of the Null & Void Event. It had higher health than every enemy that appeared before it while also being faster than every enemy except the Null Runner.
It can be spawned by the Null Commander, which boosts its Defense to 50%.
Logbook Description: "*Scout stared down the Null Scout, and the creature stared back. Scout lifted one arm, and so it mirrored. He lifted the other — Null Scout followed. Scout quickly dropped both arms and aimed his weapons at the creature, who copied it. Then from the side, Trapper threw a landmine behind the Null Scout. Scout grinned, and stepped back — ... and Null Scout followed.*"
Appearance: The **Null Scout** is a corrupted recreation of the Scout. It has light pink skin, torn black shirt and pants, and a single knee-pad. It has a few bandages wrapped around its hands. On its head, it wears a black cap and headphones, alongside cracked shades. Its entire body is covered in what appeared to be purple goo.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Outpost 16, Banlands and Blind Faith is listed instead.
- The **Null Scout** is significantly stronger than every enemy that appeared before it, making it quite tough.
- A few tower which worked on previous enemies, like the Golden Scout, Rocketeer, Military Base or Cowboy can be used to deal with this.
- As it is quite fast, stalling towers like the Freezer, Electroshocker or Toxic Gunner can be helpful here.
- Do note that when it first spawns, it is a Boss, limiting how many towers can stall it, and it always spawns with the Stun Immunity, meaning it cannot be knocked back and stuns only slow it down.
- Most stalling towers are also capable of reducing its Defense, though as it is rather low this will have minimal impact on the damage it receives.
Trivia: - The **Null Scout** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Bug**: **Null Scout** no longer has animation variants.
- **Bugfix**: **Null Scout** now uses its correct icon.
- **Null Scout** removed from the main game, now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.
- **Bug**: Cannot be spawned in Sandbox mode.
- **Bugfix**: Can now be spawned in Sandbox mode.
Notes: - ↑ Only the first **Null Scout** spawned in Outpost 16 as a boss.

Description: The **Null Sentry**, internally referred to as the **Corrupted Sentry**, was an enemy that does not appear naturally, as it can only be spawned by the Null Engineer in the Null & Void Event. It had a low amount of health, a high Defense and it cannot move. It can however, debuff a random tower, making it fire slower.
Logbook Description: "*The Null Sentry was created using the schematics stolen from Engineer. After the Nil Zone tore through the realm, it replicated her and created Null Engineer. Unlike traditional materials, Null Sentries are created out of condensed energy, which can be materialized by its creator.*"
Appearance: The **Null Sentry** is a corrupted recreation of the War Machine Sentry. It has four legs, a minigun and two missile launchers. It is colored red and black.
Mutation: Assumes that Mutation is activated and a **Gravestone** is created on the earliest wave possible of the Hard difficulty.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Blind Faith is listed instead.
- The **Null Sentry** itself is not that large of a threat, as it can only affect one tower at a time in a limited range, while also not being capable of actually reaching the exit.
- It can, however, be annoying to take out, as it will usually not be possible to be targeted by most targeting options.
- The Commander can be used to partially mitigate its debuff.
Trivia: - The **Null Sentry** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.

Description: The **Null Shrieker** was a Flying enemy that appeared in Banlands and Blind Faith as part of the Null & Void Event. It had a decent amount of health and speed. As it was a Flying enemy, only towers with flying detection can target it.
Logbook Description: "*The Null Shrieker is a flying enemy within the Nil Zone. Despite its blindness, it navigates by relying on sound to locate its prey. The bandages that cover its eyes are believed to be self-inflicted, as if the creature chose to blind itself.*"
Appearance: The **Null Shrieker** appearance resembles that of a giant bat, with purple fur, sharp teeth along with claws on its legs and arms, bat wings and pointy ears. It has an orange blindfold covering its eyes.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Banlands and Blind Faith is listed instead.
- Cheap early-game towers with flying detection like Golden Soldier, Engineer and Crook Boss along with its goons can be used to take them down comfortably.
- Later on, towers like the Pursuit or Ranger can also be used to deal with them.
- You can use the Firework Technician to give all towers within its range flying detection, making **Null Shrieker** easier to kill.
- Similarly, The Sun curse also gives all your towers to detect it but at the cost of it having all immunities, making it slightly harder to slow down.
- As the **Null Shrieker** is quite fast and on some waves spawn as Nimble, stalling towers can be useful against it.

- Due to it being a Flying enemy, not only does that mean the tower has to be able to detect it, but some that do cannot stall it at all. This heavily limits potential stalling options. One tower which can be used is the Electroshocker.
Trivia: - The **Null Shrieker** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Bugfix**: **Null Shrieker** now uses its correct icon.
- **Null Shrieker** removed from the main game, now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.
- **Bug**: Cannot be spawned in Sandbox mode.
- **Bugfix**: Can now be spawned in Sandbox mode.

Description: The **Null Warden**, internally referred to as the **Corrupted Warden**, was a tanky enemy that appeared in Outpost 16, Banlands and Blind Faith as part of the Null & Void Event. It had a high amount of health, higher than every enemy except the Null Commander, and a decently fast speed.
In the Hard difficulty of Outpost 16, it always spawned with Lead, meaning towers needed lead detection to be able to damage it.
Logbook Description: "*As the Null Warden crawled from the rift, the original tightened his gear and flicked out his baton. Warden glared at it from behind his visor. "Man you are ugly." he muttered. The Null Warden ran forward, slowed by the gear it wore. Warden planted his feet and raised his shield. "I don't know if I should feel insulted."*"
Appearance: The **Null Warden** is a corrupted recreation of the Warden. It has purple skin. It wears purple clothes, black vest, black helmet with a visor, knee-pads and gloves. What appears to be purple goo can be seen all over its body. A few pink spores can also be seen on it.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Outpost 16, Banlands and Blind Faith is listed instead.
- Towers with decent DPS, like the Golden Scout, Accelerator, Rocketeer, Ranger or Pursuit are recommended here.
- While not an issue in Easy difficulty, it is recommended that the towers brought in have lead detection, as in the Hard difficulty it always spawn as a Lead enemy.
- There are a few ways to give towers lead detection in case none of the towers brought in have it.
- The Firework Technician can be used to give all towers lead detection at the start of the wave.
- The Sun can be used to give every tower all detections, though it comes with the downside of making every enemy immune to stuns, freeze and burn.
Trivia: - The **Null Warden** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Bugfix**: **Null Warden** now uses its correct icon.
- **Null Warden** removed from the main game, now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.
- **Bug**: Cannot be spawned in Sandbox mode.

Description: The **Odd** is an early-game enemy that appears in Hardcore and Voidcore modes. It has decent health and above average speed.
Logbook Description: "*The Odd are people who have succumbed to the Void. They are considered a blank slate, something the Void Caster can build off of to create other variations of soldiers for her army. Many of the Odd were from realms the Void had fully consumed. They aren’t particularly special, but when they’re not preserved by Void Caster’s song, they ‘enjoy’ wandering cluelessly about the Void. Like souls seeking passage into the spirit world.*"
Appearance: The **Odd** has white skin, purple torso and purple legs. It has purple veins on its body. It has three walking animations it can choose from.
Strategy: - Decently strong early-game towers like the Engineer, Golden Soldier, Ace Pilot or Golden Scout can fare well against the **Odd**.
- Towers that can damage multiple enemies at once, like the Golden Pyromancer and Electroshocker, are effective at dealing with groups of **Odds**.
- While not necessary, it may be ideal to let **Odds** enter the base while upgrading Farms. However, you should not rely solely on your base health.
Trivia: - The **Odd** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Odd** now appears in Nil Zone II as part of the Halloween 2026 Live Events.
- **Odd** no longer spawns in Nil Zone II, as the Halloween 2026 Live Event has ended.

Description: The **Operator Ducky** is an enemy that appears in Bathroom Approach as part of the Ducky Revenge Event and its rerun in the Spring Frenzy Battle Pass. It has decent health and an above average speed. Upon reaching 60% of its health, it activates its *Operative Service* ability, which spawns an Aggro and Bloated Agent Ducky. It also turns it into a Hidden enemy for 20 seconds, briefly limiting the amount of towers you can use against it. Hidden disappearing after 20 seconds also happens if the **Operator Ducky** initially spawned as Hidden.
Logbook Description: "*Operator Ducky is a dedicated "War Head" who eats grenades for breakfast and military tactics for lunch. Their idea of a relaxation is planning elaborate military operations while wearing full military gear. Many of the ducks believe he's LARPing as his hand-eye coordination is as bad as Missile Ducky's inability to not blow something up.*"
Appearance: The **Operator Ducky** is regular, yellow duck with black eyes, an orange beak and flippers. It is a part of the Duck Army, meaning it wears appropriate military attire, which consists of a grey cap, headphones and headset. It has three animations that it can randomly have, where all three also have differently shaped eyes. The first animation has it have a happy expression, the second has it have a serious expression while the third one has its eyes partially closed, likely because it is scared.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Bathroom Approach is listed instead.
- As the **Operator Ducky** can become Hidden, towers such as the Golden Crook Boss, Accelerator, Turret and Golden Minigunner are good choices against the **Operator Ducky**.

- Towers without hidden detection, like the top path Pursuit, Ranger or Mortar can also be used to attack it before it turns Hidden or when it loses Hidden, though they should generally not be relied on.
- Do note that the Agent Ducky that it spawns is not Hidden, meaning towers without hidden detection can still indirectly attack the **Operator Ducky** while it is Hidden.
Trivia: - The **Operator Ducky** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Bug**: **Operator Ducky** clips into the ground when made larger or smaller.

Description: The **Operator Ducky** was an enemy that appeared exclusively in D00M's Revenge as part of the Duck Hunt Event. Currently, it can be spawned again in Sandbox mode. It had high health and an above average speed. When attacked in its non-Hidden state, it spawns three Agent Duckies with its *Secret Service* ability, which could stun towers. It also briefly turns it into a Hidden and Ghost enemy, limiting the amount of towers you could use against it, and also halves its speed. It lost its Hidden and Ghost attributes and the speed was reverted back to normal shortly after. Beyond wave 20, its health would increase over time.
Appearance: The **Operator Ducky** is a black duck with black eyes, grey feet and an orange beak. It wears black translucent shades, cap and vest. When the *Secret Service* ability is activated, it briefly becomes entirely translucent and gains a red exclamation point above its head.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in D00M's Revenge is listed instead.
- The **Operator Ducky** can spawn multiple Agent Duckies if not dealt with quickly.
- Towers like the Minigunner and Accelerator can be used to deal with **Operator Ducky** and the Agent Duckies it spawns.

- The Ranger can also be used as the **Operator Ducky** does not immediately have the hidden and ghost immunities. At Level 3, it will be able to kill it in one shot before it can use its *Secret Service* ability.
- You can also use the Commander to decrease the firerate of these towers.
- The Medic can be used to cleanse stuns from towers stunned by the Agent Duckies that the **Operator Ducky** spawns.
- A Level 5 Pursuit can be used to wipe out multiple **Operator Duckies** and Agent Duckies easily, but do note that the Pursuit may lock onto a different enemy.
- The Pursuit's missiles can be quite useful as they can deal damage to both the **Operator Ducky** and Agent Duckies at the same time.
Trivia: - The red exclamation point that appeared over the **Operator Ducky** during the *Secret Service* ability is a reference to the exclamation point from the *Metal Gear* series.
Update History: - **Operator Ducky** can now be summoned in Sandbox mode, only when the player has the Operator Ducky's Logbook from the Ducky Revenge Event.
- **Bug**: No longer turns opaque 10 seconds after using its *Secret Service* ability.

Description: **P3NGU** was an enemy that appeared in Bathroom Approach as part of the Ducky Revenge Event and its rerun in the Spring Frenzy Battle Pass. It has a high amount of health and 30% Defense, but it walks rather slowly.

**P3NGU** has one ability, *Beak Beam*, where it will attack a tower with a laser fired from its beak. This laser will attack the targeted tower, stunning it and any other nearby tower in its attack cone for 4 seconds while also dealing 20 damage to units per tick. This ability has a tick of 0.1 and a range of 15.
Logbook Description: "*P3NGU is the latest addition to Nerd Duck's inventions. Powered by cutting-edge bird technology, Nerd Duck based it on a flightless bird concept; something that's completely impossible. After all, a creature that waddles and can't fly couldn't possibly exist, right?*"
Appearance: **P3NGU** is a regular penguin turned into a mech, with the only parts of its body not being entirely covered with mechanical parts being its torso and wings. On its mechanical head, it had giant, neon red eyes, and on its torso, it has a neon red light. All of its mechanical parts are connected to its body with giant screws. **P3NGU** also has a large metal jetpack on its back.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Bathroom Approach is listed instead.
- High DPS towers like the Pursuit, Crook Boss, Golden Minigunner, Ranger or Turret can be used to kill **P3NGU**.
- As **P3NGU** can stun towers, stun immune towers like the Ranger or Pursuit are useful here, as they cannot be stunned by it.
- The Commander and DJ Booth can be used to boost the DPS of these towers.
- Defense reducing towers like the Pyromancer, Electroshocker or Freezer can be used to reduce its defense.
- Do note that, on certain waves, **P3NGU** is a Freeze Immune enemy. This means freezing towers will be unable to reduce its defense.
- As for most waves, **P3NGU** does not have any stalling immunities, some of these towers can be used to also stall them.
Trivia: - A "*Noot noot!*" sound can be heard once the **P3NGU** stops firing, which is a reference to Pingu.
- The **P3NGU** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Bug**: **P3NGU** clips into the ground when made larger or smaller.
- **Bug**: **P3NGU** cannot have its defense dropped by the Jester.
- **Bug**: **P3NGU's** head does not move with its body in the Index.
- **P3NGU** removed from the main game, now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.
- **Bug**: **P3NGU** breaks when targeting towers, causing it to get stuck.
- **P3NGU** re-added to the main game, now appears in Bathroom Approach.
- Health decreased from 7,000 to 2,500 in Easy difficulty.
- Health decreased from 10,000 to 5,000 in Hard difficulty.
- Cash given increased from $875 to $2,187 on death in Easy difficulty.
- Cash given increased from $1,000 to $2,187 on death in Hard difficulty.
- **Bugfix**: **P3NGU** no longer breaks when targeting towers.
- **Bugfix**: No longer clips into the ground when made larger or smaller.
- **P3NGU** removed from the main game, now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.

Description: **P3NGU** was an enemy that appeared exclusively in D00M's Revenge as part of the Duck Hunt Event. Currently, it can be spawned again in Sandbox mode. It had a very high amount of health compared to all other enemies in the event except Ducky D00M, and a slightly slow speed. It spawns in the sky, falling down onto one of the plots, during which it was a Flying enemy, which meant towers needed flying detection to attack it. When it got re-added in Sandbox mode, it was changed so that it also spawns in with the Stun Immunity. It lost its attributes after it landed. Unlike most other enemies in D00M's Revenge, it did not head to the exit, but instead walked on the plots. Beyond wave 20, its health would increase over time.

**P3NGU** had one ability, *Beak-A-Beam*. The ability makes it scream and fire a red laser from its beak at towers, which stuns any towers hit. Uniquely, most of the time, **P3NGU** could not decrease your base health. Rather, it stunned towers so that other enemies would have an easier time getting to the exit. This was not the case if it spawned on Wave ???, where it would act like any other enemy and head directly to the exit.
Three **P3NGUs** were spawned by Ducky D00M after it initiated its *Rage Mode* ability.
Appearance: **P3NGU** is a giant penguin covered in metal armor. Its torso and wings are black, and the front of its torso was white. Its legs, feet, lower torso, chest, face, upper arms, head and beak were covered in grey metal armor, which in turn have multiple screws and bolts on them. It also has rocket boosters built into its feet. In its beak, there is a laser that can fire a red laser which stuns towers. Its eyes and the inside of its beak are neon orange. When spawning, it slowly descends from the sky, with rocket boosters at its feet slowing its descent.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in D00M's Revenge is listed instead.
- While **P3NGU** cannot damage your base health, it can stun your towers, allowing other enemies to slip past and enter the exit.
- This, however, is not the case if it spawns on wave ???.
- Because of this, the Medic is recommended to cleanse stunned towers.

- Due to how often **P3NGU** uses its *Beak-A-Beam* ability, and that later on multiple **P3NGUs** spawn, you may need multiple Medics. One sole Medic may not be enough as *Beak-A-Beam* can be performed more often than a single Medic's ability.
- High range towers, such as a Level 3 Ranger, can be used to deal with **P3NGU**, as it can keep **P3NGU** in its range for longer.
- You should set your Rangers to *Strongest* so that they do not attack weaker enemies.
- High DPS towers like the Minigunner and Accelerator are recommended against this.
- You can also use the Commander and DJ Booth to boost their firerate and range respectively.
- The Pursuit can be useful against this, as it cannot be stunned by **P3NGU's** *Beak-A-Beam* ability.
- Do note that the Pursuit might be locked onto other enemies when **P3NGU** appears.

- While **P3NGU** can be slowed down by slowing towers, such as the Sledger, Toxic Gunner and Electroshocker, since it cannot reach the center (outside of wave ???) and that freezing or stunning it cannot stall its *Beak-A-Beam* ability, doing this has no practical use.
Trivia: - **P3NGU** is based on the P3NG-W1N from *R2DA*.
- Its *Beak-A-Beam* ability is also similar to P3NG-W1N's *Beak Beam*.
- The name *P3NGU* is similar to the TV show name Pingu, originally broadcast for Swiss television, then later British television.
- When **P3NGU** was first shown on Paradoxum Games X, it was called *P3NGWIN* instead of *P3NGU*.

- If you are on wave ??? for about half an hour, the game will begin to only spawn **P3NGUs**. Rather than them landing on the plots and walking on them, they will act like every other enemy, spawning in the outer area and heading to the exit. You are guaranteed to lose when this happens due to their high health and numbers, so it is pointless to try to defend.
- This is the only time where **P3NGU** can damage the base.
- Its *Beak-A-Beam* ability's hitbox is slightly shorter than what the laser displays.

- Sometimes when **P3NGU** spawned, it could not be attacked by any tower until it landed, even if they had flying detection. Additionally, **P3NGU** at times could spawn without Flying, only gaining it shortly after spawning, which allowed towers without flying detection to attack it.
Update History: - **Bug**: **P3NGU** never stops firing its beam when the *Beak-A-Beam* ability is used.
- **Bugfix**: **P3NGU** no longer uses its *Beak-A-Beam* ability forever.
- **P3NGU** can now be summoned in Sandbox mode, only when the player has the P3NGU's Logbook from the Ducky Revenge Event.
- Now spawns with the Stun Immunity, which is lost upon landing.
- **Bug**: **P3NGU** has a broken icon in Sandbox.
Notes: - ↑ Beyond wave 20, **P3NGU** scaled its health with time.

Description: The **Packed Ice** was an enemy that appeared exclusively in Outpost 32 as part of the Frost Invasion Event. Currently, it can be only spawned in Sandbox mode. Compared to the Snowy, the **Packed Ice** had much more health with slower speed. It also had 25% defense which reduced most forms of damage.
Upon its death, the Frost Mystery had a chance to spawn the **Packed Ice**, from wave 11 onwards.
Appearance: The **Packed Ice** has a sky blue skin. It has light blue torso and legs. The **Packed Ice** has a hole in its torso, exposing its dark blue heart. It is faceless and slightly larger than the Frozen.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Outpost 32 is listed instead.
- Use towers with high DPS while being economical in cost, like several Level 2 Minigunners or a Level 0 Accelerator, to deal with the **Packed Ice** when it initially spawns.
- A single Level 5 Swarmer can easily handle the **Packed Ice**, despite the fact that it has 25% defense.
- You can use a Level 2 Pyromancer to cut 50% of the **Packed Ice's** defense.
- Additionally, as with all enemies in the Frost Invasion Event, the Pyromancer deals double fire damage to the **Packed Ice** (though normal damage is not doubled).
- You can also use other defense dropping towers, like the Electroshocker or Freezer. However, these are more expensive and less effective as they only drop 20% defense.
- Defense is ignored by splash damage, meaning that towers and units that deal splash damage will deal 100% damage if the **Packed Ice** is caught in the epicenter.
- This makes towers like the Rocketeer and Mortar very useful against the **Packed Ice**.
- Upon collision, units, like the Railgun Tank, will ignore defense and deal full collision damage towards the **Packed Ice**.

Description: The **Painter** was an enemy that is an enemy that appeared in The Narratorium as a part of The Final Act Event. It had a decently high amount of health and an average speed.

The **Painter** has two abilities. The first ability is *Summon*, which makes it summon different enemies. These enemies can be Actor1 (60% chance), Actor2 (30% chance) and Actor3 (10% chance). The second ability is *Paint Splatter* which makes it splatter paint on a tower, which on impact causes it to fly in four different directions, creating a cross. Any tower hit will receive a 33% Scared Debuff for 8 seconds, while units receive 1,600 damage. This ability has a spread radius of 15.
Logbook Description: "*The Painters are known for being the actual legends in their field. When they are around, things just become cooler. The Producer would run to Narrator and tell him, 'Honey, we have guests. Bring out the fine paintings.'*"
Appearance: The **Painter** is an object-headed robot with an easel for a head. This easel has a canvas with three possible faces that can appear. It has a grey body, green shirt, blue pants, grey shoes and a black vest. It has two paint cans on its back and a paint brush in its right hand.
Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in The Narratorium is listed instead.
- Due to their late debut, **Painters** usually are not all too threatening with their relatively slow speed. However, be aware of the various actors they summon through their *Summon* ability.
- As one of the Actors summoned has Splash Damage Immunity, explosive towers are not always the best choice, though are still quite effective.
- While usually not problematic, **Painters** still have decently high health and appear in small groups, so your typical high damage towers will have to deal with them.
- Accelerator, Golden Minigunner, and Ranger are all more than enough to handle them alone, especially when paired with other towers or each other.
Trivia: - The final sentence of the Logbook description is a bring out the fine china meme.
- The faces seen on the enemy are also used on a version of this meme containing mugs and plates containing these three faces, meaning these two references are likely connected.
- All the faces the **Painter** can have are Roblox faces which became memes. These can be the The Winning Smile, Man Face and Woman Face
- In the Spotlight's Logbook entry, they are referred to as the *Painter Men*.
Update History: - **Painter** removed from the main game, now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.

It then gets back up, screams and raises its hands, making it temporarily regenerate 75 health every 0.1 seconds. It also gets 60% faster and makes red veins appear on its right arm, face and left leg.

Description: **Patient Zero** is the final boss of Intermediate mode. It also appears in The Takeover Event. It has a high amount of health but moves quite slowly. It has multiple immunities, making it immune to being frozen, stunned by stunning towers, slowed down by the Toxic Gunner, confused by the Jester, set on fire by towers like the Pyromancer, knocked back, slowed down by the DJ Booth, damaged by the Nuke's fallout damage or have its defense dropped, though some of these are only applied in Intermediate mode.
**Patient Zero** has multiple abilities:

- The first ability, *Stomp*, makes it jump into the air, temporarily becoming a Flying enemy, and hit the ground with its fist while landing, stunning towers for 5 seconds and dealing 400 damage to units in a wide range.
- The second ability is *Enemy Spawn*, where it spawns five enemies. These can be the Living Experiment, Boomer, Ghoul or Speedy Boss.
- The third ability is *Flask*, where it throws multiple blue potions on the path, that heal any enemy, including itself, by 10 health every 0.1 seconds.

- Its fourth ability, *Toxic*, makes it fire out multiple toxic orbs that apply a 60% Firerate Debuff (150% increase) on towers for 10-15 seconds. As units cannot have their firerate slowed down, they receive 400 damage for each orb they got hit by instead.

- Its fifth and final ability is *Index Case*, which is rage mode. Upon reaching half of its default health, which is the one seen in the Index and Sandbox mode (50,000), it will crouch down to the ground and raise its arm, gaining a temporary passive 75 health regeneration every 0.1 seconds, faster speed and red veins on its right arm, face and left leg.
Appearance: **Patient Zero** is a large humanoid with a waist, lower arms and lower legs in its rig. It has a light purple skin color, a white lab coat with a purple hexagon pattern accent and collar and a glowing green core at the middle of its chest, torn navy blue pants and grey boots. Its right hand is bionic, with glowing green wires attached and a large sickly purple and light blue arm with three fingers and a blaster in the palm of its hand. Its legs are whitish purple.

It has glowing green eyes, a large grin, white hair and glowing green goggles on its forehead. These goggles will flip down when it performs the *Toxic* ability. It also has a yellow nametag, which displays its old, more human appearance. It also wears a large, high-tech metal backpack. When the *Index Case* ability activates, it will gain glowing red veins on its right forearm, legs and head, as well as red particles at the ends of its limbs. The ability activation also makes **Patient Zero** shake the screen whenever it takes a step.

**Patient Zero** has a death animation, where it will flex its right arm, quickly spin around and then fall forward. It also plays a growling sound with a thump when it hits the floor during the death animation.
Strategy: - Towers with decent DPS, like the Militant, Brawler, Ace Pilot or Military Base can be used to deal with it, though proper late-game towers like the Crook Boss, Hunter or Minigunner can also be used.
- Support towers like the Commander, Medic and DJ Booth can be useful at boosting the statistics of these towers.
- The Commander can be useful at partially mitigating the Firerate Debuff applied by **Patient Zero**.
- The Medic can be used to shield towers from its debuffs, though it cannot protect them from the Firerate Debuff it applies.
- Due to its high number of immunities, most stalling towers are ineffective against it.

- The only towers capable of slowing down **Patient Zero** are stunning towers like the Electroshocker and Trapper, though due to its Stun Immunity they will only be able to slow it down instead of stunning it.
Trivia: - **Patient Zero**, and by extension, Intermediate mode, were originally teased through a silhouette in September of 2023 in an update forecast, being stated to release by early November of 2023.
- Prior to the 18th of May 2024, **Patient Zero's** grin was the Toon Face: Villain Smile from the Roblox catalog.
- This made it the first enemy to use dynamic heads.
- The current smile it uses appeared on all renders and promotional material at the time, however.
- **Patient Zero** is the first enemy that can target units using abilities.
- **Patient Zero** appears to be a German speaker (and possibly of German origin) according to the Intermediate mode trailer.
- **Patient Zero** said one line in German that being "Jetzt ist es an mir, die Menschheit auszulöschen!".
- Said line translates to "Now it's my turn to wipe out humanity!".
- This is the first time a non-event enemy is seen speaking.
- This is the first time someone is seen speaking a language other than English in promotional videos and trailers.
- **Patient Zero's** name comes from the noun "patient zero", used to identify the first known individual to carry a disease on an outbreak.

- **Patient Zero** is the second enemy to shake the screen without the use on ability, with the first being the Dummy Boss, which shakes the screen whenever one of its fists makes contact with the ground.

Description: The **Penumbras** was the final boss of the third night in the Solar Eclipse Event. It had a large amount of health and a very slow speed.

It had two abilities. Its first ability was *Solar Spawn*, which spawned five to eight random enemies. These could be the Cursed Guard, Cursed Knight, Lunar Shard or Solar Shard. Its second ability, *Shard Toss*, made the **Penumbras** throw shards at towers, creating an explosion, stunning towers caught on him.
Appearance: The **Penumbras** had purple skin and horns. It had three pink glowing eyes. Its arms were neon pink. It wore purple and grey shoulder-pads, chestplate and leggings. It had pink vines around its arms. It also had two floating objects shaped like a penumbra above its head. It floated slightly above the ground.
Strategy: - High DPS towers, such as the Accelerator, Ranger, Turret and **Golden** Minigunner are recommended to defeat this enemy.
- You can also use the Commander and DJ Booth to help boost the firerate and range of these towers respectively.
- The **Penumbras** can spawn multiple enemies with its ability; however, they were quite weak at that point in the game.
- Towers that deal splash damage, such as the Mortar or Pursuit, can be useful against them.
Trivia: - The **Penumbras** appears to have feelings for The Umbra, as suggested by its dialogue.

- The **Penumbras'** name comes from the word "penumbra", which is the outer shadow of any opaque object. When an eclipse happens, the celestial body caught within the penumbra of the overlapping object, causing a partial eclipse.
- It has a penumbra for a floating head piece.
- A younger **Penumbras** can be seen in cutscenes in A Dark Tale during the Lunar Overture Event.

Description: The **Phantom** is a Hidden enemy that appears in Hardcore and Voidcore modes. It has decent health and decent speed. As it is a Hidden enemy, towers need hidden detection to target it.
Logbook Description: "*Phantoms exist as those who died within the Void. Typically, one would have to turn and accept the Void’s whispers and peacefully lay their head in the flora after the shock of losing their realm subsides and dread sets in. There are some who resent and fight the Void, but others who chose to be cradled by it. Those who surrender themselves are then turned into Phantoms and are either returned to their bodies, becoming an Odd, or stay as a spirit. When a Phantom is around, the Void Energy within them acts like a black hole by drawing in anything that’s around them. It’s not powerful, but many Odds unfortunately wander into one and are subsequently crushed to the size of a baseball.*"
Appearance: The **Phantom** is a purple ghost with a translucent body. In place of legs it has a tail. It wears a purple shirt and hood. It floats above the path.
Strategy: - As the **Phantom** is a Hidden enemy that appears early on, cheap towers with hidden detection like the Engineer, Golden Pyromancer, Operator, Saboteur and various other towers can be used to handle it with ease.
Trivia: - The **Phantom** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.

Description: The **Possessed Armor** is an enemy that appears in Fallen and Fallen Arena PVP modes. It also appears in The Takeover Event. It has a decent speed and has a decent amount of health. It also has 50% defense, reducing most forms of damage by 33.33%. As it loses its Shield Health, it loses pieces of its armor. Once it loses all of its Shield Health, it will no longer have any armor. This doubles its speed and makes it a Hidden enemy, meaning that you need to use towers with hidden detection to kill it.
It can only be spawned by the Fallen King. The Awakened Fallen King also used to be able to spawn it.
Logbook Description: "*These suits of armor once belonged to the kingdom's greatest Champions, displayed in halls of honor. When the curse swept through, the residual magic within animated them. The armor conceals something inside, and many believe it holds the souls of the lost Champions trapped within. Whether the armor truly contains the Champions' souls has yet to be discovered.*"
Appearance: The **Possessed Armor** is a possessed set of armor. It is a light blue and grey armor, with multiple blue gems on it. It wears a grey helmet with two blue horns on it. As it loses shield health, it gradually loses armor until all of it is gone, revealing the entity that wears it. The entity has translucent black body with multiple blue cracks on its body. It also has neon blue eyes. It also does not have any legs.
Strategy: - Towers with high DPS, like the Minigunner, Accelerator and Engineer can be useful against this.
- The Ranger is unable to kill it as it lacks hidden detection.
- The Ace Pilot can be used to give your towers hidden detection, allowing them to target the **Possessed Armor** even after it becomes Hidden.
- The UAV can also be used, but it requires the consumable to be used and is only temporary. It does, however, provide a range boost and has map wide range.
- The **Possessed Armor** is quite fast. Because of this, slowing towers like the Freezer, Frost Blaster, Warden or Brawler can be very useful at slowing it down.
- As it is only Hidden after losing its armor, the Tesla, Sledger and Cryomancer can be used to slow it down while it is not hidden.
- Multiple of these towers can also be used to drop its defense.
Trivia: - The **Possessed Armor** is likely a reference to a *Terraria* enemy of the same name.
Update History: - **Bug**: Poison and electric defense dropping does not decrease **Possessed Armor's** defense.
- **Bugfix**: Poison and electric defense dropping now drops **Possessed Armor's** defense, though the Jester still cannot drop it

Upon explosion, they spawn the Unknown Boss (25% chance) and Unknown Small (75% chance), both with Bloated and Aggro. The Unknown Bosses also can spawn with either Nimble or Health Regen. Can only be used after **The Metamorphosis**.

Description: **Primordial Drakobloxxer**, internally just **Drakobloxxer**, was the final boss of Containment, the third Night of the Hexscape Event. It had high health, highest in the entire event, though it was also the slowest in its first phase. It emerged from the portal in a cutscene.
It had seven abilities, four that could be used at any time, its second phase and two abilities it could only use after entering its second phase:

- The first ability was *Nightmare Blast*. It made **Primordial Drakobloxxer** scream, which formed a large death beam at the center of the map, stunning towers for 5 seconds and dealing heavy damage to units.
- Its second ability was *Enforced Departure*. It made it form a small purple orb at a part of the map, which it later teleported to, dissolving the orb.
- Its third ability was *Nightmare Storm*. It made it scream and emit purple mist, summoning two Unknown Bosses on the path. **Primordial Drakobloxxer** also gained the Tank attribute briefly.

- Its fourth and last ability available from the first phase was *Nightmare Storm*, which made it emit a magenta aura around it and slam the ground. This applied a 60% Fatigue Debuff to towers for 10 seconds.

After losing half of its health in the Hard difficulty, **Primordial Drakobloxxer** would enter its second phase, making it faster by 50% and making it use its abilities more frequently. This also unlocked two additional abilities for it:
- The first was *Super Dupa Laser*, which made it create two lasers shaped like a cross that spun wildly around the map, stunning towers for 6 seconds and dealing 300 damage to units.

- Its second ability unlocked in the second phase was *Nightmare Tear*. It made it fire out five skulls that upon exploding, had a 25% chance to summon a Bloated and Aggro Unknown Boss, which also could either be Health Regen or Nimble, and a 75% chance to summon a Bloated and Aggro Unknown Small.

In both Easy and Hard difficulties, while it was suggested it ignored the path, it actually had its own nodal path which was not visible to the player. This path would eventually lead the **Primordial Drakobloxxer** to the exit.
Appearance: **Primordial Drakobloxxer** was a large, red-skinned creature with multiple red spikes on its body. Its torso had a darker skin tone than its arms. It had eight arms, each with four claws. It used six of them to support itself while walking and the other two to hold and control a God Cube shard. Its head was a large mouth with no visible eyes. It walked on fours around the map.

After first using its *Super Dupa Laser* ability, its skin would become blue and its head would become purple. It would also start walking with its tongue out. It would return to its regular colors when killed.
Strategy: **Easy Difficulty**
- Multiple high DPS, like the Accelerator, Engineer, Pursuit or Ranger, can easily kill the **Primordial Drakobloxxer**.
- Support towers like the DJ Booth can be useful at boosting your towers.
- Selling towers and replacing them near the **Primordial Drakobloxxer** is recommended due to its ability to teleport across the map.
- High range towers like the Ranger or Mortar can be quite useful because of this, as they do not require to be moved.
- The DJ Booth can be used to boost the range of your towers.
- Ensure that you have enough other towers to deal with the enemies that spawn along with it.
- Multiple Level 4 Jesters with confusion and poison bombs can greatly help hinder the advancement of the horde while also damaging them to make quick work of them.
**Hard Difficulty**

- Due to **Primordial Drakobloxxer's** higher health, placing down many high DPS towers like the Accelerator, Engineer, Golden Minigunner, Pursuit, Ranger or Turret will be able to chip away its health.
- The Commander, DJ Booth or Mercenary Base can be used to provide buffs to your towers.
- Selling towers and replacing them near the **Primordial Drakobloxxer** is recommended as **Primordial Drakobloxxer** is able to teleport out of the towers' range.
- Brawler is a good pick to fight this boss as you are able to move it using it reposition ability without having to waste the money needed to sell and replace.
- The purple aura emitting out of **Primordial Drakobloxxer'**s body will indicate that it is teleporting.
- As an alternative to selling towers, you can use long-ranged towers like the Ranger as they are more likely to keep **Primordial Drakobloxxer** in their range.

- It is recommended to set Rangers to *Strongest* for this, however one should also be wary of Flying enemies like the Cursed Horror that may leak through your defenses if your other towers lack flight detection.
- Ensure that you have enough firepower to deal with the enemy hordes that appear after **Primordial Drakobloxxer** spawns.
- Multiple Level 4 Jesters with confusion and poison bombs can greatly help hinder the advancement of the horde while also damaging them to make quick work of them.
Trivia: - **Primordial Drakobloxxer** was a reference to the Drakobloxxers from the classic Roblox game *Build To Survive Drakobloxxers!* by Papasmurf.
- Its name suggests it was a more evolved, advanced, and possibly mutated version of it.
- The name may be a reference to the Great Drakobloxxer from *Combat Initiation*, as it is classified as primordial.
- **Primordial Drakobloxxer's** internal name was just *Drakobloxxer*.
- Because of this, all the enemies it summoned were called "*Drakobloxxer's _____*" instead of "*Primordial Drakobloxxer's _____*".
- **Primordial Drakobloxxer** was the largest enemy in the game.

- **Primordial Drakobloxxer** had the second most abilities in the game, tied with the Ducky D00M and Krampus, who appeared in D00M's Revenge and Krampus Frosthold respectively, only behind the Frost Spirit from the Operation I.C.E Event.

- **Primordial Drakobloxxer** was the enemy with the longest name in the game, being 22 characters without including spaces. The length has beaten Awakened Fallen King and Korblox Deathwalker, with each having 18 characters when excluding spaces.
- The whispers heard in its theme are actual lyrics. They are these four passages repeated multiple times:
- "*I vocare te diaboli - Ustulo omnia - Nova nobis - Children Of Exo*"
- "*Our World Of Flames*"
- "*Hark the Calling of Crows*"
- "*Witness pain...*"
Update History: - **Bug**: Poison and electric defense dropping towers cannot drop its defense.
- **Primordial Drakobloxxer** can no longer have its defense decreased.
- **Bugfix**: Poison and electric defense dropping towers now can drop its defense if it is not a Boss enemy, though the Jester still cannot drop it.

Description: The **Producer** was a major boss that appeared in The Narratorium, served as a mini-boss for the The Final Act Event.
The **Producer** has four abilities:

- The first ability is *Clapboard*, which makes the **Producer** pull out a Clapper Board. After 3 seconds, this flashes the screen and slightly disorients the player, also stunning all towers in the map for 3.5 seconds and dealing 700 damage to units.

- The second ability, *Beam*, causes the **Producer** to pull out a film projector, attacking everything in a 120 degree arc with a range of 20, stunning towers for 4 seconds and dealing 1,600 damage to units. After throwing the projector, the impact causes the screen to flash, creating an afterimage of the player's screen.

- The third ability is *Summon*. In it, the **Producer** summons six Actor1s (75% chance), Actor2s (15% chance) and Actor3s (10% chance), which have a 60% to spawn with nothing, 20% chance to be Bloated and 20% chance to have Health Regen.

- The fourth and last ability, *Spotlight*, has the **Producer** begin dancing while The Narratorium dims. After 3 seconds, this created a spotlight with a radius of 14 on a random tower that applies a 75% Fatigue Debuff (42.87% increase) to any tower in it, lasting until the **Producer** is killed. All uses of this ability after the first one will simply move the spotlight to a different location instead of creating another spotlight.
Logbook Description: "*The Producer initially began as a personified manifestation of Narrator's imagination — a vision of his ideal partner that existed only in his mind after finding a projector in the trash. During the Final Act, however, this imaginary partner was recreated in reality. Though, we wonder if Narrator would be different if he only knew.*"
Appearance: The **Producer** is a projector turned into a representation of the Narrator's ideal partner. It has blonde hair and a black head. It wears a red dress, shoes, and jacket. On its legs, it wears white socks with black stripes and white gloves on its arms. It has white and black striped arm-bands with red straps and ribbons. She has a white and black mask with red and gold accents.
Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in The Narratorium is listed instead.
- High DPS towers, like the Accelerator, Ranger, Golden Minigunner, Warlock or Turret are recommended against this enemy.
- Towers like the Ranger or Pursuit can be especially useful, due to their map wide range and immunity to stuns.
- The Commander and DJ Booth can be used to boost the statistics of your towers.
- The Mercenary Base can be used to both deal damage and provide buffs to towers.
- The Medic can be used to shield towers from the **Producer's** stuns.
Trivia: - The **Producer** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Bug**: **Producer's** left eye is made out of grey plastic instead of being neon red.
- **Producer** removed from the main game, now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.

Description: The **Projector** was an enemy that appeared in The Narratorium as a part of The Final Act Event. It had a high amount of health and a slightly slow speed. It can stun towers for 2.5 seconds and deal 700 damage to units by flashing them with the light on its projector head. This ability has a range of 15 and tick of 0.1.
Logbook Description: "*The Projector Man is a stark reminder of the Narrator's twisted mind. It is used to display movies for entertainment or project screens for plays. The Projector Man was once a whole person but was reconstructed to serve the Narrator's purposes. When alone, it finds a quiet corner and projects memories of it's past life, reminiscing about happier times.*"
Appearance: The **Projector** is a tall hobject-headed robot which has a projector for a head. It wears a red shirt, blue pants and black shoes. Using its projector head, it will shoot its laser ray light to towers near it.
Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in The Narratorium is listed instead.

- While slow, **Projectors** are very tanky, especially when Bloated. High damage towers are a necessity by their debut, and only become more of a necessity due to **Projectors** being both Stun and Freeze Immune.
- If one happens to own it, Toxic Gunner can slow them down quite a lot, giving you much more free room to deal with them.
- **Projectors** can quickly stun groups of towers through their *Tachyon Light* ability, also quickly damaging any units caught in the crossfire.
- Distracting them with less valuable towers at the entrance can not only buy some time, but also keep your stronger towers safe.
Trivia: - Strangely, the **Projector** is referred to as "*Projector Man*" in its Logbook entry.
- This may be an earlier name for it, before being shortened to just "***Projector***".
- The **Projector** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Bug**: **Projector's** head does not move in the Index.
- **Projector** removed from the main game, now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.

Description: The **Quick** is the second enemy the player faces in the game in Molten, Fallen, Challenge Trials, and all PVP arena modes. While it does appear in all PVP Test ranks, it can only be sent in Fallen Arena PVP. It also appears in Badlands II and Pizza Party maps, in the Sandbox exclusive Legacy Fallen and Golden modes, and in The Takeover Event. It is faster than the Abnormal while also being tankier.
The **Quick** can be spawned by the Dark Necromancer. Upon its death, the Mystery can spawn the **Quick** in Golden and Legacy Fallen.
Logbook Description: "*The Quick zombie is a further mutation from the Abnormal. It is stronger and faster, leading it to sprint towards humans and other creatures. They are more aggressive than Normal and Abnormal zombies.*"
Appearance: **Variant 1**
The **Quick** has a desaturated blue skin color and a dirty dark brown torso and legs. It has dark blue veins on its arms and head.
**Variant 2**
**Variant 1**

The legacy **Quick** has a reflective light blue skin color and a dark blue blue granite torso and legs. It has blue diamond-plated armbands and sharp glowing light blue crystals on its shoulders. It has two diagonal lines, forming a mirrored "y" on its face.
**Variant 2**
The current Enemies Beta version of the legacy **Quick** has a desaturated light blue skin color with navy veins being visible on its head and arms. It has a desaturated cyan torso and legs.
**Variant 3**
The second version of the legacy **Quick** was similar to the current version, except it had a sad face.
**Variant 4**
The first version of the legacy **Quick** had a baby blue skin color and a blue granite torso and legs. It also had a drooling zombie face.
**Variant 3**

The legacy **Quick** has a reflective light blue skin color and a dark blue blue granite torso and legs. It has blue diamond-plated armbands and sharp glowing light blue crystals on its shoulders. It has two diagonal lines, forming a mirrored "y" on its face.
**Variant 4**
The current Enemies Beta version of the legacy **Quick** has a desaturated light blue skin color with navy veins being visible on its head and arms. It has a desaturated cyan torso and legs.
**Variant 5**
The second version of the legacy **Quick** was similar to the current version, except it had a sad face.
**Variant 6**
The first version of the legacy **Quick** had a baby blue skin color and a blue granite torso and legs. It also had a drooling zombie face.
Strategy: - Most towers can deal with the **Quick** effectively.
- Any tower catered towards early game, like the Cowboy, Toxic Gunner, Brawler, Militant or Golden Cowboy is recommended
- Towers with a slow firerate, like the Sniper or Shotgunner, may struggle against hordes of **Quicks**.
- Towers that can deal damage to multiple enemies are especially effective against **Quicks** as they spawn in hordes. Such towers include the Assassin, Electroshocker, Pyromancer and Shotgunner.

- While not recommended if you are not trying to activate the Hidden Wave, it is an option to avoid defending against the first few waves of **Quicks** and simply let them reach the exit, as their low health makes it unlikely to make you lose.
- You can use the Medic to heal the base health back, but it may not be necessary.
- As you are not spending money on defenses, you can use the Farm more effectively for the first few waves to get better towers when stronger enemies appear.
Trivia: - The second and third appearance of **Quick** looks similar to the third and fourth version of the Speedy Boss.
- While the Legacy version of the **Quick** can drop a Logbook, getting it will only give the player the modern **Quick** in the Index.

Strategy: - **Quick Pawns** are weak enemies that can be dealt with by a majority of early game towers, such as the Crook Boss, Golden Soldier and Brawler.
- As they spawn in groups, towers that can damage multiple enemies at once are effective against them.
- They can also be easily slowed down by slowing towers like the Cryomancer.

Description: The **Radioactive** was an enemy that appeared exclusively in Polluted Wasteland Fallen mode and was a replacement for the Heavy in Polluted Wasteland. The **Radioactive** had a slightly slower speed than the Quick but also had significantly more health than it.
The **Radioactive** was spawned by the Dark Necromancer and the Mystery upon its death in Polluted Wasteland Fallen mode.
Appearance: The **Radioactive** had green skin and bright white eyes, with what appeared to be green radiation fluid leaking out of its eyes and mouth. Its torso and legs were metal-plated dark green. It also wore a radioactive pack on its back.
Its appearance was similar to that of the Abnormal.
Strategy: - Place your defenses in the center of the map to deal as much damage as possible.
- In hordes, the Demoman, Rocketeer and Mortar can wipe them out.
- However, these towers have a slow projectile speed, which means that the **Radioactive** may be able to escape the explosion radius of these towers, due to its high speed.
- Additionally, they do very low damage at lower levels, so this is not recommended
- You can use towers like Freezer, Frost Blaster or Electroshocker to slow these down, as this enemy is fast.
- As the **Radioactive** spawns quite early, you need cheap, yet effective, towers.
- Ideal towers include the Soldier, Cowboy, Crook Boss, Ace Pilot and Pyromancer.
- Be aware that the Pyromancer will speed this already fast enemy up by 15%.
- It is important to defend against the **Radioactive** early on during the game, as their high health and fast speed will easily overpower you.
- A lot of Military Bases and Ace Pilots can be used to counter this.
- A Militant can fare well against **Radioactives** early on during the game.
Update History: - No longer appears in Golden mode as it has been removed.

raider_1.name: Raider 1
raider_1.description: The Raider 1 was an Area 51 enemy that only appeared during the Area 51 Event. It was the first raider to appear.
