abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Fire Gun** - Fires a burning laser at a tower. This sets it on fire so that it cannot attack for 7-10 seconds.

Description: The **Raider 1** was an Area 51 enemy that only appeared during the Area 51 Event. It was the first raider to appear.

It had the same speed as the Lawnmower and UFO, though it had much more health than both of them. It carried a gun which set a specific tower on fire when shot with the *Fire Gun* ability, stunning them for a long period of time.
Appearance: The **Raider 1** had green skin, a grey torso, black gloves and dark grey armor. It had dark navy legs and had a gas tank on its back, possibly as ammunition for the fire gun it wielded. The **Raider 1** also had a drooling zombie face.
Strategy: - The **Raider 1** is immobile for a few seconds while it aims at a tower.
- This makes it vulnerable when it is aiming at a tower. Try to have long-ranged towers damage the **Raider 1** once it is immobile.
- Weak towers, such as the Scout, can be used to direct the **Raider 1's** firepower away from the main towers.
- Since you get a paycheck just before you encounter this enemy, try to get high DPS towers, such as the Turret and Commando.
- The **Raider 1** will not target the Farm, Sentry, Turret, Military Base or spawned units.
Trivia: - The **Raider 1** was a reference to the *Storm Area 51, They Can't Stop All of Us* event where masses of people would have raided the *Nevada Test and Training Range*.
- The gun used by the **Raider 1** is the Incinerator-6000 gear from the Roblox catalog.

raider_2.name: Raider 2
raider_2.description: The Raider 2 was an Area 51 enemy that only appeared during the Area 51 Event. It was the second raider to appear after the Raider 1.

notice.text: Raider 2 has been removed from the game as of the 13th of October 2019 as it was part of the Area 51 Event.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Ice Gun** - Fires an ice laser at a tower. This would freeze that tower and other towers nearby.

Description: The **Raider 2** was an Area 51 enemy that only appeared during the Area 51 Event. It was the second raider to appear after the Raider 1.

The **Raider 2** had the same speed as the Raider 1, but had even more health. It carried an ice gun which could be used to freeze specific towers with the *Ice Gun* ability. Towers around the target would also be splashed, resulting in several towers being stunned for an extended period of time.
Appearance: The **Raider 2** had blue skin and wore dark grey armor, with black gloves. It had dark navy legs and had an ice tank on its back, possibly as ammunition for the ice gun it wielded. The **Raider 2** also had a drooling zombie face.
Strategy: - Similar to the Raider 1, try to use the Scout to distract its attack away from your main towers.
- When it is charging up its ice gun, the **Raider 2** becomes immobile, allowing any tower that is not frozen to target it.
- Due to the splash effect of the **Raider 2's** attack, it is best not to place your towers close together. This is because if one tower is hit, they will all become frozen.
- The Pyromancer does not deal any extra damage against the **Raider 2**, it will simply just slow it down like any other enemy.
- The **Raider 2** will not target the Farm, Sentry, Turret, Military Base or spawned units.
- However, the splash effect of the **Raider 2's** ice gun may still hit the Sentry and Turret.
Trivia: - The **Raider 2** was a reference to the *Storm Area 51, They Can't Stop All of Us* event where masses of people would have raided the *Nevada Test and Training Range*.
- The gun used by the **Raider 2** is the Sapphire Rapid Fire Shocker from the Roblox catalog.

raider_boss.name: Raider Boss
raider_boss.description: The Raider Boss was the final enemy of the Area 51 Event and only appeared in Area 51. Like most major bosses, it had high health and walked extremely slowly.

notice.text: Raider Boss has been removed from the game as of the 13th of October 2019 as it was part of the Area 51 Event.

stats.Attributes:

- Splash Damage Immune

abilities.label: Ability 1
abilities.text: **Raid Gun Shot** - Shoots three random towers in its range which will stun them for 10-15 seconds.

abilities.label: Ability 2
abilities.text: **Rocket Launcher** - The **Raider Boss** fires four rockets from its quad launcher, stunning towers in a large radius for 7-15 seconds.

abilities.label: Ability 3
abilities.text: **Raider Reinforcements** - The **Raider Boss** summons a small group of Raider 1s and Raider 2s which walk from the spawn.

abilities.label: Ability 4
abilities.text: **Fatal Raid Gun Shot** - The **Raider Boss** kneels down and shoots a powerful shot at a humanoid tower, killing it, preventing it from attacking. It will disappear shortly after.

Description: The **Raider Boss** was the final enemy of the Area 51 Event and only appeared in Area 51. Like most major bosses, it had high health and walked extremely slowly. This boss was challenging due to the strength of its abilities.
The **Raider Boss** had four abilities:

- Its first one was its *Raid Gun Shot*. The **Raider Boss** could shoot at three different towers, or the same tower three times with this attack. The effects did not stack if a tower was hit more than twice.

- Its second ability was its *Rocket Launcher*. Similar to the Commando, the boss would fire four rockets from its quad launcher on its back. These rockets would explode as it hit the ground, stunning all towers caught in the explosion for an extensive period of time.
- Its third ability sent in groups of Raider 1s and Raider 2s, which would assist the **Raider Boss** by stunning towers.

- Its fourth, and final, ability was the most deadly attack. The *Fatal Raid Gun Shot* involved the **Raider Boss** kneeling down, taking aim and firing a shot at a humanoid tower within its range. This killed the tower, causing it to stop attacking and eventually despawn.
Appearance: The **Raider Boss** had green skin, black gloves and wore dark grey metallic armor. Its legs were navy and it wielded a green raider gun. On its back was a quad launcher which could fire rockets. The **Raider Boss** had red eyes and had a grey bandanna wrapped around its mouth and neck. Black particles were emitted from its torso.
Strategy: - Spamming cheap towers may help with increasing the pool of towers the **Raider Boss** may shoot with the *Fatal Raid Gun Shot*.
- The **Raider Boss** is immobilized while performing its *Fatal Raid Gun Shot*. This gives an opportunity for towers to attack it, so long they are not stunned.
- When a tower is hit by the *Fatal Raid Gun Shot*, you can sell it immediately to recoup some of the cost. You must do this very quickly as the tower despawns a few seconds after it is hit.
- Try not to upgrade towers to Level 5, unless you can afford it, as if they are hit by the *Fatal Raid Gun Shot*, most of the investment is wasted.
- The **Raider Boss** will not target the Farm, Sentry, Turret, Military Base or spawned Units.
- Group Turrets and Sentries in an area without other towers nearby to maximize their damage output. They can only be stunned via the *Rocket Launcher* attack.
- Units (like those from the Military Base) are effective against the **Raider Boss** as they cannot be stunned or killed by it.
- Try to space out your towers. A hit from the Raider 2 or *Rocket Launcher* will disable most of your towers if they are grouped together.
- Cheap, fast-firing towers are recommended against the **Raider Boss**. This includes the Crook Boss and Minigunner, upgraded to Level 2 or 3.
- The Pyromancer can be used to slow the **Raider Boss** down, as well as provide a distraction if you do not have the Scout on hand.

- The Rocketer and Demoman can only deal direct damage towards the **Raider Boss** as it is immune to splash damage. It is recommended to sell these towers for towers that do not deal splash damage, like the Minigunner.
Trivia: - The Raider Boss was one of the options polled to be the final boss of Insane mode, now called the Fallen mode.

- It lost the vote to the Fallen King, meaning it alongside the Shadow Boss, an enemy not to be confused with the actually added Shadow Boss and a joke Tycoon Dropper option never made it into the mode.
- The **Raider Boss** was the first enemy capable of killing towers; the second and third being the Left and Right Hand.
- **Raider Boss** was a reference to the *Storm Area 51, They Can't Stop All of Us* event where masses of people would have raided the *Nevada Test and Training Range*.
- The gun the **Raider Boss** wielded was the Rapid Launch Blaster found in the Roblox catalog.
- The bandana used by the **Raider Boss** is the Renegade Bandana accessory from the Roblox catalog.
- The **Raider Boss** was planned to walk much faster, but its speed was decreased to make the event easier for newer players.
- The **Raider Boss's** final wave music was Cursed Abbey.
- Coincidentally, the Grave Digger uses the same song, just remixed.

Description: The **Reanimated** was an enemy that appeared exclusively in Trick or Threat Town as part of the Halloween 2020 Event.
While the **Reanimated** had a slower speed compared to the Buried, it had a high amount of health. This made it a major threat.
The **Reanimated** could be spawned by the Lord Sinister.
Appearance: The **Reanimated** had green skin, with its torso and legs colored brown. Its torso and legs were slate. Its rib and right leg were cut open and exposed, similar to the Undead. Bone could have been seen in these cuts. It also had a shocked face. Two bolts were connected to either side of its head. Its head was slightly tilted downwards.
Strategy: - Make sure to have enough towers to defeat the **Reanimated** when it first appears.
- Use high DPS towers such as the Ranger, Minigunner and Turret to defeat the **Reanimated**.
- Due to the **Reanimated's** high health, Rangers are highly recommended.
- Multiple Level 3 Rangers can easily defeat the **Reanimated**.
- The Commander's *Call to Arms* may be useful in boosting firerate. This helps in defeating the **Reanimated**.
- The Military Base can be useful, if the **Reanimated** leaves the range of all of your towers since its health is significantly low enough to be killed by a few Tanks.
Trivia: - The bolts on the head of the **Reanimated** showed resemblance to the Frankenstein, an enemy from the Halloween 2019 Event.
- The shocked face on the **Reanimated** is based on the ﾟдﾟ emoticon, popularized from 2channel.

Description: The **Reaper** is a summoner enemy that appears in Pizza Party. It has a high amount of health and below average speed. It also has two immunities, Stun Immunity and Burn Immunity. It has two abilities, the first being *Haunted Summon*, which makes it summon three Demons, which then spawn Sins upon death. The second ability is *Soul Reap*, which makes it attack a tower in its range, stunning it.
Appearance: The **Reaper** is a large humanoid with a waist in its rig. It has a black skin tone, a dark grey ragged cloak with sleeves, pants and a hood with a dark red trim, light grey legs, and a dark red cape. It has a grey chain draped across its torso and has black spikes coming out of its shoulders. It wields a white scythe with a skull on top, which has grey horns and a black blade on it.
Strategy: - High DPS towers like the Ranger, Engineer, Turret or Accelerator are recommended against this.
- Do note that on Wave 39, the **Reaper** spawns as a Hidden enemy. High DPS towers with hidden detection are needed against this.
- The Firework Technician, Ace Pilot and UAV can be used to give your towers hidden detection.
- The DJ Booth and Commander can also be quite useful at boosting their statistics.
- Its *Haunted Summon* ability summons three Demons, which then summons even more Sins, creating huge crowds of enemies.
- Area of effect towers, like the Mortar, Electroshocker or Pursuit can be used to clear out both the crowds of enemies and the **Reaper** itself.
- The Medic can be used to shield towers, preventing them from being stunned by the **Reaper**.
- Placing down cheap distraction towers near the **Reaper** can be quite useful, as it will prevent the **Reaper** from stunning more important towers.
- Additionally, in cases where it would normally be unable to hit any tower, it prevents it from being guaranteed to use its *Haunted Summon* ability, making it far easier to deal with.
Update History: - Cash given increased from $2,500 every 25% health to $4,000 every 10% health.

Description: The **Reaper** was a summoner enemy that appeared in Containment as part of the Hexscape Event. It had high health and 50% defense, but a below average speed.

The **Reaper** had two abilities. The first was *Spooky Summon*, which made it slam its scythe, creating a pentagram that summoned five enemies. These were most commonly Cursed Horrors, but it could also spawn much more rarely Enigmas, Hex Corpses and Rotting Terrors. The second ability was *Soul Reap*, which had it slash its scythe at a tower, stunning it.
Appearance: The **Reaper** was a large humanoid with a waist in its rig. It had a black skin tone, a dark grey ragged cloak with sleeves, pants and a hood with a dark red trim, light grey legs, and a dark red cape. It had a grey chain draped across its torso and had black spikes coming out of its shoulders. It wielded a white scythe with a skull on top, which had grey horns and a black blade on it.
Strategy: - High DPS towers like the Ranger, Engineer or Accelerator are recommended against this.
- The DJ Booth and Commander can also be quite useful at boosting their statistics.
- While the **Reaper** itself does not require any detections, the Cursed Horrors need flying detection to be targeted.
- Because of this, towers like the Ranger, Pursuit or Engineer can be useful here.
- The Electroshocker could also be used, dealing damage to multiple Cursed Horrors at once while also slowing them down.
- As the **Reaper** has Burn Immunity, it cannot be set on fire, preventing fire dropping towers from reducing its defense.
Trivia: - The **Reaper's** model and abilities were reused from the Lunar Overture Event's Reaper, though the enemies it summoned were altered.
Update History: - **Bug**: Poison and electric defense dropping do not decrease **Reaper's** defense.
- **Bug**: Bloated **Reapers** float slightly above the path.
- **Bugfix**: Bloated **Reapers** no longer float above the path.

abilities.label: Ability 1

abilities.label: Ability 2
abilities.text: **Soul Reap** - The **Reaper** swings its scythe at a nearby tower, stunning it and other towers near it.

Description: The **Reaper** was the third boss that appeared in the second act of the Lunar Overture Event, though only the first **Reaper** that spawned was considered a Boss. It was a tanky and slow enemy with multiple immunities, which made it immune to burn damage from towers like the Pyromancer and immune to being completely stopped by the Warden and Electroshocker, being only slowed down instead. While it was a boss enemy, it was also immune to being frozen by freezing towers and being slowed down by the Toxic Gunner. It also had 15% defense.

The **Reaper** had two abilities. The first ability, *Sin Bringing*, made it summon five enemies, some of which had their statistics altered through the Scale attribute. It could spawn the two variants of Sins, the smaller variant with above average speed and 400 health or the big variant with 800 health but below average speed, a smaller Demon with its health halved but increased speed or a Hallow Guard with a random amount of health, which is higher than 2,500 and lower than 3,000, slightly smaller size and slightly faster speed. The second ability, *Soul Reap*, made it swing its scythe at a tower, stunning it and any other tower near it.
Appearance: The **Reaper** was a large humanoid with a waist in its rig. It had a black skin tone, a dark grey ragged cloak with sleeves, pants and a hood with a dark red trim, light grey legs, and a dark red cape. It had a grey chain draped across its torso and had black spikes coming out of its shoulders. It wielded a white scythe with a skull on top, which had grey horns and a black blade on it.

The **Reaper** had a death animation, where it would drop its scythe and fall on its back, but would flash red and turn into ash in the process, with its body quickly disassembling and fading away. During its *Sin Bringing* ability, a red ritual circle appeared beneath it.
Strategy: - High DPS towers, like the Accelerator, Minigunner or Pursuit are recommended against it.
- High DPS towers with ability to hit multiple enemies at once, like the Pursuit or Ranger can hit multiple enemies that the **Reaper** spawns at once, making them more effective against it.
- The Commander and DJ Booth can be useful at boosting their firerate and range respectively.
- When it first spawns on Wave 18, it is a boss enemy, therefore it cannot be frozen by freezing towers, slowed down by the Toxic Gunner or completely stopped by the Warden and Electroshocker.
- This also means that it is unaffected by the Witch's ability.
- After Wave 18, the **Reaper** is no longer a boss, reducing its immunities to only being immune to the Warden's and Electroshocker's stun, only being slowed down by them.
- The **Reaper** is immune to being set on fire by towers like the Pyromancer, making them less effective against it.
- It also makes it immune from having its defense decreased by the Pyromancer and Golden Pyromancer but since its defense is quite low, this is not a huge issue.
Trivia: - There was a chance to get the Reaper's Gear accessory, which was based on this enemy, upon triumphing the second act of the Lunar Overture Event.
Notes: - ↑ Only first **Reaper** spawned as a boss.

Description: The **Reaper** was a summoner enemy that appeared exclusively in Trick or Threat Town as part of the Halloween 2020 Event. Currently, it only appears in Sandbox mode. It had higher health compared to the Slime, but had lower health in comparison to the Reanimated. However, it had the same speed as the Reanimated. It could also spawn enemies, namely the Undead, Bones, Hallow Bones and Buried.
Appearance: The **Reaper** is a faceless figure. The **Reaper** has white skin and a torn black cloak. It wears a black hood and had a chain across its torso. Its legs are marble grey and it wears a red belt across its waist. It wields a purple scythe to summon enemies with.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Trick or Threat Town is listed instead.
- Splash damage towers are recommended against the **Reaper** to help manage the enemies that spawn.
- High DPS towers are recommended against the **Reaper**. The Ranger and Minigunner are suitable towers for this.
- It may be ideal for these towers to be set to *Strongest* to target the **Reaper** instead of the enemies that it spawns.
- However, this may be an issue when higher health enemies appear at the same time as the **Reaper**, like the Reanimated.
- Try to defeat the **Reaper** before it crosses the bridge.
- If it gets too close to the end of the map, it may spawn a Buried which could lead to a defeat.
- If two **Reapers** are able to cross the bridge, they may summon enemies which could overpower your available towers.
Trivia: - This enemy was similar to the 2019 version of the Reaper.
- The **Reaper's** summon animation was same as the Molten Boss's *Scythe Slam*.
- The **Reaper's** scythe was also the same as the Molten Boss's scythe, except it was colored purple.
Update History: - **Reaper** can now be summoned in Sandbox mode, only when the player has the Reaper's from Pizza Party Logbook.
- No longer copies the statistics of the modern version in Sandbox mode.

Description: The **Reaper** was a summoner enemy that appeared exclusively in Nightmare Carnival as part of the Halloween 2019 Event. While it walked quite slowly, it had somewhat high health for its debut. It could also summon Scarecrows, Ghosts, Mummies, and Strong Mummies, making it the Halloween equivalent of the Necromancer.
Appearance: The **Reaper** wore a black cloak and a black hood. Its head was reflective black and was faceless. It had white cobblestone skin, grey granite legs and a chain across its torso. It also carried a scythe.
Strategy: - High DPS towers such as the Minigunner and Outlaw are recommended against this enemy.
- It may be ideal for these towers to be set to *Strongest* to target the **Reaper** instead of the enemies that it spawns.
- However, this may be an issue when higher health enemies, such as Clowns and Frankensteins, appear.
- Splash damage towers, such as the Rocketeer and Demoman, are highly recommended against the **Reaper** as the enemies it summons form large hordes.
Trivia: - The **Reaper** was based on the Grim Reaper, a personified character representing death.
- This was ironic as the **Reaper** can summon enemies, although these enemies could already be considered dead.

Description: The **Reaver** is an enemy that appears in Intermediate and Molten Arena PVP modes. It also appears in The Takeover Event. It has decent health for its debut and above average speed, but it makes up for its high Defense, making it quite dangerous.
Due to a bug, **Reavers** with the Slime attribute do not spawn the Slime upon death.

It has a very light green skin color, torn dark brown shorts, and a dark green fluid on its lower limbs. It is missing its right forearm, and has a pair of four ribs sticking out of the side of its torso. Most of the skin on its head is missing, revealing a skull. Its head also has patchy black hair on the sides, and it has green tumors across its body.
Strategy: - As the **Reaver** has 125% Defense, most sources of damage have their damage halved.

- The Trapper can be useful against this enemy, as all its traps deal damage that bypasses defense.
- Splash damage towers that can bypass defense, such as the Mortar or Rocketeer, can be useful against this enemy.
- Defense dropping towers such as the Pyromancer and Freezer can decrease its defense.

- No longer appears in Sk8 P4rk, as it has been removed.

The **Rift Walker** has seven abilities:
- *Null Bubbles*, which fires three bubbles at towers. These apply a 25% Range Debuff to any tower in it.

- *Null Invasion*, which has the **Rift Walker** create rifts to the Nil Zone, summoning in six enemies per each path. These can be the Null Engineer, Null Warden and Null Brawler.
- *Null Beam* makes the **Rift Walker** fire purple beams at towers and units, stunning them for 3 seconds and dealing 2,000 damage to units.

- *Lord Exo Attack*, which makes Lord Exo come out of the **Rift Walker**, striking the base and dealing damage equal to 50% of the max base health, accounting for the max possible Medic overheal but not the Skills overheal. This can be stopped with the Star Cannon.
- *Ancient Anger*, a rage mode ability activated at 60% health. When activated, the walk animation will change and it will unlock its *Dimensional Discharge* ability.

- *Dimensional Discharge* has the **Rift Walker** apply a random debuff to every tower on the map. This can be either a Range Debuff, Firerate Debuff or Damage Debuff, all with a value of 20% and duration of 10.
Logbook Description: "*The Rift Walker is an[sic] being who helped create the Meta with his master. Together, they maintain the balance of the realms, and will destroy any who threaten it. The Rift Walker is powerful enough to rival greatest enemies from the Old World, and his judgment is absolute. He is known to be strict, for if he fails, everyone from all realities will end up in the Nil Zone.*"
Appearance: The **Rift Walker** has black skin and purple neon eyes. Due to being possessed by Lord Exo, its torso has an exposed grey ribcage. It wears a purple robe and shoes. On its head, it wears a black hat with a purple gem on it. It has a black crow mask with purple bandages wrapped around its beak. It holds a purple and black staff.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Blind Faith is listed instead.
- High DPS towers like the Accelerator, Turret, Ranger or Warlock are required against the **Rift Walker**.
- Stun immune towers can be helpful as they cannot get stunned by it, though since a lot of its abilities apply debuffs, they are not completely immune to its attacks.
- Temperance can be used to give every tower Stun Immunity, the Medic can also be used to do this to five towers per Medic placed.
- The Commander, DJ Booth and Mercenary Base should be used to boost the statistics of your towers.
- As multiple of its abilities apply debuffs, these can also be helpful at partially mitigating the effects of the debuffs.
- The **Rift Walker's** *Lord Exo Attack* ability deals damage to the base health when finished, meaning that the **Rift Walker** can easily kill the players.

- This can be stopped with the Star Cannon, as using it during its ability stops the ability entirely. This should be done when the map starts turning yellow and Lord Exo comes out of the **Rift Walker's** body.
- It is highly recommended to wait a few seconds after this happens, so you can stall out the Rift Walker for as long as possible.
- Do note that if The Fool curse was selected, the base health will be set to 1, meaning any use of it will end the match instantly if the Star Cannon is not used to stop it.

- It is not possible to use the Medic's overheal to give yourself the ability to tank more shots, as the ability accounts for that. However, it does not account for the overheal from Skills, meaning that this can be used.

- Because of this, with Skills overheal, it is entirely possible to avoid building the Star Cannon in the Easy difficulty, as even by just investing **6,245** total into the Level 13 Over-Heal Skill, it is possible to tank two more shots than usual. Additionally, the **Rift Walker** is much weaker, so you can easily kill it before it deals enough damage to kill your base.
Trivia: - The **Rift Walker** is the first enemy to be able to freely summon enemies anywhere on the path, specifically through its *Null Invasion* ability.
- The **Rift Walker** has the most base health out of any enemy in the game's history, boasting a massive 2,500,000 health.

- If the Death curse is active, it would reach a total of 5,000,000 health from the Bloated modifier, surpassing the Conserver's previous record of 3,900,100 if not all the Super Computer Parts were collected.

- Technically, the Conserver could reach 7,800,200 if it was applied the Bloated modifier, but this was not possible to do in-game through normal means, unlike the Bloated **Rift Walker** which is possible if the Death curse is active on the final wave.
- The **Rift Walker's** design may be based on the Plague Doctors.
- The **Rift Walker** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Rift Walker** no longer becomes immune to damage while performing its *Lord Exo Attack* ability.
- **Rift Walker** removed from the main game, now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.
- **Bug**: Cannot be spawned in Sandbox mode.
- **Bugfix**: Can now be spawned in Sandbox mode.

right_hand.name: Right Hand
right_hand.description: The Right Hand, internally referred to as the Hand Boss Right, alongside the Left Hand, was the final boss of the third act in the Lunar Overture Event.

notice.text: Right Hand has been removed from the game as of the 21st of December 2023 as it was part of the Lunar Overture Event.

abilities.label: Ability 1
abilities.text: **Temper Fist** - Balls up into a fist and smashes down on a tower, creating a shockwave that stuns towers hit by it.

abilities.label: Ability 2
abilities.text: **Finger Gun** - Shoots multiple missiles from its index finger at random towers, stunning any tower caught in its explosion.

abilities.label: Ability 3
abilities.text: **Vanquish** - Grabs a tower and crushes it, killing it and giving the player that placed it down some cash. Can happen multiple times in a row.

abilities.label: Ability 4
abilities.text: **Summoning Trickery** - Dangles its fingers over a path and summons five enemies.

Description: The **Right Hand**, internally referred to as the **Hand Boss Right**, alongside the Left Hand, was the final boss of the third act in the Lunar Overture Event. It had a high amount of health, much higher than any other enemy before it, but it could not enter the base like other enemies and did not take damage the same way as other enemies. As it is a boss enemy, it was immune to being slowed down by the Toxic Gunner, could not be frozen by freezing towers and could only be slowed down by the Warden and Electroshocker.
The **Right Hand** had four abilities:
- The first ability, *Temper Fist*, made it move towards a tower, ball up to a fist and smash it, creating a shockwave that stunned any tower.
- Its second ability, *Finger Gun*, made it fire multiple missiles from its index finger at random towers, stunning any tower caught in the explosion.
- Its third ability, *Vanquish*, made it move towards a tower, grab it, squash it and then return to its original position, which killed the tower. It can do this multiple times in a row.
- Its last ability, *Summoning Trickery*, made it dangle its fingers over a path, summoning five enemies, which could be any enemy that appeared before it.
Appearance: The **Right Hand** was a disembodied human hand wearing a white glove.
The **Right Hand** had a death animation where it would make various hand signals before shrinking into nothing and emitting confetti after it disappeared.
Strategy: - Spotlights are the only reliable way to attack the **Right Hand** and Left Hand.
- Both the **Right Hand** and Left Hand cannot be targeted by towers directly, but can still be damaged indirectly from explosions or stray projectiles.
- Enemies that spawn around the map have a chance of dropping a single Battery when killed. These should be collected before Wave 14, as each Spotlight requires 10 Batteries to be used.
- In cases of emergency, it can also be used to confuse enemies coming towards the exit, so that you do not lose from them.

- It is recommended to stay next to the Spotlight which will have its duration end soon, so that it can be quickly activated again. After this, move to the next Spotlight which has the lowest amount of time before it deactivates.
- The **Right Hand** has several abilities that allow it to quickly move around the map. Players using Spotlight should reaim them as fast as possible.
- The **Right Hand** cannot kill the player by itself, but the enemies that spawn alongside it will without enough DPS, especially when combined with the **Right Hand** and Left Hand's abilities.
- Multiple high DPS towers, like the Minigunner, Accelerator or Ranger are recommended to deal with them.
- Towers like the Golden Soldier can be quite effective against them when there are multiple of them placed down.
- The Medic is a reliable tower to cleanse stuns.
- Do note that the **Right Hand** can kill your towers.
- It is advised to have bait towers, however it is not a requirement since the only way to kill the Right **Hand** is by using the Spotlight.
Trivia: - The **Right Hand** was given to the Narrator as a gift from Lord Exo. Its name is *Righty*.
- The **Right Hand** was most likely inspired by the Master Hand from *Super Smash Bros*.
- The fact that the **Right Hand** has 300,000 health could also be a reference to the Master Hand having 300 health in *Super Smash Bros*.
- After losing to the Left Hand and **Right Hand**, a laugh could be heard.
- This along with the Left Hand are the second bosses to have the ability to kill towers, with the first being the Raider Boss.
- The **Right Hand** spawned shortly after the Left Hand.
- When summoning enemies, the enemies were called "*Hand Boss Right's _____*" instead of "*Right Hand's _____*".
- The **Right Hand** would indirectly return as an enemy in The Narratorium as part of the Narrator.

ripped_elf_krampus_frosthold.name: Ripped Elf
ripped_elf_krampus_frosthold.description: The Ripped Elf was the first boss of Krampus Frosthold as part of the Krampus' Revenge Event. It was quite slow but had a high amount of health.

notice.text: Ripped Elf (Krampus Frosthold) has been removed from the game as of the 31st of January 2024 as it was part of the Krampus' Revenge Event.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Snowball Fight** - **Ripped Elf** picks up a large ball of snow and tosses it at a tower, stunning all towers around it when it lands.

Description: The **Ripped Elf** was the first boss of Krampus Frosthold as part of the Krampus' Revenge Event. It was quite slow but had a high amount of health. It was also immune to being frozen by freezing towers and being slowed down by the Toxic Gunner. The Electroshocker and Warden and could only slow it down. It had one ability, *Snowball Fight*, where it tossed a massive snowball at a tower, which stunned it and other towers near it.
Appearance: The **Ripped Elf** was a large enemy with a waist, lower legs, and arms on its rig. It had a tan skin color. It also had a red buttoned up shirt with thin white stripes which had its sleeves torn off. It also had dark grey pants with thin white stripes, along with black shoes. On its waist was a belt with a golden buckle. It wore red boxing gloves with white cuffs, as well as a white armband on its right arm. There was also a tattoo on its left arm, which was a red heart with an arrow going through it, with the words "SANTA" written on it in white. This could also be seen on the back of the shirt. It had a brown beard and long ears on its head.
Strategy: - High DPS towers, like the Golden Minigunner, Minigunner or Accelerator are recommended against this.
- The Pursuit and Ranger can be especially useful, as they are immune to being stunned.
- The Commander and DJ Booth can be used to boost the firerate and range of these towers respectively.
- It is possible to place down cheap towers, like the Pyromancer or Commander to distract the **Ripped Elf** from hitting important towers.
- The **Ripped Elf** can target cliff towers like Mortar and Ranger, but cannot stun them. These towers can also be used to prevent the **Ripped Elf** from attacking other important towers.
- Try placing your towers apart from each other as the *Snowball Fight* ability can stun multiple towers at once if they are grouped up.
Trivia: - The **Ripped Elf** had the second lowest health for a major boss in the entire game, only beaten by the Dummy Boss.

ripped_elf_cold_ambush.name: Ripped Elf
ripped_elf_cold_ambush.description: The Ripped Elf was a major boss that exclusively appeared in Cold Ambush as part of the Violent Night Event. It had a high amount of health and an average speed.

abilities.label: Ability 1
abilities.text: **Snowball Toss** - The **Ripped Elf** throws a large snowball at a tower, which explodes and stuns all towers caught in the explosion.

abilities.label: Ability 2
abilities.text: **Tree Cutting** - The **Ripped Elf** throws a large snowball at the Christmas tree, dealing 80 damage to your base.

Description: The **Ripped Elf** was a major boss that exclusively appeared in Cold Ambush as part of the Violent Night Event. It had a high amount of health and an average speed. Unlike most other enemies in Cold Ambush, it did not head to the exit, but instead walked on the plots.

It had two abilities, the first one being *Snowball Toss*. This ability made the **Ripped Elf** pick up a large snowball from the ground and throw it at towers, stunning towers in a small area at the location where the snowball landed. The second ability, *Tree Cutting*, was similar to *Snowball Toss*. However, rather than attacking towers, the **Ripped Elf** would throw onto the Christmas tree with a large snowball instead, dealing 80 damage to the base.
Appearance: The **Ripped Elf** was a large enemy with a waist, lower legs, and arms on its rig. It had a tan skin color. It also had a red buttoned up shirt with thin white stripes which had its sleeves torn off. It also had dark grey pants with thin white stripes, along with black shoes. On its waist was a belt with a golden buckle. It wore red boxing gloves with white cuffs, as well as a white armband on its right arm. There was also a tattoo on its left arm, which was a red heart with an arrow going through it, with the words "SANTA" written on it in white. This could also be seen on the back of the shirt. It had a brown beard and long ears on its head.
Strategy: - Try to have as much base health as possible before these spawn. Otherwise, you may have too little base health to survive its *Tree Cutting* ability.

- The best way to have enough base health would be purchasing multiple plots before it spawns, increasing your base health and making you heal back your base health with passive base health regeneration.
- The Medic can also be used to gain more base health before it spawns, if you lost any base health.
- Multiple early game towers with decent DPS, such as the Golden Crook Boss, Golden Cowboy, Militant or Golden Scout can do pretty well against the **Ripped Elf**.
- Stronger and more expensive towers, such as the Accelerator, Minigunner, Ranger or Engineer can also be used.
- You can also use the Commander and DJ Booth to boost the firerate and range of your towers.
- The DJ Booth can also be quite useful for decreasing upgrade costs of your towers.
- The Medic can be used to cleanse your towers from stuns caused by the **Ripped Elf**.
Trivia: - The **Ripped Elf** parallels P3NGU from the Duck Hunt Event in function.
- The **Ripped Elf**, despite wearing boxer gloves and being shown punching a Speedy Elf in a promotional image, did not actually punch towers, nor did its unit variant punch enemies.
- The **Ripped Elf** could be seen wearing shades in the trailer for the Violent Night Event, although it did not wear them in-game.
- The Ripped Elf unit is based on this enemy.
- The **Ripped Elf** was the only major boss to appear three times in a match.

- Certain bosses like the Molten Warlord could appear three times in a match due to a bug where they were not blacklisted from being duplicated by All Paths. However, as this was not intended, **Ripped Elf** is the only major boss to intentionally do that.

Description: The **Rotting Terror** was a high health enemy that spawns in The Nightmare Realm and Containment in the Hexscape Event. It had the highest health out of all enemies that appeared before it, though it was slower than most of them. It had 50% defense making it receive around 33% less damage from most sources. It also had Freeze Immunity and Stun Immunity, making it harder to slow down. When it first spawned in The Nightmare Realm, it was a Boss enemy, making it even harder to slow down. Additionally, on some waves, it could spawn as a Bloated, Nimble or Aggro enemy.
Appearance: The **Rotting Terror** was a large entity with brown skin. It had multiple neon red veins on its body. It did not have legs, instead having a brown spine. On its left arm, it had a rusty metal claw while on its right arm it has an exposed bone. On its head, it had neon red eyes and grey teeth. It had multiple spikes and tentacles which were the same color as its skin on its body. It wore a rusty red and grey helmet.
Strategy: - Multiple early-game towers, like the Golden Crook Boss, Cowboy, Militant and Golden Soldier can be quite effective against this.
- Stronger towers like the Engineer, Ranger, Minigunner or Gatling Gun can also be used here.
- As the **Rotting Terror** has quite high defense, defense dropping towers like the Pyromancer, DJ Booth or Trapper can against it.
- Because of its Freeze Immunity, freezing towers cannot be used to drop its defense. Additionally, all other forms of defense dropping are currently bugged and do not work.
- The **Rotting Terror** is quite fast for its health, making stalling towers useful. However, because of its immunities, it cannot be knocked back, chilled or frozen, while stuns only slow it down.
- Additionally, when it first spawns in The Nightmare Realm, it is as a Boss enemy, meaning that the stalling options are further limited to just stun slowdown.
- As it is a large enemy, it will be stalled for a shorter amount of time compared to average-sized enemies.
Trivia: - The **Rotting Terror's** appearance and animations are re-used from the Failed Experiment, with most noticeably having the same bone exposure on its right arm, as well as skeletal spine shape trailing out of its torso.
Update History: - **Bug**: Poison and electric defense dropping does not decrease **Rotting Terror's** defense.
- **Rotting Terror** can no longer have its defense dropped while a Boss enemy.
- **Bugfix**: Poison and electric defense dropping towers now can drop its defense, though the Jester still cannot drop it.
Notes: - ↑ Only the first **Rotting Terror** in The Nightmare Realm is a Boss enemy.

Description: The **Rusher** is an enemy that only appears in Polluted Wasteland II. When it has its shield, it has high health, extremely fast speed and high defense. When it loses all of its shield health, its shield breaks, making it slower and decreasing its defense.
The **Rusher** can be spawned by the Nuclear Monster. This means it can also appear in Oops! All slimes!, if spawned by the Nuclear Monster. It also could be spawned by the Mystery, Wave 29 onwards.
Appearance: The **Rusher** is a tall humanoid with a waist in its rig. It has a light green skin color and a dark grey torso, waist and legs. It wears riot gear, which consists of a black and grey tactical vest, knee-pads, shoulder-pads and a helmet with a grey visor. It also has a backpack on its back, which has acid in it. It has a large black riot shield that it runs with and the lower ends of it arms are covered in a green fluid. Most of its gear is worn, having chunks of material missing from its equipment.
Strategy: - Break its shield as fast as possible to slow it down before it becomes a major threat.
- Multiple high DPS towers, such as the Pursuit, Engineer, Ranger and Accelerator can quickly destroy its shield.
- The Commander can boost your towers' firerate, allowing them to kill the **Rusher** quicker.
- The DJ Booth can also be helpful at increasing the range of your towers.
- Using the Electroshocker, Freezer, Sledger or Frost Blaster to slow the **Rusher** is highly recommended due to its swift speed.
- The Electroshocker, Freezer, Frost Blaster, Pyromancer and Golden Pyromancer can also be useful at decreasing its high defense.
- Using high health units like the Mercenary Base's Riot Guards and Necromancer's Giant Skeletons can easily stop them
Trivia: - In the tweet where the **Rusher** was leaked, the meme, Rush B, was referenced.
Update History: - None of the changes are applied to the legacy version.
- Speed increased from Swift (10) to Extremely Swift (12).
- **Bug**: Appears twice in the Index, one of them not loading in any model for the preview.
- **Bugfix**: No longer appears twice in the Index.

rusher_polluted_wasteland.name: Rusher
rusher_polluted_wasteland.description: The Rusher was an enemy that only appeared in Polluted Wasteland Fallen mode, replacing the Hazard.

- Above Average (Without Shield)

Description: The **Rusher** was an enemy that only appeared in Polluted Wasteland Fallen mode, replacing the Hazard.

In Polluted Wasteland Fallen mode, the **Rusher** replaced the Hazard and was significantly faster, matching the speed of the Glitch with its shield while also boasting far more health. However, once the **Rusher's** health dropped to half, it lost its shield and became much slower. Previously, the **Rusher** was spawned by the Nuclear Fallen King and the Mystery upon their death from Wave 29 onward.
Appearance: The **Rusher** was similar to the Hazard and Fallen Rusher. However, it had a grey hazmat suit with more coverings and a tactical vest. It had a green reflective and translucent riot shield that it ran with. While the shield appeared in front of the **Rusher**, it did not negate damage. It also had diamond-plated black knee pads, gloves and boots.
Strategy: - Reduce the **Rusher's** health down to half health in order to slow it down.
- As they appear in large numbers, a Rocketeer or Mortar may be required to tackle these.
- However, due to these towers' slow projectile speed, they might not be able to hit **Rushers**.
- You may need to set these towers to target *Closest* to have a higher chance in hitting the **Rusher**.
- High DPS towers, like the Ranger, Turret or Minigunner, will be required to tackle **Rushers**.
- Due to the **Rusher's** high speed and high health, the Commander and DJ Booth may also be required to boost firerate and increase the range of towers, respectively.
- You can use the Electroshocker, Freezer or Frost Blaster to slow down **Rushers**.
Trivia: - This is the second enemy to have a negative downgrade when it loses health, after the Beehive.
- The **Rusher** and its animation is closely related to R2DA's Halloween 2019 Ticker.
- A Hardcore variant of the **Rusher** exists, the Fallen Rusher.
- The **Rusher** has more health, but the Fallen Rusher is much faster, having a speed of 15 while the **Rusher** as 12.
- Before the Overhaul Update, the **Rusher** could appear in regular Fallen mode when the Mystery died from wave 29 onwards.
- The **Rusher's** mask is the Fire Fighter Hazard Mask accessory from the Roblox catalog.
Update History: - **Rusher** can now be spawned from the Mystery upon its death in regular Fallen mode.
- **Rusher** can no longer be spawned from the Mystery upon its death in regular Fallen mode.

rusted.name: Rusted
rusted.description: The Rusted was an enemy with an average speed and more health than the Chained. Though it was not considered a boss, it had high health for its debut.

notice.text: Rusted has been removed from the game as of the 13th of October 2019.

Description: The **Rusted** was an enemy with an average speed and more health than the Chained. Though it was not considered a boss, it had high health for its debut. This could be considered a tougher variation of the Golden as it had much higher health. However, the **Rusted** was not immune to splash damage.
Appearance: The **Rusted** was made entirely out of corroded metal. It had brown skin and a brown wristband on its left arm. Its torso and legs were black. Metal protrusions could be seen just above its waist on the bottom left side of its torso. It was about the same size as the Golden.
Strategy: - The **Rusted** does not spawn in large hordes, so high DPS towers, such as the Turret and the Minigunner, can easily defeat this enemy.
- Due to **Rusteds** spawning very unfrequently, they are not much of a threat.
- Unlike Goldens, the **Rusted** is not immune to explosions.
- The **Rusted** is not immune to anything, unlike other enemies that spawn alongside it.
- This means that the Rocketer can easily wipe them out.
Trivia: - A humanoid figure similar in appearance to the **Rusted** can be found on the Legacy Gilded Path map.
- The legacy Hefty's appearance fairly resembles the **Rusted**.

sack_noob.name: Sack Noob
sack_noob.description: The Sack Noob was an enemy that appeared in The Narratorium as a part of The Final Act Event.

notice.text: Sack Noob was previously removed from the game on the 11th of March 2026 as it was part of the The Final Act Event, though it has been made available through the Sandbox mode.

Description: The **Sack Noob** was an enemy that appeared in The Narratorium as a part of The Final Act Event. It had higher health than all the enemies that appear above it, but it was also slower than them. While it did not have it by default, it generally spawned with Aggro.
Logbook Description: "*Sack Noob is designed to take punches. The stuffing inside dampens blows dealt and allows them to take a significant amount of damage. Many of the Sack Noob are hand-crafted by Righty, as it seems to enjoy the delicate process of stitching.*"
Appearance: The **Sack Noob** is a plushie that resembles a stereotypical Roblox noob. It has yellow skin, blue torso and gren legs. On its torso, it has a zipper. It has two black button eyes and a giant open mouth with a visible tongue. It has two walking animations it can use.
Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in The Narratorium is listed instead.
- Early-game towers like the Crook Boss, Golden Soldier or Golden Crook Boss are pretty useful here.
- The Toxic Gunner and Electroshocker can be used to kill multiple at once.
- Later on, the **Sack Noob** becomes rather weak, meaning most towers should be capable of defeating them, including late-game towers like the Accelerator, Turret, Ranger or Pursuit.
Trivia: - The **Sack Noob** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.

- The design concept of the **Sack Noob** is likely inspired by *Sackboy* from the *Little Big Planet* franchise, with both having a zipper on their chest, black eyes and an open smiling mouth with a visible tongue in it.
Update History: - **Sack Noob** removed from the main game, now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.

scarecrow_lunar_overture.name: Scarecrow
scarecrow_lunar_overture.description: The Scarecrow was a fast enemy that appeared in the first and second acts of the Lunar Overture Event.

notice.text: Scarecrow (Lunar Overture) has been removed from the game as of the 21st of December 2023 as it was part of the Lunar Overture Event.

Description: The **Scarecrow** was a fast enemy that appeared in the first and second acts of the Lunar Overture Event. It had higher health and was faster than every enemy that appeared before it. In the second act, it would sometimes spawn as a Hidden enemy.
Appearance: The **Scarecrow** took the appearance of a scarecrow. It was made out of orange straw. It wore a torn purple shirt and hat, which had brown patches on them. On its back, it had a wooden cross. It also had a black carved smile on its face.
Strategy: - Cheap towers with high DPS, such as the Ace Pilot, Militant or Golden Scout can be very useful against it.
- Area of effect towers, such as the Golden Pyromancer, Pyromancer and Executioner, are effective against the **Scarecrow** as it spawns in hordes.
- In later waves in the second act, this enemy spawns as hidden. However, by that point you should have high DPS towers with hidden detection, making them quite easy to kill.

Strategy: - Cheap towers with high DPS, such as the Crook Boss, Swarmer or Minigunner can be quite useful against this.

Description: The **Scarecrow** was an enemy that appeared exclusively in Nightmare Carnival as part of the Halloween 2019 Event. It had more health and was slightly faster than the Strong Mummy.
The **Scarecrow** could have been spawned by Jack O' Bot and the Reaper.
Appearance: The **Scarecrow** was based on real life scarecrows used on farms that are meant to scare off birds from eating crops. The **Scarecrow** wore dark navy overalls, pebble dark orange shirt, black pants and a black witch hat. Its skin was light orange wool to symbolize straw. Dark brown wrappings could be seen around both of its arms and across its waist. It was faceless.
Strategy: - The Shredder can be upgraded to Level 3 before wave 5 and it will be able to take out most of the **Scarecrows** that spawn using its *Knife Throw* ability.
- The Soldier and Paintballer can deal some damage to **Scarecrows**, but by the time they first appear, there should be at least a few Minigunners placed down.
- Military Bases can be used as a cheap method to reduce the impact of **Scarecrows** reaching the end of the path, though they should not be relied upon.
Trivia: - The **Scarecrow** skin for the Pyromancer has almost the same appearance to the **Scarecrow**.
- Weirdly, the **Scarecrow** appeared in the Halloween 2020 Event Trailer despite not appearing in the event.

Description: The **Scout** is an enemy that only appears in Pizza Party. It is a very troublesome foe due to its high health and speed for when it appears.
Appearance: The **Scout** is a robot that resembles the Level 0 and Level 3 Default Scout. It has pale skin, grey torso, sleeves and cap, dark grey backpack, dark green pants and knee-pad, and black shoe. The **Scout's** face is torn off and is hanging from its head, with multiple other parts of its body also being torn off, most notably its left shoulder, part of its left arm and its right foot, all of them also reveal the **Scout's** endoskeleton and wires.
On death, it will shake and flail its arms around, emit yellow sparks, and then power down, with the yellow lights on its backpack turning off. It also plays a powering down sound when it dies.
Strategy: - Cheap towers with high DPS, such as the Minigunner, Crook Boss, Brawler or multiple low Level Golden Scouts are recommended, as the **Scout** has quite high health.
- More expensive towers like the Accelerator or Golden Minigunner can also be used, if you are able to afford them.
- Towers that can slow down the **Scout**, such as the Sledger, Electroshocker, Warden or Toxic Gunner can be quite helpful, as the **Scout** is fairly fast.
- Do note that this is not possible when it first spawns, due to it being a Boss enemy. Most forms of stalling will either not affect it or be significantly weaker.
Update History: - **Bug**: **Scout's** death animation sometimes breaks, causing it to keep playing its walking animation shortly after its death animation.
- Speed increased from Average (3) to Above Average (3.5).
- **Bug**: Appears twice in the Index, one of them not loading in any model for the preview.

Description: The **SCT** was an enemy that could only be found in the legacy Hidden Wave, which meant it could only be found in Fallen mode.
The **SCT** was fast and had high health. However, in comparison to other Hidden Wave enemies, its health was relatively low. It could also shoot towers, stunning them for a short period of time.
Appearance: The **SCT** was also known as the *Fallen Scout*. This was because the **SCT** uses the same model as the Level 3 of the original default Scout. It wore a black tactical vest, knee-pads, shades and gloves. It had reflective black skin, and its torso and legs were granite green. It carried a blue HK P2000 pistol in its right hand to shoot at towers.
Strategy: - High DPS towers, such as the Ranger, Accelerator and Turret are recommended to kill this enemy.
- The Commander is essential in order to boost the firerate of towers to kill this enemy quickly.
- The Electroshocker, Freezer, Frost Blaster, Sledger and Toxic Gunner help greatly in slowing this enemy down.
- When attacking a tower, the **SCT** becomes immobile.
- For this reason, it is recommended to distract this enemy for other towers to attack it.
Trivia: - The **SCT's** appearance was very similar to the first version of the Level 3 Default Scout.
- Its name was shorthand for SCouT.
- Hence, many people called the **SCT** the *Fallen Scout*.
- Ironically, a **Fallen** skin would eventually be added for the Scout during the Fallen Foes Update.
- The **SCT's** health was likely a reference to the number 666, a number associated with the Devil.
Update History: - **SCT** now appears in the legacy Hidden Wave, which is exclusive to Sandbox mode.
- **SCT** no longer appears in the legacy Hidden Wave, as it has been removed.

Description: The **Security** was an enemy that appeared in The Narratorium as a part of The Final Act Event. It had a decently high health and a decent amount of Defense, though it walked rather slowly. It has one ability, which uses to stun towers for 4 seconds and deal 5,000 damage to units. This bypasses cliff tower stun immunity and the Medic's shield stun immunity. It will target any tower or unit in its range of 28 that is also not in its minimal range of 10.
Logbook Description: "*Security watches all corners of the theater and ensures all guests are safe from (Outside) danger. With cameras for heads, they will catch anyone in 4K if they're doing something wrong. They patrol silently through hallways and backstage areas - always watching, always listening.*"
Appearance: The **Security** has black shoes and pants with small yellow stripping running up and down. A grey vest with yellow buttons and a black tie with a white under-shirt. On top it wears a red jacket that is open in the front with yellow trimming and yellow buttons. Is has white gloves on its hands and a yellow band on its left forearm. Instead of a head it has a camera with a grey body and yellow lens along with four red dots with one being in each corner. It also wears a red military esc beret with a yellow bottom sitting on the left side of its camera. On the outside of its right leg it has a taser which has a grey body and yellow outside.
It also walks with its arms behind its back while its camera slowly moves left and right.
Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in The Narratorium is listed instead.
- High DPS towers like the Accelerator, Mercenary Base, Golden Minigunner, Warlock or Ranger are recommended against this.
- Cliff towers cannot be used to avoid its stun, as it bypasses cliff tower stun immunity. Towers like the Pursuit or Brawler can still be used however, as they will not be targeted.
- Towers like the DJ Booth or Commander can be used to boost their statistics.
- The Medic cannot be used to shield towers from its stun as the **Security** bypasses its shield.

Description: The **Shadow** is a relatively high health enemy that cannot be attacked by towers without hidden detection. The **Shadow** is faster than the Abnormal and also has more health than it. Because of its relatively early debut and because it is hidden, it can quickly become a problem without adequate hidden detection.
The **Shadow** appears Sandbox exclusive, Golden and Legacy Fallen modes.
The Dark Necromancer can also spawn the **Shadow**. It also can be spawned by the Mystery.
Appearance: **Variant 1**

The current version of the **Shadow** has a translucent black body. It has a white slash across its face with two lines leaking from the right side of it. It also emits dark purple smoke from its torso.
**Variant 2**
The Enemies Beta version of the **Shadow** has a black translucent body, with its limbs, torso and head fading into a glowing purple. It also has glowing purple veins on its head and arms.
It will fade completely, then fade back into view at regular intervals.
**Variant 3**
The original version of the **Shadow** had a translucent black body. It was faceless and emitted purple smoke from its torso.
Strategy: - Most early game towers gain hidden detection. Such towers are recommended to deal with early **Shadows**.
- As **Shadows** spawn in hordes, the Golden Pyromancer is particularly useful, being able to damage multiple enemies at once and having hidden detection by default.
- The Pyromancer can also be useful against **Shadows**, although it costs more and does not have hidden detection at base level.
- Single target towers, like the Militant, Golden Soldier, Crook Boss or Warden, can also clear out groups of **Shadows**, although they will require more cash to successfully eliminate them.
- The Minigunner and Accelerator are very strong options against **Shadows**, as lower levels have DPS relative to the **Shadows'** health.
- Use of the Farm to get these towers is recommended.
- Be wary of the Accelerator's long charge-up time, cooldown time and short overcharge, as it may allow some **Shadows** to leak without sufficient upgrades.
- For splash damage towers that cannot target **Shadows**, such as the Mortar, if a **Shadow** is caught up in an explosion, they will be dealt splash damage.
- This means that another detectable enemy must be near the **Shadow** for a splash damage tower to hit the **Shadow**.
- While the Rocketeer has hidden detection, it should not be used early on due to its high upgrade and placement cost.
- You can use the Frost Blaster, Freezer and Warden to slow this down, though it is not necessary.
- You cannot use the Toxic Gunner as it does not have hidden detection.
- The Sledger and Electroshocker, while not having hidden detection, can hit **Shadows** if another detectable enemy is near it, as they can hit multiple enemies, but this rarely occurs.
- The Necromancer can be an useful counter to **Shadows**, as its skeletons have higher health than **Shadows** and has piercing to deal with hordes of them.
- Additionally, most of its units have hidden detection, making them even more useful against **Shadows**.

- Barricades can be quite effective against **Shadows** if you are unable to get any reliable hidden detecting towers in time as it can damage hidden enemies. Do be aware that it can only defeat eight **Shadows** before it breaks.
Trivia: - The **Shadow** is the successor of the Ninja, an enemy that existed prior to the Overhaul Update.
Update History: - Now appears in Polluted Wasteland II.
- Now has a new appearance with the Enemies Beta modifier active.
- No longer appears in Fallen mode, as it has been replaced by the Fallen Soul.
- **Shadow** now appears in Golden mode and Legacy Fallen mode, if activated through Sandbox mode.
- **Shadow** no longer appears in Golden mode and Legacy Fallen mode, as they have been removed.
- **Bug**: **Shadow** creates Mystery death particles on death.
- No longer appears in Pizza Party.
- No longer appears in Badlands II.

- No longer appears in Polluted Wasteland II.
- **Bug**: **Shadow’s** model does not load in the Index.
- No longer appears in public rotation of Challenge Maps, as they exclusively appear within Sandbox mode.

Description: The **Shadow Boss** is a large and fast enemy that cannot be attacked by towers without hidden detection. Without major hidden detection defenses, this boss can easily sneak past defenses with little punishment. While it has less health than the Mega Slow and Giant Boss, it is quite fast, making it a large threat.
The **Shadow Boss** formerly appeared in Hardcore mode and Fallen mode. It also appears in two Sandbox exclusive modes, Legacy Fallen mode and Golden mode.
Upon its death, the Mystery Boss may spawn a **Shadow Boss** in Hardcore mode, Legacy Fallen mode and Golden mode. It could also be spawned by the Nuclear Monster.
Appearance: **Variant 1**

The current version of the **Shadow Boss** has a translucent black body with a white emissive slash across its face with two lines leaking from the right side of it. It wears a black cape, has white bandages on its arms and has two pairs of translucent horns on its head, with the second pair being much smaller than the first. It also emits purple smoke from its torso.
It will fade completely, then fade back into view at regular intervals. It plays a yelping sound on death.
**Variant 2**
The third version of the **Shadow Boss** is similar to the current version, except it had no horns on its head.
**Variant 3**
The second version of the **Shadow Boss** is similar to the current version, except it had no face.
**Variant 4**

The first version of the **Shadow Boss** was similar to the Ninja enemy as it had a dark navy skin color, black fabric legs and a dark navy fabric torso. It had a black fabric headband and cape and two pairs of black horns, one of which was much smaller than the other. It wore navy gloves and had multiple grey bandages on each arm. It had a drooling zombie face with glowing white eyes.
Strategy: - At least one tower with high DPS and hidden detection is needed when the **Shadow Boss** debuts.
- A Level 3 Accelerator or a few Level 2 or 3 Golden Minigunners can effectively deal with at least most of the **Shadow Boss's** health.
- However, its charge-up time, cooldown and the fast speed of the **Shadow Boss** mean that placing the Accelerator where it has less coverage of the map is very risky.
- An abundance of less powerful towers, like the Militant, Warden, Golden Scout, Golden Soldier, or Minigunners can also dispatch the **Shadow Boss**.
- It is advised not to skip Waves 22 for Hardcore mode as the enemies that spawn can take damage for the **Shadow Boss** that debut on the following wave.
- You can use the Warden, Frost Blaster, and Freezer to slow the **Shadow Boss** down, as it has a fast speed.
- Be aware that due to its large size, it is slowed down for a shorter duration of time by freezing towers and the Warden, compared to average-sized enemies.
- The Toxic Gunner cannot detect the **Shadow Boss** because it does not have hidden detection at any level.
- While the Sledger, Cryomancer and Electroshocker do not have hidden detection, they can indirectly freeze or stun the **Shadow Boss** if there is a non-hidden enemy near it.
- On Wave 25 in Hardcore Mode, three **Shadow Bosses** will spawn, which can be dangerous if you do not have a sufficient defense.

- High DPS towers, such as the Ace Pilot, Accelerator or Golden Minigunner are the best ways to counter these, although the Accelerator is preferred due to the horde of Lead Bosses spawning alongside them.
- Rangers that are buffed by a Level 4+ Ace Pilot can also be effective against them due to their high damage, though this may be more difficult to afford compared to other options.
- Towers can freeze or stun them like the Warden and Freezer can be effective as they may rush past your defenses.
- The Level 4+ Military Base's *Airstrike* ability can severely damage the three of them if you time the ability right.
- The Mortar cannot target **Shadow Bosses**, but it can hit them through splash damage, if another detectable enemy is near the **Shadow Boss**.
- The Rocketeer can be effective against the **Shadow Boss** because of its hidden detection and high DPS.
- The Commander is recommended against the **Shadow Boss** as it boosts the firerate of towers and can deal extra damage to the **Shadow Boss** itself.
- A Level 4+ Ace Pilot can give hidden detection to towers that do not have it, allowing them to deal damage to the **Shadow Boss**.
- The tower must be in range of the Ace Pilot's runway for them to receive hidden detection.
- Slow firing towers such as the Hunter are less effective against the **Shadow Boss** due to its speed.
Trivia: - The cape used by the **Shadow Boss** is a retextured version of the Guardian of the Night Cape accessory from the Roblox catalog.
- The headband used by the first version of the **Shadow Boss** is the Black Ninja Headband of the Silent Sun accessory from the Roblox catalog.
Update History: - Speed increased from Above Average to Fast (6).

- **Bugfix**: The horns on the **Shadow Boss** no longer fall off when spawning.

Description: The **Shivergeist**, internally referred to as **Frost Wraith**, is a Hidden enemy that appears in Frost mode. It is a slightly fast enemy with a decent amount of health. Due to it being a Hidden enemy, only towers with hidden detection can target it. It is also a Ghost enemy, which means units cannot collide with it. Moreover, anything that deals unit collision damage also cannot deal damage to it.
Upon death, the **Shivergeist** will apply a 33% speed boost to any enemy in its range of 15 for 5 seconds. These boosts can stack.
Appearance: The **Shivergeist** is a floating creature with no legs, instead having aquamarine chunks of ice below its torso instead. It has an entirely translucent body. Its arms are not connected to its body, nor is its head. It has icy teardrop-shaped spikes coming out of either side of its head, with more minor spikes appearing as well. It has glowing white eyes and no mouth. Its arms are covered in ice and the ice forms into claws to make for its hands. Its torso crumbles apart toward the bottom.
Strategy: - Since this enemy appears somewhat later into the match, hidden detection should be available.
- Late game tower with it like the Accelerator, Turret, Juggernaut, Engineer or Enforcer.
- As it has Ghost, summoner towers like the Necromancer or Military Base will be far less effective.
Trivia: - The name **Shivergeist** comes from a combination of two words: *shiver* from English and *geist* from German, which roughly translates to Ghost, Spirit and Mind.
- The **Shivergeist** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.

Description: The **Shotgunner** is a large and high health enemy that appears in Pizza Party. It has a high amount of health, decent defense but a slightly slow speed. It also has the Stun Immunity, which makes the Warden and Electroshocker only slow it down instead of fully stopping it and knockback towers cannot knock it back, and the Freeze Immunity, preventing it from being frozen or chilled.
Appearance: The **Shotgunner** is a robot that resembles the Level 4 Default Shotgunner. It has dark skin, black mask, torso, sleeves, pants, gloves and harness, grey headset and shoes, shotgun shell bandolier, shotgun shells belt and shotgun shell pouch on arms, and red button knee-pads. It also has yellow button eyes which are popped out of its head, wires protruding from the **Shotgunner** and a battery pack on its back.
On death, it will shake and flail its arms around, emit yellow sparks, and then power down, with the yellow light on its backpack turning off. It also plays a powering down sound when it dies.
Strategy: - When dealing with the **Shotgunner** when it first debuts, high DPS towers are best. Such towers include the Accelerator and Ranger.
- The Commander should be used to further boost the firerate of these towers.

- Do note that the Accelerator will remain locked onto the **Shotgunner** until it is defeated, letting other enemies get past. Other towers should be placed to deal with these enemies when using the Accelerator.
- The Military Base's Tank and Railgun Tank are quite strong against **Shotgunners**, as their collision and splash damage ignore the **Shotgunner's** defense.
- Later on however, stronger splash damage towers such as Mortar should be used instead of the Military Base due to **Shotgunners** appearing more frequently in later waves with higher health.
- The Ranger can be used, as in addition to dealing high DPS to the **Shotgunner**, it can counter the Balloon Kid, another enemy that appears in Pizza Party.
- With the Lost Souls modifier active, your high DPS options are mostly limited to the Minigunner and Golden Minigunner, which should be used.

- It is not recommended to skip a wave until the **Shotgunner** is defeated. Otherwise, the enemies from the following wave may overcome your towers while they are still trying to deal with the **Shotgunner**, with the **Shotgunner** acting as a meat shield.
- Later on, **Shotgunners** will spawn in hordes. Towers that can damage multiple enemies at once, like the Executioner, Mortar or Gladiator can deal lots of damage to these hordes.
- Additionally, most splash damage towers ignore the **Shotgunner's** defense, making them even more effective.
- Generally, however, these towers are unable to outright defeat hordes of **Shotgunners**, so high DPS towers should still be used alongside them.

- As it has a rather large amount of health and walks quickly, staling towers like the Electroshocker or Warden can be useful here, though a lot of them will be less effective because of its immunities.
- The Warden and Electroshocker can only slow down the **Shotgunner**, instead of fully stopping it.
- Freezing towers cannot freeze or chill it, as it has the Freeze Immunity.
- As it has the Stun Immunity, knockback towers cannot knock it back.
- The **Shotgunner's** defense can be reduced by defense dropping towers like the Pyromancer and Electroshocker.
- Freeze defense dropping towers cannot be used due to the **Shotgunner's** Freeze Immunity.
Update History: - Energy Immunity replaced with Stun Immunity.
- **Bug**: Appears twice in the Index, one of them not loading in any model for the preview.
- Cash given increased from $1,000 to $1,500 every 50% health lost.
- **Bugfix**: No longer appears twice in the Index.
Notes: - ↑ Only the first **Shotgunner** is a Boss enemy.

shrike_crystal.name: Shrike Crystal
shrike_crystal.description: The Shrike Crystal was a crystal that appeared once a Controlled was killed. The crystal stunned nearby towers and were resistant to explosions.

notice.text: Shrike Crystal has been removed from the game as of the 13th of October 2019.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Crystallise** - Gradually expands, stunning all towers within a 7.5 stud radius until it reaches its maximum size.

Description: The **Shrike Crystal** was a crystal that appeared once a Controlled was killed. The crystal stunned nearby towers and were resistant to explosions. You could not lose to these as they could not move, but they had a large amount of health, more than the Slow Boss, and allowed other enemies to pass through. The **Shrike Crystal** was mostly a support enemy as it allowed other enemies to pass stunned towers.
Appearance: At the center of **Shrike Crystals** were Controlled enemies, and white, slightly transparent, marble crystals expanded from it. The **Shrike Crystal** could grow to a size larger than the player.
Strategy: - While you cannot die to the **Shrike Crystal**, they are very dangerous, as the towers near to it cannot attack, allowing faster enemies to overwhelm your defenses.
- These are immune to splash damage from the Demoman, Rocketer and Commando, meaning that they are quite hard to destroy.
- While also immune to splash damage from the Military Base's units, Tanks and Railgun Tanks are effective against the **Shrike Crystal** as their ranged weapons cannot be stunned.
- Other units, such as the Enforcer's SWAT Van and the Crook Boss's Crook 1 and Crook 2, are very effective against the **Shrike Crystal**.
- Long-ranged towers, such as the Outlaw, are recommended as they can be placed far away from the **Shrike Crystal**.
- Make sure you place towers a distance away from the spawn, in case a Controlled is spawn-killed, and make sure you do not place long-ranged towers near the path.
- If you can, relocate your towers away from the **Shrike Crystal**.
- Additionally, you can wait until the **Shrike Crystal** reaches its maximum size as they can no longer stun towers at its greatest size.
Trivia: - The **Shrike Crystal** was a reference to the Shrike from the *Marvel Cinematic Universe*.

Description: The **Shroogma** was the first enemy that spawned in the second night of the Solar Eclipse Event. It had a high amount of health for its debut and had average speed.

Strategy: - Cheap towers with high DPS, such as the Scout, Crook Boss and Ace Pilot are recommended.
- For the Scout and Crook Boss, you can use their **Golden** skin for better performance.
- As these spawn in hordes, towers that can damage multiple enemies at once like the Gladiator and Mortar are recommended.
Trivia: - The **Shroogma's** design is based on the fly agaric, a mushroom.

Description: The **Siege Engine**, internally referred to as **Frost Spawner**, was an enemy that only appears in Outpost 32 as part of the Operation I.C.E Event. Unlike other enemies in the event and even the game in general, it does not head to the exit and instead acts as the entrance for enemies to spawn from. It is still an enemy despite this, having its own statistics, an Index entry and even being affected by modifiers which apply hats to enemies like the Fireworks modifier.

It will kill units that collide with it and trigger road obstacles. As it drives on the path, it will run over all enemies in its path, killing them. It uses its own path instead of the regular one, though the main difference here is that its path takes a few shortcuts. This enemy is not required to be destroyed for waves to progress. While it has multiple attributes, they are all applied so that it is immune to as many sources of damage as possible and to prevent towers from attacking it. Its No Target and God attributes can be removed with the Pumpkin Bomb, which will also boost its health from 0 to 50,000 (100,000 if the Pumpkin Bomb also applied Bloated), making it possible to be destroyed.
Logbook Description: "*The Frost Spawner used in Outpost 32 to take down the Outpost's defenses. How did you get this anyways?!?*"
Appearance: The **Siege Engine** is a light blue siege engine, mostly empty except for a blue portal. When it moves on the path, the portal will be closed via an overhead hatch, and a trail of wind will appear near it.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Outpost 32 is listed instead.
- You do not need to, and cannot, destroy the **Siege Engine** in most regular occurrences.
- If you need to destroy the **Siege Engine** for the Logbook do note that it is extremely cumbersome and time-consuming.

- You require the use of the Pumpkin Bomb removing the No Target and the God attributes. Therefore, it can only be destroyed on Outpost 32 Easy difficulty, as the Hard difficulty does not permit the use of consumables.
- The odds of this occurring is extremely low, so you will likely require multiple Pumpkin Bomb for these attributes to be removed.

- Once God and No Target attributes are removed, you can set any towers to target last which will enable you to destroy the **Siege Engine**, with the exception of the Accelerator, which is unable to target the **Siege Engine**, even with No Target removed.
- Towers with long range, such as the Ranger, and the Pursuit are suited for this.
- You can also use the Nuke to destroy the **Siege Engine**, though the God attribute must be removed first.
- After it is destroyed, enemies will still spawn normally at where the **Siege Engine** was at before.
- The Gatling Gun can bypass the No Target attribute with its *FPS* ability, however you still need to get rid of the God attribute.
Trivia: - This is the second enemy with the God attribute.
- If the player spawns a **Siege Engine** in Sandbox mode, it will head towards the exit without stopping.
Update History: - **Bug**: **Siege Engines** can sometimes be positioned at the wrong angle.
- **Bug**: **Siege Engine** can sometimes stay closed after it stops moving, though this is purely visual.
- Now has a description in the Index.
- **Siege Engine** removed from the main game, now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.
Notes: - ↑ Dependent on how quickly barriers are broken.
