Description: The **Sin** is an enemy that only appears when summoned on death by a Demon. It has a rather low amount of health for its debut, though it spawns in large hordes from the Demon. It also has the Burn Immunity, meaning it cannot be set on fire.
Appearance: The **Sin** has a black and red magma body, with a head that had an open mouth with jagged teeth and a pair of horns. The interior of the head is glowing yellow. It also has a small tail.
Strategy: - High DPS towers, like the Pursuit, Engineer, Accelerator, Ranger or Turret are recommended against this.
- As it always spawns in groups from Demons, high DPS towers with splash damage capabilities, like the Ranger, Pursuit or Engineer can be especially useful here.
- The Commander and DJ Booth can be used to boost the statistics of these towers.
- Area of effect towers, like the Mortar or Electroshocker can be helpful at clearing out the **Sins**.
Trivia: - The **Sin** and the Pumpkid are some of the smallest enemies in the game.

notice.text: Sin (Lunar Overture) has been removed from the game as of the 21st of December 2023 as it was part of the Lunar Overture Event.

Description: The **Sin** is an enemy that only appeared in the second act of the Lunar Overture Event. It did not spawn naturally, instead being spawned by other enemies. It had two variants, a small variant which had 400 health and a large variant with 800 health. The small variant also had an above average speed, while the big variant had below average speed.
The **Sin** was spawned by the Demon upon its death, but only the small variant. It could also be summoned by the Reaper, which could summon both the small and big variant.
Appearance: The **Sin** had a small humanoid with it's black and red magma body, with a head that had an open mouth with jagged teeth and a pair of horns. The interior of the head was glowing yellow. It also had a small tail.
Strategy: - High DPS towers, like the Golden Minigunner, Accelerator or Minigunner are useful against this.

- Towers with sufficient damage and range, such as the Mortar and Ranger, are also viable due to the fact that the **Sin** may occasionally leak through defense as they are accompanied by large hordes of enemies with substantial health.
- As these spawn in hordes, splash damage towers like the Mortar or Pursuit can be very useful here.
- Do note that you do not earn any money from the **Sin** as it is a summoned enemy.
- The Cowboy and Golden Cowboy can still generate cash from **Sins** with its Cash Shot, but not by damaging them.
- However, these towers have their income reduced in the second act of the Lunar Overture Event, making them much less effective.
Trivia: - The **Sin** and the Pumpkid are some of the smallest enemies in the game.

Description: **Sir Hopsalot** was a knight-bunny enemy that exclusively appeared in Eggy Island as part of the Spring 2020 Event. This debuted in easy mode with 2,250 health and in hard mode with 2,750 health. **Sir Hopsalot** moved quite slowly in easy mode but moved just slightly slower than the Bunny in hard mode.

**Sir Hopsalot** had two abilities. Similar to the Bunny, it could throw a carrot club at a tower, which stunned it and any other towers in the immediate area. However, it could also use its shield to limit most forms of damage to two per firerate.
Appearance: **Sir Hopsalot** wore a grey knight helmet, carried an egg shield and wielded a carrot club. It was similar in appearance to the Bunny, except its torso had a pink egg design, instead of a grey one. It had grey skin and its bunny ears are sticking out of its helmet.
Strategy: - The *Shield* ability is activated very often by **Sir Hopsalot**. As most forms of damage are capped to a maximum of two, towers with a fast firerate, such as the Minigunner, Crook Boss and Soldier, are very effective against **Sir Hopsalot**.
- Slow firing towers, such as the Sniper and Outlaw, are not recommended against **Sir Hopsalot**.
- The Commander can be used to boost the firerate of towers and assist in defeating **Sir Hopsalot**.
- In hard mode, units, such as the Enforcer's SWAT Van and Military Base's Tank, deal full collision damage to **Sir Hopsalot**.
- The Pyromancer, Electroshocker and Freezer are recommended to slow this enemy down.
- Try not to cluster towers close together as **Sir Hopsalot** will be able to stun lots of them with just one *Carrot Throw*.
- You may also use cheap towers, such as the Scout or Soldier, to distract **Sir Hopsalot** as it is immobile while performing its *Carrot Throw* ability.
Trivia: - Similar to the Bunny, **Sir Hopsalot** was likely based on *R2DA's* Easter Brute, in terms of attack.
- The name **Sir Hopsalot** is a reference to Sir Lancelot, one of the greatest Knights of the Round Table.
- **Sir Hopsalot** is a portmanteau of Sir Lancelot and the word "hop".

Description: The **Skeleton** is an enemy that appears in Easy, Casual, Challenge Trials, Badlands II, Polluted Wasteland II, Basic Arena PVP and Molten Arena PVP modes. It also appears in the tutorial and first chapters of Story mode. The **Skeleton** is primarily summoned by the Necromancer, it does not appear naturally in most modes except Badlands II. A **Skeleton** summoned by the Necromancer has a chance to have the Hidden attribute. It has a decent amount health and speed.
The **Skeleton** was replaced by the Brick Man in Headache Headquarters.
Appearance: The **Skeleton** is made entirely of white parts that resemble a skeletal humanoid. It does not have a full torso, but instead has the bone cage for it. Its head is slightly smaller than most other enemies and has two large black eyeholes.
On death, the **Skeleton** falls into a pile of bones while playing a bone shaking sound. Its legacy version was pretty similar, though it has a different walking animation and no death animation.
Strategy: - The **Skeleton** can be a threat when it first appears, as many can be summoned by the Necromancer if it is not killed quickly, leading to other problems.
- Killing the Necromancer before it can summon any **Skeletons** is recommended.
- Towers like the Soldier, Golden Scout, Militant or Ace Pilot can be quite effective against this.

- High DPS towers like the Minigunner, Crook Boss and Accelerator can be prepared specifically for this enemy if early game towers are not enough, using the Farm to get them as they may be quite expensive.
- Do note that the Accelerator, if locked onto the Necromancer or other strong enemies, will ignore the **Skeletons** until the targeted enemy is defeated or leaves its range.

- The Ranger struggles against hordes of **Skeletons** due to its slow firerate. It can instead be set to *Strongest* to target and kill the Necromancer while other towers take care of the **Skeletons**.
- Area of effect towers, like the Mortar, Rocketeer or Assassin can be quite useful as they can damage all the **Skeletons** as well as the Necromancer at once.
- The **Skeletons** can be converted by the Hacker to damage the Necromancer that summoned them.
- Do note that you do not earn any money from the **Skeleton** as it is a summoned enemy.
- The **Skeleton** moves at a somewhat fast pace. You may want to use crowd control towers like the Sledger, Warden or Electroshocker, though this is not necessary.

- The Sledger, Frost Blaster and Electroshocker are particularly effective as they can slow multiple **Skeletons** down at once. Additionally, their high damage makes them also useful at killing **Skeletons**.
Trivia: - The **Skeleton** reuses the Lunar Overture Skeleton's walking and death animations.
- The **Skeleton** reuses the **Graveyard** Farm's cash production sound for its death sound.
- The **Skeleton's** previous death sound was similar to the Skeleton hurt sound from *Minecraft*.
- The **Skeleton** is very similar to the Bones that appeared in the Halloween 2020 Event and Solar Eclipse Event.

Description: The **Sleigh** was an enemy that appeared on Wave 20 in Krampus Frosthold as part of the Krampus' Revenge Event. It had a decent amount of health, average speed and moderate defense. It also flew on a sleigh, meaning that it could not collide with most units, as well as being undetectable by a majority of towers and units.
Appearance: The **Sleigh** was a brownish orange and white sleigh. It had golden rims along most of its structure, as well as golden thrusters on the back of its feet. It had yellow headlights and small wings as well. The sleigh was piloted by an elf with pale skin. It had a green shirt with white fur along the sleeves, as well as stitch lines on the sides of the arms. It had a black belt, dark green pants and black shoes. It also wore a green Christmas hat.
Strategy: - The **Sleigh** appears in hordes alongside many other enemies and Krampus.
- The Mortar is a strong option against the **Sleigh**, as well as being strong against all hordes in general. Its long range also ensures that the **Sleigh** does not get past your defenses.
- The Executioner is strong for the same reasons the Mortar is, though with the added benefit of being a good option early game.
- The Ranger and Pursuit can also deal with the **Sleigh**, as well as having strong single-target damage against enemies like Krampus.

Description: The **Sleigh** was an enemy that only appeared in Cold Ambush as part of the Violent Night Event. It had a decent amount of health, an average speed and 35% defense. It also, as the name suggests, used a sleigh to fly, making it a Flying enemy. This means that it could not collide with units, as well as being undetectable by a majority of towers and units.
Appearance: The **Sleigh** was a brownish orange and white sleigh. It had golden rims along most of its structure, as well as golden thrusters on the back of its feet. It had yellow headlights and small wings as well. The sleigh was piloted by an elf with pale skin. It had a green shirt with white fur along the sleeves, as well as stitch lines on the sides of the arms. It had a black belt, dark green pants and black shoes. It also wore a green Christmas hat.
Strategy: - As the **Sleigh** is a Flying enemy, it can only be attacked by towers with flying detection.
- The Ace Pilot cannot be used, as it cannot be placed down in Cold Ambush.
- The Executioner can be used against this. Its bouncing mechanic also allows it to be useful at clearing out hordes of enemies that appear in Cold Ambush.
- The Ranger can be quite effective against this, due to its high damage.
- The Engineer can also be used, though do note that only the Engineer itself can detect the **Sleigh**, not its sentries.

- The Gift Bomber unit from the Elf Camp is based on this enemy.
- This enemy returns in the Krampus' Revenge Event with different stats.

Description: The **Slime** is an enemy that appears in Intermediate mode. It can also appear in Molten Arena PVP and The Takeover Event, if a Failed Experiment is killed in it. It has a high amount of health and a decent speed. Additionally, it is spawned by all enemies that have the Slime attribute, with the exception of other **Slimes**.
It is also a primary focus of the Oops! All slimes! challenge map, as all enemies spawn with the Slime attribute, therefore making the **Slime** spawn from every enemy.

As most enemies with the Slime attribute spawn the **Slime**, it can also appear in the Jailed Towers, Back to Basics, Legion and Oops! All slimes! challenge maps. It also appeared in The Classic Event through the Slime attribute.
Appearance: The **Slime** is a humanoid made of a translucent green goo, with bones inside each part of its body. It has a ribcage with a spine, a long bone in each limb, and a skull, which is cracked at the top, going from the middle of the facial area to its right eyehole.
It does a front flip and emits liquid green particles whenever it spawns in. It does not emit shards or dust on death.
Strategy: - Towers with good DPS, such as the Minigunner, Crook Boss, Military Base or Hunter can be quite effective against it.
- Towers with high damage, such as the Rocketeer or Ranger can kill the **Slime** in a single shot.
- The **Slimes** that spawn from enemies with the Slime attribute and the Failed Experiment do not count as summoned enemies, which means they do give you cash upon death.
- Because of this, the Cowboy can be used to generate cash from **Slimes** if they appear from these sources.
Trivia: - The **Slime** used to have an ability that allowed it to transform into the strongest non-boss enemy currently on the map.
- This ability technically was not removed. Instead, the transformation time was increased from 12.5 seconds to 10,000, meaning it takes around three hours for it to transform.
- With the Sandbox mode stat editor, it is possible to give towers fast firerates and no damage, allowing for it to be stalled long enough for the ability to trigger.
- The skeletal system inside of the **Slime** is incredibly different to that of the Skeleton's regular appearance.
- The Fallen Skeleton, however, has a skull that is similar to that of the **Slime**.
- The **Slime** is the only enemy to not emit the shard and dust particles on death since the Entity System Update.
Update History: - Now appears in Classic Candy Cane Lane, Classic Winter, Classic Forest Camp and Classic Island Chaos.
- Has 50 health in Classic Candy Cane Lane and Classic Winter, and 100 in Classic Forest Camp and Classic Island Chaos.
- **Bug**: Nuclear Monster spawns the **Slime** instead of the Radioactive Slime with its *Nuclear Summon* ability.
- No longer appears in Classic Candy Cane Lane, Classic Winter, Classic Forest Camp and Classic Island Chaos, as they have been removed.

- **Bug**: Restarting after dying on wave where the **Slime** starts turning into Failed Experiments will make it always turn into Failed Experiments, even multiple waves before its first wave appearance.
- First wave appearance changed from 10 to 11 in Intermediate mode.

- Now appears in Mid Rank PVP Test.
- No longer appears in the PVP Test as it has been removed.
- Now appears in Molten Arena PVP, carrying over all of its PVP Test statistics.
- Now appears in Sk8 P4rk Pro difficulty as part of The Takeover Event.
- No longer appears in Sk8 P4rk, as it has been removed.

Description: The **Slime** was an enemy that appeared exclusively in Trick or Threat Town as part of the Halloween 2020 Event. It had less health than the Reanimated, but had an average walk speed. When it died, a small slime bubble would be made, which would spawn two Goos.
The **Slime** could be spawned by Lord Sinister.
Appearance: The **Slime** was a completely lime green faceless enemy. All of its body parts were encased in a slime capsule which was slightly translucent. Goo particles were emitted from its body. It was larger than the Undead.
Strategy: - The Goos that the **Slime** splits into are very quick. Make sure to deal with these enemies.
- The Turret deals high damage and has long range, so can perform well against the **Slime** and the Goos that spawn.
- The Ranger and Military Base's units can also work well against the **Slime**.
- These towers are best paired with the Commander as it boosts their firerate.
- If a **Slime** is near the end of the path, try not to kill it, if it is at low health. When it is killed, it will spawn into two Goos which will result in a defeat.
Trivia: - The **Slime** behaved very similar to the Splitter.
- However, the **Slime** did not stun towers when it died.
- The **Slime** may be a reference to the Slime from *Minecraft*.
- The **Slime** was inspired by the Slime from *Evolution Evade*.
- Its mechanics were similar to the Slime from *Tower Battles*.

Description: The **Slow** is an enemy that appears in the Easy, Casual, Challenge Trials, Legacy Molten, Intermediate, Basic Arena PVP and Molten Arena PVP modes, as well as the tutorial and first chapters of Story mode. As the name of it suggests, it is a slow, but relatively strong enemy that requires tower upgrades to be countered.

The **Slow** also has a chance to be spawned by the Mystery upon its death in the Legacy Molten mode. The Grave Digger had a chance to spawn the **Slow** with its *Triumphing Sheol* ability in Easy mode. The **Slow** was also formerly spawned by the Necromancer before its replacement. In The Heights, the **Slow** could have been spawned by the Swordmaster or from the Tombstone when it was destroyed.
It also appeared as parts of the SFOTH Event, Metaverse Champions Event, The Classic Event and The Takeover Event.
Appearance: **Variant 1**

Strategy: - Most towers can deal with the **Slow** effectively.
- Any tower catered towards early game, like the Soldier, Assassin, Brawler, Cowboy, Militant or Cowboy is recommended.
- It is unnecessary to try to get stronger, more expensive towers like the Minigunner solely to deal with **Slows**, as cheaper options fare well against them already.
- Towers that can deal damage to multiple enemies are especially effective against **Slows** as they spawn in hordes. Such towers include the Demoman, Electroshocker, Pyromancer and Shotgunner.

- While not recommended if you do not have high base health, it is an option to avoid defending against the first few waves of **Slows** and simply let them reach the exit, as their low health makes it unlikely to make you lose.
- You can use the Medic to heal the base health back, but it is not necessary.
- As you are not spending money on defenses, you can use the Farm more effectively for the first few waves to get better towers when stronger enemies appear.

Description: The **Slow Boss**, previously known as **Boss2**, is a slow and tough boss that appears in the Easy, Casual, Legacy Molten and Basic Arena PVP modes. It also appeared in the SFOTH Event, The Classic Event and The Takeover Event. Though the **Slow Boss** is slower than the Normal Boss and Necromancer, its high health makes it a considerable threat. Later on in the game, it will appear in large, mostly packed, hordes, causing many problems if you lack high DPS towers.

The **Slow Boss** can be spawned by the Mystery Boss upon its death in the Legacy Molten and Easy modes. In Easy mode, the Grave Digger used to rarely spawn the **Slow Boss**. The **Slow Boss** could also have been spawned by the Swordmaster.
Appearance: **Variant 1**
**Variant 1**

Strategy: - Many towers can be used to deal with the **Slow Boss** on its debut.
- High-DPS towers like the Minigunner and Turret are able to defeat the **Slow Boss** rather quickly.
- Stronger early game towers like the Golden Scout, Militant, Soldier, Brawler, Ace Pilot and Cowboy, when upgraded to higher levels are strong options against the **Slow Boss**.
- Multiple towers can take advantage of the **Slow Boss'** slow speed.
- Short-ranged towers like the Assassin are able to get many more hits in, making them more effective.
- The Military Base and Crook Boss' units will have more time to shoot at the **Slow Boss** before colliding into it.
- The Brawler on Levels 2 and above is able to stunlock multiple **Slow Bosses**.
- Though not necessary, all stalling towers will work against the **Slow Boss**, and can slow it down significantly.
- However, the first **Slow Boss** in Easy mode is a Boss enemy. This means it is either fully or partially unaffected by all forms of stalling.
- Do note that the **Slow Boss** large size makes the freezing, knockback and stunning towers like Freezer, Brawler and Warden less effective than usual.
Trivia: - The original name and appearance were based on the Boss2 from *Tower Battles*.
- When the Uber Mystery was in the game, it had a chance of spawning the **Slow Boss** upon its death in Golden and Fallen modes.
- In Hardcore Testing BETA, the **Slow Boss** had 10 defense.
- This would be later re-added for the modern version with 25% defense. Although the legacy version has none.
- The death sound **Slow Boss** makes is a deeper sound than Boss2's from *Tower Battles*.
- The Slow King and the Mega Slow can be considered 2 Hardcore variants of the **Slow Boss**.

- Due to a bug, the **Slow Bosses** spawning on wave 29 of Easy mode were separated by an extremely long amount of time. Because of this, even without skipping the wave, the enemies would not have enough time to spawn, causing them to spawn on Wave 30 instead.

- Since these enemies would not count as enemies that spawned on Wave 30, you could have them spawn after triumphing by killing just the enemies that spawned on wave 30. You could reach zero base health after triumphing this way, but this would not make you lose.
- This was later fixed on 12th of March 2022, where the time between each spawn is now quicker, with each spawn being 2 seconds instead of 8 seconds.

slow_king.description: The Slow King is a high health enemy that appears in Hardcore and Voidcore modes. It has high health and Shield Health, alongside a high amount of Defense.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Royal Aura** - Has a forcefield which gives it 60% Defense. Once all of its Shield Health is depleted, its Defense gained from the forcefield is removed alongside Freeze Immunity and Aggro, if it has it.

Description: The **Slow King** is a high health enemy that appears in Hardcore and Voidcore modes. It has high health and Shield Health, alongside a high amount of Defense. When it spawns in, it has a forcefield around itself which grants it 60% Defense. Once all of its Shield Health is depleted, the forcefield will disappear, removing the Defense, and if the **Slow King** has it, the Freeze Immunity and Aggro it has.
Logbook Description: "*Where a realm falls, its king is not always quick enough to fall with it. The Slow King sat in the ruins of their realm after trying to save their people. As the Void bloomed across the landscape and everything they had built came crumbling down, the Slow King was the last to accept defeat. It was not until they were recognized by Void Caster that they could continue on beside their people, who were now Souls for the Void.*"
Appearance: The **Slow King** has a white body with a large hole in its face. It wears a purple king's robe, black pants, gold armbands, a purple cape, a gold crown and a glowing purple necklace. When initially spawning in, it has a purple forcefield around it which disappears when its Shield Health is depleted.
Strategy: - High DPS towers like the Juggernaut, Turret, Engineer, Accelerator or Kingpin can be used against this.

- Splash damage towers like the Mortar, Rocketeer and Golden Demoman ignore the **Slow King's** Defense, allowing them to take out its shield much earlier, while also handling the hordes they often appear in.
- High DPS towers are recommended against the **Slow King** once its shield is broken. Additionally, it also loses its Freeze Immunity, though it retains its Stun Immunity.
- Towers that melt Defense such as the Pyromancer and Golden Pyromancer can greatly weaken groups of **Slow Kings**.
Trivia: - The modern **Slow King** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.

Description: The **Slow King** was a slightly slow and tanky enemy that appeared in Hardcore mode. Currently, it can only be spawned in Sandbox mode if the player has the Sandbox Plus+ gamepass. It is similar to the Mega Slow, but has more health and faster speed. The **Slow King** also has Shield Health, and this is attached to its forcefield that it spawns with. With this forcefield, the **Slow King** has a high defense value. Without its shield, it will be reduced to 10%, regardless of what defense it spawned with. If it loses defense, the defense it changes to will include the defense reduction. For example, if its defense got reduced from 80% to 75%, it will have 5% defense after losing all of its Shield Health. The **Slow King** also has Stun Immunity, meaning that the Warden and Electroshocker can only slow it down, while knockback towers cannot knock it back.
The **Slow King** can be spawned by the Void Reaver. The Mystery Boss can spawn the **Slow King** upon its death in Hardcore mode, wave 41 onwards.
Appearance: **Variant 1**
The current **Slow King** is similar to the previous version, except it has a huge slash across its face.
When the **Slow King** spawns, it has a translucent pink forcefield surrounding it. This forcefield disappears when the **Slow King** loses its shield health.
**Variant 2**

The original **Slow King** had green reflective skin. It had tumors on both arms. Its torso and legs were black granite, and it wore diamond-plated armbands. Its cape was black granite and had brown hooks on its shoulders. It wore a slightly tilted dark green granite crown, which indicates that this enemy was royalty. It emitted green particles from its torso and purple particles from its arms. On its torso, was a pink gem. It was faceless and had a twisted left leg.
When the **Slow King** spawns, it has a translucent pink forcefield surrounding it. This forcefield disappears when the **Slow King** loses its shield health.
Strategy: This strategy refers to the state of the game while the **Invisible** still appeared in the Hardcore mode.
- The forcefield around the **Slow King** can be problematic if not taken care of. This is because it gives the **Slow King** a very high defense value.
- The Pursuit can be useful here because of its high DPS and its missiles dealing full damage to defense enemies.
- While being relatively slow, it allows other enemies, like the Lava and Fallen Titan, to go much further along the path.
- Defense dropping towers like the Freezer, Pyromancer or Jester can be used to drop its defense, allowing your towers to deal more damage to it.
- The Electroshocker, Warden or Sledger can be used to slow this down.
- Do note that due to its large size, freezing towers and the Warden will slow it down for a shorter amount of time.

- The **Slow King** also has Stun Immunity, which means that stunning towers like the Warden can only slow it down instead of stopping it completely while knockback towers like the Brawler cannot knock it back.
- After the **Slow King's** forcefield disappears, other towers with high DPS, like the Minigunner, Turret, Accelerator and Ranger, can be used to defeat the **Slow King**.
Trivia: - The **Slow King's** cape is a re-textured version of the Atomic Prussian Cloak accessory from the Roblox catalog.
- This may be considered the Hardcore version of the Slow Boss.
- Oddly, the **Slow King's** forcefield is orange in the Index instead of purple.
Update History: - **Bug**: If the defense of the **Slow King** is decreased, there is a chance that its defense will not decrease to 10% after losing its shield health.
- **Bugfix**: Defense now properly decreases when reduced.
- Energy Immunity replaced with Stun Immunity.
- **Slow King** removed from the main game, now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.
- No longer appears in the Index.

Description: The **Snow Minion** is a enemy that appears in the Frost mode. Like most of that mode's enemies, it first appeared in the Operation I.C.E Event. It is very slow and due to its ability having a very low cooldown, it will spend most of its time throwing snowballs at towers. With these snowballs, it will target a tower or unit, which to the former applies a 70% Fatigue Debuff for 5 seconds and to the latter deal 10 damage to units.
Logbook Description: "*Snow Minions are rascals who enjoy terrorizing other frost creatures with snowballs. It’s believed the Snowmen learned this habit from watching the Snow Minions. While universally despised among the frost army as pests, their cunning nature makes them valuable distractions. They will throw snowballs at towers and units to freeze or slow.*"
Appearance: The **Snow Minion** is an entity with blue skin. It wears a white robe with a hood, which shrouds its head in darkness, only two glowing white eyes being visible. It haso two blue horns coming out of its hood, with the right one being bigger. It wears a grey shirt and pants. It picks up snowballs which it throws at enemies.
Strategy: - Early-game towers like the Golden Scout, Golden Soldier, Brawler or Cowboy can be used to take down the **Snow Minion**.
- The **Snow Minion** only targets one tower or unit at a time. Therefore, groups of towers and units are preferred here, as they will be far less affected by its single target ability.
- Similarly, stun immune early-game towers can also be useful as the **Snow Minion** cannot stun them. This includes towers like the Ace Pilot or Brawler.
- Due to it being rather slow and it being summoned by enemies faster than it, the **Snow Minion** will end up left behind other enemies, allowing it to easily attack towers.
- Changing tower targeting to either *Last Enemy* or if there are not many low health enemies, *Weakest* can help out with clearing these out.

- The Frost Necromancer summons multiple at a time while Frost Mysteries will spawn in groups. This makes AOE towers quite effective at killing them, being able to kill multiple often without even needing to target them directly.
- The **Snow Minion** will target any tower in its range, even if its debuff has no effect on it. This means towers like the DJ Booth, Farm, Military Base or Elf Camp can be used to bait its attack.
Trivia: - The **Snow Minion** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Bug**: **Snow Minion** cannot have its defense dropped by the Jester.

notice.text: Snowman (Village of Despair) has been removed from the game as of the 26th of January 2020 as it was part of the Christmas 2019 Event.

Description: The **Snowman** was an enemy that only appeared in Village of Despair as part of the Christmas 2019 Event. It was slightly faster and had more health than the Frozen. It also could not be frozen by the Freezer or Frost Blaster.
Appearance: The **Snowman** had white sand skin to represent snow. The **Snowman** also wore a top hat on its head and had a carrot nose. There were three black buttons on its torso, and its mouth and eyes were also made out of buttons.
Strategy: - The **Snowman** is completely immune to the Freezer and Frost Blaster, including the Freezer's *Ice Age*.
- This leaves the Pyromancer as a viable option to slow it down.
- As the **Snowman** normally spawns in hordes, the Rocketeer, Mortar and Holiday Archer are quite effective against it.
- A simple Minigunner or Outlaw should be able to take care of these.
- However, as they debut early on during the game, you will have to save for these towers.

Description: The **Snowy** is a fast enemy that appears in the Frost mode. Like most of that mode's enemies, it first appeared in the Operation I.C.E Event. It has a low amount of health and fast speed. During the event, it walked at the same speed as the Frozen.
Logbook Description: "*Snowy is a creature that dwells on mountain peaks and within ice caves. What resembles fur is actually compacted snow from blizzards, and their sharp claws are used to climb ice. They often hunt in packs but remain mostly solitary.*"
Appearance: The **Snowy** is a Yeti-like creature with white fur and neon blue eyes. It has two sharp blue teeth in its mouth and multiple blue horns its body.
Strategy: - Early-game towers like the Golden Scout, Golden Soldier, Cowboy or Crook Boss can be useful against it.
- As these spawn in hordes, AOE towers like the Electroshocker or Archer can also be pretty effective.
- As the **Snowy** is somewhat fast, early-game towers which can stall it, like the Toxic Gunner or Electroshocker can help with its speed, while also being strong enough to deal decent damage to it.
Trivia: - The **Snowy** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Snowy** removed from the main game, now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.
- **Snowy** re-added to the main game, now appears in Frost mode.
- Now gives $20 on death in Frost mode.
- Speed increased from Slightly Fast (4.5) to Fast (6.25).
- Health increased from 8 to 14 in Sandbox mode.
- **Bug**: **Snowy** uses Snowman‘s model in the Index.
- **Bugfix**: **Snowy** no longer uses Snowman‘s model in the Index.
- Health increased from 14 to 16 in Frost mode.
- First wave appearance changed from 3 to 2.
- Health decreased from 16 to 15 in Frost mode.
- Cash given decreased from $20 to $15 on death.

Description: The **Snowy** was an enemy that first appeared in the second phase of Krampus Frosthold as part of the Krampus' Revenge Event. It had above average speed and a fairly low health for its debut, though it spawned in large hordes to compensate.
Appearance: The **Snowy** was a humanoid entirely made out of ice. It had light a blue head and arms, with a light grey torso and legs. It had two white eyes and a snarling monster face. It wobbled as it walked.
Strategy: - Area of effect towers, like the Mortar, Pursuit or Golden Pyromancer can be very useful against this, as this generally spawns in hordes.

Trivia: - On the second stage in Krampus Frosthold, two **Snowies** can be seen on two watchtowers with their arms raised in the air.

Description: The **Snowy** was an enemy that appeared exclusively in Outpost 32, and was the first enemy to spawn, as part of the Frost Invasion Event. Currently, it can be spawned again in Sandbox mode, though it uses the Operation I.C.E Event Snowy statistics. It had average speed, but low health.
Upon its death, the Frost Mystery had a chance to spawn the **Snowy**.
Appearance: The **Snowy** has light blue head and arms, along with a light grey torso and legs which are made presumably made out of powdered snow. It has no facial features.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Outpost 32 is listed instead.
- **Snowies** come in hordes at the start of the game and should be dealt with accordingly, generally with towers that can damage multiple enemies at once.

- The Pyromancer is the best way to combat the **Snowy**. It is a multi-hit tower, deals double fire damage to the **Snowy** (as with all enemies in the Frost Invasion Event) and can be placed down at the start of the game.
- There should be at least two Level 2 Pyromancers placed down at the start of the map to deal with the first few hordes of **Snowies**.
- Splash damage towers like the Mortar can do fairly well against the **Snowy**.
- The Swarmer's *Beehive Grenade* ability is excellent at dealing with **Snowies**, though it is too expensive to upgrade the Swarmer early on in the game.
- Later on in the game, **Snowies** are not an issue and can be dealt with using late game towers.
- As your base health in Outpost 32 is set to 200, it is not a major issue if multiple **Snowies** get to the exit at the start of the match.
Trivia: - The **Snowy** originally had a slightly different design before being added, where it had a shocked face, similar to one used by other event enemies, like the Undead or Reanimated.
Update History: - **Snowy** can now be summoned in Sandbox mode, only when the player has the Snowy's Logbook from the Operation I.C.E Event.
- No longer copies the statistics of the modern version in Sandbox mode.

Appearance: The **Sock Puppet** is a large sock puppet that is mounted on six mechanical legs. The sock puppet itself is an orange sock with black stripes, eyes and a mouth with white teeth and a tongue dangling out of it. Upon death, it makes a hissing noise, thus the sock resembled a snake.
Strategy: - High DPS towers, like the Ranger, Pursuit, Accelerator or Golden Minigunner are recommended.
- The Commander and DJ Booth can be very useful at boosting the firerate and range of your towers.
- Stalling towers such as the Archer can be quite useful against this, due to its very fast speed.
- As it has no immunities, any form of stalling can be used effectively.
- Its lack of immunities means that some of the stalling towers, like the Freezer, can also be used to drop its defense.
Update History: - **Bug**: **Sock Puppet's** reward threshold is set to a insanely high number, making it not give any cash when damaged or killed.

Description: The **Solar Servant** was one of the bosses of the fourth night of the Solar Eclipse Event. It had a high amount of health and a slow speed. It had one ability, where the **Solar Servant** smashed its axe at nearby towers, causing three explosions and stunning towers that were caught in its radius.
Appearance: The **Solar Servant** had neon orange skin. Its legs and torso were purple. It had a grey mask on its face and two neon orange horns. It wore purple shoulder-pads on its arms and a chestplate. It had a sun shaped object behind it. It wielded a solar axe.
Strategy: - High DPS towers such as the Accelerator, Turret and Ranger are recommended to defeat this enemy.
- The Commander and DJ Booth can help boost these towers.
- Because of its freeze and poison immunities, the Toxic Gunner, Freezer, Frost Blaster and Sledger cannot slow this down.
- As it has Energy Immunity, the Electroshocker can only slow it down instead of stunning it. Additionally, due to its large size, it can also only slow this down for a short amount of time.
- Be aware that the enemies that spawn before the **Solar Servant** have relatively high health, allowing it to walk further before getting damaged.
- Additionally, the **Solar Servant** will spawn one more time on wave 16 with the Lunar Servant and The Umbra, making it even more dangerous.
- You can set some high DPS towers' targeting to *Strongest* to deal with the **Solar Servant** early.
- When wave 16 starts, they will target The Umbra instead of the **Solar Servant.**

Description: The **Soul** is a Hardcore and Voidcore mode enemy that cannot be attacked by towers without hidden detection. While its health is low for its debut, it is quick and can take unprepared defenses by surprise. As it is a Ghost enemy, units cannot collide with it. Anything that deals unit collision damage also cannot deal damage to it.
Logbook Description: "*The Soul is what is left when a realm ends and the dead have not passed into the afterlife. They will drift aimlessly across the Nil Zone once the realm is completely destroyed, and are either eaten up by whatever may have survived the collapse or captured for use. In this case, the Void consumed many realms before their battle with TDS. Where there were once countless realms, the Void devoured nearly all of them in a short span of time. Now, few remain unaccounted for.*"
Appearance: **Variant 1**
The **Soul** has a white translucent body and no legs. It wears a white, black and purple robe that covers most of its body.
**Variant 2**
The legacy **Soul** is a white translucent and faceless enemy. It emits light when it runs.
Due to its transparency, the Hidden attribute applied to it makes it fade completely then fades back into view at regular intervals.
Strategy: - DPS towers with hidden detection such as the Accelerator, Engineer, Turret or Juggernaut can be used to defeat **Souls**.
- Support towers like the Commander, DJ Booth and Mercenary Base can aid in further boosting the DPS of towers.
- You can use the Ace Pilot to give hidden detection to towers that lack the detection such as the Ranger and Kingpin.
- As the **Soul** is a Ghost enemy, units such as the Railgun Tank cannot collide with it. They can however, damage the **Soul** with their ranged attacks if they are able to detect Hidden enemies.
Trivia: - The legacy **Soul** uses a very similar model to all versions of the Ghost before the Lunar Overture version.
- During Hardcore Testing BETA, the **Soul** had a trudging animation (similar to the Molten) as opposed to the current running one.
- The **Soul** was also slower, having a speed of Above Average.
- The modern **Soul** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - Now has 2,500 health in Hardcore mode and Sandbox mode.
- Now has 3,000 health in Voidcore mode.
- Now gives $2,250 on death in Hardcore mode.
- Now gives $1,750 on death in Voidcore mode.
- Cash given on death decreased from $1,750 to $1,500.

soul_boss.name: Soul Boss
soul_boss.description: The Soul Boss was an enemy that cannot be attacked by towers without hidden detection. It only appeared in Hardcore mode.

notice.text: Soul Boss was previously removed on the 5th of June 2026, though it has been made available through the Sandbox mode later.

Description: The **Soul Boss** was an enemy that cannot be attacked by towers without hidden detection. It only appeared in Hardcore mode. Currently, it can only be spawned in Sandbox mode if the player has the Sandbox Plus+ gamepass. It has mediocre health for its debut and has average speed, about the same speed as the Mystery Boss. Additionally, it is a Ghost enemy, meaning that units cannot collide with it. Anything that deals unit collision damage also cannot deal damage to it.
The Mystery Boss can spawn the **Soul Boss** upon its death in Hardcore mode, wave 47 onwards.
Appearance: The **Soul Boss** is a white translucent enemy with white wings and a yellow halo. It emits light and is faceless.
Due to its transparency, the Hidden attribute applied to it makes it fade completely then fades back into view at regular intervals.
Strategy: This strategy refers to the state of the game while the **Invisible** still appeared in the Hardcore mode.
- Towers with high DPS and hidden detection generally fare well against the **Soul Boss**. Such towers include the Minigunner, Turret and Accelerator.
- Do be aware that when using the Accelerator, it may lock onto other enemies, allowing the **Soul Boss** to slip past.
- At Level 4+, the Ace Pilot is able to give towers in its range permanent hidden detection, allowing towers without hidden detection to be able to attack the **Soul Boss**.
- This is most useful for the Ranger, because it deals high damage and has high range.
- The Mortar cannot detect the **Soul Boss**, but their splash damage can indirectly damage it.
- Another detectable enemy must be near the **Soul Boss** for these towers to hit it.
- The Electroshocker can indirectly slowdown the **Soul Boss** as it is average-sized and does not have an energy immunity though another detectable enemy must be nearby.
- The Frost Blaster, Freezer and Jester can also be used to slow down the **Soul Boss**, but the Toxic Gunner, Cryomancer and Sledger cannot as they do not have hidden detection.
- However, the Sledger and Cryomancer can indirectly freeze it if another detectable enemy is near the **Soul Boss**, although this should not to be relied on, as it may appear on its own.
- All units that only deal collision damage such as the Humvee and Elf are completely useless against this enemy.

- As the Trapper's spikes and bear traps deal unit collision damage, they do not deal any damage to the **Soul Boss**. If used to kill the **Soul Boss**, the Trapper should be set to place down landmines, as these deal explosion and burn damage.
Update History: - **Soul Boss** removed from the main game, as it has been replaced by Elite Soul. Now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.
- No longer appears in the Index.

Description: The **Soul Stealer** is a mini-boss that appears in Voidcore mode. It has high health but it walks rather slowly.
It has two abilities:

- The first ability is *Curse Tower*. When performed, the **Soul Stealer** curses a tower, making it unable to attack until the **Soul Stealer** is dead. Ability usage for the cursed tower is also disabled, but any passive ability may still work. Additionally, it will steal the soul of the tower and summon in a Soul enemy. Only 20 towers can be cursed by a **Soul Stealer** at once, with cursed towers that were sold not being included in this limit. In cases where the ability is used when the limit is reached, it will only summon in a Soul.
- The second ability, *Summon*, makes the **Soul Stealer** summon in three Souls and one Void Eye. During this, it will also become a Hidden enemy for 12 seconds.
Logbook Description: "*The Soul Stealer is one of the highest ranking in the Void Army, and is considered by Void Caster to be invaluable. She created the Soul Stealer to manage the growth of her army, and will only send it out when she feels victory could be achieved. They manage the souls who roam the Void, as well as claim them from whatever realms their rifts begin to tear into. They lack personality and are more like a drone who serves a specific task and does so without fanfare. It is considered ‘lame’, but it does not seem to care.*"
Appearance: The **Soul Stealer** has a large, golden lock for a head. It has a single, large eye in the center, with a pupil resembling a key hole. Its chest has numerous gold rectangular pieces attached to it. The **Soul Stealer** also has a deep purple hood over its head, adorned with golden buttons. It has no legs, rather having a single body segment where the legs would be, all tied up in numerous belts, while its arms are separated from the torso. One of its arms has a golden key attached to it while the other has a lock.
Strategy: - High DPS towers, preferably ones with hidden detection due to its summons and it becoming Hidden every time it uses *Summon* are recommended. Such towers include the Accelerator, Turret, Juggernaut, Engineer or Mercenary Base.
- The Ace Pilot can be used to make towers which cannot detect it, like the Ranger, to be able to do so.
- The **Soul Stealer** can curse towers, which will make them do nothing until the **Soul Stealer** is killed.
- If an important tower was cursed by the **Soul Stealer**, it is recommended to sell and place it down again if possible, as this will remove the curse.
- The Medic cannot protect towers from being cursed.
Trivia: - When first added in v2.0.0, the **Soul Stealer** had a third ability where it would turn into a Hidden enemy at 25% of its health. This ended up getting removed in v2.1.0.
- This was seemingly replaced by having it incorporated into its *Summon* ability, as since the same update it now gives it Hidden temporarily for 12 seconds.
- The **Soul Stealer** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - *Summon* now gives it Hidden for 12 seconds every time it is used.
- Health increased from 300,000 to 375,000 in Voidcore mode.
- Number of summoned Souls decreased from 4 to 3.
- Void Eye is no longer Hidden.
Notes: - ↑ Only a Boss in Voidcore mode.

soul_stealer_legacy.name: Soul Stealer
soul_stealer_legacy.description: The Soul Stealer was an enemy that only appears in Hardcore mode. Currently, it can only be spawned in Sandbox mode if the player has its Logbook.

notice.text: Soul Stealer (Legacy) was previously removed on the 5th of June 2026, though it has been made available through the Sandbox mode later.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Soul Steal** - The **Soul Stealer** attacks one tower using its axe, spawning one Soul from the attacked tower and giving it an 150% Fatigue Debuff (60% increase).

Description: The **Soul Stealer** was an enemy that only appears in Hardcore mode. Currently, it can only be spawned in Sandbox mode if the player has its Logbook. It has a high amount of health, but walks quite slowly. Its main ability is to attack towers with its axe. It swings its axe at a random nearby tower, which spawns one Soul from it and applies a 150% Fatigue Debuff.
Appearance: The **Soul Stealer** has glowing pink arms and its head is purple. It wears a black dominus with purple horns and is faceless. It wears diamond-plated black armor and pauldrons, with a pink gem on its chestplate, and purple gauntlets on both arms, both with a pink gem. Its torso, legs, and boots are granite purple. Purple particles are emitted from its boots and gauntlets, and pink particles are emitted from its arms.
It wields a black axe with a wrapped handle and a purple outline near its cutting edge.
Strategy: This strategy refers to the state of the game while the **Soul Stealer** still appeared in the Hardcore mode.
- The **Soul Stealer** should not usually be too much of a problem.
- However, be aware that they will usually spawn in pairs or threes, making them a little more difficult to deal with.
- The Ranger can make light work of these enemies. The Commander is recommended to boost the firerate of the Ranger to try and defeat the **Soul Stealer** as quickly as possible.
- While the Ranger is immune to stuns, it is not immune to the Fatigue Debuff applied by the **Soul Stealer**.
- High DPS towers, such as the Turret or Accelerator, can be great against the **Soul Stealer**.
- The Turret can be especially useful against the **Soul Stealer**, as it is not affected by its Fatigue Debuff and it does not spawn any Soul.

- The Engineer can also be very useful, as the **Soul Stealer** cannot attack its sentries or damage them. It can however make it so it takes longer for Engineer to get enough scrap required to build a sentry.
- Try not to place towers near the start of the path, or close to it, if you can.
- This makes them a target for the **Soul Stealer** to spawn a Soul from and increase their firerate.
- If any towers are hit by the **Soul Stealer**, the Commander can mitigate some of the effects.
- The Military Base can be used against the **Soul Stealer** as its units cannot be attacked.
- Any stalling tower can be used to slow the **Soul Stealer** down as it has no immunities.
- Be aware that, due to its large size, it can only be stunned by the Warden and frozen by freezing towers for a shorter period of time compared to an average-sized enemy.
Trivia: - The **Soul Stealer** was considered a major boss during Hardcore Testing BETA due to a bug.

- Before the Entity System Update, if the **Soul Stealer** used its ability on a tower, the Soul spawned from the tower will be the "*Tower's Soul*" with the tower's name being the one that the Soul spawned from, instead of "**Soul Stealer's** Soul".
- The axe used by the **Soul Stealer** is a re-textured version of the Zombie Axe gear from the Roblox catalog.
Update History: - **Bug**: *Soul Steal* ability can spawn Souls from a tower even if it is not a humanoid.
- **Bug**: **Soul Stealer** gets permanently stuck after using its *Soul Steal* ability.
- **Bugfix**: **Soul Stealer** can no longer spawn a Soul from a tower that is not a humanoid.
- **Bugfix**: **Soul Stealer** no longer gets permanently stuck after using its *Soul Steal* ability.
- **Bug**: Summons an invisible Soul in Sandbox mode when there is no Legacy modifier applied.
- **Soul Stealer** removed from the main game, now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.
- No longer appears in the Index.

Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in The Narratorium is listed instead.
- High DPS towers with hidden detection, like the Turret, Accelerator, Warlock, bottom path Pursuit or Golden Minigunner are recommended to take this down.

- Towers which normally do not have it, like the Ranger or top path Pursuit can still be used, however they need to be able to see them with the help of another tower, like the Ace Pilot or Spotlight Tech.
- As the **Spectator** is quite fast, stalling towers with hidden detection, like the Freezer, or towers which can consistently hit them without it, like the DJ Booth, can be very useful.

Description: The **Speedy King** was a large and fast enemy that only appeared in Hardcore mode. Currently, it can only be spawned in Sandbox mode if the player has the Sandbox Plus+ gamepass. For its debut, it has high health and fast speed. It has an ability where upon death, it can make surrounding enemies faster, if there are any enemies in a certain proximity. This speed-boost affects Boss enemies like the Fallen Swordmaster.
The **Speedy King** can be spawned by the Void Reaver. The Mystery Boss can spawn the **Speedy King** in Hardcore mode, from wave 44 onwards.
Appearance: **Variant 1**
The current **Speedy King** is identical to its original version, except it has two slanted lines perpendicular to each other as its face.
**Variant 2**

The original **Speedy King** looked similar to the Speedy Boss's third version and fourth version appearance. It had light blue skin and wore reflective blue shoulder-pads and arm-pads. Its torso and legs were dark blue granite. It wore blue boots with white socks, a slightly slanted blue crown, symbolizing royalty, and a dark blue cape. Blue electricity can be seen emitted from its legs and arms. It was faceless.
Strategy: This strategy refers to the state of the game while the **Invisible** still appeared in the Hardcore mode.
- The Military Base's units can be effective against the **Speedy King** as it can escape the range of towers before it can be killed.
- High DPS towers, such as Accelerator, Ranger, Turret, and Minigunner are recommended to kill it.
- The Freezer, Frost Blaster and Sledger cannot freeze or slow down the **Speedy King**, as it has Freeze Immunity.
- Stalling towers such as the Warden and Trapper's bear traps can only slow down the Speedy King, instead of completely stopping its movement while knockback towers cannot knock it back.
- Additionally, the Warden can only slow down the **Speedy King** for a short amount of time due to its large size.
- Upon death, the **Speedy King** can speed up other enemies around it with its *Charge* ability.
- This makes it a very big threat, especially if a major boss such as the Fallen Swordmaster is present.
- The **Speedy King** often spawns in groups and alongside the Circuit, increasing the number of enemies that can speed up other enemies.
Trivia: - The **Speedy King** has a death animation where it raises one arm, then slumps to the ground.
- The **Speed King's** *Charge* ability is nearly the same as the Hardcore Circuit's *Super Charge* ability and the same as the Polluted Wasteland II Circuit's *Short-Circuit* ability.

- The **Speedy King**, alongside the Circuit from Hardcore mode, the Circuit from Polluted Wasteland II and the Commander from Pizza Party, are the only enemies that are capable of speeding up other enemies.
- The cape used by the **Speedy King** is the Blue Royal Cape accessory from the Roblox catalog.
- This may be considered the Hardcore version of the Speedy Boss.
- The crown that the **Speedy King** uses is a re-textured version of the Black Iron Crown of Pwnage accessory from the Roblox catalog.
Update History: - **Bug**: Its ability can cause frozen enemies to start moving temporarily.
- Energy Immunity replaced with Stun Immunity.
- **Speedy King** removed from the main game, now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.
- No longer appears in the Index.

Strategy: - Early-game towers like the Militant, Toxic Gunner, Cowboy, Ace Pilot and Military Base can do quite well against this.
- DPS towers like the Accelerator, Minigunner or Ranger can also be used, though they are not necessary, especially in easier modes.
- As the **Speedy Boss** is quite fast, stalling towers like the Freezer, Electroshocker, Warden or Brawler can be used to slow it down.
- Do note that its size will make it affected less by various forms of stalling, such as freeze or knockback.
Trivia: - The original name and appearance of the **Speedy Boss** was based on the Boss3 from *Tower Battles*.
- When the Uber Mystery was in the game, it had a chance of spawning the **Speedy Boss** upon its death in Golden and Fallen modes.
- The Speedy King can be considered as a Hardcore variant of the **Speedy Boss**.
- The skull shoulder pads used by the fifth appearance of the **Speedy Boss** are re-textured versions of the The Riddling Skull accessory from the Roblox catalog.
- Despite being a boss version of the Speedy, the third and fourth versions of the **Speedy Boss** looked more similar to the Quick than the Speedy.
- Oddly, in v1.23.0, the appearance of the **Speedy Boss** was not updated to always use the Enemies Beta appearance like how other Molten mode enemies were.
- This is most likely due to the fact that the **Speedy Boss** did not appear in Easy mode at the time, since the Molten mode enemies that had their appearances changed also appeared in Easy mode.
- The "*32*" writing on the side-end of the **Speedy Boss's** metal booster is a reference to the 32 meme within the Tower Defense Simulator community.
- The word "*Durablox*" written on the batteries is a portmanteau of Duracell, which is a real-life battery brand, and Roblox.

speedy_elf_krampus_frosthold.name: Speedy Elf
speedy_elf_krampus_frosthold.description: The Speedy Elf was the second enemy that debuted in Krampus Frosthold as part of the Krampus' Revenge Event.

notice.text: Speedy Elf (Krampus Frosthold) has been removed from the game as of the 31st of January 2024 as it was part of the Krampus' Revenge Event.

Description: The **Speedy Elf** was the second enemy that debuted in Krampus Frosthold as part of the Krampus' Revenge Event. It had slightly higher health than the enemy that spawned before it, the Basic Elf, and was faster, which made it a slightly bigger threat. Additionally, on later waves, it spawned as a hidden enemy, which made it it even more threatening with adequate hidden detection.
Appearance: The **Speedy Elf** had pale skin. It had a light blue shirt with white fur along the sleeves, as well as stitch lines on the sides of the arms. It had a black belt, dark cyan pants and black shoes. It also wore a blue Christmas hat with a lightning bolt emblem on it.
Strategy: - The **Speedy Elf** typically spawns in hordes. Area of effect towers like the Pyromancer or Mortar should be used to easily deal with this enemy.

- Hidden **Speedy Elves** appear at Wave 6, which can slip past unprepared defenses. Towers with cheap hidden detection, like the Golden Pyromancer, Accelerator or Minigunner can be effective against them.

speedy_elf_cold_ambush.name: Speedy Elf
speedy_elf_cold_ambush.description: The Speedy Elf was an enemy that exclusively appeared in Cold Ambush as part of the Violent Night Event.

notice.text: Speedy Elf (Cold Ambush) has been removed from the game as of the 4th of February 2023 as it was part of the Violent Night Event.

Description: The **Speedy Elf** was an enemy that exclusively appeared in Cold Ambush as part of the Violent Night Event. It had a slightly fast speed and a somewhat high amount of health for its debut.
Appearance: The **Speedy Elf** had pale skin. It had a light blue shirt with white fur along the sleeves, as well as stitch lines on the sides of the arms. It had a black belt, dark cyan pants and black shoes. It also wore a blue Christmas hat with a lightning bolt emblem on it.
Strategy: - Early game towers like the Golden Scout, Cowboy, Golden Cowboy, Militant or Crook Boss can do quite well against these.
- As these enemies spawn in large numbers, towers that can damage multiple enemies at once, such as the Executioner can be useful against this.
- Later on during the game, stronger towers like the Accelerator or Minigunner can kill the **Speedy Elf** quite easily.
Trivia: - Its appearance and purpose parallels that of the Speedy. Both are purposed to be a fast enemy and both also have blue in their color palettes.

speedy_king.name: Speedy King
speedy_king.description: The Speedy King is a fast support enemy that appears in Hardcore and Voidcore modes.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **King's Charge** - Upon death, creates a purple circle around itself that applies a 50% speed buff to any enemy in it for 10 seconds.

Description: The **Speedy King** is a fast support enemy that appears in Hardcore and Voidcore modes. It has decent health and fast speed, alongside Stun Immunity that makes it harder to stall. Upon death, it will create a purple circle which applies a 50% speed buff to any enemy in it for 10 seconds.
Logbook Description: "*The one time the Speedy King was not quick enough was when it came to saving what was left of his kingdom. Unlike the Slow King, the Speedy King fought the Void head on. In battle, their actions could have been described as desperate as they tried to face the Void Reaver. In the wake of their defeat the flowers bloomed, and now they sprint across the same flora they once fought against.*"
Appearance: The **Speedy King** has a white body with a cracked face. It wears a purple shirt, cape, black pants, a bronze crown, armbands, shoes and vest.
Strategy: - High DPS towers like the Juggernaut, Engineer, Accelerator, Kingpin or Ranger can be used to deal with the **Speedy King**.
- The DJ Booth's purple track can be useful with its Range Buff, making it harder for sped up enemies to get out of a tower's range. Additionally, its ability can be used to slow them down.
- Setting towers to *Last Enemy* can prevent **Speedy Kings** from reaching far enough to boost stronger enemies on certain waves.
Trivia: - The **Speedy King** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.

spindling.name: Spindling
spindling.description: The Spindling was a fast and tanky enemy that appeared in The Narratorium as a part of The Final Act Event.

notice.text: Spindling was previously removed from the game on the 11th of March 2026 as it was part of the The Final Act Event, though it has been made available through the Sandbox mode.

spindling.mode_appearance:

- Originally:
- The Final Act (Easy)
- The Final Act (Hard)

Description: The **Spindling** was a fast and tanky enemy that appeared in The Narratorium as a part of The Final Act Event. Its high speed and health could make it a threat for unprepared players.
Logbook Description: "*The Spindling is a fast-charging enemy that was created out of whim. The Narrator doesn't remember why he created the Spindling, but then again, after thousands of years one wouldn't normally be sane of mind.*"
Appearance: The **Spindling** is a robot with a giant spin wheel in the place of its head. This wheel goes through its torso and has a stick and its head on it. It has a grey body, red shirt and wooden legs. It has multiple needles in its body.
Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in The Narratorium is listed instead.
- High DPS towers like the Accelerator, Ranger Golden Minigunner, Turret or Warlock are very useful against this.
- The Commander and DJ Booth can be used to boost the statistics of these towers.
- As the **Spindling** has no immunities, all stalling towers can be used to slow it down. Examples of such towers include the Freezer, Electroshocker, DJ Booth and Toxic Gunner.
- Do note that, due to it being bigger than the average enemy, certain forms of stalling like knockback or freeze will be less effective on it.
Trivia: - The **Spindling** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Spindling** removed from the main game, now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.

split.name: Split
split.description: The Split, internally called Hex Corpse Upper, is an enemy summoned by the Splitter upon its death. Normally when summoned, it is instead called Upper Body.

Description: The **Split**, internally called **Hex Corpse Upper**, is an enemy summoned by the Splitter upon its death. Normally when summoned, it is instead called *Upper Body*. The only way for its display name to be seen is by summoning it in the Sandbox mode. It is faster than the Splitter and has as much health as it does upon healing itself. The **Split** has the Burn Immunity
Appearance: The **Split** is the upper half of the Splitter's body. It has brown skin with a brown shirt. Its face is covered with multiple, large teeth.
Strategy: - Multiple high DPS towers, like the Pursuit, Accelerator, Ranger and Engineer are recommended to take down the **Split**.
- Support towers like the Commander and DJ Booth can be useful at boosting the DPS of your towers.
- As this enemy is quite fast, slowing towers like the Electroshocker and Freezer can be very useful against this.
- Multiple such towers can also be used to drop its defense.
- As it has the Burn Immunity, it cannot be set on fire, also making it immune to having its defense reduced through burn.
Trivia: - It is named "*Hex Corpse's Lower Body's Upper Body*" in-game when summoned by a Splitter, rather than "*Splitter's Split*".
- This is due to an oversight where the names applied to both of these enemies upon the death of a Splitter have not been changed.
Update History: - Health increased from 800 to 1,250 in Polluted Wasteland II.

split_polluted_wasteland.name: Split
split_polluted_wasteland.description: The Split was an enemy that only appeared in Polluted Wasteland Fallen mode. It did not spawn naturally, and was instead spawned by the Splitter upon its death.

notice.text: Split (Polluted Wasteland) has been removed from the game as of the 8th of May 2021.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Explode** - Upon death, the **Split** creates a bile bubble, stunning nearby towers.

Description: The **Split** was an enemy that only appeared in Polluted Wasteland Fallen mode. It did not spawn naturally, and was instead spawned by the Splitter upon its death. This enemy was much faster than the Splitter, but was also weaker than it. In addition, upon its death, the **Split** stunned towers within a small radius.
Appearance: The **Split's** appearance was similar to the Splitter, but was much smaller. It had light blue skin and a large bloated stomach. Its navel was blue. It wore black shorts and has grey legs. Its eyes were white, and a radioactive substance leaked out of its eyes and mouth.
Strategy: - The Rocketeer and Mortar are recommended against the **Split** as they spawn in pairs.
- You can use the Medic's ability to cleanse towers from their stun after a Splitter's death to attack the **Split**.
- As the **Split** moves very quickly, they can run past your towers if you aren't careful.
- For this reason, the Military Base can be quite useful against this enemy as units cannot be stunned by the **Split**.
- You can use the Frost Blaster, Freezer and Electroshocker to slow the **Split** down.
Trivia: - This is closely related to the Swarm, an enemy that appeared before the MEGA Update, as it was also spawned by another enemy upon death, the Carrier.
- Weirdly, its legs are the same as the ones used by the second version of the Tank.
- This enemy was effectively replaced by the Goo in Polluted Wasteland II, as both have very similar mechanics.
Update History: - Partial Electric Immunity replaced with Energy Immunity.
- No longer appears in Golden mode as it has been removed.

splitter.name: Splitter
splitter.description: The Splitter, internally referred to as Hex Corpse, is an enemy that appears in Polluted Wasteland II. It has a high amount of health and quite fast speed.
splitter.mode_appearance:
- Polluted Wasteland
- Challenges
  - Oops! All slimes!

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Self Severance** - Upon its death, the **Splitter** splits in half. **Splitter** heals itself by 800 health and changes its name to **Lower Body**, while also summoning the Split.

Description: The **Splitter**, internally referred to as **Hex Corpse**, is an enemy that appears in Polluted Wasteland II. It has a high amount of health and quite fast speed. Upon death, it will split in half, changing itself into the **Lower Body**, while also summoning the Split, which is referred to as *Lower Body* by the game when summoned by it. The **Splitter** will also gain 800 health from this ability.
The **Splitter** can be summoned by the Nuclear Monster with its *Nuclear Summon* ability.
Appearance: The **Splitter** has black skin and giant teeth covering face. It wears torn brown clothes. Its torso is cut in half. Upon turning into the **Lower Body**, its entire upper body disappears, leaving only its lower torso and legs.
Strategy: - Multiple high DPS towers, like the Pursuit, Accelerator, Ranger and Engineer are recommended to take down the **Splitter**.
- Support towers like the Commander and DJ Booth can be useful at boosting the DPS of your towers.
- As this enemy is quite fast, slowing towers like the Electroshocker and Freezer can be very useful against this.
- Multiple such towers can also be used to drop its defense.
- As it has the Burn Immunity, it cannot be set on fire, also making it immune to having its defense reduced through burn.
Trivia: - The **Splitter** was originally from The Nightmare Realm and Containment of the Hexscape Event under the name *"Hex Corpse"*.
Update History: - **Bug**: Damage dealt to the **Splitter's** regenerated health does not increase various damage based meters, like the Accelerator's overcharge or Engineer's scrap meter.
- **Bug**: Units instantly kill the **Splitter** upon collision after it has turned into the **Lower Body**.
- Health increased from 1,600 to 2,500 in Polluted Wasteland II.

splitter_polluted_wasteland.name: Splitter
splitter_polluted_wasteland.description: The Splitter was an enemy that only appeared in Polluted Wasteland Fallen mode, replacing the Boomer.

notice.text: Splitter (Polluted Wasteland) has been removed from the game as of the 8th of May 2021.

stats.Spawned By:
- Mystery Boss (Polluted Wasteland Fallen, wave 35 onwards)
- Summoner Boss (Formerly)

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Explode** - Upon its death, the **Splitter** creates a bile bubble, stunning nearby towers. Also causes 2 Splits to be spawned.

Description: The **Splitter** was an enemy that only appeared in Polluted Wasteland Fallen mode, replacing the Boomer. While replacing the Boomer whenever it was meant to spawn in Fallen mode in Polluted Wasteland, the **Splitter** had much more health than the Boomer. However, the **Splitter** moved much more slower compared to the Boomer. In addition upon its death, as well as stunning towers in a large radius, it spawned two Splits.
The **Splitter** used to be spawned from the Mystery Boss upon its death in Fallen mode in Polluted Wasteland, wave 35 onwards.
Appearance: The **Splitter** had green skin and a large bloated stomach. Its navel was dark green. It wore black shorts and had grey legs. Its eyes were white, and a radioactive substance leaked out of its eyes and mouth. Green particles were emitted from its torso.
Strategy: - The **Splitter** can stun towers upon its death. This allows other enemies to pass stunned towers with little damage being done to them.
- While the **Splitter** has incredibly slow speed, it should be killed as soon as possible, and as far away from your main towers as possible.
- The Rocketeer or Mortar are recommended against the **Splitter** as it will spawn two fast Splits when it dies.
- Killing the **Splitter** before it gets within range of most of your towers is the most ideal way to deal with it. Keep in mind that it also has a long stun time.
- The Ranger is the best at keeping distance away from the **Splitter**. Long range towers, such as Minigunner and Turret, are also excellent options.
- The DJ Booth allows towers to shoot the **Splitter** from further away, potentially killing it before it can stun your towers.
- You can use the Medic's ability to cleanse your towers of the **Splitter's** stun, so long it is not stunned itself.

- If a **Splitter** is near the end of the path on low health, try not to kill it and let it enter the base. When it is killed, it will spawn two Splits which can easily run into your base and result in a defeat.
Trivia: - This enemy is very similar to the removed Carrier as that enemy also spawned a smaller enemy upon its death.
- The Commander improperly calls this enemy as a Boomer.
- The **Splitter's** legs are the same legs of the second version of the Tank.
- The **Splitter** was effectively replaced by the Super Slime in Polluted Wasteland II, as both have very similar mechanics.
- Later on, an identically named enemy, Splitter, would also be added, though functionally the Super Slime is far closer to the **Splitter** than the new Splitter enemy.
- The **Splitter** is similar to the Breaker enemies.
Update History: - Can no longer be spawned from the Summoner Boss.
- Partial Electric Immunity replaced with Energy Immunity.
- No longer appears in Golden mode as it has been removed.

spotlight_enemy.name: Spotlight
spotlight_enemy.description: Spotlight was a support that appeared in The Narratorium as a part of The Final Act Event.

notice.text: Spotlight (Enemy) was previously removed from the game on the 11th of March 2026 as it was part of the The Final Act Event, though it has been made available through the Sandbox mode.

spotlight_enemy.mode_appearance:
- Sandbox via Logbooks
- Originally:
- The Final Act (Easy)
- The Final Act (Hard)

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **In The Spotlight** - Casts light upon an enemy in its range of 15, healing all enemies in a 15 radius by 40 health every 0.2 tick.

Description: **Spotlight** was a support that appeared in The Narratorium as a part of The Final Act Event. It was a large flying enemy that had significantly higher health but slower speed than the Performer that appeared before it. It has one ability, where it casts light from its spotlight head to heal enemies by 40 health every 0.2 tick. This ability has a range of 15 and a spotlight radius of 15.
Logbook Description: "*The Spotlight is a flying enemy with a large spotlight for a head that illuminates Narrator's stage. The Spotlight has the ability to heal other enemies, making it a priority target. Sometimes, the Painter Men will stand beneath it to paint on their canvas faces.*"
Appearance: The **Spotlight** is a humanoid object-headed robot which has a giant spotlight instead of a head. It has black arms and a floating ring above it. It wears a red shirt, blue pants and black shoes. Using its spotlight head, it will cast light on enemies near it.
Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in The Narratorium is listed instead.

- **Spotlights** themselves are not a threat due to their mediocre speed and comparatively low health, rather becoming a problem through their main ability, *In The Spotlight*. This ability heals any enemies in a radius, which can become a major issue if left unattended.
- The Ranger can quickly deal with them, though due to their slowness, enemies being healed will likely need to be cleared out first.
- The Mortar is also particularly effective, thanks to being indiscriminate towards the concept of crowds.

- The Pursuit can also be used, as it has flying detection, full map wide range through its *Reposition* and it has missiles that allow it to deal damage to both the **Spotlight** and the enemies it is healing.
- The Firework Technician can be used to give towers flying detection if needed.
- The UAV can also be used, but only in the Easy difficulty.
Trivia: - The **Spotlight** is the largest enemy in the game to always have the Flying attribute.
- Counting enemies that have Flying added through abilities, the Frost Spirit takes this spot instead.
- Adding onto this, the **Spotlight** is one of the largest non-boss enemies in the entire game, possibly only being beaten out by the Null Accelerator or Null Necromancer.
- The **Spotlight** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Bugfix**: **Spotlight's** model is now in the sky again.
- **Spotlight** removed from the main game, now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.

spy_ducky_ducky_revenge.name: Spy Ducky
spy_ducky_ducky_revenge.description: The Spy Ducky was a Hidden enemy that appeared in Bathroom Approach as part of the Ducky Revenge Event and its rerun in the Spring Frenzy Battle Pass.

notice.text: Spy Ducky (Ducky Revenge) was previously removed on the 5th June 2026, though it has been made available through the Sandbox mode later.

spy_ducky_ducky_revenge.mode_appearance:

- Originally:
- Ducky Revenge (Easy)
- Ducky Revenge (Hard)

Description: The **Spy Ducky** was a Hidden enemy that appeared in Bathroom Approach as part of the Ducky Revenge Event and its rerun in the Spring Frenzy Battle Pass. It has decent health and an above average speed.
Logbook Description: "*Spy Ducky is a ghost, a mystery. He changes disguises faster than one could quack. Infiltrating the highest level of government secrets and being internationally wanted for espionage, Spy Ducky could be a villain in his own right. He could be anywhere, anything, anyone. Spy Ducky could even[sic] you.*"
Appearance: The **Spy Ducky** is a regular yellow duck with black eyes, orange beak and orange flippers. It wears a brown hat and a mask. As it is a Hidden enemy, its body is entirely translucent. It has three animations that it can randomly have, where all three also have differently shaped eyes. The first animation has it have a happy expression, the second has it have a serious expression while the third one has its eyes partially closed, likely because it is scared.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Bathroom Approach is listed instead.
- Towers with hidden detection that are effective early on are pretty useful against the **Spy Ducky**. Such towers include the Ace Pilot, Crook Boss, Militant and Cowboy.
- The Golden Crook Boss and Golden Cowboy are more effective against it, although not required.
- The Ace Pilot can also be used to give towers which normally do not have hidden detection, like the Mortar or Pursuit, hidden detection, making the **Spy Ducky** far easier to deal with.

- Like all Hidden enemies, towers with splash damage or multi-targeting, such as the Mortar and Electroshocker can damage them without hidden detection. These should not be entirely relied on, and should be backed up by the above towers.
Trivia: - The **Spy Ducky** is based on the Spy from *Team Fortress 2*.
- The last sentence of its Logbook description is a reference to Meet The Spy.
- The **Spy Ducky** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Bug**: **Spy Ducky** clips into the ground when made larger or smaller.
- **Bug**: Logbook description incorrectly uses "***Spy Ducky** could even you.*" instead of the correct "***Spy Ducky** could even be you.*".
- **Spy Ducky** from the main game, now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.
- **Spy Ducky** re-added to the main game, now appears in Bathroom Approach.
- Health decreased from 60 to 125 in Easy difficulty.
- Health decreased from 125 to 250 in Hard difficulty.
- Cash given increased from $60 to $375 on death in Easy difficulty.
- Cash given increased from $100 to $375 on death in Hard difficulty.
- **Bugfix**: No longer clips into the ground when made larger or smaller.
- **Spy Ducky** from the main game, now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.
