The **Spy Ducky** could be spawned by the Eggroll.
Appearance: The **Spy Ducky** is a black translucent duck with black eyes and an orange beak and feet. It has a piece of paper with a head of a yellow humanoid drawn on it.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in D00M's Revenge is listed instead.
- Towers with cheap hidden detection like the Soldier and Golden Scout fare well against the **Spy Ducky**.
- Multiple Snipers are recommended for their long range. In addition, the Sniper can also counter the Flying Ducky that debuts later on in the game.
Trivia: - The piece of paper on the **Spy Ducky's** head is a reference to the Spy from *Team Fortress 2*, more precisely the disguise mask teammates can see on a disguised Spy.
Update History: - **Spy Ducky** can now be summoned in Sandbox mode, only when the player has the Spy Ducky's Logbook from the Ducky Revenge Event.
Notes: - ↑ Beyond wave 15, **Spy Ducky** scaled its health with time.

stereo_man.name: Stereo Man
stereo_man.description: The Stereo Man was a tanky enemy that appeared in The Narratorium as a part of The Final Act Event.

notice.text: Stereo Man was previously removed from the game on the 11th of March 2026 as it was part of the The Final Act Event, though it has been made available through the Sandbox mode.

stereo_man.mode_appearance:
- Sandbox via Logbooks
- Originally:
- The Final Act (Easy)
- The Final Act (Hard)

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Stereo Madness** - Upon losing all of its Shield Health, lets out a strong sound with a radius of 15 that stuns towers for 2 seconds and deals 750 damage to units. Also makes it drop its shield, removing its Defense.

Description: The **Stereo Man** was a tanky enemy that appeared in The Narratorium as a part of The Final Act Event. It was an enemy that had a high amount of health and Shield Health but its speed is average. It has one ability where upon losing all of its Shield Health, it will drop the shield it has been carrying, removing its Defense, then let out a sound soundwave with a radius of 15. This stuns towers for 2 seconds and deals 750 damage to units.
Logbook Description: "*The Stereo-Man was created by Narrator so he could listen to his favorite tunes throughout the ages. He would spend hours listening as he writes his plays. If tuned to the correct frequency, it sends out a shockwave. Lefty particularly dislikes the Stereo-man as the music plays is often warped or distorted.*"
Appearance: The **Stereo Man** has the appearance of an object-headed enemy with a stereo for a head, hand-crafted by The Narrator. It wears a red shirt with golden accents and a gear, black pants and shoes. On its back it has a phonograph, which can let out a shockwave. It also carries a shield made of speakers for protection, which it drops when it loses all of its Shield Health.
Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in The Narratorium is listed instead.
- High DPS towers like the Accelerator, Mercenary Base, Golden Minigunner, Warlock or Ranger are recommended against this.
- Stun immune towers like the Ranger and Pursuit can be especially useful, as they cannot be stunned by it.
- Towers like the DJ Booth or Commander can be used to boost their statistics.
- As the **Stereo Man** has both the Stun Immunity and Freeze Immunity, knockback towers like the Brawler and freezing towers like the Freezer cannot be used on it.
- While stunning towers like the Electroshocker can still be used, they will only slow it down instead of fully stopping it.
- While the DJ Booth cannot knock it back, its slowdown is not affected by its immunities.
- Other forms of stalling like confusion or poison are not affected by its immunities, making them pretty effective.
Trivia: - The **Stereo Man** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Stereo Man** removed from the main game, now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.

stone_viking.name: Stone Viking
stone_viking.description: The Stone Viking was an enemy that appeared exclusively in The Heights as part of the SFOTH Event.

notice.text: Stone Viking has been removed from the game as of the 13th of October 2019 as it was part of the SFOTH Event.

Description: The **Stone Viking** was an enemy that appeared exclusively in The Heights as part of the SFOTH Event. It had the same speed as the Normal, meaning it was faster than the Knight and Slow, while also having more health than the Knight. It could have also been spawned by the Swordmaster.
Appearance: The **Stone Viking** had grey skin with the slate texture. It had straps across their body and wore an 8-bit Viking helmet. It was completely faceless and wielded a stone sword. However, the **Stone Viking** could not attack towers with its sword.
Strategy: - While high DPS towers, like the Minigunner, are effective, it is also recommended to have splash damage towers, such as the Rocketer, as the **Stone Viking** spawn in hordes.
- The Commander can also assist in defeating the **Stone Viking** as it boosts the firerate of these towers.
- As the **Stone Viking** is faster than the Knight, having a Pyromancer or Freezer is recommended to slow it down.
Trivia: - Actual Vikings did not have horns on their helmets, meaning the **Stone Viking** was a false depiction of them.
- Despite the fact that the **Stone Viking** had a sword, it did not attack towers with it, making it purely comestic.
- The **Stone Viking's** helmet is a re-textured version of the 8-Bit Viking accessory from the Roblox catalog.

streamer.name: Streamer
streamer.description: The Streamer was a fast enemy that appeared in Headache Headquarters, replacing the Speedy.

notice.text: Streamer was previously removed on the 8th of April 2026, though it has been made available through the Sandbox mode later.

streamer.mode_appearance:
- Sandbox via Logbooks and Brain Rot
- Originally:
- Toilet

Description: The **Streamer** was a fast enemy that appeared in Headache Headquarters, replacing the Speedy. Currently, it only appears when the Brain Rot modifier is activated in Sandbox mode, replacing every Speedy and Quick modern variant, or with its Logbook. It has a high amount of health and a rather fast speed.
Appearance: The **Streamer** has dark skin, a realistic head and brown dreads. It wears a Manchester United jersey with Portugal national team shorts. It also has brown shoes.
Headache Headquarters Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Headache Headquarters is listed instead.
- Strong early-game towers like the Militant, Golden Scout or Golden Cowboy are very effective here.
- Towers with area of effect capabilities, like the Electroshocker or Mortar, can also be useful here.
- High DPS towers like the Minigunner can be quite effective against this.
- Stunning/freezing towers like the Warden, Cryomancer, Tesla or Freezer can be effective at stopping them as it is quite fast.
Trivia: - This enemy is based on the popular streamer IShowSpeed (Darren Jason Watkins Jr.).
- The outfit that the **Streamer** wore is based on Cristiano Ronaldo, one of Speed's icons.
- The shirt is from the Manchester United 2022-23 home kit, while the shorts are from the Portugal national team's 2021-22 home kit.
- The shoes are the Adidas Yeezy Foam Runner Stone Sage variant that Speed frequently wears.
- The fact that this enemy replaced the Speedy was likely inspired by the fact that *Speed* is in his name.
Update History: - **Bug**: Head does not move in the Index.
- **Streamer** now appears in Headache Headquarters as part of April Fools 2025 Event.
- **Streamer** no longer appears in Headache Headquarters, now only appears in Sandbox mode.
- **Streamer** now appears in Headache Headquarters as part of Aprilini Foolsini Eventini.
- **Streamer** no longer appears in Headache Headquarters, now only appears in Sandbox mode.

strong.name: Strong
strong.description: The Strong was a stronger variant of the Slow that appeared in Easy mode. It had more health than the Slow and had the same speed as the Normal Boss.

notice.text: Strong has been removed from the game as of the 19th of July 2024.

stats.Spawned By:
- Grave Digger (Easy only)
- Mystery (Easy only)
- Necromancer 2 (Formerly)

Description: The **Strong** was a stronger variant of the Slow that appeared in Easy mode. It had more health than the Slow and had the same speed as the Normal Boss. It did not appear naturally, rather it could only be spawned by the Grave Digger.
The **Strong** could be spawned by the Mystery upon its death in Easy mode. They could have also been spawned by the Necromancer 2 when it was in the game.
Appearance: **Variant 1**

The third version of the **Strong** had a desaturated tan skin. It had a grey pebble torso and dark navy pebble legs. It also had a grey diamond-plated armband around its right arm and a dark grey diamond-plated band around its left leg.
**Variant 2**
The second version of the **Strong** is similar to the current version, except it had a drooling zombie face.
**Variant 3**
The first version of the **Strong** had a light green skin color, as well as a dark blue torso and navy legs. It had a trudging animation and a sad drooling face.
Strategy: - Despite its name, beginner towers such as the Scout, Sniper and Soldier are enough to take down the **Strong**.
- Cheap towers with decent DPS, like the Ace Pilot, Militant or Crook Boss can be very effective against the **Strong** as well.
- Due to its slow walk speed, the Gladiator and Shotgunner can be very effective against the **Strong** with their ability to hit multiple enemies at once.
- High DPS towers, such as the Turret, Accelerator and Minigunner, perform admirably against the **Strong**.
- Splash damage towers, such as the Demoman and Rocketeer, are useful against the **Strong** as it normally spawns in hordes.
- Later on, the Rocketeer and Mortar will have enough splash damage to kill **Strongs** in one shot.
Trivia: - After Easy got reworked on the 24th of February 2024, the **Strong** was mostly replaced by the Armored. However, it could still appear if summoned by the Grave Digger, as its summons were not updated.
- This would later change on 19th of July 2024, alongside the Mystery and Mystery Boss being replaced or removed. Interestingly, it was not replaced by the Armored, it was instead removed completely.
- Despite its removal, it can still appear in Kill ENEMY! quests.
Update History: - Speed decreased from Average to Slightly Slow (2).
- First wave appearance changed from wave 21 to wave 20 in Easy mode (now Easy mode).
- First wave appearance changed from wave 20 to wave 14 in Beginner's mode (now Easy mode).
- No longer naturally appears in Easy mode, as it has been replaced by the Armored, now can only be spawned by the Grave Digger.

strong_alien.name: Strong Alien
strong_alien.description: The Strong Alien was the second enemy that spawned in Area 51 as part of the Area 51 Event. It had the same speed as the Alien, but had higher health.

notice.text: Strong Alien has been removed from the game as of the 13th of October 2019 as it was part of the Area 51 Event.

Description: The **Strong Alien** was the second enemy that spawned in Area 51 as part of the Area 51 Event. It had the same speed as the Alien, but had higher health.
Appearance: The **Strong Alien** was an extraterrestrial enemy that had grey skin and a rounded grey alien head.
Strategy: - Similar to the Alien, they can be killed with Crook Bosses or Minigunners, though you may have to upgrade your current ones or buy new towers to cope with the **Strong Alien's** health.
- Rocketers and Demomen can deal significant damage to hordes of **Strong Aliens**.
Trivia: - Similar to the Alien, the **Strong Alien** was a reference to Area 51 conspiracy theories speculating that the US Government is hiding extraterrestrial proof in the military base.
- The **Strong Alien's** head was the Retro Gray Alien accessory in the Roblox catalog.

strong_mummy.name: Strong Mummy
strong_mummy.description: The Strong Mummy was an enemy that appeared in Nightmare Carnival as part of the Halloween 2019 Event. Compared to the Mummy, it had more health, but was slower.

notice.text: Strong Mummy has been removed from the game as of the 9th of November 2019 as it was part of the Halloween 2019 Event.

Description: The **Strong Mummy** was an enemy that appeared in Nightmare Carnival as part of the Halloween 2019 Event. Compared to the Mummy, it had more health, but was slower. It could also be spawned by the Jack O' Bot and Reaper.
Appearance: Similar to the Mummy, the **Strong Mummy** was wrapped around with bandages, which covered most of its body, exposing only some of its arms and its head. However, the bandages were slightly darker compared to the Mummy. Its torso and legs were white. It had dark-ish green skin and was faceless.
Strategy: - Early on, Soldiers or Paintballers can help clear through **Strong Mummies** quite easily.
- This is favorable while you save up for better towers for the stronger enemies that debut later in Nightmare Carnival.
- As they spawn in hordes, splash damage towers such as the Demoman and Rocketeer can be very useful.
- Minigunners and Outlaws can easily clear out hordes of **Strong Mummies**. However, you will need to save up cash in order to afford them early on.
- If you already have the Shredder, it can be helpful in defeating it.
Trivia: - The **Strong Mummy** had the same appearance as the Mummy, but it was just slightly darker.

stunt_man.name: Stunt Man
stunt_man.description: The Stunt Man was a summoner enemy that appeared in The Narratorium as part of The Final Act Event.

notice.text: Stunt Man was previously removed from the game on the 11th of March 2026 as it was part of the The Final Act Event, though it has been made available through the Sandbox mode.

stunt_man.mode_appearance:

- Originally:
- The Final Act (Easy)
- The Final Act (Hard)

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Stunt Double** - Upon death, spawns a Stunt Man Double.

Description: The **Stunt Man** was a summoner enemy that appeared in The Narratorium as part of The Final Act Event. It had slightly fast speed and a decently high health for its speed. On top of this, it also summons in the Stunt Man Double, which effectively is the same enemy but smaller and with less health.
Logbook Description: "*This daredevil was once a celebrated stunt performer, known for their death-defying acts and fearless attitude. However, a tragic accident during a high-risk stunt left them trapped in a liminal space between life and death. Now, they roam the battlefield, driven by an insatiable urge to perform their stunts, regardless of the consequences.*"
Appearance: The **Stunt Man** is a daredevil with a black body. It wears a red vest, pants and hat, all with gold accents. It also has a white shirt and frilled gloves, black shoes and a white mask. On its death, its double will jump out of it. It has two walking animations to choose from.
Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in The Narratorium is listed instead.
- The **Stunt Man** can summon its Stunt Man Double, which can only happen upon death.
- The Hacker can negate its ability, preventing it from summoning the Stunt Man Double.
- High DPS towers, like the Turret, Golden Minigunner, Ranger, Warlock and Pursuit are recommended against this.
- The **Stunt Man** is quite fast, making stalling towers like the Freezer, DJ Booth and Electroshocker useful against it.
Trivia: - The **Stunt Man** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Stunt Man** removed from the main game, now appears exclusively in Sandbox mode.

sugrawr.name: Sugrawr
sugrawr.description: The Sugrawr was an enemy that appeared exclusively in Eggy Island as part of the Spring 2020 Event.

notice.text: Sugrawr has been removed from the game as of the 26th of May 2020 as it was part of the Spring 2020 Event.

stats.Speed:

- Fast (6, Hard Mode)

Description: The **Sugrawr** was an enemy that appeared exclusively in Eggy Island as part of the Spring 2020 Event. It appeared in easy mode with 30 health and in hard mode with 50 health. It had slightly above average speed in easy mode but was much faster in hard mode.
Appearance: The **Sugrawr** had cyan blue skin, and its torso and legs were yellow. It wore a cut in half candy wrapper and had a smile face. It had an unusual running animation, flailing its arms as it ran.
Strategy: - In easy mode, several Soldiers is enough defeat the **Sugrawr**.
- You can also save up for the Minigunner, so long someone else places down other towers to defend from the Zombeggs that debut before the **Sugrawr**.
- The Pyromancer can slow down hordes of **Sugrawrs**. Additionally, in hard mode, the Electroshocker and Frost Blaster can also be used to slow down the **Sugrawr**.
- The Freezer can also be used, though be aware of its slow projectile speed.
- In hard mode, the Holiday Archer can be used as an effective tower against the **Sugrawr**.
Trivia: - The **Sugrawr** was a portmanteau of the words "sugar" and "rawr", with the latter being an onomatopoeia of "roar".

summoner_boss.description: The Summoner Boss is a boss enemy that can summon Mysteries and Mystery Bosses. For its debut...

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Summon** - Summons four Mysteries and occassionally Mystery Bosses.

Description: The **Summoner Boss** is a boss enemy that can summon Mysteries and Mystery Bosses. For its debut, it has high health (higher than the Tank) but slightly slow speed (slower than the Mystery Boss). It debuts alongside the Error.
The **Summoner Boss** only appears in the Golden mode and Legacy Fallen mode. It also appears in certain Challenge Maps.
The **Summoner Boss** is replaced by the Necromancer King in any map with the Enemies Beta modifier active.
Appearance: The **Summoner Boss** has reflective grey skin and purple glowing eyes. Because of its reflective skin, its skin color will be different on various maps, though generally it is black or dark grey. Its torso and legs are pebble black. It also wears a reflective dark granite cloak. It has red diamond-plated armbands and large grey skull shoulder-pads, with purple eyes and large horns. It wears a purple respirator mask, a bowler hat with playing cards on it and wields a staff that emits purple electricity whenever enemies are summoned. It has a twisted left leg.
Strategy: - Deal with this enemy as soon as possible. Leaving the **Summoner Boss** alive for too long will allow it to summon a vast amount of enemies.
- Place towers closer to the spawn to have a better chance at dealing with the **Summoner Boss** before it can summon anything.
- The Ranger, Accelerator, Minigunner and Turret are great at dealing with the **Summoner Boss** and the Mystery Bosses it summons.
- You may want to set these towers to *Strongest* to ignore the enemies that the **Summoner Boss** spawns.
- You can boost the firerate of these towers with the Commander's *Call to Arms* ability whenever the **Summoner Boss** spawns.
- Area of effect towers, such as the Executioner, Rocketeer or Mortar, can be great at dealing with enemies summoned by the **Summoner Boss**.
- They can also be useful at dealing damage to the **Summoner Boss**. Do note, however, that these towers do not have enough DPS to deal with the **Summoner Boss** on their own.
Trivia: - The **Summoner Boss** is considered to be the successor of the Necromancer 2.
- The **Summoner Boss's** breathing mask is a re-textured version of the Deep Space Half Gas Mask from the Roblox catalog.
- The **Summoner Boss's** face is a re-textured version of the Ghostface from the Roblox catalog.
- Prior to the Entity System Update, the **Summoner Boss** could summon enemies which remained in the air.
- Prior to the Overhaul Update, the **Summoner Boss** was one of the few enemies to gain a shield. This shield reduced the damage dealt by most towers to 2-4.
Update History: - Speed increased from Average to Above Average.
- **Summoner Boss** now gains a temporary shield after summoning.
- Shield maximum damage increased from 1 to 2-4.
- **Summoner Boss** now spawns the Mystery and Mystery Boss instead of the Ultra Mystery, Boomer (Splitter in Polluted Wasteland) and Uber Mystery.
- *Summon* no longer gives a temporary shield.
- Speed decreased from Above Average to Slightly Slow (2).
- Summoned enemies no longer give money when damaged.
- Partial Electric Immunity replaced with Energy Immunity.
- No longer appears in Golden mode as it has been removed.
- Energy Immunity replaced with Stun Immunity.
- No longer appears in Fallen mode, as it has been replaced by the Fallen Summoner.
- **Summoner Boss** now appears in Golden mode and Legacy Fallen mode, if activated through Sandbox mode.
- **Summoner Boss** no longer appears in Golden mode and Legacy Fallen mode, as they has been removed.
- **Summoner Boss** now appears in Golden mode and Legacy Fallen mode, if activated through Sandbox mode.
- **Bug**: **Summoner Boss** no longer appears in the Index.
- **Bug**: **Summoner Boss** no longer uses the death sound effect.
- No longer appears in public rotation of Challenge Maps, as they exclusively appear within Sandbox mode.
Notes: - ↑ Only the first two **Summoner Bosses** are a Boss enemy in Golden mode.

super_mutant.name: Super Mutant
super_mutant.description: The Super Mutant, internally referred to as Mutated Boss, a name still used by its legacy version, is an enemy that appears in Polluted Wasteland II.

Description: The **Super Mutant**, internally referred to as **Mutated Boss**, a name still used by its legacy version, is an enemy that appears in Polluted Wasteland II. It has high health and a slightly fast speed.

The **Super Mutant** could be spawned by the Nuclear Monster. This means it could also appear in Oops! All slimes!, if spawned by the Nuclear Monster. It also could be spawned by the Mystery and Mystery Boss.
Appearance: The **Super Mutant** has a chartreuse skin color and a black torso, waist and legs. It wears black armbands with grey spikes. Veins are visible on its head and arms. It is faceless and it emits light green particles.
Strategy: - Strong early-game towers like the Golden Crook Boss, Golden Cowboy or Engineer can be used to deal decent damage to it.
- Expensive high DPS towers like the Pursuit, Accelerator or Ranger can be bought for this wave if possible, though it is not necessary.
- Because the **Super Mutant** moves quite quickly for its high health, slowing towers like the Electroshocker, Freezer and Sledger can be useful against this.

- Defense dropping towers like the Golden Pyromancer, Cryomancer or Freezer can be used to drop its defense, while also being able to slow it down or deal with hordes of enemies that spawn alongside it.
Trivia: - The **Super Mutant's** name may be a reference to Super mutants from *Fallout*.
Update History: - None of the changes are applied to the legacy version.
- Name changed from *Mutated Boss* to *Super Mutant*.
- **Bug**: Appears twice in the Index, one of them not loading in any model for the preview.
- **Bug**: Enemy does not become transparent when converted by Hacker.
- **Bugfix**: No longer appears twice in the Index.

super_mystery.name: Super Mystery
super_mystery.description: The Super Mystery, originally called the Mystery 2, was an enemy similar to the Mystery, but upon its death, it spawned the Molten, Normal Boss, Necromancer...

notice.text: Super Mystery has been removed from the game as of the 26th of May 2020.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Spawn** - Upon its death, the **Super Mystery** spawns the Molten, Shock, Slow Boss, Necromancer, Normal Boss or Hidden Boss.

Description: The **Super Mystery**, originally called the **Mystery 2**, was an enemy similar to the Mystery, but upon its death, it spawned the Molten, Normal Boss, Necromancer, Shock, Slow Boss or Hidden Boss. It could spawn any of these enemies, regardless of what the mode was. It had the same amount of health as the Strong, but was as fast as the Speedy.
The **Super Mystery** could have been spawned by the Mystery Boss and Grave Digger. The **Super Mystery** used to appear in Beginner's and Molten modes. It was replaced with the Mystery Boss.
Appearance: **Variant 1**
The third version of the **Super Mystery** was a translucent, glossy blue enemy with a glowing yellow question mark on its torso. It had a drooling zombie face and yellow glowing eyes.
**Variant 2**
The second version of the **Super Mystery** had a transparent yellow body. It had an orange question mark on its torso and a drooling zombie face.
**Variant 3**
The first version of the **Super Mystery** had a transparent red body. It had an orange question mark on its torso and a drooling zombie face.
Strategy: - Since the **Super Mystery** comes out after some several high health enemies, such as the Speedy Boss, it is recommended to have high DPS towers present to defeat that enemy before moving onto this enemy.
- Since the **Super Mystery** mostly come in hordes, Rocketeers and Mortars are also recommended.
- High DPS towers, such as the Minigunner, are recommended for the enemies that spawn from the **Super Mystery**.
- Do not underestimate the **Super Mystery** as they can advance very far down the path and spawn their high health enemy.
- If a low health **Super Mystery** is near the end of the path, try not to kill it as it is likely that, when killed, it will spawn a high health enemy which will lead to a defeat.
- The enemies that spawn from the **Super Mystery** do not need to be killed for wave progression to occur.
- If you are speedrunning a map, you should focus on killing the **Super Mysteries** first before moving onto the enemies that spawn.
Trivia: - The appearance and name of the **Super Mystery** were originally based on the Mystery2 from *Tower Battles*.
- The last version of the **Super Mystery** looked similar to the first version of the Mystery.
- The **Super Mystery** was similar to the Uber Mystery as they could spawn enemies that did not normally appear in Beginner's mode.
- All the enemies that it could spawn appeared naturally in Molten mode.
- The question mark on the **Super Mystery** is a re-textured version of the Question Mark accessory from the Roblox catalog.
- The **Super Mystery** was replaced by the Mystery Boss.
Update History: - Now only spawns in Easy and Normal modes (later Beginner's and Molten modes).
- Can now spawn the Necromancer and Normal Boss.

- **Bug**: **Super Mystery** upon death has a chance to not disappear, instead it will have negative health and continue walking, stopping when it reaches a turn or the exit. Increases base health if it reaches the exit.
- Removed, replaced with the Mystery Boss.

super_slime.name: Super Slime
super_slime.description: The Super Slime, formerly known as the Slime and the Radioactive Slime, with the latter still being used as its internal name and its name for the legacy version...

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Gooey Death** - Upon its death, the **Super Slime** explodes into a slime bubble that stuns all towers caught in the bubble, and spawns three Goos.

Description: The **Super Slime**, formerly known as the **Slime** and the **Radioactive Slime**, with the latter still being used as its internal name and its name for the legacy version in Sandbox mode, is an enemy that appears in Polluted Wasteland II and it used to appear in Pizza Party. It has a high amount of health and an average speed. It has one ability, where upon death, it will explode into a slime bubble, stunning any towers caught in it and spawn three Goos.

The **Super Slime** used to replace the Boomer in Polluted Wasteland II and Pizza Party before their respective reworks; it now only appears in Polluted Wasteland II. The **Super Slime** could formerly be spawned by the Nuclear Monster before v1.23.0. It could also formerly be spawned from the Mystery Boss upon its death from wave 35 onwards.
Appearance: The **Super Slime** is a large faceless humanoid with a waist in its rig. It has a green skin color and a brown torso and legs. All of its body parts are encased in translucent green slime, which constantly emits green particles.
Strategy: - Use high DPS towers such as the Accelerator, Ranger, Pursuit and Engineer to defeat this enemy.
- The Commander and DJ Booth can be very useful at decreasing the firerate of towers and increasing their range.
- The Medic can be useful at shielding the towers from the stuns caused by the **Super Slime**, allowing them to deal with the Goos spawned by it.
Trivia: - This enemy is very similar to the Slime that appeared in Trick or Threat Town.
- The **Super Slime** appears in the trailer for Badlands II; however, it does not appear in that map in the actual game.

notice.text: Super Soldier Ducky was previously removed on the 5th June 2026, though it has been made available through the Sandbox mode later.

abilities.label: Ability Cooldown: 10
abilities.text: **Industrial Military Terrorism** - Shoots out three plasma projectiles from its plasma blaster at a tower or unit in its range of 20, creating an explosion with a 6 explosion radius that stuns towers for 3 seconds and deals 500 damage to units.

Description: The **Super Soldier Ducky** was an enemy that appears in Bathroom Approach Hard difficulty as part of the Ducky Revenge Event and its rerun in the Spring Frenzy Battle Pass. It is a stronger version of the Missile Ducky. It has high health, a bit lower than the Ducky Unit, 25% defense making most sources of damage deal 20% less damage to it and above average speed.

It has one ability where it will fire three plasma projectiles from its plasma blaster at units and towers in its range of 20. These plasma blasters create explosions with a radius of 6 that stun towers for 3 seconds and deal 500 damage to units.
Logbook Description: "*Super Soldier Duck is what "beak" performance looks like. He is the type to take himself too seriously and can be overdramatic when it comes to his dramatizations of past events, telling insane mission stories like flying a jet through a train tunnel and kidnapping someone named "Scout." Although, who knows what stories are true.*"
Appearance: The **Super Soldier Ducky** is a small, armored yellow duck. It wears dark green chest armor, boots and gloves that it wears on its wings. It also has a gas mask with a green visor over its head. It wields a plasma blaster with its right wing, which it uses to attack towers and units.
Event Strategy: As this enemy only appears through Sandbox mode, no strategy section is made for its current version. Instead, a strategy section for the one that appeared without Sandbox mode in Bathroom Approach is listed instead.
- High DPS towers like the Ranger, Pursuit, Turret, Accelerator or Golden Minigunner are recommended against this.
- The Ranger and Pursuit are especially useful as they are immune to its stuns.
- The Commander and the DJ Booth can be used to boost the DPS of these towers.
Trivia: - The **Super Soldier Ducky** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Acid Bath** - Creates an acidic puddle upon death, which rapidly heals any enemy that is walking through it.

Description: The **Super Toxic** is a large tanky enemy that appears in Polluted Wasteland II. It has a high amount of health and an average speed. It has one ability where upon death, it creates an acidic puddle that rapidly heals any enemy that walks through it. It also has the Stun Immunity, meaning that the Warden and Electroshocker can only slow it down instead of stunning it and prevents it from being knocked back, Freeze Immunity, preventing it from being frozen or chilled and Corpse, making it turn into a Corpse on death.

The **Super Toxic** replaces the Fallen Hero in Oops! All slimes! challenge. The **Super Toxic** used to be spawned by the Nuclear Monster. It also could have been spawned from the Mystery Boss wave 38 onwards in Polluted Wasteland II.
Appearance: The **Super Toxic** is a large humanoid with a waist and lower arms in its rig. It has glowing light green skin and a black torso, waist and legs. It has corrugated metal shoulder-pads and grey metal neck-guards next to its head, both of which are covered in blood. It has a canister on its back, which is filled with acid. Green veins can be seen on its body and tumors can be seen on its head. It also emits green particles and pulses from its torso.
Strategy: - Towers with high DPS such as the Accelerator, Ranger, Turret or the Engineer are recommended to be used against this enemy.
- You can also use support towers such as the Commander and DJ Booth to buff these towers.
- Be careful of the **Super Toxic's** *Acid Bath* ability as it can rapidly heal other enemies, making it a much bigger threat when there are large groups of enemies.
- This ability also works on the Nuclear Monster.
- If it proves problematic, this ability can be cancelled out by the Hacker's enemy conversion, as that also cancels abilities that activate on death.
Trivia: - The **Super Toxic** despite being an acidic enemy, does not have any immunity to the Toxic Gunner.
Update History: - Health decreased from 12,000 to 5,000 in Oops! All slimes!.
- None of the changes are applied to the legacy version.
- Speed decreased from Above Average (3.5) to Average (3).
- **Bug**: Appears twice in the Index, one of them not loading in any model for the preview.
- **Bug**: No longer creates acid puddles on death, but still heals enemies.
- **Bugfix**: No longer appears twice in the Index.
Notes: - ↑ Only the first **Super Toxic** is a Boss enemy.

swamp_monster.name: Swamp Monster
swamp_monster.description: The Swamp Monster was the final boss of the second night in the Solar Eclipse Event. It had a large amount of health for its appearance and a very slow speed.

notice.text: Swamp Monster has been removed from the game as of the 26th of January 2022 as it was part of the Solar Eclipse Event.

stats.Attributes:

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Trident Throw** - Throws four tridents at towers, one at each tower, stunning them and any tower near it. This attack deals at least 400 damage to units hit by it.

Description: The **Swamp Monster** was the final boss of the second night in the Solar Eclipse Event. It had a large amount of health for its appearance and a very slow speed. When using its *Trident Throw* ability, it would stop moving and threw four tridents at towers, stunning them. It was immune to being frozen and slowed down by the Toxic Gunner. Additionally, the Electroshocker could only slow it down instead of stunning it.
Appearance: The **Swamp Monster** had dark green and green skin. It was faceless but had two large yellow eyes on its torso and one on its left arm, and two large yellow eyes on its back and the back of its left arm. It had four dark green tentacles, all of which held a blue glowing trident, which it used to stun towers.
Strategy: - Use high DPS towers, such as the Swarmer, Minigunner or Accelerator to defeat this.
- While it may look like the Accelerator does not attack the **Swamp Monster**, it is only a visual bug. The Accelerator does deal damage to it.
- The Commander is recommended to boost the firerate of the towers.
- The *Trident Throw* ability will make the **Swamp Monster** stop moving for a long period of time, you can use this to your advantage to deal as much damage as possible.
- While the *Trident Throw* ability cannot directly target units, it can still damage them.
- Because of its immunities, it can only be slowed down by the Electroshocker.
- However, because of its Energy Immunity, it could only be slowed down instead of completely stopped. Its large size also reduced the Electroshocker's shock time.
Trivia: - The **Swamp Monster** is very similar to the Swamp Thing from the Nightmare Carnival.
- The **Swamp Monster's** theme uses the old You Lost! theme as a leitmotif.
- Interestingly, the **Swamp Monster** was seen in Tower Outskirts in the Solar Eclipse Trailer despite it never appearing there.

debuts.title: Foggy Forest (Solar Eclipse Event, Night II)

swamp_thing.name: Swamp Thing
swamp_thing.description: The Swamp Thing was an enemy that appeared exclusively in Nightmare Carnival as part of the Halloween 2019 Event.

notice.text: Swamp Thing has been removed from the game as of the 9th of November 2019 as it was part of the Halloween 2019 Event.

Description: The **Swamp Thing** was an enemy that appeared exclusively in Nightmare Carnival as part of the Halloween 2019 Event. While it walked quite slowly, it had very high health, with only the Jaxe and Jack O' Bot having higher health.
The **Swamp Thing** could have been spawned by Jack O' Bot.
Appearance: The **Swamp Thing** was a large enemy, similar in size to the Slow Boss. It had dark green marble skin and its torso and legs were dark green granite. It was also faceless. Multiple green tentacles came out from its back and green particles are emitted from its torso. Its head was slightly tilted downwards and it had no face.
Strategy: - Multiple Minigunners, Outlaws and other high DPS towers are able to defeat this enemy.
- While not having any special attacks, this is a major threat due to its high health.
- The Commander and John can help boost the DPS of towers around them, giving you a better chance of defeating the **Swamp Thing**.
Trivia: - The name of this enemy could have been inspired by the Swamp Thing from *Terraria* or the Swamp Thing from *Kingdom Rush*.
- The **Swamp Thing** is very similar to the Swamp Monster.

swamper.name: Swamper
swamper.description: The Swamper was a slow and tanky enemy that was exclusive to the Lunar Overture Event.

notice.text: Swamper has been removed from the game as of the 21st of December 2023 as it was part of the Lunar Overture Event.

Description: The **Swamper** was a slow and tanky enemy that was exclusive to the Lunar Overture Event. It had higher health than every enemy that appeared before it but was slower than every one of them. It had defense, reducing the amount of damage towers deal to it. Additionally, it was immune to being frozen by freezing towers and it could only be slowed down by the Warden and Electroshocker because of its immunities.
Appearance: The **Swamper** was a large, dark, green-colored entity with multiple tentacles on its back. It had dark green skin, and it wore a dark green shirt and pants. It had multiple thorns coming out of its body and two yellow glowing eyes on its torso.
Strategy: - Multiple cheaper towers with decent DPS, such as the Golden Scout, Militant or Golden Soldier can be a good way to eliminate this enemy.
- Alternatively, efficient, high DPS towers like the Minigunner can also be used, though due to their cost they may be a bit hard to afford when it first spawns.
- Accelerator also works wonders against this enemy, easily being able to make short work of it due to its high DPS.
- Because of its immunities, freezing towers like the Freezer or Sledger cannot freeze it.
- Additionally, the Warden and Electroshocker can only slow it down instead of fully stopping it.
- Though this is mostly not necessary if you have enough DPS towers.
- The Pyromancer and Golden Pyromancer can be used to decrease its defense, while also dealing damage to weaker enemies that spawn alongside it.
Trivia: - The **Swamper** is based on the Swamp Monster boss from the Solar Eclipse Event, which in turn is based on the Swamp Thing from the Halloween 2019 Event.

debuts.title: A Dark Tale (Lunar Overture Event, Act I)

swarm.name: Swarm
swarm.description: The Swarm, in-game referred to as Swarm 1 despite there only being one Swarm enemy, was a four-legged enemy that was spawned from the Carrier when it died.

notice.text: Swarm has been removed from the game as of the 13th of October 2019.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Explode** - Stuns nearby towers within a small radius upon its death.

Description: The **Swarm**, in-game referred to as **Swarm 1** despite there only being one Swarm enemy, was a four-legged enemy that was spawned from the Carrier when it died. It was faster than the Carrier and had more health than the Molten. The **Swarm** created a bubble when it died, and any towers caught in it were stunned. This was similar to the Carrier, although the bubble was smaller.
Appearance: Compared to the average enemy, the **Swarm** had quite an unusual design as it had four dark green legs, with black claws. It was smaller than the Carrier. It had a long green neck that was bent and glowing green eyes. It had a zombie face that was not seen on any other enemy. It did not have any arms.
Strategy: - The bubble that the **Swarm** creates upon its death will not destroy or stun any units from the Military Base or Crook Boss if any of them are caught in the bubble.
- This makes them very useful when other towers are stunned.
- The Rocketer can be very useful against the **Swarm** due to its splash damage.

- Long range towers, such as the Outlaw and Sniper, are effective against the **Swarm** as they can shoot it from a distance. This means that they are less likely to be caught in the bubble when the **Swarm** dies.
- The bubble created by the **Swarm** can be completely avoided by towers.
- Try not to kill the **Swarm** next to your towers.
- If required, you can use the Freezer's *Ice Drop* ability to stop the **Swarm** in its track, even if the Freezer is stunned.
Trivia: - In-game, the **Swarm** was called *Swarm 1*, even though there was no *Swarm 2*.
- This enemy could possibly be a reference to the *Mutant Creeper* mob from a *Minecraft* mod.

swift.name: Swift
swift.description: The Swift is an early-game enemy that appears in Hardcore and Voidcore modes. It has higher health and speed than the Odd.

Description: The **Swift** is an early-game enemy that appears in Hardcore and Voidcore modes. It has higher health and speed than the Odd.
Logbook Description: "*Swift are Odds that interacted with the Void Gem. Although none of the Odds could be considered ‘alive’ after embracing the Void, many won’t survive the transformation of becoming a Swift as the power of the gem ingrains itself into them. Void Gems are both extremely dangerous and valuable for their strengthening abilities, but it’s surmised that those ‘infected’ can only hear the calling of the eternal nothing.*"
Appearance: The **Swift** has white skin, purple torso and purple legs. It has purple veins on its body. It has bands around its arm and two purple crystals coming out of its shoulders. Has three walking animations it can choose from.
Strategy: - Decently strong early-game towers like the Engineer, Golden Soldier, Ace Pilot or Golden Scout can be effective at dealing with the **Swift**.
- Towers with stalling capabilities such as the Saboteur or Electroshocker can also be used to slow down the **Swift** because of its fast speed.
Trivia: - The appearance of the **Swift** is based on the legacy appearance of the Quick.
- The concept art of the **Swift** was created by @TheClassicRose.
- The **Swift** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Swift** now appears in Nil Zone II as part of the Halloween 2026 Live Events.
- **Swift** no longer spawns in Nil Zone II, as the Halloween 2026 Live Event has ended.

swordmaster.name: Swordmaster
swordmaster.description: The Swordmaster wore a red cloak and pants. Painted on its cloak appeared to be a necklace. It had green skin, light red legs and a dark red shirt.

notice.text: Swordmaster has been removed from the game as of the 13th of October 2019 as it was part of the SFOTH Event.

abilities.label: Ability 1
abilities.text: **Sword Swing** - Stuns nearby towers for 5 seconds with a sword swing.

abilities.label: Ability 2
abilities.text: **Sword Smash** - Stuns nearby towers for 5 seconds by smashing the ground with its sword.

abilities.label: Ability 3
abilities.text: **Summon** - Spawns various enemies at the spawn in random amounts.

Description: The **Swordmaster** was the first, and only, boss in The Heights. It walked very slowly, but had lots of health; more than the Molten Boss before the MEGA Update, with three abilities. Upon its death, if the mode was Normal+, all players were rewarded with the Gladiator.
It had three abilities:
- The first ability involved the **Swordmaster** swinging its sword in a full rotation, stunning all towers hit by the sword.
- The next ability was quite similar, smashing its sword into the ground stunning all ground towers within a radius.

- Its third and final ability involved the **Swordmaster** pointing its sword forwards and spawning random enemies, in a random amount, at the start of the map. These random enemies could be the Fallen Hero, the Slow Boss, the Necromancer, the Stone Viking, the Brute or the Slow.
Appearance: The **Swordmaster** wore a red cloak and pants. Painted on its cloak appeared to be a necklace. It had green skin, light red legs and a dark red shirt. It had several pouches on its belt and wore a yellow crown. It wielded a Darkheart sword by its right side. It had red glowing eyes and had a drooling zombie face.
Strategy: - You can use the Freezer's *Ice Drop* ability to stop the **Swordmaster**. This gives you much more time to defeat the boss.
- You can sell and re-buy the Freezer quickly to use the ability again. Do be aware that it is quite expensive.
- Pyromancers can burn the **Swordmaster**, slowing it down.
- Support towers, such as the John and Commander, are a given due to your tight budget.
- This means that you should spam cheap high DPS towers, such as the Minigunner, around these support towers.
- The Outlaw can also be effective, though do be aware of its high cost.
- Relocate your towers whenever the **Swordmaster** is out of range so that you can maximize damage.
- However, it may be ideal to keep some towers near the start of the map to deal with the enemies that the **Swordmaster** spawns.
Trivia: - The Fallen Swordmaster is the resurrected version of the **Swordmaster**, as stated by a tweet.
- The crown that the **Swordmaster** wore was the Golden Crown hat from the Roblox catalog.
- The **Swordmaster** was the first major boss to be added to the game, predating even the Molten Boss.
- The **Swordmaster's** appearance was based on an outfit that Shedletsky/Telamon used to wear.
- Shedletsky is the creator of Sword Fights on the Heights IV, which The Heights was based on.
- Upon release, the **Swordmaster** used to damage the base health for every tower that it stunned, with any of its abilities. This could lead to you losing if the base health reached 0.
- Therefore, this was the first enemy that was able to damage the base with an ability, but it was removed shortly after its addition.
Update History: - Stuns can no longer deal damage to the base health.

synaptic.name: Synaptic
synaptic.description: The Synaptic was an enemy that spawned in Failed Gateway as part of the Hexscape Event. It was a fast enemy with high health and defense.

notice.text: Synaptic has been removed from the game as of the 20th of November 2024 as it was part of the Hexscape Event.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Neuroplasm** - The **Synaptic** leaves a trail of puddles on the ground that last one second, which apply a short 0.1 second regeneration that heals any enemy that walks over them by 10 for its duration.

Description: The **Synaptic** was an enemy that spawned in Failed Gateway as part of the Hexscape Event. It was a fast enemy with high health and defense. It had one ability, where it left purple puddle trails. These trails applied a short 0.1 second regeneration that healed any enemy that walked over them by 10 health for the 0.1 second duration. It also had Freeze Immunity and Stun Immunity, making it harder to slow down.
Appearance: The **Synaptic** took the appearance of a brain in an orange container, which piloted a scrappy mech with four limbs. The mech itself was covered with spikes and bore a mouth full of sharp teeth. As the **Synaptic** ran, it left behind purple puddle trails, which were part of its *Neuroplasm* ability.
Strategy: - **Synaptics** are fast, dangerous enemies. Towers with high damage are required in order to kill them.
- Towers like the Militant, Minigunner, Crook Boss or Golden Soldier can be quite effective here.
- Because of its immunities, it cannot be frozen or chilled, knocked back and is only slowed down by stunning towers, making it harder to slow down.
- Additionally, as it is immune to freeze, it also cannot have its defense dropped by freezing towers.
- The **Synaptic** leaves puddles on the ground which heal enemies when they walk over them.
- However, these puddles will rarely heal an enemy unless a **Synaptic** walks through them. Even in such cases, the healing will be quite insignificant because of how low it is.
- Due to the **Synaptic's** fast speed, the Military Base may be quite useful in case they get past your defenses.
Update History: - **Bug**: Poison and electric defense dropping does not decrease **Synaptic's** defense.
- **Bugfix**: Poison and electric defense dropping now drops **Synaptic's** defense, though the Jester still cannot drop it.

tank.name: Tank
tank.description: Tank, previously known as the Tank 1, is a large and tanky boss that appears in Legacy Fallen mode and Golden mode.

notice.text: Tank was previously removed on the 24th of September 2025, though it has been made available through the Sandbox mode later.

Description: **Tank**, previously known as the **Tank 1**, is a large and tanky boss that appears in Legacy Fallen mode and Golden mode. The **Tank** is a fast, high health enemy, with speeds similar to the Quick and much higher health than the Giant Boss. It can be a major threat to unprepared defenses.
Appearance: **Variant 1**

The **Tank** has a khaki-grey skin color and a grey cobblestone torso and legs. It has chains wrapped around its torso, left arm and right leg. Its right arm is slightly bigger than its left arm. It has rusted rebar impaled into its back and the top of its torso is beveled. The **Tank** has glowing red eyes, which have slanted tops to express anger, and no mouth. It runs hunchbacked and uses its right arm to push itself forward.
**Variant 2**

The Enemies Beta version of the **Tank** is a large humanoid with a waist and lower arms in its rig. It has a tannish-grey skin color as well as a reddish-brown torso, waist and legs. It has black armbands with grey spikes and abs with tumors and wounds on its chest. The lower sides of its limbs are coated in dried blood and its body is covered in dirt.
**Variant 3**

The third version of **Tank** had a khaki-grey skin color and a grey cobblestone torso and legs. It had chains wrapped around its torso, left arm and right leg. Its right arm was slightly bigger than its left arm. It had rusted rebar impaled into its back and the top of its torso was beveled. The **Tank** had a drooling zombie face with glowing red eyes, which had slanted tops to express anger. It ran hunchbacked and used its right arm to push itself forward.
**Variant 4**

The second version of **Tank** had a tannish-grey skin color and black pebble pants on its legs. It had long muscular arms and a large torso and legs. It walked slightly hunchbacked and had a drooling zombie face with glowing red eyes.
**Variant 5**
The first version of **Tank** is similar to the second version, except it had brown pants.
Strategy: - Fast firing towers, such as the Minigunner, Accelerator or Turret, are recommended to kill **Tanks**.
- The Commander can boost their firerate with its *Call to Arms* ability.
- Because of the **Tank's** fast speed, long range towers, such as the Ranger, are recommended, as the **Tank** will take more time to get out of their range.
- The DJ Booth can also help increase range of towers that have shorter range, such as the Accelerator or the Minigunner.
- It is recommended to use the Commander's *Call to Arms* ability to boost the Ranger's firerate.
- You can use slowing towers, like the Electroshocker, Warden, Brawler or Sledger to slow down the **Tank**.
- Slowing it down is generally favored, due to the **Tank's** obscene speed.
- Be aware that, due to the **Tank's** large size, the Warden and freezing towers can only slow the **Tank** down for a shorter period of time compared to an average-sized enemy.
Trivia: - The **Tank** originally had an ability called *Rock Throw* where it would throw boulders at towers. This would stun them for a period of time.
- This ability was based on the *Left 4 Dead* zombie, the Tank.
- When the **Tank** was first added, the *Rock Throw* could vary in velocity. It could go far, or it could crumble right upon the first tower it hit.
- The bits of rock that the boulder split into also had irregular hitboxes.
- The boulders could be blocked by a player's torso.
- The first two versions of the **Tank** had arms taken from the Superhero package in the Roblox catalog.
- The first two versions of the **Tank** resembled the Tank from *R2D* and are likely a reference to said game.
- Unlike its counterpart, the Speedy Boss, the **Tank** cannot be spawned from the Mystery Boss.
- This is likely due to the **Tank** having a high amount of health and a very fast speed, which would make the game incredibly difficult if it spawned from Mystery Bosses.
- The current appearance of the **Tank** is similar to the Charger from *Left 4 Dead 2*.
- It could also draw inspiration to the current Boss4 from *Tower Battles*.
- The Commander's dialogue suggests the **Tank** can throw boulders. However, this never happens in-game.
- This is because the dialogue was made during Hardcore Testing BETA, where the **Tank** still had its *Rock Throw* ability. The dialogue was not changed for the Overhaul Update.
- The dialogue also suggests that the **Tank** used to play in Baseball leagues.
- The **Tank** was a sendable enemy in PVP Test since the first test, however, it could not actually be sent as it only had 25 waves.
- This was not the case since the second test, as it was extended to 30 waves there.
- Its stats were also not finished, with both its speed and health being set to 0.
Update History: - First wave appearance changed from wave 39 to wave 30 in Hard and Insane modes (now Golden and Fallen modes).

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: '**Molten Rock Throw** - The **Tank 2** picks up a boulder and throws it at nearby towers, stunning towers hit.

Description: The **Tank 2** was a stronger form of the Tank 1. It had the same speed as the Tank 1 while also having much more health than it. The **Tank 2** was also immune to the Pyromancer, meaning that it was harder to slow down.
Appearance: The **Tank 2** was the same size as Tank 1. The **Tank 2** had glowing yellow eyes, a drooling zombie face and maroon skin. The **Tank 2** also had smoke emitting from its torso with a magma trail being left when it walked, similar to the Molten Boss. It had long muscular arms and walked slightly hunchbacked.
Strategy: - The **Tank 2** is immune to the Pyromancer, so if you want to slow the **Tank 2** down, then you will have to use the Freezer.
- The Pyromancer will not even target the **Tank 2**.
- All units (such as those from the Military Base and Crook Boss) are destroyed when hit by rocks from the **Tank 2**.
- You can use towers that do not value as much as cheap distractions, such as the Scout or Pyromancer.
- This makes the **Tank 2** immobilised for a while, allowing other towers that are not stunned to attack it.
- Towers with a fast firerate, such as the Minigunner or Turret, are recommended to kill the **Tank 2**.
- The Rocketer can also be used as **Tanks 2** normally spawn in groups.
- Long range towers, such as the Outlaw, are recommended as they can be placed out of range of the **Tank 2's** *Molten Rock Throw*.
- The Freezer's *Ice Drop* can stop the **Tank 2** in its tracks.
- However, this does not prevent the **Tank 2** from attacking.
Trivia: - The arms of this enemy were taken from the Superhero package in the Roblox catalog.
- They also resembled the Tank from *R2D* and were likely a reference to the game.
- The **Tank 2** was also based on the Tank from *Left 4 Dead*.
- The Bulwark, an enemy added five years later after its removal, has a similar appearance to the **Tank 2**.

abilities.label: Ability 1
abilities.text: **Healing Gas** - Upon losing 66.67% of its health, the **Tanker** will release gas that is supposed to heal enemies around it in a radius of 12 by 1 health every 0.5 ticks for 15 seconds. However, due to bugs, this only happens once meaning this just heals 1 health. The **Tanker** cannot heal itself but can heal other **Tankers**.

abilities.label: Ability 2
abilities.text: **Toxic Fumes** - Upon death, applies a 70% Fatigue Debuff and a 20% Range Debuff to towers in a radius of 12, which lasts 10 seconds.

Description: The **Tanker** is a support enemy that appears in Molten mode, Challenge Trials and Badlands II. It also appears in The Takeover Event. It functions similarly to the Boomer, though in comparison it has higher health, slower speed and increased debuffs.

It has two abilities, all of which happen upon losing certain amounts of health. Upon losing 67% of its health, it will release gas that heals enemies in a radius of 12. While this is meant to heal them by 1 every 0.5 tick for 15 seconds, this due to bugs only happens once, meaning this ability in total heals 1 health for each enemy near it. The **Tanker** cannot heal itself but can heal other **Tankers**. Its second ability happens upon death, where it will apply a 70% Fatigue Debuff and a 20% Range Debuff to all towers in a radius of 12, which lasts 10 seconds.
Appearance: The **Tanker** has light green skin. It wears red pants with a black belt and brown bandages around its mutated arms. It also has grey hair. As its name suggests, it has multiple tanks on its body, some at the front of its torso and others at the back, held together with chains. Its arms also have multiple tubes going through them. On its head, it also wears a brown gas mask with neon red lens.
Strategy: - Killing the **Tanker** before it gets within range of your towers is the most ideal way to deal with **Tanker**. Keep in mind that it has quite a long debuff time.
- Placing your towers away from the path is a good way to avoid the **Tanker's** debuff.
- Long-range towers, such as the Hunter, Ranger or Turret are the best at keeping a distance away from the **Tanker**.
- The Engineer's sentries can also be useful, as the sentries cannot be debuffed.
- The DJ Booth allows towers to shoot the **Tanker** from further away, potentially defeating it before it blows up near your towers.
- It and the Commander can also partially negate the **Tanker's** debuffs.

- While the Medic is not able to shield towers from the Fatigue Debuff or Range Debuff, the shield on towers is not broken by them, meaning its Firerate Buff can be used to partially mitigate the **Tanker's** debuffs.
- Towers which are normally immune to stuns by default are not immune to the debuffs either.
Update History: - **Bug**: **Tanker's** *Healing Gas* ability only heals enemies once, resulting in it healing just 1 health in total when activated.
- Cash given increased from $2,000 to $2,500 every 50% health.
- **Bug**: No longer creates an explosion upon death or release toxic fumes after losing 66.7% of its health, unless triggered while it has Corpse.
- Now appears in Sk8 P4rk Master difficulty as part of The Takeover Event.
- No longer appears in Sk8 P4rk, as it has been removed.
- Health increased from 10,000 to 17,500 in Molten mode.
- Cash given increased from $2,500 to $8,750 every 50% health lost in Molten mode.
- **Bugfix**: Now can creates an explosion upon death without triggered through corpse.
- Cash given increased from $3 to $3,750 every 50% health lost in Challenge Trials.

templar.name: Templar
templar.description: The Templar was a high health enemy which appears in the Sandbox mode exclusive Legacy Fallen mode.

notice.text: Templar was previously removed on the 2nd of August 2024, though it has been made available through the Sandbox mode later.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Minigun** - The **Templar** stops and fires its laser minigun at nearby towers, stunning all towers hit for a period of time.

Description: The **Templar** was a high health enemy which appears in the Sandbox mode exclusive Legacy Fallen mode. It wields a minigun which is used to fire at towers randomly, which stuns them for a short period of time. It has defense, meaning that most forms of damage against the **Templar** is decreased. It also has 2,000 Shield Health.
Appearance: The **Templar** appears to be a futuristic warrior, with shiny metal armor and a laser minigun which glows neon red. It wears black and light grey armor and has green skin. It also wears black gloves. It wears a helmet with horns, with its eyes covered with a red strobe of light. It is slightly larger than the average enemy.
The **Templar** has a death animation, where it will drop its laser minigun and slowly fall backwards.
Strategy: - Like all other tanky enemies, high DPS towers like the Accelerator or Minigunner should be used to take the **Templar** down.
- The Commander should be used to boost the firerate of these towers.
- The Engineer is recommended, as its sentries will continue firing even when the Engineer is stunned by the **Templar's** *Minigun* ability.
- The Ranger and Pursuit cannot be stunned by the **Templar's** *Minigun* ability.
- The Military Base's units deal full collision damage to the **Templar**, regardless of its defense, making them quite useful.
- Do note that their ranged damage is still decreased.
- It is recommended to place your towers away from the path to avoid getting stunned by the **Templar's** *Minigun* ability.
- It may be viable to have a cheap distraction tower, like a Level 0 Commander, to distract the **Templar's** *Minigun* from your main offensive towers.
- When the **Templar** spawns, it will not use its *Minigun* ability for a few seconds. Use this period of time to defeat the **Templar** before it can stun any towers.
- The Medic can be used to cleanse towers of the **Templar's** stun with its *Revive* ability.
- Do note that this will be ineffective while the **Templar** is still firing its *Minigun*, as the towers will be continuously stunned until the ability is over.
- The Gladiator's stun blocking is ineffective against the **Templar**, as the first stun will be blocked, but not any subsequent stuns from the *Minigun's* continuous stream of bullets.
- Slowing towers like the Cryomancer, Electroshocker, Warden or Freezer can be used to slow down the **Templar**.
- However, because of its large size, freezing towers and the Warden will slow it down for a shorter amount of time.
- Additionally, stunning towers like the Electroshocker can only slow it down instead of stunning it because of its Stun Immunity.
- Do note that the **Templar** will not stop using its *Minigun* ability when frozen or stunned.
- Defense dropping towers like the Pyromancer, Jester or Freezer can help to reduce the **Templar's** defense.
Trivia: - The **Templar** is likely named after the Knights Templar, a Catholic medieval chivalric order, most infamously known for the Crusades.
- The **Templar's** original helmet is similar to the Great Helm, a helmet that was common in the Christendom of the Middle Ages.
- The **Templar** was loosely based on the Clay Templar from *Risk Of Rain 2*.
- The original **Templar** can be seen as a chess piece in the Chess Board map, parodying the Rook chess piece.
- Prior to the Overhaul Update, the **Templar** was one of the few enemies to gain a Shield. This Shield reduced the damage dealt by most towers to 2.
- The minigun it wields is a modified version of the Galactic Laser Gun gear from the Roblox catalog.
- While in-game the enemy has light green skin, in promotional renders it has red skin and its arms were covered in grey armor instead of being exposed. This is likely a development oversight.
Update History: - **Bug**: **Templar** never stops firing its minigun when the *Minigun* ability is used.
- **Bugfix**: **Templar** no longer uses its ability for an infinite amount of time.
- Energy Immunity replaced with Stun Immunity.
- **Templar** removed and replaced by the Warden in Fallen mode and replaced by the Warden in Hardcore mode.
- **Templar** now appears in Legacy Fallen mode, if activated through Sandbox mode.
- **Templar** no longer appears in Legacy Fallen mode, as it has been removed.
- **Templar** now appears in Legacy Fallen mode, if activated through Sandbox mode.
- Legacy version no longer copies the statistics of the modern version in Sandbox mode.
- **Bug**: **Templar** no longer uses the death sound effect.

the_umbra.name: The Umbra
the_umbra.description: The Umbra was the final boss of the Solar Eclipse Event. It had an extremely high amount of health but it had a very slow speed.

notice.text: The Umbra has been removed from the game as of the 26th of January 2022 as it was part of the Solar Eclipse Event.

stats.Attributes:

  - Energy Immunity

abilities.label: Ability 1
abilities.text: **Shot of the Century** - **The Umbra** starts laughing and then lines up a bow shot at the Star Cannon, decreasing the base health by 40. This has a cooldown of 60 seconds.

abilities.label: Ability 2
abilities.text: **Shooting Lunar** - **The Umbra** lines up a bow shot at the sky which rains arrows on towers, stunning towers hit for 10-14 seconds.

abilities.label: Ability 3
abilities.text: **Blazing Rage** - When **The Umbra** reaches half health, it speeds up significantly. It will also perform its *Shot of the Century* ability, regardless of cooldown status.

Description: **The Umbra** was the final boss of the Solar Eclipse Event. It had an extremely high amount of health but it had a very slow speed. It had two abilities, one where it fired multiple arrows on towers, stunning them and an ability where it fired at the Star Cannon, decreasing the base health by 40. When it reached half health, it increased its speed significantly. **The Umbra** was also immune to being slowed down by the Toxic Gunner and frozen by towers like the Sledger or Freezer. Additionally, because of its Energy Immunity, the Electroshocker could only slow down **The Umbra** instead of stunning it.
Uniquely, **The Umbra** could be stunned by the Star Cannon. This also prevented the *Shot of the Century* ability from finishing.
Appearance: **The Umbra** had black skin. It wore a magenta chestplate and leggings, with yellow patterns on them. It had brown hair with ponytails. It had a purple crown with a headpiece which represents the sun on its back. It had glowing yellow eyes. It has a purple bow on its back that it used to perform its abilities with. During *Blazing Rage*, **The Umbra** would emit a red aura around it.
Strategy: - High DPS towers, such as the Accelerator, Ranger, Pursuit and Turret, are recommended to defeat this boss.
- Support towers such as the Commander and DJ Booth are crucial since they can boost the firerate and range respectively.
- It is highly recommended to use the Star Cannon to stun **The Umbra**, and may be necessary to survive the *Shot of the Century* ability.

- The Star Cannon is best used when **The Umbra** is about to perform its *Shot of the Century* ability, as it cancels it out and prevents the loss of base health, which could otherwise lead to a defeat.
- **The Umbra** will laugh before it uses its *Shot of the Century* ability. This can be used to tell when to use the Star Cannon.
- It is recommended for one player to operate the Star Cannon, while one or two players look for Charges.
- It is not recommended to use the Star Cannon when **The Umbra** is not using its *Shot of the Century*, as you may not have enough Charges when it actually does use it, causing you to lose health.
- However, if **The Umbra** is near the exit, you should use the Star Cannon to prevent it from reaching the exit to give your towers more time to attack it.
- The Electroshocker can only slow down **The Umbra** instead of stunning it. It can also only slow down **The Umbra** for a shorter amount of time because of its large size.
- Other slowing towers are unable to slow **The Umbra** down.
Trivia: - **The Umbra's** name is the word for the inner shadow of any opaque object. When an eclipse happens, the celestial body caught within the umbra of the overlapping object experiences a total eclipse.
- **The Umbra** is the second enemy in the game to reach 1,000,000 base health, the first being the Frost Spirit.
- **The Umbra** is the second enemy to have voice acting, the first being Lord Sinister.
- **The Umbra** is voiced by AerelisVA.
- Before Wave 16, **The Umbra** could be seen walking across the side of Totality Tower.
- Upon death, glitch particles were emitted from **The Umbra's** body and the voicelines appeared to lag.
- On multiple renders and icons, **The Umbra** can be seen holding 2 daggers, one purple and one brown. These weapons never ended up being used when Totality Tower released, for unknown reasons.
- **The Umbra** appeared in a short video that promoted the MERRY2021 code, where it would give you a present.
- **The Umbra's** theme, Totality, is the term used to say the moment where there is total obscuration of the sun during an eclipse.
- This coincides with Totality Tower turning dark on Wave 16, representing a total solar eclipse.
- If Tower Defense Simulator won the Roblox Innovation Awards 2022, **The Umbra** was promised to return to the game.
- As this did not happen, **The Umbra** did not return. However, the Mimic Umbra enemy could be a reference to this.
- A younger **The Umbra** can be seen in cutscenes in A Dark Tale and The Haunted Past during the Lunar Overture Event.
- **The Umbra** is also featured in the beginning of the cutscene for Outpost 16 during the Null & Void Event.
- In the end of the second The Narratorium cutscene, Lord Exo places **The Umbra's** crown as the vessel on Dispatcher's head. This results in **The Umbra** being brought back to life.
- **The Umbra's** crown, Eclipse Crown was released as a limited UGC that could be obtained by beating The Great Finale, it had 12,000 stock.
Update History: - **Bug**: **The Umbra** can move while being stunned by the Star Cannon.

abilities.text: **Dark Decoy** - **Titus** summons five Neuro Runners and five Bloated Brain Bounds, all with a 0.2 second delay between each spawn. Gains Aggro and Tank attributes temporarily and a permanent 5% defense each ability usage.

Description: **Titus**, also referred to as **Maximus** in cutscenes, was the final boss of Failed Gateway, the first night of the Hexscape Event. It had a high amount of health and a fairly fast speed when compared to other bosses.

It had two abilities. The first was *Void Stream*, where **Titus** would windup and attack several towers in proximity. This would apply a 60% Firerate Debuff (150% increase) to them and regenerate its own health by 15 for each tower attacked at rapid speed. Its second ability, *Dark Decoy*, made it summon five Neuro Runners and five Bloated Brain Bounds, all with a 0.2 second delay between each spawn. Additionally, **Titus** itself would temporarily gain the Aggro and Tank attributes, while also gaining a permanent 5% defense increase.
Appearance: **Titus** had tan skin, with a part of its face being purple. Its right arm was replaced with a mechanical arm, which had three claws and a laser blaster in it. It had blond hair. It wore a khaki shirt and blue pants, alongside brown shoes. On its left arm, it had a metal shoulder-pad, multiple brown bandages, brown glove and black brass knuckles with spikes. It also wore a purple bandanna. On its torso, it had a large brown belt connected to a brown armor piece, which protected part of its mechanical arm that was connected to the torso. It had a brown belt with pouches and a grey plate with "*4OBIA*" written on it. It also had grey knee-pads.
Strategy: - Due to the low amount of waves to prepare, it is recommended to use more cost effective towers against **Titus**, such as the Golden Soldier, Militant or Engineer.
- In Easy mode, **Titus** has a lot less health, so it should not be a big issue. The DPS options that the preset loadouts contain should take care of it easily.
- You may bring support towers such as the DJ Booth and Commander to help boost your towers.

- Military Base is also a good option against **Titus**, due to the high health units dealing lots of collision damage. The high health units are also a great counter for *Dark Decoy*, as the units will buffer the enemies spawned in, helping reduce the effectiveness of the Aggro modifier.
- It is recommended to place a few towers as distraction so that **Titus** uses *Void Stream* on them instead of your DPS towers.
Trivia: - **Titus** is the name of a epistle in the New Testament, as well as the name of a Roman Emperor.
- Titus was one of the most common names in Ancient Rome.

- **Titus** was referred to as Maximus in Failed Gateway's beginning cutscene. As for some of the audio files, it is referred to as Titus Maximus, it is highly likely it is either its last name or some form of a secondary title.
- The belt **Titus** wears has the nameplate "*4OBIA*", which is a wordplay on the word "*phobia*".
- The voice actor of **Titus** is Enthrallist, who also works as a composer for Tower Defense Simulator.
- **Titus** had a cash/health ratio of 5 to 1 in Hard difficulty and 13.33 to 1 in Easy, the highest in the game.
- For context, **Titus** had 40,000 health in Hard and 15,000 in Easy and gave $200,000 total.
Update History: - **Bug**: Poison and electric defense dropping towers cannot drop its defense.
- **Bug**: **Titus** receives damage at rapid speed from unit collision, if the damage dealt is to its healed health.
- **Titus** can no longer have its defense decreased.
- **Bugfix**: Poison and electric defense dropping towers now can drop its defense if it is not a Boss enemy, though the Jester still cannot drop it.
