Description: The **Void** was an exclusive boss only available via admin commands during certain 2020 private testing sessions, and has not been in the game in any way since. The only public showcase of this enemy was done in a video made by JOHN ROBLOX, which also contains footage of features that never made it out of private tests, such as certain UI elements. The enemy itself was made as a joke which was never going to make it into the actual game. It had a high amount of health, a slow speed and three abilities.
It had three abilities:
- Its first ability was *Stomp*, which stunned towers for around 5 seconds.
- Its second ability was *Summon*, where it would summon multiple random enemies. These could be the Mystery, Mystery Boss, Glitch, Lava, Mega Slow, Abnormal Bosses and Shadow Boss.
- Its third ability, *Rage*, only happened at half health. It made it scream and slowly turn its torso, leg and crown color from purple to red, then summoning four First Forms.
Appearance: The **Void** had black head and arms. Its torso and legs were purple in colors, and there is a large pink gem on its torso. It had multiple small humanoids protruding from its body. It also wore a purple crown. After *Rage*, all its purple parts turned red, with the exception of the gem on its torso.
Trivia: - The **Void** is based on the boss with the same name from *Tower Battles*.
- Its regular appearance is a recreation of the third version of the Void.
- Its *Rage* appearance is a recreation of the second version of the Void.
- The First Forms it spawns are a recreation of the first version of the Void.
- The **Void's** crown is a retextured version of The Void Star accessory from the Roblox Catalog.
Notes: - ↑ https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HENz0rjbAE4

void_brute.name: Void Brute
void_brute.description: The Void Brute is a mini-boss that appears in both Hardcore and Voidcore modes. It has high health but rather slow speed.

stats.Attributes:
- Aggro (Bound Crush)
- Boss Immunities:
  - Freeze Immunity
  - Stun Immunity
  - Poison Slowdown
  - Confusion
  - Thorn Slowdown
  - Nuke Fallout Damage
  - DJ Booth Slowdown
  - Defense Dropping
  - Hacker Conversion
  - Hacker Slowdown
  - Slowed Immunity

abilities.label: Ability Cooldown: 27.5 Starting CD: 24
abilities.text:
**Bound Crush** - The **Void Brute** picks up a boulder from the ground, then throws it at a tower or unit in its range of 25, inflicting all towers in the radius of 6.5 with a 40% Fatigue Debuff (22.22% DPS loss) for 15 seconds while also dealing 100 damage to units. The boulder also splits into 8 smaller pieces, also inflicting the same Fatigue.
After using this ability, the **Void Brute** sets its Shield Health to 6,000 and gains Aggro which remains on it until all of its Shield Health is depleted.

Description: The **Void Brute** is a mini-boss that appears in both Hardcore and Voidcore modes. It has high health but rather slow speed.

The **Void Brute** has one ability, where it will pick up a boulder from the ground and throw it at a tower or unit in its range of 25. Upon impact, the boulder will split into multiple smaller boulders, which apply the same effects as it does. Any tower hit receives a 40% Fatigue Debuff (22.22% increase) while units receive 100 damage. When performing this ability, the Shield Health of the **Void Brute** is set to 6,000. While this Shield Health exists, the **Void Brute** becomes an Aggro enemy and stays this way until all the Shield Health is depleted. As it just changes the Shield Health rather than adding it, this means that if this ability is used while the Shield Health from the previous ability usage has not been fully depleted, it will not add 6,000 Shield Health on top of the currently existing Shield Health, but instead just changes it back to 6,000 again.
Logbook Description: "*Void Brutes are the strongest fighters of bloomed realms, fallen victim to the whispers of the Void. The power held within the gems strengthened their bodies and gradually began consuming them, solidifying into a singular giant mass that they use as a weapon. They are naturally a bit dumb, and spend most of their time laying in a field of flowers as their bodies slowly turn into stone and gem.*"
Appearance: The **Void Brute** is a creature with white skin. The left side of its body has been fully corrupted, turning its skin black there, also giving it purple veins, purple crystals, flowers and purple. In its torso, it has a giant hole. It wears beige cloth around its waist. It has a white head with part of it missing, being filled in with a mixture of small white and black pieces.
Strategy: - High DPS towers such as the Engineer, Kingpin, Accelerator and Juggernaut are required to deal with the **Void Brute**.
- The Commander can be a good support option to dealing with the **Void Brute's** Aggro target and Shield Health.
- Dealing with the other enemies will make the **Void Brute's** *Bound Crush* ability less threatening.
- In Voidcore mode, it is recommended to deal as much damage to the **Void Brute** as possible before Wave 35 starts, as the **Void Brute** and Void Keeper together can be quite threatening.
- The **Void Brute** can often reach far enough to leave the range of towers. If using the DJ Booth, it is recommended to switch to the Purple track once it leaves the range of towers.
Trivia: - The **Void Brute's** name, appearance and ability are based on the Brute enemy.
- The *Bound Crush* ability resembles the *Rock Throw* ability from the Brute from the SFOTH Event and Tank's first and second version.
- Ironically, **Void Brute** has fewer abilities than Brute.
- The **Void Brute's** concept art has the **Void Brute** wear chains on its left arm while also having an eye on its face, though these details are not present in-game.
- The **Void Brute** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - Health increased from 75,000 to 80,000 in Voidcore mode.
- *Bound Crush* starting ability cooldown increased from 17.5 to 24.
- **Void Brute** now appears in Nil Zone II as part of the Halloween 2026 Live Events.
- **Void Brute** no longer spawns in Nil Zone II, as the Halloween 2026 Live Event has ended.
Notes: - ↑ Only the first **Void Brute** spawned in Hardcore and Voidcore modes is a boss.

void_caster.name: Void Caster
void_caster.description: The Void Caster is the final boss of Voidcore mode, alongside with the Void Reaver at the final wave.

stats.Attributes:
- Boss
- No Target (When Void Reaver is alive)
- God (When Void Reaver is alive)

abilities.label: Ability 1 Cooldown: 45
abilities.text: **Shield** - Shields the Void Reaver, briefly giving it Health Regen, then sets its Shield Health to 40,000.

abilities.label: Ability 2 Cooldown: 125
abilities.text: **Summon** - Summons in a portal that lasts on the map for 16 seconds, with each set of spawns taking up 4 seconds of that duration. Each time it will spawn 22 enemies, which can be the Mandragora with a 20% chance (2 max, 0.15 delay), Slow King with a 15% chance (1 max, 0.3 delay), Blighted with a 25% chance (10 max, 0.15 delay), Unknown Small with a 15% chance (3 max, 0.15 delay) and Elite Void Rusher with a 27.78% chance (6 max, 0.03 delay).

abilities.label: Ability 3
abilities.text: **Revive** - When the Void Reaver dies, it will spend 12 seconds reviving the Void Reaver to 420,000 health, but it loses the No Target and God attributes for the duration. Upon defeat, instantly revives the Void Reaver to 240,000 health, and activates its *Void's Deathwish* ability.

abilities.label: Ability 4
abilities.text: **Rage** - Upon reaching 40% of its health, the **Void Caster** changes its appearance and reduces its speed to 1.

Description: The **Void Caster** is the final boss of Voidcore mode, alongside with the Void Reaver at the final wave. It does not spawn in naturally, and can be only spawned when the Void Reaver reaches half of its health. It has extremely high amount of health, around half of the Void Reaver's, and has No Target and God. When the Void Reaver is killed, the **Void Caster** loses its shield. While vulnerable, it begins to revive the Void Reaver for a short period of time. Once revived, the **Void Caster** becomes invulnerable again. This process repeats itself until the **Void Caster** is defeated, where it revives the Void Reaver one last time with its *Void's Deathwish* ability active.
The **Void Caster** has four abilities:
- *Shield*, where it shields the Void Reaver, briefly giving it Health Regen, then sets its Shield Health to 40,000.

- *Summon*, causing it to summons in a portal that lasts on the map for 16 seconds, with each set of spawns taking up 4 seconds of that duration. Each time, it will spawn 22 enemies, which can be the Mandragora with a 20% chance (2 max, 0.15 delay), Slow King with a 15% chance (1 max, 0.3 delay), Blighted with a 25% chance (10 max, 0.15 delay), Unknown Small with a 15% chance (3 max, 0.15 delay) and Elite Void Rusher with a 25% chance (6 max, 0.03 delay).

- *Revive*, which happens when the Void Reaver dies. It will spend 12 seconds reviving the Void Reaver to 420,000 health, but it will also lose the No Target and God attributes for the duration. Upon defeat, it instantly revives the Void Reaver to 240,000 health and activates its *Void's Deathwish* ability.
- *Rage*, which is a rage mode ability triggered at 40% health. The **Void Caster** changes its appearance and reduce its speed to 1.
Logbook Description: "*Before there was anything to call the Old World, the Void was already waiting in the dark. It cannot be considered a place or a creature, but something else entirely. It is a quiet hunger that lurks beneath the notice of every being, the presence that can be felt when nothing is around. The pale flora that blooms in a place where nothing exists is where it finds its peace. It is of one mind, though it wears a thousand faces. One could call it an incurable infection.*

*The brothers feared it, and even Lord Exo and Two X, who feared so little, understood that there was no killing a thing without a body. For the first and final time, they drove it deep down into the foundations of the world, into a dark so total its song could never be heard again. There were a handful of witnesses to this event, but all knew that the Void was only contained, not gone. They all knew the difference, and never spoke of it again.*

*Somewhere in time within the Void, a flower grew, blossoming with a vibrant hue of purple. It was beautiful. From it grew a vessel, and soon, it grew a voice. The child opened her eyes to find nothing but darkness, and smiled the widest smile. Looking down, she picked up a fallen petal from where she grew and crushed it within her palm. The falling dust, scattered through the empty wind, and suddenly flora began to grow. The child was not the Void. The child called it Mother. What she did know was that she was the Void Caster, the daughter of the Void.*

*Once Lord Exo learned of her existence, he saw an opportunity. He did not trust her so much as he used her. When the war between him and Two X began, he unearthed the Void and offered a deal to the Void Caster. She would walk beside him as his prized General, and in return the flora of the Void would take root in every realm and bloom. She still intends to keep that promise.*

*When Lord Exo was sealed away, Two X turned his attention to the Void itself, hunting it throughout the Nil Zone. So the Void slunk back into the depths from which it was sealed, and the Void Caster went to the one place Two X would never follow. Straight into the heart of the Void itself. Even he would not set foot there. Even though a God cannot be killed, there are things worse than death that the Void was patiently waiting to do.*

*The Meta exists everywhere across the entire Nil Zone, but it was not until the Rift Walker fell and the realms began to destabilize that the seams gave. Holes formed that connected the two worlds, and through the thinnest of those tears the Void crept out once more. In the barrens of the Nil Zone, where there was once life, a single lone flower blossomed from the earth.*

*To kill the Void Caster is to misunderstand what she is. The body may no longer exist, and her song may go quiet for a while. But deep within the dark, it will begin again. At best, all one can do is send her home to Mother."*
Appearance: The **Void Caster** has a black body, purple eyes, and purple hair. She wears a purple and black robe with flowers on it, a black shirt, purple pants with a purple high-low skirt that is really short, a purple belt, purple shoes, and black gloves. She has purple horns on her head that have dark purple vines circling them, 2 on each horn, and a halo floating above her head. She carries a staff and a spell book in her hands. Once she has entered her second phase, she starts wearing a hood, and six horns will come out of her torso.

On the matchmaking render, her robe is light purple, a light purple shirt, and black strings holding the sides of her robe loosely close. Her torso horns are black with light purple tips that glow. Her face is obscured by her hair, which is purple, and by a cage mask (This is assumed, please change if wrong), similar to the Void Reaver's, but only on her face, which also seems to be extending to her shoulders from the right and left grilles. Her pants are also light purple now, and her skin is purple.
Strategy: - Prioritize the **Void Caster** as soon as the Void Reaver's health reaches 0.
- Abilities like the Medic's *Ubercharge*, the Commander's *Call to Arms* and the Saboteur's *Aggressive Toxins* are best used here.

- When **Void Caster** dies, the Void Reaver will use its *Void Deathwish* ability where it sprints towards the base. It is advised that you use all of your abilities and move your towers to the back once **Void Caster** dies to avoid being killed by the Void Reaver.
Trivia: - The **Void Caster** is the first boss enemy that gets slower upon activating its second phase.
- The **Void Caster** has the longest logbook description in the entire game, also having the only description with multiple paragraphs.
- The **Void Caster** could be considered as the only Boss enemy not to naturally spawn in.

- The Awakened Fallen King may be considered an enemy that does not naturally spawn into the Hidden Wave, but it may also be considered the second phase of the Fallen King, which does naturally spawn into Fallen mode.
- The **Void Caster** was planned to be a secondary boss for Hardcore mode back in 2020, but was cut due to time and technical constraints.
- It is likely that **Void Caster** being cut is the reason why Hardcore mode initially had two Void Reavers before v1.2.1.
- The **Void Caster** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
- The **Void Caster's** theme Vocatis Inanis, when translated from Latin to English, translates to "*Call of the void*", "*Called from the void*" or "*You call the void*".
Update History: - No longer summons the Void Brute, as it is been removed from the summon pool. Had 2.5% chance to be spawned with 1 max spawns and 3 delay.
- Slow King chance decreased from 17.5% to 15%.
- Mandragora max spawns decreased from 6 to 3.
- Unknown Small max spawns decreased from 9 to 5.
- Slow King max spawns decreased from 6 to 3.
- Cash given changed from $1,000,000 on death to $275,000 every 25% health lost.
- *Revive* Void Reaver health increased from 360,000 to 420,000.
- Elite Void Rusher delay decreased from 0.2 to 0.03.
- Elite Void Rusher max spawns decreased from 20 to 6.
- Unknown Small delay decreased from 0.25 to 0.15.
- Unknown Small max spawns decreased from 5 to 3.
- Blighted max spawns decreased from 20 to 10.
- Slow King delay decreased from 0.6 to 3.
- Slow King max spawns decreased from 3 to 1.
- Mandragora max spawns decreased from 3 to 2.
Notes: - ↑ https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qXsG3Lxnasg (1:22:57)

void_cultist.name: Void Cultist
void_cultist.description: The Void Cultist is a support enemy that appears in both Hardcore and Voidcore modes. It has decent health and slightly slow speed.

stats.Attributes:
- Stun Immune
- Freeze Immune
- Health Regen (Variable)

abilities.label: Ability Cooldown: 6 Starting CD: 6
abilities.text: **Incantation Spell** - Spawns a Healing Beacon.

Description: The **Void Cultist** is a support enemy that appears in both Hardcore and Voidcore modes. It has decent health and slightly slow speed. It has one ability where it will summon a Healing Beacon on the path that heals any enemy it passes through by 675 every 0.1 seconds. This Healing Beacon lasts 6 seconds and, once gone, the **Void Cultist** will wait around 6 seconds more before summoning another one.
Logbook Description: "*The Void Cultist is a specialized Odd who found purpose in the Void. When their realms were being destroyed, they welcomed the end with open arms. For that, the Void rewarded them and Void Caster turned them into the Void Cultist. They preach the whispers of the Void and hold ceremonies for the army to partake in. Where others in the army were taken by the Void, the Cultists chose it, and they carry that distinction with quiet pride. Their devotion is expressed not through combat but through care, mending their fellow followers so that the army may march on. They are pacifists by conviction, and they chose to keep it that way.*"
Appearance: The **Void Cultist** has a black body. It wears a purple robe with a gold and purple cape and purple hood. It has a few purple and gold thorns coming out of its back. It has a gold and purple mask with multiple flowers covering its face. It will occasionally summon incantation circles around itself when using its ability.
Strategy: - It is important to focus best on taking down the **Void Cultist** as soon as possible when it spawns. While their Healing Beacons cannot damage your base, they can rapidly heal enemies within those beacons.
- Setting the targeting to some of your towers on *Last Enemy*, especially those of higher DPS, can help take down the **Void Cultists** as fast as possible, as they usually spawn in the back.
- If you have the Gatling Gun, you can freely focus on the **Void Cultist(s)** when in *FPS* mode, even if there are nearby enemies with Aggro.

- If you have a Saboteur that is at least at Level 3, you can use its *Aggressive Toxins* ability on the **Void Cultist(s)** to force nearby towers to target them, even if other nearby enemies have Aggro.
Trivia: - The **Void Cultist** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Void Cultist** added, replacing the Health Cultist.
- Health decreased from 25,000 to 20,000 in Voidcore mode.

void_eye.name: Void Eye
void_eye.description: The Void Eye is an enemy that appears in Hardcore Mode and the Voidcore Mode. The Void Eye is primarily summoned by the Void Reaver and the Soul Stealer...

abilities.label: Ability Cooldown: 4-5
abilities.text: **The Void's Gaze** - Fires at a tower or unit in its range of 22.5 but not in its minimal range of 7.5, creating an explosion with a radius of 4 that stuns towers for 3 seconds and deals 200 damage to units.

Description: The **Void Eye** is an enemy that appears in Hardcore Mode and the Voidcore Mode. The **Void Eye** is primarily summoned by the Void Reaver and the Soul Stealer, it does not appear naturally in either of the two modes. The **Void Eye** has a decent amount of health and moves at such a slow speed it is practically immobile. It will fire a projectile every 4-5 seconds at a tower or unit that crates an explosion with a radius of 4, stunning towers for 3 seconds and dealing 200 damage to units.
Logbook Description: "*The Void Eyes are pulled from what were once creatures that roamed the Void. Even now, there are many things that have bloomed within the darkness after realms have found their peace. Nothing is left to waste, and some of the more valuable parts are turned into pieces of the Void Caster’s army. When they aren’t attacking, they weep quietly to themselves, hidden off in a corner until they are needed again.*"
Appearance: The **Void eye** is a floating purple eyeball with a black eye socket as its body. Around it is a purple-like effect and in its center it has a black elliptical pupil.
Strategy: - To prevent the **Void Eye** from stunning towers, you can set high DPS towers, such as the Juggernaut to *Weakest* or to *Last Enemy* to deal with them.
- Towers such as the Farm can be used to bait their attacks.
- Despite stunning towers, the **Void Eye** will actually target towers immune to stuns, allowing practically any tower to be used for this purpose.
- The Mercenary Base's *Air-Drop* ability with the units all set to Riot Guard can be used by sending the units directly at the **Void Eye**.
Trivia: - The **Void Eye** is most likely based on the Roblox accessory, the The Hematite Eye.
- Excluding immobile enemies, the **Void Eye** is the slowest enemy in the game, as it is ten times slower than the Ice Beacon.
- The **Void Eye** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - Health decreased from 20,000 to 15,000 in Voidcore mode.

void_floater.name: Void Floater
void_floater.description: The Void Floater is a Flying enemy that appeared in Hardcore mode and Voidcore mode. It is serves as a stronger Balloon for later waves of these modes.

stats.Speed:
- Above Average (4, with pod)
- Below Average (2.7, without pod)

Description: The **Void Floater** is a Flying enemy that appeared in Hardcore mode and Voidcore mode. It is serves as a stronger Balloon for later waves of these modes. When it loses the Shield Health, the pod that the **Void Floater** has with it breaks, causing it to fall down to the ground. This makes it lose the the Flying attribute, making it vulnerable to towers without flying detection, and also multiplies its speed by 0.675, reducing its speed down to 2.7.
Logbook Description: "*To take care of a ‘Pod’ is to take care of a child. It needs to be nurtured from start to forever. Vast amounts of Void energy are crammed into these floating pods that are so proudly held overhead by the Void Floater. They are extremely passionate about taking care of it. Once the Pod is destroyed, it will fall to the ground and the Void Floater experiences something like agony, as it is the equivalent of losing their child.*"
Appearance: The **Void Floater** has glowing purple skin. It wears a black and purple robe, purple pants, purple belt and black shoes. It had a glowing purple pod overhead which it uses to float above the path. This pod appears to be a purple opaque team beacon from the classic game *Crossroads*. Once it loses all of its Shield Health, the pod will break, causing it to fall to the ground.
Strategy: - The **Void Floater** is one of the most dangerous enemies in the modes it appears in, with high health, the Flying attribute, and often appears in large groups. As such, high DPS towers with flying detection like the Ranger and Pursuit are required to deal with it.
- Early on, the Engineer can handle **Void Floaters** somewhat consistently, though it is not recommended to completely depend on it.
- AOE damage from towers like the Tesla and Mortar is recommended against large groups of **Void Floaters**.
- The Firework Technician can provide flying detection to nearby towers to help against the **Void Floater**.
- Note that the detection duration lasts for a rather short interval.
- As the **Void Floater** has Stun Immune, stun effects from towers such as Tesla are ineffective against it.
Trivia: - The **Void Floater** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Void Floater** now appears in Nil Zone II as part of the Halloween 2026 Live Events.
- **Void Floater** no longer spawns in Nil Zone II, as the Halloween 2026 Live Event has ended.

void_guardian.name: Void Guardian
void_guardian.description: The Void Guardian is a tanky enemy that appears in both Hardcore and Voidcore modes. It has high health but rather slow speed.

abilities.label: Ability
abilities.text: **Spear of the Void** - Attacks a tower or unit in its range of 24, then thrusts its spear which creates an attack area with the same range but an angle of 15. Any tower hit is frozen for 10 seconds while units receive 250 damage instead. Also sets its Shield Health to 25,000.

Description: The **Void Guardian** is a tanky enemy that appears in both Hardcore and Voidcore modes. It has high health but rather slow speed.

The **Void Guardian** has one ability, where it will attack a tower or unit in its range of 24, then thrust a spear at it, creating an attack with the same range but an angle of 15. Towers hit by this move will get frozen for 10 seconds while units receive 250 damage. When performing this ability, the Shield Health of the **Void Guardian** is set to 25,000. As it just changes the Shield Health rather than adding it, this means that if this ability is used while the Shield Health from the previous ability usage has not been fully depleted, it will not add 25,000 Shield Health on top of the currently existing Shield Health, but instead just change it back to 25,000 again.
Logbook Description: "*The Void Guardian is usually found surrounding the outskirts of the Void Army to protect them from the creatures that lie within it. Many of the giants that were created during the Old World by both Void Caster and Lord Exo have fallen, but not all died. Some slunk back into the darkness of the Void where they continue to reside. It’s unknown if they would ever resurface, but the Void Guardian stands guard regardless, for even the Void Caster barely has control over the creatures she had created. The will of the Void is a dangerous thing.*"
Appearance: The **Void Guardian** has a black body. It wears purple pants, shirt, gloves and belt. It has a purple chestplate on its torso with chains wrapped around it and a visor on its head. It has purple horns coming out of its head and corruption on its right shoulder. It wears a brown cape it covers its left arm with. It carries a purple and gold spear it attacks towers and units with.
Strategy: - High DPS towers like the Juggernaut, Turret and Pursuit are recommended against the **Void Guardian**.
- Towers with high range are also recommended, as they can be placed at a safe distance from the **Void Guardian**.
- The **Void Guardian's** *Spear of the Void* ability can be quite dangerous, as without the Medic, majority of the towers are not immune to freeze.
- Using the Juggernaut's top path can negate some of the freeze time.
- Note that stalling the **Void Guardian** is much harder than with most other enemies, as it is both Stun and Freeze Immune.
- Towers that inflict Slowed like the Hacker and DJ Booth can still slow the **Void Guardian** down. Poison towers such as the Saboteur are also fully effective against it.
Trivia: - The **Void Guardian** in Voidcore mode has the highest health for a non-Boss enemy in the game.
- The non-Boss enemy with the second highest health, the Nuclear Guardian, only has 175,000 health, not accounting for Bloated during its first wave appearance.
- The **Void Guardian** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - Cash given on death increased from $75,000 to $100,000 in Voidcore mode.

void_keeper.name: Void Keeper
void_keeper.description: The Void Keeper, internally referred to as Void Grave Digger, is a mini-boss that appears in both the Hardcore and Voidcore modes.

abilities.label: Ability 1 Cooldown: 30
abilities.text: **Shovel** - Digs up multiple rocks from the ground with its shovel, then flings them at towers in a range of 20. Stuns towers for 4 seconds and deals 150 damage to units.

abilities.label: Ability 2 Cooldown: 27.5
abilities.text: **Summon** - Points its shovel into the air, causing it to get struck with lightning, temporarily giving it No Target. This leads to multiple enemies getting summoned for 4 seconds, which can be the Voidling (6% chance, 0.55 delay), Elite Lead (32% chance, 0.125 delay) or Mandrake (62% chance, 0.125 delay). Afterwards it receives around a 25% speed boost for 16 seconds.

abilities.label: Ability 3 Cooldown: 35
abilities.text: **Stomp** - Stomps the ground, creating a shockwave that stuns towers for 3 seconds and deals 150 damage to units.

abilities.label: Ability 4
abilities.text: **Wayfarer** - Upon reaching 25% of its health, speed is set to 3.5.

Description: The **Void Keeper**, internally referred to as **Void Grave Digger**, is a mini-boss that appears in both the Hardcore and Voidcore modes. It has a high amount of health and a decent fast speed, especially when combined with two of its abilities which either permanently or temporarily boost its speed.
The **Void Keeper** has four abilities:

- The first ability, *Shovel*, has the **Void Keeper** digging up rocks from the ground, then flinging them at towers or units in a range of 20. Any tower hit by these rocks will get stunned for 4 seconds while units receive 150 damage.

- The second ability, *Summon*, makes the **Void Keeper** point its shovel into the air, temporarily giving it No Target. This makes purple lightning hit it, causing various enemies to start spawning for 4 seconds. These can be the Voidling (6% chance, 0.55 delay), Elite Lead (32% chance, 0.125 delay) or Mandrake (62% chance, 0.125 delay). Afterwards it receives around a 25% speed boost for 16 seconds.
- The third ability is *Stomp*. When performed, the **Void Keeper** will stomp the ground, creating a shockwave that stuns towers for 3 seconds and deals 150 damage to units.
- The last ability is a rage mode type ability, the *Wayfarer*, triggered when it reaches 25% of its health. Once reached, it will boost its speed to 3.5.
Logbook Description: "*The Void Keeper is a specialized variant of Slow King who wallowed in the depths of their agony and decided they had to take on the task of burying their kingdom. After a realm collapse, the Void Keeper will quietly carry the dead and bury them. Some of the corpses will turn into food for the flora while others will either reanimate into Odds or decompose into skeletons. It is not known how the Void Keeper feels about this, but to this day it still quietly shovels away grave after grave.*"
Appearance: The **Void Keeper** has a black body and purple eyes. It wears a purple coat with a hood, purple pants, black shoes, brown belts and multiple brown bandages. Its body is overgrown in various plants and flowers. On its left shoulder, it has a skull shoulder-pad while on its right, it has a regular purple shoulder-pad. It has a cracked purple tombstone attached to its right arm. On its back, it has a giant tombstone which is attached to its with a set of chains. It carries a shovel with its right arm.
Strategy: - High DPS towers such as the Crook Boss, Juggernaut and Turret are required to deal with the **Void Keeper**.
- The Engineer is recommended against the Void Keeper, with its sentries bypassing the **Void Keeper's** stuns and handling the large hordes that both spawn from and alongside it.
- In Voidcore mode, the **Void Keeper** is spawned alongside the Void Brute and a large group of enemies. Bringing splash damage towers like the Mortar and Rocketeer is recommended.
- During the **Void Keeper's** *Summon* ability, it gains the No Target attribute, preventing it from being attacked normally. As such, towers will be forced to to target its summons.

- The Medic can be used to negate the **Void Keeper's** stuns, allowing for the **Void Keeper** to be killed before other enemies arrive to support it. Alternatively, stun immune towers like the Pursuit can be used instead.

- Once the **Void Keeper** activates its *Wayfarer* ability, it becomes significantly faster. As such, bringing high range towers like the Ranger and Turret can prevent it from exiting the range of your towers.

- The **Void Keeper** has no direct immunities other than those that come with the Boss attribute, so most freeze towers can help slow it down. Due to its size and the Boss attribute, stuns will only slow it down.
Trivia: - The **Void Keeper's** appearance and abilities are based on the Grave Digger enemy.
- Internally, it is also called the *Void Grave Digger* and was referred to as the *Voidgraver* by BelowNatural when first announced.
- Its current name is likely a reference to the Gravekeeper enemy that existed before the MEGA Update.
- Despite all of these similarities, the **Void Keeper** is actually just a variant of the Slow King that decided they had to bury their kingdom.
- The concept art of the **Void Keeper** was created by @DaddyDonuts.
- The **Void Keeper** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Void Keeper** added, replacing the Grave Digger.
- Health increased from 90,000 to 100,000 in Hardcore mode.
- Health increased from 30,000 to 40,000 in Voidcore mode.
- No longer summons the Void Rusher, which used to have a 20% chance and a 0.3 delay.
- Elite Lead chance increased from 30% to 32%.
- Elite Lead delay decreased from 0.15 to 0.125.
Notes: - ↑ https://x.com/BelowNatural/status/2055747734204830141

void_knight.name: Void Knight
void_knight.description: The Void Knight is a tanky enemy that appears in Hardcore and Voidcore modes. It has high health and below average speed...

stats.Attributes:
- Stun Immune
- Freeze Immune
- Health Regen (Sword of Loyalty)

abilities.label: Ability Cooldown: 12
abilities.text: **Sword of Loyalty** - Swings its sword up to two times at a tower or unit, slashing everything in a radius of 8 and an angle of 20 for 5 seconds and dealing 132 damage to units. After attacking, gains Health Regen for 6 seconds.

Description: The **Void Knight** is a tanky enemy that appears in Hardcore and Voidcore modes. It has high health and below average speed, alongside multiple immunities to many forms of stalling. It has one ability where it will swing its sword up to two times at a tower or unit, creating a slash with a radius of 8 and an angle of 20. This will stun towers for 5 seconds and deal 132 damage to units. Using this ability will also give it Health Regen for 6 seconds.
Logbook Description: "*Void Knights are the trusted warriors of Void Caster. They follow her everywhere and were the first to be woken from their slumber when the time came to march again. These Knights serve the Void Caster’s will absolutely, commanded by the Void Sword Master, her lead knight and the only one permitted to give them orders in her absence. They train without rest, sparring against one another and whatever unfortunate creatures stumble too close in the Void. They are known hunters, relentless in pursuit, and will chase a target across the nothing for as long as it takes. They do not stop. They do not tire. And they have never once failed to complete a mission, which is something the Void Sword Master makes sure everyone in the army is aware of.*"
Appearance: The **Void Knight** has a black body. It wears purple and gold body armor consisting of a chestplate, leggings, shoulder pads, armbands, shoes and helmet. It wears a brown cape. Various purple spikes come out of its armor and on many spots of it there are purple gems. On the top of its helmet, it has a purple plume. Purple aura comes out of right eye. It wields a purple sword which it attacks towers and units with.
Strategy: - The **Void Knight** has high health, meaning units with high DPS such as the Juggernaut, Accelerator and Pursuit are recommended against it.
- Support towers like the Commander, DJ Booth or Medic can be used to boost the DPS of your towers.
- The **Void Knight** stuns towers, making stun immune towers useful here.
- The Medic can be used to protect towers by either giving them Stun Immunity or giving them a shield which will need to recharge when broken.
- Top path Juggernaut can also be used to reduce the stun duration on towers in its secondary range.
Trivia: - The **Void Knight** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - Cash given on death decreased from $42,000 to $35,000.

void_pike.name: Void Pike
void_pike.description: The Void Pike is a Lead enemy that appears in Hardcore and Voidcore modes. It is the third Lead enemy to appear in these modes, being stronger on them.

Description: The **Void Pike** is a Lead enemy that appears in Hardcore and Voidcore modes. It is the third Lead enemy to appear in these modes, being stronger on them. Unlike all the ones that appeared before it, it never loses its Lead.
Logbook Description: "*Void Pikes acted as the transporters that drove the army. They would gather supplies, help move weapons, and work on general tasks. They sprint from one place to another without ever seeming to tire, and they never complain. It seems they know every route, including places they have never been to. You can always tell a Void Pike apart by the armor they wear.*"
Appearance: The **Void Pike** has dark skin. It wears a purple shirt, purple checkered chestplate, grey gloves, grey pants, brown shoes and a cracked helmet.
Strategy: - Unlike the Lead and Elite Lead, **Void Pike** does not lose the Lead attribute. Therefore, upgrading towers with lead detection to higher levels is essential to dealing with **Void Pikes**.
- Towers that deal splash damage, such as the Mortar and Golden Demoman, are especially useful against **Void Pikes** because of how they tend to spawn in groups.
- Other towers with lead detection like the Engineer or Saboteur can also be used.
Trivia: - The **Void Pike** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
- The appearance of this enemy appears to have been based on the Pike from the Solar Eclipse Event.

void_portal.name: Void Portal
void_portal.description: The Void Portal is an immobile summoner enemy that appears in Hardcore and Voidcore modes. It does not appear naturally and instead spawned by the Void Trickster.

abilities.label: Ability Cooldown: 14
abilities.text: **Void Vault** - Summons in eight Voidlings with a 0.15 delay between each.

Description: The **Void Portal** is an immobile summoner enemy that appears in Hardcore and Voidcore modes. It does not appear naturally and instead spawned by the Void Trickster. It has decent health and cannot move. Its only purpose is to spawn eight Voidlings every 14 seconds, with a 0.15 delay between each Voidling spawn.
Logbook Description: "*The Void Portal is circular in shape, does a lot of spooky sounding things, and otherwise doesn’t like to be bothered. It simply likes to connect one place to another. That’s about it. If someone from the Void Army pesters a Void Portal enough it will intentionally send them to the outer far reaches of the eternal nothing, leaving them all alone for eternity. Void Caster knows the Void Portal does this, and out of pity will go and bring the unfortunate creature back to her army. Sometimes, she scolds the portal for it. The portal, however, doesn’t seem to care and will absolutely do it again. In fact. It already did.*"
Appearance: The **Void Portal** is a large purple portal in the shape of a circle.
Strategy: - The **Void Portal** should be dealt with as soon as possible, otherwise it is likely you will be overwhelmed by the large hordes of Voidlings spawned. This is even more important if several **Void Portals** are active as they can collectively spawn a vast number of Voidlings.
- Long-range towers like the Ranger or Pursuit set to *Last Enemy* are highly effective at taking out **Void Portals** quickly, along with the Void Tricksters that create them.
- You can also use the Gatling Gun to focus on **Void Portals** before they spawn too many Voidlings.
- Splash damage towers like the Mortar can be used to clear out the groups of Voidlings spawned.
Trivia: - The **Void Portal** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - Voidling spawn count increased from 6 to 8.
- **Void Portal** now appears in Nil Zone II as part of the Halloween 2026 Live Events.
- **Void Portal** no longer spawns in Nil Zone II, as the Halloween 2026 Live Event has ended.

void_reaper.name: Void Reaper
void_reaper.description: The Void Reaper is a summoner enemy that appears in Hardcore and Voidcore modes. It has decent health, around the same as the Voidling, but only an average speed.

stats.Attributes:
- Stun Immune
- Freeze Immune
- Health Regen (Variable)

abilities.label: Ability Cooldown: 20
abilities.text: **Summon** - Slams its scythe and summons in four Mysteries, each with a 0.4 delay before another.

Description: The **Void Reaper** is a summoner enemy that appears in Hardcore and Voidcore modes. It has decent health, around the same as the Voidling, but only an average speed. It has one ability where it will scythe and summon in four Mysteries. There is a 0.4 delay between each spawn.
Logbook Description: "*The Void Reaper hunts the wandering Souls that are created after a realm’s death. They herd them like sheep and drive the Souls into finding their individual identity once more so they can be fully incorporated into the Void army. Some Souls can be disobedient or still hold onto fragments of their past selves. If this is the case, the Void Reaper will slice the Soul in two, and they will be forever lost to the Void.*"
Appearance: The **Void Reaper** has black skin, pink eyes and no legs. It floats above the path. It wears a purple robe with a hood and a brown belt with a few skulls tied to it. Its left arm. Its left arm is entirely made out of bones and it has a skull shoulder-pad with neon purple eyes there. On its chest, it has a partially exposed ribcage. On its face, it has a few flowers growing on its eyes and two horns. It carries a scythe with chains wrapped around it.
Strategy: - High DPS towers like the Crook Boss, Golden Minigunner, Engineer or Kingpin can be used to take it down.
- AOE towers like the Mortar or Rocketeer can be used to help clear out it and the enemies it summons.
- Support towers like the Commander, DJ Booth or Medic can be used to boost the DPS of your towers.
- Due to its immunities, the **Void Reaper** cannot be frozen or chilled by freezing towers.
- Similarly, stunning towers will only slow it down instead of stunning it.
Trivia: - The **Void Reaper** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Void Reaper** added, replacing the Fallen Reaper.
- **Void Reaper** now appears in Nil Zone II as part of the Halloween 2026 Live Events.
- **Void Reaper** no longer spawns in Nil Zone II, as the Halloween 2026 Live Event has ended.

void_reaver.description: The Void Reaver is the final boss of Hardcore mode and Voidcore mode that spawns on Wave 45 and 50 respectively.

- Extremely Slow (0.65, Voidcore)
- Extremely Slow (0.9, Sandbox)
- Very Slow (1.0625, Void Wrath, Hardcore)
- Extremely Slow (0.85, Void Wrath, Voidcore)
- Slightly Fast (4.5, Void Deathwish)
stats.Attributes:

  - Freeze Immunity
  - Stun Immunity
  - Poison Slowdown

  - Nuke Fallout Damage
  - DJ Booth Slowdown

  - Hacker Slowdown

abilities.label: Ability 1 Cooldown: 17.5
abilities.text: **Cursed Blade** - The **Void Reaver** slashes its sword forward, creating a straight shockwave which applies a 100% Fatigue Debuff (40% DPS loss) and 20% Scared Debuff that last 8 seconds. Towers hit up close will have the debuff values doubled to them. Performing this ability also spawns in six Blessed Souls.

abilities.label: Ability 2 Cooldown: 50
abilities.text: **Void Judgement** - The **Void Reaver** raises its sword and unleashes six beams on towers, cursing them, making it unable to attack until the **Void Reaver** reaches 0 health.

abilities.label: Ability 3 Cooldown: 35
abilities.text: **Unnerving Gaze** - The **Void Reaver** slams its sword in the ground, summoning three portals nearby, which each create a Void Eye.

abilities.label: Ability 4
abilities.text: **Void's Wrath** - Upon going below 60% of its health, stops moving for a few seconds, glitches, rips off its mask and enters its rage mode, gaining a new appearance, boosting its speed by 25% in both Hardcore and Voidcore modes and unlocking its *Void Rupture* ability. If in Voidcore mode, also summons the Void Caster.

abilities.label: Ability 5 Cooldown: 50
abilities.text: **Void Rupture** - The **Void Reaver** slashes three times, stunning towers for 5 second and applying a 25% Fatigue Debuff to them. After this, it charges its sword, before gigantifying and slashing the sword in a circle, stunning all towers for 12 seconds and dealing 1,500 damage to all units. Can be parried by dealing 300,000 damage to it.

abilities.label: Ability 6
abilities.text: **Void Deathwish** - Upon reaching 180,000 health in Hardcore mode or on the Void Caster's defeat in Voidcore mode, the **Void Reaver** speeds up to a speed of 4.5 and stops using all of its abilities.

Description: The **Void Reaver** is the final boss of Hardcore mode and Voidcore mode that spawns on Wave 45 and 50 respectively. It has the highest health out of all enemies that appeared before it, but it is also the slowest until *Void Deathwish* is activated. In Voidcore mode, it debuts alongside the Void Caster, which acts as a support for the **Void Reaver**, reviving it, summoning in enemies and giving it a shield.
The **Void Reaver** has six abilities:

- The first is *Cursed Blade*, where the **Void Reaver** slashes its sword forward, applying a 100% Fatigue Debuff and 20% Scared Debuff to towers. For towers hit up close, the debuff values are doubled. In both cases the debuffs will last 8 seconds. Additionally, the attack also summons in six Blessed Souls.
- The second is *Void Judgement*, in which the **Void Reaver** raises its sword into the sky and causes beams to appear on six towers, cursing them until the **Void Reaver** reaches 0 health.

- The third is *Unnerving Gaze* which has the **Void Reaver** slam its sword into the ground, causing three portals to appear that later turn into a Void Eye, an enemy which will fire projectiles at towers and units, stunning and damaging them.

- The fourth is the second phase for the **Void Reaver** is *Void's Wrath*, triggered once it reaches 60% of its health. In all modes, this unlocks its next ability, *Void Rupture*, but in Hardcore and Voidcore modes, it will also gain a 25% speed boost and in Voidcore specifically, it also summons in the Void Caster. Entering its second phase also gives it a new appearance.

- The fifth ability that is unlocked after *Void Wrath* is *Void Rupture*. It starts off with the **Void Reaver** slamming its sword at towers three times, stunning them for 5 seconds and applying a 25% Fatigue Debuff. Afterwards, it will start to charge up its sword which, if not stopped, this will cause it to stun all towers for 12 seconds and deal 100,000 damage to units. If 300,000 damage is dealt to it during that, the attack will get parried and the **Void Reaver** will become temporarily immobile.

- The sixth ability is its third phase, the *Void Deathwish*. Its triggering method depends on the mode, with Hardcore mode requiring its health to be reduced to 15%, so 180,000 of its health, while in Voidcore mode, it will happen once the Void Caster is killed. This phase sets its speed to 4.5 and it will stop using its abilities.
Logbook Description: "*Being the right hand and most prized giant created by the Void Caster and enhanced by Lord Exo, the Void Reaver is the epitome of the Void. Its power alone makes it one of the strongest creatures conceived. As it crossed the battlefield alongside Void Caster during the battle of the Old World, the Void Reaver slew countless Two X’s warriors. Many of the giants fell during the battle, making them incredibly rare to find. As it walks, it contaminates the ground for the Void flora to grow. Where the Void Reaver walks, the Void takes root, the soil blooming with the pale, quiet flowers that mark land the eternal nothing has claimed. No one has ever seen the limit of its strength, because nothing has ever come close to using it. The battle of the Old World ended before the Void Reaver was truly tested, and Void Caster has not since found someone worthy for it to target. What it is truly capable of still remains a question. Above all, the Void Reaver answers only to her, and it falls still the moment her song reaches it.*"
Appearance: The **Void Reaver** has dark purple skin and six eyes. It wears black and purple body armor covering its entire body and a mask covering most of its head. There is a purple hexagon on its chest. The **Void Reaver** has purple spikes and horns on its body, which once in *Void Wrath*, are accompanied by even more pink spikes. Upon entering *Void Wrath* it will also rip its mask off. It carries a large broadsword to attack towers with.
Strategy: - As with most major bosses, high DPS towers such as the Juggernaut, Pursuit, Ranger, Turret and Accelerator are recommended to deal with the **Void Reaver**.
- The Commander, Medic and DJ Booth can also be used to boost these towers.
- As the **Void Reaver** has the Boss attribute, meaning majority of stalling options are unable to stall it.
- The Freezer, Frost Blaster and Sledger can only chill the **Void Reaver** instead of freezing it.
- The Electroshocker, Tesla and Warden also cannot stun it, and have a weaker slowing effect on it.

- Make sure to sell any Farms to maximize the number of towers attacking the **Void Reaver**. They do not produce any income anymore, still count towards your tower limit, and can be replaced by a more useful tower.

- The **Void Reaver's** *Void's Deathwish* ability activates at 180,000 health in Hardcore mode or if the Void Caster is killed in Voidcore mode, making it significantly faster, running past defenses.
- Replace your towers quickly when the **Void Reaver** gets out of range.
- Use towers with long ranges like the Ranger as you will no need to waste cash replacing it.
- Using high health units such as Riot Guard is recommended.
- The Pursuit is also very effective as you can reposition it.
- The **Void Reaver** can curse towers, which effectively stuns them until its health goes down to 0.
- For more important towers, it is generally recommended to sell and rebuy them.
Update History: - **Bug**: **Void's Wrath** retains a slightly incorrect appearance, still wielding the normal variant of its sword, as opposed to the intended version.
- **Bug**: **Void Reaver** has a grey cube on its torso.
- *Void Rupture* parry threshold increased from 75,000 to 300,000.
- Speed decreased from 0.95 to 0.9 in Hardcore mode.
- Speed decreased from 0.95 to 0.9 in Sandbox mode.
- Speed decreased from 0.9 to 0.85 in Hardcore mode.
- Speed increased from 0.65 to 0.68 in Voidcore mode.
- Cash given changed from $480,000 every 20% health to $240,000 every 10% health in Hardcore mode.
- Cash given changed from $400,000 every 20% health to $150,000 every 10% health in Voidcore mode.
- *Cursed Blade* Soul spawn count decreased from 8 to 6.
- *Void Judgement* beam count increased from 5 to 6.
- Speed boost is now triggered in Hardcore mode.
- *Void Rupture* unit damage decreased from 100,000 to 1,500.

abilities.label: Ability 1
abilities.text: **Void Stomp** - The **Void Reaver** stomps on the ground, which creates a shockwave, stunning nearby ground towers and dealing 5,000 damage to units. Can only be performed when first spawning or after ***Void Rage*** becomes active.

abilities.label: Ability 2
abilities.text: **Void Energy** - The **Void Reaver** conjures up multiple void-energized pink spheres that stun towers.

abilities.label: Ability 3
abilities.text: **Void Slam** - The **Void Reaver** slams its broadsword into the ground, creating a straight shockwave that stuns towers caught on hit and deals 5,000 damage to units. Every humanoid tower stunned by this ability will spawn a Soul. It is unable to perform this attack when *Void Rage* becomes active.

abilities.label: Ability 4
abilities.text: **Void Portal** - The **Void Reaver** points its hand forward, summoning portals behind it that can summon anywhere from around 10-20 enemies. These spawn Fallens, Mega Slows, Lavas, Unknowns, Slow Kings, Speedy Kings, Mystery Bosses, Fallen Heroes and Mysteries. When the Enemies Beta modifier is active, it spawns Breaker2s and Breaker4s instead of Mysteries and Mystery Bosses.

abilities.label: Ability 5
abilities.text: **Void Rage** - At 600,000 health, the **Void Reaver** throws its broadsword at the end of the path, reducing the base health by 160, though it cannot reduce it to anything lower than 1. Then, it tears off its mask and stomps the ground, which creates a large shockwave. No longer can perform the *Void Slam* ability and the *Void Portal* ability can summon more enemies.

abilities.label: Ability 6
abilities.text: **Void's Deathwish** - At 240,000 health, the **Void Reaver** puts its hand slightly forward, speeding it up significantly.

Description: The **Void Reaver** was the final boss in Hardcore mode before getting replaced by its modern version. Currently, it can only be spawned in Sandbox mode if the player has the Sandbox Plus+ gamepass. It moves at an extremely slow speed, but it has an extremely high amount of health, higher than all other non-event enemies in the game except the Nuclear Monster. The **Void Reaver** has many abilities that can stun towers, decrease base health, destroy and kill units or increase its speed. It is one of the toughest enemies in the game.
Appearance: The **Void Reaver** wields a dark brown broadsword with a bright purple glowing crystal. It has black reflective skin, but its right arm is purple. It has dark purple curvy horns on its head and arms. It wears granite armor, and its chestplate is purple and grey. In the middle of the chestplate is a purple gem. It also wears a purple and grey glove and dark purple boots. Its legs are purple granite. It has a mask that resembles an African tribal mask and has six eyes.

When *Void Rage* is activated, it transforms; its horns, eyes and right arm glow pink. Its mask is destroyed. Pink particles are now emitted from its hands and legs. When *Void's Deathwish* is activated, it will put its hand slightly forward and significantly speed up.
Strategy: This strategy refers to the state of the game while the **Void Reaver** still appeared in the Hardcore mode.
- The Ranger and Pursuit are recommended to deal with the **Void Reaver** as they are immune to stuns.
- Be aware that Ranger; and Pursuit when upgraded on the top path, do not have hidden detection, so they cannot deal with the Souls that spawn from the **Void Reaver**.
- However, the Pursuit's missiles may indirectly hit the Souls spawned from the **Void Reaver** if there is a detectable enemy nearby.
- Air-based towers, such as the Ace Pilot, cannot be stunned by the **Void Reaver**.
- The Turret, Golden Minigunner and Accelerator are recommended towers against the **Void Reaver** due to their high DPS and ability to target the Souls that the **Void Reaver** can spawn.
- Turrets and Golden Minigunner can help with Souls if placed at the back, as they will not be hit by the **Void Reaver's** *Void Slam*.
- However, if the Accelerators are locked onto the **Void Reaver**, they cannot target the Souls spawned by them.
- The Engineer can be very useful due to its sentries having high DPS while also being immune to damage from stuns while their shield is active.

- This shield is only active when the Engineer is not stunned. The Medic is recommended because it can shield the Engineer from the stun, preventing the Engineer itself from being stunned. This makes sentries practically invulnerable to damage from abilities.
- The Medic is also unable to be stunned by the **Void Reaver**.
- The **Void Reaver** has extremely high health and becomes significantly faster during its *Void Deathwish* ability. This means that you may need to sell and replace your towers in the back.

- However, because of how income works in Hardcore mode, you will not earn any cash from damaging the **Void Reaver** until you kill it. Because of this, you may need to save some money to relocate your towers beforehand.
- The Gladiator and Warden can block one of the **Void Reaver's** attacks every few seconds.
- Despite being able to block the stun, the Gladiator and Warden will still have a Soul spawned from it when attacked with *Void Slam*.
- They are still not recommended against the **Void Reaver** despite this, due to their very short range.
- It is recommended to chain the Commander's *Call to Arms* ability to ensure that your towers are always shooting as fast as possible.

- Due to its Stun Immunity, Electroshocker, Warden and Archer can only slow down the **Void Reaver** instead of stunning it. Additionally, the Warden can only slow it down for a shorter time, because of its large size.

- Freezing towers like the Cryomancer or Freezer can slow down the **Void Reaver** with their chillness, though the effect will be weaker on the **Void Reaver** as it is a boss. It also cannot be frozen.
- The Jester cannot confuse the **Void Reaver**, but it can still slow it down with its ice bombs.
- The DJ Booth cannot slow it down, as it is a boss enemy.
- You can place a few Level 0 towers as a bait near the track so that when the **Void Reaver** uses its *Void Slam*, it has a chance to target that tower instead of your important, attacking towers.

- Do note that some towers that could have been useful for this, like the Farm or Military Base, cannot be attacked by the **Void Reaver**. Towers like the Commander or Golden Scout can be used instead.
- Spreading these towers can also greatly help limit the number of Souls spawned by the **Void Reaver**.
Trivia: - The **Void Reaver** was originally called *Paidion* as it was an enemy made by a contributor.
- This is the second enemy that can damage base health without dying, the first being the Swordmaster.

- The Umbra, Ducky D00M, Mecha-claus, Rift Walker and Narrator could also damage the base health without dying. However, unlike the **Void Reaver**, they could actually decrease your base health to zero.
- Upon death, it collapses onto the floor with two hands on the floor and kneeling down. After a short period, it starts to dematerialize.
- This could be a reference to Thanos' Snap.
- This could also be a reference to *Tower Battles'* Void, which has a similar death animation.
- The **Void Reaver** used to be the second major boss that spawned twice in the same wave prior to the 23rd of April 2022.
- The first to do so was the Gravekeeper, but it was replaced by the Grave Digger.
- After the 23rd of April 2022, the **Void Reaver** only spawns once at Wave 50 of Hardcore Mode.
- The **Void Reaver's** rage mode scream and death sound are the yell sound from *Call of Duty: Black Ops II*, specifically, the Zombies mode.
- The **Void Reaver** has the slowest speed for any boss in the game outside of its *Void's Deathwish* ability.
- The **Void Reaver's** theme, Raze the Void, was first played on the final wave during Hardcore Testing BETA. This was changed when it was added to the Overhaul Update.
- The second version of the **Void Reaver's** theme is a remix of Devourer of Gods from *Terraria Calamity Mod*.
- This was changed back in the Frost Invasion Update due to a copyright issue with the original creator.
- The *Void Portal* ability has the same sound as the horde sound from *Left 4 Dead 2*.
- During Hardcore Testing BETA, the **Void Reaver** had 600,000 health and spawned twice.

- Before the Entity System Update, if the **Void Reaver** used its *Void Slam* ability on a tower, the Soul spawned from the tower would be called "*Tower's Soul*" with the tower's name being the one that the Soul spawned from instead of "**Void Reaver's** Soul".
- Weirdly, the **Void Reaver** can still spawn a Soul from a non-humanoid tower. This includes towers like Turret or Ace Pilot.
- The **Void Reaver's** *Void Energy* ability is similar to the Void Reaver's *Nullifier Artillery* ability from *Risk of Rain 2*.
- The **Void Reaver's** stomp shockwave is actually smaller than the legacy Fallen King's stomp shockwave, despite being stronger.
- However, its actual stomp radius is actually much bigger than the legacy Fallen King's stomp radius.
Update History: - **Bug**: *Void Rage* ability does not work properly on Autumn Falling. The **Void Reaver** does not throw its sword at the exit and decrease the base health, instead it stops moving until its *Void's Deathwish* ability is activated.
- **Bug**: *Void Slam* ability can spawn Souls from a tower even if it is not a humanoid.

Description: The **Void Rusher** is a fast enemy that appears in Hardcore and Voidcore modes. It has lower health than most enemies it spawns alongside with, however, it is way faster than all of them. It has Shield Health which, once depleted, causes the shield its holding to break, more than halving its speed and removing its Defense.
Logbook Description: "*Void Rushers are created once Swifts earn their ranking and are promoted into carrying the Shield of the Void. How they go about choosing who is and who is not fit for the title is unknown, but once they pick up the shield it is forbidden to place it down. The shield weighs more than their own bodies, yet even that is lighter than the burden of holding the frontline of the Void.*"
Appearance: The **Void Rusher** has black skin and purple markings on its body. It wears purple armor on its torso and legs and also has a purple helmet. It carries the Shield of the Void which is destroyed when its Shield Health is depleted.
Strategy: - Depleting the **Void Rusher's** Shield Health as fast as possible is crucial to dramatically slowing it down before it becomes a major threat.
- Utilizing high DPS towers such as the Engineer, Accelerator, Juggernaut or Kingpin can quickly drain the **Void Rusher's** Shield Health.
- The Commander and Medic can decrease the firerate of your towers, allowing them to kill the **Void Rusher** faster.
- The DJ Booth can also increase your towers' range to cover more path.
- Because of its extremely swift speed, using towers such as the Electroshocker, Tesla, Freezer or Frost Blaster can slow down the **Void Rusher**.
- In addition, defense melting towers like the Pyromancer, Frost Blaster or Golden Pyromancer can decrease the high Defense of the **Void Rusher**.
Trivia: - The **Void Rusher** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Void Rusher** added, replacing the Fallen Rusher.

abilities.label: Ability 1 Cooldown: 25
abilities.text: **Void Tear** - The **Void Swordmaster** grabs its swords and slices the ground in the shape of a cross, each part with four explosions each, giving itself Health Regen for 5.67 seconds, stunning towers for 10 seconds and dealing 150 damage to units. Has a range of 15.

abilities.label: Ability 2 Cooldown: 35
abilities.text: **Impaling Sword** - The **Void Swordmaster** impales the ground, causing multiple explosions that apply a 150% Fatigue Debuff (37.5% DPS loss) and 12.5% Scared Debuff to towers for 17.5 seconds and also dealing 500 damage to units. Has a range of 30 and can hit up to 25 towers.

abilities.label: Ability 3
abilities.text: **Undying Will** - At half health, the **Void Swordmaster** gains 150,000 Shield Health, gains a 50% speed boost and has its *Impaling Sword* cooldown reduced to 20.

Description: The **Void Swordmaster** is a major boss from the Hardcore and Voidcore modes, spawning on Wave 43 and Wave 48 respectively. It has the highest health of all enemies that appeared before it and a slightly slow speed, eventually speeding up to be average.
The **Void Swordmaster** has three abilities:

- The first is *Void Tear*, where the **Void Swordmaster** slices the ground, creating four lines of four explosions forming a cross. Any tower hit by an explosion gets stunned for 10 seconds while units receive 150 damage. The **Void Swordmaster** itself will also gain Health Regen for 5.67 seconds while performing this.

- The second is *Impaling Sword*, where the **Void Swordmaster** impales the ground, creating multiple explosions that apply a 150% Fatigue Debuff and 12.5% Scared Debuff, which both last for 17.5 seconds. This ability also deals 500 damage to units and can hit up to 25 towers.
- The third is *Undying Will*, which triggers at half health. The **Void Swordmaster** gains 150,000 Shield Health, a 50% speed boost, and has its *Impaling Sword* cooldown halved.
Logbook Description: "*The Void Sword Master is the commander of the Void Knights. Guided by the Void, he is deadly in his art. Void Caster, surprisingly, did not create the Void Sword Master. She found him. He’s a remnant of the Old World who had already made a name for himself, but he had no purpose to achieve. Seeing an opportunity, the Void Caster gave him one. The Void Sword Master does not speak often, and there is no record of him losing a fight. (Until today.) Void Caster trusts him completely, but even she does not know the extent of what he is capable of. Instead, she has decided there is not a need to.*"
Appearance: The **Void Swordmaster** has a black, muscular body and a glowing purple face. There are many spots on its body which are glowing purple. It wears a purple robe with gold accents and runes written on it, a black and gold belt, a gold armband on its left arm and a gold crown. On its back it carries two swords which it uses to attack towers and units with.
Strategy: - The **Void Swordmaster** is widely considered one of the greatest run-killers in Hardcore mode. It should be treated as a high priority target.
- High DPS towers like the Juggernaut. Accelerator or Turret are recommended for use against the **Void Swordmaster**.
- Towers like the DJ Booth, Commander, and Medic can be used to enhance the DPS of those towers.
- Do not underestimate the **Void Swordmaster's** speed, as it is one of the bosses with the fastest base speed, especially after using the ability *Undying Will*.
- Towers like the Freezer, Cryomancer and Sledger cannot freeze the **Void Swordmaster**, but they can add chill to it, slowing it down and giving more time to attack.

- Towers that apply stun, like the Electroshocker, Tesla and Warden can slow it too, yet these are less reliable either due to their stun times being quite low or, in the case of the Warden, the **Void Swordmaster's** size reducing it significantly.
- The Medic can be used to protect towers from the **Void Swordmaster's** *Void Tear* ability, as it stun time is rather long.
- Do note that, although it can be used to protect from stuns, it cannot grant immunity to debuffs such as those from the *Impaling Sword* ability.
- It is recommended to temporarily set one or two of your DPS towers to target the *Last* or the *Weakest* enemy to dispose of the Void Cultists that accompany the **Void Swordmaster**.
Trivia: - The **Void Swordmaster** is based on the Fallen Swordmaster from the original Hardcore mode, who in turn was based on the Swordmaster from the SFOTH Event.
- The concept art of the **Void Swordmaster** is created by DaddyDonuts.
- The **Void Swordmaster** is based on Pontiff Sulyvanh from *Dark Souls 3*, Xeroc from the *Calamity Mod*, and Gorr the God Butcher.
- The **Void Swordmaster** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Bug**: **Void Swordmaster** will appear as unlocked in the Index, but players will be unable to summon it in Sandbox mode without Sandbox Plus+.
- Health increased from 650,000 to 700,000 in Voidcore mode.
- Speed decreased from Slightly Slow (2) to Slow (1.75).
- *Void Tear* now gives the **Void Swordmaster** Health Regen for 5.67 seconds.
- *Undying Will* Shield Health increased from 100,000 to 150,000.

It has high health, higher than every enemy that appeared before it, though it walks at a below average speed. It has one ability where it will slam its hammer at a tower or unit in its range of 10. This will cause a line of shockwave to appear, starting with a shockwave made where the targeted tower or unit is and continuing forward, creating three more shockwaves. Any tower hit by it will get stunned for 3 seconds, while units receive 135 damage.
Logbook Description: "*During the battle with Two X and Lord Exo, the Void Titans stood with their hammers on the frontlines of battle. They slaughtered countless fighters and were part of the effort when Lord Exo was slaying millions. Lord Exo's influence would not have been as vast without the efforts of the Void, and residents were hunted down and gathered by the Titans to be offered to the Void Caster.*"

It wears a purple chestplate with shoulder-pads that covers its torso, shoulders and waist, a few bands on its arms with glowing purple crystals and a purple helmet. It has glowing purple horns on its head. It carries a large hammer that it uses to stun towers and damage units.

void_trickster.name: Void Trickster
void_trickster.description: The Void Trickster is a summoner enemy that appears in Hardcore and Voidcore modes. It has decent health but also walks rather slowly.

abilities.label: Ability 1 Cooldown: 18
abilities.text: **Portal** - Fires a few projectiles from its staff which create a Void Portal on the path.

abilities.label: Ability 2 Cooldown: 30
abilities.text: **Summon** - Slams its staff, summoning in a Speedy King.

Description: The **Void Trickster** is a summoner enemy that appears in Hardcore and Voidcore modes. It has decent health but also walks rather slowly. It has both the Stun Immunity and Freeze Immunity, making it harder to stall.

It has two ability, the first, *Portal*, has it fire a few projectiles which will travel a short distance before making a Void Portal on the path. This portal will periodically summon in enemies. The second ability is *Summon*, in which the **Void Trickster** slams its staff and summons in a Speedy King.
Logbook Description: "*The Void Trickster is a summoner who opens the gate for enemies to run through. In the Void, there are places called Vaults where thousands of enemies reside. The Vaults are puts in the ground that enemies cannot escape from, where the ground is loaded with plants and flowers for the creatures to lay theirs heads upon. When a gate is created instinctually[sic] the enemies will run in that direction and spew out the other side, attacking the first thing they see. Void Tricksters are a specialized variant of Odd that Void Caster bestows a curse upon. The clothes they wear are to symbolize their group. Although time isn't able to be told in the Void, they often meet to share stories, practice magic, and have the occasional gossip.*"
Appearance: The **Void Trickster** has purple body and has multiple glowing purple lines on its body. It wears a black robe, a black wizard's hat with a gem on it, black pants and purple shoes. It wields a staff which it uses to cast various spells.
Strategy: - Deal with this enemy as soon as possible. Leaving it alive for too long will allow it to create many Void Portals from its *Portal* ability, which then continuously spawn a huge amount of Voidlings, overwhelming your towers.

- You will also want to defeat it quickly, as its other ability, *Summon*, spawns a Speedy King, which upon defeated will increase the speed of enemies. This can be even deadlier if the enemy that it boosts has high health, such as the Unknown Boss.
- The Saboteur tower is a nuisance against this enemy, since its *Aggressive Toxins* ability lets towers target it directly and further weaken it.
- High DPS towers like the Accelerator, Juggernaut, Engineer and Turret should be used to take it down quickily.
- Support towers such as the Medic, Commander and DJ Booth can further speed up the **Void Trickster's** death.

- Since the **Void Trickster** has both the Freeze and Stun immunities, freezing towers like the Freezer and stunning towers like the Tesla cannot freeze or stun the **Void Trickster**, though the latter can still slow it down.
Trivia: - The **Void Trickster** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Void Trickster** added, replacing the Necromancer Boss.

Description: The **Voidling** is a fast enemy that appears in both Hardcore and Voidcore mode. It has rather high health though lower than the Blighted, but it is twice as fast as it.

It has one ability where on maps with more than one path, it will jump from one path to another around every 8 to 12 seconds. During this, it becomes a Flying enemy. As no maps in either mode it appears in have more than one path, this ability cannot be seen in normal gameplay.
Logbook Description: "*Voidlings are the army’s standard issue. They are an Odd crammed into a set of armor and set loose into the world. When possible, they will throw themselves across the field and continue their path towards the enemy without any regard to their safety. They simply go where they are told and will do everything they can to get there.*"
Appearance: The **Voidling** has purple skin and neon pink eyes. One of its arms is visibly shorter than the other. It wears grey armor on its feet, shoulders neck and waist, strapped to it with brown clothing. It also has multiple neon pink crystals growing on its body.
Strategy: - DPS towers such as the Crook Boss, Accelerator, Enforcer, and Engineer can be helpful at taking down the **Voidling**.
- Support towers such as the Commander and DJ Booth can further support your towers to defeating it quicker.
- As the **Voidling** is quite fast, slowing towers such as the Freezer, Electroshocker, and Tesla can be used to slow and stun it, mitigating its speed.
- Do be aware that due to its normally large size, it can only be slowed down for a short amount of time compared to smaller enemies.
Trivia: - The **Voidling's** ability to jump between paths goes unused in both Hardcore and Voidcore modes as neither mode actually contains maps with more than one path, though it was shown during its appearance in Nil Zone II.
- Despite this being unused in Hardcore and Voidcore, its logbook description still mentions this ability.
- This technically makes the **Voidling** the first non-boss enemy able to switch lanes, and also the second evergreen enemy to be able to do so (the first being Frost Spirit).
- The **Voidling** is unaffected by enemy appearance modifiers, such as Talk Like a Pirate Day.
Update History: - **Voidling** now appears in Nil Zone II as part of the Halloween 2026 Live Events.
- **Voidling** no longer spawns in Nil Zone II, as the Halloween 2026 Live Event has ended.

abilities.label: Ability Cooldown: 10
abilities.text: **Heartfelt Laser** - The **Warden** fires out a laser from its exposed heart for 3.5 seconds, stunning towers for 2 seconds and dealing 8 damage to units every tick. Has an attack range of 20.

Description: The **Warden**, internally referred to as the **Templar**, is an enemy that appears in Polluted Wasteland II and Challenge Trials. It also spawns once in Fallen mode during the Hidden Wave. It has very high health with high defense and average speed. It has an ability where it fires a glowing purple laser from its chest to stun every tower and damage every unit that comes in contact with it, making it very dangerous and a number-one priority.
Appearance: The **Warden** is a large humanoid entity with a waist in its rig. It has a dark blue skin color and the ends of its limbs are covered in a cyan fluid. It has an energy pack on its back with an antenna that emits yellow sparks along with batteries connected to it. This energy pack has grey straps. The **Warden** also has metal plating on its body. Its chest has a gaping cavity, revealing its rib cage and a pink cube inside, which emits light blue particles. It has red wounds that span horizontally across the chest cavity.
Strategy: - The **Warden** is a high health enemy which is also Hidden, making it particularly dangerous.
- High DPS towers like the Accelerator or Minigunner should be used to take the **Warden** down.
- Towers like the Ranger can be used if combined with a way to make it target the **Warden**, like the Spotlight Tech or Firework Technician.
- The Commander should be used to boost the firerate of these towers.
- The Engineer is recommended, as its sentries will continue firing even when the Engineer is stunned by the **Warden's** *Heartfelt Laser* ability.
- The Pursuit cannot be stunned by the **Warden's** *Heartfelt Laser* ability.
- The Military Base's units deal full collision damage to the **Warden**, regardless of its defense, making them quite useful.
- Do note that their ranged damage is still decreased.
- It is recommended to place your towers away from the path to avoid getting stunned by the **Warden's** *Heartfelt Laser* ability.
- It may be viable to have a cheap distraction tower to distract the **Warden's** *Heartfelt Laser* from your main offensive towers.
- When the **Warden** spawns, it will not use its *Heartfelt Laser* ability for a few seconds. Use this period of time to defeat the **Warden** before it can stun any towers.
- The Medic can be used to shield towers that, preventing them from being stunned by the **Warden's** *Heartfelt Laser* ability.
- Do note that this will be ineffective while the **Warden** is still using *Heartfelt Laser*, as the towers will be continuously stunned until the ability is over.

- The Gladiator's stun blocking is ineffective against the **Warden**, since even after it successfully blocks *Heartfelt Laser's* initial stun, it will be stunned again because of how long the ability lasts.
- Slowing towers like the Saboteur, Electroshocker, Warden or Freezer can be used to slow down the **Warden**.
- However, because of its large size, freezing towers and the Warden will slow it down for a shorter amount of time.
- Do note that the **Warden** will not stop using its ability when frozen or stunned.
- Defense dropping towers like the Pyromancer, Jester or Freezer can help to reduce the **Warden's** defense.
Trivia: - The **Warden** is very similar to Warden enemy of the same name, first added in v1.3.0 for the very first version of Polluted Wasteland II.

- Despite their similarities in name, design and functionality, they are technically not the legacy and modern variants of each other, as the **Warden** currently seen in Polluted Wasteland II is in reality the modern version of the Templar enemy.
- Because of this, both of them have two separate Logbooks that require to be collected.
Update History: - **Bug**: Poison and electric defense dropping no longer decreases **Templar's** defense.
- **Bugfix**: Poison and electric defense dropping now drops **Templar's** defense, though the Jester still cannot drop it.
- Now appears in Polluted Wasteland II, replacing the Warden.

- Do note that this will be ineffective while the **Warden** is still firing its *Heartfelt Laser*, as the towers will be continuously stunned until the ability is over.
